body.text: Saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtram |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīkasūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Lotus of the True Dharma).

body.text: || namaḥ sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ | namaḥ sarvatathāgatapratyekabuddhāryaśrāvakebhyo 'tītānāgatapratyutpannebhyaśca bodhisattvebhyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Homage to all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! Homage to all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and noble <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past, future, and present!

body.text: Saddhp_1: nidānaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 1: The <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction) Chapter.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma gṛdhrakūṭe parvate mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ dvādaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ sarvairarhadbhiḥ kṣīṇāsravairniḥkleśairvaśībhūtaiḥ suvimuktacittaiḥ suvimuktaprajñairājāneyairmahānāgaiḥ kṛtakṛtyaiḥ kṛtakaraṇīyairapahṛtabhārairanuprāptasvakārthaiḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaiḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaiḥ sarvacetovaśitāparamapāramitāprāptairabhijñātābhijñātairmahāśrāvakaiḥ | tadyathā - āyuṣmatā ca ājñātakauṇḍinyena, āyuṣmatā ca aśvajitā, āyuṣmatā ca bāṣpeṇa, āyuṣmatā ca mahānāmnā, āyuṣmatā ca bhadrikeṇa, āyuṣmatā ca mahākāśyapena, āyuṣmatā ca urubilvakāśyapena, āyuṣmatā ca nadīkāśyapena, āyuṣmatā ca gayākāśyapena, āyuṣmatā ca śāriputreṇa, āyuṣmatā ca mahāmaudgalyāyanena, āyuṣmatā ca mahākātyāyanena, āyuṣmatā ca aniruddhena, āyuṣmatā ca revatena, āyuṣmatā ca kapphinena, āyuṣmatā ca gavāṃpatinā, āyuṣmatā ca pilindavatsena, āyuṣmatā ca bakkulena, āyuṣmatā ca mahākauṣṭhilena, āyuṣmatā ca bharadvājena, āyuṣmatā ca mahānandena, āyuṣmatā ca upanandena, āyuṣmatā ca sundaranandena, āyuṣmatā ca pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputreṇa, āyuṣmatā ca subhūtinā āyuṣmatā ca rāhulena | ebhiścānyaiśca mahāśrāvakaiḥ - āyuṣmatā ca ānandena śaikṣeṇa | anyābhyāṃ ca dvābhyāṃ bhikṣusahasrābhyāṃ śaikṣāśaikṣābhyām | mahāprajāpatīpramukhaiśca ṣaḍbhirbhikṣuṇīsahasraiḥ |
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain, together with a great assembly of monks — twelve hundred monks in all, all of them <s>Arhats</s>, with outflows destroyed, free from afflictions, self-mastered, with well-liberated minds, with well-liberated wisdom, thoroughbreds, great elephants, who had done what was to be done, done what needed doing, cast off the burden, attained their own goal, exhausted the fetters of becoming, with minds well-liberated through right knowledge, who had attained the supreme perfection of mastery over all mental states, known and recognized — great <s>Śrāvakas</s>. Namely: the venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, the venerable <s>Aśvajit</s>, the venerable <s>Bāṣpa</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānāman</s>, the venerable <s>Bhadrika</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Urubilvakāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>, the venerable <s>Revata</s>, the venerable <s>Kapphina</s>, the venerable <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, the venerable <s>Pilindavatsa</s>, the venerable <s>Bakkula</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākauṣṭhila</s>, the venerable <s>Bharadvāja</s>, the venerable <s>Mahānanda</s>, the venerable <s>Upananda</s>, the venerable <s>Sundarananda</s>, the venerable <s>Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>. Together with these and other great <s>Śrāvakas</s> — including the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, a learner. And with two other thousands of monks, both learners and those beyond learning. And with six thousand nuns led by <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s>.

body.text: yaśodharayā ca bhikṣuṇyā rāhulamātrā saparivārayā | aśītyā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ sarvairavaivartikairekajātipratibaddhairyaduta anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, dhāraṇīpratilabdhairmahāpratibhānapratiṣṭhitairavaivartyadharmacakrapravartakairbahubuddhaśataparyupāsitairbahubuddha śatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlairbuddhaśatasahasrasaṃstutairmaitrīparibhāvitakāyacittaistathāgatajñānāvatāraṇakuśalairmahāprajñaiḥ prajñāpāramitāgatiṃgatairbahulokadhātuśatasahasraviśrutairbahuprāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrasaṃtārakaiḥ | tadyathā - mañjuśriyā ca kumārabhūtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, avalokiteśvareṇa ca mahāsthāmaprāptena ca sarvārthanāmnā ca nityodyuktena ca anikṣiptadhureṇa ca ratnapāṇinā ca bhaiṣajyarājena ca bhaiṣajyasamudgatena ca vyūharājena ca pradānaśūreṇa ca ratnacandreṇa ca ratnaprabheṇa
body.translated_text: And with the nun <s>Yaśodharā</s>, the mother of <s>Rāhula</s>, together with her retinue. And with eighty thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all irreversible, bound to one [more] birth — that is, to unsurpassed perfect awakening — who had obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mnemonic power), established in great eloquence, turners of the irreversible <s>Dharma</s>-wheel, who had attended upon many hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s>, who had planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, who were praised by hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, whose body and mind were suffused with <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), skilled in descending into the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, of great wisdom, who had gone to the furthest shore of the perfection of wisdom, renowned throughout many hundreds of thousands of world-systems, who had saved many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundreds of thousands of beings. Namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, <s>Sarvārthanāman</s>, <s>Nityodyukta</s>, <s>Anikṣiptadhura</s>, <s>Ratnapāṇi</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyasamudgata</s>, <s>Vyūharāja</s>, <s>Pradānaśūra</s>, <s>Ratnacandra</s>, <s>Ratnaprabha</s>,

body.text:
ca pūrṇacandreṇa ca mahāvikrāmiṇā ca anantavikrāmiṇā ca trailokyavikrāmiṇā ca mahāpratibhānena ca satatasamitābhiyuktena ca dharaṇīdhareṇa ca akṣayamatinā ca padmaśriyā ca nakṣatrarājena ca maitreyeṇa ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena, siṃhena ca bodhisattvena mahāsattvena | bhadrapālapūrvaṃgamaiśca ṣoḍaśabhiḥ satpuruṣaiḥ sārdham | tadyathā - bhadrapālena ca ratnākareṇa ca susārthavāhena ca naradattena ca guhyaguptena ca varuṇadattena ca indradattena ca uttaramatinā ca viśeṣamatinā ca vardhamānamatinā ca amoghadarśinā ca susaṃprasthitena ca suvikrāntavikrāmiṇā ca anupamamatinā ca sūryagarbheṇa ca dharaṇīṃdhareṇa ca | evaṃpramukhairaśītyā ca bodhisattvasahasraiḥ sārdham | śakreṇa ca devānāmindreṇa sārdhaṃ viṃśatidevaputrasahasraparivāreṇa | tadyathā - candreṇa ca devaputreṇa sūryeṇa ca devaputreṇa samantagandhena ca devaputreṇa ratnaprabheṇa ca devaputreṇa avabhāsaprabheṇa ca devaputreṇa | evaṃpramukhairviśatyā ca devaputrasahasraiḥ | caturbhiśca mahārājaiḥ sārdhaṃ triṃśaddevaputrasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - virūḍhakena ca mahārājena, virūpākṣeṇa ca mahārājena, dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa ca mahārājena, vaiśravaṇena ca mahārājena | īśvareṇa ca devaputreṇa ca maheśvareṇa ca devaputreṇa triṃśaddevaputrasahasraparivārābhyām | brahmaṇā ca sahāṃpatinā sārdhaṃ dvādaśabrahmakāyikadevaputrasahasraparivāreṇa
| tadyathā - śikhinā ca brahmaṇā jyotiṣprabheṇa ca brahmaṇā | evaṃpramukhairdvādaśabhiśca brahmakāyikadevaputrasahasraiḥ | aṣṭābhiśca nāgarājaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahunāgakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - nandena ca nāgarājena, upanandena ca nāgarājena, sāgareṇa ca vāsukinā ca takṣakeṇa ca manasvinā ca anavataptena ca utpalakena ca nāgarājena | caturbhiśca kinnararājaiḥ sārdhaṃ bahukinnarakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - drumeṇa ca kinnararājena, mahādharmeṇa ca kinnararājena, sudharmeṇa ca kinnararājena, dharmadhareṇa ca kinnararājena | caturbhiśca gandharvakāyikadevaputraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahugandharvaśatasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - manojñena ca gandharveṇa manojñasvareṇa ca madhureṇa ca madhurasvareṇa ca gandharveṇa | caturbhiścāsurendraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahvasurakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - balinā ca asurendreṇa, kharaskandhena ca asurendreṇa, vemacitriṇā ca asurendreṇa, rāhuṇā ca asurendreṇa | caturbhiśca garuḍendraiḥ sārdhaṃ bahugaruḍakoṭīśatasahasraparivāraiḥ | tadyathā - mahātejasā ca garuḍendreṇa, mahākāyena ca mahāpūrṇena ca maharddhiprāptena ca garuḍendreṇa | rājñā ca ajātaśatruṇā māgadhena vaidehīputreṇa sārdham ||
body.translated_text: <s>Pūrṇacandra</s>, <s>Mahāvikrāmin</s>, <s>Anantavikrāmin</s>, <s>Trailokyavikrāmin</s>, <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s>, <s>Dharaṇīdhara</s>, <s>Akṣayamati</s>, <s>Padmaśrī</s>, <s>Nakṣatrarāja</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Siṃha</s>. And with sixteen good men led by <s>Bhadrapāla</s>. Namely: <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, <s>Ratnākara</s>, <s>Susārthavāha</s>, <s>Naradatta</s>, <s>Guhyagupta</s>, <s>Varuṇadatta</s>, <s>Indradatta</s>, <s>Uttaramati</s>, <s>Viśeṣamati</s>, <s>Vardhamānamati</s>, <s>Amoghadarśin</s>, <s>Susaṃprasthita</s>, <s>Suvikrāntavikrāmin</s>, <s>Anupamamati</s>, <s>Sūryagarbha</s>, and <s>Dharaṇīṃdhara</s>. Together with eighty thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> led by these. And with <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, together with a retinue of twenty thousand <s>devaputras</s> (divine sons). Namely: the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Candra</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Sūrya</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Samantagandha</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Ratnaprabha</s>, the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Avabhāsaprabha</s>. Together with twenty thousand <s>devaputras</s> led by these. And with the four great kings together with their retinues of thirty thousand <s>devaputras</s>. Namely: the great king <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the great king <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, the great king <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and the great king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. And with the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Īśvara</s> and the <s>devaputra</s> <s>Maheśvara</s>, together with their retinues of thirty thousand <s>devaputras</s>. And with <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, together with a retinue of twelve thousand <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s>. Namely: <s>Brahmā Śikhin</s> and <s>Brahmā Jyotiṣprabha</s>. Together with twelve thousand <s>Brahmakāyika</s> <s>devaputras</s> led by these. And with eight <s>Nāga</s>-kings together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Nāgas</s>. Namely: the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Nanda</s>, the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Upananda</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Manasvin</s>, <s>Anavatapta</s>, and the <s>Nāga</s>-king <s>Utpalaka</s>. And with four <s>Kinnara</s>-kings together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Kinnaras</s>. Namely: the <s>Kinnara</s>-king <s>Druma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king <s>Mahādharma</s>, the <s>Kinnara</s>-king <s>Sudharma</s>, and the <s>Kinnara</s>-king <s>Dharmadhara</s>. And with four <s>Gandharva</s> <s>devaputras</s> together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s>. Namely: the <s>Gandharva</s> <s>Manojña</s>, <s>Manojñasvara</s>, <s>Madhura</s>, and the <s>Gandharva</s> <s>Madhurasvara</s>. And with four <s>Asura</s>-lords together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Asuras</s>. Namely: the <s>Asura</s>-lord <s>Balin</s>, the <s>Asura</s>-lord <s>Kharaskandha</s>, the <s>Asura</s>-lord <s>Vemacitrin</s>, and the <s>Asura</s>-lord <s>Rāhu</s>. And with four <s>Garuḍa</s>-lords together with retinues of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Garuḍas</s>. Namely: the <s>Garuḍa</s>-lord <s>Mahātejas</s>, the <s>Garuḍa</s>-lord <s>Mahākāya</s>, <s>Mahāpūrṇa</s>, and the <s>Garuḍa</s>-lord <s>Maharddhiprāpta</s>. And with King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, son of <s>Vaidehī</s>, and his retinue.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavāṃścatasṛbhiḥ parṣadbhiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rcito 'pacāyito mahānirdeśaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ bhāṣitvā tasminneva mahādharmāsane paryaṅkamābhujya anantanirdeśapratiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūdaniñjamānena kāyena sthito 'niñjaprāptena ca cittena | samanantarasamāpannasya khalu punarbhagavato māndāravamahāmāndāravāṇāṃ mañjūṣakamahāmañjūṣakāṇāṃ divyānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ mahatpuṣpavarṣamabhiprāvarṣat, bhagavantaṃ tāśca catasraḥ parṣado 'bhyavākiran |
body.translated_text: At that time, the Blessed One, surrounded and attended by the fourfold assembly, honored, respected, revered, venerated, worshipped, and esteemed, having taught the <s>dharma</s>-discourse called the <s>Mahānirdeśa</s> (Great Exposition), a <s>sūtrānta</s>, a great <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive teaching), an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by all <s>Buddhas</s> — while seated on that very great <s>dharma</s>-throne, having crossed his legs, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called <s>Anantanirdeśapratiṣṭhāna</s> (The Foundation of Infinite Exposition), remaining with an unmoving body and with a mind that had attained immovability. No sooner had the Blessed One entered this concentration than a great shower of divine <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s>, <s>Mañjūṣaka</s> and great <s>Mañjūṣaka</s> flowers rained down, showering upon the Blessed One and those four assemblies.

body.text: sarvāvacca buddhakṣetraṃ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitamabhūccalitaṃ saṃpracalitaṃ vedhitaṃ saṃpravedhitaṃ kṣubhitaṃ saṃprakṣubhitam | tena khalu punaḥ samayena tasyāṃ parṣadi bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ saṃnipatitā abhūvan saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ, rājānaśca maṇḍalino balacakravartinaścaturdvīpakacakravartinaśca | te sarve saparivārā bhagavantaṃ vyavalokayanti sma āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā audbilyaprāptāḥ ||
body.translated_text: And the entire <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) trembled with six kinds of earthquakes — it shook, shook greatly, quaked, quaked greatly, trembled, and trembled greatly. At that time, in that assembly there had gathered and were seated monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans; and kings — local rulers, mighty universal monarchs, and universal monarchs of the four continents. All of them, with their retinues, gazed upon the Blessed One, filled with wonder, amazement, and elation.

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavato bhrūvivarāntarādūrṇākośādekā raśmirniścaritā | sā pūrvasyāṃ diśi aṣṭādaśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇi prasṛtā | tāni ca sarvāṇi buddhakṣetrāṇi tasyā raśmeḥ prabhayā suparisphuṭāni saṃdṛśyante sma yāvadavīcirmahānirayo yāvacca bhavāgram | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ṣaṭsu gatiṣu sattvāḥ saṃvidyante sma, te sarve 'śeṣeṇa saṃdṛśyante sma | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti ca, te 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma | yaṃ ca te buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti, sa ca sarvo nikhilena śrūyate sma | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā yogino yogācārāḥ prāptaphalāścāprāptaphalāśca, te 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu bodhisattvā mahāsattvā anekavividhaśravaṇārambaṇādhimuktihetukāraṇairupāyakauśalyairbodhisattvacaryāṃ caranti, te 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavantaḥ parinirvṛtāḥ, te 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma | ye ca teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu parinirvṛtānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ dhātustūpā ratnamayāḥ te 'pi sarve saṃdṛśyante sma ||
body.translated_text: Then, at that moment, from the tuft of white hair between the Blessed One's eyebrows — from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (hair-whorl) — a single ray of light issued forth. It extended eastward over eighteen thousand <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields). All those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, illuminated by the radiance of that ray, became clearly visible — down to the great <s>Avīci</s> hell and up to the summit of existence. And all the beings existing in the six destinies in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were seen without exception. And the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who lived, endured, and sustained themselves in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too were all seen. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, were teaching — all of it was heard completely. And the monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, practitioners, yogic adepts, those who had attained the fruit and those who had not yet attained the fruit in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too were all seen. And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> who were practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct through various means of hearing, support, aspiration, and causes, with skillful means — they too were all seen. And the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too were all seen. And the jeweled <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary shrines) of the relics of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, who had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> — they too were all seen.

body.text: atha khalu maitreyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyaitadabhūt - mahānimittaṃ prātihāryaṃ batedaṃ tathāgatena kṛtam | ko nvatra heturbhaviṣyati kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yadbhagavatā idamevaṃrūpaṃ mahānimittaṃ prātihāryaṃ kṛtam? bhagavāṃśca samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ | imāni caivaṃrūpāṇi mahāścaryādbhutācintyāni maharddhiprātihāryāṇi saṃdṛśyante sma | kiṃ nu khalvahametamarthaṃ paripraṣṭavyaṃ paripṛccheyam? ko nvatra samarthaḥ syādetamarthaṃ visarjayitum? tasyaitadabhūt - ayaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ pūrvajinakṛtādhikāro 'varopitakuśalamūlo bahubuddhaparyupāsitaḥ | dṛṣṭapūrvāṇi ca anena mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena pūrvakāṇāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmevaṃrūpāṇi nimittāni bhaviṣyanti, anubhūtapūrvāṇi ca mahādharmasāṃkathyāni | yannvahaṃ mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametamarthaṃ paripṛccheyam ||
body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "What a great sign and miracle has been performed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>! What could be the reason, what could be the cause, for the Blessed One to have performed this great sign and miracle? The Blessed One has entered <s>samādhi</s>, and these great, wondrous, marvelous, inconceivable displays of supernatural power are being seen. Whom should I ask about this matter? Who could be capable of explaining this matter?" Then this occurred to him: "This <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, has served former <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), has planted roots of merit, and has attended upon many <s>Buddhas</s>. <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, must have previously seen such signs of former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones, and must have experienced great <s>Dharma</s>-discussions before. Let me ask <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, about this matter."

body.text: tāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ bahūnāṃ ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāmimamevaṃrūpaṃ bhagavato mahānimittaṃ prātihāryāvabhāsaṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptānāmadbhutaprāptānāṃ kautūhalaprāptānāmetadabhavat - kiṃ nu khalu vayamimamevaṃrūpaṃ bhagavato maharddhiprātihāryāvabhāsaṃ kṛtaṃ paripṛcchema?
body.translated_text: The fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and the many <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — having seen this great sign, this miraculous radiance of the Blessed One, filled with wonder and amazement and curiosity — this thought occurred to them: "Whom should we ask about this great display of supernatural power and radiance performed by the Blessed One?"

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte tāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya ātmanā ca dharmasaṃśayaprāptastasyāṃ velāyāṃ mañjuśriyaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, at that very moment and instant, knowing with his mind the mental deliberation of those four assemblies, and himself having arrived at doubt regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, at that time said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>

body.text: kumārabhūtametadavocat - ko nvatra mañjuśrīrhetuḥ kaḥ pratyayo yadayamevaṃrūpa āścaryādbhuto bhagavatā ṛddhayavabhāsaḥ kṛtaḥ, imāni cāṣṭādaśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇi vicitrāṇi darśanīyāni paramadarśanīyāni tathāgatapūrvaṃgamāni tathāgatapariṇāyakāni saṃdṛśyante?
body.translated_text: <s>Kumārabhūta</s> (the prince): 'What, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the cause, what is the condition, for this kind of marvelous and wondrous display of supernatural power made by the Blessed One, and [that] these eighteen thousand Buddha-fields appear, variegated, beautiful, most beautiful, preceded by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, guided by the <s>Tathāgata</s>?'

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtamābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> addressed <s>Mañjuśrī</s> <s>Kumārabhūta</s> with these verses:

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mañjuśirī iyaṃ hi raśmiḥ pramuktā naranāyakena /
children.translated_text: For what reason, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, has this ray been released by the Leader of Men,

children.text: prabhāsayantī bhramukāntarātu ūrṇāya kośādiyamekaraśmiḥ // Saddhp_1.1 //
children.translated_text: illuminating from between the eyebrows, from the sheath of the <s>ūrṇā</s> — this single ray? || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.1 ||

children.text: māndāravāṇāṃ ca mahanta varṣaṃ puṣpāṇi muñcanti surāḥ suhṛṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: A great shower of <s>māndārava</s> [flowers], and the <s>devas</s>, greatly delighted, release flowers,

children.text: mañjūṣakāṃścandanacūrṇamiśrān divyān sugandhāṃśca manoramāṃśca // Saddhp_1.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>mañjūṣaka</s> [flowers] mixed with sandal-powder — divine, fragrant, and delightful. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.2 ||

children.text: yehī mahī śobhatiyaṃ samantāt parṣāśca catvāra sulabdhaharṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: By which this earth shines on all sides, and the four assemblies have attained great joy,

children.text: sarvaṃ ca kṣetraṃ imu saṃprakampitaṃ ṣaḍbhirvikārehi subhīṣmarūpam // Saddhp_1.3 //
children.translated_text: and this entire field has been shaken with six kinds of convulsions, of most fearsome form. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.3 ||

children.text: sā caiva raśmī purimādiśāya aṣṭādaśakṣetrasahasra pūrṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And that very ray, to the eastern direction, fills eighteen thousand fields completely,

children.text: avabhāsayī ekakṣaṇena sarve suvarṇavarṇā iva bhonti kṣetrāḥ // Saddhp_1.4 //
children.translated_text: illuminating all in a single instant — the fields become as if golden-colored. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.4 ||

children.text: yāvānavīcī paramaṃ bhavāgraṃ kṣetreṣu yāvanti ca teṣu sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Avīci</s> [hell] to the highest peak of existence — as many beings as there are in those fields,

children.text: ṣaṭsū gatīṣū tahi vidyamānā cyavanti ye cāpyupapadyi tatra // Saddhp_1.5 //
children.translated_text: existing in the six destinies — those who pass away and those who are reborn there. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.5 ||

children.text: karmāṇi citrā vividhāni teṣāṃgatīṣu dṛśyanti sukhā dukhā ca /
children.translated_text: Their variegated <s>karmas</s> of many kinds are seen in the destinies — both pleasant and painful,

children.text: hīnā praṇītā tatha madhyamā ca iha sthito addaśi sarvametat // Saddhp_1.6 //
children.translated_text: low, excellent, and middling — standing here, [<s>Maitreya</s>] saw all of this. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.6 ||

body.text: buddhāṃśca paśyāmi narendrasiṃhān prakāśayanto vivaranti dharmam /
body.translated_text: And I see Buddhas, lions among men, who illuminate and expound the <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: praśāsamānān bahusattvakoṭīḥ udāharanto madhurasvarāṃ giram // Saddhp_1.7 //
body.translated_text: calming many millions of beings, uttering speech with sweet voices. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.7 ||

children.text: gambhīranirghoṣamudāramadbhutaṃ muñcanti kṣetreṣu svakasvakeṣu /
children.translated_text: They release a deep, magnificent, and wondrous sound in their respective fields,

children.text: dṛṣṭāntahetūnayutāna koṭibhiḥ prakāśayanto imu buddhadharmam // Saddhp_1.8 //
children.translated_text: illuminating this Buddha-<s>Dharma</s> with examples, reasons, and tens of millions of illustrations. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.8 ||

children.text: duḥkhena saṃpīḍita ye ca sattvā jātījarākhinnamanā ajānakāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those beings who are oppressed by suffering, whose minds are wearied by birth and old age, who are ignorant —

children.text: teṣāṃ prakāśenti praśāntanirvṛtiṃ duḥkhasya anto ayu bhikṣave ti // Saddhp_1.9 //
children.translated_text: to them they illuminate the peaceful cessation: 'This is the end of suffering, O <s>bhikṣus</s>!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.9 ||

children.text: udārasthāmādhigatāśca ye narāḥ puṇyairupetāstatha buddhadarśanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And those men who have attained great power, endowed with merit and with the sight of the Buddhas —

children.text: pratyekayānaṃ ca vadanti teṣāṃ saṃvarṇayanto ima dharmanetrīm // Saddhp_1.10 //
children.translated_text: to them they speak of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, praising this <s>Dharma</s>-guide. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.10 ||

children.text: ye cāpi anye sugatasya putrā anuttaraṃ jñāna gaveṣamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: And yet others, sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, seeking unsurpassed knowledge,

children.text: vividhāṃ kriyāṃ kurviṣu sarvakālaṃ teṣāṃ pi bodhāya vadanti varṇam // Saddhp_1.11 //
children.translated_text: performing various practices at all times — to them too they proclaim the excellence of awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.11 ||

children.text: śṛṇomi paśyāmi ca mañjughoṣa iha sthito īdṛśakāni tatra /
children.translated_text: I hear and see, O <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, standing here, such things there;

children.text: anyā viśeṣāṇa sahasrakoṭyaḥ pradeśamātraṃ tatu varṇayiṣye // Saddhp_1.12 //
children.translated_text: and other thousands of millions of distinctions — I shall describe but a portion of them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.12 ||

children.text: paśyāmi kṣetreṣu bahūṣu cāpi ye bodhisattvā yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: I see in many fields <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: koṭīsahasrāṇi analpakāni vividhena vīryeṇa janenti bodhim // Saddhp_1.13 //
children.translated_text: thousands of millions, not few, who generate awakening with varied vigor. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.13 ||

children.text: dadanti dānāni tathaiva kecid dhanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ suvarṇam /
children.translated_text: Some give gifts likewise — wealth, gold, silver, and gold-coins,

children.text: muktāmaṇiṃ śaṅkhaśilāpravālaṃ dāsāṃśca dāsī rathaaśvaeḍakān // Saddhp_1.14 //
children.translated_text: pearls, gems, conch, crystal, and coral, male and female servants, chariots, horses, and sheep. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.14 ||

children.text: śibikāstathā ratnavibhūṣitāśca dadanti dānāni prahṛṣṭamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: And palanquins adorned with gems — they give gifts with delighted minds,

children.text: pariṇāmayanto iha agrabodhau vayaṃ hi yānasya bhavema lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_1.15 //
children.translated_text: dedicating [the merit] here to supreme awakening: 'May we become gainers of the vehicle!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.15 ||

children.text: traidhātuke śreṣṭhaviśiṣṭayānaṃ yadbuddhayānaṃ sugatehi varṇitam /
children.translated_text: 'In the three realms, the most excellent and distinguished vehicle — the Buddha-vehicle praised by the <s>Sugatas</s> —

children.text: ahaṃ pi tasyo bhavi kṣipra lābhī dadanti dānāni imīdṛśāni // Saddhp_1.16 //
children.translated_text: may I too quickly become a gainer of that!' — giving such gifts. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.16 ||

children.text: caturhayairyuktarathāṃśca kecit savedikān puṣpadhvajairalaṃkṛtān /
children.translated_text: Some [give] chariots yoked with four horses, with railings adorned with flower-banners,

children.text: savaijayantān ratanāmayāni dadanti dānāni tathaiva kecit // Saddhp_1.17 //
children.translated_text: with victory-columns — and some give jeweled gifts likewise. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.17 ||

children.text: dadanti putrāṃśca tathaiva putrīḥ priyāṇi māṃsāni dadanti kecit /
children.translated_text: Some give their sons and daughters too; some give their beloved flesh;

children.text: hastāṃśca pādāṃśca dadanti yācitāḥ paryeṣamāṇā imamagrabodhim // Saddhp_1.18 //
children.translated_text: when asked, they give their hands and feet, seeking this supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.18 ||

children.text: śirāṃsi kecinnayanāni kecid dadanti kecitpravarātmabhāvān /
children.translated_text: Some [give] their heads, some their eyes; some give their supreme own bodies;

children.text: datvā ca dānāni prasannacittāḥ prārthenti jñānaṃ hi tathāgatānām // Saddhp_1.19 //
children.translated_text: and having given gifts with joyful minds, they aspire to the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.19 ||

children.text: paśyāmyahaṃ mañjuśirī kahiṃcit sphītāni rājyāni vivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: I see, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, in certain places, having abandoned prosperous kingdoms,

children.text: antaḥpurān dvīpa tathaiva sarvān amātyajñātīṃśca vihāya sarvān // Saddhp_1.20 //
children.translated_text: inner palaces, islands, and all, and all ministers and relatives — || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.20 ||

children.text: upasaṃkramī lokavināyakeṣu pṛcchanti dharmaṃ pravaraṃ śivāya /
children.translated_text: they approach the Guides of the World, asking for the supreme <s>Dharma</s> for welfare;

children.text: kāṣāyavastrāṇi ca prāvaranti keśāṃśca śmaśrūṇyavatārayanti // Saddhp_1.21 //
children.translated_text: they put on saffron-colored robes and shave off their hair and beards. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.21 ||

body.text: kāṃścicca paśyāmyahu bodhisattvān bhikṣū samānāḥ pavane vasanti /
body.translated_text: And I see some <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who, being like <s>bhikṣus</s>, dwell in the forest,

body.text: śūnyānyaraṇyāni niṣevamāṇān uddeśasvādhyāyaratāṃśca kāṃścit // Saddhp_1.22 //
body.translated_text: frequenting empty woodlands, and some delighting in recitation and self-study. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.22 ||

children.text: kāṃścicca paśyāmyahu bodhisattvān girikandareṣu praviśanti dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: And I see some <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — the steadfast enter mountain caves,

children.text: vibhāvayanto imu buddhajñānaṃ paricintayanto hyupalakṣayanti // Saddhp_1.23 //
children.translated_text: discerning this Buddha-knowledge, reflecting and contemplating. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.23 ||

children.text: utsṛjya kāmāṃśca aśeṣato 'nye paribhāvitātmāna viśuddhagocarāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others, having completely abandoned desires, self-cultivated, of purified conduct,

children.text: abhijña pañceha ca sparśayitvā vasantyaraṇye sugatasya putrāḥ // Saddhp_1.24 //
children.translated_text: having touched the five superknowledges here, the sons of the <s>Sugata</s> dwell in the forest. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.24 ||

children.text: pādaiḥ samaiḥ sthitviha keci dhīrāḥ kṛtāñjalī saṃmukhi nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: Some steadfast ones, standing here with even feet, with joined palms facing the Leaders,

children.text: abhistavantīha harṣaṃ janitvā gāthāsahasrehi jinendrarājam // Saddhp_1.25 //
children.translated_text: having generated joy, praise the King of <s>Jinas</s> with thousands of verses. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.25 ||

children.text: smṛtimanta dāntāśca viśāradāśca sūkṣmāṃ cariṃ keci prajānamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Mindful, tamed, and confident, some knowing the subtle practice,

children.text: pṛcchanti dharmaṃ dvipadottamānāṃ śrutvā ca te dharmadharā bhavanti // Saddhp_1.26 //
children.translated_text: ask for the <s>Dharma</s> from the Best of Bipeds, and having heard, they become bearers of the <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.26 ||

children.text: paribhāvitātmāna jinendraputrān kāṃścicca paśyāmyahu tatra tatra /
children.translated_text: And I see self-cultivated sons of the Lord of <s>Jinas</s>, here and there,

children.text: dharmaṃ vadanto bahuprāṇakoṭināṃ dṛṣṭāntahetūnayutairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_1.27 //
children.translated_text: speaking the <s>Dharma</s> to many millions of beings, with examples, reasons, and innumerable illustrations. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.27 ||

children.text: prāmodyajātāḥ pravadanti dharmaṃ samādapento bahubodhisattvān /
children.translated_text: Born of delight, they proclaim the <s>Dharma</s>, exhorting many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;

children.text: nihatya māraṃ sabalaṃ savāhanaṃ parāhanantī imu dharmadundubhim // Saddhp_1.28 //
children.translated_text: having defeated <s>Māra</s> with his army and vehicles, they strike this drum of <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.28 ||

children.text: paśyāmi kāṃścit sugatasya śāsane saṃpūjitānnaramaruyakṣarākṣasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: I see some in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>, honored by humans, <s>Maruts</s> (gods), <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: avismayantān sugatasya putrān anunnatān śāntapraśāntacārīn // Saddhp_1.29 //
children.translated_text: sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, unastonished, not puffed up, practicing the peaceful and tranquil conduct. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.29 ||

children.text: vanaṣaṇḍa niśrāya tathānyarūpā avabhāsu kāyātu pramuñcamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: And others of different form, dwelling in forest groves, releasing radiance from their bodies,

children.text: abhyuddharanto narakeṣu sattvāṃstāṃścaiva bodhāya samādapenti // Saddhp_1.30 //
children.translated_text: lifting up beings from the hells and exhorting them too to awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.30 ||

children.text: vīrye sthitāḥ keci jinasya putrā middhaṃ jahitvā ca aśeṣato 'nye /
children.translated_text: Some sons of the <s>Jina</s>, established in vigor, having completely abandoned sloth,

children.text: caṃkramyayuktāḥ pavane vasanti vīryeṇa te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.31 //
children.translated_text: engaged in walking meditation, dwell in the forest — through vigor they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.31 ||

children.text: ye cātra rakṣanti sadā viśuddhaṃ śīlaṃ akhaṇḍaṃ maṇiratnasādṛśam /
children.translated_text: And those here who always guard pure, unbroken discipline, like a gem-jewel —

children.text: paripūrṇacārī ca bhavanti tatra śīlena te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.32 //
children.translated_text: and are of fully complete conduct therein — through discipline they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.32 ||

children.text: kṣāntībalā keci jinasya putrā adhimānaprāptāna kṣamanti bhikṣuṇām /
children.translated_text: Some sons of the <s>Jina</s>, strong in patience, endure the arrogant <s>bhikṣus</s>,

children.text: ākrośa paribhāṣa tathaiva tarjanāṃ kṣāntyā hi te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.33 //
children.translated_text: abuse, reproach, and likewise threats — through patience they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.33 ||

children.text: kāṃścicca paśyāmyahu bodhisattvān krīḍāratiṃ sarva vivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: And I see some <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having abandoned all play and amusement,

children.text: bālān sahāyān parivarjayitvā āryeṣu saṃsargaratān samāhitān // Saddhp_1.34 //
children.translated_text: having avoided foolish companions, delighting in association with the noble, concentrated. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.34 ||

children.text: vikṣepacittaṃ ca vivarjayantān ekāgracittān vanakandareṣu /
children.translated_text: Abandoning the distracted mind, single-pointed in forest caves,

children.text: dhyāyanta varṣāṇa sahasrakoṭyo dhyānena te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.35 //
children.translated_text: meditating for thousands of millions of years — through meditation they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.35 ||

children.text: dadanti dānāni tathaiva kecit saśiṣyasaṃgheṣu jineṣu saṃmukham /
children.translated_text: Some give gifts likewise, directly to the <s>Jinas</s> together with their disciples and assemblies —

children.text: khādyaṃ ca bhojyaṃ ca tathānnapānnaṃ gilānabhaiṣajya bahū analpakam // Saddhp_1.36 //
children.translated_text: food and drink, and likewise meals and beverages, and abundant medicine for the sick, not little. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.36 ||

body.text: vastrāṇa koṭīśata te dadanti sahasrakoṭīśatamūlya kecit /
body.translated_text: They give hundreds of millions [of sets of] garments, and some [give garments] worth a hundred thousand millions,

body.text: anarghamūlyāṃśca dadanti vastrān saśiṣyasaṃghāna jināna saṃmukham // Saddhp_1.37 //
body.translated_text: and they give priceless garments directly to the <s>Jinas</s> together with their disciples and assemblies. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.37 ||

children.text: vihāra koṭīśata kārayitvā ratnāmayāṃśco tatha candanāmayān /
children.translated_text: Having caused to be built hundreds of millions of monasteries, made of jewels and likewise of sandalwood,

children.text: prabhūtaśayyāsanamaṇḍitāṃśca niryātayanto sugatāna saṃmukham // Saddhp_1.38 //
children.translated_text: adorned with abundant beds and seats, they offer [them] directly to the <s>Sugatas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.38 ||

children.text: ārāma caukṣāṃśca manoramāṃśca phalairupetān kusumaiśca citraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Lovely and delightful parks, endowed with fruits and variegated blossoms,

children.text: divāvihārārtha dadanti kecit saśrāvakāṇāṃ puruṣarṣabhāṇām // Saddhp_1.39 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of day-resting places, some give to the bulls among men together with <s>Śrāvakas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.39 ||

children.text: dadanti dānānimamevarūpā vividhāni citrāṇi ca harṣajātāḥ /
children.translated_text: They give gifts of such a kind, various and variegated, born of joy;

children.text: datvā ca bodhāya janenti vīryaṃ dānena te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.40 //
children.translated_text: and having given, they generate vigor for awakening — through giving they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.40 ||

children.text: dharmaṃ ca kecit pravadanti śāntaṃ dṛṣṭāntahetūnayutairanekaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And some proclaim the peaceful <s>Dharma</s>, with innumerable examples, reasons, and illustrations;

children.text: deśenti te prāṇasahasrakoṭināṃ jñānena te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.41 //
children.translated_text: they teach to thousands of millions of beings — through knowledge they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.41 ||

children.text: nirīhakā dharma prajānamānā dvayaṃ pravṛttāḥ khagatulyasādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Without striving, knowing the <s>Dharma</s>, having gone beyond duality, resembling space,

children.text: anopaliptāḥ sugatasya putrāḥ prajñāya te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.42 //
children.translated_text: unstained, sons of the <s>Sugata</s> — through wisdom they have set out for supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.42 ||

children.text: bhūyaśca paśyāmyahu mañjughoṣa parinirvṛtānāṃ sugatāna śāsane /
children.translated_text: Furthermore I see, O <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, in the teachings of <s>Sugatas</s> who have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: utpanna dhīrā bahubodhisattvāḥ kurvanti satkāru jināna dhātuṣu // Saddhp_1.43 //
children.translated_text: many steadfast <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have arisen, making offerings to the relics of the <s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.43 ||

children.text: stūpāna paśyāmi sahasrakoṭyo analpakā yathariva gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: I see thousands of millions of <s>stūpas</s>, not few, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: yebhiḥ sadā maṇḍita kṣetrakoṭiyo ye kāritā tehi jinātmajehi // Saddhp_1.44 //
children.translated_text: by which millions of fields are always adorned — they were caused to be built by those sons of the <s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.44 ||

children.text: ratnāna saptāna viśiṣṭa ucchritāḥ sahasra pañco paripūrṇa yojanā /
children.translated_text: Distinguished among the seven jewels, rising high, five thousand <s>yojanas</s> in full [height],

children.text: dve co sahasre pariṇāhavantaśchatradhvajāsteṣu sahasrakoṭayaḥ // Saddhp_1.45 //
children.translated_text: and two thousand in circumference — with thousands of millions of parasols and banners upon them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.45 ||

children.text: savaijayantāḥ sada śobhamānā ghaṇṭāsamūhai raṇamāna nityam /
children.translated_text: With victory-columns always shining, constantly resounding with assemblages of bells,

children.text: puṣpaiśca gandhaiśca tathaiva vādyaiḥ saṃpūjitā naramaruyakṣarākṣasaiḥ // Saddhp_1.46 //
children.translated_text: honored with flowers, incense, and likewise music by humans, <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.46 ||

children.text: kārāpayantī sugatasya putrā jināna dhātuṣviha pūjamīdṛśīm /
children.translated_text: The sons of the <s>Sugata</s> cause such worship to be made to the relics of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: yebhirdiśāyo daśa śobhitā yaḥ supuṣpitairvā yatha pārijātaiḥ // Saddhp_1.47 //
children.translated_text: by which the ten directions are adorned — like well-blossoming <s>Pārijāta</s> trees. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.47 ||

children.text: ahaṃ cimāśco bahuprāṇakoṭya iha sthitāḥ paśyiṣu sarvametat /
children.translated_text: I and these many millions of beings, standing here, see all of this;

children.text: prapuṣpitaṃ lokamimaṃ sadevakaṃ jinena muktā iyamekaraśmiḥ // Saddhp_1.48 //
children.translated_text: this world with its <s>devas</s> has been made to blossom — this single ray released by the <s>Jina</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.48 ||

children.text: aho prabhāvaḥ puruṣarṣabhasya aho 'sya jñānaṃ vipulaṃ anāsravam /
children.translated_text: Oh, the power of the Bull among Men! Oh, his vast and undefiled knowledge!

children.text: yasyaikaraśmiḥ prasṛtādya loke darśeti kṣetrāṇa bahū sahasrān // Saddhp_1.49 //
children.translated_text: That by a single ray released today into the world, he shows many thousands of fields! || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.49 ||

children.text: āścaryaprāptāḥ sma nimitta dṛṣṭvā imamīdṛśaṃ cādbhutamaprameyam /
children.translated_text: We have been struck with wonder, having seen this sign — such a marvel, immeasurable!

children.text: vadasva mañjusvara etamarthaṃ kautūhalaṃ hyapanaya buddhaputra // Saddhp_1.50 //
children.translated_text: Tell us, O <s>Mañjusvara</s>, this meaning — remove the curiosity, O son of the <s>Buddha</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.50 ||

children.text: catvārimā parṣa udagracittāstvāṃ cābhivīkṣantiha māṃ ca vīra /
children.translated_text: These four assemblies with uplifted minds look upon you and upon me, O hero;

children.text: janehi harṣaṃ vyapanehi kāṅkṣāṃ tvaṃ vyākarohī sugatasya putra // Saddhp_1.51 //
children.translated_text: generate joy, remove doubt — prophesy, O son of the <s>Sugata</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.51 ||

body.text: kimarthameṣaḥ sugatena adya prabhāsa etādṛśako vimuktaḥ /
body.translated_text: For what purpose has this radiance of such a kind been released today by the <s>Sugata</s>?

body.text: aho prabhāvaḥ puruṣarṣabhasya aho 'sya jñānaṃ vipulaṃ viśuddham // Saddhp_1.52 //
body.translated_text: Oh, the power of the Bull among Men! Oh, his vast and purified knowledge! || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.52 ||

children.text: yasyaikaraśmī prasṛtādya loke darśeti kṣetrāṇa bahūn sahasrān /
children.translated_text: By a single ray released today into the world, he shows many thousands of fields;

children.text: etādṛśo artha ayaṃ bhaviṣyati yenaiṣa raśmī vipulā pramuktā // Saddhp_1.53 //
children.translated_text: Such will be the meaning of this, for which this great ray has been emitted. (Saddhp 1.53)

children.text: ye agradharmā sugatena spṛṣṭāstada bodhimaṇḍe puruṣottamena /
children.translated_text: Those supreme teachings that were realized by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the best of men, at the seat of enlightenment —

children.text: kiṃ teha nirdekṣyati lokanātho atha vyākariṣyatyayu bodhisattvān // Saddhp_1.54 //
children.translated_text: will the Lord of the World expound them here, or will he give predictions (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) to <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? (Saddhp 1.54)

children.text: analpakaṃ kāraṇametta bheṣyati yaddarśitāḥ kṣetrasahasra neke /
children.translated_text: No small cause shall this be, for thousands of realms have been displayed,

children.text: sucitracitrā ratanopaśobhitā buddhāśca dṛśyanti anantacakṣuṣaḥ // Saddhp_1.55 //
children.translated_text: beautifully adorned and decorated with jewels, and <s>Buddhas</s> of infinite vision are seen. (Saddhp 1.55)

children.text: pṛccheti maitreyu jinasya putra spṛhenti te naramaruyakṣarākṣasāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s>, son of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), asks — humans, gods, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s> are eager to know,

children.text: catvārimā parṣa udīkṣamāṇā mañjusvaraḥ kiṃ nviha vyākariṣyati // Saddhp_1.56 //
children.translated_text: these four assemblies are looking on expectantly — what will <s>Mañjusvara</s> (<s>Mañjuśrī</s>) now declare? (Saddhp 1.56)

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ taṃ ca sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇamāmantrayate sma - mahādharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyamidaṃ kulaputrāstathāgatasya kartumabhiprāyaḥ, mahādharmavṛṣṭhayabhipravarṣaṇaṃ ca mahādharmadundubhisaṃpravādanaṃ ca mahādharmadhvajasamucchrayaṇaṃ ca mahādharmolkāsaṃprajvālanaṃ ca mahādharmaśaṅkhābhiprapūraṇaṃ ca mahādharmabherīparāhaṇanaṃ ca mahādharmanirdeśaṃ ca adya kulaputrāstathāgatasya kartumabhiprāyaḥ | yathā mama kulaputrāḥ pratibhāti, yathā ca mayā pūrvakāṇāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmidamevaṃrūpaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ dṛṣṭamabhūt, teṣāmapi pūrvakāṇāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmevaṃ raśmipramocanāvabhāso 'bhut | tenaivaṃ prajānāmi - mahādharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyaṃ tathāgataḥ kartukāmo mahādharmaśravaṇaṃ śrāvayitukāmaḥ, yathedamevaṃrūpaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ prāduṣkṛtavān | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvalokavipratyanīyakadharmaparyāyaṃ śrāvayitukāmastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, yathedamevaṃrūpaṃ mahāprātihāryaṃ raśmipramocanāvabhāsaṃ ca pūrvanimittamupadarśayati ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, addressed <s>Maitreya</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> and that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "O sons of good family, it is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> intention to give a great Dharma-discourse (<s>mahādharmaśravaṇa</s>), to shower a great rain of Dharma, to sound the great drum of Dharma (<s>mahādharmadundubhi</s>), to raise the great banner of Dharma (<s>mahādharmadhvaja</s>), to kindle the great torch of Dharma (<s>mahādharmolkā</s>), to blow the great conch of Dharma (<s>mahādharmaśaṅkha</s>), to beat the great kettledrum of Dharma (<s>mahādharmabherī</s>), and to deliver a great exposition of Dharma. Today, O sons of good family, it is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> intention to do so. As it appears to me, sons of good family, and as I have seen this very same preliminary sign among former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones — those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones also displayed such a radiance of ray-emission. Therefore I understand thus: the <s>Tathāgata</s> wishes to give a great Dharma-discourse, wishes to make heard a great teaching of Dharma, inasmuch as he has manifested this preliminary sign. For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One wishes to proclaim a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) that is contrary to all worldly understanding, and therefore he displays this great miracle of ray-emission and radiance as a preliminary sign."

body.text: anusmarāmyahaṃ kulaputrā atīte 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairvipulairaprameyairacintyairaparimitairapramāṇaistataḥpareṇa parataraṃ yadāsīt - tena kālena tena samayena candrasūryapradīpo nāma
body.translated_text: "I recall, O sons of good family, in the past, in ages gone by, innumerable <s>kalpas</s> ago — innumerable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, unlimited, incalculable, and even beyond that — at that time, in that era, there appeared in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s> (Sun-Moon-Light),

body.text:
tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | sa dharmaṃ deśayati sma ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam |
svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma | yaduta śrāvakāṇāṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprayuktaṃ pratītyasamutpādapravṛttaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsānāṃ samatikramāya nirvāṇaparyavasānam | bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ ca ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya sarvajñajñānaparyavasānaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma ||
body.translated_text: an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. He taught the Dharma, excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent in the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless. He illuminated the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). That is to say, for the <s>Śrāvakas</s> he taught the Dharma connected with the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>), proceeding from dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), leading to the transcendence of birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, culminating in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, he taught the Dharma connected with the six perfections (<s>ṣaṭpāramitā</s>), beginning with supreme perfect enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) and culminating in the knowledge of the Omniscient One (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>)."

body.text: tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ candrasūryapradīpasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pareṇa parataraṃ candrasūryapradīpa eva nāmnā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi | iti hi ajita etena paraṃparodāhāreṇa candrasūryapradīpanāmakānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmekanāmadheyānāmakekulagotrāṇāṃ yadidaṃ bharadvājasagotrāṇāṃ viṃśatitathāgatasahasrāṇyabhūvan | tatra ajita teṣāṃ viṃśatitathāgatasahasrāṇāṃ pūrvakaṃ tathāgatamupādāya yāvat paścimakastathāgataḥ, so 'pi candrasūryapradīpanāmadheya eva tathāgato 'bhūdarhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | so 'pi dharmaṃ deśitavān ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇam | svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśitavān | yaduta śrāvakāṇāṃ caturāryasatyasaṃyuktaṃ pratītyasamutpādapravṛttaṃ dharmaṃ deśitavān jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsānāṃ samatikramāya nirvāṇaparyavasānam | bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ ca ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya sarvajñajñānaparyavasānaṃ dharma deśitavān ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O sons of good family, after that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, there appeared in the world yet another <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One also named <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>. Thus, O <s>Ajita</s>, by this succession, there were twenty thousand <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones all bearing the single name <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, all of one clan and lineage, namely of the <s>Bharadvāja</s> <s>gotra</s>. There, O <s>Ajita</s>, from the first <s>Tathāgata</s> of those twenty thousand <s>Tathāgatas</s> up to the last — that last one too was a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Tamer of Men, Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. He too taught the Dharma, excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent in the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless. He illuminated the holy life. That is to say, for the <s>Śrāvakas</s> he taught the Dharma connected with the Four Noble Truths, proceeding from dependent origination, leading to the transcendence of birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, culminating in <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. And for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, he taught the Dharma connected with the six perfections, beginning with supreme perfect enlightenment and culminating in the knowledge of the Omniscient One."

body.text:
tasya khalu punarajita bhagavataścandrasūryapradīpasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūrvaṃ kumārabhūtasyānabhiniṣkrāntagṛhāvāsasya aṣṭau putrā abhūvan | tadyathā - matiśca nāma rājakumāro 'bhūt | sumatiśca nāma rājakumāro 'bhūt |
anantamatiśca nāma, ratnamatiśca nāma, viśeṣamatiśca nāma, vimatisamuddhāṭī ca nāma, ghoṣamatiśca nāma, dharmamatiśca nāma rājakumāro 'bhūt | teṣāṃ khalu punarajita aṣṭānāṃ rājakumārāṇāṃ tasya bhagavataścandrasūryapradīpasya tathāgatasyaputrāṇāṃ vipularddhirabhūt | ekaikasya catvāro mahādvīpāḥ paribhogo 'bhūt | teṣveva ca rājyaṃ kārayāmāsuḥ | te taṃ bhagavantamabhiniṣkrāntagṛhāvāsaṃ viditvā anuttarāṃ ca samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaṃ śrutvā sarvarājyaparibhogānutsṛjya taṃ bhagavantamanu pravrajitāḥ | sarve ca anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃprasthitā dharmabhāṇakāścābhuvan | sadā ca brahmacāriṇo bahubuddhaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlāśca te rājakumārā abhuvan ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, when he was formerly a prince, before he had gone forth from the household life, had eight sons. Namely: the prince named <s>Mati</s>, the prince named <s>Sumati</s>, the one named <s>Anantamati</s>, the one named <s>Ratnamati</s>, the one named <s>Viśeṣamati</s>, the one named <s>Vimatisamuddhāṭin</s> (Dispeller of Doubt), the one named <s>Ghoṣamati</s>, and the prince named <s>Dharmamati</s>. Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, those eight princes, sons of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, possessed great supernatural powers. Each one had four great continents as his domain, and they ruled over those kingdoms. When they learned that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had gone forth from the household life, and when they heard that he had attained supreme perfect enlightenment, they all renounced their royal enjoyments and went forth following that <s>Bhagavān</s>. They all set out toward supreme perfect enlightenment and became preachers of the Dharma (<s>dharmabhāṇaka</s>). Those princes were always practitioners of the holy life and had planted roots of merit under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>."

body.text: tena khalu punarajita samayena sa bhagavāṃścandrasūryapradīpastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho mahānirdeśaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ bhāṣitvā
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, having spoken the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) called <s>Mahānirdeśa</s> (Great Exposition), a <s>sūtra</s> of great extent (<s>mahāvaipulya</s>), an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by all <s>Buddhas</s>,

body.text: tasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte tasminneva parṣatsaṃnipāte tasminneva mahādharmāsane paryaṅkamābhujya anantanirdeśapratiṣṭhānaṃ nāma samādhiṃ samāpanno 'bhūdaniñjamānena kāyena sthitena aniñjamānena cittena | samanantarasamāpannasya khalu punastasya bhagavato māndāravamahāmāndāravāṇāṃ mañjūṣakamahāmañjūṣakāṇāṃ ca divyānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ mahatpuṣpavarṣamabhiprāvarṣat | taṃ bhagavantaṃ saparṣadamabhyavākirat, sarvāvacca tad buddhakṣetraṃ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitamabhūt calitaṃ saṃpracalitaṃ vedhitaṃ saṃpravedhitaṃ kṣubhitaṃ saṃprakṣubhitam | tena khalu punarajita samayena tena kālena ye tasyāṃ parṣadi bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ saṃnipatitā abhūvan saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ, rājānaśca maṇḍalino balacakravartinaścaturdvīpakacakravartinaśca, te sarve saparivārāstaṃ bhagavantaṃ vyavalokayanti sma āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā audbilyaprāptāḥ | atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tasya bhagavataścandrasūryapradīpasya tathāgatasya bhrūvivarāntarādūrṇākośādekā raśmirniścaritā | sā pūrvasyāṃ diśi aṣṭādaśabuddhakṣetrasahasrāṇi prasṛtā | tāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇi sarvāṇi tasyā raśmeḥ prabhayā suparisphuṭāni saṃdṛśyante sma, tadyathāpi nāma ajita etarhyetāni buddhakṣetrāṇi saṃdṛśyante ||
body.translated_text: at that very instant, at that very moment, in that very assembly, on that very great Dharma-seat, having crossed his legs, he entered the <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Anantanirdeśapratiṣṭhāna</s> (Foundation of Infinite Exposition), his body unmoving, his mind unmoving. Immediately upon the <s>Bhagavān's</s> entering that <s>samādhi</s>, a great shower of divine flowers rained down — <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s>, <s>Mañjūṣaka</s> and great <s>Mañjūṣaka</s> flowers — and it scattered over the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with his assembly, and the entire <s>Buddha</s>-field trembled in six ways: it moved and moved greatly, shook and shook greatly, quaked and quaked greatly. Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, at that time, those who had assembled and were seated in that assembly — <s>Bhikṣus</s>, <s>Bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>Upāsakas</s>, <s>Upāsikās</s>, gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, as well as kings, feudal lords, rulers of armies, and universal monarchs of four continents (<s>Cakravartins</s>) — all of them with their retinues gazed at the <s>Bhagavān</s>, filled with wonder, amazement, and delight. Then at that moment, from the tuft of hair between the eyebrows (<s>ūrṇākośa</s>) of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, a single ray of light issued forth. It extended to eighteen thousand <s>Buddha</s>-fields in the eastern direction, and all those <s>Buddha</s>-fields were clearly illuminated by the radiance of that ray, just as, O <s>Ajita</s>, these <s>Buddha</s>-fields are seen now."

body.text: tena khalu punarajita samayena tasya bhagavato viṃśatibodhisattvakoṭyaḥ samanubaddhā abhuvan | ye tasyāṃ parṣadi dharmaśravaṇikāḥ, te āścaryaprāptā abhūvan adbhutaprāptā audbilyaprāptāḥ kautūhalasamutpannā etena mahāraśmyavabhāsenāvabhāsitaṃ lokaṃ dṛṣṭvā ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, at that time, twenty <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were following that <s>Bhagavān</s>, and those in the assembly who had come to hear the Dharma were filled with wonder, amazement, and delight, having seen the world illuminated by this great radiance of rays."

body.text: tena khalu punarajita samayena tasya bhagavataḥ śāsane varaprabho nāma bodhisattvo 'bhūt | tasyāṣṭau śatānyantevāsināmabhūvan | sa ca bhagavāṃstataḥ samādhervyutthāya taṃ varaprabhaṃ bodhisattvamārabhya saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa | yāvat paripūrṇān ṣaṣṭyantarakalpān bhāṣitavān ekāsane niṣaṇṇo 'saṃpravedhamānena kāyena aniñjamānena cittena | sā ca sarvāvatī parṣadekāsane niṣaṇṇā tān ṣaṣṭyantarakalpāṃstasya bhagavato 'ntikāddharmaṃ śṛṇoti sma | na ca tasyāṃ parṣadi ekasattvasyāpi kāyaklamatho 'bhūt, na ca cittaklamathaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, at that time, in the teaching of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, there was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Varaprabha</s> (Excellent Light). He had eight hundred disciples. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, arising from that <s>samādhi</s>, beginning with that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Varaprabha</s>, proclaimed the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> called <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma). For a full sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> he spoke, seated on a single seat, with body unwavering and mind unmoving. And that entire assembly, seated on their single seats, listened to the Dharma from that <s>Bhagavān</s> for those sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And not a single being in that assembly experienced bodily fatigue or mental fatigue."

body.text: atha sa bhagavāṃścandrasūryapradīpastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ṣaṣṭayantarakalpānāmatyayāt taṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ nirdiśya tasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte parinirvāṇamārocitavān sadevakasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ purastāt - adya bhikṣavo 'syāmeva rātryāṃ madhyame yāme tathāgato 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyatīti ||
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, after the passage of sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, having expounded that <s>dharmaparyāya</s> called <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, a <s>sūtra</s> of great extent, an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by all <s>Buddhas</s>, at that very instant and moment announced his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> before the world with its gods, <s>Māras</s>, and <s>Brahmās</s>, before the assembly of ascetics and brahmins, before gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>: "Today, O <s>Bhikṣus</s>, in the middle watch of this very night, the <s>Tathāgata</s> will enter final <s>Nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>Nirvāṇa</s>-realm without remainder (<s>anupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>)."

body.text: atha khalvajita sa bhagavāṃścandrasūryapradīpastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ śrīgarbhaṃ nāma bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtya tāṃ sarvāvatīṃ parṣadamāmantrayate sma - ayaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śrīgarbho bodhisattvo mamānantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate | vimalanetro nāma tathogato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Ajita</s>, that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One, gave the prediction (<s>vyākaraṇa</s>) of supreme perfect enlightenment to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Śrīgarbha</s> (Glorious Womb), and addressed that entire assembly: "O <s>Bhikṣus</s>, this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīgarbha</s>, immediately after me, will attain supreme perfect enlightenment. He will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Vimalanettra</s> (Stainless Eye)."

body.text: atha khalvajita sa bhagavāṃścandrasūryapradīpastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastasyāmeva rātryāṃ madhyame yāme 'nupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ | taṃ ca saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sa varaprabho bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhāritavān | aśītiṃ cāntarakalpāṃstasya bhagavataḥ parinirvṛtasya śāsanaṃ sa varaprabho bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhāritavān saṃprakāśitavān | tatra ajita ye tasya bhagavato 'ṣṭau putrā abhūvan, matipramukhāḥ, te tasyaiva varaprabhasya bodhisattvasyāntevāsino 'bhūvan | te tenaiva paripācitā abhūvannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | taiśca tataḥ paścādbahūni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi dṛṣṭāni satkṛtāni ca | sarve ca te 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ | paścimakaśca teṣāṃ dīpaṃkaro 'bhūttathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Ajita</s>, that Blessed One <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, on that very night, in the middle watch, passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the remainderless <s>nirvāṇa</s>-realm. And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Varaprabha</s> retained that <s>dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>. For eighty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Varaprabha</s> retained and proclaimed the teaching of that Blessed One after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Now, O <s>Ajita</s>, those eight sons of that Blessed One, led by <s>Mati</s>, became pupils of that very <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Varaprabha</s>. They were brought to maturity by him in unsurpassed perfect awakening. And they subsequently saw, honored, and served many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. And all of them realized unsurpassed perfect awakening. The last of them was the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.

body.text: teṣāṃ ca aṣṭānāmantevāsiśatānāmeko bodhisattvo 'dhimātraṃ lābhaguruko 'bhūt satkāraguruko jñātaguruko yaśaskāmaḥ | tasyoddiṣṭoddiṣṭāni padavyañjanānyantardhīyante na saṃtiṣṭhante sma | tasya yaśaskāma ityeva saṃjñābhūt | tenāpi tena kuśalamūlena bahūni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyārāgitānyabhūvan | ārāgayitvā ca satkṛtāni gurukṛtāni mānitāni pūjitānyarcitānyapacāyitāni | syātkhalu punaste ajita kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena varaprabho nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhūddharmabhāṇakaḥ | na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena varaprabho nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhūddharmabhāṇakaḥ | yaścāsau yaśaskāmo nāma bodhisattvo 'bhūt kausīdyaprāptaḥ, tvameva ajita sa tena kālena tena samayena yaśaskāmo nāma bodhisattvo 'bhūt kausīdyaprāptaḥ | iti hi ajita ahamanena paryāyeṇedaṃ bhagavataḥ pūrvanimittaṃ dṛṣṭvā evaṃrūpāṃ raśmimutsṛṣṭāmevaṃ parimīmāṃse, yathā bhagavānapi taṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ bhāṣitukāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Among those eight hundred pupils, there was one <s>Bodhisattva</s> who was excessively devoted to gain, devoted to honor, devoted to being known, desirous of fame. When teachings were recited to him, the words and syllables would vanish and not remain. His name was <s>Yaśaskāma</s> ("Desirous of Fame"). Yet even he, through those roots of merit, gratified many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. Having gratified them, he honored, respected, revered, venerated, worshipped, and esteemed them. Now then, O <s>Ajita</s>, you might have a doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation — that it was someone else who was at that time, on that occasion, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Varaprabha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. But you should not view it thus. Why? Because I myself was at that time, on that occasion, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Varaprabha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. And the one who was that <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Yaśaskāma</s>, who had fallen into indolence — you yourself, O <s>Ajita</s>, were at that time, on that occasion, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Yaśaskāma</s>, who had fallen into indolence. Thus, O <s>Ajita</s>, by this reasoning, having seen this prior sign of the Blessed One — a ray of this very form having been emitted — I consider thus: the Blessed One too wishes to teach that <s>dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the great <s>vaipulya sūtrānta</s>, the instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by all <s>Buddhas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta etamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā pradarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, in order to demonstrate this very meaning more extensively, spoke these verses on that occasion:

children.text: atītamadhvānamanusmarāmi acintiye aparimitasmi kalpe /
children.translated_text: I recall the past, in inconceivable, immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: yadā jino āsi prajāna uttamaścandrasya sūryasya pradīpa nāma // Saddhp_1.57 //
children.translated_text: when there was a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), supreme among beings, named Lamp of the Moon and Sun. [Saddhp 1.57]

children.text: saddharma deśeti prajāna nāyako vineti sattvāna anantakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The leader of beings teaches the true <s>Dharma</s>; he disciplines infinite <s>koṭis</s> of beings,

children.text: samādapetī bahubodhisattvānacintiyānuttami buddhajñāne // Saddhp_1.58 //
children.translated_text: and brings many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to maturity in the inconceivable, unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. [Saddhp 1.58]

children.text: ye cāṣṭa putrāstada tasya āsan kumārabhūtasya vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: And there were eight sons of that Guide, princes;

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ pravrajitaṃ mahāmuniṃ jahitva kāmāṃllaghu sarvi prāvrajan // Saddhp_1.59 //
children.translated_text: having seen that great <s>Muni</s> go forth, they renounced desires and all quickly went forth [themselves]. [Saddhp 1.59]

children.text: dharmaṃ ca so bhāṣati lokanātho anantanirdeśavaraṃ ti sūtram /
children.translated_text: And that Lord of the World teaches the <s>Dharma</s> — the supreme sūtra of infinite exposition;

children.text: nāmeva vaipulyamidaṃ pravucyati prakāśayī prāṇisahasrakoṭinām // Saddhp_1.60 //
children.translated_text: this very <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive teaching) is called by name — he proclaimed it to <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of living beings. [Saddhp 1.60]

children.text: samanantaraṃ bhāṣiya so vināyakaḥ paryaṅka bandhitva kṣaṇasmi tasmin /
children.translated_text: Immediately after teaching, that Guide, sitting cross-legged at that very moment,

children.text: anantanirdeśavaraṃ samādhiṃ dharmāsanastho muniśreṣṭha dhyāyī // Saddhp_1.61 //
children.translated_text: seated on the <s>Dharma</s>-throne, the foremost of <s>Munis</s>, meditating — entered the supreme <s>samādhi</s> of infinite exposition. [Saddhp 1.61]

children.text: divyaṃ ca māndāravavarṣamāsīdaghaṭṭitā dundubhayaśca neduḥ /
children.translated_text: And there was a divine shower of <s>Māndārava</s> [flowers], and drums sounded untouched;

children.text: devāśca yakṣāśca sthitāntarīkṣe kurvanti pūjāṃ dvipadottamasya // Saddhp_1.62 //
children.translated_text: <s>devas</s> and <s>yakṣas</s>, stationed in the sky, made offerings to the supreme among bipeds. [Saddhp 1.62]

children.text: sarvaṃ ca kṣetraṃ pracacāla tatkṣaṇam āścaryamatyadbhutamāsi tatra /
children.translated_text: And the entire field trembled at that moment — a wonder, most marvelous, occurred there;

children.text: raśmiṃ ca ekāṃ pramumoca nāyako bhruvāntarāttāmatidarśanīyām // Saddhp_1.63 //
children.translated_text: the Guide sent forth a single ray from between his eyebrows, supremely beautiful. [Saddhp 1.63]

children.text: pūrvāṃ ca gatvā diśa sā hi raśmiraṣṭādaśakṣetrasahasra pūrṇā /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the eastern direction, that ray filled eighteen thousand fields,

children.text: prabhāsayaṃ bhrājati sarvalokaṃ darśeti sattvāna cyutopapādam // Saddhp_1.64 //
children.translated_text: illuminating and making radiant all the worlds, showing beings their death and rebirth. [Saddhp 1.64]

children.text: ratnāmayā kṣetra tathātra kecidvaiḍūryanirbhāsa tathaiva kecit /
children.translated_text: And some fields appeared to be made of jewels, and some likewise shining with <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli),

children.text: dṛśyanti citrā atidarśanīyā raśmiprabhāsena vināyakasya // Saddhp_1.65 //
children.translated_text: seen as variegated and supremely beautiful through the radiance of the Guide's ray. [Saddhp 1.65]

body.text: devā manuṣyāstatha nāga yakṣā gandharva tatrāpsarakinnarāśca /
body.translated_text: <s>Devas</s>, humans, and also <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsaras</s>, and <s>Kinnaras</s> there,

body.text: ye cābhiyuktāḥ sugatasya pūjayā dṛśyanti pūjenti ca lokadhātuṣu // Saddhp_1.66 //
body.translated_text: and those devoted to the worship of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) — they are seen worshipping in those world-realms. [Saddhp 1.66]

children.text: buddhāśca dṛśyanti svayaṃ svayaṃbhuvaḥ suvarṇayūpā iva darśanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: And <s>Buddhas</s> are seen, Self-born Ones, beautiful like golden sacrificial posts,

children.text: vaiḍūryamadhye ca suvarṇabimbaṃ parṣāya madhye pravadanti dharmam // Saddhp_1.67 //
children.translated_text: like a golden image in the midst of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> — they teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the midst of their assemblies. [Saddhp 1.67]

children.text: tahi śrāvakāṇāṃ gaṇanā na vidyate te cāpramāṇāḥ sugatasya śrāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: In each field, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Sugatas</s> are innumerable, beyond counting;

children.text: ekaikakṣetrasmi vināyakānāṃ raśmiprabhā darśayate hi sarvān // Saddhp_1.68 //
children.translated_text: the radiance of the ray reveals them all in each field of the Guides. [Saddhp 1.68]

children.text: vīryairupetāśca akhaṇḍaśīlā acchidraśīlā maṇiratnasādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Endowed with vigor, of unbroken morality, of flawless morality, like precious jewels —

children.text: dṛśyanti putrā naranāyakānāṃ viharanti ye parvatakandareṣu // Saddhp_1.69 //
children.translated_text: the sons of the Leaders of Men are seen, those who dwell in mountain caves. [Saddhp 1.69]

children.text: sarvasvadānāni parityajantaḥ kṣāntībalā dhyānaratāśca dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Renouncing all their possessions, endowed with the power of patience, delighting in meditation, steadfast —

children.text: bahubodhisattvā yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ sarve 'pi dṛśyanti tayā hi raśmyā // Saddhp_1.70 //
children.translated_text: many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, are all seen by that ray. [Saddhp 1.70]

children.text: aniñjamānāśca avedhamānāḥ kṣāntau sthitā dhyānaratāḥ samāhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Unmoved and unshaken, established in patience, delighting in meditation, concentrated —

children.text: dṛśyanti putrāḥ sugatasya aurasā dhyānena te prasthita agrabodhim // Saddhp_1.71 //
children.translated_text: the true sons of the <s>Sugata</s> are seen — through meditation, they have set forth toward supreme awakening. [Saddhp 1.71]

children.text: bhūtaṃ padaṃ śāntamanāsravaṃ ca prajānamānāśca prakāśayanti /
children.translated_text: Knowing the true station that is peaceful and without outflows, they proclaim it;

children.text: deśenti dharmaṃ bahulokadhātuṣu sugatānubhāvādiyamīdṛśī kriyā // Saddhp_1.72 //
children.translated_text: they teach the <s>Dharma</s> in many world-realms — such activity comes through the power of the <s>Sugata</s>. [Saddhp 1.72]

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tā parṣa catasra tāyinaścandrārkadīpasya imaṃ prabhāvam /
children.translated_text: Having seen this power of <s>Candrasūryapradīpa</s>, the four assemblies and the Protector,

children.text: harṣasthitāḥ sarvi bhavitva tatkṣaṇamanyonya pṛcchanti kathaṃ nu etat // Saddhp_1.73 //
children.translated_text: all filled with joy at that moment, asked one another, "How is this?" [Saddhp 1.73]

children.text: acirācca so naramaruyakṣapūjitaḥ samādhito vyutthita lokanāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: And before long, that Lord of the World, worshipped by men, <s>Maras</s>, and <s>Yakṣas</s>,

children.text: varaprabhaṃ putra tadādhyabhāṣata yo bodhisattvo vidu dharmabhāṇakaḥ // Saddhp_1.74 //
children.translated_text: arose from <s>samādhi</s> and then addressed his son <s>Varaprabha</s>, the wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> and <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. [Saddhp 1.74]

children.text: lokasya cakṣuśca gatiśca tvaṃ vidurvaiśvāsiko dharmadharaśca mahyam /
children.translated_text: "You are the eye and the refuge of the world, O wise one; you are the trustworthy bearer of the <s>Dharma</s> for me.

children.text: tvaṃ hyatra sākṣī mama dharmakośe yathāhu bhāṣiṣyi hitāya prāṇinām // Saddhp_1.75 //
children.translated_text: You are indeed the witness to my <s>Dharma</s>-treasury — as I shall teach for the benefit of beings. [Saddhp 1.75]

children.text: saṃsthāpayitvā bahubodhisattvān harṣitva saṃvarṇiya saṃstavitvā /
children.translated_text: Having established many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having delighted, praised, and lauded them,

children.text: prabhāṣate tajjina agradharmān paripūrṇa so antarakalpa ṣaṣṭim // Saddhp_1.76 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Jina</s> teaches the supreme <s>Dharma</s> for a full sixty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. [Saddhp 1.76]

children.text: yaṃ caiva so bhāṣati lokanātho ekāsanasthaḥ pravarāgradharmam /
children.translated_text: And whatever supreme <s>Dharma</s> that Lord of the World teaches while seated on a single seat,

children.text: taṃ sarvamādhārayi so jinātmajo varaprabho yo abhu dharmabhāṇakaḥ // Saddhp_1.77 //
children.translated_text: all of it was retained by that son of the <s>Jina</s>, <s>Varaprabha</s>, who was the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. [Saddhp 1.77]

children.text: so co jino bhāṣiya agradharmaṃ praharṣayitvā janatāmanekām /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Jina</s>, having taught the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, having delighted many people,

children.text: tasmiṃśca divase vadate sa nāyakaḥ purato hi lokasya sadevakasya // Saddhp_1.78 //
children.translated_text: on that day, the Guide speaks before the world together with the <s>devas</s>: [Saddhp 1.78]

children.text: prakāśitā me iya dharmanetrī ācakṣito dharmasvabhāva yādṛaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: "My <s>Dharma</s>-eye has been proclaimed; the nature of <s>Dharma</s> has been declared as it truly is.

children.text: nirvāṇakālo mama adya bhikṣavo rātrīya yāmasmiha madhyamasmin // Saddhp_1.79 //
children.translated_text: The time of my <s>nirvāṇa</s> is today, O monks, in the middle watch of the night. [Saddhp 1.79]

children.text: bhavathāpramattā adhimuktisārā abhiyujyathā mahya imasmi śāsane /
children.translated_text: Be heedful, with the essence of determination; exert yourselves in this, my teaching.

children.text: sudurlabhā bhonti jinā maharṣayaḥ kalpāna koṭīnayutāna atyayāt // Saddhp_1.80 //
children.translated_text: For <s>Jinas</s>, the great sages, appear rarely — after the passage of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>." [Saddhp 1.80]

body.text: saṃtāpajātā bahubuddhaputrā duḥkhena cogreṇa samarpitābhavan /
body.translated_text: The many sons of the <s>Buddha</s>, stricken with grief, were overcome with terrible suffering,

body.text: śrutvāna ghoṣaṃ dvipadottamasya nirvāṇaśabdaṃ atikṣiprametat // Saddhp_1.81 //
body.translated_text: having heard the voice of the Supreme among Bipeds, the word "<s>nirvāṇa</s>," so swiftly. [Saddhp 1.81]

children.text: āśvāsayitvā ca narendrarājā tāḥ prāṇakoṭyo bahavo acintiyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Having comforted those inconceivably many <s>koṭis</s> of beings, the King among Lords of Men [said]:

children.text: mā bhāyathā bhikṣava nirvṛte mayi bhaviṣyatha buddha mamottareṇa // Saddhp_1.82 //
children.translated_text: "Do not fear, O monks, at my passing away; there will be a <s>Buddha</s> after me. [Saddhp 1.82]

children.text: śrīgarbha eṣo vidu bodhisattvo gatiṃ gato jñāni anāsravasmin /
children.translated_text: This wise <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śrīgarbha</s>, having gone to the stage of the knower, [established] in the outflow-free,

children.text: spṛśiṣyate uttamamagrabodhiṃ vimalāgranetro ti jino bhaviṣyati // Saddhp_1.83 //
children.translated_text: shall touch the supreme, unsurpassed awakening — he shall be a <s>Jina</s> named <s>Vimalāgranetra</s>." [Saddhp 1.83]

children.text: tāmeva rātriṃ tada yāmi madhyame parinirvṛto hetukṣaye va dīpaḥ /
children.translated_text: On that very night, in the middle watch, he passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, like a lamp whose fuel is exhausted.

children.text: śarīra vaistāriku tasya cābhūt stūpāna koṭīnayutā anantakā // Saddhp_1.84 //
children.translated_text: And his relics were distributed; <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>stūpas</s>, infinite [in number, were erected]. [Saddhp 1.84]

children.text: bhikṣuśca tatrā tatha bhikṣuṇīyo ye prasthitā uttamamagrabodhim /
