children.translated_text: And the monks there, and likewise the nuns, who had set forth toward supreme awakening,

children.text: analpakāste yatha gaṅgabālikā abhiyukta tasyo sugatasya śāsane // Saddhp_1.85 //
children.translated_text: they were not few, numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, devoted to the teaching of that <s>Sugata</s>. [Saddhp 1.85]

children.text: yaścāpi bhikṣustada dharmabhāṇako varaprabho yena sa dharma dhāritaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that monk who was the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, <s>Varaprabha</s>, by whom that <s>Dharma</s> was retained —

children.text: aśīti so antarakalpa pūrṇāṃ tahi śāsane bhāṣati agradharmān // Saddhp_1.86 //
children.translated_text: for eighty full intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, he taught the supreme <s>Dharma</s> in that teaching. [Saddhp 1.86]

children.text: aṣṭāśataṃ tasya abhūṣi śiṣyāḥ paripācitā ye tada tena sarve /
children.translated_text: He had eight hundred disciples, all of whom were brought to maturity by him;

children.text: dṛṣṭā ca tebhirbahubuddhakoṭyaḥ satkāru teṣāṃ ca kṛto maharṣiṇām // Saddhp_1.87 //
children.translated_text: and they saw many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> and rendered honor to those great sages. [Saddhp 1.87]

body.text: caryāṃ caritvā tada ānulomikīṃ buddhā abhūvan bahulokadhātuṣu

children.text: parasparaṃ te ca anantareṇa anyonya vyākarṣu tadāgrabodhaye // Saddhp_1.88 //
children.translated_text: and in immediate succession, they predicted one another for supreme awakening. [Saddhp 1.88]

body.translated_text: Having practiced the proper conduct, they became <s>Buddhas</s> in many world-realms;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca buddhāna paraṃpareṇa dīpaṃkaraḥ paścimako abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: And of those <s>Buddhas</s>, in succession, <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> was the last;

children.text: devātidevo ṛṣisaṃghapūjito vinītavān prāṇisahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_1.89 //
children.translated_text: the god above gods, worshipped by hosts of sages, he disciplined <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of living beings. [Saddhp 1.89]

children.text: yaścāsi tasyo sugatātmajasya varaprabhasyo tada dharma bhāṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: And the one who was a disciple of that son of the <s>Sugata</s>, <s>Varaprabha</s>, when he was teaching the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: śiṣyaḥ kusīdaśca sa lolupātmā lābhaṃ ca jñānaṃ ca gaveṣamāṇaḥ // Saddhp_1.90 //
children.translated_text: a lazy one, of covetous nature, seeking gain and renown, [Saddhp 1.90]

children.text: yaśorthikaścāpyatimātra āsīt kulākulaṃ ca pratipannamāsīt /
children.translated_text: and who was excessively desirous of fame, and had gone from family to non-family —

children.text: uddeśa svādhyāyu tathāsya sarvo na tiṣṭhate bhāṣitu tasmi kāle // Saddhp_1.91 //
children.translated_text: his recitations and study would all not remain when spoken at that time. [Saddhp 1.91]

children.text: nāmaṃ ca tasyo imamevamāsīd yaśakāmanāmnā diśatāsu viśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: And his name was this very one — renowned in all directions by the name <s>Yaśaskāma</s>;

children.text: sa cāpi tenākuśalena karmaṇā kalmāṣabhūtenabhisaṃskṛtena // Saddhp_1.92 //
children.translated_text: and he too, through that unskillful <s>karma</s>, mixed and conditioned, [Saddhp 1.92]

children.text: ārāgayī buddhasahasrakoṭyaḥ pūjāṃ ca teṣāṃ vipulāmakārṣīt /
children.translated_text: gratified <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> and made vast offerings to them;

children.text: cīrṇā ca caryā vara ānulomikī dṛṣṭaśca buddho ayu śākyasiṃhaḥ // Saddhp_1.93 //
children.translated_text: he practiced the supreme, proper conduct and saw the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>). [Saddhp 1.93]

children.text: ayaṃ ca so paścimako bhaviṣyati anuttarāṃ lapsyati cāgrabodhim /
children.translated_text: And this one shall be the last [<s>Buddha</s>]; he shall attain unsurpassed, supreme awakening;

children.text: maitreyagotro bhagavān bhaviṣyati vineṣyati prāṇasahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_1.94 //
children.translated_text: he shall be a Blessed One of the <s>Maitreya</s> lineage and shall discipline <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of living beings. [Saddhp 1.94]

children.text: kausīdyaprāptastada yo babhūva parinirvṛtasya sugatasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: The one who had fallen into indolence in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: tvameva so tādṛśako babhūva ahaṃ ca āsīttada dharmabhāṇakaḥ // Saddhp_1.95 //
children.translated_text: you yourself were that one; and I was the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher at that time. [Saddhp 1.95]

children.text: imena haṃ kāraṇahetunādya dṛṣṭvā nimittaṃ idamevarūpam /
children.translated_text: For this reason and by this cause, today, having seen this sign of such a form,

children.text: jñānasya tasya prathitaṃ nimittaṃ prathamaṃ mayā tatra vadāmi dṛṣṭam // Saddhp_1.96 //
children.translated_text: this sign of that knowledge — [such a sign was] first seen by me there, I declare. [Saddhp 1.96]

children.text: dhruvaṃ jinendro 'pi samantacakṣuḥ śākyādhirājaḥ paramārthadarśī /
children.translated_text: Surely, the Lord of Conquerors, the all-seeing eye, the supreme ruler of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the seer of ultimate truth,

children.text: tameva yaṃ icchati bhāṣaṇāya paryāyamagraṃ tadadyo mayā śrutaḥ // Saddhp_1.97 //
children.translated_text: wishes to teach that very supreme <s>dharma</s>-discourse — it was heard by me today. [Saddhp 1.97]

children.text: tadeva paripūrṇa nimittamadya upāyakauśalya vināyakānām /
children.translated_text: That very sign is now fulfilled — the skillful means of the Guides;

children.text: saṃsthāpanaṃ kurvati śākyasiṃho bhāṣiṣyate dharmasvabhāvamudrām // Saddhp_1.98 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>) makes the establishment — he shall teach the seal of the nature of <s>Dharma</s>. [Saddhp 1.98]

children.text: prayatā sucittā bhavathā kṛtāñjalī bhāṣiṣyate lokahitānukampī /
children.translated_text: Be attentive, with pure minds and joined palms — the one compassionate for the world's welfare shall speak;

children.text: varṣiṣyate dharmamanantavarṣaṃ tarpiṣyate ye sthita bodhihetoḥ // Saddhp_1.99 //
children.translated_text: he shall rain down a <s>Dharma</s>-rain of infinite extent, and shall satisfy those who stand for the sake of awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.99 ||

children.text: yeṣāṃ ca saṃdehagatīha kācid ye saṃśayā yā vicikitsa kācit /
children.translated_text: And whatever doubts there are here, whatever uncertainty, whatever hesitation —

children.text: vyapaneṣyate tā vidurātmajānāṃ ye bodhisattvā iha bodhiprasthitāḥ // Saddhp_1.100 //
children.translated_text: those will be dispelled for the wise ones' sons who are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> set forth toward awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 1.100 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dhamaparyāye nidānaparivarto nāma prathamaḥ ||1||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the first chapter, called the <s>Nidāna</s> (Introduction) chapter, in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_2: upāyakauśalyaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 2: The chapter on skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalyaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān smṛtimān saṃprajānaṃstataḥ samādhervyutthitaḥ | vyutthāya āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramāmantrayate sma - gambhīraṃ śāriputra durdṛśaṃ duranubodhaṃ buddhajñānaṃ tathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ pratibuddham, durvijñeyaṃ sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhaiḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraparyupāsitāvino hi śāriputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasracīrṇacaritāvino 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau dūrānugatāḥ kṛtavīryā āścaryādbhutadharmasamanvāgatā durvijñeyadharmasamanvāgatā durvijñeyadharmānujñātāvinaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, mindful and fully aware, arose from that <s>samādhi</s>. Having arisen, he addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Profound, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, hard to see, hard to comprehend is the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge realized by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — hard to understand by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, have attended upon many hundred-thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>; they have traversed the course under many hundred-thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>; they have gone far in unsurpassed perfect awakening; they are of accomplished vigor, endowed with wondrous and marvelous <s>dharmas</s>, endowed with hard-to-understand <s>dharmas</s>, knowers of hard-to-understand <s>dharmas</s>.'

body.text: durvijñeyaṃ śāriputra saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām | tatkasya hetoḥ? svapratyayān dharmān prakāśayanti vividhopāyakauśalyajñānadarśanahetukāraṇanirdeśanārambaṇaniruktiprajñaptibhistairupāyakauśalyaistasmiṃstasmiṃllagnān sattvān pramocayitum | mahopāyakauśalyajñānadarśanaparamapāramitāprāptāḥ śāriputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | asaṅgāpratihatajñānadarśanabalavaiśāradyāveṇikendriyabalabodhyaṅgadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattyadbhutadharmasamanvāgatā vividhadharmasaṃprakāśakāḥ | mahāścaryādbhutaprāptāḥ śāriputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | alaṃ śāriputra etāvadeva bhāṣituṃ bhavatu - paramāścaryaprāptāḥ śāriputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | tathāgata eva śāriputra tathāgatasya dharmān deśayet, yān dharmāṃstathāgato jānāti | sarvadharmānapi śāriputra tathāgata eva deśayati | sarvadharmānapi tathāgata eva jānāti, ye ca te dharmāḥ, yathā ca te dharmāḥ, yādṛśāśca te dharmāḥ, yallakṣaṇāśca te dharmāḥ, yatsvabhāvāśca te dharmāḥ, ye ca yathā ca yādṛśāśca yallakṣaṇāśca yatsvabhāvāśca te dharmā iti | teṣu dharmeṣu tathāgata eva pratyakṣo 'parokṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Hard to understand, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the teaching with intended purport (<s>saṃdhābhāṣya</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. For what reason? They illuminate their <s>dharmas</s> [realized] through their own specific conditions, through various expositions by means of skill in means — knowledge, vision, grounds, causes, and indications — with eloquence and designations. Through those skillful means, they liberate beings attached here and there. The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, have attained the supreme perfection of the great skill in means of knowledge and vision. They are endowed with unobstructed, unhindered knowledge-and-vision, powers, confidences, unique faculties, strengths, limbs of awakening, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, <s>samādhis</s>, and attainments — and wondrous <s>dharmas</s>; they are illuminators of various <s>dharmas</s>. Endowed with great wondrous attainments, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, are the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. Enough, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, let this much be said: The <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, have attained the supreme wonder. Only a <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, can teach the <s>dharmas</s> of a <s>Tathāgata</s> — whatever <s>dharmas</s> the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows. The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone teaches all <s>dharmas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone knows all <s>dharmas</s> — and what those <s>dharmas</s> are, and how those <s>dharmas</s> are, and of what kind those <s>dharmas</s> are, and what characteristics those <s>dharmas</s> have, and what inherent nature those <s>dharmas</s> have — what they are, how they are, of what kind, what characteristics, and what inherent nature those <s>dharmas</s> have. Regarding those <s>dharmas</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone is directly perceptive, not indirectly.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānetamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, to further demonstrate this very meaning in greater measure, at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: aprameyā mahāvīrā loke samarumānuṣe /
children.translated_text: Immeasurable are the Great Heroes in the world with its <s>Maras</s> and humans;

children.text: na śakyaṃ sarvaśo jñātuṃ sarvasattvairvināyakāḥ // Saddhp_2.1 //
children.translated_text: all beings cannot fully know the Guides in every way. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.1 ||

children.text: balā vimokṣā ye teṣāṃ vaiśāradyāśca yādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Their powers, liberations, and what their confidences are like,

children.text: yādṛśā buddhadharmāśca na śakyaṃ jñātu kenacit // Saddhp_2.2 //
children.translated_text: and what the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s> are like — none can know. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.2 ||

children.text: pūrve niṣevitā caryā buddhakoṭīna antike /
children.translated_text: The conduct previously practiced in the presence of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> —

children.text: gambhīrā caiva sūkṣmā ca durvijñeyā sudurdṛśā // Saddhp_2.3 //
children.translated_text: both profound and subtle, hard to understand, and very hard to see. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.3 ||

children.text: tasyāṃ cīrṇāya caryāyāṃ kalpakoṭyo acintiyā /
children.translated_text: Having traversed that conduct for inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: phalaṃ me bodhimaṇḍasmin dṛṣṭaṃ yādṛśakaṃ hi tat // Saddhp_2.4 //
children.translated_text: the fruit was seen by me at this <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> — such as it was. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.4 ||

children.text: ahaṃ ca tatprajānāmi ye cānye lokanāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: I myself know that, and so do the other world-guides —

children.text: yathā yad yādṛśaṃ cāpi lakṣaṇaṃ cāsya yādṛśam // Saddhp_2.5 //
children.translated_text: how it is, what it is, of what kind, and what its characteristic is. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.5 ||

children.text: na taddarśayituṃ śakyaṃ vyāhāro 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: That cannot be shown; there is no utterance for it;

children.text: nāpyasau tādṛśaḥ kaścit sattvo lokasmi vidyate // Saddhp_2.6 //
children.translated_text: nor is there any being in the world of such [capacity] || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.6 ||

children.text: yasya taṃ deśayeddharma deśitaṃ cāpi jāniyāt /
children.translated_text: to whom one could teach that <s>Dharma</s> and who could understand what is taught —

children.text: anyatra bodhisattvebhyo adhimuktīya ye sthitāḥ // Saddhp_2.7 //
children.translated_text: except for <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who stand firm in aspiration. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.7 ||

children.text: ye cāpi te lokavidusya śrāvakāḥ kṛtādhikārāḥ sugatānuvarṇitāḥ /
children.translated_text: And those <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the Knower of the World who have performed [great] deeds, praised by the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: kṣīṇāsravā antimadehadhāriṇo na teṣa viṣayo 'sti jināna jñāne // Saddhp_2.8 //
children.translated_text: with outflows destroyed, bearers of the final body — even their domain does not extend to the knowledge of the <s>Jinas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.8 ||

children.text: sa caiva sarvā iya lokadhātu pūrṇā bhavecchārisutopamānām /
children.translated_text: Even if this entire world-realm were filled with those comparable to the son of <s>Śāri</s> (<s>Śāriputra</s>),

children.text: ekībhavitvāna vicintayeyuḥ sugatasya jñānaṃ na hi śakya jānitum // Saddhp_2.9 //
children.translated_text: and having become one, they were to reflect — the knowledge of the <s>Sugata</s> cannot be known. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.9 ||

children.text: saceha tvaṃ sādṛśakehi paṇḍitaiḥ pūrṇā bhaveyurdaśā pi ddiśāyo /
children.translated_text: If here the ten directions were filled with such wise ones as you,

children.text: ye cāpi mahyaṃ imi śrāvakānye teṣāṃ pi pūrṇā bhavi evameva // Saddhp_2.10 //
children.translated_text: and also these other <s>Śrāvakas</s> of mine — even filled with them in the same way — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.10 ||

children.text: ekībhavitvāna ca te 'dya sarve vicintayeyuḥ sugatasya jñānam /
children.translated_text: having become one, they all were now to reflect on the <s>Sugata</s>'s knowledge —

children.text: na śakta sarve sahitā pi jñātuṃ yathāprameyaṃ mama buddhajñānam // Saddhp_2.11 //
children.translated_text: all together they would be unable to know my immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.11 ||

children.text: pratyekabuddhāna anāsravāṇāṃ tīkṣṇendriyāṇāntimadehadhāriṇām /
children.translated_text: Of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> without outflows, with sharp faculties, bearers of the final body —

children.text: diśo daśaḥ sarva bhaveyuḥ pūrṇā yathā naḍānāṃ vanaveṇunāṃ vā // Saddhp_2.12 //
children.translated_text: if all ten directions were full of them, like reeds or forest bamboos — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.12 ||

children.text: eko bhavitvāna vicintayeyurmamāgradharmāṇa pradeśamātram /
children.translated_text: having become one, were they to reflect on even a portion of my supreme <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: kalpāna koṭīnayutānanantānna tasya bhūtaṃ parijāni artham // Saddhp_2.13 //
children.translated_text: for <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> without end — they would not fully know the real meaning. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.13 ||

body.text: navayānasaṃprasthita bodhisattvāḥ kṛtādhikārā bahubuddhakoṭiṣu /
body.translated_text: Newly set forth <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who have performed deeds under many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>,

body.text: suviniścitārthā bahudharmabhāṇakāsteṣāṃ pi pūrṇā daśimā diśo bhavet // Saddhp_2.14 //
body.translated_text: well-ascertained in meaning, speakers of many <s>dharmas</s> — even if these ten directions were full of them, || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.14 ||

children.text: naḍāna veṇūna va nityakālamacchidrapūrṇo bhavi sarvalokaḥ /
children.translated_text: the entire world filled without gaps, always, like reeds or bamboos,

children.text: ekībhavitvāna vicintayeyuryo dharma sākṣāt sugatena dṛṣṭaḥ // Saddhp_2.15 //
children.translated_text: having become one, were they to reflect on the <s>Dharma</s> directly seen by the <s>Sugata</s> — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.15 ||

children.text: anucintayitvā bahukalpakoṭyo gaṅgā yathā vālika aprameyāḥ /
children.translated_text: having reflected for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, immeasurable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: ananyacittāḥ sukhumāya prajñayā teṣāṃ pi cāsmin viṣayo na vidyate // Saddhp_2.16 //
children.translated_text: single-minded, with subtle wisdom — even their domain does not extend to this. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.16 ||

children.text: avivartikā ye bhavi bodhisattvā analpakā yathariva gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, not few, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: ananyacittāśca vicintayeyusteṣāṃ pi cāsmin viṣayo na vidyate // Saddhp_2.17 //
children.translated_text: single-minded, were they to reflect — even their domain does not extend to this. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.17 ||

children.text: gambhīra dharmā sukhumā pi buddhā atarkikāḥ sarvi anāsravāśca /
children.translated_text: Profound, subtle, the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> — all beyond logic and without outflows;

children.text: ahaṃ ca jānāmiha yādṛśā hi te te vā jinā loki daśaddiśāsu // Saddhp_2.18 //
children.translated_text: I know here what they are like, and so do those <s>Jinas</s> in the world in the ten directions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.18 ||

children.text: yaṃ śāriputro sugataḥ prabhāṣate adhimuktisaṃpanna bhavāhi tatra /
children.translated_text: What the <s>Sugata</s> proclaims to <s>Śāriputra</s> — be endowed with aspiration therein;

children.text: ananyathāvādi jino maharṣī cireṇa pī bhāṣati uttamārtham // Saddhp_2.19 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s>, the great sage, speaks no otherwise — after a long time too he speaks the supreme meaning. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.19 ||

children.text: āmantrayāmī imi sarvaśrāvakān pratyekabodhāya ca ye 'bhiprasthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: I address all these <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and those set forth toward <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>,

children.text: saṃsthāpitā ye maya nirvṛtīya saṃmokṣitā duḥkhaparaṃparātaḥ // Saddhp_2.20 //
children.translated_text: whom I have established in cessation and liberated from the succession of suffering. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.20 ||

children.text: upāyakauśalya mametadagraṃ bhāṣāmi dharmaṃ bahu yena loke /
children.translated_text: This is my foremost skill in means — I speak much <s>Dharma</s> in the world by which

children.text: tahiṃ tahiṃ lagna pramocayāmi trīṇī ca yānānyupadarśayāmi // Saddhp_2.21 //
children.translated_text: I liberate those attached here and there, and I show three vehicles. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.21 ||

body.text: atha khalu ye tatra parṣatsaṃnipāte mahāśrāvakā ājñātakauṇḍinyapramukhā arhantaḥ kṣīṇāsravā dvādaśa vaśībhūtaśatāni ye cānye śrāvakayānikā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā ye ca pratyekabuddhayānasaṃprasthitāḥ, teṣāṃ sarveṣāmetadabhavat - ko nu hetuḥ kiṃ kāraṇaṃ yad bhagavānadhimātramupāyakauśalyaṃ tathāgatānāṃ saṃvarṇayati? gambhīraścāyaṃ mayā dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddha iti saṃvarṇayati? durvijñeyaśca sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairiti saṃvarṇayati? yathā tāvad bhagavatā ekaiva vimuktirākhyātā, vayamapi buddhadharmāṇāṃ lābhino nirvāṇaprāptāḥ | asya ca vayaṃ bhagavato bhāṣitasyārtha na jānīmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then, in that assembly, the great <s>Śrāvakas</s> — the <s>Arhats</s> with outflows destroyed, twelve hundred who had attained mastery, led by <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, and the other monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, and those set forth in the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle — to all of them this thought occurred: 'What is the reason, what is the cause, that the Blessed One so greatly praises the skill in means of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>? That he praises thus: "This <s>Dharma</s> I have realized is profound"? That he praises: "Hard to understand by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>"? Inasmuch as the Blessed One has hitherto declared only a single liberation, we too are obtainers of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, attainers of <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Yet we do not understand the meaning of this speech of the Blessed One.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputrastāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ vicikitsākathaṃkathāṃ viditvā cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya ātmanā ca dharmasaṃśayaprāptastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayo yad bhagavānadhimātraṃ punaḥ punastathāgatānāmupāyakauśalyajñānadarśanadharmadeśanāṃ saṃvarṇayati - gambhīraśca me dharmo 'bhisaṃbuddha iti | durvijñeyaṃ ca saṃghābhāṣyamiti punaḥ punaḥ saṃvarṇayati | na ca me bhagavato 'ntikādevaṃrūpo dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutapūrvaḥ | imāśca bhagavaṃścatasraḥ parṣado vicikitsākathaṃkathāprāptāḥ | tatsādhu bhagavānnirdiśatu yatsaṃghāya tathāgato gambhīrasya tathāgatadharmasya punaḥ punaḥ saṃvarṇanāṃ karoti ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having known the doubt and uncertainty of those four assemblies by mind reading their mental deliberation, and himself having reached doubt in the <s>Dharma</s>, at that time said this to the Blessed One: 'What, Blessed One, is the reason, what is the condition, that the Blessed One again and again so greatly praises the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' skill in means, knowledge, and vision — [saying]: "And this <s>Dharma</s> realized by me is profound," and again and again praises: "Hard to understand is the teaching with intended purport"? Such a <s>Dharma</s>-discourse has not been heard by me before from the Blessed One. And these four assemblies, Blessed One, have arrived at doubt and uncertainty. May the Blessed One kindly explain to the assembly why the <s>Tathāgata</s> again and again praises the profundity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputrastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: cirasyādya narāditya īdṛśīṃ kurute kathām /
children.translated_text: Today, after a long time, the Sun of Men makes such a discourse;

children.text: balā vimokṣā dhyānāśca aprameyā mi sparśitāḥ // Saddhp_2.22 //
children.translated_text: powers, liberations, and <s>dhyānas</s> — he has declared these immeasurables touched [by him]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.22 ||

children.text: bodhimaṇḍaṃ ca kīrtesi pṛcchakaste na vidyate /
children.translated_text: He extols the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, yet no one questions him;

children.text: saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ ca kīrtesi na ca tvāṃ kaści pṛcchati // Saddhp_2.23 //
children.translated_text: he extols the teaching with intended purport, yet no one asks him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.23 ||

children.text: apṛcchito vyāharasi caryāṃ varṇesi cātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Unasked, he speaks; he praises his own conduct;

children.text: jñānādhigama kīrtesi gambhīraṃ ca prabhāṣase // Saddhp_2.24 //
children.translated_text: he extols the attainment of knowledge and speaks of the profound. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.24 ||

children.text: adyeme saṃśayaprāptā vaśībhūtā anāsravāḥ /
children.translated_text: Today these masters without outflows have arrived at doubt —

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ prasthitā ye ca kimetad bhāṣate jinaḥ // Saddhp_2.25 //
children.translated_text: those set forth toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> — what does the <s>Jina</s> declare? || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.25 ||

children.text: pratyekabodhiṃ prārthentā bhikṣuṇyo bhikṣavastathā /
children.translated_text: Those who aspire to <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, nuns and monks likewise,

children.text: devā nāgāśca yakṣāśca gandharvāśca mahoragāḥ // Saddhp_2.26 //
children.translated_text: <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, and great serpents (<s>mahoragas</s>) — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.26 ||

children.text: samālapanto anyonyaṃ prekṣante dvipadottamam /
children.translated_text: conversing with one another, they gaze upon the Foremost of Bipeds;

children.text: kathaṃkathī vicintentā vyākuruṣva mahāmune // Saddhp_2.27 //
children.translated_text: filled with uncertainty, they reflect — explain, O great sage! || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.27 ||

children.text: yāvantaḥ śrāvakāḥ santi sugatasyeha sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: However many <s>Śrāvakas</s> there are here of the <s>Sugata</s>, in every way,

children.text: ahamatra pāramīprāpto nirdiṣṭaḥ paramarṣiṇā // Saddhp_2.28 //
children.translated_text: I have here attained the perfection and have been declared so by the supreme sage. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.28 ||

children.text: mamāpi saṃśayo hyatra svake sthāne narottama /
children.translated_text: Even I have doubt here regarding my own position, O best of men —

children.text: kiṃ niṣṭhā mama nirvāṇe atha caryā mi darśitā // Saddhp_2.29 //
children.translated_text: is my end in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, or has [a further] course been shown to me? || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.29 ||

children.text: pramuñca ghoṣaṃ varadundubhisvarā udāharasvā yatha eṣa dharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: Release the sound, with the voice of an excellent drum — proclaim what this <s>Dharma</s> is!

children.text: ime sthitā putra jinasya aurasā vyavalokayantaśca kṛtāñjalī jinam // Saddhp_2.30 //
children.translated_text: These natural-born sons of the <s>Jina</s> stand here, gazing at the <s>Jina</s> with joined palms. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.30 ||

children.text: devāśca nāgāśca sayakṣarākṣasāḥ koṭīsahasrā yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>, in thousands of <s>koṭis</s> like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: ye cāpi prārthenti samagrabodhiṃ sahasraśītiḥ paripūrṇa ye sthitāḥ // Saddhp_2.31 //
children.translated_text: and those too who aspire to complete awakening — eighty thousand stand here, fully [devoted]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.31 ||

children.text: rājāna ye mahipati cakravartino ye āgatāḥ kṣetrasahasrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings who are sovereigns of the earth, wheel-turners, who have come from thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields,

children.text: kṛtāñjalī sarvi sagauravāḥ sthitāḥ kathaṃ nu caryāṃ paripūrayema // Saddhp_2.32 //
children.translated_text: all stand with joined palms, respectful — how may we fulfill the course? || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.32 ||

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - alaṃ śāriputra | kimanenārthena bhāṣitena? tatkasya hetoḥ? utrasiṣyati śāriputra ayaṃ sadevako loko 'sminnarthe vyākriyamāṇe | dvaitīyakamapyāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - bhāṣatāṃ bhagavān, bhāṣatāṃ sugata etamevārtham | tatkasya hetoḥ? santi bhagavaṃstasyāṃ parṣadi bahūni prāṇiśatāni bahūni prāṇisahasrāṇi bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi bahūni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi pūrvabuddhadarśāvīni prajñāvanti, yāni bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ śraddhāsyanti pratīyiṣyanti udgrahīṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Enough, <s>Śāriputra</s>! What need is there to speak of this matter? Why? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, this world with its gods would be frightened if this matter were declared." A second time too, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> entreated the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One speak, let the <s>Sugata</s> speak of this very matter! Why? Because, Blessed One, in this assembly there are many hundreds of beings, many thousands of beings, many hundreds of thousands of beings, many koṭis, nayutas, and hundreds of thousands of beings who have seen former <s>Buddhas</s> and who are wise — they will have faith in, understand, and take up what the Blessed One says."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantamanayā gāthayādhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the Blessed One with this verse:

children.text: vispaṣṭu bhāṣasva jināna uttamā santīha parṣāya sahasra prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: "Speak clearly, O supreme among <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors)! There are thousands of beings here in this assembly

children.text: śrāddhāḥ prasannāḥ sugate sagauravā jñāsyanti ye dharmamudāhṛtaṃ te // Saddhp_2.33 //
children.translated_text: who are faithful, devoted to the <s>Sugata</s>, and reverent — they will understand the <s>Dharma</s> declared by you." [Saddhp 2.33]

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān dvaitīyakamapyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - alaṃ śāriputra anenārthena prakāśitena | utrasiṣyati śāriputra ayaṃ sadevako loko 'sminnarthe vyākriyamāṇe | abhimānaprāptāśca bhikṣavo mahāprapātaṃ prapatiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One spoke a second time to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Enough, <s>Śāriputra</s>, with making this matter known! <s>Śāriputra</s>, this world with its gods would be frightened if this matter were declared. And conceited monks would fall into a great precipice."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke this verse:

children.text: alaṃ hi dharmeṇiha bhāṣitena sūkṣmaṃ idaṃ jñānamatarkikaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "Enough! The <s>Dharma</s> should not be spoken here — this knowledge is subtle and beyond reasoning;

children.text: abhimānaprāptā bahu santi bālā nirdiṣṭadharmasmi kṣipe ajānakāḥ // Saddhp_2.34 //
children.translated_text: there are many conceited fools who, when the <s>Dharma</s> is declared, would reject it, not understanding." [Saddhp 2.34]

body.text: traitīyakamapyāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantamadhyeṣate sma - bhāṣatāṃ bhagavān, bhāṣatāṃ sugata etamevārtham | mādṛśānāṃ bhagavanniha parṣadi bahūni prāṇiśatāni saṃvidyante, anyāni ca bhagavan bahūni prāṇiśatāni bahūni prāṇisahasrāṇi bahūni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi bahūni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi, yāni bhagavatā pūrvabhaveṣu paripācitāni, tāni bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ śraddhāsyanti pratīyiṣyanti udgahīṣyanti | teṣāṃ tadbhabhaviṣyati dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāyeti ||
body.translated_text: A third time too, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> entreated the Blessed One: "Let the Blessed One speak, let the <s>Sugata</s> speak of this very matter! Blessed One, in this assembly there are many hundreds of beings like myself, and also, Blessed One, many other hundreds of beings, many thousands, many hundreds of thousands, many koṭis, nayutas, and hundreds of thousands of beings who have been matured by the Blessed One in former existences — they will have faith in, understand, and take up what the Blessed One says. For them it will be for their long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputrastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: bhāṣasva dharmaṃ dvipadānamuttamā ahaṃ tvāmadhyeṣami jyeṣṭhaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: "Speak the <s>Dharma</s>, O supreme among bipeds! I, your eldest son, entreat you.

children.text: santīha prāṇīna sahasrakoṭayo ye śraddadhāsyanti te dharma bhāṣitam // Saddhp_2.35 //
children.translated_text: There are here koṭis and thousands of beings who will have faith in the <s>Dharma</s> you speak." [Saddhp 2.35]

children.text: ye ca tvayā pūrvabhaveṣu nityaṃ paripācitāḥ sattva sudīrgharātram /
children.translated_text: "And those beings who have been matured by you, always, in former existences, for a very long time —

children.text: kṛtāñjalī te pi sthitātra sarve ye śraddadhāsyanti tavaita dharmam // Saddhp_2.36 //
children.translated_text: all of them stand here with joined palms, who will have faith in this <s>Dharma</s> of yours." [Saddhp 2.36]

children.text: asmādṛśā dvādaśime śatāśca ye cāpi te prasthita agrabodhaye /
children.translated_text: "These twelve hundred like us, and also those who have set out for supreme awakening —

children.text: tān paśyamānaḥ sugataḥ prabhāṣatāṃ teṣāṃ ca harṣaṃ paramaṃ janetu // Saddhp_2.37 //
children.translated_text: looking upon them, may the <s>Sugata</s> speak, and may he generate supreme joy in them!" [Saddhp 2.37]

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstraitīyakamapyāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyādhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - yadidānīṃ tvaṃ śāriputra yāvatraitīyakamapi tathāgatamadhyeṣase | evamadhyeṣamāṇaṃ tvāṃ śāriputra kiṃ vakṣyāmi ? tena hi śāriputra śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having understood even the third entreaty of the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "Since you, <s>Śāriputra</s>, now entreat the <s>Tathāgata</s> even a third time — being so entreated, <s>Śāriputra</s>, what shall I say to you? Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, listen, and attend well and carefully. I shall speak to you."

body.text: samanantarabhāṣitā ceyaṃ bhagavatā vāk, atha khalu tataḥ parṣada ābhimānikānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāmupāsakānāmupāsikānāṃ pañcamātrāṇi sahasrāṇyutthāya āsanebhyo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā tataḥ parṣado 'pakrāmanti sma, yathāpīdamabhimānākuśalamūlena aprāpte prāptasaṃjñino 'nadhigate 'dhigatasaṃjñinaḥ | te ātmānaṃ savraṇaṃ jñātvā tataḥ parṣado 'pakrāntāḥ | bhagavāṃśca tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayati sma ||
body.translated_text: No sooner had this word been spoken by the Blessed One than five thousand conceited monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen rose from their seats, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, and departed from that assembly — because, through unwholesome roots of conceit, they thought they had attained what they had not attained, and thought they had realized what they had not realized. Knowing themselves to be flawed, they departed from that assembly. And the Blessed One consented through silence.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputramāmantrayate sma - nippalāvā me śāriputra parṣat apagataphalguḥ śraddhāsāre pratiṣṭhitā | sādhu śāriputra eteṣāmābhimānikānāmato 'pakramaṇam | tena hi śāriputra bhāṣiṣye etamartham | sādhu bhagavannityāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: "My assembly, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is now freed from chaff, rid of worthless husks, established in the essence of faith. It is good, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that those conceited ones have departed. Therefore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I shall speak of this matter." "Very well, Blessed One!" — the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> assented to the Blessed One.

body.text:
bhagavānetadavocat - kadācit karhicicchāriputra tathāgata evaṃrūpāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kathayati | tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra udumbarapuṣpaṃ kadācit karhicit saṃdṛśyate, evameva śāriputra tathāgato 'pi kadācit karhicit evaṃrūpāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kathayati | śraddadhata me śāriputra, bhūtavādyahamasmi, tathāvādyahamasmi, ananyathāvādyahamasmi | durbodhyaṃ śāriputra tathāgatasya saṃdhābhāṣyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? nānāniruktinirdeśābhilāpanirdeśanairmayā śāriputra vividhairupāyakauśalyaśatasahasrairdharmaḥ saṃprakāśitaḥ | atarko 'tarkāvacarastathāgatavijñeyaḥ śāriputra saddharmaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? ekakṛtyena śāriputra ekakaraṇīyena tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate mahākṛtyena mahākaraṇīyena | katamaṃ ca śāriputra tathāgatasya ekakṛtyamekakaraṇīyaṃ mahākṛtyaṃ mahākaraṇīyaṃ yena kṛtyena tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate? yadidaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpanahetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśanahetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraṇahetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | tathāgatajñānapratibodhanahetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraṇahetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | idaṃ tacchāriputra tathāgatasya ekakṛtyamekakaraṇīyaṃ mahākṛtyaṃ mahākaraṇīyamekaprayojanaṃ loke prādurbhāvāya | iti hi śāriputra yattathāgatasya ekakṛtyamekakaraṇīyaṃ mahākṛtyaṃ mahākaraṇīyam, tattathāgataḥ karoti | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpaka evāhaṃ śāriputra, tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśaka evāhaṃ śāriputra, tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraka evāhaṃ śāriputra, tathāgatajñānadarśanapratibodhaka evāhaṃ śāriputra, tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraka evāhaṃ śāriputra | ekamevāhaṃ śāriputra yānamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharma deśayāmi yadidaṃ buddhayānam | na kiṃcicchāriputra dvitīyaṃ vā tṛtīyaṃ vā yānaṃ saṃvidyate | sarvatraiṣā śāriputra dharmatā daśadigloke | tatkasya hetoḥ? ye 'pi tu śāriputra atīta
'dhvanyabhūvan daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca | ye nānābhinirhāranirdeśavividhahetukāraṇanidarśanārambaṇaniruktyupāyakauśalyairnānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhātvāśayānāmāśayaṃ viditvā dharmaṃ deśitavantaḥ | te 'pi sarve śāriputra buddhā bhagavanta ekameva yānamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśitavantaḥ, yadidaṃ buddhayānaṃ sarvajñatāparyavasānam, yadidaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpanameva sattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraṇameva tathāgatajñānadarśanapratibodhanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraṇameva sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśitavantaḥ | yairapi śāriputra sattvaisteṣāmatītānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantikāt saddharmaḥ śrutaḥ, te 'pi sarve 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherlābhino 'bhūvan ||
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said this: "Rarely, <s>Śāriputra</s>, very rarely, does the <s>Tathāgata</s> give such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>udumbara</s> flower is seen only rarely, so too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> gives such a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching only rarely. Believe me, <s>Śāriputra</s> — I am a speaker of truth, a speaker of what is so, a speaker of what is not otherwise. Hard to understand, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> intentional speech. Why? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, through various etymologies, expositions, expressions, and declarations, through hundreds of thousands of various skillful means, I have illuminated the <s>Dharma</s>. Beyond reasoning, beyond the scope of reasoning, is the true <s>Dharma</s>, knowable only by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>. Why? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, appears in the world with one task, one duty, one great task, one great duty. And what, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> one task, one duty, one great task, one great duty, for which the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, appears in the world? The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, appears in the world for the cause and purpose of leading beings to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. The <s>Tathāgata</s> appears for the cause and purpose of showing beings the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. The <s>Tathāgata</s> appears for the cause and purpose of causing beings to enter the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. The <s>Tathāgata</s> appears for the cause and purpose of awakening beings to the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. The <s>Tathāgata</s> appears for the cause and purpose of causing beings to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata's</s> one task, one duty, one great task, one great duty, the single purpose for his appearance in the world. Thus, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> performs that which is his one task, one duty, one great task, one great duty. Why? Because I, <s>Śāriputra</s>, am the one who leads beings to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision; I, <s>Śāriputra</s>, am the one who shows them the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision; I am the one who causes them to enter the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision; I am the one who awakens them to the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision; I am the one who causes them to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. Beginning with one single vehicle, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle). There is no second or third vehicle to be found, <s>Śāriputra</s>. This, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things) everywhere in the ten-directional world. Why? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, even the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones who existed in the past, in the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems of the ten directions — for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of beings, of gods and humans — who, having understood the dispositions of beings with various inclinations and various natures of temperament, through various displays of manifestation, varied expositions of causes and conditions, demonstrations, supports, etymologies, and skillful means, taught the <s>Dharma</s> — they too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, beginning with one single vehicle, taught the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle), culminating in omniscience. They taught the <s>Dharma</s> to beings precisely for the purpose of leading them to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, showing them the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, causing them to enter it, awakening them to it, and causing them to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. And all those beings, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who heard the true <s>Dharma</s> from those past <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones — all of them attained unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: ye 'pi te śāriputra anāgate 'dhvani bhaviṣyanti daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, ye ca nānābhirnihāranirdeśavividhahetukāraṇanidarśanārambaṇaniruktyupāyakauśalyairnānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhātvāśayānāmāśayaṃ viditvā dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti, te 'pi sarve śāriputra buddhā bhagavanta ekameva yānamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti yadidaṃ buddhayānaṃ sarvajñatāparyavasānam, yadidaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpanameva sattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraṇameva tathāgatajñānadarśanapratibodhanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraṇameva sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyanti | ye 'pi te śāriputra sattvāsteṣāmanāgatānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantikāt taṃ dharmaṃ śroṣyanti, te 'pi sarve 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherlābhino bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: And those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones who will exist in the future, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems of the ten directions — for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of beings, of gods and humans — who, having understood the dispositions of beings with various inclinations and various natures of temperament, through various displays of manifestation, varied expositions of causes and conditions, demonstrations, supports, etymologies, and skillful means, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> — they too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, beginning with one single vehicle, will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle), culminating in omniscience. They will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings precisely for the purpose of leading them to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, showing them the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, causing them to enter it, awakening them to it, and causing them to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. And all those beings, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who will hear that <s>Dharma</s> from those future <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones — all of them will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: ye 'pi te śāriputra etarhi pratyutpanne 'dhvani daśasu dikṣvaprameyeṣvasaṃkhyeyeṣu lokadhātuṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstiṣṭhanti ghriyante yāpayanti, dharmaṃ ca deśayanti bahujanahitāya bahujanahitāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca, ye nānābhinirhāranirdeśavividhahetukāraṇanidarśanārambaṇaniruktyupāyakauśalyairnānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhātvāśayānāmāśayaṃ viditvā dharmaṃ deśayanti, te 'pi sarve śāriputra buddhā bhagavanta ekameva yānamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti yadidaṃ buddhayānaṃ sarvajñatāparyavasānam, yadidaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpanameva sattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraṇameva tathāgatajñānadarśanapratibodhanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraṇameva sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti | ye 'pi te śāriputra sattvāsteṣāṃ pratyutpannānāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantikāt taṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti, te 'pi sarve 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherlābhino bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: And those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones who exist at present, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the immeasurable and incalculable world-systems of the ten directions, who abide, live, and carry on, and who teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit and welfare of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of beings, of gods and humans — who, having understood the dispositions of beings with various inclinations and various natures of temperament, through various displays of manifestation, varied expositions of causes and conditions, demonstrations, supports, etymologies, and skillful means, teach the <s>Dharma</s> — they too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, all those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, beginning with one single vehicle, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle), culminating in omniscience. They teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings precisely for the purpose of leading them to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, showing them the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, causing them to enter it, awakening them to it, and causing them to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. And all those beings, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who hear that <s>Dharma</s> from those present <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones — all of them will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening.

body.text: ahamapi śāriputra etarhi tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca nānābhinirhāranirdeśavividhahetukāraṇanidarśanārambaṇaniruktyupāyakauśalyairnānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhātvāśayānāmāśayaṃ viditvā dharmaṃ deśayāmi | ahamapi śāriputra ekameva yānamārabhya sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi yadidaṃ buddhayānaṃ sarvajñatāparyavasānam, yadidaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasamādāpanameva sattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanasaṃdarśanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanāvatāraṇameva tathāgatajñānadarśanapratibodhanameva tathāgatajñānadarśanamārgāvatāraṇameva sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi | ye 'pi te śāriputra sattvā etarhi mamemaṃ dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti, te 'pi sarve 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherlābhino bhaviṣyanti | tadanenāpi śāriputra paryāyeṇa evaṃ veditavyaṃ yathā nāsti dvitīyasya yānasya kvaciddaśasu dikṣu loke prajñaptiḥ, kutaḥ punastṛtīyasya ||
body.translated_text: I too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, at present, being the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened one, for the benefit and welfare of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of beings, of gods and humans — having understood the dispositions of beings with various inclinations and various natures of temperament, through various displays of manifestation, varied expositions of causes and conditions, demonstrations, supports, etymologies, and skillful means — I teach the <s>Dharma</s>. I too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, beginning with one single vehicle, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle), culminating in omniscience. I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings precisely for the purpose of leading them to undertake the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, showing them the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision, causing them to enter it, awakening them to it, and causing them to enter the path of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. And all those beings, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who now hear this <s>Dharma</s> of mine — all of them will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. By this method too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it should be understood that there is nowhere in the world of the ten directions the designation of a second vehicle, let alone a third.

body.text: api tu khalu punaḥ śāriputra yadā tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā kalpakaṣāye
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones arise in the decay of the age (<s>kalpakaṣāya</s>),

body.text: votpadyante sattvakaṣāye vā kleśakaṣāye vā dṛṣṭikaṣāye vā āyuṣkaṣāye votpadyante | evaṃrūpeṣu śāriputra kalpasaṃkṣobhakaṣāyeṣu bahusattveṣu lubdheṣvalpakuśalamūleṣu tadā śāriputra tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā upāyakauśalyena tadevaikaṃ buddhayānaṃ triyānanirdeśena nirdiśanti | tatra śāriputra ye śrāvakā arhantaḥ pratyekabuddhā vā imāṃ kriyāṃ tathāgatasya buddhayānasamādapanāṃ na śṛṇvanti nāvataranti nāvabudhyanti, na te śāriputra tathāgatasya śrāvakā veditavyāḥ, nāpyarhanto nāpi pratyekabuddhā veditavyāḥ | api tu khalu punaḥ śāriputra yaḥ kaścid bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vā arhattvaṃ pratijānīyāt, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau praṇidhānamaparigṛhya ucchinno 'smi buddhayānāditi vadet, etāvanme samucchrayasya paścimakaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ vadet, ābhimānikaṃ taṃ śāriputra prajānīyāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? asthānametacchāriputra anavakāśo yadbhikṣurarhan kṣīṇāsravaḥ saṃmukhībhūte tathāgate imaṃḥ dharmaṃ śrutvā na śraddadhyāt sthāpayitvā parinirvṛtasya tathāgatasya | tatkasya hetoḥ? na hi śāriputra śrāvakāstasmin kāle tasmin samaye parinirvṛte tathāgate eteṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntānāṃ dhārakā vā deśakā vā bhaviṣyanti | anyeṣu punaḥ śāriputra tathāgateṣvarhatsu samyaksaṃbuddheṣu niḥsaṃśayā bhaviṣyanti | imeṣu buddhadharmeṣu śraddadhādhvaṃ me śāriputra pattīyata avakalpayata | na hi śāriputra tathāgatānāṃ mṛṣāvādaḥ saṃvidyate | ekamevedaṃ śāriputra yānaṃ yadidaṃ buddhayānam ||
body.translated_text: or in the decay of beings, or in the decay of afflictions, or in the decay of views, or in the decay of the lifespan — in such a corruption and turbulence of the age, <s>Śāriputra</s>, when beings are numerous, greedy, and of few wholesome roots — then, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones, through skillful means, expound that very single <s>Buddhayāna</s> by means of a teaching of three vehicles. Therein, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who do not hear, do not enter into, and do not understand this activity of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — the exhortation to the <s>Buddhayāna</s> — they, <s>Śāriputra</s>, should not be considered <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor should they be considered <s>Arhats</s> or <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, if any monk or nun should claim <s>Arhatship</s> — not having embraced the aspiration for unsurpassed perfect awakening, saying 'I am cut off from the <s>Buddhayāna</s>,' saying 'This is my final <s>parinirvāṇa</s> at this level of attainment' — you should know that one, <s>Śāriputra</s>, as conceited. For what reason? This is impossible, <s>Śāriputra</s>, this cannot happen — that a monk who is an <s>Arhat</s>, whose defilements are exhausted, would not have faith upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s> in the direct presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, except after the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time and occasion after the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, no <s>Śrāvakas</s> will be bearers or teachers of such sūtras. But they will have no doubt regarding other <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, perfectly enlightened ones. Have faith in these Buddha-<s>dharmas</s> of mine, <s>Śāriputra</s>, trust and accept [them]. For, <s>Śāriputra</s>, false speech is not found among the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. There is, <s>Śāriputra</s>, this one vehicle alone — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānetamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in order to display this very meaning even further, spoke at that time these verses:

children.text: athābhimānaprāptā ye bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then those conceited monks, nuns, laymen,

children.text: upāsikāśca aśrāddhāḥ sahasrāḥ pañcanūnakāḥ // Saddhp_2.38 //
children.translated_text: and laywomen, faithless — five thousand less [than the full assembly] — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.38 ||

children.text: apaśyanta imaṃ doṣaṃ chidraśikṣāsamanvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: not seeing their own fault, possessed of broken discipline,

children.text: vraṇāṃśca parirakṣantaḥ prakrāntā bālabuddhayaḥ // Saddhp_2.39 //
children.translated_text: guarding their own wounds, those of foolish understanding departed. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.39 ||

children.text: parṣatkaṣāyatāṃ jñātvā lokanātho 'dhivāsayi /
children.translated_text: Knowing the corruption of the assembly, the Lord of the World consented [to their departure];

children.text: tatteṣāṃ kuśalaṃ nāsti śṛṇuyurdharma ye imam // Saddhp_2.40 //
children.translated_text: there is no good in those — those who would [not] hear this <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.40 ||

children.text: śuddhā ca niṣpalāvā ca susthitā pariṣanmama /
children.translated_text: My assembly is now pure, free from chaff, well-established;

children.text: phalguvyapagatā sarvā sārā ceyaṃ pratiṣṭhitā // Saddhp_2.41 //
children.translated_text: rid of all worthless husks, and this [assembly] is established in the essence. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.41 ||

children.text: śṛṇohi me śārisutā yathaiṣa saṃbuddha dharmaḥ puruṣottamehi /
children.translated_text: Hear me, O son of <s>Śāri</s> — how this <s>Dharma</s> of the perfectly enlightened ones, the supreme among men,

children.text: yathā ca buddhāḥ kathayanti nāyakā upāyakauśalyaśatairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_2.42 //
children.translated_text: and how the Buddhas, the Leaders, speak through hundreds of innumerable skillful means. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.42 ||

body.text: yathāśayaṃ jāniya te cariṃ ca nānādhimuktāniha prāṇakoṭinām /
body.translated_text: Having known the dispositions and conduct, and the various inclinations here of millions of beings,

body.text: citrāṇi karmāṇi viditva teṣāṃ purākṛtaṃ yatkuśalaṃ ca tehi // Saddhp_2.43 //
body.translated_text: and having known their various <s>karmas</s>, and what wholesome [deeds] were formerly done by them — || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.43 ||

children.text: nānāniruktīhi ca kāraṇehi saṃprāpayāmī ima teṣa prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: through various etymologies and reasons, I bring these beings to this [<s>Dharma</s>];

children.text: hetūhi dṛṣṭāntaśatehi cāhaṃ tathā tathā toṣayi sarvasattvān // Saddhp_2.44 //
children.translated_text: and with reasons and hundreds of examples, I thus and thus satisfy all beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.44 ||

children.text: sūtrāṇi bhāṣāmi tathaiva gāthā itivṛttakaṃ jātakamadbhutaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: I speak <s>sūtras</s> and likewise verses, <s>itivṛttaka</s> (historical accounts), <s>jātaka</s> (birth stories), and the marvelous,

children.text: nidāna aupamyaśataiśca citrairgeyaṃ ca bhāṣāmi tathopadeśān // Saddhp_2.45 //
children.translated_text: and with <s>nidāna</s> (causal narratives) and hundreds of similes, and <s>geya</s> (mixed prose-verse), I speak the <s>upadeśas</s> (instructions). || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.45 ||

children.text: ye bhonti hīnābhiratā avidvasū acīrṇacaryā bahubuddhakoṭiṣu /
children.translated_text: Those who are of low inclination, ignorant, who have not practiced the course under many millions of Buddhas,

children.text: saṃsāralagnāśca suduḥkhitāśca nirvāṇa teṣāmupadarśayāmi // Saddhp_2.46 //
children.translated_text: and who are attached to <s>saṃsāra</s> and greatly afflicted — to them I show <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.46 ||

children.text: upāyametaṃ kurute svayaṃbhūrbauddhasya jñānasya prabodhanārtham /
children.translated_text: The Self-Arisen One employs this skillful means for the purpose of awakening to Buddha-knowledge;

children.text: na cāpi teṣāṃ pravade kadācid yuṣme 'pi buddhā iha loki bheṣyatha // Saddhp_2.47 //
children.translated_text: but never do I say to them: 'You too shall become Buddhas in this world.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.47 ||

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ kālamavekṣya tāyī kṣaṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tatu paśca bhāṣate /
children.translated_text: For what reason? The Protector, observing the time and seeing the right moment, speaks of that afterwards;

children.text: so 'yaṃ kṣaṇo adya kathaṃci labdho vadāmi yeneha ca bhūtaniścayam // Saddhp_2.48 //
children.translated_text: that moment has now been somehow obtained today — [the moment] by which I speak the true determination here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.48 ||

children.text: navāṅgametanmama śāsanaṃ ca prakāśitaṃ sattvabalābalena /
children.translated_text: This ninefold teaching of mine has been made known according to the strength and weakness of beings;

children.text: upāya eṣo varadasya jñāne praveśanārthāya nidarśito me // Saddhp_2.49 //
children.translated_text: this is the skillful means of the best of givers, shown by me for the purpose of entry into knowledge. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.49 ||

children.text: bhavanti ye ceha sadā viśuddhā vyaktā śucī sūrata buddhaputrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are here always purified, clear, pure, well-behaved sons of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: kṛtādhikārā bahubuddhakoṭiṣu vaipulyasūtrāṇi vadāmi teṣām // Saddhp_2.50 //
children.translated_text: who have performed their duties under many millions of Buddhas — to them I speak the <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive) sūtras. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.50 ||

children.text: tathā hi te āśayasaṃpadāya viśuddharūpāya samanvitābhūn /
children.translated_text: For they are endowed with the perfection of disposition and purified form;

children.text: vadāmi tān buddha bhaviṣyatheti anāgate 'dhvāni hitānukampakāḥ // Saddhp_2.51 //
children.translated_text: I say to them: 'You shall be Buddhas in the future age' — compassionate benefactors. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.51 ||

children.text: śrutvā ca prītisphuṭa bhonti sarve buddhā bhaviṣyāma jagatpradhānāḥ /
children.translated_text: And having heard, all are suffused with delight: 'We shall become Buddhas, foremost in the world!';

children.text: punaśca haṃ jāniya teṣa caryāṃ vaipulyasūtrāṇi prakāśayāmi // Saddhp_2.52 //
children.translated_text: and again I, knowing their conduct, illuminate the <s>vaipulya</s> sūtras for them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.52 ||

children.text: ime ca te śrāvaka nāyakasya yehi śrutaṃ śāsanametamagryam /
children.translated_text: And these <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the Leader, who have heard this supreme teaching,

children.text: ekāpi gāthā śruta dhāritā vā sarveṣa bodhāya na saṃśayo 'sti // Saddhp_2.53 //
children.translated_text: even if they have heard or retained a single verse — there is no doubt about awakening for all of them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.53 ||

children.text: ekaṃ hi yānaṃ dvitiyaṃ na vidyate tṛtiyaṃ hi naivāsti kadāci loke /
children.translated_text: For there is one vehicle; a second does not exist; a third indeed never exists in the world;

children.text: anyatrupāyā puruṣottamānāṃ yadyānanānātvupadarśayanti // Saddhp_2.54 //
children.translated_text: except as the skillful means of the supreme among men, when they show a diversity of vehicles. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.54 ||

children.text: bauddhasya jñānasya prakāśanārthaṃ loke samutpadyati lokanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of illuminating Buddha-knowledge, the Lord of the World arises in the world;

children.text: ekaṃ hi kāryaṃ dvitiyaṃ na vidyate na hīnayānena nayanti buddhāḥ // Saddhp_2.55 //
children.translated_text: there is one task alone, a second does not exist — Buddhas do not guide by a lesser vehicle. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.55 ||

children.text: pratiṣṭhito yatra svayaṃ svayaṃbhūryaccaiva buddhaṃ yatha yādṛśaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Where the Self-Arisen One himself is established, and what the Buddha is and of what kind,

children.text: balāśca ye dhyānavimokṣa-indriyāstatraiva sattvā pi pratiṣṭhapeti // Saddhp_2.56 //
children.translated_text: and his powers, <s>dhyānas</s>, liberations, and faculties — in that very [state] he establishes beings too. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.56 ||

children.text: mātsaryadoṣo hi bhaveta mahyaṃ spṛśitva bodhiṃ virajāṃ viśiṣṭām /
children.translated_text: There would be the fault of miserliness in me if, having touched the stainless, distinguished awakening,

children.text: yadi hīnayānasmi pratiṣṭhapeyamekaṃ pi sattvaṃ na mamate sādhu // Saddhp_2.57 //
children.translated_text: I were to establish even a single being in a lesser vehicle — this would not be good for me. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.57 ||

body.text: mātsarya mahyaṃ na kahiṃci vidyate īrṣyā na me nāpi ca chandarāgaḥ /
body.translated_text: Miserliness is nowhere found in me; there is no envy in me, nor passionate desire;

body.text: ucchinna pāpā mama sarvadharmāstenāsmi buddho jagato 'nubodhāt // Saddhp_2.58 //
body.translated_text: all evil <s>dharmas</s> of mine are cut off — therefore I am a <s>Buddha</s>, from awakening the world. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.58 ||

children.text: yathā hyahaṃ citritu lakṣaṇehi prabhāsayanto imu sarvalokam /
children.translated_text: Just as I, adorned with variegated marks, illuminating this entire world,

children.text: puraskṛtaḥ prāṇiśatairanekairdeśemimāṃ dharmasvabhāvamudrām // Saddhp_2.59 //
children.translated_text: attended by innumerable hundreds of beings, teach this <s>Dharma</s>-seal of the true nature. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.59 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca cintemyahu śāriputra kathaṃ nu evaṃ bhavi sarvasattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus I think, O <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'How may it be that all beings',

children.text: dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhāriṇaḥ svayaṃprabhā lokavidū svayaṃbhūḥ // Saddhp_2.60 //
children.translated_text: 'bearing the form of the thirty-two marks, may become self-radiant, world-knowing, self-arisen!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.60 ||

children.text: yathā ca paśyāmi yathā ca cintaye yathā ca saṃkalpa mamāsi pūrvam /
children.translated_text: As I see and as I think, and as was my former resolution,

children.text: paripūrṇametat praṇidhānu mahyaṃ buddhā ca bodhiṃ ca prakāśayāmi // Saddhp_2.61 //
children.translated_text: this aspiration of mine is fulfilled — and I illuminate the Buddhas and awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.61 ||

children.text: sacedahaṃ śārisutā vadeyaṃ sattvāna bodhāya janetha chandam /
children.translated_text: If I, O son of <s>Śāri</s>, were to say to beings: 'Generate the desire for awakening!' —

children.text: ajānakāḥ sarva bhrameyuratra na jātu gṛhṇīyu subhāṣitaṃ me // Saddhp_2.62 //
children.translated_text: all, being ignorant, would be confused here and would never grasp my well-spoken [words]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.62 ||

children.text: tāṃścaiva haṃ jāniya evarūpān na cīrṇacaryāḥ purimāsu jātiṣu /
children.translated_text: And I know those of such a type — who have not practiced the course in former births,

children.text: adhyoṣitāḥ kāmaguṇeṣu saktāstṛṣṇāya saṃmūrchita mohacittāḥ // Saddhp_2.63 //
children.translated_text: who are settled in sense-pleasures, attached, confused and deluded of mind through craving. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.63 ||

children.text: te kāmahetoḥ prapatanti durgatiṃ ṣaṭsū gatīṣū parikhidyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of desires they fall into bad destinies, being wearied in the six courses;

children.text: kaṭasī ca vardhenti punaḥ punaste duḥkhena saṃpīḍita alpapuṇyāḥ // Saddhp_2.64 //
children.translated_text: and the embryonic forms grow again and again — those of little merit, oppressed by suffering. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.64 ||

children.text: vilagna dṛṣṭīgahaneṣu nityamastīti nāstīti tathāsti nāsti /
children.translated_text: Attached to the thickets of views, always [thinking] 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' 'thus it exists,' 'thus it does not exist,'

children.text: dvāṣaṣṭi dṛṣṭīkṛta niśrayitvā asanta bhāvaṃ parigṛhya te sthitāḥ // Saddhp_2.65 //
children.translated_text: having relied upon sixty-two views, they stand grasping the unreal as real. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.65 ||

children.text: duḥśodhakā mānina dambhinaśca vaṅkāḥ śaṭhā alpaśrutāśca bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hard to purify, conceited, deceitful, crooked, treacherous, of little learning, and foolish —

children.text: te naiva śṛṇvanti subuddhaghoṣaṃ kadāci pi jātisahasrakoṭiṣu // Saddhp_2.66 //
children.translated_text: they never hear the beautiful sound of the <s>Buddha</s>, even in thousands of millions of births. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.66 ||

children.text: teṣāmahaṃ śārisutā upāyaṃ vadāmi duḥkhasya karotha antam /
children.translated_text: For them, O son of <s>Śāri</s>, I speak skillful means: 'Make an end of suffering!';

children.text: duḥkhena saṃpīḍita dṛṣṭva sattvān nirvāṇa tatrāpyupadarśayāmi // Saddhp_2.67 //
children.translated_text: having seen beings oppressed by suffering, I show <s>nirvāṇa</s> even there. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.67 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca bhāṣāmyahu nityanirvṛtā ādipraśāntā imi sarvadharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus I speak: these are always ceased, originally quiescent are all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: caryāṃ ca so pūriya buddhaputro anāgate 'dhvāni jino bhaviṣyati // Saddhp_2.68 //
children.translated_text: and he who has fulfilled the course, a son of the <s>Buddha</s>, shall become a <s>Jina</s> in the future age. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.68 ||

children.text: upāyakauśalya mamaivarūpaṃ yat trīṇi yānānyupadarśayāmi /
children.translated_text: My skillful means is of this kind — that I show three vehicles;

children.text: ekaṃ tu yānaṃ hi nayaśca eka ekā ciyaṃ deśana nāyakānām // Saddhp_2.69 //
children.translated_text: but there is one vehicle alone, one method, and one teaching of the Leaders. || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.69 ||

children.text: vyapanehi kāṅkṣāṃ tatha saṃśayaṃ ca yeṣāṃ ca keṣāṃ ciha kāṅkṣa vidyate /
children.translated_text: Remove doubt and likewise uncertainty — for whomsoever here there may be doubt;

children.text: ananyathāvādina lokanāyakā ekaṃ idaṃ yānu dvitīyu nāsti // Saddhp_2.70 //
children.translated_text: the Lords of the World speak without deviation — this vehicle is one, a second does not exist! || <s>Saddhp</s> 2.70 ||

children.text: ye cāpyabhūvan purimāstathāgatāḥ parinirvṛtā buddhasahasra neke /
children.translated_text: And those former <s>Tathāgatas</s> who passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, many thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: atītamadhvānamasaṃkhyakalpe teṣāṃ pramāṇaṃ na kadāci vidyate // Saddhp_2.71 //
children.translated_text: in past ages, in incalculable <s>kalpas</s> — their measure is never found. [Saddhp 2.71]

children.text: sarvehi tehi puruṣottamehi prakāśitā dharma bahū viśuddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: By all those supreme among men, many pure <s>dharmas</s> were illuminated,

children.text: dṛṣṭāntakaiḥ kāraṇahetubhiśca upāyakauśalyaśatairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_2.72 //
children.translated_text: through parables, reasons and causes, and through innumerable hundreds of skillful means. [Saddhp 2.72]

body.text: sarve ca te darśayi ekayānamekaṃ ca yānaṃ avatārayanti /
body.translated_text: And all of them showed the one vehicle, and they caused [beings] to enter into the one vehicle;

body.text: ekasmi yāne paripācayanti acintiyā prāṇisahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_2.73 //
body.translated_text: in the one vehicle they matured inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings. [Saddhp 2.73]

children.text: anye upāyā vividhā jinānāṃ yehī prakāśentimamagradharmam /
children.translated_text: Various are the skillful means of the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), by which they illuminate this supreme <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: jñātvādhimuktiṃ tatha āśayaṃ ca tathāgatā loki sadevakasmin // Saddhp_2.74 //
children.translated_text: having understood the inclinations and dispositions [of beings] — the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in this world with its gods. [Saddhp 2.74]

children.text: ye cāpi sattvāstahi teṣa saṃmukhaṃ śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ atha vā śrutāvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those beings who, in the presence of those [<s>Buddhas</s>], heard the <s>Dharma</s>, or who were learned,

children.text: dānaṃ ca dattaṃ caritaṃ ca śīlaṃ kṣāntyā ca saṃpādita sarvacaryāḥ // Saddhp_2.75 //
children.translated_text: and who gave gifts and practiced moral discipline, and who accomplished all practices through patience, [Saddhp 2.75]

children.text: vīryeṇa dhyānena kṛtādhikārāḥ prajñāya vā cintita eti dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: who made efforts through vigor and <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), or who contemplated <s>dharmas</s> through wisdom,

children.text: vividhāni puṇyāni kṛtāni yehi te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.76 //
children.translated_text: who performed various kinds of merit — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.76]

children.text: parinirvṛtānāṃ ca jināna teṣāṃ ye śāsane kecidabhūṣi sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: And of those <s>Jinas</s> who passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, whatever beings were in their teaching,

children.text: kṣāntā ca dāntā ca vinīta tatra te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.77 //
children.translated_text: patient, tamed, and disciplined there — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.77]

children.text: ye cāpi dhātūna karonti pūjāṃ jināna teṣāṃ parinirvṛtānām /
children.translated_text: And those who make offerings to the relics of those <s>Jinas</s> who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: ratnāmayān stūpasahasra nekān suvarṇarūpyasya ca sphāṭikasya // Saddhp_2.78 //
children.translated_text: building many thousands of <s>stūpas</s> made of jewels — of gold, silver, and crystal, [Saddhp 2.78]

children.text: ye cāśmagarbhasya karonti stūpān karketanāmuktamayāṃśca kecit /
children.translated_text: and those who build <s>stūpas</s> of precious stone, and some of <s>karketana</s> and pearl,

children.text: vaiḍūryaśreṣṭhasya tathendranīlān te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.79 //
children.translated_text: of the finest <s>vaidūrya</s> and of <s>indranīla</s> — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.79]

children.text: ye cāpi śaileṣu karonti stūpān ye candanānāmagurusya kecit /
children.translated_text: And those who build <s>stūpas</s> on mountains, and some of sandalwood and <s>aguru</s> (aloewood),

children.text: ye devadārūsya karonti stūpān ye dārusaṃghātamayāṃśca kecit // Saddhp_2.80 //
children.translated_text: and those who build <s>stūpas</s> of <s>devadāru</s> (cedar), and some of wooden construction, [Saddhp 2.80]

children.text: iṣṭāmayān mṛttikasaṃcitān vā prītāśca kurvanti jināna stūpān /
children.translated_text: or of brick or piled-up clay — and those who joyfully make <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: uddiśya ye pāṃsukarāśayo 'pi aṭavīṣu durgeṣu ca kārayanti // Saddhp_2.81 //
children.translated_text: or who build them, even heaps of dust, dedicated [to the <s>Jinas</s>], in forests and in difficult places, [Saddhp 2.81]

children.text: sikatāmayān vā puna kūṭa kṛtvā ye keciduddiśya jināna stūpān /
children.translated_text: or who make peaks of sand, dedicated as <s>stūpas</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: kumārakāḥ krīḍiṣu tatra tatra te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.82 //
children.translated_text: even children at play, here and there — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.82]

children.text: ratnāmayā bimba tathaiva kecid dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those who caused images made of jewels to be made, bearing the form of the thirty-two marks,

children.text: uddiśya kārāpita yehi cāpi te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.83 //
children.translated_text: dedicated [to the <s>Buddhas</s>] — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.83]

children.text: ye saptaratnāmaya tatra kecid ye tāmrikā vā tatha kāṃsikā vā /
children.translated_text: And those who made some of the seven jewels, or of copper, or of bronze,

children.text: kārāpayīṣu sugatāna bimbā te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.84 //
children.translated_text: who caused images of the <s>Sugatas</s> to be made — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.84]

children.text: sīsasya lohasya ca mṛttikāya vā kārāpayīṣu sugatāna vigrahān /
children.translated_text: And those who caused forms of the <s>Sugatas</s> to be made of lead, iron, or clay,

children.text: ye pustakarmāmaya darśanīyāṃste sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.85 //
children.translated_text: or beautiful ones made of stucco — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.85]

children.text: ye citrabhittīṣu karonti vigrahān paripūrṇagātrān śatapuṇyalakṣaṇān /
children.translated_text: And those who make forms on painted walls, complete in limbs, bearing the marks of a hundred merits,

children.text: likhetsvayaṃ cāpi likhāpayedvā te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.86 //
children.translated_text: whether painting themselves or causing others to paint — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.86]

children.text: ye cāpi kecittahi śikṣamāṇāḥ krīḍāratiṃ cāpi vinodayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: And even those who, while in training, amusing themselves in play and sport,

children.text: nakhena kāṣṭhena kṛtāsi vigrahān bhittīṣu puruṣā ca kumārakā vā // Saddhp_2.87 //
children.translated_text: make forms with fingernails or with wood on walls — whether adults or children — [Saddhp 2.87]

body.text: sarve ca te kārūṇikā abhūvan sarve 'pi te tārayi prāṇikoṭyaḥ /
body.translated_text: all of them became compassionate ones; all of them saved <s>koṭis</s> of beings;

body.text: samādapentā bahubodhisatvāṃste sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.88 //
body.translated_text: encouraging many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.88]

children.text: dhātūṣu yaiścāpi tathāgatānāṃ stūpeṣu vā mṛttikavigraheṣu vā /
children.translated_text: And those who offered flowers and incense to the relics of <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: ālekhyabhittīṣvapi pāṃsustūpe puṣpā ca gandhā ca pradatta āsīt // Saddhp_2.89 //
children.translated_text: at <s>stūpas</s>, or at clay images, or at paintings on walls, or at dust-<s>stūpas</s>, [Saddhp 2.89]

children.text: vādyā ca vādāpita yehi tatra bheryo 'tha śaṅkhāḥ paṭahāḥ sughoṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: and those by whom music was played there — drums, conch-shells, and kettle-drums of sweet sound,

children.text: nirnāditā dundubhayaśca yehi pūjāvidhānāya varāgrabodhinām // Saddhp_2.90 //
children.translated_text: and by whom large drums were sounded for the purpose of worshipping the supreme, foremost awakened ones, [Saddhp 2.90]

children.text: vīṇāśca tālā paṇavāśca yehi mṛdaṅga vaṃśā tuṇavā manojñāḥ /
children.translated_text: and <s>vīṇās</s> (lutes), cymbals, and <s>paṇavas</s> (small drums), <s>mṛdaṅgas</s> (drums), flutes, and delightful <s>tuṇavas</s> (pipes),

children.text: ekotsavā vā sukumārakā vā te sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.91 //
children.translated_text: or even single-toned or delicate [instruments] — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.91]

children.text: vādāpitā jhallariyo 'pi yehi jalamaṇḍakā carpaṭamaṇḍakā vā /
children.translated_text: And those by whom <s>jhallarīs</s> (small cymbals) were played, or <s>jalamaṇḍakās</s> or <s>carpaṭamaṇḍakās</s>,

children.text: sugatāna uddiśyatha pūjanārthaṃ gītaṃ sugītaṃ madhuraṃ manojñam // Saddhp_2.92 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of worshipping the <s>Sugatas</s>, with singing — well-sung, sweet, and delightful. [Saddhp 2.92]

children.text: sarve ca te buddha abhūṣi loke kṛtvāna tāṃ bahuvidhadhātupūjām /
children.translated_text: All of them became <s>Buddhas</s> in the world, having made those manifold offerings to the relics;

children.text: kimalpakaṃ pi sugatāna dhātuṣu ekaṃ pi vādāpiya vādyabhāṇḍam // Saddhp_2.93 //
children.translated_text: even a small [offering] to the relics of the <s>Sugatas</s> — even playing a single musical instrument — [Saddhp 2.93]

children.text: puṣpeṇa caikena pi pūjayitvā ālekhyabhittau sugatāna bimbān /
children.translated_text: or worshipping with even a single flower the images of the <s>Sugatas</s> on painted walls,

children.text: vikṣiptacittā pi ca pūjayitvā anupūrva drakṣyanti ca buddhakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_2.94 //
children.translated_text: even worshipping with a distracted mind — they shall gradually see <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. [Saddhp 2.94]

children.text: yaiścāñjalistatra kṛto 'pi stūpe paripūrṇa ekā talasaktikā vā /
children.translated_text: And those who made even a single <s>añjali</s> (salutation) at a <s>stūpa</s>, complete, or even with one hand,

children.text: unnāmitaṃ śīrṣamabhūnmuhūrtamavanāmitaḥ kāyu tathaikavāram // Saddhp_2.95 //
children.translated_text: or who raised their head for a moment, or bowed their body even once — [Saddhp 2.95]

children.text: namo 'stu buddhāya kṛtaikavāraṃ yehī tadā dhātudhareṣu teṣu /
children.translated_text: those who said 'Homage to the <s>Buddha</s>' even once at those reliquary shrines,

children.text: vikṣiptacittairapi ekavāraṃ te sarvi prāptā imamagrabodhim // Saddhp_2.96 //
