children.translated_text: even with distracted minds, even once — all of them attained this supreme awakening. [Saddhp 2.96]

children.text: sugatāna teṣāṃ tada tasmi kāle parinirvṛtānāmatha tiṣṭhatāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Of those <s>Sugatas</s>, at that time,

children.text: ye dharmanāmāpi śruṇiṃsu sattvāste sarvi bodhāya abhūṣi lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_2.97 //
children.translated_text: whether passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> or still living, those beings who heard even the name of the <s>Dharma</s> — all of them became attainers of awakening. [Saddhp 2.97]

children.text: anāgatā pī bahubuddhakoṭyo acintiyā yeṣu pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: And in the future, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, inconceivable, in whom there is no measure —

children.text: te pī jinā uttamalokanāthāḥ prakāśayiṣyanti upāyametam // Saddhp_2.98 //
children.translated_text: they too, the <s>Jinas</s>, the supreme lords of the world, will illuminate this very skillful means. [Saddhp 2.98]

children.text: upāyakauśalyamanantu teṣāṃ bhaviṣyati lokavināyakānām /
children.translated_text: Infinite will be the skillful means of those leaders of the world,

children.text: yenā vineṣyantiha prāṇakoṭyo bauddhasmi jñānasmi anāsravasmin // Saddhp_2.99 //
children.translated_text: by which they will guide <s>koṭis</s> of beings here toward the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, the outflow-free. [Saddhp 2.99]

children.text: eko 'pi sattvo na kadāci teṣāṃ śrutvāna dharmaṃ na bhaveta buddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not even a single being of theirs, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, will fail to become a <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: praṇidhānametaddhi tathāgatānāṃ caritva bodhāya carāpayeyam // Saddhp_2.100 //
children.translated_text: for this is the vow of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'Having practiced the awakening-conduct, I shall lead [others] to practice it.' [Saddhp 2.100]

children.text: dharmāmukhā koṭisahasra neke prakāśayiṣyanti anāgate 'dhve /
children.translated_text: Many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Dharma</s>-doors they will illuminate in the future age,

children.text: upadarśayanto imamekayānaṃ vakṣyanti dharmaṃ hi tathāgatatve // Saddhp_2.101 //
children.translated_text: displaying this one vehicle — they will teach the <s>Dharma</s> in the nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. [Saddhp 2.101]

body.text: sthitikā hi eṣā sada dharmanetrī prakṛtiśca dharmāṇa sadā prabhā[sate] /
body.translated_text: For this is the enduring nature of the <s>Dharma</s>-eye, and the nature of <s>dharmas</s> always shines forth;

body.text: viditva buddhā dvipadānamuttamā prakāśayiṣyanti mamekayānam // Saddhp_2.102 //
body.translated_text: knowing this, the <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme among bipeds, will illuminate my one vehicle. [Saddhp 2.102]

children.text: dharmasthitiṃ dharmaniyāmatāṃ ca nityasthitāṃ loki imāmakampyām /
children.translated_text: The stability of <s>Dharma</s>, the fixed order of <s>Dharma</s>, eternally established in this world, unshakeable —

children.text: buddhāśca bodhiṃ pṛthivīya maṇḍe prakāśayiṣyanti upāyakauśalam // Saddhp_2.103 //
children.translated_text: and awakening on the seat of the earth — the <s>Buddhas</s> will illuminate this skillful means. [Saddhp 2.103]

children.text: daśasū diśāsū naradevapūjitāstiṣṭhanti buddhā yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the ten directions, honored by gods and humans, the <s>Buddhas</s> abide, [numerous] like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: sukhāpanārthaṃ iha sarvaprāṇināṃ te cāpi bhāṣantimamagrabodhim // Saddhp_2.104 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of bringing happiness to all beings here, they too teach this supreme awakening. [Saddhp 2.104]

children.text: upāyakauśalya prakāśayanti vividhāni yānānyupadarśayanti /
children.translated_text: They illuminate skillful means and display various vehicles,

children.text: ekaṃ ca yānaṃ paridīpayanti buddhā imāmuttamaśāntabhūmim // Saddhp_2.105 //
children.translated_text: yet it is one vehicle that the <s>Buddhas</s> elucidate — this supreme, peaceful stage. [Saddhp 2.105]

children.text: caritaṃ ca te jāniya sarvadehināṃ yathāśayaṃ yacca purā niṣevitam /
children.translated_text: And they know the conduct of all embodied beings, their dispositions, and what was formerly practiced;

children.text: vīryaṃ ca sthāmaṃ ca viditva teṣāṃ jñātvādhimuktiṃ ca prakāśayanti // Saddhp_2.106 //
children.translated_text: knowing their vigor, strength, and inclinations, they illuminate [the <s>Dharma</s>]. [Saddhp 2.106]

children.text: dṛṣṭāntahetūn bahu darśayanti bahukāraṇān jñānabalena nāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: They show many parables and reasons, many causes, through the power of knowledge, these Leaders;

children.text: nānādhimuktāṃśca viditva sattvān nānābhinirhārupadarśayanti // Saddhp_2.107 //
children.translated_text: knowing beings of various inclinations, they display various manifestations. [Saddhp 2.107]

children.text: ahaṃ pi caitarhi jinendranāyako utpanna sattvāna sukhāpanārtham /
children.translated_text: I too, at this time, the supreme leader among <s>Jinas</s>, have arisen for the sake of bringing happiness to beings;

children.text: saṃdarśayāmī ima buddhabodhiṃ nānābhinirhārasahasrakoṭibhiḥ // Saddhp_2.108 //
children.translated_text: I display this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening through thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of various manifestations. [Saddhp 2.108]

children.text: deśemi dharmaṃ ca bahuprakāraṃ adhimuktimadhyāśaya jñātva prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: I teach the <s>Dharma</s> in many ways, knowing the inclinations and dispositions of beings;

children.text: saṃharṣayāmī vividhairupāyaiḥ pratyātmikaṃ jñānabalaṃ mamaitat // Saddhp_2.109 //
children.translated_text: I bring joy through various skillful means — this is my own power of knowledge. [Saddhp 2.109]

body.text: ahaṃ pi paśyāmi daridrasattvān prajñāya puṇyehi ca viprahīṇān /
body.translated_text: I too see wretched beings, bereft of wisdom and merit,

body.text: praskanna saṃsāri niruddha durge magnāḥ punarduḥkhaparaṃparāsu // Saddhp_2.110 //
body.translated_text: fallen into <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), blocked in a difficult place, immersed in continuous suffering. [Saddhp 2.110]

children.text: tṛṣṇāvilagnāṃścamarīva bāle kāmairihāndhīkṛta sarvakālam /
children.translated_text: Clinging to craving like a yak to its tail, the childish, blinded by desires at all times —

children.text: na buddhameṣanti mahānubhāvaṃ na dharma mārganti dukhāntagāminam // Saddhp_2.111 //
children.translated_text: they do not seek the <s>Buddha</s> of great power, nor do they seek the <s>Dharma</s> that leads to the end of suffering. [Saddhp 2.111]

children.text: gatīṣu ṣaṭsu pariruddhacittāḥ kudṛṣṭidṛṣṭīṣu sthitā akampyāḥ /
children.translated_text: With minds confined in the six destinies, firmly established in evil views, unshakeable —

children.text: duḥkhātu duḥkhānupradhāvamānāḥ kāruṇya mahyaṃ balavantu teṣu // Saddhp_2.112 //
children.translated_text: from suffering rushing toward suffering — my compassion is mighty for them. [Saddhp 2.112]

children.text: so 'haṃ viditvā tahi bodhimaṇḍe saptāha trīṇi paripūrṇa saṃsthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: So I, having understood [this] at the seat of awakening, remained there for three full weeks,

children.text: arthaṃ vicintemimamevarūpaṃ ullokayan pādapameva tatra // Saddhp_2.113 //
children.translated_text: contemplating this very matter, gazing upon that very tree. [Saddhp 2.113]

children.text: prekṣāmi taṃ cānimiṣaṃ drumendraṃ tasyaiva heṣṭhe anucaṃkramāmi /
children.translated_text: I gaze upon that king of trees with unblinking eyes, and walk back and forth beneath it;

children.text: āścaryajñānaṃ ca idaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ sattvāśca mohāndha avidvasū ime // Saddhp_2.114 //
children.translated_text: this wondrous knowledge is distinguished — yet these beings are blind with delusion and ignorant. [Saddhp 2.114]

children.text: brahmā ca māṃ yācati tasmi kāle śakraśca catvāri ca lokapālāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> entreats me at that time, and <s>Śakra</s>, and the four world-guardians,

children.text: maheśvaro īśvara eva cāpi marudgaṇānāṃ ca sahasrakoṭayaḥ // Saddhp_2.115 //
children.translated_text: <s>Maheśvara</s> and <s>Īśvara</s> himself, and thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of hosts of <s>Maruts</s> (storm-gods). [Saddhp 2.115]

children.text: kṛtāñjalī sarvi sthitāḥ sagauravā arthaṃ ca cintemi kathaṃ karomi /
children.translated_text: All standing with joined palms, reverently — and I contemplate the matter: 'What shall I do?'

children.text: ahaṃ ca bodhīya vadāmi varṇān ime ca duḥkhairabhibhūta sattvāḥ // Saddhp_2.116 //
children.translated_text: I would speak the praises of awakening, yet these beings are overwhelmed by suffering. [Saddhp 2.116]

children.text: te mahya dharmaṃ kṣipi bālabhāṣitaṃ kṣipitva gaccheyurapāyabhūmim /
children.translated_text: They would quickly reject my <s>Dharma</s>, calling it childish talk; and having rejected it, they would go to the lower realms.

children.text: śreyo mamā naiva kadāci bhāṣituṃ adyaiva me nirvṛtirastu śāntā // Saddhp_2.117 //
children.translated_text: It would be better for me never to speak at all — let my <s>nirvāṇa</s> be today, peaceful! [Saddhp 2.117]

children.text: purimāṃśca buddhān samanusmaranto upāyakauśalyu yathā ca teṣām /
children.translated_text: But remembering the former <s>Buddhas</s>, and their skillful means —

children.text: yaṃ nūna haṃ pi ima buddhabodhiṃ tridhā vibhajyeha prakāśayeyam // Saddhp_2.118 //
children.translated_text: 'What if I too should illuminate this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening, dividing it into three?' [Saddhp 2.118]

children.text: evaṃ ca me cintitu eṣa dharmo ye cānye buddhā daśasu ddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Thus, as I contemplated this <s>Dharma</s>, those other <s>Buddhas</s> in the ten directions

children.text: darśiṃsu te mahya tadātmabhāvaṃ sādhuṃ ti ghoṣaṃ samudīrayanti // Saddhp_2.119 //
children.translated_text: showed me their own forms, uttering the cry 'Excellent!' [Saddhp 2.119]

children.text: sādhū mune lokavināyakāgra anuttaraṃ jñānamihādhigamya /
children.translated_text: 'Excellent, O sage, foremost leader of the world! Having attained this unsurpassed knowledge,

children.text: upāyakauśalyu vicintayanto anuśikṣase lokavināyakānām // Saddhp_2.120 //
children.translated_text: you contemplate skillful means, following the [example of] the leaders of the world. [Saddhp 2.120]

children.text: vayaṃ pi buddhāya paraṃ tadā padaṃ tṛdhā ca kṛtvāna prakāśayāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'We too, at that supreme stage of <s>Buddhahood</s>, divide it into three and illuminate it;

children.text: hīnādhimuktā hi avidvasū narā bhaviṣyathā buddha na śraddadheyuḥ // Saddhp_2.121 //
children.translated_text: for beings of inferior inclinations and ignorant — they would not believe in <s>Buddhahood</s> [directly]. [Saddhp 2.121]

children.text: tato vayaṃ kāraṇasaṃgraheṇa upāyakauśalya niṣevamāṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore we, through the method of reasoning, employing skillful means,

children.text: phalābhilāṣaṃ parikīrtayantaḥ samādapemo bahubodhisattvān // Saddhp_2.122 //
children.translated_text: proclaiming the desire for fruits, encourage many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.' [Saddhp 2.122]

children.text: ahaṃ cudagrastada āsi śrutvā ghoṣaṃ manojñaṃ puruṣarṣabhāṇām /
children.translated_text: And I was elated then, having heard the delightful cry of those bulls among men;

children.text: udagracitto bhaṇi teṣa tāyināṃ na mohavādī pravarā maharṣī // Saddhp_2.123 //
children.translated_text: with an elated mind, I said to those Protectors: 'The supreme great sages are not speakers of delusion.' [Saddhp 2.123]

children.text: ahaṃ pi evaṃ samudācariṣye yathā vadantī vidu lokanāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I too shall act just as the wise leaders of the world say;

children.text: ahaṃ pi saṃkṣobhi imasmi dāruṇe utpanna sattvāna kaṣāyamadhye // Saddhp_2.124 //
children.translated_text: I too was born in turmoil, in the midst of beings in a defiled age.' [Saddhp 2.124]

body.text: tato hyahaṃ śārisutā viditvā vārāṇasīṃ prasthitu tasmi kāle /
body.translated_text: Then, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, having understood [this], I set out for <s>Vārāṇasī</s> at that time;

body.text: tahi pañcakānāṃ pravadāmi bhikṣuṇāṃ dharmaṃ upāyena praśāntabhūmim // Saddhp_2.125 //
body.translated_text: there, to the five monks, I taught the <s>Dharma</s> through skillful means — the peaceful stage. [Saddhp 2.125]

children.text: tataḥ pravṛttaṃ mama dharmacakraṃ nirvāṇaśabdaśca abhūṣi loke /
children.translated_text: Then my <s>Dharma</s>-wheel was set in motion, and the word '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' came into being in the world;

children.text: arhantaśabdastatha dharmaśabdaḥ saṃghasya śabdaśca abhūṣi tatra // Saddhp_2.126 //
children.translated_text: and the word '<s>Arhat</s>' and the word '<s>Dharma</s>' and the word '<s>Saṃgha</s>' came into being there. [Saddhp 2.126]

children.text: bhāṣāmi varṣāṇi analpakāni nirvāṇabhūmiṃ cupadarśayāmi /
children.translated_text: For not a few years I have taught, displaying the stage of <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: saṃsāraduḥkhasya ca eṣa anto evaṃ vadāmī ahu nityakālam // Saddhp_2.127 //
children.translated_text: and this is the end of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> — thus do I always declare." [Saddhp 2.127]

children.text: yasmiṃśca kāle ahu śāriputra paśyāmi putrān dvipadottamānām /
children.translated_text: "And at whatever time, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, I see the sons of the Supreme among Bipeds,

children.text: ye prasthitā uttamamagrabodhiṃ koṭīsahasrāṇi analpakāni // Saddhp_2.128 //
children.translated_text: those who have set forth toward supreme awakening — not a few, [but] thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, [Saddhp 2.128]

children.text: upasaṃkramitvā ca mamaiva antike kṛtāñjalīḥ sarvi sthitāḥ sagauravāḥ /
children.translated_text: having approached my presence, all standing with joined palms, respectful,

children.text: yehī śruto dharma jināna āsīt upāyakauśalyu bahuprakāram // Saddhp_2.129 //
children.translated_text: who have heard the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s> — skillful means of many kinds, [Saddhp 2.129]

children.text: tato mamā etadabhūṣi tatkṣaṇaṃ samayo mamā bhāṣitumagradharmam /
children.translated_text: then this thought occurs to me at that very moment: the time has come for me to teach the supreme <s>Dharma</s> —

children.text: yasyāhamarthaṃ iha loki jātaḥ prakāśayāmī tamihāgrabodhim // Saddhp_2.130 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of which I was born here in the world; I shall proclaim here that supreme awakening. [Saddhp 2.130]

children.text: duḥśraddadhaṃ etu bhaviṣyate 'dya nimittasaṃjñāniha bālabuddhinām /
children.translated_text: It will be hard to believe today — this perception of signs for the childish-minded,

children.text: adhimānaprāptāna avidvasūnāṃ ime tu śroṣyanti hi bodhisattvāḥ // Saddhp_2.131 //
children.translated_text: for the conceited and the ignorant; but these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will hear. [Saddhp 2.131]

children.text: viśāradaścāhu tadā prahṛṣṭaḥ saṃlīyanāṃ sarva vivarjayitvā /
children.translated_text: And I, confident and delighted then, having set aside all timidity,

children.text: bhāṣāmi madhye sugatātmajānāṃ tāṃścaiva bodhāya samādapemi // Saddhp_2.132 //
children.translated_text: speak in the midst of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>, and bring those very ones to maturity for awakening. [Saddhp 2.132]

children.text: saṃdṛśya caitādṛśabuddhaputrāṃstavāpi kāṅkṣā vyapanīta bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Buddha</s>-sons of such a kind, your doubt too shall be removed;

children.text: ye cā śatā dvādaśime anāsravā buddhā bhaviṣyantimi loki sarve // Saddhp_2.133 //
children.translated_text: these twelve hundred who are without outflows — all of them shall become <s>Buddhas</s> in this world. [Saddhp 2.133]

children.text: yathaiva teṣāṃ purimāṇa tāyināṃ anāgatānāṃ ca jināna dharmatā /
children.translated_text: Just as it is the nature of those former Protectors and of the <s>Jinas</s> yet to come,

children.text: mamāpi eṣaiva vikalpavarjitā tathaiva haṃ deśayi adya tubhyam // Saddhp_2.134 //
children.translated_text: so too is mine, free from conceptualization — thus do I teach you today. [Saddhp 2.134]

children.text: kadāci kahiṃci kathaṃci loke utpādu bhoti puruṣarṣabhāṇām /
children.translated_text: Rarely, somewhere, somehow, in the world, does the arising of the Bulls among Men occur;

children.text: utpadya cā loki anantacakṣuṣaḥ kadācidetādṛśu dharma deśayuḥ // Saddhp_2.135 //
children.translated_text: and having arisen in the world, those of infinite vision rarely teach such <s>Dharma</s>. [Saddhp 2.135]

children.text: sudurlabho īdṛśu agradharmaḥ kalpāna koṭīnayutairapi syāt /
children.translated_text: Such a supreme <s>Dharma</s> is extremely rare — even in <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sudurlabhā īdṛśakāśca sattvāḥ śratvāna ye śraddadhi agradharmam // Saddhp_2.136 //
children.translated_text: and such beings are extremely rare — those who, having heard, have faith in the supreme <s>Dharma</s>. [Saddhp 2.136]

children.text: audumbaraṃ puṣpa yathaiva durlabhaṃ kadāci kahiṃci kathaṃci dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>udumbara</s> flower is rare — rarely, somewhere, somehow, it is seen,

children.text: manojñarūpaṃ ca janasya tadbhavedāścaryu lokasya sadevakasya // Saddhp_2.137 //
children.translated_text: and it would be beautiful in form and pleasing to people — a wonder for the world together with the <s>devas</s>. [Saddhp 2.137]

children.text: ataśca āścaryataraṃ vadāmi śrutvāna yo dharmamimaṃ subhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: And I declare something even more wondrous than that: whoever, having heard this well-spoken <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: anumodi ekaṃ pi bhaṇeya vācaṃ kṛta sarvabuddhāna bhaveya pūjā // Saddhp_2.138 //
children.translated_text: rejoices and speaks even a single word — [by that] worship of all <s>Buddhas</s> would be accomplished. [Saddhp 2.138]

children.text: vyapanehi kāṅkṣāmiha saṃśayaṃ ca ārocayāmi ahu dharmarājā /
children.translated_text: Remove doubt and hesitation here — I, the <s>Dharma</s>-King, declare:

children.text: samādapemi ahamagrabodhau na śrāvakāḥ kecidihāsti mahyam // Saddhp_2.139 //
children.translated_text: I bring [beings] to maturity in supreme awakening — I have no <s>Śrāvakas</s> here whatsoever. [Saddhp 2.139]

body.text: tava śāriputraitu rahasyu bhotu ye cāpi me śrāvaka mahya sarve /
body.translated_text: Let this, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, be your secret, and [the secret] of all my <s>Śrāvakas</s>;

body.text: ye bodhisattvāśca ime pradhānā rahasyametanmama dhārayantu // Saddhp_2.140 //
body.translated_text: and these foremost <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — let them retain this secret of mine. [Saddhp 2.140]

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ pañcakaṣāyakāle kṣudrāśca duṣṭāśca bhavanti sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: For what reason? In the age of the five corruptions, beings are petty and wicked,

children.text: kāmairihāndhīkṛta bālabuddhayo na teṣa bodhāya kadāci cittam // Saddhp_2.141 //
children.translated_text: blinded here by desires, of childish intelligence — they never have a thought toward awakening. [Saddhp 2.141]

children.text: śrutvā ca yānaṃ mama etadekaṃ prakāśitaṃ tena jinena āsīt /
children.translated_text: And having heard this single vehicle of mine, [which] was proclaimed by that <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: anāgate 'dhvāni bhrameyu sattvāḥ sūtraṃ kṣipitvā narakaṃ vrajeyuḥ // Saddhp_2.142 //
children.translated_text: beings in the future would go astray, and having rejected the sūtra, would go to hell. [Saddhp 2.142]

children.text: lajjī śucī ye ca bhaveyu sattvāḥ saṃprasthitā uttamamagrabodhim /
children.translated_text: But for those beings who would be modest and pure, set forth toward supreme awakening,

children.text: viśārado bhūtva vademi teṣāmekasya yānasya anantavarṇān // Saddhp_2.143 //
children.translated_text: being confident, I speak to them the infinite praises of the one vehicle. [Saddhp 2.143]

children.text: etādṛśī deśana nāyakānāmupāyakauśalyamidaṃ variṣṭham /
children.translated_text: Such is the teaching of the Guides — this is the supreme skill in means,

children.text: bahūhi saṃdhāvacanehi coktaṃ durbodhyametaṃ hi aśikṣitehi // Saddhp_2.144 //
children.translated_text: spoken in many intentional statements — it is hard to understand by the untrained. [Saddhp 2.144]

children.text: tasmāddhi saṃdhāvacanaṃ vijāniyā buddhāna lokācariyāṇa tāyinām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should understand the intentional statements of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the World-Teachers, the Protectors;

children.text: jahitva kāṅkṣāṃ vijahitva saṃśayaṃ bhaviṣyathā buddha janetha harṣam // Saddhp_2.145 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned doubt and having discarded hesitation, you shall become <s>Buddhas</s> — generate joy!" [Saddhp 2.145]

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye upāyakauśalyaparivarto nāma dvitīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second chapter, named the Chapter on Skillful Means, in the <s>dharma</s>-discourse of the Noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_3: aupamyaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 3: The Chapter on Parables.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputrastasyāṃ velāyāṃ tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavato 'bhimukho bhagavantameva vyavalokayamāno bhagavantametadavocat - āścaryādbhutaprāpto 'smi bhagavan audbilyaprāptaḥ idamevaṃrūpaṃ bhagavato 'ntikād ghoṣaṃ śrutvā | tatkasya hetoḥ? aśrutvaiva tāvadahaṃ bhagavan idamevaṃrūpaṃ bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ tadanyān bodhisattvān dṛṣṭvā bodhisattvānāṃ ca anāgate 'dhvani buddhanāma śrutvā atīva śocāmi atīva saṃtapye, bhraṣṭo 'smyevaṃrūpāt tathāgatajñānagocarād jñānadarśanāt | yadā cāhaṃ bhagavan abhīkṣṇaṃ gacchāmi parvatagirikandarāṇi vanaṣaṇḍānyārāmanadīvṛkṣamūlānyekāntāni divāvihārāya, tadāpyahaṃ bhagavan yadbhūyastvena anenaiva vihāreṇa viharāmi | tulye nāma dharmadhātupraveśe vayaṃ bhagavatā hīnena yānena niryātitāḥ | evaṃ ca me bhagavaṃstasmin samaye bhavati - asmākamevaiṣo 'parādhaḥ, naiva bhagavato 'parādhaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? sacedbhagavānasmābhiḥ pratīkṣitaḥ syāt sāmutkarṣikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kathayamānaḥ, yadidamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya, teṣveva vayaṃ bhagavan dharmeṣu niryātāḥ syāma | yatpunarbhagavan asmābhiranupasthiteṣu bodhisattveṣu saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ bhagavato 'jānamānaistvaramāṇaiḥ prathamabhāṣitaiva tathāgatasya dharmadeśanā śrutvodgṛhītā dhāritā bhāvitā cintitā manasikṛtā | so 'haṃ bhagavan ātmaparibhāṣaṇayaiva bhūyiṣṭhena rātriṃdivānyatināmayāmi | adyāsmi bhagavan nirvāṇaprāptaḥ | adyāsmi bhagavan parinirvṛtaḥ | adya me bhagavan arhattvaṃ prāptam | adyāhaṃ bhagavan bhagavataḥ putro jyeṣṭha auraso mukhato jāto dharmajo dharmanirmito dharmadāyādo dharmanirvṛttaḥ | apagataparidāho 'smyadya bhagavan imamevaṃrūpamadbhutadharmamaśrutapūrvaṃ bhagavato 'ntikād ghoṣaṃ śrutvā ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time, joyful, elated, delighted, glad, filled with delight and satisfaction, bowing with joined palms toward the Blessed One, facing the Blessed One, gazing upon the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: "I am struck with wonder and amazement, Blessed One! I have attained exultation upon hearing such a proclamation from the Blessed One! Why? Because, Blessed One, before hearing such <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One, upon seeing other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and hearing the name '<s>Buddha</s>' [applied] to <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in the future, I would grieve exceedingly, I would be tormented — 'I have fallen from such a domain of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, from [such] knowledge and vision!' And whenever I, Blessed One, would frequently go to mountain caves and forest groves, to solitary parks, river banks, and tree-roots for daytime dwelling, even then, Blessed One, I would most often dwell with this very dwelling: 'Having entered the same <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of <s>Dharma</s>), we have been led forth by the Blessed One with an inferior vehicle!' And this, Blessed One, would occur to me at that time: 'This is our own fault, not the fault of the Blessed One.' Why? For if the Blessed One had been waited upon by us while giving the teaching that leads upward — concerning unsurpassed perfect awakening — we, Blessed One, would have been led forth in those very <s>dharmas</s>. But since, Blessed One, not understanding that this was the Blessed One's intentional speech, we, in the absence of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in haste, heard, took up, retained, cultivated, reflected on, and attended to the very first teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore I, Blessed One, spent nights and days mostly in self-reproach. Today, Blessed One, I have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>! Today, Blessed One, I have attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! Today, Blessed One, I have attained <s>Arhatship</s>! Today, Blessed One, I am the eldest son of the Blessed One, born from his breast, born from his mouth, born from the <s>Dharma</s>, formed by the <s>Dharma</s>, heir of the <s>Dharma</s>, produced by the <s>Dharma</s>! My burning is gone today, Blessed One, having heard from the Blessed One this wonderful <s>Dharma</s> of such a form, never heard before!"

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputrastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantamābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time, addressed the Blessed One with these verses:

children.text: āścaryaprāpto 'smi mahāvināyaka audbilyajāto imu ghoṣa śrutvā /
children.translated_text: "I have been struck with wonder, O Great Guide! I have attained exultation upon hearing this proclamation.

children.text: kathaṃkathā mahya na bhūya kācit paripācito 'haṃ iha agrayāne // Saddhp_3.1 //
children.translated_text: No doubt whatsoever remains for me — I have been matured in the foremost vehicle. [Saddhp 3.1]

children.text: āścaryabhūtaḥ sugatāna ghoṣaḥ kāṅkṣāṃ ca śokaṃ ca jahāti prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: Wondrous is the proclamation of the <s>Sugatas</s>; it removes the doubt and grief of beings.

children.text: kṣīṇāsravasyo mama yaśca śoko vigato 'sti sarvaṃ śruṇiyāna ghoṣam // Saddhp_3.2 //
children.translated_text: For me whose outflows are destroyed, all grief is gone upon hearing the proclamation. [Saddhp 3.2]

body.text: divāvihāramanucaṃkramanto vanaṣaṇḍa ārāmatha vṛkṣamūlam /
body.translated_text: During daytime dwelling, walking about in forest groves, parks, and tree-roots,

body.text: girikandarāṃścāupyupasevamāno anucintayāmī imameva cintām // Saddhp_3.3 //
body.translated_text: and frequenting mountain caves — I would ponder this very thought: [Saddhp 3.3]

children.text: aho 'smi parivañcitu pāpacittaistulyeṣu dharmeṣu anāsraveṣu /
children.translated_text: 'Alas, I have been deceived by my own evil thoughts! In the same outflow-free <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: yannāma traidhātuki agradharmaṃ na deśayiṣyāmi anāgate 'dhve // Saddhp_3.4 //
children.translated_text: I shall not be able to teach the supreme <s>Dharma</s> of the three realms in the future!' [Saddhp 3.4]

children.text: dvātriṃśatī lakṣaṇa mahya bhraṣṭā suvarṇavarṇacchavitā ca bhraṣṭā /
children.translated_text: The thirty-two marks are lost to me, and the golden-colored skin is lost;

children.text: balā vimokṣāścimi sarvi riñcitā tulyeṣu dharmeṣu aho 'smi mūḍhaḥ // Saddhp_3.5 //
children.translated_text: the powers and liberations — all these are forfeited by me. In the same <s>dharmas</s>, alas, I am deluded! [Saddhp 3.5]

children.text: anuvyañjanā ye ca mahāmunīnāmaśīti pūrṇāḥ pravarā viśiṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text: And the eighty minor marks of the great <s>Munis</s>, full, supreme, and distinguished,

children.text: aṣṭādaśāveṇika ye ca dharmāste cāpi bhraṣṭā ahu vañcito 'smi // Saddhp_3.6 //
children.translated_text: and the eighteen unique <s>dharmas</s> — these too are lost; I have been deceived! [Saddhp 3.6]

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca tvāṃ lokahitānukampī divāvihāraṃ parigamya caikaḥ /
children.translated_text: And seeing you, compassionate benefactor of the world, going alone for daytime dwelling,

children.text: hā vañcito 'smīti vicintayāmi asaṅgajñānātu acintiyātaḥ // Saddhp_3.7 //
children.translated_text: I would think, 'Alas, I have been deceived!' — because of the inconceivable, unattached knowledge. [Saddhp 3.7]

children.text: rātriṃdivāni kṣapayāmi nātha bhūyiṣṭha so eva vicintayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: I spend the nights and days, O Lord, mostly reflecting upon this very [thought];

children.text: pṛcchāmi tāvad bhagavantameva bhraṣṭo 'hamasmītyatha vā na veti // Saddhp_3.8 //
children.translated_text: I shall ask the Blessed One himself — am I lost, or not? [Saddhp 3.8]

children.text: evaṃ ca me cintayato jinendra gacchanti rātriṃdiva nityakālam /
children.translated_text: And as I reflect thus, O Lord of Conquerors, the nights and days pass by constantly.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca anyān bahubodhisattvān saṃvarṇitāṃllokavināyakena // Saddhp_3.9 //
children.translated_text: And seeing many other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> praised by the Guide of the World, [Saddhp 3.9]

children.text: śrutvā ca so 'haṃ imu buddhadharmaṃ saṃghāya etatkila bhāṣitaṃ ti /
children.translated_text: and hearing this <s>Buddha</s>-<s>Dharma</s> — thinking, 'This was spoken for the <s>Saṅgha</s>,' —

children.text: atarkikaṃ sūkṣmamanāsravaṃ ca jñānaṃ praṇetī jina bodhimaṇḍe // Saddhp_3.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> leads [beings] to knowledge that is beyond reasoning, subtle, and without outflows, at the seat of awakening. [Saddhp 3.10]

children.text: dṛṣṭīvilagno hyahamāsi pūrvaṃ parivrājakastīrthikasaṃmataśca /
children.translated_text: For I was formerly attached to views, a wandering ascetic honored by heretical teachers;

children.text: tato mamā āśayu jñātva nātho dṛṣṭīvimokṣāya bravīti nirvṛtim // Saddhp_3.11 //
children.translated_text: then the Lord, having known my disposition, teaches cessation for the liberation from views. [Saddhp 3.11]

children.text: vimucya tā dṛṣṭikṛtāni sarvaśaḥ śūnyāṃśca dharmānahu sparśayitvā /
children.translated_text: Having freed myself from all those view-fabrications entirely, and having touched the empty <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: tato vijānāmyahu nirvṛto 'smi na cāpi nirvāṇamidaṃ pravucyati // Saddhp_3.12 //
children.translated_text: then I know, 'I have attained cessation' — yet this is not called <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [Saddhp 3.12]

children.text: yadā tu buddho bhavate 'grasattvaḥ puraskṛto naramaruyakṣarākṣasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: But when one becomes the supreme being, a <s>Buddha</s>, honored by men, <s>Maras</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and <s>Rākṣasas</s>,

children.text: dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhārī aśeṣato nirvṛtu bhoti tatra // Saddhp_3.13 //
children.translated_text: bearing the form of the thirty-two marks — then there is cessation completely. [Saddhp 3.13]

children.text: vyapanīta sarvāṇi mi manyitāni śrutvā ca ghoṣaṃ ahamadya nirvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: All my conceitful thoughts have been removed; and hearing this proclamation, I am today at peace,

children.text: yadāpi vyākurvasi agrabodhau purato hi lokasya sadevakasya // Saddhp_3.14 //
children.translated_text: when you predict supreme awakening before the world together with the <s>devas</s>. [Saddhp 3.14]

children.text: balavacca āsīnmama chambhitatvaṃ prathamaṃ giraṃ śrutva vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: And there was strong trembling in me at first, hearing the voice of the Guide —

children.text: mā haiva māro sa bhavedviheṭhako abhinirmiṇitvā bhuvi buddhaveṣam // Saddhp_3.15 //
children.translated_text: lest this be <s>Māra</s>, a tormentor, having manifested the appearance of a <s>Buddha</s> on earth! [Saddhp 3.15]

children.text: yadā tu hetūhi ca kāraṇaiśca dṛṣṭāntakoṭīnayutaiśca darśitā /
children.translated_text: But when through reasons and causes, and through <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of examples, it was shown —

children.text: suparisthitā sā varabuddhabodhistato 'smi niṣkāṅkṣu śruṇitva dharmam // Saddhp_3.16 //
children.translated_text: that supreme <s>Buddha</s>-awakening is well-established — then I am free from doubt, hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. [Saddhp 3.16]

children.text: yadā ca me buddhasahasrakoṭyaḥ kīrteṣyatī tān parinirvṛtān jinān /
children.translated_text: When he shall celebrate the thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: yathā ca tairdeśitu eṣa dharma upāyakauśalya pratiṣṭhihitvā // Saddhp_3.17 //
children.translated_text: and how they taught this <s>Dharma</s>, having established skillful means, [Saddhp 3.17]

body.text: anāgatāśco bahu buddha loke tiṣṭhanti ye co paramārthadarśinaḥ /
body.translated_text: and the many <s>Buddhas</s> yet to come who stand in the world, seers of the ultimate truth —

body.text: upāyakauśalyaśataiśca dharmaṃ nidarśayiṣyantyatha deśayanti ca // Saddhp_3.18 //
body.translated_text: they too shall demonstrate and teach the <s>Dharma</s> through hundreds of skillful means, [Saddhp 3.18]

children.text: tathā ca te ātmana yādṛśī carī abhiniṣkramitvā prabhṛtīya saṃstutā /
children.translated_text: and likewise, their own conduct, of whatever kind, praised from the time of going forth onward —

children.text: buddhaṃ ca te yādṛśu dharmacakraṃ tathā ca te 'vasthita dharmadeśanā // Saddhp_3.19 //
children.translated_text: and whatever kind of <s>Dharma</s>-wheel of those <s>Buddhas</s>, and how they stand in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching — [Saddhp 3.19]

children.text: tataśca jānāmi na eṣa māro bhūtāṃ cariṃ darśayi lokanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: then I know, this is not <s>Māra</s> — the Lord of the World has shown the true conduct.

children.text: na hyatra mārāṇa gatī hi vidyate mamaiva cittaṃ vicikitsaprāptam // Saddhp_3.20 //
children.translated_text: The path of <s>Māras</s> is not found here — it was my own mind that had reached doubt. [Saddhp 3.20]

children.text: yadā tu madhureṇa gabhīravalgunā saṃharṣito buddhasvareṇa cāham /
children.translated_text: But when I was gladdened by the sweet, profound, and pleasant voice of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: tadā mi vidhvaṃsita sarvasaṃśayā vicikitsa naṣṭā ca sthito 'smi jñāne // Saddhp_3.21 //
children.translated_text: then all my doubt was shattered, and my uncertainty destroyed — I stand in knowledge. [Saddhp 3.21]

children.text: niḥsaṃśayaṃ bheṣyi tathāgato 'haṃ puraskṛto loki sadevake 'smin /
children.translated_text: Without doubt, I shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, honored in this world together with the <s>devas</s>;

children.text: saṃghāya vakṣye imu buddhabodhiṃ samādapento bahubodhisattvān // Saddhp_3.22 //
children.translated_text: I shall teach this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening to the <s>Saṅgha</s>, bringing many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> to maturity. [Saddhp 3.22]

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - ārocayāmi te śāriputra, prativedayāmi te asya sadevakasya lokasya purataḥ samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ purataḥ | mayā tvaṃ śāriputra viṃśatīnāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmantike paripācito 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | mama ca tvaṃ śāriputra dīrgharātramanuśikṣito 'bhūt | sa tvaṃ śāriputra bodhisattvasaṃmantritena bodhisattvarahasyena iha mama pravacane upapannaḥ | sa tvaṃ śāriputra bodhisattvādhiṣṭhānena tatpaurvakaṃ caryāpraṇidhānaṃ bodhisattvasaṃmantritaṃ bodhisattvarahasyaṃ na samanusmarasi | nirvṛto 'smīti manyase | so 'haṃ tvāṃ śāriputra pūrvacaryāpraṇidhānajñānānubodhamanusmārayitukāma imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ saṃprakāśayāmi ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'I announce to you, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I make known to you — before this world with its gods, before [the world] with its <s>Māras</s>, with its <s>Brahmās</s>, before the assembly of ascetics and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. You, <s>Śāriputra</s>, have been matured by me in the presence of twenty <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> for unsurpassed perfect awakening. And you, <s>Śāriputra</s>, have been trained by me through this long night. And you, <s>Śāriputra</s>, by the counseling of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, by the secret of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, have been reborn here in my teaching. And you, <s>Śāriputra</s>, by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s resolve, do not remember that former conduct-and-vow, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-counseling, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-secret. You think: "I have attained cessation." It is I, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who, wishing to remind you of the awakening to the knowledge of your former conduct and vow, illuminate this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — a <s>sūtrānta</s>, a great <s>vaipulya</s>, an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, encompassed by all <s>Buddhas</s> — for the <s>Śrāvakas</s>.'

body.text: api khalu punaḥ śāriputra, bhaviṣyasi tvamanāgate 'dhvani aprameyaiḥ kalpairacintyairapramāṇairbahūnāṃ tathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saddharmaṃ dhārayitvā vividhāṃ ca pūjāṃ kṛtvā imāmeva bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrya padmaprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyasi
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in the future course, after immeasurable, inconceivable, and incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, having upheld the True <s>Dharma</s> of many hundred-thousands of <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and having made various offerings, and having fulfilled this very <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, you shall become in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, named <s>Padmaprabha</s> (Lotus-Light),

body.text: vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān ||
body.translated_text: endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One.'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ śāriputra samayena tasya bhagavataḥ padmaprabhasya tathāgatasya virajaṃ nāma buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ paramasudarśanīyaṃ pariśuddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca ṛddhaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca bahujananārīgaṇākīrṇaṃ ca maruprakīrṇaṃ ca vaiḍūryamayaṃ suvarṇasūtrāṣṭāpadanibaddham | teṣu ca aṣṭāpadeṣu ratnavṛkṣā bhaviṣyanti saptānāṃ ratnānāṃ puṣpaphalaiḥ satatasamitaṃ samarpitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time, the <s>Buddha</s>-field of that Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmaprabha</s>, shall be named <s>Virajā</s> (Stainless) — level, delightful, pleasant, supremely beautiful to behold, pure, prosperous, rich, secure, with abundant food, thronged with many people and women, scattered with divine beings, made of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), bound with golden threads in an eightfold grid. And in those squares there shall be jewel-trees, constantly adorned with flowers and fruits of seven kinds of precious things.'

body.text: so 'pi śāriputra padmaprabhastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastrīṇyeva yānānyārabhya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati | kiṃcāpi śāriputra sa tathāgato na kalpakaṣāya utpatsyate, api tu praṇidhānavaśena dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati | mahāratnapratimaṇḍitaśca nāma śāriputra sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra kena kāraṇena sa kalpo mahāratnapratimaṇḍita ityucyate? ratnāni śāriputra buddhakṣetre bodhisattvā ucyante | te tasmin kāle tasyāṃ virajāyāṃ lokadhātau bahavo bodhisattvā bhaviṣyantyaprameyā asaṃkhyeyā acintyā atulyā amāpyā gaṇanāṃ samatikrāntā anyatra tathāgatagaṇanayā | tena kāraṇena sa kalpo mahāratnapratimaṇḍita ityucyate ||
body.translated_text: 'That <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmaprabha</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, <s>Śāriputra</s>, shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> beginning with three vehicles. Although, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>Tathāgata</s> will not arise in a defiled <s>kalpa</s>, yet by the power of his vow he shall teach the <s>Dharma</s>. And that <s>kalpa</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, shall be named <s>Mahāratnapratimaṇḍita</s> (Adorned with Great Jewels). Why do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>kalpa</s> is called Adorned with Great Jewels? In a <s>Buddha</s>-field, <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are called jewels. Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, at that time, in that <s>Virajā</s> world-realm, shall be many — immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable, immense, beyond counting except by the <s>Tathāgata's</s> calculation. For that reason, that <s>kalpa</s> is called Adorned with Great Jewels.'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ śāriputra samayena bodhisattvāstasmin buddhakṣetre yadbhūyasā ratnapadmavikrāmiṇo bhaviṣyanti | anādikarmikāśca te bodhisattvā bhaviṣyanti | ciracaritakuśalamūlā bahubuddhaśatasahasracīrṇabrahmacaryāḥ, tathāgataparisaṃstutā buddhajñānābhiyuktā mahābhijñāparikarmanirjātāḥ sarvadharmanayakuśalā mārdavāḥ smṛtimantaḥ | bhūyiṣṭhena śāriputra evaṃrūpāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ paripūrṇaṃ tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, at that time, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in that <s>Buddha</s>-field shall for the most part be <s>Ratnapadmavikrāmins</s> (Those Who Stride on Jewel-Lotuses). And those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> shall be of beginningless <s>karma</s> — [that is,] with long-cultivated wholesome roots, who have practiced the holy life under many hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, praised by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, devoted to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, produced through the preparation of great superknowledges, skilled in the method of all <s>dharmas</s>, gentle, and mindful. For the most part, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that <s>Buddha</s>-field shall be filled with <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of such form.'

body.text: tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra padmaprabhasya tathāgatasya dvādaśāntarakalpā āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati sthāpayitvā kumārabhūtatvam | teṣāṃ ca sattvānāmaṣṭāntarakalpā āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | sa ca śāriputra padmaprabhastathāgato dvādaśānāmantarakalpānāmatyayena dhṛtiparipūrṇaṃ nāma bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ vyākṛtya anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau parinirvāsyati | ayaṃ bhikṣavo dhṛtiparipūrṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mamānantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate | padmavṛṣabhavikrāmī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tasyāpi śāriputra padmavṛṣabhavikrāmiṇastathāgatasya evaṃrūpameva buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmaprabha</s> shall be twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, excluding the time of being a prince. And the lifespan of those beings shall be eight intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmaprabha</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, at the end of twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, having given prophecy to a <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Dhṛtiparipūrṇa</s> (Full of Steadfastness) for unsurpassed perfect awakening, shall enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. [He shall say:] "This <s>Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dhṛtiparipūrṇa</s>, O monks, shall attain unsurpassed perfect awakening immediately after me. He shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One in the world named <s>Padmavṛṣabhavikrāmin</s> (Lotus-Bull-Strider), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, a knower of the world, unsurpassed, a tamer of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One." And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmavṛṣabhavikrāmin</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, shall have a <s>Buddha</s>-field of the very same form.'

body.text: tasya khalu punaḥ śāriputra padmaprabhasya tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya dvātriṃśadantarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | tatastasya tasmin saddharme kṣīṇe dvātriṃśadantarakalpān saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthāsyati ||
body.translated_text: 'Furthermore, <s>Śāriputra</s>, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmaprabha</s>, the True <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for thirty-two full intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And then, when that True <s>Dharma</s> has been exhausted, a counterfeit of the True <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for thirty-two intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.'

body.text:
atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
bhaviṣyase śārisutā tuhaṃ pi anāgate 'dhvāni jinastathāgataḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses: 'You too, O son of <s>Śāri</s>, in the future course, shall be a <s>Jina</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>,

body.text: padmaprabho nāma samantacakṣurvineṣyase prāṇisahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_3.23 //
body.translated_text: named <s>Padmaprabha</s>, the All-Seeing One — you shall guide thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of living beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.23 ||

children.text: bahubuddhakoṭīṣu karitva satkriyāṃ caryābalaṃ tatra upārjayitvā /
children.translated_text: Having made worship under <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, having there accumulated the power of [<s>Bodhisattva</s>-]conduct,

children.text: utpādayitvā ca daśo balāni spṛśiṣyase uttamamagrabodhim // Saddhp_3.24 //
children.translated_text: and having generated the ten powers — you shall touch the supreme, foremost awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.24 ||

children.text: acintiye aparimitasmi kalpe prabhūtaratnastada kalpu bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: In an inconceivable, limitless <s>kalpa</s>, that <s>kalpa</s> shall be called 'Abundant Jewels';

children.text: virajā ca nāmnā tada lokadhātuḥ kṣetraṃ viśuddhaṃ dvipadottamasya // Saddhp_3.25 //
children.translated_text: and the world-realm shall be named <s>Virajā</s> — the pure field of the Foremost of Bipeds. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.25 ||

children.text: vaidūryasaṃstīrṇa tathaiva bhūmiḥ suvarṇasūtrapratimaṇḍitā ca /
children.translated_text: The ground there shall be strewn with <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, adorned with golden threads,

children.text: ratnāmayairvṛkṣaśatairupetā sudarśanīyaiḥ phalapuṣpamaṇḍitaiḥ // Saddhp_3.26 //
children.translated_text: furnished with hundreds of jewel-trees, beautiful to behold, decorated with flowers and fruits. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.26 ||

children.text: smṛtimanta tasmin bahubodhisattvāḥ caryābhinirhārasukovidāśca /
children.translated_text: In that [field], many mindful <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, skilled in accomplishing the conduct,

children.text: ye śikṣitā buddhaśateṣu caryāṃ te tatra kṣetre upapadya santi // Saddhp_3.27 //
children.translated_text: who have trained in the conduct under hundreds of <s>Buddhas</s> — they shall be reborn in that field. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.27 ||

children.text: so cejjinaḥ paścimake samucchraye kumārabhūmīmatināmayitvā /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Jina</s>, in his final existence, having passed beyond the stage of prince,

children.text: jahitva kāmānabhiniṣkamitvā spṛśiṣyate uttamamagrabodhim // Saddhp_3.28 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned desires and gone forth — he shall touch the supreme, foremost awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.28 ||

children.text: sama dvādaśā antarakalpa tasya bhaviṣyate āyu tadā jinasya /
children.translated_text: Twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s> — that shall be the lifespan of that <s>Jina</s> at that time;

children.text: manujānapī antarakalpa aṣṭa āyuṣpramāṇaṃ tahi teṣa bheṣyati // Saddhp_3.29 //
children.translated_text: and eight intermediate <s>kalpas</s> for humans — that shall be the measure of their lifespan. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.29 ||

children.text: parinirvṛtasyāpi jinasya tasya dvātriṃśatiṃ antarakalpa pūrṇām /
children.translated_text: Even after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Jina</s>, for thirty-two full intermediate <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: saddharma saṃsthāsyati tasmi kāle hitāya lokasya sadevakasya // Saddhp_3.30 //
children.translated_text: the True <s>Dharma</s> shall endure at that time, for the benefit of the world with its gods. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.30 ||

children.text: saddharmi kṣīṇe pratirūpako 'sya dvātriṃśatī antarakalpa sthāsyati /
children.translated_text: When the True <s>Dharma</s> is exhausted, its counterfeit shall stand for thirty-two intermediate <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: śarīravaistārika tasya tāyinaḥ susatkṛto naramarutaiśca nityam // Saddhp_3.31 //
children.translated_text: the relics of that Protector, widely distributed, shall be honored by humans and gods constantly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.31 ||

children.text: etādṛśaḥ so bhagavān bhaviṣyati prahṛṣṭa tvaṃ śārisutā bhavasva /
children.translated_text: Such shall that Blessed One be — rejoice, O son of <s>Śāri</s>!

children.text: tvameva so tādṛśako bhaviṣyasi anābhibhūto dvipadānamuttamaḥ // Saddhp_3.32 //
children.translated_text: You yourself shall be such — unsurpassed, the highest of bipeds! || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.32 ||

body.text: atha khalu tāścatasraḥ parṣado bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyā āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyedaṃ vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bhagavato 'ntikāt saṃmukhaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasaḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātāḥ svakasvakaiścīvarairbhagavantamabhicchādayāmāsuḥ | śakraśca devānāmindro brahmā ca sahāṃpatiranyāśca devaputraśatasahasrakoṭyo bhagavantaṃ divyairvastrairabhicchādayāmāsuḥ | divyaiśca māndāravairmahāmāndaravaiśca puṣpairabhyavakiranti sma | divyāni ca vastrāṇyuparyantarīkṣe bhrāmayanti sma | divyāni ca tūryaśatasahasrāṇi dundubhayaścoparyantarīkṣe parāhananti sma | mahāntaṃ ca puṣpavarṣamabhipravarṣayitvā evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣante sma - pūrvaṃ bhagavatā vārāṇasyāmṛṣipatane mṛgadāve dharmacakraṃ pravartitam | idaṃ punarbhagavatā adya anuttaraṃ dvitīyaṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartitam | te ca devaputrāstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those four assemblies — monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — having heard this prophecy for the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening, directly from the Blessed One, were delighted, elated, joyful, glad, and filled with pleasure and gladness. Each covered the Blessed One with their own robes. And <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, and <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s>, and other hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>devaputras</s> covered the Blessed One with divine garments, showered him with divine <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, tossed divine garments high in the sky, and divine musical instruments in hundreds of thousands, and drums, sounded high in the sky. And having rained down a great shower of flowers, they spoke these words: 'The Blessed One formerly at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park, turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. And now, today, the Blessed One has turned the second, unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-wheel.' And those <s>devaputras</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: dharmacakraṃ pravartesi loke apratipudgala /
children.translated_text: 'You turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel in the world, O one without rival —

children.text: vārāṇasyāṃ mahāvīra skandhānāmudayaṃ vyayam // Saddhp_3.33 //
children.translated_text: at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, great hero — the arising and passing of the aggregates. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.33 ||

children.text: prathamaṃ pravartitaṃ tatra dvitīyamiha nāyaka /
children.translated_text: That was turned first there; this second [is turned] here, O Guide —

children.text: duḥśraddadheya yasteṣāṃ deśito 'dya vināyaka // Saddhp_3.34 //
children.translated_text: hard to believe is what has been taught today to them, O <s>Vināyaka</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.34 ||

children.text: bahu dharmaḥ śruto 'smābhiarlokanāthasya saṃmukham /
children.translated_text: Much <s>Dharma</s> has been heard by us face to face from the Lord of the World,

children.text: na cāyamīdṛśo dharmaḥ śrutapūrvaḥ kadācana // Saddhp_3.35 //
children.translated_text: yet never has such a <s>Dharma</s> been heard before. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.35 ||

children.text: anumodāma mahāvīra saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ maharṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: We rejoice, O great hero, in the teaching with intended purport of the great sage —

children.text: yathārtho vyākṛto hyeṣa śāriputro viśāradaḥ // Saddhp_3.36 //
children.translated_text: inasmuch as this confident <s>Śāriputra</s> has been given prophecy. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.36 ||

children.text: vayamapyedṛśāḥ syāmo buddhā loke anuttarāḥ /
children.translated_text: May we too become such — unsurpassed <s>Buddhas</s> in the world,

children.text: saṃdhābhāṣyeṇa deśento buddhabodhimanuttarām // Saddhp_3.37 //
children.translated_text: teaching by means of intended purport the unsurpassed <s>Buddhabodhi</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.37 ||

children.text: yacchrutaṃ kṛtamasmābhirasmiṃlloke paratra vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever we have done or heard, in this world or the next,

children.text: ārāgitaśca yadbuddhaḥ prārthanā bhotu bodhaye // Saddhp_3.38 //
children.translated_text: and whatever <s>Buddhas</s> we have pleased — may [all this] be a prayer for awakening!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.38 ||

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān śāriputro bhagavantametadavocat - niṣkāṅkṣo 'smi bhagavan vigatakathaṃkatho bhagavato 'ntikāt saṃmukhamidamātmano vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | yāni ca imāni bhagavan dvādaśa vaśībhūtaśatāni bhagavatā pūrvaṃ śaikṣabhūmau sthāpitāni evamavavaditāni evamanuśiṣṭānyabhūvan etatparyavasāno me bhikṣavo dharmavinayo yadidaṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokasamatikramo nirvāṇasamavasaraṇaḥ | ime ca bhagavan dve bhikṣusahasre śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ bhagavataḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ sarveṣāmātmadṛṣṭibhavadṛṣṭivibhavadṛṣṭisarvadṛṣṭivivarjitānāṃ nirvāṇabhūmisthitāḥ smaḥ ityātmanaḥ saṃjānatām, te bhagavato 'ntikādimamevaṃrūpamaśrutapūrvaṃ dharma śrutvā kathaṃkathāmāpannāḥ | tatsādhu bhagavān bhāṣatāmeṣāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ kaukṛtyavinodanārtha yathā bhagavannetāścatasraḥ parṣado niṣkāṅkṣā nirvicikitsā bhaveyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> spoke this to the Blessed One: 'I am free from doubt, Blessed One, rid of uncertainty, having heard this prophecy of mine face to face from the Blessed One regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening. But these twelve hundred masters, Blessed One, who were formerly established by the Blessed One on the learner's stage, who were thus admonished, thus instructed — [told that] "This is the final conclusion of my <s>Dharma</s>-Vinaya for you monks — namely, the transcendence of birth, old age, sickness, death, and grief, the arrival at <s>nirvāṇa</s>" — and these two thousand monks of the Blessed One's <s>Śrāvakas</s>, both learners and those beyond learning, all of whom are free from the view of self, the view of becoming, the view of annihilation, and all views, and consider themselves as standing on the ground of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — they, having heard this unprecedented <s>Dharma</s> from the Blessed One, have arrived at doubt. Therefore, Blessed One, please speak to these monks for the removal of their remorse, so that, Blessed One, these four assemblies may be free from doubt and uncertainty.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - nanu te mayā śāriputra pūrvamevākhyātaṃ yathā nānābhinirhāranirdeśavividhahetukāraṇanidarśanārambaṇaniruktyupāyakauśalyairnānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāṃ nānādhātvāśayānāmāśayaṃ viditvā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho dharmaṃ deśayati | imāmevānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya sarvadharmadeśanābhirbodhisattvayānameva samādāpayati | api tu khalu punaḥ śāriputra aupamyaṃ te kariṣyāmi asyaivārthasya bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśanārtham | tatkasya hetoḥ? upamayā iha ekatyā vijñapuruṣā bhāṣitasyārthamājānanti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Have I not told you before, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened one, having understood the dispositions of beings with various inclinations and various natures of temperament, through various displays of manifestation, varied expositions of causes and conditions, demonstrations, supports, etymologies, and skillful means, teaches the <s>Dharma</s>? All his <s>Dharma</s>-teachings are precisely for the purpose of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> vehicle, beginning with this very unsurpassed perfect awakening. Moreover, <s>Śāriputra</s>, I shall make a simile for you, for the purpose of showing this very meaning even further. For what reason? Because by means of a simile, certain wise persons understand the meaning of what is spoken.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra iha syāt kasmiṃścideva grāme vā nagare vā nigame vā janapade vā janapadapradeśe vā rāṣṭre vā rājadhānyāṃ vā gṛhapatirjīrṇo vṛddho mahallako 'bhyatītavayo 'nuprāpta āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ | mahaccāsya niveśanaṃ bhaveducchritaṃ ca vistīrṇaṃ ca cirakṛtaṃ ca jīrṇaṃ ca dvayorvā trayāṇāṃ vā caturṇāṃ vā pañcānāṃ vā prāṇiśatānāmāvāsaḥ | ekadvāraṃ ca tanniveśanaṃ bhavet | tṛṇasaṃchannaṃ ca bhavet | vigalitaprāsādaṃ ca bhavet | pūtistambhamūlaṃ ca bhavet | saṃśīrṇakuḍyakaṭalepanaṃ ca bhavet | tacca sahasaiva mahātāgniskandhena sarvapārśveṣu sarvāvantaṃ niveśanaṃ pradīptaṃ bhavet | tasya ca puruṣasya bahavaḥ kumārakāḥ syuḥ pañca vā daśa vā viṃśatirvā | sa ca puruṣastasmānniveśanād bahirnirgataḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: 'Suppose, <s>Śāriputra</s>, in some village, town, market-town, district, provincial territory, kingdom, or royal capital, there were a householder — old, aged, advanced in years, having gone beyond his time — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions. And he would have a great dwelling — lofty, spacious, long-built, and old — a habitation for two, three, four, or five hundred living beings. And that dwelling would have a single door. And it would be covered with thatch. And its upper stories would have crumbled. And the bases of its pillars would be rotten. And its walls, plaster, and coating would be decayed. And that [dwelling] would suddenly be ablaze on all sides with a great mass of fire — the entire dwelling burning. And that man would have many young sons — five, ten, or twenty. And that man would have gone outside that dwelling.'

body.text:
atha khalu śāriputra sa puruṣastaṃ svakaṃ niveśanaṃ mahātāgniskandhena samantāt
saṃprajvalitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhītastrasta udvignacitto bhavet, evaṃ cānuvicintayet - pratibalo 'hamanena mahatāgniskandhenāsaṃspṛṣṭo 'paridagdhaḥ kṣiprameva svastinā asmād gṛhādādīptād dvāreṇa nirgantuṃ nirdhāvitum | api tu ya ime mamaiva putrā bālakāḥ kumārakā asminneva niveśane ādīpte taistaiḥ krīḍanakaiḥ krīḍanti ramanti paricārayanti, imaṃ cāgāramādīptaṃ na jānanti na budhyante na vidanti na cetayanti nodvegamāpadyante, saṃtapyamānā apyanena mahatāgniskandhena mahatā ca duḥkhaskandhena spṛṣṭāḥ samānā na duḥkhaṃ manasi kurvanti, nāpi nirgamanamanasikāramutpādayanti ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that man, upon seeing his own dwelling blazing on all sides with a great mass of fire, would become frightened, terrified, and alarmed in mind, and would reflect thus: "I am able, untouched and unburnt by this great mass of fire, to exit quickly and safely from this burning house through the door. But these my own sons — small children, young boys — in this very burning dwelling, play, amuse themselves, and enjoy themselves with various toys. They do not know, do not understand, do not perceive, do not comprehend this burning house, and do not become alarmed. Being scorched by this great mass of fire, touched by this great mass of suffering, they do not take suffering to heart, nor do they generate the mental intention to escape."'

body.text: sa ca śāriputra puruṣo balavān bhaved bāhubalikaḥ | sa evamanuvicintayet - ahamasmi balavān bāhubalikaśca | yannvahaṃ sarvānimān kumārakānekapiṇḍayitvā utsaṅgenādāya asmād gṛhānnirgamayeyam | sa punarevamanuvicintayet - idaṃ khalu niveśanamekapraveśaṃ saṃvṛtadvārameva | kumārakāścapalāścañcalā bālajātīyāśca | mā haiva paribhrameyuḥ | te 'nena mahatāgniskandhenānayavyasanamāpadyeran | yannūnamahametān saṃcodayayam | iti pratisaṃkhyāya tān kumārakānāmantrayate sma - āgacchata bhavantaḥ kumārakāḥ, nirgacchata | ādīptamidaṃ gṛhaṃ mahatā agniskandhena | mā haivātraiva sarve 'nena mahatāgniskandhena dhakṣyatha, anayavyasanamāpatsyatha | atha khalu te kumārakā evaṃ tasya hitakāmasya puruṣasya tadbhāṣitaṃ nāvabudhyante nodvijanti notrasanti na saṃtrasanti na saṃtrāsamāpadyante, na vicintayanti na nirdhāvanti, nāpi jānanti na vijānanti kimetadādīptaṃ nāmeti | anyatra tena tenaiva dhāvanti vidhāvanti, punaḥ punaśca taṃ pitaramavalokayanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpīdaṃ bālabhāvatvāt ||
body.translated_text: 'And that man, <s>Śāriputra</s>, would be strong, endowed with physical might. He would reflect thus: "I am strong and endowed with physical might. What if I were to gather all these children together in a bundle, take them in my arms, and carry them out of this house?" But then he would reflect again thus: "This dwelling has a single entrance and a narrow door. And the children are fickle, restless, and childish by nature. They might become confused and run about. They might meet with calamity and disaster through this great mass of fire. What if I were to urge them on?" Having thus deliberated, he addressed those children: "Come, good children, come out! This house is ablaze with a great mass of fire. Do not let yourselves all be burnt here by this great mass of fire and meet with calamity and disaster!" But those children did not understand the speech of that man who wished their welfare; they did not become alarmed, did not become frightened, did not become terrified, were not gripped with terror; they did not reflect, did not run out, and did not even know or understand what "ablaze" means. Instead, they ran here and there, and again and again looked back at their father. For what reason? Because of their childish nature.'

body.text: atha khalu sa puruṣa evamanuvicintayet - ādīptamidaṃ niveśanaṃ mahatāgniskandhena saṃpradīptam | mā haivāhaṃ ceme ca kumārakā ihaivānena mahātāgniskandhena anayavyasanamāpatsyāmahe | yannvahamupāyakauśalyenemān kumārakān asmād gṛhāt niṣkrāmayeyam | sa ca puruṣasteṣāṃ kumārakāṇāmāśayajño bhavet, adhimuktiṃ ca vijānīyāt | teṣāṃ ca kumārakāṇāmanekavidhānyanekāni krīḍanakāni bhaveyurvividhāni ca ramaṇīyakānīṣṭāni kāntāni priyāṇi manaāpāni, tāni ca durlabhāni bhaveyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Then that man reflected thus: "This dwelling is ablaze, burning with a great mass of fire. Let not I and these children here meet with calamity and disaster through this great mass of fire. What if I were to bring these children out of this house through skillful means?" And that man knew the dispositions of those children and understood their inclinations. And those children would have many various toys and delightful playthings of many kinds — desired, charming, beloved, and agreeable — and those [playthings] would be hard to obtain.'

body.text: atha khalu sa puruṣasteṣāṃ kumārakāṇāmāśayaṃ jānaṃstān kumārakānetadavocat - yāni tāni kumārakā yuṣmākaṃ krīḍanakāni ramaṇīyakānyāścaryādbhutāni, yeṣāmalābhāt saṃtapyatha, nānāvarṇāni bahuprakārāṇi | tadyathā gorathakānyajarathakāni mṛgarathakāni | yāni bhavatāmiṣṭāni kāntāni priyāṇi manaāpāni | tāni ca mayā sarvāṇi bahinirveśanadvāre sthāpitāni yuṣmākaṃ krīḍanahetoḥ | āgacchantu bhavanto nirdhāvantvasmānniveśanāt | ahaṃ vo yasya yasya yenārtho yena prayojanaṃ bhaviṣyati, tasmai tasmai tatpradāsyāmi | āgacchata śīghraṃ teṣāṃ kāraṇam, nirdhāvata | atha khalu te kumārakāsteṣāṃ krīḍanakānāṃ ramaṇīyakānāmarthāya yathepsitānāṃ yathāsaṃkalpitānāmiṣṭānāṃ kāntānāṃ priyāṇāṃ manaāpānāṃ nāmadheyāni śrutvā tasmādādīptādagārāt kṣipramevārabdhavīryā balavatā javena anyonyamapratīkṣamāṇāḥ kaḥ prathamaṃ kaḥ prathamataramityanyonyaṃ saṃghaṭṭitakāyāstasmādādīptādagārāt kṣiprameva nirdhāvitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Then that man, knowing the dispositions of those children, said this to them: "Children, those toys and playthings of yours that are marvelous and wondrous, for the lack of which you are distressed — of various colors and many kinds, such as ox-carts, goat-carts, and deer-carts — which are desired, charming, beloved, and agreeable to you — all of those have been placed by me outside the door of the dwelling for you to play with. Come, good ones, run out of this dwelling! I shall give each of you whatever you need and whatever you desire. Come quickly, for that purpose — run out!" Then those children, having heard the names of those toys and delightful playthings — exactly as wished, exactly as imagined, desired, charming, beloved, and agreeable — quickly, with aroused vigor, with great speed, not waiting for one another, [thinking] "Who [will be] first? Who [will be] the very first?" — jostling one another's bodies, they quickly ran out of that burning house.'

body.text: atha sa puruṣaḥ kṣemasvastinā tān kumārakān nirgatān dṛṣṭvā abhayaprāptāniti viditvā ākāśe grāmacatvare upaviṣṭaḥ prītiprāmodyajāto nirupādāno vigatanīvaraṇo 'bhayaprāpto bhavet | atha khalu te kumārakā yena sa pitā tenopasaṃkrāman, upasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadeyuḥ - dehi nastāta tāni vividhāni krīḍanakāni ramaṇīyāni | tadyathā - gorathakānyajarathakāni mṛgarathakāni | atha khalu śāriputra sa puruṣasteṣāṃ svakānāṃ putrāṇāṃ vātajavasaṃpannān
body.translated_text: 'Then that man, upon seeing those children safely emerged and knowing that they had attained fearlessness, sat down in the open air at the village crossroads, filled with delight and joy, free from attachment, free from hindrances, and having attained fearlessness. Then those children approached their father and, having approached, said thus: "Give us, father, those various delightful toys — such as ox-carts, goat-carts, and deer-carts!" Then, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that man gave to those his own sons ox-carts alone endowed with the swiftness of the wind,

body.text: gorathakānevānuprayacchet saptaratnamayān savedikān sakiṅkiṇījālābhipralambitānuccān pragṛhītānāścaryādbhutaratnālaṃkṛtān ratnadāmakṛtaśobhān puṣpamālyālaṃkṛtāṃstūlikāgoṇikāstaraṇān dūṣyapaṭapratyāstīrṇānubhayato lohitopadhānān śvetaiḥ prapāṇḍaraiḥ śīghrajavairgoṇairyojitān bahupuruṣaparigṛhītān | savaijayantān gorathakāneva vātabalajavasaṃpannānekavarṇānekavidhānekaikasya dārakasya dadyāt | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi śāriputra sa puruṣa āḍhyaśca bhavenmahādhanaśca prabhūtakoṣṭhāgāraśca | sa evaṃ manyeta - alaṃ ma eṣāṃ kumārakāṇāmanyairyānairdattairiti | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarva evaite kumārakā mamaiva putrāḥ, sarve ca me priyā manaāpāḥ | saṃvidyante ca me imānyevaṃrūpāṇi mahāyānāni | samaṃ ca mayaite kumārakāḥ sarve cintayitavyā na viṣamam | ahamapi bahukoṣakoṣṭhāgāraḥ | sarvasattvānāmapyahamimānyevaṃrūpāṇi mahāyānāni dadyām, kimaṅga punaḥ svakānāṃ putrāṇām | te ca dārakāstasmin samaye teṣu mahāyāneṣvabhiruhya āścaryādbhutaprāptā bhaveyuḥ | tatkiṃ manyase śāriputra mā haiva tasya puruṣasya mṛṣāvādaḥ syāt, yena teṣāṃ dārakāṇāṃ pūrvaṃ trīṇi yānānyupadarśayitvā paścātsarveṣāṃ mahāyānānyeva dattāni, udārayānānyeva dattāni?
body.translated_text: made of the seven jewels, with railings, with hanging nets of small bells, tall, adorned with wondrous and marvelous gems, beautified with gem-garlands, decorated with flower-wreaths, with cushions of cotton and felt, spread with silk and fine cloth, with red pillows on both sides, yoked with white, very white, swift-footed oxen, attended by many men. With victory-columns, he gave ox-carts alone endowed with the power and swiftness of the wind, of one color, of one kind, one to each child. For what reason? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that man was wealthy, of great riches, and of abundant storehouses. He would think thus: "Let me not give these children other, [inferior] vehicles." For what reason? "All these children are indeed my own sons, and all are dear and agreeable to me. And I have such great vehicles as these. And I should consider all these children equally, not unequally. And I, having abundant treasuries and storehouses, should give such great vehicles even to all beings, how much more so to my own sons!" And those children, at that time, having mounted those great vehicles, would be struck with wonder and amazement. What do you think, <s>Śāriputra</s> — would that man not be guilty of false speech, having first shown those children three vehicles and then given all of them great vehicles alone, magnificent vehicles alone?'

body.text: śāriputra āha - na hyetad bhagavan, na hyetat sugata | anenaiva tāvad bhagavan kāraṇena sa puruṣo na mṛṣāvādī bhaved yattena puruṣeṇopāyakauśalyena te dārakāstasmādādīptād gṛhānniṣkāsitāḥ, jīvitena ca abhicchāditāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? ātmabhāvapratilambhenaiva bhagavan sarvakrīḍanakāni labdhāni bhavanti | yadyapi tāvad bhagavan sa puruṣasteṣāṃ kumārakāṇāmekarathamapi na dadyāt, tathāpi tāvad bhagavan sa puruṣo na mṛṣāvādī bhavet | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi bhagavaṃstena puruṣeṇa pūrvameva evamanuvicintitam - upāyakauśalyena ahamimān kumārakāṃstasmānmahato duḥkhaskandhāt parimocayiṣyāmīti | anenāpi bhagavan paryāyeṇa tasya puruṣasya na mṛṣāvādo bhavet | kaḥ punarvādo yattena puruṣeṇa prabhūtakośakoṣṭhāgāramastīti kṛtvā putrapriyatāmeva manyamānena ślāghamānenaikavarṇānyekayānāni dattāni, yaduta mahāyānāni | nāsti bhagavaṃstasya puruṣasya mṛṣāvādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'No indeed, Blessed One! No indeed, <s>Sugata</s>! For this very reason alone, Blessed One, that man would not be a false speaker — because by that man, through skillful means, those children were brought out of that burning house and were sheltered with life [itself]. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, by the very attainment of their own bodies, all their toys have been obtained. Even if, Blessed One, that man had not given those children even a single cart, he still, Blessed One, would not be a false speaker. For what reason? Because, Blessed One, that man had already reflected beforehand thus: "Through skillful means, I shall liberate these children from this great mass of suffering." For this reason too, Blessed One, there would be no false speech for that man. How much less so, given that that man, knowing that he has abundant treasuries and storehouses, out of consideration for the love of his children, thinking highly [of them], gave them carts of one color, of one vehicle — namely, great vehicles! There is no false speech for that man, Blessed One.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputrametadavocat - sādhu sādhu śāriputra | evametacchāriputra, evametad yathā vadasi | evameva śāriputra tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvabhayavinivṛttaḥ sarvopadravopāyāsopasargaduḥkhadaurmanasyāvidyāndhakāratamastimirapaṭalaparyavanāhebhyaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā vipramuktaḥ | tathāgato jñānabalavaiśāradyāveṇikabuddhadharmasamanvāgataḥ ṛddhibalenātibalavāṃllokapitāḥ, mahopāyakauśalyajñānaparamapāramitāprāpto mahākāruṇiko 'parikhinnamānaso hitaiṣī anukampakaḥ | sa traidhātuke mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyaskandhena ādīptajīrṇapaṭalaśaraṇaniveśanasadṛśa utpadyate sattvānāṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāvidyāndhakāratamastimirapaṭalaparyavanāhapratiṣṭhānāṃ rāgadveṣamohaparimocanahetoranuttarāyāṃ
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Śāriputra</s>! So it is, <s>Śāriputra</s>, so it is, just as you say. Even so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, perfectly enlightened one, free from all fears, completely and utterly liberated in every way from all calamities, troubles, dangers, sufferings, sorrows, the darkness of ignorance, and the covering veil of obscuration — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowed with the knowledge-powers, confidences, and distinctive Buddha-<s>dharmas</s>, of exceedingly great power through the power of supernatural ability, the father of the world, who has attained the highest perfection of the great <s>upāyakauśalya</s>-knowledge, who is greatly compassionate, whose mind is unwearied, who desires welfare and is considerate — he arises in the three realms, which resemble a blazing, old, dilapidated, thatch-covered dwelling ablaze with a great mass of suffering and sorrow, for the purpose of liberating beings from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, sorrow, distress, the darkness of ignorance, and the covering veil of obscuration — from the [bondage of] passion, hatred, and delusion — for unsurpassed

body.text: samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpanahetoḥ | sa utpannaḥ samānaḥ paśyati sattvān dahyataḥ pacyamānāṃstapyamānān paritapyamānān jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ, paribhoganimittaṃ ca kāmahetunidānaṃ ca anekāvidhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti | dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ ca paryeṣṭinidānaṃ parigrahanidānaṃ sāṃparāyikaṃ narakatiryagyoniyamalokeṣvanekavidhāni duḥkhāni pratyanubhaviṣyanti | devamanuṣyadāridryamaniṣṭasaṃyogamiṣṭavinābhāvikāni ca duḥkhāni pratyanubhavanti | tatraiva ca duḥkhaskandhe parivartamānāḥ krīḍanti ramante paricārayanti notrasanti na saṃtrasanti na saṃtrāsamāpadyante na budhyante na cetayanti nodvijanti na niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante | tatraiva ca ādīptāgārasadṛśe traidhātuke 'bhiramanti, tena tenaiva vidhāvanti | tena ca mahatā duḥkhaskandhena abhyāhatā na duḥkhamanasikārasaṃjñāmutpādayanti ||
body.translated_text: for the purpose of leading [beings] to undertake unsurpassed perfect awakening. Being born [in the world], he sees beings burning, being cooked, scorched, and utterly tormented by birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, and he sees them experiencing manifold sufferings on account of enjoyments, through the cause and origin of desires. And they will experience manifold sufferings in this very life on account of searching and acquisition, and in future lives in the hells, animal realms, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>. They experience the sufferings of poverty among gods and humans, of unwanted association, and of separation from the desired. And while revolving in that very mass of suffering, they play, delight, and amuse themselves; they are not afraid, not terrified, not struck with terror; they do not understand, do not take heed, are not alarmed, and do not seek escape. In that very triple world, which resembles a burning house, they take delight, running here and there. And though struck by that great mass of suffering, they do not generate the perception of attending to suffering.

body.text: tatra śāriputra tathāgata evaṃ paśyati - ahaṃ khalveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ pitā | mayā hyete sattvā asmādevaṃrūpānmahato duḥkhaskandhāt parimocayitavyāḥ, mayā caiṣāṃ sattvānāmaprameyamacintyaṃ buddhajñānasukhaṃ dātavyam, yenaite sattvāḥ krīḍiṣyanti ramiṣyanti paricārayiṣyanti, vikrīḍitāni ca kariṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: There, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> sees thus: 'Truly, I am the father of these beings. These beings must be freed by me from this great mass of suffering. And I must give these beings the immeasurable, inconceivable happiness of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, in which these beings will play, delight, and amuse themselves, and find their enjoyment.'

body.text: tatra śāriputra tathāgata evaṃ paśyati - sacedahaṃ jñānabalo 'smīti kṛtvā ṛddhibalo 'smīti kṛtvā anupāyenaiṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānabalavaiśāradyāni saṃśrāvayeyam, naite sattvā ebhirdharbhairniryāyeyuḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? adhyavasitā hyamī sattvāḥ pañcasu kāmaguṇeṣu traidhātukaratyām | aparimuktā jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsebhyaḥ | dahyante pacyante tapyante paritapyante | anirdhāvitāstraidhātukādādīptajīrṇapaṭalaśaraṇaniveśanasadṛśāt kathamete buddhajñānaṃ paribhotsyante?
body.translated_text: There, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> sees thus: 'If I, on account of being endowed with the power of knowledge, on account of being endowed with the power of supernatural ability, were to declare to these beings, without skillful means, the powers and fearlessnesses of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge, these beings would not escape by those means. Why? Because these beings are deeply attached to the five strands of sense-desire, to the delight of the triple world. They are not freed from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. They are burning, being cooked, scorched, and utterly tormented. They have not run out from the triple world, which resembles a blazing, decrepit, thatched shelter. How could they comprehend the <s>Buddha's</s> knowledge?'

body.text: tatra śāriputra tathāgato yadyathāpi nāma sa puruṣo bāhubalikaḥ sthāpayitvā bāhubalam, upāyakauśalyena tān kumārakāṃstasmādādīptādagārānniṣkāsayet, niṣkāsayitvā sa teṣāṃ paścādudārāṇi mahāyānāni dadyāt, evameva śāriputra tathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddhastathāgatajñānabalavaiśāradyasamanvāgataḥ sthāpayitvā tathāgatajñānabalavaiśāradyam, upāyakauśalyajñānenādīptajīrṇapaṭalaśaraṇaniveśanasadṛśāt traidhātukāt sattvānāṃ niṣkāsanahetostrīṇi yānānyupadarśayati yadut śrāvakayānaṃ pratyekabuddhayānaṃ bodhisattvayānamiti | tribhiśca yānaiḥ sattvāṃllobhayati, evaṃ caiṣāṃ vadati - mā bhavanto 'sminnādīptāgārasadṛśe traidhātuke 'bhiramadhvaṃ hīneṣu rūpaśabdagandharasasparśeṣu | atra hi yūyaṃ traidhātuke 'bhiratāḥ pañcakāmaguṇasahagatayā tṛṣṇayā dahyatha tapyatha paritapyatha | nirdhāvadhvamasmāt traidhātukāt | trīṇi yānānyanuprāpsyatha yadidaṃ śrāvakayānaṃ pratyekabuddhayānaṃ bodhisattvayānamiti | ahaṃ vo 'tra sthāne pratibhūḥ | ahaṃ vo dāsyāmyetāni trīṇi yānāni | abhiyujyadhve traidhātukānni 'saraṇahetoḥ | evaṃ caitāṃllobhayāmi - etāni bhoḥ sattvā yāni āryāṇi ca āryapraśastāni ca mahāramaṇīyakasamanvāgatāni ca | akṛpaṇametairbhavantaḥ krīḍiṣyatha ramiṣyatha paricārayiṣyatha | indriyabalabodhyaṅgadhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattibhiśca mahatīṃ ratiṃ pratyanubhaviṣyatha | mahatā ca sukhasaumanasyena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyatha ||
body.translated_text: There, <s>Śāriputra</s>, just as that man of strong arms, setting aside his physical strength, rescued those children from that burning house through skillful means, and after rescuing them, gave them magnificent great vehicles — just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, endowed with the <s>Tathāgata's</s> powers of knowledge and fearlessness, setting aside the <s>Tathāgata's</s> powers of knowledge and fearlessness, through the knowledge of skillful means, for the purpose of rescuing beings from the triple world that resembles a blazing, decrepit, thatched shelter, displays three vehicles — namely, the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle. And with these three vehicles he entices beings, and he says to them thus: 'Do not, sirs, take delight in this triple world that resembles a burning house, in these inferior forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and touches! For while you take delight in this triple world, you are burning, scorching, and utterly tormented by the craving associated with the five strands of sense-desire. Run out from this triple world! You will obtain three vehicles — namely, the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle. I am your guarantor in this matter. I will give you these three vehicles. Strive for the sake of escaping from the triple world!' And thus he entices them: 'These vehicles, sirs, are noble, praised by the noble, endowed with great delight. With these, you will play without stint, delight, and amuse yourselves. And through the <s>indriyas</s> (faculties), <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> (attainments), you will experience great delight. And you will be endowed with great happiness and ease of mind.'

body.text:
