tatra śāriputra ye sattvāḥ paṇḍitajātīyā bhavanti, te tathāgatasya lokapiturabhiśraddadhanti | abhiśraddadhitvā ca tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante udyogamāpadyante | tatra kecit sattvā paraghoṣaśravānugamanamākāṅkṣamāṇā ātmaparinirvāṇahetoścaturāryasatyānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante | te ucyante śrāvakayānamākāṅkṣamāṇāḥ traidhātukānnirdhāvanti | tadyathāpi nāma tasmādādīptādagārādanyatare dārakā mṛgarathamākāṅkṣamāṇā nirdhāvitāḥ | anye sattvā anācāryakaṃ jñānaṃ damaśamathamākāṅkṣamāṇā ātmaparinirvāṇahetorhetupratyayānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante, te ucyante pratyekabuddhayānamākāṅkṣamāṇāstraidhātukānnirdhāvanti | tadyathāpi nāma tasmādādīptādagārādanyatare dārakā ajarathamāṅkṣamāṇā nirdhāvitāḥ | apare punaḥ sattvāḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ buddhajñānaṃ svayaṃbhūjñānamanācāryakaṃ jñānamākāṅkṣamāṇā bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca sarvasattvaparinirvāṇahetostathāgatajñānabalavaiśāradyānubodhāya tathāgataśāsane 'bhiyujyante | te ucyante mahāyānamākāṅkṣamāṇāstraidhātukānnirdhāvanti | tena kāraṇenocyante bodhisattvā mahāsattvā iti | tadyathāpi nāma tasmādādīptādagārādanyatare dārakā gorathamākāṅkṣamāṇānirdhāvitāḥ | tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra sa puruṣastān kumārakāṃstasmādādīptādagārānnirdhāvitān dṛṣṭvā kṣemasvastibhyāṃ parimuktānabhayaprāptāniti viditvā ātmānaṃ ca mahādhanaṃ viditvā teṣāṃ dārakāṇāmekameva yānamudāramanuprayacchet, evameva śāriputra tathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho yadā paśyati - anekāḥ sattvakoṭīstraidhātukāt parimuktā duḥkhabhayabhairavopadravaparimuktāstathāgataśāsanadvāreṇa nirdhāvitāḥ parimuktāḥ sarvabhayopadravakāntārebhyaḥ | nirvṛtisukhaprāptāḥ nirvṛtisukhāprāptāḥ | tānetān śāriputra tasmin samaye tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ prabhūto mahājñānabalavaiśāradyakośa iti viditvā sarve caite mamaiva putrā iti jñātvā buddhayānenaiva tān sattvān parinirvāpayati | na ca kasyacit sattvasya pratyātmikaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ vadati | sarvāṃśca tān sattvāṃstathāgataparinirvāṇena mahāparinirvāṇena
parinirvāpayati | ye cāpi te śāriputra sattvāstraidhātukāt parimuktā bhavanti, teṣāṃ tathāgato dhyānavimokṣasamādhisamāpattīrāryāṇi paramasukhāni krīḍanakāni ramaṇīyakāni dadāti, sarvāṇyetānyekavarṇāni | tadyathāpi nāma śāriputra tasya puruṣasya na mṛṣāvādo bhavet, yena trīṇi yānānyupadarśayitvā teṣāṃ kumārakāṇāmekameva mahāyānaṃ sarveṣāṃ dattaṃ saptaratnamayaṃ sarvālaṃkāravibhūṣitamekavarṇameva udārayānameva sarveṣāmagrayānameva dattaṃ bhavet | evameva śāriputra tathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho na mṛṣāvādī bhavati, yena pūrvamupāyakauśalyena trīṇi yānānyupadarśayitvā paścānmahāyānenaiva sattvān parinirvāpayati | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgato hi śāriputra prabhūtajñānabalavaiśāradyakośakoṣṭhāgārasamanvāgataḥ pratibalaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ sarvajñajñānasahagataṃ
body.translated_text: There, <s>Śāriputra</s>, those beings who are of a wise nature place their faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the father of the world. Having placed their faith, they strive and exert themselves in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching. Among them, some beings, desiring to follow the voice of another, strive in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching for the sake of their own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for the realization of the four noble truths. They are called those who desire the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle; they run out from the triple world — just as some of those children ran out from that burning house desiring a deer-cart. Other beings, desiring teacher-less knowledge, self-mastery, and tranquility, strive in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching for the sake of their own <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, for the realization of causes and conditions. They are called those who desire the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle; they run out from the triple world — just as some of those children ran out from that burning house desiring a goat-cart. And yet other beings, desiring omniscient knowledge, <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, self-born knowledge, teacher-less knowledge, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of the great body of beings, of gods and humans, for the sake of the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of all beings, strive in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching for the realization of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> powers of knowledge and fearlessness. They are called those who desire the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle); they run out from the triple world. For this reason they are called <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>. Just as some of those children ran out from that burning house desiring an ox-cart. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that man, having seen those children run out from that burning house and knowing them to be safe and sound, free from danger, and knowing himself to be wealthy, gives those children a single magnificent vehicle — just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, when he sees many <s>koṭis</s> of beings freed from the triple world, freed from the suffering, fear, terror, and calamity, having run out through the gate of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching, freed from all fearful, calamitous wilderness — having attained the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, or not yet having attained the happiness of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — at that time, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, knowing that his own treasury of great knowledge, powers, and fearlessness is abundant, and knowing 'all these are indeed my children,' extinguishes those beings through the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle) alone. He does not declare individual <s>parinirvāṇa</s> for any being. He extinguishes all those beings through the <s>Tathāgata's</s> <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And to those beings, <s>Śāriputra</s>, who are freed from the triple world, the <s>Tathāgata</s> gives <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations), and <s>samāpattis</s> — noble, supremely blissful playthings — all of one flavor. Just as, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that man would not be a speaker of falsehood, who, having displayed three vehicles, gave all those children a single great vehicle made of the seven jewels, adorned with all ornaments, of one flavor, a magnificent vehicle, the supreme vehicle for all — just so, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one, is not a speaker of falsehood, who, having previously displayed three vehicles through skillful means, afterward extinguishes beings through the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle) alone. Why? Because, <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, endowed with a treasury, a storehouse, of abundant knowledge, powers, and fearlessness, is capable of displaying to all beings the <s>Dharma</s> accompanied by omniscient knowledge.

body.text: dharmamupadarśayitum | anenāpi śāriputra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyam, yathā upāyakauśalyajñānābhinirhāraistathāgata ekameva mahāyānaṃ deśayati ||
body.translated_text: By this explanation too, <s>Śāriputra</s>, it should be understood that through the manifestations of the knowledge of skillful means, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches one single <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: yathā hi puruṣasya bhavedagāraṃ jīrṇaṃ mahantaṃ ca sudurbalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: "Just as there might be a man's house, old, large, and very decrepit,

children.text: viśīrṇa prāsādu tathā bhaveta stambhāśca mūleṣu bhaveyu pūtikāḥ // Saddhp_3.39 //
children.translated_text: and the building would be likewise ruined, and the pillars rotten at their bases, [Saddhp 3.39-3.40]

children.text: gavākṣaharmyā galitaikadeśā viśīrṇa kuḍayaṃ kaṭalepanaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: the windows and upper stories fallen apart in places, the walls and plaster crumbled,

children.text: jīrṇu pravṛddhoddhṛtavedikaṃ ca tṛṇacchadaṃ sarvata opatantam // Saddhp_3.40 //
children.translated_text: worn out, with the balustrade fallen away, and the thatch-covering falling on all sides,

children.text: śatāna pañcāna anūnakānāṃ āvāsu so tatra bhaveta prāṇinām /
children.translated_text: and no fewer than five hundred living beings would dwell therein,

children.text: bahūni cā niṣkuṭasaṃkaṭāni uccārapūrṇāni jugupsitāni // Saddhp_3.41 //
children.translated_text: and many narrow, cramped quarters, filled with excrement, disgusting, [Saddhp 3.41]

children.text: gopānasī vigalita tatra sarvā kuḍayāśca bhittīśca tathaiva srastāḥ /
children.translated_text: all the rafters would be rotting there, and the walls and partitions likewise collapsed;

children.text: gṛdhrāṇa koṭyo nivasanti tatra pārāvatolūka tathānyapakṣiṇaḥ // Saddhp_3.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>koṭis</s> of vultures dwell there, and doves, owls, and other birds; [Saddhp 3.42]

children.text: āśīviṣā dāruṇa tatra santi deśapradeśeṣu mahāviṣogrāḥ /
children.translated_text: there are terrible poisonous snakes, in every spot, with great fierce venom,

children.text: vicitrikā vṛścikamūṣikāśca etāna āvāsu suduṣṭaprāṇinām // Saddhp_3.43 //
children.translated_text: centipedes, scorpions, and mice — those are the dwellings of wicked creatures; [Saddhp 3.43]

children.text: deśe ca deśe amanuṣya bhūyo uccāraprasrāvavināśitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: and in every place there are many non-human beings, and it is befouled with excrement and urine,

children.text: kṛmikīṭakhadyotakapūritaṃ ca śvabhiḥ śṛgālaiśca nināditaṃ ca // Saddhp_3.44 //
children.translated_text: filled with worms, beetles, and fireflies, and resounding with dogs and jackals; [Saddhp 3.44]

children.text: bheruṇḍakā dāruṇā tatra santi manuṣyakuṇapāni ca bhakṣayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: there are terrible <s>bheruṇḍaka</s> creatures who eat human corpses,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca niryāṇu pratīkṣamāṇāḥ śvānāḥ śṛgālāśca vasantyaneke // Saddhp_3.45 //
children.translated_text: and waiting for their leavings, many dogs and jackals dwell there; [Saddhp 3.45]

children.text: te durbalā nitya kṣudhābhibhūtā deśeṣu deśeṣu vikhādamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: weak, always overcome by hunger, tearing at each other in every spot,

children.text: kalahaṃ karontāśca ninādayanti subhairavaṃ tadgṛhamevarūpam // Saddhp_3.46 //
children.translated_text: fighting and howling — such is that frightful house; [Saddhp 3.46]

children.text: suraudracittā pi vasanti yakṣā manuṣyakuṇapāni vikaḍḍhamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: and <s>yakṣas</s> of exceedingly fierce disposition dwell there, dragging human corpses;

children.text: deśeṣu deśeṣu vasanti tatra śatāpadī gonasakāśca vyālāḥ // Saddhp_3.47 //
children.translated_text: in every spot there dwell centipedes, mongooses, and serpents; [Saddhp 3.47]

children.text: deśeṣu deśeṣu ca nikṣipanti te potakānyālayanāni kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: in every spot they deposit their young, having made their nests;

children.text: nyastāni nyastāni ca tāni teṣāṃ te yakṣa bhūyo paribhakṣayanti // Saddhp_3.48 //
children.translated_text: and those deposited [young] of theirs — those <s>yakṣas</s> devour them again and again; [Saddhp 3.48]

children.text: yadā ca te yakṣa bhavanti tṛptāḥ parasattva khāditva suraudracittāḥ /
children.translated_text: and when those <s>yakṣas</s> are sated, having eaten other beings with fierce minds,

children.text: parasattvamāṃsaiḥ paritṛptagātrāḥ kalahaṃ tadā tatra karonti tīvram // Saddhp_3.49 //
children.translated_text: their bodies full from the flesh of other beings, then they fight there fiercely; [Saddhp 3.49]

children.text: vidhvastaleneṣu vasanti tatra kumbhāṇḍakā dārūṇaraudracittāḥ /
children.translated_text: in the ruined spaces there dwell <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, of terrible fierce minds,

children.text: vitastimātrāstatha hastamātrā dvihastamātrāścanucaṃkramanti // Saddhp_3.50 //
children.translated_text: some a span tall, some a cubit, some two cubits — they pace about there; [Saddhp 3.50]

children.text: te cāpi śvānān parigṛhya pādairuttānakān kṛtva tathaiva bhūmau /
children.translated_text: and they too, seizing dogs by the feet, throwing them on their backs on the ground,

children.text: grīvāsu cotpīḍya vibhartsayanto vyābādhayantaśca ramanti tatra // Saddhp_3.51 //
children.translated_text: squeezing their necks, threatening them, tormenting them — they take their pleasure there; [Saddhp 3.51]

children.text: nānāśca kṛṣṇāśca tathaiva durbalā uccā mahantāśca vasanti pretāḥ /
children.translated_text: and various black and emaciated, tall and large <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) dwell there,

children.text: jighatsitā bhojana mārgamāṇā ārtasvaraṃ krandiṣu tatra tatra // Saddhp_3.52 //
children.translated_text: starving, seeking food, wailing miserably here and there; [Saddhp 3.52]

body.text: sūcīmukhā goṇamukhāśca kecit manuṣyamātrāstatha śvānamātrāḥ /
body.translated_text: some with needle-mouths, some with ox-mouths, some the size of humans, some the size of dogs —

body.text: prakīrṇakeśāśca karonti śabdamāhāratṛṣṇāparidahyamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.53 //
body.translated_text: With hair disheveled, they cry out, burning with hunger and thirst. // Saddhp 3.53 //

children.text: caturdiśaṃ cātra vilokayanti gavākṣa-ullokanakehi nityam /
children.translated_text: And they constantly look in the four directions through the windows and openings,

children.text: te yakṣa pretāśca piśācakāśca gṛdhrāśca āhāra gaveṣamāṇāḥ // Saddhp_3.54 //
children.translated_text: those <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and <s>piśācas</s> (flesh-eating demons), and vultures, seeking food. // Saddhp 3.54 //

children.text: etādṛśaṃ bhairavu tad gṛhaṃ bhavet mahantamuccaṃ ca sudurbalaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Such was that terrifying house, great and tall yet extremely decrepit,

children.text: vijarjaraṃ durbalamitvaraṃ ca puruṣasya ekasya parigrahaṃ bhavet // Saddhp_3.55 //
children.translated_text: crumbling, weak, and perishable, and it was the property of a single man. // Saddhp 3.55 //

children.text: sa ca bāhyataḥ syātpuruṣo gṛhasya niveśanaṃ tacca bhavetpradīptam /
children.translated_text: That man was outside the house, and that dwelling was ablaze,

children.text: sahasā samantena caturdiśaṃ ca jvālāsahasraiḥ paridīpyamānam // Saddhp_3.56 //
children.translated_text: suddenly on all sides, in the four directions, blazing with thousands of flames. // Saddhp 3.56 //

children.text: vaṃśāśca dārūṇi ca agnitāpitāḥ karonti śabdaṃ gurukaṃ subhairavam /
children.translated_text: The bamboos and timbers, heated by fire, make a loud and terrible sound,

children.text: pradīpta stambhāśca tathaiva bhittayo yakṣāśca pretāśca mucanti nādam // Saddhp_3.57 //
children.translated_text: the pillars are ablaze and likewise the walls, and the <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>pretas</s> emit cries. // Saddhp 3.57 //

children.text: jvālūṣitā gṛdhraśatāśca bhūyaḥ kumbhāṇḍakāḥ ploṣṭamukhā bhramanti /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of vultures, scorched by flames, and <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> (gourd-demons) with burning faces wander about,

children.text: samantato vyālaśatāśca tatra nadanti krośanti ca dahyamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.58 //
children.translated_text: and on all sides hundreds of serpents there hiss and shriek, being burned. // Saddhp 3.58 //

children.text: piśācakāstatra bahū bhramanti saṃtāpitā agnina mandapuṇyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many <s>piśācas</s> wander there, tormented by fire, of little merit,

children.text: dantehi pāṭitva ti anyamanyaṃ rudhireṇa siñcanti ca dahyamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.59 //
children.translated_text: tearing each other with their teeth and drenching one another with blood as they burn. // Saddhp 3.59 //

children.text: bherūṇḍakāḥ kālagatāśca tatra khādanti sattvāśca ti anyamanyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Bherūṇḍas</s> (two-headed birds) and dead creatures are there, and beings devour each other,

children.text: uccāra dahyatyamanojñagandhaḥ pravāyate loki caturdiśāsu // Saddhp_3.60 //
children.translated_text: the excrement burns and its foul stench spreads to the four directions of the world. // Saddhp 3.60 //

children.text: śatāpadīyo prapalāyamānāḥ kumbhāṇḍakāstāḥ paribhakṣayanti /
children.translated_text: Centipedes fleeing in all directions are devoured by the <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>,

children.text: pradīptakeśāśca bhramanti pretāḥ kṣudhāya dāhena ca dahyamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.61 //
children.translated_text: and <s>pretas</s> with blazing hair wander about, burning with hunger and the heat of fire. // Saddhp 3.61 //

children.text: etādṛśaṃ bhairava tanniveśanaṃ jvālāsahasrairhi viniścaradbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Such was that terrifying dwelling, with thousands of flames pouring forth,

children.text: puruṣaśca so tasya gṛhasya svāmī dvārasmi asthāsi vipaśyamānaḥ // Saddhp_3.62 //
children.translated_text: and that man, the owner of the house, stood at the door, watching. // Saddhp 3.62 //

children.text: śṛṇoti cāsau svake atra putrān krīḍāpanaiḥ krīḍanasaktabuddhīn /
children.translated_text: And he hears that his own children inside are absorbed in play, their minds attached to their toys,

children.text: ramanti te krīḍanakapramattā yathāpi bālā avijānamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.63 //
children.translated_text: they delight, intoxicated with their playthings, like ignorant children who do not understand. // Saddhp 3.63 //

children.text: śrutvā ca so tatra praviṣṭu kṣipraṃ pramocanārthāya tadātmajānām /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, he wished to enter quickly to rescue his children,

children.text: mā mahya bālā imi sarva dārakā dahyeyu naśyeyu ca kṣiprameva // Saddhp_3.64 //
children.translated_text: thinking: 'Let not these children, all my young ones, be burned and perish at once!' // Saddhp 3.64 //

children.text: sa bhāṣate teṣamagāradoṣān duḥkhaṃ idaṃ bhoḥ kulaputra dāruṇam /
children.translated_text: He tells them of the dangers of the house: 'O noble sons, this suffering is terrible!

children.text: vividhāśca sattveha ayaṃ ca agni mahantikā duḥkhaparaṃparā tu // Saddhp_3.65 //
children.translated_text: Various creatures are here, and this fire — it is a great succession of miseries!' // Saddhp 3.65 //

children.text: āśīviṣā yakṣa suraudracittāḥ kumbhāṇḍa pretā bahavo vasanti /
children.translated_text: 'Poisonous snakes, <s>yakṣas</s> of exceedingly fierce minds, <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s>, and many <s>pretas</s> dwell here,

children.text: bheruṇḍakāḥ śvānaśṛgālasaṃghā gṛdhrāśca āhāra gaveṣamāṇāḥ // Saddhp_3.66 //
children.translated_text: <s>bherūṇḍas</s>, packs of dogs and jackals, and vultures seeking food. // Saddhp 3.66 //

children.text: etādṛśāsmin bahavo vasanti vināpi cāgneḥ paramaṃ subhairavam /
children.translated_text: So many such creatures dwell in this place — even without the fire it is supremely terrifying,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ idaṃ kevalamevarūpaṃ samantataścāgnirayaṃ pradīptaḥ // Saddhp_3.67 //
children.translated_text: this suffering is nothing but of this nature, and on all sides this fire blazes!' // Saddhp 3.67 //

body.text: te codyamānāstatha bālabuddhayaḥ kumārakāḥ krīḍanake pramattāḥ /
body.translated_text: But those boys, exhorted thus, with childish understanding and intoxicated with play,

body.text: na cintayante pitaraṃ bhaṇantaṃ na cāpi teṣāṃ manasīkaronti // Saddhp_3.68 //
body.translated_text: do not heed their father's words, nor do they take them to heart. // Saddhp 3.68 //

children.text: puruṣaśca so tatra tadā vicintayet suduḥkhito 'smī iha putracintayā /
children.translated_text: Then that man reflected there: 'I am deeply grieved with worry for my children.

children.text: kiṃ mahya putrehi aputrakasya mā nāma dahyeyurihāgninā ime // Saddhp_3.69 //
children.translated_text: What use are children to me if I become childless? Let these not be burned here by the fire!' // Saddhp 3.69 //

children.text: upāyu so cintayi tasmi kāle lubdhā ime krīḍanakeṣu bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: He devised a <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) at that time: 'These children are greedy for their toys,

children.text: na cātra krīḍā ca ratī ca kācid bālāna ho yādṛśu mūḍhabhāvaḥ // Saddhp_3.70 //
children.translated_text: and there is no play or pleasure here of the kind that would suit the foolishness of children.' // Saddhp 3.70 //

children.text: sa tānavocachṛṇuthā kumārakā nānāvidhā yānaka yā mamāsti /
children.translated_text: He said to them: 'Listen, boys! I have various kinds of carts,

children.text: mṛgairajairgoṇavaraiśca yuktā uccā mahantā samalaṃkṛtā ca // Saddhp_3.71 //
children.translated_text: yoked with deer, goats, and fine oxen — tall, great, and well-adorned! // Saddhp 3.71 //

children.text: tā bāhyato asya niveśanasya nirdhāvathā tehi karotha kāryam /
children.translated_text: They are outside this dwelling. Run out! Make use of them!

children.text: yuṣmākamarthe maya kāritāni niryātha taistuṣṭamanāḥ sametya // Saddhp_3.72 //
children.translated_text: They have been made for your sake by me. Come out and enjoy them with satisfied minds!' // Saddhp 3.72 //

children.text: te yāna etādṛśakā niśāmya ārabdhavīryāstvaritā hi bhūtvā /
children.translated_text: Hearing of such carts, they put forth vigorous effort, and swiftly

children.text: nirdhāvitāstatkṣaṇameva sarve ākāśi tiṣṭhanti dukhena muktāḥ // Saddhp_3.73 //
children.translated_text: all of them rushed out at that very moment and stood in the open, freed from suffering. // Saddhp 3.73 //

children.text: puruṣaśca so nirgata dṛṣṭva dārakān grāmasya madhye sthitu catvarasmin /
children.translated_text: The man, seeing his children had come out, sat down in the middle of the village at the crossroads,

children.text: upaviśya siṃhāsani tānuvāca aho ahaṃ nirvṛtu adya mārṣāḥ // Saddhp_3.74 //
children.translated_text: and sitting upon a lion-throne, he said to them: 'Ah, I am content today, dear ones! // Saddhp 3.74 //

children.text: ye duḥkhalabdhā mama te tapasvinaḥ putrā priyā orasa viṃśa bālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those pitiable sons of mine, obtained through hardship, dear, born of my own body, twenty boys —

children.text: te dārūṇe durgagṛhe abhūvan bahūjantūpūrṇe ca subhairave ca // Saddhp_3.75 //
children.translated_text: they were in that dreadful, dangerous house, filled with many creatures and supremely terrifying. // Saddhp 3.75 //

children.text: ādīptake jvālasahasrapūrṇe ratā ca te krīḍaratīṣu āsan /
children.translated_text: It was ablaze, filled with thousands of flames, yet they were absorbed in the delights of play.

children.text: mayā ca te mocita adya sarve yenāhu nirvāṇu samāgato 'dya // Saddhp_3.76 //
children.translated_text: But today I have rescued them all, and therefore I have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> (peace) today.' // Saddhp 3.76 //

children.text: sukhasthitaṃ taṃ pitaraṃ viditvā upagamya te dāraka evamāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Knowing that their father was comfortably seated, the children approached him and said:

children.text: dadāhi nastāta yathābhibhāṣitaṃ trividhāni yānāni manoramāṇi // Saddhp_3.77 //
children.translated_text: 'Give us, father, what you promised — the three kinds of delightful carts!' // Saddhp 3.77 //

children.text: sacettava satyaka tāta sarvaṃ yadbhāṣitaṃ tatra niveśane te /
children.translated_text: 'If all your words are true, father, what you spoke of in that dwelling —

children.text: trividhāni yānāni ha saṃpradāsye dadasva kālo 'yamihādya teṣām // Saddhp_3.78 //
children.translated_text: the three kinds of carts — please give them to us. Now is the time for those today!' // Saddhp 3.78 //

children.text: puruṣaśca so kośabalī bhaveta suvarṇarūpyāmaṇimuktakasya /
children.translated_text: Now that man was wealthy in treasure-stores of gold, silver, gems, and pearls,

children.text: hiraṇya dāsāśca analpakāḥ syurupasthape ekavidhā sa yānā // Saddhp_3.79 //
children.translated_text: with gold, numerous servants, and attendants — he prepared carts of one single kind: // Saddhp 3.79 //

children.text: ratnāmayā goṇarathā viśiṣṭā savedikāḥ kiṅkiṇijālanaddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: ox-carts made of jewels, magnificent, with railings and nets of tinkling bells,

children.text: chatradhvajebhiḥ samalaṃkṛtāśca muktāmaṇījālikachāditāśca // Saddhp_3.80 //
children.translated_text: adorned with parasols and banners, and covered with nets of pearls and gems. // Saddhp 3.80 //

children.text: suvarṇapuṣpāṇa kṛtaiśca dāmairdeśeṣu deśeṣu pralambamānaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With garlands made of golden flowers, hanging here and there in every place,

children.text: bastrairudāraiḥ parisaṃvṛtāśca pratyāstṛtā dūṣyavaraiśca śuklaiḥ // Saddhp_3.81 //
children.translated_text: covered with splendid fabrics, and spread with the finest white silks. // Saddhp 3.81 //

children.text: mṛdukān paṭṭāna tathaiva tatra varatūlikāsaṃstṛta ye 'pi te rathāḥ /
children.translated_text: Soft fine cloths were there also, and those carts were spread with the finest quilted cushions,

children.text: pratyāstṛtāḥ koṭisahasramūlyairvaraiśca kockairbakahaṃsalakṣaṇaiḥ // Saddhp_3.82 //
children.translated_text: covered with coverings worth millions of <s>koṭis</s>, and with fine woolen blankets marked with the signs of herons and geese. // Saddhp 3.82 //

children.text: śvetāḥ supuṣṭā balavanta goṇā mahāpramāṇā abhidarśanīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: White, well-fed, powerful oxen of great size, beautiful to behold,

children.text: ye yojitā ratnaratheṣu teṣu parigṛhītāḥ puruṣairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_3.83 //
children.translated_text: were yoked to those jeweled carts, attended by numerous men. // Saddhp 3.83 //

children.text: etādṛśān so puruṣo dadāti putrāṇa sarvāṇa varān viśiṣṭān /
children.translated_text: Such excellent and distinguished carts that man gave to all his children,

children.text: te cāpi tuṣṭāttamanāśca tehi diśāśca vidiśāśca vrajanti krīḍakāḥ // Saddhp_3.84 //
children.translated_text: and they, satisfied and delighted with them, go playing in all directions and quarters. // Saddhp 3.84 //

children.text: emeva haṃ śārisutā maharṣī sattvāna trāṇaṃ ca pitā ca bhomi /
children.translated_text: Just so, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, I am the great sage, the protector and father of all beings.

children.text: putrāśca te prāṇina sarvi mahyaṃ traidhātuke kāmavilagna bālāḥ // Saddhp_3.85 //
children.translated_text: All living beings are my children — children in the three realms, attached to desires, like infants. // Saddhp 3.85 //

children.text: traidhātukaṃ co yatha tanniveśanaṃ subhairavaṃ duḥkhaśatābhikīrṇam /
children.translated_text: And the three realms are like that dwelling — terrifying, strewn with hundreds of sufferings,

children.text: aśeṣataḥ prajvalitaṃ samantājjātījarāvyādhiśatairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_3.86 //
children.translated_text: completely ablaze on every side with countless hundreds of birth, old age, and disease. // Saddhp 3.86 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca traidhātukamukta śānto ekāntasthāyī pavane vasāmi /
children.translated_text: And I, freed from the three realms, am tranquil, dwelling alone in the forest in peace.

children.text: traidhātukaṃ co mamidaṃ parigraho ye hyatra dahyanti mamaiti putrāḥ // Saddhp_3.87 //
children.translated_text: And this triple world is my domain, for those who burn here are my children. // Saddhp 3.87 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca ādīnava tatra darśayī viditva trāṇaṃ ahameva caiṣām /
children.translated_text: And I show them the dangers there; knowing this, I alone am their protector.

children.text: na caiva me te śruṇi sarvi bālā yathāpi kāmeṣu vilagnabuddhayaḥ // Saddhp_3.88 //
children.translated_text: But none of those children listen to me, for their minds are attached to desires, like infants. // Saddhp 3.88 //

children.text: upāyakauśalyamahaṃ prayojayī yānāni trīṇi pravadāmi caiṣām /
children.translated_text: I employ <s>upāya-kauśalya</s> (skillful means), and I proclaim to them the three vehicles,

children.text: jñātvā ca traidhātuki nekadoṣān nirdhāvanārthāya vadāmyupāyam // Saddhp_3.89 //
children.translated_text: and knowing the many faults of the three realms, I teach a means for running forth from them. // Saddhp 3.89 //

body.text: māṃ caiva ye niśrita bhonti putrāḥ ṣaḍabhijña traividya mahānubhāvāḥ /
body.translated_text: And those children who rely on me become possessed of the six <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), the triple knowledge, and great power —

body.text: pratyekabuddhāśca bhavanti ye 'tra avivartikā ye ciha bodhisattvāḥ // Saddhp_3.90 //
body.translated_text: some become <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones), and others are <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who will not turn back. // Saddhp 3.90 //

children.text: samāna putrāṇa hu teṣa tatkṣaṇamimena dṛṣṭāntavareṇa paṇḍita /
children.translated_text: To all those children at that very moment, O wise one, by means of this supreme simile,

children.text: vadāmi ekaṃ imu buddhayānaṃ parigṛhṇathā sarvi jinā bhaviṣyatha // Saddhp_3.91 //
children.translated_text: I proclaim this one <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle): 'Accept it, all of you, and you shall become <s>Jinas</s> (victors)!' // Saddhp 3.91 //

children.text: taccā variṣṭhaṃ sumanoramaṃ ca viśiṣṭarūpaṃ ciha sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: And that is the most excellent, most delightful, of the most distinguished form in all the world —

children.text: buddhāna jñānaṃ dvipadottamānāmudārarūpaṃ tatha vandanīyam // Saddhp_3.92 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the best among two-footed beings, of noble form and worthy of veneration. // Saddhp 3.92 //

children.text: balāni dhyānāni tathā vimokṣāḥ samādhināṃ koṭiśatā ca nekā /
children.translated_text: The <s>balas</s> (powers), <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), and <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations), and many hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) —

children.text: ayaṃ ratho īdṛśako variṣṭho ramanti yeno sada buddhaputrāḥ // Saddhp_3.93 //
children.translated_text: this cart is of such a kind, most excellent; the children of the <s>Buddha</s> always delight in it. // Saddhp 3.93 //

children.text: krīḍanta etena kṣapenti rātrayo divasāṃśca pakṣānṛtavo 'tha māsān /
children.translated_text: Playing with it, they spend nights and days, and fortnights, seasons, and months,

children.text: saṃvatsarānantarakalpameva ca kṣapenti kalpāna sahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_3.94 //
children.translated_text: and years and intermediate <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) — they spend hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. // Saddhp 3.94 //

children.text: ratnāmayaṃ yānamidaṃ variṣṭhaṃ gacchanti yeno iha bodhimaṇḍe /
children.translated_text: This jeweled vehicle, the most excellent, is that by which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> proceed to the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),

children.text: vikrīḍamānā bahubodhisattvā ye co śṛṇonti sugatasya śrāvakāḥ // Saddhp_3.95 //
children.translated_text: sporting and playing, along with the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One). // Saddhp 3.95 //

children.text: evaṃ prajānāhi tvamadya tiṣya nāstīha yānaṃ dvitiyaṃ kahiṃcit /
children.translated_text: Therefore know this today, O <s>Tiṣya</s> (Śāriputra): there is no second vehicle anywhere.

children.text: diśo daśā sarva gaveṣayitvā sthāpetvupāyaṃ puruṣottamānām // Saddhp_3.96 //
children.translated_text: Search in all the ten directions — apart from the <s>upāya</s> (skillful means) of the supreme among men, there is none. // Saddhp 3.96 //

children.text: putrā mamā yūyamahaṃ pitā vo mayā ca niṣkāsita yūya duḥkhāt /
children.translated_text: You are my children and I am your father; by me you have been brought out from suffering,

children.text: paridahyamānā bahukalpakoṭayastraidhātukāto bhayabhairavātaḥ // Saddhp_3.97 //
children.translated_text: you who were being burned for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> in the fearful and terrifying triple world. // Saddhp 3.97 //

children.text: evaṃ ca haṃ tatra vadāmi nirvṛtimanirvṛtā yūya tathaiva cādya /
children.translated_text: And thus I declare <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation) there, though you are not yet truly in <s>nirvāṇa</s> even now;

children.text: saṃsāraduḥkhādiha yūya muktā bauddhaṃ tu yānaṃ va gaveṣitavyam // Saddhp_3.98 //
children.translated_text: you are freed here from the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), but the <s>Bauddha-yāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle) is still to be sought. // Saddhp 3.98 //

children.text: ye bodhisattvāśca ihāsti kecicchṛṇvanti sarve mama buddhanetrīm /
children.translated_text: And whatever <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are here, all of them hear my guidance as the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: upāyakauśalyamidaṃ jinasya yeno vinetī bahubodhisattvān // Saddhp_3.99 //
children.translated_text: this is the <s>upāya-kauśalya</s> (skillful means) of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), by which he trains many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. // Saddhp 3.99 //

children.text: hīneṣu kāmeṣu jugupsiteṣu ratā yadā bhontimi atra sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: When beings here are attached to base and contemptible desires,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ tadā bhāṣati lokanāyako ananyathāvādirihāryasatyam // Saddhp_3.100 //
children.translated_text: then the <s>Lokanāyaka</s> (Leader of the World) speaks of suffering — he who speaks nothing but truth — the <s>Āryasatya</s> (Noble Truth). // Saddhp 3.100 //

children.text: ye cāpi duḥkhasya ajānamānā mūlaṃ na paśyantiha bālabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those who, not knowing the root of suffering, with childish understanding do not see it —

children.text: mārgaṃ hi teṣāmanudarśayāmi samudāgamastṛṣṇa dukhasya saṃbhavaḥ // Saddhp_3.101 //
children.translated_text: to them I show the path: the arising (<s>samudaya</s>) is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>), the origin of suffering. // Saddhp 3.101 //

children.text: tṛṣṇānirodho 'tha sadā aniśritā nirodhasatyaṃ tṛtiyaṃ idaṃ me /
children.translated_text: The cessation of craving, ever unattached — this is my third truth, the truth of <s>nirodha</s> (cessation),

children.text: ananyathā yena ca mucyate naro mārgaṃ hi bhāvitva vimukta bhoti // Saddhp_3.102 //
children.translated_text: by which, unfailingly, a person is liberated; for having cultivated the <s>mārga</s> (path), one becomes liberated. // Saddhp 3.102 //

children.text: kutaśca te śārisutā vimuktā asantagrāhātu vimukta bhonti /
children.translated_text: But from what, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, are they liberated? They are freed from the grasping at what does not exist.

children.text: na ca tāva te sarvata mukta bhonti anirvṛtāṃstān vadatīha nāyakaḥ // Saddhp_3.103 //
children.translated_text: Yet they are not fully liberated in every respect — the <s>Nāyaka</s> (Guide) declares them to be not yet in <s>nirvāṇa</s>. // Saddhp 3.103 //

children.text: kikāraṇaṃ nāsya vadāmi mokṣamaprāpyimāmuttamamagrabodhim /
children.translated_text: For what reason do I not declare their liberation? Because they have not attained this supreme, foremost <s>bodhi</s> (awakening).

children.text: mamaiṣa chando ahu dharmarājā sukhāpanārthāyiha loki jātaḥ // Saddhp_3.104 //
children.translated_text: This is my desire — I am the <s>Dharmarāja</s> (King of the Dharma), born into the world for the purpose of bringing happiness. // Saddhp 3.104 //

body.text: iya śāriputrā mama dharmamudrā yā paścime kāli mayādya bhāṣitā /
body.translated_text: This, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is my <s>dharmamudrā</s> (dharma-seal), which I have proclaimed today in this final age.

body.text: hitāya lokasya sadevakasya diśāsu vidiśāsu ca deśayasva // Saddhp_3.105 //
body.translated_text: For the benefit of the world with its gods, teach it in all directions and quarters! // Saddhp 3.105 //

children.text: yaścāpi te bhāṣati kaści sattvo anumodayāmīti vadeta vācam /
children.translated_text: And if any being speaks to you and says the words, 'I rejoice in this!',

children.text: mūrdhnena cedaṃ pratigṛhya sūtraṃ avivartikaṃ taṃ naru dhārayestvam // Saddhp_3.106 //
children.translated_text: and receives this <s>sūtra</s> upon the crown of their head — know that person to be <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible, never turning back). // Saddhp 3.106 //

children.text: dṛṣṭāśca teno purimāstathāgatāḥ satkāru teṣāṃ ca kṛto abhūṣi /
children.translated_text: By that one, the former <s>Tathāgatas</s> have been seen, and worship of them has been performed,

children.text: śrutaśca dharmo ayamevarūpo ya eta sūtraṃ abhiśraddadheta // Saddhp_3.107 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Dharma</s> of this very nature has been heard — whoever has faith in this <s>sūtra</s>. // Saddhp 3.107 //

children.text: ahaṃ ca tvaṃ caiva bhaveta dṛṣṭo ayaṃ ca sarvo mama bhikṣusaṃghaḥ /
children.translated_text: I and you have been seen by such a one, and also all this community of my <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks),

children.text: dṛṣṭāśca sarve imi bodhisattvā ye śraddadhe bhāṣitameta mahyam // Saddhp_3.108 //
children.translated_text: and all these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> have been seen — by those who have faith in this, my teaching. // Saddhp 3.108 //

children.text: sūtraṃ imaṃ bālajanapramohanamabhijñajñānāna mi etu bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: This <s>sūtra</s>, which bewilders foolish people, has been spoken for those possessed of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) and <s>jñāna</s> (wisdom).

children.text: viṣayo hi naivāstiha śrāvakāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhāna gatirna cātra // Saddhp_3.109 //
children.translated_text: For this is not the domain of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), nor is it the sphere of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones). // Saddhp 3.109 //

children.text: adhimuktisārastuva śāriputra kiṃ vā punarmahya ime 'nyaśrāvakāḥ /
children.translated_text: The essence of your aspiration, O <s>Śāriputra</s> — and what more of these other <s>Śrāvakas</s> of mine?

children.text: ete 'pi śraddhāya mamaiva yānti pratyātmikaṃ jñānu na caiva vidyate // Saddhp_3.110 //
children.translated_text: They too go only by faith in my [teaching]; self-realized knowledge does not exist [for them]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.110 ||

children.text: mā caiva tvaṃ stambhiṣu mā ca māniṣu māyuktayogīna vadesi etat /
children.translated_text: Do not tell this to the obstinate, nor to the conceited, nor to those engaged in corrupt yoga;

children.text: bālā hi kāmeṣu sadā pramattā ajānakā dharmu kṣipeyu bhāṣitam // Saddhp_3.111 //
children.translated_text: for the childish, always heedless in sensual pleasures, unknowing, would reject the <s>Dharma</s> that is spoken. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.111 ||

children.text: upāyakauśalya kṣipitva mahyaṃ yā buddhanetrī sada loki saṃsthitā /
children.translated_text: Having rejected my skill in means — the guidance of the <s>Buddha</s> always established in the world —

children.text: bhṛkuṭiṃ karitvāna kṣipitva yānaṃ vipāku tasyeha śṛṇohi tīvram // Saddhp_3.112 //
children.translated_text: frowning and having rejected the vehicle — hear here the severe ripening [consequence] of that! || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.112 ||

children.text: kṣipitva sūtraṃ idamevarūpaṃ mayi tiṣṭhamāne parinirvṛte vā /
children.translated_text: Having rejected a <s>sūtra</s> of this kind — whether while I am present or after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: bhikṣūṣu vā teṣu khilāni kṛtvā teṣāṃ vipākaṃ mamihaṃ śṛṇohi // Saddhp_3.113 //
children.translated_text: or having harbored animosity toward those monks — hear from me here the ripening of that! || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.113 ||

children.text: cyutvā manuṣyeṣu avīci teṣāṃ pratiṣṭha bhotī paripūrṇakalpāt /
children.translated_text: Having fallen from among humans, their destination is <s>Avīci</s> — they stay there for a full <s>kalpa</s>;

children.text: tataśca bhūyo 'ntarakalpa nekāṃścyutāścyutāstatra patanti bālāḥ // Saddhp_3.114 //
children.translated_text: and then again, for many intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the childish fall there again and again, having fallen. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.114 ||

children.text: yadā ca narakeṣu cyutā bhavanti tataśca tiryakṣu vrajanti bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when they pass away from the hells, then they go again into the animal realm;

children.text: sudurbalāḥ śvānaśṛgālabhūtāḥ pareṣa krīḍāpanakā bhavanti // Saddhp_3.115 //
children.translated_text: feeble, becoming dogs and jackals — they become playthings for others. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.115 ||

children.text: varṇena te kālaka tatra bhonti kalmāṣakā vrāṇika kaṇḍulāśca /
children.translated_text: In color they become dark, spotted, mangy, and itchy;

children.text: nirlomakā durbala bhonti bhūyo vidveṣamāṇā mama agrabodhim // Saddhp_3.116 //
children.translated_text: hairless, they become weak again — those who loathe my supreme awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.116 ||

children.text: jugupsitā prāṇiṣu nitya bhonti loṣṭaprahārābhihatā rudantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Despised constantly among living beings, they weep, struck by clods;

children.text: daṇḍena saṃtrāsita tatra tatra kṣudhāpipāsāhata śuṣkagātrāḥ // Saddhp_3.117 //
children.translated_text: frightened here and there by sticks, with bodies dried up from hunger and thirst. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.117 ||

children.text: uṣṭrātha vā gardabha bhonti bhūyo bhāraṃ vahantaḥ kaśadaṇḍatāḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Or they become camels or donkeys again, carrying burdens, beaten with whips and sticks,

children.text: āhāracintāmanucintayanto ye buddhanetrī kṣipi bālabuddhayaḥ // Saddhp_3.118 //
children.translated_text: constantly thinking of food — those of childish intellect who reject the <s>Buddha's</s> guidance. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.118 ||

children.text: punaśca te kroṣṭuka bhonti tatra bībhatsakāḥ kāṇaka kuṇṭhakāśca /
children.translated_text: And again they become jackals there — repulsive, one-eyed, and stunted,

children.text: utpīḍitā grāmakumārakehi loṣṭaprahārābhihatāśca bālāḥ // Saddhp_3.119 //
children.translated_text: oppressed by village boys, the childish ones struck by clods. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.119 ||

body.text: tataścyavitvāna ca bhūyu bālāḥ pañcāśatīnāṃ sama yojanānām /
body.translated_text: Having fallen from there again, the childish become creatures with bodies fifty <s>yojanas</s> long —

body.text: dīrghātmabhāvā hi bhavanti prāṇino jaḍāśca mūḍhāḥ parivartamānāḥ // Saddhp_3.120 //
body.translated_text: stupid and dull, rolling about. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.120 ||

children.text: apādakā bhonti ca kroḍasakkino vikhādyamānā bahuprāṇikoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: They become footless, belly-crawlers, devoured by many <s>koṭis</s> of creatures;

children.text: sudāruṇāṃ te anubhonti vedanāṃ kṣipitva sūtraṃ idamevarūpam // Saddhp_3.121 //
children.translated_text: they experience terrible pain — having rejected a <s>sūtra</s> of this kind. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.121 ||

children.text: puruṣātmabhāvaṃ ca yada labhante te kuṇṭhakā laṅgaka bhonti tatra /
children.translated_text: And when they obtain a human body, they become stunted, lame,

children.text: kubjātha kāṇā ca jaḍā jaghanyā aśraddadhantā ima sūtra mahyam // Saddhp_3.122 //
children.translated_text: hunchbacked, one-eyed, stupid, and lowly — those who do not believe in this <s>sūtra</s> of mine. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.122 ||

children.text: apratyanīyāśca bhavanti loke pūtī mukhātteṣa pravāti gandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: They become unapproachable in the world — a foul stench issues from their mouths;

children.text: yakṣagraho ukrami teṣa kāye aśraddadhantānima buddhabodhim // Saddhp_3.123 //
children.translated_text: a <s>yakṣa</s>-possession lodges in their bodies — those who do not believe in this <s>Buddhabodhi</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.123 ||

children.text: daridrakā peṣaṇakārakāśca upasthāyakā nitya parasya durbalāḥ /
children.translated_text: They are poor, drudge-workers, always servants of others, feeble;

children.text: ābādha teṣāṃ bahukāśca bhonti anāthabhūtā viharanti loke // Saddhp_3.124 //
children.translated_text: their illnesses are many — they wander in the world as orphans. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.124 ||

children.text: yasyaiva te tatra karonti sevanāmadātukāmo bhavatī sa teṣām /
children.translated_text: The very one they there seek to serve becomes unwilling to give to them;

children.text: dattaṃ pi co naśyati kṣiprameva phalaṃ hi pāpasya imevarūpam // Saddhp_3.125 //
children.translated_text: and even what is given perishes quickly — such is the fruit of evil. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.125 ||

children.text: yaccāpi te tatra labhanti auṣadhaṃ suyuktarūpaṃ kuśalehi dattam /
children.translated_text: And whatever medicine they obtain there, well-compounded and given by the skilled,

children.text: tenāpi teṣāṃ ruja bhūyu vardhate so vyādhirantaṃ na kadāci gacchati // Saddhp_3.126 //
children.translated_text: even by that their disease further increases — that illness never comes to an end. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.126 ||

children.text: anyehi cauryāṇi kṛtāni bhonti ḍamarātha ḍimbāstatha vigrahāśca /
children.translated_text: Thefts committed by others, and riots, tumults, and conflicts,

children.text: dravyāpahārāśca kṛtāstathānyairnipatanti tasyopari pāpakarmaṇaḥ // Saddhp_3.127 //
children.translated_text: and robberies committed by others — [the consequences] fall upon that evil-doer. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.127 ||

body.text: na jātu so paśyati lokanāthaṃ narendrarājaṃ mahi śāsamānam /
body.translated_text: Never does he see the Lord of the World, the king among men, ruling the earth;

body.text: tasyākṣaṇeṣveva hi vāsu bhoti imāṃ kṣipitvā mama buddhanetrīm // Saddhp_3.128 //
body.translated_text: his dwelling is indeed in unfavorable states — having rejected this <s>Buddha</s>-guidance of mine. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.128 ||

children.text: na cāpi so dharma śṛṇoti bālo badhiraśca so bhoti acetanaśca /
children.translated_text: Nor does that fool hear the <s>Dharma</s> — he becomes deaf and unconscious;

children.text: kṣipitva bodhīmimamevarūpāmupaśānti tasyo na kadāci bhoti // Saddhp_3.129 //
children.translated_text: having rejected this awakening of such a kind, peace never comes to him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.129 ||

children.text: sahasra nekā nayutāṃśca bhūyaḥ kalpāna koṭyo yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: For many thousands, and <s>nayutas</s>, and furthermore <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: jaḍātmabhāvo vikalaśca bhoti kṣipitva sūtraṃ imu pāpakaṃ phalam // Saddhp_3.130 //
children.translated_text: he becomes stupid and crippled — the evil fruit of having rejected this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.130 ||

children.text: udyānabhūmī narako 'sya bhoti niveśanaṃ tasya apāyabhūmiḥ /
children.translated_text: A park-ground is his hell; his dwelling is the realm of misery;

children.text: kharasūkarā kroṣṭuka bhūmisūcakāḥ pratiṣṭhitasyeha bhavanti nityam // Saddhp_3.131 //
children.translated_text: donkeys, pigs, jackals, and earthworms are his constant companions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.131 ||

children.text: manuṣyabhāvatvamupetya cāpi andhatva badhiratva jaḍatvameti /
children.translated_text: And when he attains a human state, he goes to blindness, deafness, and stupidity;

children.text: parapreṣya so bhoti daridra nityaṃ tatkāli tasyābharaṇānimāni // Saddhp_3.132 //
children.translated_text: he is always a servant of others, poor — such are his ornaments at that time. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.132 ||

children.text: vastrāṇi co vyādhayu bhonti tasya vraṇāna koṭīnayutāśca kāye /
children.translated_text: Diseases are his garments; wounds in <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> on his body;

children.text: vicarcikā kaṇḍu tathaiva pāmā kuṣṭhaṃ kilāsaṃ tatha āmagandhaḥ // Saddhp_3.133 //
children.translated_text: eczema, itch, and scabs, leprosy, leucoderma, and raw stench. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.133 ||

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭiśca ghanāsya bhoti udīryate krodhabalaṃ ca tasya /
children.translated_text: The view of the personal body (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) becomes dense for him; the force of anger rises in him;

children.text: saṃrāgu tasyātibhṛśaṃ ca bhoti tiryāṇa yonīṣu ca so sadā ramī // Saddhp_3.134 //
children.translated_text: his passion is exceedingly intense, and he always delights in animal wombs. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.134 ||

children.text: sacedahaṃ śārisutādya tasya paripūrṇakalpaṃ pravadeya doṣān /
children.translated_text: If I, O son of <s>Śāri</s>, were to speak today for a full <s>kalpa</s> of the faults of him

children.text: yo hī mamā etu kṣipeta sūtraṃ paryantu doṣāṇa na śakya gantum // Saddhp_3.135 //
children.translated_text: who rejects this <s>sūtra</s> of mine — the end of [his] faults cannot be reached. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.135 ||

children.text: saṃpaśyamāno idameva cārthaṃ tvāṃ saṃdiśāmī ahu śāriputra /
children.translated_text: Looking upon this very matter, I instruct you, O <s>Śāriputra</s> —

children.text: mā haiva tvaṃ bālajanasya agrato bhāṣiṣyase sūtramimevarūpam // Saddhp_3.136 //
children.translated_text: you should never speak such a <s>sūtra</s> before childish people! || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.136 ||

children.text: ye tū iha vyakta bahuśrutāśca smṛtimanta ye paṇḍita jñānavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: But those here who are clear[-minded], of much learning, mindful, wise, and possessed of knowledge,

children.text: ye prasthitā uttamamagrabodhiṃ tān śrāvayestvaṃ paramārthametat // Saddhp_3.137 //
children.translated_text: and those set forth toward the supreme, foremost awakening — to them you should proclaim this supreme truth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.137 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭāśca yehī bahubuddhakoṭyaḥ kuśalaṃ ca yai ropitamaprameyam /
children.translated_text: And those by whom many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> have been seen, and immeasurable merit has been planted,

children.text: adhyāśayāścā dṛḍha yeṣa co syāttān śrāvayestvaṃ paramārthametat // Saddhp_3.138 //
children.translated_text: and whose aspiration is firm — to them you should proclaim this supreme truth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.138 ||

children.text: ye vīryavantaḥ sada maitracittā bhāventi maitrīmiha dīrgharātram /
children.translated_text: Those who are vigorous, always with minds of loving-kindness, who cultivate <s>maitrī</s> through this long night,

children.text: utsṛṣṭakāyā tatha jīvite ca teṣāmidaṃ sūtra bhaṇeḥ samakṣam // Saddhp_3.139 //
children.translated_text: who have surrendered body and life — before them you should recite this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.139 ||

children.text: anyonyasaṃkalpa sagauravāśca teṣāṃ ca bālehi na saṃstavo 'sti /
children.translated_text: Those who are respectful toward one another and are not in the company of the childish,

children.text: ye cāpi tuṣṭā girikandareṣu tān śrāvayestvaṃ ida sūtra bhadrakam // Saddhp_3.140 //
children.translated_text: and those who are contented in mountain caves — to them you should proclaim this excellent <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.140 ||

children.text: kalyāṇamitrāṃśca niṣevamāṇāḥ pāpāṃśca mitrān parivarjayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who attend upon good friends and avoid evil friends —

children.text: yānīdṛśān paśyasi buddhaputrāṃsteṣāmidaṃ sūtra prakāśayesi // Saddhp_3.141 //
children.translated_text: whatever sons of the <s>Buddha</s> of such a kind you see — to them you should illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.141 ||

children.text: acchidraśīlā maṇiratnasādṛśā vaipulyasūtrāṇa parigrahe sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of unbroken morality, resembling a jewel-gem, established in the preservation of <s>vaipulya sūtras</s> —

children.text: paśyesi yānīdṛśa buddhaputrāṃsteṣāgrataḥ sūtramidaṃ vadesi // Saddhp_3.142 //
children.translated_text: whatever sons of the <s>Buddha</s> of such a kind you see — before them you should speak this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.142 ||

body.text: akrodhanā ye sada ārjavāśca kṛpāsamanvāgata sarvaprāṇiṣu /
body.translated_text: Those who are always free from anger, upright, compassionate toward all living beings,

body.text: sagauravā ye sugatasya antike teṣāgrataḥ sūtramidaṃ vadesi // Saddhp_3.143 //
body.translated_text: and respectful in the presence of the <s>Sugata</s> — before them you should speak this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.143 ||

children.text: yo dharmu bhāṣe pariṣāya madhye asaṅgaprāpto vadi yuktamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who speaks the <s>Dharma</s> in the midst of an assembly, who is unattached, who speaks with a focused mind,

children.text: dṛṣṭāntakoṭīnayutairanekaistasyeda sūtraṃ upadarśayesi // Saddhp_3.144 //
children.translated_text: with innumerable <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of illustrations — to him you should show this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.144 ||

children.text: mūrdhnāñjaliṃ yaśca karoti baddhvā sarvajñabhāvaṃ parimārgamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And one who makes prostration with joined palms at the head, seeking the state of omniscience,

children.text: daśo diśo yo 'pi ca caṃkrameta subhāṣitaṃ bhikṣu gaveṣamāṇaḥ // Saddhp_3.145 //
children.translated_text: who walks back and forth in the ten directions, a monk seeking well-spoken [teachings] — || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.145 ||

children.text: vaipulyasūtrāṇi ca dhārayeta na cāsya rucyanti kadācidanye /
children.translated_text: who upholds <s>vaipulya sūtras</s> and never delights in other [texts],

children.text: ekāṃ pi gāthāṃ na ca dhāraye 'nyatastaṃ śrāvayestvaṃ varasūtrametat // Saddhp_3.146 //
children.translated_text: who would not even retain a single verse from elsewhere — to him you should proclaim this excellent <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.146 ||

children.text: tathāgatasyo yatha dhātu dhārayettathaiva yo mārgati koci taṃ naraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as one would preserve a relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so one who seeks that man;

children.text: emeva yo mārgati sūtramīdṛśaṃ labhitva yo mūrdhani dhārayeta // Saddhp_3.147 //
children.translated_text: just so, one who seeks a <s>sūtra</s> of this kind — having obtained it, he should uphold it upon his head. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.147 ||

children.text: anyeṣu sūtreṣu na kāci cintā lokāyatairanyataraiśca śāstraiḥ /
children.translated_text: One who has no interest in other <s>sūtras</s>, in <s>Lokāyata</s>, or in other treatises —

children.text: bālāna etādṛśa bhonti gocarāstāṃstvaṃ vivarjitva prakāśayeridam // Saddhp_3.148 //
children.translated_text: such are the domains of the childish — avoiding them, you should illuminate this [sūtra]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.148 ||

children.text: pūrṇaṃ pi kalpaṃ ahu śāriputra vadeyamākāra sahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even for a full <s>kalpa</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, I could describe hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of forms [of recipients];

children.text: ye prasthitā uttamamagrabodhiṃ teṣāgrataḥ sūtramidaṃ vadesi // Saddhp_3.149 //
children.translated_text: those set forth toward the supreme, foremost awakening — before them you should speak this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 3.149 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye aupamyaparivarto nāma tṛtīyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the third chapter, called the chapter on simile (<s>aupamyaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_4: adhimuktiparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 4: The chapter on resolve (<s>adhimuktiparivarta</s>).

body.text:
atha khalvāyuṣmān subhūtirāyuṣmāṃśca mahākātyāyanaḥ āyuṣmāṃśca mahākāśyapaḥ āyuṣmāṃśca mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ imamevaṃrūpamaśrutapūrvaṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā bhagavato 'ntikāt saṃmukhamāyuṣmataśca śāriputrasya vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā audbilyaprāptā stasyāṃ velāyāmutthāyāsanebhyo yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāman | upasaṃkramya ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānuṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantamabhimukhamullokayamānā avanakāyā abhinatakāyāḥ praṇatakāyāstasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantametadavocan - vayaṃ hi bhagavan jīrṇā vṛddhā mahallakā asmin bhikṣusaṃghe sthavirasaṃmatā jarājīrṇībhūtā nirvāṇaprāptāḥ sma iti bhagavan nirudyamā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāvapratibalāḥ smaḥ, aprativīryārambhāḥ smaḥ | yadāpi bhagavān dharmaṃ deśayati, ciraṃ niṣaṇṇaśca bhagavān bhavati, vayaṃ ca tasyāṃ dharmadeśanāyāṃ pratyupasthitā bhavāmaḥ, tadāpyasmākaṃ bhagavan ciraṃ niṣaṇṇānāṃ bhagavantaṃ ciraṃ paryupāsitānāmaṅgapratyaṅgāni duḥkhanti, saṃdhivisaṃdhayaśca duḥkhanti |
tato vayaṃ bhagavan bhagavato dharmaṃ deśayamānasya śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitaṃ sarvamāviṣkurmaḥ | nāsmābhireṣu buddhadharmeṣu buddhakṣetravyūheṣu vā bodhisattvavikrīḍiteṣu vā tathāgatavikrīḍiteṣu vā spṛhotpāditā | tatkasya hetoḥ? yaccāsmādbhagavaṃstraidhātukānnirdhāvitā nirvāṇasaṃjñinaḥ, vayaṃ ca jarājīrṇāḥ | tato bhagavan asmābhirapyanye bodhisattvā avavaditā abhūvannanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, anuśiṣṭāśca | na ca bhagavaṃstatrāsmābhirekamapi spṛhācittamutpāditamabhūt | te vayaṃ bhagavannetarhi bhagavato 'ntikācchrāvakāṇāmapi vyākaraṇamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau bhavatīti śrutvā āścaryādbhutaprāptā mahālābhaprāptāḥ smaḥ | bhagavannadya sahasaivemamevaṃrūpamaśrutapūrvaṃ tathāgataghoṣaṃ śrutvā mahāratnapratilabdhāśca smaḥ | bhagavan aprameyaratnapratilabdhāśca smaḥ | bhagavan amārgitamaparyeṣṭamacintitamaprārthitaṃ cāsmābhirbhagavannidamevaṃ rūpaṃ mahāratnaṃ pratilabdham | pratibhāti no bhagavan, pratibhāti naḥ sugata | tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan kaścideva puruṣaḥ piturantikādapakrāmet | so 'pakramya anyataraṃ janapadapradeśaṃ gacchet | sa tatra bahūni varṣāṇi vipravased viṃśatiṃ vā triṃśadvā catvāriṃśadvā pañcāśadvā | atha sa bhagavan mahān puruṣo bhavet | sa ca daridraḥ syāt | sa ca vṛttiṃ paryeṣamāṇa āhāracīvarahetordiśo vidiśaḥ prakāman anyataraṃ janapadapradeśaṃ gacchet | tasya ca sa pitā anyatamaṃ janapadaṃ prakrāntaḥ syāt | bahudhanadhānyahiraṇyakośakoṣṭhāgāraśca bhavet | bahusuvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatasamanvāgataśca bhavet | bahudāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyaśca bhavet | bahuhastyaśvarathagaveḍakasamanvāgataśca bhavet | mahāparivāraśca bhavet | mahājanapadeṣu ca dhanikaḥ syāt | āyogaprayogakṛṣivaṇijyaprabhūtaśca bhavet ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, and the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having heard from the Blessed One this <s>Dharma</s> of such a form, never heard before, and having heard the prophecy for the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening directly [from the Blessed One], were struck with wonder, amazement, and exultation. At that time, they rose from their seats and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, placing their right knees on the ground, bowing with joined palms toward the Blessed One, gazing upon the Blessed One face to face, with bodies bowed, bent, and inclined, they said this to the Blessed One at that time: "We, Blessed One, are old, aged, and decrepit in this community of monks, honored as elders, worn out with age. We were, Blessed One, [thinking ourselves] 'We have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>,' without exertion toward unsurpassed perfect awakening, without vigor or effort. Even when the Blessed One teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, and the Blessed One has been seated for a long time, and we have been present at that <s>Dharma</s>-teaching — even then, Blessed One, after we have been seated for a long time and have attended upon the Blessed One for a long time, our limbs and joints ache, and our joints and sinews ache. Therefore, Blessed One, hearing the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s>, we acknowledged everything — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. We did not generate any aspiration for these <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, or for the arrays of <s>Buddha</s>-fields, or for the sport of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, or for the sport of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Why? Because, Blessed One, we have been driven out from the three realms, perceiving ourselves as attainers of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and we are worn out with age. Therefore, Blessed One, though we have admonished other <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and instructed them in unsurpassed perfect awakening, not even a single thought of aspiration was generated by us regarding that. But now, Blessed One, hearing from the Blessed One that there is a prophecy for <s>Śrāvakas</s> too regarding unsurpassed perfect awakening, we have been struck with wonder and amazement and attained great gain! Blessed One, today, suddenly, hearing this unprecedented proclamation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> of such a form, we have obtained a great treasure! Blessed One, we have obtained an immeasurable treasure! Blessed One, this great treasure of such a form has been obtained by us unsought, unlooked for, unthought of, and unprayed for. A parable occurs to us, Blessed One; a parable occurs to us, <s>Sugata</s>. It is as if, Blessed One, a certain man departed from his father's presence. Having departed, he would go to another region of the country. He would live there in exile for many years — twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty. Then, Blessed One, that man would become old. And he would be poor. And while seeking a livelihood, for the sake of food and clothing, he would go in all directions to another region of the country. And his father would have moved to another country. He would have great wealth — grain, gold, treasuries, and storehouses. He would be endowed with much gold, silver, jewels, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch-shells, crystal, coral, real gold, and refined silver. He would have many male and female servants, workers, and attendants. He would be endowed with many elephants, horses, chariots, cattle, and sheep. He would have a great retinue. And he would be wealthy in great countries. He would be prosperous in trade, farming, commerce, and industry."

body.text: athe khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣa āhāracīvaraparyeṣṭihetorgrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīṣu paryaṭamāno 'nupūrveṇa yatrāsau puruṣo bahudhanahiraṇyasuvarṇakośakoṣṭhāgārastasyaiva pitā vasati, tannagaramanuprāpto bhavet | atha khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣasya pitā bahudhanahiraṇyakośakoṣṭhāgārastasmin nagare vasamānastaṃ pañcāśadvarṣanaṣṭaṃ putraṃ satatasamitamanusmaret | samanusmaramāṇaśca na kasyacidācakṣedanyatraika evātmanādhyātmaṃ saṃtapyet, evaṃ ca cintayet - ahamasmi jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ | prabhūtaṃ me hiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāraṃ saṃvidyate | na ca me putraḥ kaścidasti | mā haiva mama kālakriyā bhavet | sarvamidamaparibhuktaṃ vinaśyet | sa taṃ punaḥ punaḥ putramanusmaret - aho nāmāhaṃ nirvṛtiprāpto bhaveyaṃ yadi me sa putra imaṃ dhanaskandhaṃ paribhuñjīta ||
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that poor man, while wandering through villages, towns, marketplaces, countries, kingdoms, and capital cities in search of food and clothing, would gradually arrive at that very city where his father — the man of great wealth, gold, treasuries, and storehouses — was dwelling. Now, Blessed One, that poor man's father, the man of great wealth, gold, treasuries, and storehouses, while dwelling in that city, would constantly remember that son who had been lost for fifty years. While remembering, he would not tell anyone, but would grieve inwardly all alone, and would think thus: 'I am old, aged, and decrepit. I have abundant gold, silver, wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. But I have no son. What if my death should come! All this would perish unenjoyed.' He would remember that son again and again — 'Ah, if only I could attain contentment, if my son could enjoy this mass of wealth!'"

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣa āhāracīvaraṃ paryeṣamāṇo 'nupūrveṇa yena tasya prabhūtahiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasya samṛddhasya puruṣasya niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmet | atha khalu bhagavan sa tasya daridrapuruṣasya pitā svake niveśanadvāre mahatyā brāhmaṇakṣatriyaviṭśūdrapariṣadā parivṛtaḥ puraskṛto mahāsiṃhāsane sapādapīṭhe suvarṇarūpyapratimaṇḍite upaviṣṭo hiraṇyakoṭīśatasahasrairvyavahāraṃ kurvan vālavyajanena vījyamāno vitatavitāne pṛthivīpradeśe muktakusumābhikīrṇe ratnadāmābhipralambite mahatyaddharyā upaviṣṭaḥ syāt | adrākṣīt sa bhagavan daridrapuruṣastaṃ svakaṃ pitaraṃ svake niveśanadvāre evaṃrūpayā ṛdhyā upaviṣṭaṃ mahatā janakāyena parivṛtaṃ gṛhapatikṛtyaṃ kurvāṇam | dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhītastrastaḥ saṃvignaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaromakūpajātaḥ udvignamānasaḥ evamanuvicintayāmāsa - sahasaivāyaṃ mayā rājā vā rājamātro vā āsāditaḥ | nāstyasmākamiha kiṃcit karma | gacchāmo vayaṃ yena daridravīthī, tatrāsmākamāhāracīvaramalpakṛcchreṇaiva utpatsyate | alaṃ me ciraṃ vilambitena | mā haivāhamiha vaiṣṭiko vā gṛhyeya, anyataraṃ vā doṣamanuprāpnuyām ||
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that poor man, while seeking food and clothing, would gradually approach the residence of that prosperous man of great gold, silver, wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. Now, Blessed One, the father of that poor man, at the door of his own residence, surrounded and honored by a great assembly of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, <s>vaiśyas</s>, and <s>śūdras</s>, was seated on a great lion-throne with footstool, adorned with gold and silver, transacting business with hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of gold, being fanned with a yak-tail fan, on a stretch of ground under a wide canopy, strewn with loose flowers, hung with jeweled garlands, seated in great splendor. That poor man, Blessed One, saw his own father seated at the door of his own residence in such splendor, surrounded by a great assembly of people, performing the duties of a householder. Having seen him, he became frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, with an agitated mind, and reflected thus: 'I have suddenly encountered a king or one equal to a king! There is no work for me here. Let me go to the poor quarter — there, food and clothing will be obtained with little difficulty. Enough of my long delay here! Lest I be seized here as a forced laborer, or incur some other punishment.'"

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣo duḥkhaparaṃparāmanasikārabhayabhītastvaramāṇaḥ prakrāmet palāyet, na tatra saṃtiṣṭhet | atha khalu bhagavan sa āḍhyaḥ puruṣaḥ svake niveśanadvāre siṃhāsane upaviṣṭastaṃ svakaṃ putraṃ sahadarśanenaiva pratyabhijānīyāt | dṛṣṭvā ca punastuṣṭa udagra āttamanaskaḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhavet, evaṃ ca cintayet - āścaryaṃ yāvad yatra hi nāma asya mahato hiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgārasya paribhoktā upalabdhaḥ | ahaṃ caitameva punaḥ punaḥ samanusmarāmi | ayaṃ ca svayamevehāgataḥ | ahaṃ ca jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ ||
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that poor man, frightened by the succession of suffering, mindful of fear, went hastily, fled, and did not remain there. Now, Blessed One, that wealthy man, seated on his lion-throne at the door of his own residence, recognized that very son of his at the very first glance. Having seen him, he was joyful, elated, delighted, glad, filled with pleasure and gladness, and thought thus: 'How wonderful, that the one who will enjoy this great [wealth of] gold, silver, property, grain, treasuries, and storehouses has been found! And I have been remembering him again and again! And he himself has come here! And I am old, aged, and decrepit.'"

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa puruṣaḥ putratṛṣṇāsaṃpīḍitastasmin kṣaṇalavamuhūrte javanān puruṣān saṃpreṣayet - gacchata mārṣā etaṃ puruṣaṃ śīghramānayadhvam | atha khalu bhagavaṃste puruṣāḥ rsava eva javena pradhāvitāstaṃ daridrapuruṣamadhyālambeyuḥ | atha khalu daridrapuruṣastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhītastrastaḥ saṃvignaḥ saṃhṛṣṭaromakūpajātaḥ udvigramānaso dāruṇamārtasvaraṃ muñcedāraved viravet | nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ kiṃcidaparādhyāmīti vācaṃ bhāṣeta | atha khalu te puruṣā balātkāreṇa taṃ
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that man, tormented by longing for his son, at that very moment dispatched swift men: 'Go, sirs, bring that man here quickly!' Then, Blessed One, those men, running at great speed, seized that poor man. Then, at that time, the poor man, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, with an agitated mind, uttered a terrible cry of distress, wailing and crying out: 'I have committed no offense against you!' — he spoke these words. But those men forcibly dragged that poor man, even as he cried out. Then that poor man, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with an agitated mind, thought thus: 'Surely I shall be punished or beaten! I am ruined!' He fainted and fell to the ground, and became unconscious. And his father was nearby. He said to those men: 'Do not, sirs, bring this man!' And having sprinkled him with cool water, he spoke to him no further. Why? That householder knew the low disposition of that poor man, and [knew] his own exalted position. And he knew: 'This is my son.'"

body.text: daridrapuruṣaṃ viravantamapyākarṣeyuḥ | atha khalu sa daridrapuruṣo bhītastrastaḥ saṃvigna udvignamānasa evaṃ ca cintayet - mā tāvadahaṃ vadhyo daṇḍayo bhaveyam | naśyāmīti | sa mūrchito dharaṇyāṃ prapatet, visaṃjñaśca syāt | āsanne cāsya sa pitā bhavet | sa tān puruṣānevaṃ vadet - mā bhavanta etaṃ puruṣamānayantviti | tamenaṃ śītalena vāriṇā parisiñcitvā na bhūya ālapet | tatkasya hetoḥ? jānāti sa gṛhapatistasya daridrapuruṣasya hīnādhimuktikatāmātmanaścodārasthāmatām | jānīte ca mamaiṣa putra iti ||
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that poor man, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with an agitated mind, thought thus: 'Let me not be subject to execution or punishment! I am lost!' He fainted and fell to the ground, and became unconscious. And his father was nearby. He said to those men: 'Do not, sirs, bring this man!' And having sprinkled him with cool water, he spoke to him no further. Why? That householder knew the low disposition of that poor man, and [knew] his own exalted position. And he knew: 'This is my son.'"

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa gṛhapatirupāyakauśalyena na kasyacidācakṣet - mamaiṣa putra iti | atha khalu bhagavan sa gṛhapatiranyataraṃ puruṣamāmantrayet - gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa | enaṃ daridrapuruṣamevaṃ vadasva - gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa yenākāṅkṣasi | mukto 'si | evaṃ vadati sa puruṣastasmai pratiśrutya yena sa daridrapuruṣastenopasaṃkrāmet | upasaṃkramya taṃ daridrapuruṣamevaṃ vadet - gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa yenākāṅkṣasi | mukto 'sīti | atha khalu sa daridrapuruṣa idaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā āścaryādbhutaprāpto bhavet | sa utthāya tasmāt pṛthivīpradeśādyena daridravīthī tenopasaṃkrāmedāhāracīvaraparyeṣṭihetoḥ | atha khalu sa gṛhapatistasya daridrapuruṣasyākarṣaṇahetorupāyakauśalyaṃ prayojayet | sa tatra dvau puruṣau prayojayet durvarṇāvalpaujaskau - gacchatāṃ bhavantau yo 'sau puruṣa ihāgato 'bhūt, taṃ yuvāṃ dviguṇayā divasamudrayā ātmavacanenaiva bharayitveha mama niveśane karma kārāpayethām | sacet sa evaṃ vadet - kiṃ karma kartavyamiti, sa yuvābhyāmevaṃ vaktavyaḥ - saṃkāradhānaṃ śodhayitavyaṃ sahāvābhyāmiti | atha tau puruṣau taṃ daridrapuruṣaṃ paryeṣayitvā tayā kriyayā saṃpādayetām | atha khalu tau dvau puruṣau sa ca daridrapuruṣo vetanaṃ gṛhītvā tasya mahādhanasya puruṣasyāntikāttasminneva niveśane saṃkāradhānaṃ śodhayeyuḥ | tasyaiva ca mahādhanasya puruṣasya gṛhaparisare kaṭapalikuñcikāyāṃ vāsaṃ kalpayeyuḥ | sa cāḍhyaḥ puruṣo gavākṣavātāyanena taṃ svakaṃ putraṃ paśyet saṃkāradhānaṃ śodhayamānam | dṛṣṭvā ca punarāścaryaprāpto bhavet ||
body.translated_text: "Then, Blessed One, that householder, through skillful means, did not tell anyone: 'This is my son.' Then, Blessed One, that householder addressed a certain man: 'Go, good man. Say this to that poor man: Go, good man, wherever you wish. You are free.' That man, having assented, approached that poor man. Having approached, he said this to the poor man: 'Go, good man, wherever you wish. You are free.' Then that poor man, hearing these words, was struck with wonder and amazement. He arose from that spot and went to the poor quarter, in search of food and clothing. Then that householder, in order to attract that poor man, employed skillful means. He employed two men there — ugly and of little strength: 'Go, both of you. That man who came here — you two, hiring him at double the daily wage, with your own words, have him do work here at my residence. If he should say, "What work is to be done?" — you two should say to him: "The refuse-heap is to be cleaned, together with both of us."' Then those two men, having sought out that poor man, engaged him in that task. Then those two men and that poor man, having received wages from that man of great wealth, cleaned the refuse-heap at that very residence. And they arranged their dwelling in a reed-hut on the grounds of that very wealthy man's estate. And that wealthy man would observe his own son through a lattice window, cleaning the refuse-heap. Having seen him, he would be struck with wonder."

body.text: atha khalu sa gṛhapatiḥ svakānniveśanādavatīrya apanayitvā mālyābharaṇani, apanayitvā mṛdukāni vastrāṇi, caukṣāṇyudārāṇi malināni vastrāṇi prāvṛtya, dakṣiṇena pāṇinā piṭakaṃ parigṛhya pāṃsunā svagātraṃ dūṣayitvā dūrata eva saṃbhāṣamāṇo yena sa daridrapuruṣastenopasaṃkrāmet | upasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadet - vahantu bhavantaḥ piṭakāni, mā tiṣṭhata, harata pāṃsūni | anenopāyena taṃ putramālapet saṃlapecca | enaṃ vadet - ihaiva tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa karma kuruṣva | mā bhūyo 'nyatra gamiṣyasi | saviśeṣaṃ te 'haṃ vetanakaṃ dāsyāmi | yena yena ca te kārya bhavet, tadviśrabdhaṃ māṃ yāceḥ, yadi vā kuṇḍamūlyena yadi vā kuṇḍikāmūlyena yadi vā sthālikāmūlyena yadi vā kāṣṭhamūlyena yadi vā lavaṇamūlyena yadi vā bhojanena yadi vā prāvaraṇena | asti me bhoḥ puruṣa jīrṇaśāṭī | sacettayā te kāryaṃ syāt, yāceḥ, ahaṃ te 'nupradāsyāmi | yena yena te bhoḥ puruṣa kāryamevaṃrūpeṇa pariṣkāreṇa, taṃ tamevāhaṃ te sarvamanupradāsyāmi | nirvṛtastvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa bhava | yādṛśaste pitā, tādṛśaste 'haṃ mantavyaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? ahaṃ
body.translated_text: 'Then that householder, descending from his own dwelling, having removed his garlands and ornaments, having removed his soft garments, putting on pure, magnificent, [but] soiled garments, grasping a basket in his right hand, smearing his own body with dust, speaking from a distance, would approach that poor man. Having approached, he would say thus: "Carry the baskets, sirs, do not stand idle, remove the rubbish!" By this means he would entice that son and converse with him. He would say to him: "Do your work right here, good man! Do not go elsewhere again. I shall give you extra wages. Whatever you may need, ask me for it confidently — whether for the price of a pot, or a water-jar, or a pan, or firewood, or salt, or food, or a covering garment. I have, good man, an old cloak. If you should need it, ask, and I shall give it to you. Whatever you need, good man, in the way of such provisions — all that I shall give to you. Be at ease, good man. Consider me as if I were your father. For what reason? I am

body.text: ca vṛddhaḥ, tvaṃ ca daharaḥ | mama ca tvayā bahu karma kṛtamimaṃ saṃkāradhānaṃ śodhayatā | na ca tvayā bhoḥ puruṣa atra karma kurvatā śāṭhayaṃ vā vakratā vā kauṭilyaṃ vā māno vā mrakṣo vā kṛtapūrvaḥ, karoṣi vā | sarvathā te bhoḥ puruṣa na samanupaśyāmyekamapi pāpakarma, yathaiṣāmanyeṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ karma kurvatāmime doṣāḥ saṃvidyante | yādṛśo me putra aurasaḥ, tādṛśastvaṃ mama adyāgreṇa bhavasi ||
body.translated_text: old, and you are young. And much work has been done by you for me in cleaning this rubbish-heap. And while doing work here, good man, you have never before committed treachery, crookedness, deceit, conceit, or hypocrisy, nor do you [now]. In every way, good man, I do not observe even a single evil deed in you, whereas these faults are found in other men doing work. You are, from today onward, like my own natural-born son."'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa gṛhapatistasya daridrapuruṣasya putra iti nāma kuryāt | sa ca daridrapuruṣastasya gṛhapaterantike pitṛsaṃjñāmutpādayet | anena bhagavan paryāyeṇa sa gṛhapatiḥ putrakāmatṛṣito viṃśativarṣāṇi taṃ putraṃ saṃkāradhānaṃ śodhāpayet | atha viṃśatervarṣāṇāmatyayena sa daridrapuruṣastasya gṛhapaterniveśane viśrabdho bhavenniṣkramaṇapraveśe, tatraiva ca kaṭapalikuñcikāyāṃ vāsaṃ kalpayet ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, Blessed One, that householder would give to that poor man the name of "son." And that poor man would generate the perception of "father" toward that householder. In this way, Blessed One, that householder, consumed by the longing for a son, would have that son clean the rubbish-heap for twenty years. After the passage of twenty years, that poor man would become confident in the householder's dwelling regarding going out and coming in, and would take up his lodging right there in the straw hut.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavaṃstasya gṛhapaterglānyaṃ pratyupasthitaṃ bhavet | sa maraṇakālasamayaṃ ca ātmanaḥ pratyupasthitaṃ samanupaśyet | sa taṃ daridrapuruṣamevaṃ vadet - āgaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa | idaṃ mama prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāramasti | ahaṃ bāḍhaglānaḥ | icchāmyetaṃ yasya dātavyaṃ yataśca grahītavyaṃ yacca nidhātavyaṃ bhavet, sarvaṃ saṃjānīyāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yādṛśa eva ahamasya dravyasya svāmī, tādṛśastvamapi | mā ca me tvaṃ kiṃcidato vipraṇāśayiṣyasi ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, Blessed One, illness would afflict that householder. And he would perceive the time of death as having arrived for himself. He would say to that poor man thus: "Come, good man. I have here abundant gold, silver, riches, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. I am severely ill. I wish [you] to know all of this — to whom it should be given, from whom it should be received, and what should be stored. For what reason? Just as I myself am the owner of this wealth, so too are you. And you shall not let any of it be lost."'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣo 'nena paryāyeṇa tacca tasya gṛhapateḥ prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāraṃ saṃjānīyāt | ātmanā ca tato niḥspṛho bhavet | na ca tasmāt kiṃcit prārthayet, antaśaḥ saktuprasthamūlyamātramapi | tatraiva ca kaṭapalikuñcikāyāṃ vāsaṃ kalpayet, tāmeva daridracintāmanuvicintayamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, Blessed One, that poor man, through this method, would know about that householder's abundant gold, silver, riches, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. But he himself would have no desire for it. He would not seek even the slightest thing from it — not even the price of a handful of barley-flour. He would take up his lodging right there in the straw hut, still reflecting on his own poor thoughts.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa gṛhapatistaṃ putraṃ śaktaṃ paripālakaṃ paripakvaṃ viditvā avamarditacittamudārasaṃjñayā ca paurvikayā daridracintayā ārtīyantaṃ jehrīyamāṇaṃ jugupsamānaṃ viditvā maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite taṃ daridrapuruṣamānāyya mahato jñātisaṃghasyopanāmayitvā rājño vā rājamātrasya vā purato naigamajānapadānāṃ ca saṃmukhamevaṃ saṃśrāvayet - śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ, ayaṃ mama putra auraso mayaiva janitaḥ | amukaṃ nāma nagaram | tasmādeṣa pañcāśadvarṣo naṣṭaḥ | amuko nāmaiṣa nāmnā | ahamapyamuko nāma | tataścāhaṃ nagarādetameva mārgamāṇa ihāgataḥ | eṣa mama putraḥ, ahamasya pitā | yaḥ kaścinmamopabhogo 'sti, taṃ sarvamasmai puruṣāya niryātayāmi | yacca me kiṃcidasti pratyātmakaṃ dhanam, tatsarvameṣa eva jānāti ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, Blessed One, that householder, knowing that son to be capable, responsible, and mature, and perceiving that his mind was humbled, that he was distressed, ashamed, and self-reproaching because of his former poor mentality and its exalted [new] perception — when the time of death was at hand, he would summon that poor man, bring him before a great assembly of relatives, and in the presence of the king or a royal minister, and before townspeople and country folk, he would make this announcement: "Hear, sirs! This is my natural-born son, begotten by me. He was lost from such-and-such a city. He has been missing for fifty years. His name is such-and-such. My name too is such-and-such. And I came here from that city, searching for this very [son]. This is my son, and I am his father. Whatever possessions I have — all of them I transfer to this man. And whatever personal wealth I have — all of that he alone knows."'
