body.text: atha khalu bhagavan sa daridrapuruṣastasmin samaye imamevaṃrūpaṃ ghoṣaṃ śrutvā āścaryādbhutaprāpto bhavet | evaṃ ca vicintayet - sahasaiva mayedameva tāvad hiraṇyasuvarṇadhanadhānyakośakoṣṭhāgāraṃ pratilabdhamiti ||
body.translated_text: 'Then, Blessed One, that poor man, at that time, having heard such a proclamation, would be struck with wonder and amazement. And he would reflect thus: "Suddenly indeed, I have now obtained this very gold, silver, riches, grain, treasuries, and storehouses!"'

body.text:
evameva bhagavan vayaṃ tathāgatasya putrapratirūpakāḥ | tathāgataśca asmākamevaṃ vadati - putrā mama yūyamiti, yathā sa gṛhapatiḥ | vayaṃ ca bhagavaṃstisṛbhirduḥkhatābhiḥ saṃpīḍitā abhūma | katamābhistisṛbhiḥ? yaduta duḥkhaduḥkhatayā saṃskāraduḥkhatayā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā ca | saṃsāre ca hīnādhimuktikāḥ | tato vayaṃ bhagavatā bahūn dharmān pratyavarān saṃkāradhānasadṛśānanuvicintayitāḥ | teṣu cāsma prayuktā ghaṭamānā vyāyacchamānāḥ | nirvāṇamātraṃ ca vayaṃ bhagavan divasamudrāmiva paryeṣamāṇā mārgāmaḥ | tena ca vayaṃ bhagavan nirvāṇena pratilabdhena tuṣṭā bhavāmaḥ | bahu ca labdhamiti manyāmahe tathāgatasyāntikāt eṣu dharmeṣvabhiyuktā ghaṭitvā vyāyamitvā | prajānāti ca tathāgato 'smākaṃ hīnādhimuktikatām, tataśca bhagavānasmānupekṣate, na saṃbhinatti, nācaṣṭe - yo 'yaṃ tathāgatasya jñānakośaḥ, eṣa eva yuṣmākaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | bhagavāṃścāsmākamupāyakauśalyena asmiṃstathāgatajñānakośe dāyādān saṃsthāpayati | niḥspṛhāśca vayaṃ bhagavan | tata evaṃ jānīma - etadevāsmākaṃ bahukaraṃ yadvayaṃ tathāgatasyāntikāddivasamudrāmiva nirvāṇaṃ pratilabhāmahe | te vayaṃ bhagavan bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanamārabhya udārāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kurmaḥ | tathāgatajñānaṃ vivarāmo darśayāma upadarśayāmaḥ | vayaṃ bhagavaṃstato niḥspṛhāḥ samānāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? upāyakauśalyena tathāgato 'smākamadhimuktiṃ prajānāti | tacca vayaṃ na jānīmo na budhyāmahe yadidaṃ bhagavatā etarhi kathitam - yathā vayaṃ bhagavato bhūtāḥ putrāḥ, bhagavāṃścāsmākaṃ smārayati tathāgatajñānadāyādān | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpi nāma vayaṃ tathāgatasya bhūtāḥ putrāḥ iti, api tu khalu punarhīnādhimuktāḥ | saced bhagavānasmākaṃ paśyedadhimuktibalam, bodhisattvaśabdaṃ bhagavānasmākamudāharet | vayaṃ punarbhagavatā dve kārye kārāpitāḥ - bodhisattvānāṃ cāgrato hīnādhimuktikā ityuktāḥ, te codārāyāṃ buddhabodhau samādāpitāḥ, asmākaṃ cedānīṃ bhagavānadhimuktibalaṃ jñātvā idamudāhṛtavān | anena vayaṃ bhagavan paryāyeṇaivaṃ vadāmaḥ - sahasaivāsmābhirniḥspṛhairākāṅkṣitamamārgitamaparyeṣitamacintitamaprārthitaṃ
sarvajñatāratnaṃ pratilabdhaṃ yathāpīdaṃ tathāgatasya putraiḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Even so, Blessed One, we are like stand-ins for the sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> says to us thus: "You are my sons" — just as that householder. And we, Blessed One, were afflicted by three kinds of suffering. Which three? Namely, the suffering of suffering, the suffering of formations, and the suffering of change. And we were of lowly inclination in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore we were caused by the Blessed One to contemplate many inferior <s>dharmas</s> resembling a rubbish-heap. And we were engaged, striving, and exerting ourselves in those. Seeking merely <s>nirvāṇa</s>, Blessed One, like a day's wages, we searched for it. And we, Blessed One, were satisfied with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> thus obtained. And we thought much had been gained from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having been engaged, striving, and exerting ourselves in these <s>dharmas</s>. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> perceives our lowly inclination, and therefore the Blessed One disregards us and does not explain or declare: "This treasure-store of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge — this very thing shall be yours." But the Blessed One, through skillful means, establishes us as heirs in this treasure-store of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge. And we, Blessed One, were without desire. Therefore we know thus: "This alone is of great benefit to us — that we obtain <s>nirvāṇa</s>, like a day's wages, from the <s>Tathāgata</s>." And we, Blessed One, teach the exalted <s>Dharma</s>-teaching to <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, beginning with the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge and vision. We illuminate, show, and display the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge. Yet we, Blessed One, are without desire for it. For what reason? Because the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through skillful means, perceives our inclination. But we did not know or understand that which the Blessed One has now declared — namely, that we are truly the sons of the Blessed One, and the Blessed One reminds us that we are heirs to the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge. For what reason? Because, even though we are truly the sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, we are nevertheless of lowly inclination. If the Blessed One had seen in us the strength of inclination, the Blessed One would have used the word "<s>Bodhisattva</s>" for us. But we have been put to work on two tasks by the Blessed One — we were called "of lowly inclination" before the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and those [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>] were exhorted to supreme Buddha-awakening. But now the Blessed One, knowing the strength of our inclination, has declared this. By this method, Blessed One, we say thus: "Suddenly, by us who were without desire, unsought, unsearched-for, unthought-of, unasked-for — the jewel of omniscience has been obtained, just as by the sons of the <s>Tathāgata</s>."'

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān mahākāśyapastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣat -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: āścaryabhūtāḥ sma tathādbhutāśca audbilyaprāptāḥ sma śruṇitva ghoṣam /
children.translated_text: We are struck with wonder and amazement,

children.text: sahasaiva asmābhirayaṃ tathādya manojñaghoṣaḥ śrutu nāyakasya // Saddhp_4.1 //
children.translated_text: having arrived at elation upon hearing the cry — || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.1 ||

body.text: viśiṣṭaratnāna mahantarāśirmuhūrtamātreṇayamadya labdhaḥ /
body.translated_text: A great heap of distinguished jewels has been obtained today in just a moment,

body.text: na cintito nāpi kadāci prārthitastaṃ śrutva āścaryagatāḥ sma sarve // Saddhp_4.2 //
body.translated_text: unthought-of and never before sought — hearing [this], we are all struck with wonder. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.2 ||

children.text: yathāpi bālaḥ puruṣo bhaveta utplāvito bālajanena santaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as there might be a foolish man, a good person,

children.text: pituḥ sakāśātu apakrameta anyaṃ ca deśaṃ vraji so sudūram // Saddhp_4.3 //
children.translated_text: driven away by foolish people from his father's side, going to another, very distant land — || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.3 ||

children.text: pitā ca taṃ śocati tasmi kāle palāyitaṃ jñātva svakaṃ hi putram /
children.translated_text: and the father, at that time, grieves, knowing his own son to have fled,

children.text: śocantu so digvidiśāsu añce varṣāṇi pañcāśadanūnakāni // Saddhp_4.4 //
children.translated_text: and he grieves, searching in all directions, for no fewer than fifty years. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.4 ||

children.text: tathā ca so putra gaveṣamāṇo anyaṃ mahantaṃ nagaraṃ hi gatvā /
children.translated_text: And so, seeking that son, having gone to another great city,

children.text: niveśanaṃ māpiya tatra tiṣṭhet samarpito kāmugaṇehi pañcabhiḥ // Saddhp_4.5 //
children.translated_text: he would build a dwelling there and remain, occupied with the five strands of sense-pleasure. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.5 ||

children.text: bahuṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇarūpyaṃ dhānyaṃ dhanaṃ śaṅkhaśilāpravālam /
children.translated_text: Much gold and silver, grain and wealth, conch, crystal, and coral,

children.text: hastī ca aśvāśca padātayaśca gāvaḥ paśūścaiva tathaiḍakāśca // Saddhp_4.6 //
children.translated_text: elephants and horses, and foot-soldiers, cows and cattle, and likewise sheep — || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.6 ||

children.text: prayoga āyoga tathaiva kṣetrā dāsī ca dāsā bahu preṣyavargaḥ /
children.translated_text: investments, enterprises, and likewise fields, female and male servants, a large retinue of attendants —

children.text: susatkṛtaḥ prāṇisahasrakoṭibhī rājñaśca so vallabhu nityakālam // Saddhp_4.7 //
children.translated_text: honored by thousands of millions of beings, and always a favorite of the king. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.7 ||

children.text: kṛtāñjalī tasya bhavanti nāgarā grāmeṣu ye cāpi vasanti grāmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The townspeople stand with joined palms before him, and those villagers who dwell in villages too;

children.text: bahuvāṇijāstasya vrajanti antike bahūhi kāryehi kṛtādhikārāḥ // Saddhp_4.8 //
children.translated_text: many merchants approach him, having performed many duties. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.8 ||

children.text: etādṛśo ṛddhimato naraḥ syājjīrṇaśca vṛddhaśca mahallakaśca /
children.translated_text: Such would be that man of prosperity — old, aged, and advanced in years;

children.text: sa putraśokaṃ anucintayantaḥ kṣapeya rātriṃdiva nityakālam // Saddhp_4.9 //
children.translated_text: and he, reflecting on the grief for his son, would spend night and day, always. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.9 ||

children.text: sa tādṛśo durmati mahya putraḥ pañcāśa varṣāṇi tadā palānakaḥ /
children.translated_text: That son of mine is of poor understanding — gone for fifty years now, a fugitive;

children.text: ayaṃ ca kośo vipulo mamāsti kālakriyā co mama pratyupasthitā // Saddhp_4.10 //
children.translated_text: 'And this vast treasury of mine — and my death is near at hand.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.10 ||

children.text: so cāpi bālo tada tasya putro daridrakaḥ kṛpaṇaku nityakālam /
children.translated_text: And that son, the foolish one — then, always poor and wretched,

children.text: grāmeṇa grāmaṃ anucaṃkramantaḥ paryeṣate bhakta athāpi colam // Saddhp_4.11 //
children.translated_text: wandering from village to village, he seeks food and also clothing. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.11 ||

children.text: paryeṣamāṇo 'pi kadāci kiṃcillabheta kiṃcit puna naiva kiṃcit /
children.translated_text: And while seeking, sometimes he obtains something, sometimes again nothing at all;

children.text: sa śuṣyate paraśaraṇeṣu bālo dadrūya kaṇḍūya ca digdhagātraḥ // Saddhp_4.12 //
children.translated_text: that foolish one withers at others' shelters, his body covered with sores and scabs. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.12 ||

children.text: so ca vrajettaṃ nagaraṃ yahiṃ pitā anupūrvaśo tatra gato bhaveta /
children.translated_text: And he would go to that city where his father [lives], having gradually arrived there,

children.text: bhaktaṃ ca colaṃ ca gaveṣamāṇo niveśanaṃ yatra pituḥ svakasya // Saddhp_4.13 //
children.translated_text: seeking food and clothing — to the dwelling of his own father. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.13 ||

children.text: so cāpi āḍhyaḥ puruṣo mahādhano dvārasmi siṃhāsani saṃniṣaṇṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And that wealthy man of great riches, seated at the door on a lion-throne,

children.text: parivāritaḥ prāṇiśatairanekairvitāna tasyā vitato 'ntarīkṣe // Saddhp_4.14 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by innumerable hundreds of beings, with a canopy spread over him in the sky — || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.14 ||

children.text: āpto janaścāsya samantataḥ sthito dhanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca gaṇenti kecit /
children.translated_text: trusted persons standing all around him, some counting wealth and gold,

children.text: kecittu lekhānapi lekhayanti kecit prayogaṃ ca prayojayanti // Saddhp_4.15 //
children.translated_text: some writing documents too, and some conducting business. || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.15 ||

children.text: so cā daridro tahi etu dṛṣṭvā vibhūṣitaṃ gṛhapatino niveśanam /
children.translated_text: And that poor man, coming there, having seen the householder's adorned dwelling, [thinks:]

children.text: kahiṃ nu adya ahamatra āgato rājā ayaṃ bheṣyati rājamātraḥ // Saddhp_4.16 //
children.translated_text: 'Where have I come to now? This must be a king or a royal minister!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 4.16 ||

body.text: mā dāni doṣaṃ pi labheyamatra gṛhṇitva veṣṭiṃ pi ca kārayeyam /
body.translated_text: 'Let me not incur blame here; having seized him, I could have him bound.'

body.text: anucintayantaḥ sa palāyate naro daridravīthīṃ paripṛcchamānaḥ // Saddhp_4.17 //
body.translated_text: Reflecting thus, that man flees, asking [his way] along the streets of the poor. [Saddhp 4.17]

children.text: so cā dhanī taṃ svaku putra dṛṣṭvā siṃhāsanasthaśca bhavet prahṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: But that wealthy man, seeing his own son, seated on his lion-throne, would be delighted;

children.text: sa dūtakān preṣayi tasya antike ānetha etaṃ puruṣaṃ daridram // Saddhp_4.18 //
children.translated_text: he sends messengers to his presence: 'Bring this poor man here!' [Saddhp 4.18]

children.text: samanantaraṃ tehi gṛhītu so naro gṛhītamātro 'tha ca mūrccha gacchet /
children.translated_text: Immediately he is seized by them — that man, once seized, falls into a swoon;

children.text: dhrūvaṃ khu mahyaṃ vadhakā upasthitāḥ kiṃ mahya colenatha bhojanena vā // Saddhp_4.19 //
children.translated_text: 'Surely executioners have come for me! What use to me are clothes or food?' [Saddhp 4.19]

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca so paṇḍitu taṃ mahādhanī hīnādhimukto ayu bāla durmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing this, that wise, wealthy man [reflects]: 'This one is of inferior disposition, foolish, and dull-witted;

children.text: na śraddadhī mahyamimāṃ vibhūṣitāṃ pitā mamāyaṃ ti na cāpi śraddadhīt // Saddhp_4.20 //
children.translated_text: he would not believe in this splendor of mine, nor would he believe "this is my father."' [Saddhp 4.20]

children.text: puruṣāṃśca so tatra prayojayeta vaṅkāśca ye kāṇaka kuṇṭhakāśca /
children.translated_text: And he would employ men there — crooked, one-eyed, and crippled,

children.text: kucelakāḥ kṛṣṇaka hīnasattvāḥ paryeṣathā taṃ naru karmakārakam // Saddhp_4.21 //
children.translated_text: dressed in rags, dark-skinned, of lowly condition — 'Go seek that man as a laborer.' [Saddhp 4.21]

children.text: saṃkāradhānaṃ imu mahya pūtikamuccāraprasrāvavināśitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: 'This refuse-heap of mine is foul, befouled with excrement and urine;

children.text: taṃ śodhanārthāya karohi karma dviguṇaṃ ca te vetanakaṃ pradāsye // Saddhp_4.22 //
children.translated_text: do the work of cleaning it, and I shall give you double wages.' [Saddhp 4.22]

children.text: etādṛśaṃ ghoṣa śruṇitva so naro āgatya saṃśodhayi taṃ pradeśam /
children.translated_text: Having heard such an announcement, that man comes and cleans that place;

children.text: tatraiva so āvasathaṃ ca kuryānniveśanasyopalikuñcike 'smin // Saddhp_4.23 //
children.translated_text: and right there he would make his dwelling, in a hovel near the house. [Saddhp 4.23]

children.text: so cā dhanī taṃ puruṣaṃ nirīkṣed gavākṣaolokanake 'pi nityam /
children.translated_text: And that wealthy man would constantly observe that man, even through a window;

children.text: hīnādhimukto ayu mahya putraḥ saṃkāradhānaṃ śucikaṃ karoti // Saddhp_4.24 //
children.translated_text: 'This son of mine is of inferior disposition — he cleans the refuse-heap.' [Saddhp 4.24]

children.text: sa otaritvā piṭakaṃ gṛhītvā malināni vastrāṇi ca prāvaritvā /
children.translated_text: He comes down, and taking a basket, putting on soiled clothes,

children.text: upasaṃkramettasya narasya antike avabhartsayanto na karotha karma // Saddhp_4.25 //
children.translated_text: approaches that man, reprimanding him: 'You are not doing the work!' [Saddhp 4.25]

children.text: dviguṇaṃ ca te vetanakaṃ dadāmi dviguṇāṃ ca bhūyastatha pādamrakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: 'I shall give you double wages, and moreover double ointment for your feet;

children.text: saloṇabhaktaṃ ca dadāmi tubhya śākaṃ ca śāṭiṃ ca punardadāmi // Saddhp_4.26 //
children.translated_text: I shall give you salted food, and vegetables, and I shall give you a garment too.' [Saddhp 4.26]

children.text: evaṃ ca taṃ bhartsiya tasmi kāle saṃśleṣayettaṃ punareva paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus, having scolded him at that time, the wise man would then draw him close;

children.text: suṣṭhuṃ khalū karma karoṣi atra putro 'si vyaktaṃ mama nātra saṃśayaḥ // Saddhp_4.27 //
children.translated_text: 'You do the work well here — you are indeed my son, there is no doubt about this.' [Saddhp 4.27]

children.text: sa stokastokaṃ ca gṛhaṃ praveśayet karmaṃ ca kārāpayi taṃ manuṣyam /
children.translated_text: Little by little he would bring him into the house and have that man do the work;

children.text: viṃśacca varṣāṇi supūritāni krameṇa viśrambhayi taṃ naraṃ saḥ // Saddhp_4.28 //
children.translated_text: and for a full twenty years, gradually he wins the confidence of that man. [Saddhp 4.28]

children.text: hiraṇyu so mauktiku sphāṭikaṃ ca pratisāmayettatra niveśanasmin /
children.translated_text: He would entrust him with gold, pearls, and crystal in that dwelling;

children.text: sarvaṃ ca so saṃgaṇanāṃ karoti arthaṃ ca sarvaṃ anucintayeta // Saddhp_4.29 //
children.translated_text: and he would make all the accounts, and would consider all the wealth. [Saddhp 4.29]

children.text: bahirdhā so tasya niveśanasya kuṭikāya eko vasamānu bālaḥ /
children.translated_text: But outside that dwelling, the fool would dwell in a hut by himself,

children.text: daridracintāmanucintayeta na me 'sti etādṛśa bhoga kecit // Saddhp_4.30 //
children.translated_text: thinking thoughts of poverty: 'I have no such possessions.' [Saddhp 4.30]

children.text: jñātvā ca so tasya imevarūpamudārasaṃjñābhigato mi putraḥ /
children.translated_text: And knowing that his [son's] disposition was such — 'My son has arrived at a noble conception' —

children.text: sa ānayitvā suhṛjñātisaṃghaṃ niryātayiṣyāmyahu sarvamartham // Saddhp_4.31 //
children.translated_text: he summons a gathering of relatives and friends: 'I shall now transfer to him all this wealth.' [Saddhp 4.31]

body.text: rājāna so naigamanāgarāṃśca samānayitvā bahuvāṇijāṃśca /
body.translated_text: Having assembled the king, townsmen, countryfolk, and many merchants,

body.text: uvāca evaṃ pariṣāya madhye putro mamāyaṃ cira vipranaṣṭakaḥ // Saddhp_4.32 //
body.translated_text: he declared thus in the midst of the assembly: 'This is my son, long lost.' [Saddhp 4.32]

children.text: pañcāśa varṣāṇi supūrṇakāni anye ca 'to viṃśatiye mi dṛṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For a full fifty years — and for twenty more he has been seen by me;

children.text: amukātu nagarātu mamaiṣa naṣṭo ahaṃ ca mārganta ihaivamāgataḥ // Saddhp_4.33 //
children.translated_text: from such-and-such a city he was lost to me, and I, seeking him, came here.' [Saddhp 4.33]

children.text: sarvasya dravyasya ayaṃ prabhurme etasya niryātayi sarvaśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'He is the master of all my property; I transfer everything to him without remainder.

children.text: karotu kāryaṃ ca piturdhanena sarvaṃ kuṭumbaṃ ca dadāmi etat // Saddhp_4.34 //
children.translated_text: Let him do what is to be done with his father's wealth — I give him this entire estate.' [Saddhp 4.34]

children.text: āścaryaprāptaśca bhavennaro 'sau daridrabhāvaṃ purimaṃ smaritvā /
children.translated_text: And that man would be struck with wonder, remembering his former poverty;

children.text: hīnādhimuktiṃ ca pituśca tān guṇāṃllabdhvā kuṭumbaṃ sukhito 'smi adya // Saddhp_4.35 //
children.translated_text: recalling his inferior disposition and his father's virtues — 'Having obtained this estate, I am happy today.' [Saddhp 4.35]

children.text: tathaiva cāsmāka vināyakena hīnādhimuktitva vijāniyāna /
children.translated_text: Just so, our Guide, knowing our inferior disposition,

children.text: na śrāvitaṃ buddha bhaviṣyatheti yūyaṃ kila śrāvaka mahya putrāḥ // Saddhp_4.36 //
children.translated_text: has not proclaimed 'You shall become <s>Buddhas</s>' — 'You are indeed my <s>Śrāvaka</s> sons.' [Saddhp 4.36]

children.text: asmāṃśca adhyeṣati lokanātho ye prasthitā uttamamagrabodhim /
children.translated_text: And the Lord of the world exhorts us — those who have set out for supreme awakening;

children.text: teṣāṃ vade kāśyapa mārga nuttaraṃ yaṃ mārga bhāvitva bhaveyu buddhāḥ // Saddhp_4.37 //
children.translated_text: 'Teach them, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the supreme path — the path by cultivating which they become <s>Buddhas</s>.' [Saddhp 4.37]

children.text: vayaṃ ca teṣāṃ sugatena preṣitā bahubodhisattvāna mahābalānām /
children.translated_text: And we, sent by the <s>Sugata</s> to those many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great power,

children.text: anuttaraṃ mārga pradarśayāma dṛṣṭāntahetūnayutāna koṭibhiḥ // Saddhp_4.38 //
children.translated_text: show them the supreme path through <s>koṭis</s> and <s>ayutas</s> of parables and reasons. [Saddhp 4.38]

children.text: śrutvā ca asmāku jinasya putrā bodhāya bhāventi sumārgamagryam /
children.translated_text: And having heard us, the sons of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) cultivate the supreme path to awakening;

children.text: te vyākriyante ca kṣaṇasmi tasmin bhaviṣyathā buddha imasmi loke // Saddhp_4.39 //
children.translated_text: they are prophesied at that very moment: 'You shall become <s>Buddhas</s> in this world.' [Saddhp 4.39]

children.text: etādṛśaṃ karma karoma tāyinaḥ saṃrakṣamāṇā ima dharmakośam /
children.translated_text: We perform such work for the Protector, guarding this <s>Dharma</s>-treasury;

children.text: prakāśayantaśca jinātmajānāṃ vaiśvāsikastasya yathā naraḥ saḥ // Saddhp_4.40 //
children.translated_text: and illuminating it for the sons of the <s>Jina</s> — like that trustworthy man. [Saddhp 4.40]

children.text: daridracintāśca vicintayāma viśrāṇayanto imu buddhakośam /
children.translated_text: And we think thoughts of poverty, while distributing this <s>Buddha</s>-treasury;

children.text: na caiva prārthema jinasya jñānaṃ jinasya jñānaṃ ca prakāśayāmaḥ // Saddhp_4.41 //
children.translated_text: we do not aspire to the <s>Jina's</s> knowledge, yet we illuminate the <s>Jina's</s> knowledge. [Saddhp 4.41]

children.text: pratyātmikīṃ nirvṛti kalpayāma etāvatā jñānamidaṃ na bhūyaḥ /
children.translated_text: We conceive of individual <s>nirvāṇa</s> [only] — 'This much is our knowledge, no more';

children.text: nāsmāka harṣo 'pi kadācia bhoti kṣetreṣu buddhāna śruṇitva vyūhān // Saddhp_4.42 //
children.translated_text: and we feel no joy when hearing of the splendid adornments of the <s>Buddha</s>-fields. [Saddhp 4.42]

children.text: śāntāḥ kilā sarvimi dharmanāsravā nirodhautpādavivarjitāśca /
children.translated_text: All these <s>dharmas</s> are said to be peaceful, free from outflows,

children.text: na cātra kaścidbhavatīha dharmo evaṃ tu cintetva na bhoti śraddhā // Saddhp_4.43 //
children.translated_text: free from cessation and arising; yet there is no <s>dharma</s> here — reflecting thus, there is no faith. [Saddhp 4.43]

children.text: suniḥspṛhā smā vaya dīrgharātraṃ bauddhasya jñānasya anuttarasya /
children.translated_text: For a long time we were thoroughly free from desire for the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: praṇidhānamasmāka na jātu tatra iyaṃ parā niṣṭha jinena uktā // Saddhp_4.44 //
children.translated_text: we never had any aspiration for it — 'This is the final conclusion,' was spoken by the <s>Jina</s>. [Saddhp 4.44]

children.text: nirvāṇaparyanti samucchraye 'smin paribhāvitā śūnyata dīrgharātram /
children.translated_text: In this culmination leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, we have cultivated <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) for a long time,

children.text: parimukta traidhātukaduḥkhapīḍitāḥ kṛtaṃ ca asmābhi jinasya śāsanam // Saddhp_4.45 //
children.translated_text: freed from the torments of suffering in the triple world — and we have fulfilled the <s>Jina's</s> teaching. [Saddhp 4.45]

children.text: yaṃ hi prakāśema jinātmajānāṃ ye prasthitā bhonti ihāgrabodhau /
children.translated_text: That which we illuminate for the sons of the <s>Jina</s>, those who have set out for supreme awakening,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yatkiṃci vadāma dharmaṃ spṛha tatra asmāka na jātu bhoti // Saddhp_4.46 //
children.translated_text: and whatever <s>Dharma</s> we speak to them — for that, we never feel any aspiration. [Saddhp 4.46]

children.text: taṃ cāsma lokācariyaḥ svayaṃbhūrupekṣate kālamavekṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And the self-born teacher of the world has looked upon us, biding his time;

children.text: na bhāṣate bhūtapadārthasaṃdhiṃ adhimuktimasmāku gaveṣamāṇaḥ // Saddhp_4.47 //
children.translated_text: he does not speak the conjunction of true realities, searching for our disposition. [Saddhp 4.47]

children.text: upāyakauśalya yathaiva tasya mahādhanasya puruṣasya kāle /
children.translated_text: Just as at the time of that wealthy man, skillful means [were used] —

children.text: hīnādhimuktaṃ satataṃ dameti damiyāna cāsmai pradadāti vittam // Saddhp_4.48 //
children.translated_text: he constantly tames the one of inferior disposition, and having tamed him, gives him the wealth. [Saddhp 4.48]

children.text: suduṣkaraṃ kurvati lokanātho upāyakauśalya prakāśayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the world performs what is most difficult, illuminating skillful means;

children.text: hīnādhimuktān damayantu putrān dametva ca jñānamidaṃ dadāti // Saddhp_4.49 //
children.translated_text: taming his children of inferior disposition, and having tamed them, gives them this knowledge. [Saddhp 4.49]

children.text: āścaryaprāptāḥ sahasā sma adya yathā daridro labhiyāna vittam /
children.translated_text: We are suddenly struck with wonder today — like a poor man obtaining wealth;

children.text: phalaṃ ca prāptaṃ iha buddhāśāsane prathamaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ ca anāsravaṃ ca // Saddhp_4.50 //
children.translated_text: the fruit obtained here in the <s>Buddha's</s> teaching is the foremost, the distinguished, the outflow-free. [Saddhp 4.50]

children.text: yacchīlamasmābhi ca dīrgharātraṃ saṃrakṣitaṃ lokavidusya śāsane /
children.translated_text: The moral discipline that we have guarded for a long time in the teaching of the Knower of the world —

children.text: asmābhi labdhaṃ phalamadya tasya śīlasya pūrvaṃ caritasya nātha // Saddhp_4.51 //
children.translated_text: today we have obtained the fruit of that discipline formerly practiced, O Lord. [Saddhp 4.51]

children.text: yad brahmacaryaṃ paramaṃ viśuddhaṃ niṣevitaṃ śāsani nāyakasya /
children.translated_text: The supreme, pure <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy conduct) practiced in the teaching of the Guide —

children.text: tasyo viśiṣṭaṃ phalamadya labdhaṃ śāntaṃ udāraṃ ca anāsravaṃ ca // Saddhp_4.52 //
children.translated_text: its distinguished fruit has been obtained today — peaceful, magnificent, and outflow-free. [Saddhp 4.52]

children.text: adyo vayaṃ śrāvakabhūta nātha saṃśrāvayiṣyāmatha cāgrabodhim /
children.translated_text: Today we have become true <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers), O Lord; we shall proclaim supreme awakening;

children.text: bodhīya śabdaṃ ca prakāśayāmasteno vayaṃ śrāvaka bhīṣmakalpāḥ // Saddhp_4.53 //
children.translated_text: and we illuminate the word of awakening — therefore we are <s>Śrāvakas</s> of awesome aspect. [Saddhp 4.53]

children.text: arhantabhūtā vayamadya nātha arhāmahe pūja sadevakātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Today we have become <s>Arhats</s>, O Lord; we are worthy of worship from the world with its gods,

children.text: lokātsamārātu sabrahmakātaḥ sarveṣa sattvāna ca antikātaḥ // Saddhp_4.54 //
children.translated_text: from the world including <s>Māra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, and from all beings everywhere. [Saddhp 4.54]

children.text: ko nāma śaktaḥ pratikartu tubhyamudyuktarūpo bahukalpakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who could repay you, striving earnestly for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>?

children.text: suduṣkarāṇīdṛśakā karoṣi suduṣkarān yāniha martyaloke // Saddhp_4.55 //
children.translated_text: You perform what is most difficult to accomplish — things most difficult in this mortal world. [Saddhp 4.55]

children.text: hastehi pādehi śireṇa cāpi pratipriyaṃ duṣkarakaṃ hi kartum /
children.translated_text: With hands, feet, and head, it would be difficult to make a return;

children.text: śireṇa aṃsena ca yo dhareta paripūrṇakalpān yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ // Saddhp_4.56 //
children.translated_text: even one who bore [you] on head and shoulders for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — [Saddhp 4.56]

children.text: khādyaṃ dadedbhojanavastrapānaṃ śayanāsanaṃ co vimalottaracchadam /
children.translated_text: or who gave food, drink, clothing, and beverages, bedding and seats, and immaculate upper garments,

children.text: vihāra kārāpayi candanāmayān saṃstīrya co dūṣyayugehi dadyāt // Saddhp_4.57 //
children.translated_text: or who had monasteries built of sandalwood, and spread with pairs of fine fabrics to offer — [Saddhp 4.57]

children.text: gilānabhaiṣajya bahuprakāraṃ pūjārtha dadyāt sugatasya nityam /
children.translated_text: or who constantly gave medicines of many kinds to the <s>Sugata</s> for the purpose of worship —

children.text: dadeya kalpān yatha gaṅgavālikā naivaṃ kadācit pratikartu śakyam // Saddhp_4.58 //
children.translated_text: even giving for <s>kalpas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, one could never repay [you] thus. [Saddhp 4.58]

children.text: mahātmadharmā atulānubhāvā maharddhikāḥ kṣāntibale pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Of great soul, of <s>dharma</s> incomparable in power, of great supernatural ability, established in the power of patience —

children.text: buddhā mahārāja anāsravā jinā sahanti bālāna imīdṛśāni // Saddhp_4.59 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s>, great kings, free from outflows, Conquerors, bear such things from the childish. [Saddhp 4.59]

children.text: anuvartamānastatha nityakālaṃ nimittacārīṇa bravīti dharmam /
children.translated_text: Always conforming [to beings], teaching <s>dharma</s> to those who follow signs —

children.text: dharmeśvaro īśvaru sarvaloke maheśvaro lokavināyakendraḥ // Saddhp_4.60 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, the Lord of the entire world, the Great Lord, the supreme leader and guide of the world. [Saddhp 4.60]

children.text: pratipatti darśeti bahuprakāraṃ sattvāna sthānāni prajānamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: He shows practice in many ways, knowing the stations of beings;

children.text: nānādhimuktiṃ ca viditva teṣāṃ hetūsahasrehi bravīti dharmam // Saddhp_4.61 //
children.translated_text: and knowing their various dispositions, he teaches <s>dharma</s> with thousands of reasons. [Saddhp 4.61]

children.text: tathāgataścarya prajānamānaḥ sarveṣa sattvānatha pudgalānām /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing [the nature] of all beings and persons,

children.text: bahuprakāraṃ hi bravīti dharmaṃ nidarśayanto imamagrabodhim // Saddhp_4.62 //
children.translated_text: teaches <s>dharma</s> in many ways, displaying this supreme awakening. [Saddhp 4.62]

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye adhimuktiparivarto nāma caturthaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the Noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharmaparyāya</s>, called <s>Adhimukti</s> (Disposition).

body.text: Saddhp_5: oṣadhīparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 5: The <s>Oṣadhī</s> (Medicinal Herbs) Chapter.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapaṃ tāṃścānyān sthavirān mahāśrāvakānāmantrayāmāsa - sādhu sādhu mahākāśyapa | sādhu khalu punaryuṣmākaṃ kāśyapa yadyūyaṃ tathāgatasya bhūtān guṇavarṇān bhāṣadhve | ete ca kāśyapa tathāgatasya bhūtā guṇāḥ | ataścānye 'prameyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ, yeṣāṃ na sukaraḥ paryanto 'dhigantumaparimitānapi kalpān bhāṣamāṇaiḥ | dharmasvāmī kāśyapa tathāgataḥ, sarvadharmāṇāṃ rājā prabhurvaśī | yaṃ ca kāśyapa tathāgato dharmaṃ yatropanikṣipati, sa tathaiva bhavati | sarvadharmāśca kāśyapa tathāgato yuktyopanikṣipati | tathāgatajñānenopanikṣipati | yathā te dharmāḥ sarvajñabhūmimeva gacchanti | sarvadharmārthagatiṃ ca tathāgato vyavalokayati | sarvadharmārthavaśitāprāptaḥ sarvadharmādhyāśayaprāptaḥ sarvadharmaviniścayakauśalyajñānaparamapāramitāprāptaḥ sarvajñajñānasaṃdarśakaḥ sarvajñajñānāvatārakaḥ sarvajñajñānopanikṣepakaḥ kāśyapa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> and those other elder great <s>Śrāvakas</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>! Excellent indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that you speak these true praises of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> qualities. And these, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are indeed the true qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And beyond these, there are other immeasurable, incalculable [qualities], whose limit would not be easy to reach even if one were to speak for unlimited <s>kalpas</s>. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the master of the <s>Dharma</s>, the king, lord, and sovereign of all <s>dharmas</s>. And whatever <s>dharma</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> sets forth — that is exactly how it is. The <s>Tathāgata</s> sets forth all <s>dharmas</s> with proper method. He sets them forth with the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge, so that those <s>dharmas</s> go precisely to the stage of omniscience. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> surveys the course of the meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>. He has attained mastery over the meaning of all <s>dharmas</s>, has attained [insight into] the dispositions of all <s>dharmas</s>, has attained the supreme perfection of the knowledge of skillful determination of all <s>dharmas</s>, is the one who shows omniscient knowledge, is the one who causes entry into omniscient knowledge, is the one who sets forth omniscient knowledge — the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly enlightened one.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa asyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau yāvantastṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo nānāvarṇā nānāprakārā oṣadhigrāmā nānānāmadheyāḥ pṛthivyāṃ jātāḥ parvatagirikandareṣu vā | meghaśca mahāvāriparipūrṇa unnamet, unnamitvā sarvāvatīṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃchādayet | saṃchādya ca sarvatra samakālaṃ vāri pramuñcet | tatra kāśyapa ye tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo 'syāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau, tatra ye taruṇāḥ komalanālaśākhāpatrapalāśāstṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo drumā mahādrumāḥ, sarve te tato mahāmeghapramuktādvāriṇo yathābalaṃ yathāviṣayamabdhātuṃ pratyāpibanti | te caikarasena vāriṇā prabhūtena meghapramuktena yathābījamanvayaṃ vivṛddhiṃ virūḍhiṃ vipulatāmāpadyante, tathā ca puṣpaphalāni prasavanti | te ca pṛthak pṛthagū nānānāmadheyāni pratilabhante | ekadharaṇīpratiṣṭhitāśca te sarve oṣadhigrāmā bījagrāmā ekarasatoyābhiṣyanditāḥ | evameva kāśyapa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka utpadyate | yathā mahāmeghaḥ unnamate, tathā tathāgato 'pyutpadya sarvāvantaṃ sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ svareṇābhivijñāpayati | tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mahāmeghaḥ sarvāvatīṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātumavacchādayati, evameva kāśyapa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya purata evaṃ śabdamudīrayati, ghoṣamanuśrāvayati - tathāgato 'smi bhavanto devamanuṣyāḥ arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tīrṇastārayāmi, mukto mocayāmi, āśvasta āśvāsayāmi, parinirvṛtaḥ parinirvāpayāmi | ahamimaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ samyak prajñayā yathābhūtaṃ prajānāmi sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī | upasaṃkrāmantu māṃ bhavanto devamanuṣyā dharmaśravaṇāya | ahaṃ mārgasyākhyātā mārgadeśiko mārgavit mārgakovidaḥ | tatra kāśyapa bahūni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi tathāgatasya dharmaśravaṇāyopasaṃkrāmanti | atha tathāgato 'pi teṣāṃ sattvānāmindriyavīryaparāparavaimātratāṃ
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, in this trichiliocosm, however many grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees — of various colors and various kinds, groups of herbs of various names — have grown on the earth, or in mountains, valleys, and ravines; and a cloud, filled with great water, would rise up, and having risen, would cover this entire trichiliocosm; and having covered it, would release water everywhere at the same time — therein, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, whatever grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees are in this trichiliocosm, whether they are young, tender-stalked, with soft branches, leaves, and foliage — the grasses, shrubs, herbs, forest trees, [small] trees, and great trees — all of these absorb water from the water released by that great cloud according to their strength and according to their capacity. And those, by that abundant water of one flavor released from the cloud, reach growth, development, and abundance according to their seed and lineage, and produce flowers and fruits. And they separately obtain various names. Yet all those groups of herbs and seed-families, established on one earth, are moistened by water of a single flavor. Even so, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, arises in the world. Just as a great cloud rises up, so also the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having arisen, makes known to the entire world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> through his voice. Just as, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the great cloud covers this entire trichiliocosm, even so, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, before the world of gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, raises such a voice, proclaims such an announcement: "I am the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O honored gods and humans, the <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One; having crossed, I cause others to cross; freed, I free others; consoled, I console others; fully ceased, I bring others to complete cessation. I know this world and the next world truly with correct wisdom. I am all-knowing, all-seeing. Come to me, O honored gods and humans, for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. I am the announcer of the path, the teacher of the path, the knower of the path, skilled in the path." Therein, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundred-thousands of living beings approach the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> also, having known the high-and-low differences in those beings' faculties, vigor, and capacities,

body.text:
jñātvā tāṃstān dharmaparyāyānupasaṃharati, tāṃ tāṃ dharmakathāṃ kathayati bahvīṃ vicitrāṃ harṣaṇīyāṃ paritoṣaṇīyāṃ prāmodyakaraṇīyāṃ hitasukhasaṃvartanakaraṇīyām | yayā
kathaya te sattvāḥ dṛṣṭa eva dharme sukhitā bhavanti, kālaṃ ca kṛtvā sugatīṣūpapadyante, yatra prabhūtāṃśca kāmān paribhuñjante, dharmaṃ ca śṛṇvanti | śrutvā ca taṃ dharmaṃ vigatanīvaraṇā bhavanti | anupūrveṇa ca sarvajñadharmeṣvabhiyujyante yathābalaṃ yathāviṣayaṃ yathāsthānam ||
body.translated_text: applies those various <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, speaks those various <s>Dharma</s>-talks — abundant, varied, gladdening, satisfying, producing delight, conducive to benefit and happiness. By which talk those beings are made happy in this very life, and having died, are reborn in good destinies, where they enjoy abundant pleasures and hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, they become free from hindrances. And gradually they apply themselves to the omniscient <s>dharmas</s>, according to their strength, according to their capacity, according to their position.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kāśyapa mahāmeghaḥ sarvāvatīṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃchādya samaṃ vāri pramuñcati, sarvāṃśca tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatīn vāriṇā saṃtarpayati | yathābalaṃ yathāviṣayaṃ yathāsthāmaṃ ca te tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatayo vāryāpibanti, svakasvakāṃ ca jātipramāṇatāṃ gacchanti | evameva kāśyapa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yaṃ dharmaṃ bhāṣate, sarvaḥ sa dharma ekaraso yaduta vimuktiraso virāgaraso nirodharasaḥ sarvajñajñānaparyavasānaḥ | tatra kāśyapa ye te sattvāstathāgatasya dharmaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya śṛṇvanti dhārayanti abhisaṃyujyante, na te ātmanātmānaṃ jānanti vā vedayanti vā budhyanti vā | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgata eva kāśyapa tān sattvāṃstathā jānāti, ye ca te, yathā ca te, yādṛśāśca te | yaṃ ca te cintayanti, yathā ca te cintayanti, yena ca te cintayanti | yaṃ ca te bhāvayanti, yathā ca te bhāvayanti, yena ca te bhāvayanti | yaṃ ca te prāpnuvanti, yathā ca te prāpnuvanti, yena ca te prāpnuvanti | tathāgata eva kāśyapa tatra pratyakṣaḥ pratyakṣadarśī yathā ca darśī teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tāsu tāsu bhūmiṣu sthitānāṃ tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ hīnotkṛṣṭamadhyamānām | so 'haṃ kāśyapa ekarasadharma viditvā yaduta vimuktirasaṃ nirvṛtirasaṃ nirvāṇaparyavasānaṃ nityaparinirvṛtamekabhūmikamākāśagatikamadhimuktiṃ sattvānāmanurakṣamāṇo na sahasaiva sarvajñajñānaṃ saṃprakāśayāmi | āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā yūyaṃ kāśyapa yadyūyaṃ saṃdhābhāṣitaṃ tathāgatasya na śaknutha avataritum | tatkasya hetoḥ? durvijñeyaṃ kāśyapa tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ saṃdhābhāṣitamiti ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the great cloud, having covered this entire trichiliocosm, releases water evenly and satisfies all grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees with water; and according to their strength, according to their capacity, according to their stature, those grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees absorb the water and each reaches its own specific size of birth — even so, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> that the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One speaks — all that <s>Dharma</s> is of one flavor, namely, the flavor of liberation, the flavor of dispassion, the flavor of cessation, culminating in omniscient knowledge. Therein, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, those beings who hear the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as he speaks, who retain it and apply it — they do not know or perceive or understand themselves by themselves. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, knows those beings as they are — what they are, how they are, and of what kind they are; what they think about, how they think, and by what they think; what they cultivate, how they cultivate, and by what they cultivate; what they attain, how they attain, and by what they attain. The <s>Tathāgata</s> alone, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is there directly perceiving, with direct vision, seeing how those beings, established in those various stages, are like the grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees — low, high, and middling. And I, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, knowing the <s>Dharma</s> of one flavor — namely, the flavor of liberation, the flavor of cessation, culminating in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, always fully ceased, [entering] one stage, the course of space — while guarding the aspiration of beings, do not immediately make manifest the omniscient knowledge. It is wonderful and marvelous that you have attained, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, that you are unable to penetrate the teaching with intended purport of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? Hard to understand, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the teaching with intended purport of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamāna imā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, to further demonstrate this very meaning in greater measure, spoke these verses:

children.text: dharmarājā ahaṃ loke utpanno bhavamardanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I am the <s>Dharma</s>-king, arisen in the world, the crusher of existence;

children.text: dharmaṃ bhāṣāmi sattvānāmadhimuktiṃ vijāniya // Saddhp_5.1 //
children.translated_text: I speak the <s>Dharma</s> to beings, knowing [their] aspiration. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.1 ||

children.text: dhīrabuddhī mahāvīrā ciraṃ rakṣanti bhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: The firm-minded great heroes long guard what is spoken,

children.text: rahasyaṃ cāpi dhārenti na ca bhāṣanti prāṇinām // Saddhp_5.2 //
children.translated_text: and also retain the secret — they do not speak it to beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.2 ||

children.text: durbodhyaṃ cāpi tajjñānaṃ sahasā śrutva bāliśāḥ /
children.translated_text: That knowledge is hard to comprehend, and upon suddenly hearing it, the childish

children.text: kāṅkṣāṃ kuryuḥ sudurmedhāstato bhraṣṭā bhrameyu te // Saddhp_5.3 //
children.translated_text: of poor intellect would doubt — fallen from it, they would go astray. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.3 ||

children.text: yathāviṣayu bhāṣāmi yasya yādṛśakaṃ balam /
children.translated_text: I speak according to [each one's] capacity, and according to whatever strength each has;

children.text: anyamanyehi arthehi dṛṣṭiṃ kurvāmi ujjukām // Saddhp_5.4 //
children.translated_text: through different meanings for different ones, I make the view straight. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.4 ||

children.text: yathāpi kāśyapā megho lokadhātūya unnataḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a cloud rises over the world-realm,

children.text: sarvamonahatī cāpi chādayanto vasuṃdharām // Saddhp_5.5 //
children.translated_text: covering all and obscuring the earth — || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.5 ||

children.text: so ca vārisya saṃpūrṇo vidyunmālī mahāmbudaḥ /
children.translated_text: that great cloud, full of water, wreathed in lightning,

children.text: nirnādayanta śabdena harṣayet sarvadehinaḥ // Saddhp_5.6 //
children.translated_text: resounding with thunder, would gladden all living beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.6 ||

children.text: sūryaraśmī nivāritvā śītalaṃ kṛtva maṇḍalam /
children.translated_text: Having blocked the sun's rays, having made the region cool,

children.text: hastaprāpto 'vatiṣṭhanto vāri muñcet samantataḥ // Saddhp_5.7 //
children.translated_text: standing within hand's reach, it releases water on all sides. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.7 ||

children.text: sa caiva mama muñceta āpaskandhamanalpakam /
children.translated_text: And that [cloud] releases no small mass of water —

children.text: prākharantaḥ samantena tarpayenmedinīmimām // Saddhp_5.8 //
children.translated_text: pouring forth all around, it satisfies this earth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.8 ||

children.text: iha yā kāci medinyāṃ jātā oṣadhayo bhavet /
children.translated_text: Here, whatever herbs have grown on the earth,

children.text: tṛṇagulmavanaspatyo drumā vātha mahādrumāḥ // Saddhp_5.9 //
children.translated_text: grasses, shrubs, forest trees, [small] trees, or great trees, || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.9 ||

children.text: sasyāni vividhānyeva yadvāpi haritaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: various crops, and whatever is green,

children.text: parvate kandare caiva nikuñjeṣu ca yadbhavet // Saddhp_5.10 //
children.translated_text: on mountains, in ravines, and in groves — || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.10 ||

children.text: sarvān saṃtarpayenmeghastṛṇagulmavanaspatīn /
children.translated_text: the cloud satisfies all — grasses, shrubs, and forest trees;

children.text: tṛṣitāṃ dharaṇīṃ tarpet pariṣiñcati cauṣadhīḥ // Saddhp_5.11 //
children.translated_text: it satisfies the thirsty earth and sprinkles the herbs. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.11 ||

children.text: tacca ekarasaṃ vāri meghamuktamihasthitam /
children.translated_text: And that water of one flavor, released from the cloud, stands here;

children.text: yathābalaṃ yathāviṣayaṃ tṛṇagulmā pibanti tat // Saddhp_5.12 //
children.translated_text: according to their strength and capacity, the grasses and shrubs drink it. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.12 ||

children.text: drumāśca ye keci mahādrumāśca khudrāka madhyāśca yathāvayāśca /
children.translated_text: Whatever trees, great trees — small, middling, and according to their size —

children.text: yathābalaṃ sarve pibanti vāri pibanti vardhanti yathecchakāmāḥ // Saddhp_5.13 //
children.translated_text: all drink water according to their strength; they drink and grow as they desire. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.13 ||

children.text: kāṇḍena nālena tvacā yathaiva śākhāpraśākhāya tathaiva patraiḥ /
children.translated_text: By stem, by stalk, by bark, and likewise by branches and branchlets, and by leaves —

children.text: vardhanti puṣpehi phalehi caiva meghābhivṛṣṭena mahauṣadhīyaḥ // Saddhp_5.14 //
children.translated_text: the great herbs grow, with flowers and fruits, [nourished] by the rain from the cloud. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.14 ||

children.text: yathābalaṃ tā viṣayaśca yādṛśo yāsāṃ ca yad yādṛśakaṃ ca bījam /
children.translated_text: According to their strength and whatever capacity they have, and whatever seed each has —

children.text: svakasvakaṃ tāḥ prasavaṃ dadanti vāriṃ ca taṃ ekarasaṃ pramuktam // Saddhp_5.15 //
children.translated_text: each produces its own fruit, though the water released is of one flavor. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.15 ||

children.text: emeva buddho 'pi ha loke kāśyapa utpadyate vāridharo va loke /
children.translated_text: Even so, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Buddha</s> arises in the world — like a rain-bearer in the world;

children.text: utpadya ca bhāṣati lokanātho bhūtāṃ cariṃ darśayate ca prāṇinām // Saddhp_5.16 //
children.translated_text: and having arisen, the Lord of the World speaks and shows the true conduct to beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.16 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca saṃśrāvayate maharṣiḥ puraskṛto loke sadevake 'smin /
children.translated_text: Thus the great sage proclaims, honored in this world with its gods:

children.text: tathāgato 'haṃ dvipadottamo jino utpannu lokasmi yathaiva meghaḥ // Saddhp_5.17 //
children.translated_text: "I am the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Foremost of Bipeds, the <s>Jina</s>, arisen in the world just as a cloud." || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.17 ||

children.text: saṃtarpayiṣyāmyahu sarvasattvān saṃśuṣkagātrāṃstribhave vilagnān /
children.translated_text: "I shall satisfy all beings — those with withered limbs, caught in the three realms of existence;

children.text: duḥkhena śuṣyanta sukhe sthapeyaṃ kāmāṃśca dāsyāmyahu nirvṛtiṃ ca // Saddhp_5.18 //
children.translated_text: those drying up through suffering, I shall place in happiness; I shall give pleasures and also cessation. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.18 ||

children.text: śṛṇotha me devamanuṣyasaṃghā upasaṃkramadhvaṃ mama darśanāya /
children.translated_text: Hear me, assembly of gods and humans! Come near for a vision of me;

children.text: tathāgato 'haṃ bhagavānanābhibhūḥ saṃtāraṇārthaṃ iha loki jātaḥ // Saddhp_5.19 //
children.translated_text: I am the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Blessed One, the Unconquered — born here in the world for the purpose of crossing [beings] over. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.19 ||

children.text: bhāṣāmi ca prāṇisahasrakoṭināṃ dharmaṃ viśuddhaṃ abhidarśanīyam /
children.translated_text: I speak the <s>Dharma</s>, pure and worthy of display, to thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of living beings;

children.text: ekā ca tasyo samatā tathatvaṃ yadidaṃ vimuktiścatha nirvṛtī ca // Saddhp_5.20 //
children.translated_text: and its equality and suchness is one — namely, liberation and cessation. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.20 ||

children.text: svareṇa caikena vadāmi dharmaṃ bodhiṃ nidānaṃ kariyāna nityam /
children.translated_text: With a single voice I speak the <s>Dharma</s>, always making awakening the basis;

children.text: samaṃ hi etadviṣamatva nāsti na kaści vidveṣu na rāgu vidyate // Saddhp_5.21 //
children.translated_text: for this is equal — there is no inequality; there is no hatred and no passion found. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.21 ||

children.text: anunīyatā mahya na kācidasti premā ca doṣaśca na me kahiṃcit /
children.translated_text: There is no partiality whatsoever in me; no love and no fault anywhere;

children.text: samaṃ ca dharmaṃ pravadāmi dehināṃ yathaikasattvasya tathā parasya // Saddhp_5.22 //
children.translated_text: I teach the <s>Dharma</s> equally to all beings — to one being as to another. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.22 ||

body.text: ananyakarmā pravadāmi dharmaṃ gacchantu tiṣṭhantu niṣīdamānaḥ /
body.translated_text: I speak the <s>Dharma</s> with no other occupation — whether going, standing, or sitting;

body.text: niṣaṇṇa śayyāsanamāruhitvā kilāsitā mahya na jātu vidyate // Saddhp_5.23 //
body.translated_text: seated or having mounted a bed — weariness is never found in me. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.23 ||

children.text: saṃtarpayāmī imu sarvalokaṃ megho va vāriṃ sama muñcamānaḥ /
children.translated_text: I satisfy this whole world — like a cloud releasing water equally;

children.text: āryeṣu nīceṣu ca tulyabuddhirduḥśīlabhūteṣvatha śīlavatsu // Saddhp_5.24 //
children.translated_text: with equal mind toward the noble and the lowly, toward those of broken morality and those of good morality. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.24 ||

children.text: vinaṣṭacāritra tathaiva ye narāścāritraācārasamanvitāśca /
children.translated_text: Those of destroyed conduct, and those endowed with conduct and good behavior,

children.text: dṛṣṭisthitā ye ca vinaṣṭadṛṣṭī samyagdṛśo ye cāviśuddhadṛṣṭayaḥ // Saddhp_5.25 //
children.translated_text: those established in views and those of destroyed views, those of right vision and those of impure vision — || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.25 ||

children.text: hīneṣu cotkṛṣṭamatīṣu cāpi mṛdvindriyeṣu pravadāmi dharmam /
children.translated_text: to the lowly and to those of the highest intellects, to those of soft faculties, I speak the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: kilāsitāṃ sarva vivarjayitvā samyak pramuñcāmyahu dharmavarṣam // Saddhp_5.26 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all weariness, I rightly release the <s>Dharma</s>-rain. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.26 ||

children.text: yathābalaṃ ca śruṇiyāna mahyaṃ vividhāsu bhūmīṣu pratiṣṭhihanti /
children.translated_text: And according to their strength, those who hear me are established in various stages —

children.text: deveṣu martyeṣu manorameṣu śakreṣu brahmeṣvatha cakravartiṣu // Saddhp_5.27 //
children.translated_text: among gods, among humans, in the delightful [realms], among <s>Śakras</s>, <s>Brahmās</s>, and wheel-turners. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.27 ||

children.text: kṣudrānukṣudrā ima oṣadhīyo kṣudrīka etā iha yāva loke /
children.translated_text: Small and very small — these herbs are the smallest in the world;

children.text: anyā ca madhyā mahatī ca oṣadhī śṛṇotha tāḥ sarva prakāśayiṣye // Saddhp_5.28 //
children.translated_text: and the middling and the great herb — hear, I shall illuminate all of them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.28 ||

children.text: anāsravaṃ dharma prajānamānā nirvāṇaprāptā viharanti ye narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the undefiled <s>Dharma</s> and dwell having attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍabhijña traividya bhavanti ye ca sā kṣudrikā oṣadhi saṃpravuttā // Saddhp_5.29 //
children.translated_text: those with the six superknowledges and the triple knowledge — that is called the small herb. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.29 ||

children.text: girikandeṣū viharanti ye ca pratyekabodhiṃ spṛhayanti ye narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who dwell in mountain caves, and those who aspire to <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> —

children.text: ye īdṛśā madhyaviśuddhabuddhayaḥ sā madhyamā oṣadhi saṃpravuttā // Saddhp_5.30 //
children.translated_text: those of such middling pure intellects — that is called the middling herb. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.30 ||

children.text: ye prārthayante puruṣarṣabhatvaṃ buddho bhaviṣye naradevanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who aspire to the state of the Bull among Men — 'I shall become a <s>Buddha</s>, the Lord of gods and humans' —

children.text: vīryaṃ ca dhyānaṃ ca niṣevamāṇāḥ sā oṣadhī agra iyaṃ pravuccati // Saddhp_5.31 //
children.translated_text: cultivating vigor and <s>dhyāna</s> — that herb is called the supreme. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.31 ||

children.text: ye cāpi yuktāḥ sugatasya putrā maitrīṃ niṣevantiha śāntacaryām /
children.translated_text: And those sons of the <s>Sugata</s> who are devoted, cultivating <s>maitrī</s> here and the conduct of peace,

children.text: niṣkāṅkṣaprāptā puruṣarṣabhatve ayaṃ drumo vucyati evarūpaḥ // Saddhp_5.32 //
children.translated_text: attained to certainty in the state of the Bull among Men — such a one is called a tree. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.32 ||

children.text: avivarticakraṃ hi pravartayantā ṛddhībalasmin sthita ye ca dhīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those steadfast ones who, established in the power of miraculous abilities, turn the irreversible wheel,

children.text: pramocayanto bahu prāṇikoṭī mahādrumo so ca pravuccate hi // Saddhp_5.33 //
children.translated_text: liberating many koṭis of beings — he is called the great tree. [Saddhp 5.33]

children.text: samaśca so dharma jinena bhāṣito meghena vā vāri samaṃ pramuktam /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Dharma</s> taught by the <s>Jina</s> is equal [for all], like water released equally from a cloud;

children.text: citrā abhijñā ima evarūpā yathauṣadhīyo dharaṇītalasthāḥ // Saddhp_5.34 //
children.translated_text: these varied superknowledges of such a form are like medicinal herbs on the surface of the earth. [Saddhp 5.34]

children.text: anena dṛṣṭāntanidarśanena upāyu jānāhi tathāgatasya /
children.translated_text: By this demonstration through parable, understand the skillful means of the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

children.text: yathā ca so bhāṣati ekadharmaṃ nānāniruktī jalabindavo vā // Saddhp_5.35 //
children.translated_text: how he speaks a single <s>Dharma</s>, with various expressions, like drops of water. [Saddhp 5.35]

children.text: mamāpi co varṣatu dharmavarṣaṃ loko hyayaṃ tarpitu bhoti sarvaḥ /
children.translated_text: I too rain a rain of <s>Dharma</s>; and this entire world is satiated;

children.text: yathābalaṃ cānuvicintayanti subhāṣitaṃ ekarasaṃ pi dharmam // Saddhp_5.36 //
children.translated_text: and they reflect according to their capacity on the well-spoken <s>Dharma</s> of a single flavor. [Saddhp 5.36]

children.text: tṛṇagulmakā vā yatha varṣamāṇe madhyā pi vā oṣadhiyo yathaiva /
children.translated_text: Just as grasses and shrubs, when rained upon, and the medium herbs likewise,

children.text: drumā pi vā te ca mahādrumā vā yatha śobhayante daśadikṣu sarve // Saddhp_5.37 //
children.translated_text: and the trees and the great trees — they all shine beautifully in the ten directions. [Saddhp 5.37]

children.text: iyaṃ sadā lokahitāya dharmatā tarpeti dharmeṇimu sarvalokam /
children.translated_text: This is always the nature of [things] for the welfare of the world — it satiates all the world with <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: saṃtarpitaścāpyatha sarvalokaḥ pramuñcate oṣadhi puṣpakāṇi // Saddhp_5.38 //
children.translated_text: and when all the world has been satiated, it produces herbs and flowers. [Saddhp 5.38]

children.text: madhyāpi ca oṣadhiyo vivardhayī arhanta ye te sthita āsravakṣaye /
children.translated_text: And the medium herbs mature — those <s>Arhats</s> who stand in the destruction of outflows;

children.text: pratyekabuddhā vanaṣaṇḍacāriṇo niṣpādayī dharmamimaṃ subhāṣitam // Saddhp_5.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, wanderers in the forest groves, fulfill this well-spoken <s>Dharma</s>. [Saddhp 5.39]

children.text: bahubodhisattvāḥ smṛtimanta dhīrāḥ sarvatra traidhātuki ye gatiṃgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, mindful and steadfast, who have attained the courses everywhere in the three realms,

children.text: paryeṣamāṇā imamagrabodhiṃ drumā va vardhanti ti nityakālam // Saddhp_5.40 //
children.translated_text: seeking this supreme awakening — they grow always like trees. [Saddhp 5.40]

children.text: ye ṛddhimantaścatudhyānadhyāyino ye śūnyatāṃ śrutva janenti prītim /
children.translated_text: Those possessed of miraculous powers, who meditate on the four <s>dhyānas</s>, who generate joy upon hearing emptiness,

children.text: raśmīsahasrāṇi pramuñcamānāste caiva vuccanti mahādrumā iha // Saddhp_5.41 //
children.translated_text: who emit thousands of rays of light — these are here called the great trees. [Saddhp 5.41]

children.text: etādṛśī kāśyapa dharmadeśanā meghena vā vāri samaṃ pramuktam /
children.translated_text: Such, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching — like water released equally from a cloud;

children.text: bahvī vivardhanti mahauṣadhīyo manuṣyapuṣpāṇi anantakāni // Saddhp_5.42 //
children.translated_text: many great herbs grow — the infinite flowers of humanity. [Saddhp 5.42]

children.text: svapratyayaṃ dharma prakāśayāmi kālena darśemi ca buddhabodhim /
children.translated_text: I proclaim the <s>Dharma</s> according to each one's capacity, and in time I show <s>Buddha</s>-awakening;

children.text: upāyakauśalyu mamaitadagraṃ sarveṣa co lokavināyakānām // Saddhp_5.43 //
children.translated_text: this is my supreme skillful means, and [that] of all Guides of the World. [Saddhp 5.43]

children.text: paramārtha evaṃ mayaṃ bhūtabhāṣito te śrāvakāḥ sarvi na enti nirvṛtim /
children.translated_text: The ultimate truth that I have truly spoken is this: all those <s>Śrāvakas</s> do not attain [final] cessation;

children.text: caranti ete vara bodhicārikāṃ buddhā bhaviṣyantimi sarvaśrāvakāḥ // Saddhp_5.44 //
children.translated_text: they practice the supreme <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct — all these <s>Śrāvakas</s> shall become <s>Buddhas</s>. [Saddhp 5.44]

body.text: punaraparaṃ kāśyapa tathāgataḥ sattvavinaye samo na cāsamaḥ | tadyathā kāśyapa candrasuryaprabhā sarvalokamavabhāsayati kuśalakāriṇamakuśalakāriṇaṃ cordhvāvasthitamadharāvasthitaṃ ca sugandhi durgandhi, sā sarvatra samaṃ prabhā nipatati na viṣamam, evameva kāśyapa tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ sarvajñajñānacittaprabhā sarveṣu pañcagatyupapanneṣu sattveṣu yathādhimuktiṃ mahāyānikapratyekabuddhayānikaśrāvakayānikeṣu saddharmadeśanā samaṃ pravartate | na ca tathāgatasya jñānaprabhāyā ūnatā vā atiriktatā vā yathāpuṇyajñānasamudāgamāya saṃbhavati | na santi kāśyapa trīṇi yānāni | kevalamanyonyacaritāḥ sattvāḥ, tena trīṇi yānāni prajñapyante ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is equal in the discipline of beings, and not unequal. Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the light of the moon and sun illuminates the entire world — the doer of good and the doer of evil, the one standing above and the one standing below, the fragrant and the malodorous — that light falls everywhere equally, not unequally. Even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the light of the omniscient knowledge-mind of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, proceeds equally in the teaching of the True <s>Dharma</s> toward all beings born in the five destinies — toward those of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>, and the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> — according to their dispositions. And there is neither deficiency nor excess in the light of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge for the accomplishment of each one's merit and knowledge. There are not three vehicles, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. Rather, beings are of varied conduct, and therefore three vehicles are designated.

body.text: evamukte āyuṣmān mahākāśyapo bhagavantametadavocat - yadi bhagavan na santi trīṇi yānāni, kiṃ kāraṇaṃ pratyutpanne 'dhvani śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvānāṃ prajñaptiḥ prajñapyate? evamukte bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapametadavocat - tadyathā kāśyapa kumbhakāraḥ samāsu mṛttikāsu bhājanāni karoti | tatra kānicid guḍabhājanāni bhavanti, kānicid ghṛtabhājanāni, kānicid dadhikṣīrabhājanāni, kānicid hīnānyaśucibhājanāni bhavanti, na ca mṛttikāyā nānātvam, atha ca dravyaprakṣepamātreṇa bhājanānāṃ nānātvaṃ prajñāyate | evameva kāśyapa ekamevedaṃ yānaṃ yaduta buddhayānam | na dvitīyaṃ na tṛtīyaṃ vā yānaṃ saṃvidyate ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> said this to the Blessed One: "If, Blessed One, there are not three vehicles, for what reason is the designation of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> designated in the present time?" When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: "Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a potter makes vessels from the same clay. Among them, some are vessels for molasses, some are vessels for ghee, some are vessels for curds and milk, and some are lowly, impure vessels. There is no diversity in the clay, but the diversity of vessels is recognized merely through the diversity of contents put in them. Even so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there is just this one vehicle — namely, the <s>Buddhayāna</s> (Buddha-vehicle). There is no second or third vehicle to be found."

body.text:
evamukte āyuṣmān mahākāśyapo bhagavantametadavocat - yadyapi bhagavan sattvā nānādhimuktayo ye traidhātukānniḥsṛtāḥ, kiṃ teṣāmekaṃ nirvāṇamuta dve trīṇi vā? bhagavānāha - sarvadharmasamatāvabodhāddhi kāśyapa nirvāṇam | taccaikam, na dve na trīṇi | tena hi kāśyapa upamāṃ te kariṣyāmi | upamayā ihaikatyā vijñapuruṣā bhāṣitasyārthamājānanti | tadyathā kāśyapa jātyandhaḥ puruṣaḥ | sa evaṃ brūyānna santi suvarṇadurvaṇāni rūpāṇi, na santi suvarṇadurvarṇānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ draṣṭāraḥ, na staḥ sūryācandramasau, na santi nakṣatrāṇi, na santi grahāḥ, na santi grahāṇāṃ draṣṭāraḥ | athānye puruṣāstasya jātyandhasya puruṣasya purata evaṃ vadeyuḥ - santi suvarṇadurvarṇāni rūpāṇi, santi suvarṇadurvarṇānāṃ rūpāṇāṃ draṣṭāraḥ, staḥ sūryācandramasau, santi nakṣatrāṇi, santi grahāḥ, santi grahāṇāṃ draṣṭāraḥ | sa ca jātyandhaḥ puruṣasteṣāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ na śraddadhyāt, noktaṃ gṛhṇīyāt | atha kaścid vaidyaḥ sarvavyādhijñaḥ syāt | sa taṃ jātyandhaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyet | tasyaivaṃ syāt - tasya puruṣasya pūrvapāpena karmaṇā vyādhirutpannaḥ | ye ca kecana vyādhaya utpadyante, te sarve caturvidhāḥ - vātikāḥ paittikāḥ ślaiḥmikāḥ sāṃnipātikāśca | atha sa vaidyastasya vyādhervyupaśamanārthaṃ punaḥ punarupāyaṃ cintayet |
tasyaivaṃ syāt - yāni khalvimāni dravyāṇi pracaranti, na taiḥ śakyo 'yaṃ vyādhiścikitsitum | santi tu himavati parvatarāje catasra oṣadhayaḥ | katamāścatasraḥ? tadyathā - prathamā sarvavarṇarasasthānānugatā nāma, dvitīyā sarvavyādhipramocanī nāma, tṛtīyā sarvaviṣavināśanī nāma, caturthī yathāsthānasthitasukhapradā nāma | imāścatasraḥ oṣadhayaḥ | atha sa vaidyastasmin jātyandhe kāruṇyamutpādya tādṛśamupāyaṃ cintayet, yenopāyena himavantaṃ parvatarājaṃ śaknuyādgantam | gatvā cordhvamapyārohet, adho 'pyavataret, tiryagapipravicinuyāt | sa evaṃ pravicinvaṃstāścatasra oṣadhīrārāgayet | ārāgya ca kāṃciddantaiḥ kṣoditāṃ kṛtvā dadyāt, kāṃcit peṣayitvā dadyāt, kāṃcidanyadravyasaṃyojitāṃ pācayitvā dadyāt, kāṃcidāmadravyasaṃyojitāṃ kṛtvā dadyāt, kāṃcicchalākayā śarīrasthānaṃ viddhvā dadyāt, kāṃcidagninā paridāhya dadyāt, kāṃcidanyonyadravyasaṃyuktāṃ yāvat pānabhojanādiṣvapi yojayitvā dadyāt | atha sa jātyandhapuruṣastenopāyayogena cakṣuḥ pratilabheta | sa pratilabdhacakṣurbahiradhyātmaṃ dūre āsanne ca candrasūryaprabhāṃ nakṣatrāṇi grahān sarvarūpāṇi ca paśyet | evaṃ ca vadet - aho batāhaṃ mūḍhaḥ, yo 'haṃ pūrvamācakṣamāṇānāṃ na śraddadhāmi, noktaṃ
body.translated_text: When this was said, the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s> said this to the Blessed One: "Even if, Blessed One, beings are of varied dispositions who have emerged from the three realms, is their <s>nirvāṇa</s> one, or two, or three?" The Blessed One said: "<s>Nirvāṇa</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, comes from the awakening to the equality of all <s>dharmas</s>. And that is one, not two, not three. Therefore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, I shall make a parable for you. For through a parable, some wise persons here understand the meaning of what has been spoken. Just as, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, there is a man blind from birth. He would say thus: 'There are no beautiful or ugly forms, there are no seers of beautiful or ugly forms, there is no sun or moon, there are no stars, there are no planets, there are no seers of planets.' Then other men would say before that man born blind: 'There are beautiful and ugly forms, there are seers of beautiful and ugly forms, there is a sun and moon, there are stars, there are planets, there are seers of planets.' But that man born blind would not trust those men and would not accept what was said. Then there would be a physician who knows all diseases. He would see that man born blind. He would think: 'This man's disease has arisen from past evil karma. And all diseases that arise are of four kinds: caused by wind, caused by bile, caused by phlegm, and caused by a combination of all three.' Then that physician, for the purpose of curing that disease, would ponder means again and again. He would think: 'The medicines that are currently available cannot cure this disease. But on <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains, there are four medicinal herbs. Which four? Namely: the first, called Endowed with All Colors, Flavors, and Forms; the second, called Liberator from All Diseases; the third, called Destroyer of All Poisons; the fourth, called Bestower of Happiness in One's Proper Place. These are the four medicinal herbs.' Then that physician, generating compassion for that man born blind, would devise a means by which he could go to <s>Himavat</s>, the king of mountains. Having gone, he would climb upward, descend below, and search horizontally. Searching thus, he would obtain those four medicinal herbs. Having obtained them, he would crush some with his teeth and give them, grind some and give them, cook some mixed with other substances and give them, prepare some mixed with raw substances and give them, pierce the body with a probe and give some, burn some with fire and give them, mix some with other substances and even add them to food and drink and give them. Then that man born blind, through that application of means, would recover his sight. Having recovered his sight, he would see external and internal things, far and near — the light of the moon and sun, the stars, the planets, and all forms. And he would say thus: 'Alas, I was a fool, that I did not trust those who told me before, and did not accept what was said!

body.text:
gṛhṇāmi | so 'hamidānīṃ sarvaṃ paśyāmi | mukto 'smi andhabhāvāt | pratilabdhacakṣuścāsmi | na ca me kaścid viśiṣṭataro 'stīti | tena ca samayena pañcābhijñā ṛṣayo bhaveyurdivyacakṣurdivyaśrotraparacittajñānapūrvanivāsānusmṛtijñānarddhivimokṣakriyākuśalāḥ, te taṃ puruṣamevaṃ vadeyuḥ - kevalaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa tvayā cakṣuḥ pratilabdham | na tu bhavān kiṃcijjānāti | kuto 'bhimānaste samutpannaḥ? na ca te 'sti prajñā | na cāsi paṇḍitaḥ | tamenamevaṃ vadeyuḥ - yadā tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa antargṛhaṃ niṣaṇṇo bahiranyāni rūpāṇi na paśyasi, na ca jānāsi, nāpi te ye sattvāḥ snigdhacittā vā drugdhacittā vā | na vijānīṣe pañcayojanāntarasthitasya janasya bhāṣamāṇasya | bherīśaṅkhādīnāṃ śabdaṃ na prajānāsi, na śṛṇoṣi | krośāntaramapyanutkṣipya pādau na śaknoṣi gantum | jātasaṃvṛddhaścāsi mātuḥ kukṣau | tāṃ ca kriyāṃ na smarasi | tatkathamasi paṇḍitaḥ? kathaṃ ca sarvaṃ paśyāmīti
vadasi? tatsādhu bhoḥ puruṣa yadandhakāraṃ tatprakāśamiti saṃjānīṣe, yacca prakāśaṃ tadandhakāramiti saṃjānīṣe ||
body.translated_text: Now I see everything! I am freed from blindness! And I have recovered my sight! And there is no one superior to me!' Then at that time, there would be sages possessed of the five superknowledges — skilled in the exercise of the divine eye, divine ear, knowledge of others' minds, recollection of former lives, and miraculous powers and liberations. They would say to that man: 'You, good man, have merely recovered your sight. You do not know anything. Whence has this conceit arisen in you? You have no wisdom. You are not learned.' They would say this to him: 'When you, good man, are seated inside a house and do not see external forms, and do not know them, and those beings who have minds friendly or hostile toward you — you do not perceive them. You do not recognize or hear the voice of a person standing five yojanas away, or the sound of drums, conch-shells, and the like. You cannot walk even a krośa without lifting your feet. And you were born and raised in your mother's womb. And you do not remember that event. How then are you learned? How can you say I see everything? Good man, it is proper for you to know this: what is darkness, you take for light; and what is light, you take for darkness.'"

body.text: atha sa puruṣastān ṛṣīnevaṃ vadet - ka upāyaḥ, kiṃ vā śubhaṃ karma kṛtvedṛśīṃ prajñāṃ pratilabheya, yuṣmākaṃ prasādāccaitān guṇān pratilabheya? atha khalu te ṛṣayastasya puruṣasyaivaṃ kathayeyuḥ - yadīcchasi, araṇye vasa | parvataguhāsu vā niṣaṇṇo dharmaṃ cintaya | kleśāśca te prahātavyāḥ | tathā dhūtaguṇasamanvāgato 'bhijñāḥ pratilapsyase | atha sa puruṣastamarthaṃ gṛhītvā pravrajitaḥ | araṇye vasan ekāgracitto lokatṛṣṇāṃ prahāya pañcābhijñāḥ prāpnuyāt | pratilabdhābhijñaśca cintayet - yadahaṃ pūrvamanyatkarma kṛtavān, tena me na kaścid guṇo 'dhigataḥ | idānīṃ yathācintitaṃ gacchāmi | pūrvaṃ cāhamalpaprajño 'lpapratisaṃvedī andhabhūto 'smyāsīt ||
body.translated_text: "Then that man would say to those sages: 'What means, what good karma should be performed to obtain such wisdom as yours, and to obtain these qualities through your grace?' Then those sages would say this to that man: 'If you wish, dwell in the forest! Or seated in mountain caves, reflect on the Dharma! And your afflictions should be abandoned! Then, endowed with the dhūtaguṇas (ascetic qualities), you shall obtain the superknowledges.' Then that man, having accepted that instruction, went forth into the homeless life. Dwelling in the forest, with a one-pointed mind, having abandoned worldly craving, he would attain the five superknowledges. Having attained the superknowledges, he would reflect: 'Whatever other karma I performed in the past, by that, no quality was attained by me. Now I go wherever I intend. And formerly, I was of little wisdom, little discernment — I was blind!'"

body.text: iti hi kāśyapa upamaiṣā kṛtā asyārthasya vijñaptaye | ayaṃ ca punaratrārtho draṣṭavyaḥ | jātyandha iti kāśyapa ṣaḍgatisaṃsārasthitānāṃ sattvānāmetadadhivacanam, ye saddharmaṃ na jānanti, kleśatamondhakāraṃ ca saṃvardhayanti | te cāvidyāndhāḥ | avidyāndhāśca saṃskārānupavicinvati, saṃskārapratyayaṃ ca nāmarūpam, yāvadevamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | evamavidyāndhāstiṣṭhanti sattvāḥ saṃsāre | tathāgatastu karuṇāṃ janayitvā traidhātukānniḥsṛtaḥ piteva priye ekaputrake karuṇāṃ janayitvā traidhātuke 'vatīrya sattvān saṃsāracakre paribhramataḥ saṃpaśyati | na ca te saṃsārānniḥsaraṇaṃ prajānanti | atha bhagavāṃstān prajñācakṣuṣā paśyati | dṛṣṭvā ca jānāti - amī sattvāḥ pūrvaṃ kuśalaṃ kṛtvā mandadveṣāstīvrarāgāḥ, mandarāgāstīvradveṣāḥ, kecidalpaprajñāḥ, kecit paṇḍitāḥ, kecitparipākaśuddhāḥ, kecinmithyādṛṣṭayaḥ | teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tathāgata upāyakauśalyena trīṇi yānāni deśayati | tatra yathā te ṛṣayaḥ pañcābhijñā viśuddhacakṣuṣaḥ, evaṃ bodhisattvā bodhicittānyutpādya anutpattikīṃ dharmakṣāntiṃ pratilabhya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyante ||
body.translated_text: 'Thus, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, this simile has been made for the understanding of this meaning. And this meaning herein should be seen as follows: "One blind from birth" — this, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, is a designation for beings established in the cycle of the six destinies of existence, who do not know the true <s>Dharma</s> and increase the darkness of afflictions. And they are blinded by ignorance. And being blinded by ignorance, they accumulate formations; from formations as condition, name-and-form [arises], and so on, until thus there is the arising of this entire great mass of suffering. Thus beings, blinded by ignorance, remain in <s>saṃsāra</s>. But the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having generated compassion, has emerged from the three realms — like a father generating compassion for his dear only child — having descended into the three realms, he sees beings revolving in the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>. But they do not know the escape from <s>saṃsāra</s>. Then the Blessed One sees them with the eye of wisdom. Having seen, he knows: "These beings, having formerly done wholesome deeds — some have slight hatred but intense passion, some have slight passion but intense hatred, some are of little wisdom, some are learned, some are purified and mature, and some hold wrong views." For those beings, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through skillful means, teaches three vehicles. Therein, just as those <s>ṛṣis</s> possessed the five superknowledges and purified vision, so <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having generated the thought of awakening and having attained the patience of non-arising of <s>dharmas</s>, fully awaken to unsurpassed perfect awakening.'

body.text: tatra yathāsau mahāvaidyaḥ, evaṃ tathāgato draṣṭavyaḥ | yathāsau jātyandhastathā mohāndhāḥ sattvā draṣṭavyāḥ | yathā vātapittaśleṣmāṇaḥ, evaṃ rāgadveṣamohāḥ, dvāṣaṣṭi ca dṛṣṭikṛtāni draṣṭavyāni | yathā catasra oṣadhayastathā śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanirvāṇadvāraṃ ca draṣṭavyam | yathā yathā dravyāṇyupayujyante, tathā tathā vyādhayaḥ praśāmyantīti | evaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitāni vimokṣamukhāni bhāvayitvā sattvā avidyāṃ nirodhayanti | avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ, yāvadevamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati | evaṃ cāsya cittaṃ na kuśale tiṣṭhati na pāpe ||
body.translated_text: 'Therein, just as that great physician [should be seen], so should the <s>Tathāgata</s> be seen. Just as that one blind from birth, so should beings blinded by delusion be seen. Just as wind, bile, and phlegm [should be seen], so should passion, hatred, and delusion, and the sixty-two views, be seen. Just as the four medicines, so should emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), signlessness (<s>animitta</s>), wishlessness (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and the gate of <s>nirvāṇa</s> be seen. Just as when the substances are applied, just so the diseases are calmed — even so, having cultivated the three gates of liberation — emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness — beings destroy ignorance. From the destruction of ignorance, the destruction of formations [follows], and so on, until thus there is the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering. And thus his mind does not abide in the wholesome or the unwholesome.'

body.text: yathā andhaścakṣuḥ pratilabhate, tathā śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānīyo draṣṭavyaḥ | saṃsārakleśabandhanāni cchinatti | kleśabandhanānnirmuktaḥ pramucyate ṣaṅgatikāt traidhātukāt | tena śrāvakayānīyaḥ evaṃ jānāti, evaṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣate - na santyapare dharmā abhisaṃboddhavyāḥ | nirvāṇaprāpto 'smīti | atha khalu tathāgatastasmai dharmaṃ deśayati | yena sarvadharmā na prāptāḥ, kutastasya nirvāṇamiti? taṃ bhagavān bodhau samādāpayati | sa utpannabodhicitto na saṃsārasthito na nirvāṇaprāpto bhavati | so 'vabudhya traidhātukaṃ daśasu dikṣu śūnyaṃ nirmitopamaṃ māyopamaṃ svapnamarīcipratiśrutkopamaṃ lokaṃ paśyati | sa sarvadharmānanutpannānaniruddhān abaddhānamuktān atamondhakārān naprakāśān paśyati | ya evaṃ gambhīrān dharmān paśyati, sa paśyati apaśyanayā sarvatraidhātukaṃ paripūrṇamanyonyasattvāśayādhimuktam ||
body.translated_text: 'Just as the blind one obtains sight, so should the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle practitioner and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle practitioner be seen. He cuts the bonds of afflictions of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Freed from the bonds of afflictions, he is liberated from the six-destiny triple world. Therefore the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle practitioner knows thus, and speaks thus: "There are no other <s>dharmas</s> to be awakened to. I have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>." Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches him the <s>Dharma</s>: "One by whom all <s>dharmas</s> are not attained — how can there be <s>nirvāṇa</s> for him?" The Blessed One exhorts him to awakening. He, having generated the thought of awakening, is neither established in <s>saṃsāra</s> nor has he attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Having understood, he sees the triple world as empty in the ten directions — resembling an emanation, resembling illusion, resembling a dream, mirage, and echo. He sees all <s>dharmas</s> as non-arisen and non-ceased, unbound and unliberated, without darkness and without light. He who sees such profound <s>dharmas</s>, he sees — by the method of non-seeing — the entire triple world as filled with the varied dispositions and inclinations of beings.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānaḥ tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, in order to display this very meaning even further, spoke at that time these verses:

children.text: candrasūryaprabhā yadvannipatanti samaṃ nṛṣu /
children.translated_text: Just as the radiance of the moon and the sun falls equally upon people —

children.text: guṇavatsvatha pāpeṣu prabhāyā nonapūrṇatā // Saddhp_5.45 //
