children.translated_text: on those endowed with qualities and on the wicked — in radiance there is no deficiency. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.45 ||

children.text: tathāgatasya prajñābhā samā hyādityacandravat /
children.translated_text: So is the wisdom-radiance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, equal like the sun and moon;

children.text: sarvasattvān vinayate na conā naiva cādhikā // Saddhp_5.46 //
children.translated_text: it disciplines all beings — it is neither less nor more. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.46 ||

children.text: yathā kulālo mṛdbhāṇḍaṃ kurvan mṛtsu samāsvapi /
children.translated_text: Just as a potter, making clay vessels from clays that are equal,

children.text: bhavanti bhājanā tasya guḍakṣīradhṛtāmbhasām // Saddhp_5.47 //
children.translated_text: produces vessels for molasses, milk, ghee, and water, || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.47 ||

children.text: aśuceḥ kānicittatra dadhno 'nyāni bhavanti tu /
children.translated_text: some for what is impure, and others for curds,

children.text: mṛdamekāṃ sa gṛhṇāti kurvan bhāṇḍāni bhārgavaḥ // Saddhp_5.48 //
children.translated_text: that descendent of <s>Bhṛgu</s>, taking one [same] clay, makes [different] vessels — || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.48 ||

children.text: yādṛk prakṣipyate dravyaṃ bhājanaṃ tena lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: according to whatever substance is placed [in it], the vessel is characterized by that;

children.text: sattvāviśeṣe 'pi tathā rucibhedāttathāgatāḥ // Saddhp_5.49 //
children.translated_text: even so, although beings are undifferentiated, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, according to the difference of inclinations, || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.49 ||

children.text: yānabhedaṃ varṇayanti buddhayānaṃ tu niṃścitam /
children.translated_text: describe the differentiation of vehicles — but the <s>Buddhayāna</s> is definitive;

children.text: saṃsāracakrasyājñānānnirvṛtiṃ na vijānate // Saddhp_5.50 //
children.translated_text: because of ignorance of the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s>, they do not know cessation. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.50 ||

children.text: yastu śūnyān vijānāti dharmānātmavivarjitān /
children.translated_text: But one who knows <s>dharmas</s> as empty and devoid of self,

children.text: saṃbuddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ bodhiṃ jānāti tattvataḥ // Saddhp_5.51 //
children.translated_text: he knows in truth the awakening of the Blessed <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.51 ||

children.text: prajñāmadhyavyavasthānāt pratyekajina ucyate /
children.translated_text: Through being established midway in wisdom, one is called a <s>Pratyekajina</s> (solitary conqueror);

children.text: śūnyajñānavihīnatvācchrāvakaḥ saṃprabhāṣyate // Saddhp_5.52 //
children.translated_text: through being devoid of the knowledge of emptiness, one is called a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.52 ||

children.text: sarvadharmāvabodhāttu samyaksaṃbuddha ucyate /
children.translated_text: But through the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, one is called a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (perfectly awakened one);

children.text: tenopāyaśatairnityaṃ dharmaṃ deśeti prāṇinām // Saddhp_5.53 //
children.translated_text: and he, always with hundreds of skillful means, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.53 ||

children.text: yathā hi kaścijjātyandhaḥ sūryendugrahatārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as a certain person blind from birth, not seeing the sun, moon, planets, and stars,

children.text: apaśyannevamāhāsau nāsti rūpāṇi sarvaśaḥ // Saddhp_5.54 //
children.translated_text: would say thus: 'There are no forms anywhere.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.54 ||

children.text: jātyandhe tu mahāvaidyaḥ kāruṇyaṃ saṃniveśya ha /
children.translated_text: A great physician, establishing compassion toward the one blind from birth,

children.text: himavantaṃ sa gatvāna tiryagūrdhvamadhastathā // Saddhp_5.55 //
children.translated_text: having gone to the <s>Himavat</s> (Himalayas) — across, above, and below — || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.55 ||

children.text: sarvavarṇarasthānā nagāllabhata oṣadhīḥ /
children.translated_text: from the mountains, from places of all colors and tastes, he obtains herbs;

children.text: evamādīścatasro 'tha prayogamakarottataḥ // Saddhp_5.56 //
children.translated_text: and taking these four [kinds] and more, he prepared a treatment from them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.56 ||

children.text: dantaiḥ saṃcūrṇya kāṃcittu piṣṭvā cānyāṃ tathāparām /
children.translated_text: Some he ground with his teeth, some he crushed, and yet another,

children.text: sūcyagreṇa praveśyāṅge jātyandhāya prayojayet // Saddhp_5.57 //
children.translated_text: inserting [them] into the body with the tip of a needle, he would administer [them] to the one blind from birth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.57 ||

children.text: sa labdhacakṣuḥ saṃpaśyet sūryendugrahatārakāḥ /
children.translated_text: He, having gained sight, would see the sun, moon, planets, and stars;

children.text: evaṃ cāsya bhavetpūrvajñānāttadudāhṛtam // Saddhp_5.58 //
children.translated_text: and thus it would be for him — declared from his former knowledge. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.58 ||

children.text: evaṃ sattvā mahājñānā jātyandhāḥ saṃsaranti hi /
children.translated_text: Thus beings of great knowledge, blind from birth, transmigrate

children.text: pratītyotpādacakrasya ajñānādduḥkhavartmanaḥ // Saddhp_5.59 //
children.translated_text: because of ignorance of the wheel of dependent origination, the path of suffering. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.59 ||

children.text: evamajñānasaṃmūḍhe loke sarvaviduttamaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this world deluded by ignorance, the supreme knower of all,

children.text: tathāgato mahāvaidya utpannaḥ karuṇātmakaḥ // Saddhp_5.60 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the great physician, has arisen, whose nature is compassion. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.60 ||

children.text: upāyakuśalaḥ śāstā saddharmaṃ deśayatyasau /
children.translated_text: The Teacher, skilled in means, teaches the true <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: anuttarāṃ buddhabodhiṃ deśayatyagrayānike // Saddhp_5.61 //
children.translated_text: he teaches the unsurpassed Buddha-awakening to those of the foremost vehicle. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.61 ||

children.text: prakāśayati madhyāṃ tu madhyaprajñāya nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: But he illuminates the intermediate [awakening] for those of intermediate wisdom — the Leader;

children.text: saṃsārabhīrave bodhimanyāṃ saṃvarṇayatyapi // Saddhp_5.62 //
children.translated_text: and for one terrified of <s>saṃsāra</s>, he praises yet another awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.62 ||

children.text: traidhātukānniḥsṛtasya śrāvakasya vijānataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the <s>Śrāvaka</s> who has escaped from the triple world and understands,

children.text: bhavatyevaṃ mayā prāptaṃ nirvāṇamamalaṃ śivam // Saddhp_5.63 //
children.translated_text: it is thus: 'I have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> — stainless, auspicious.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.63 ||

children.text: tāmeva tatra prakāśemi naitannirvāṇamucyate /
children.translated_text: That very thing I illuminate for him there: 'This is not called <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: sarvadharmāvabodhāttu nirvāṇaṃ prāpyate 'mṛtam // Saddhp_5.64 //
children.translated_text: through the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, the immortal <s>nirvāṇa</s> is attained.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.64 ||

children.text: maharṣayo yathā tasmai karuṇāṃ saṃniveśya vai /
children.translated_text: Just as those great sages, having established compassion toward him,

children.text: kathayanti ca mūḍho 'si mā te 'bhūjjñānavānaham // Saddhp_5.65 //
children.translated_text: say to him: 'You are deluded! Do not think yourself knowledgeable! || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.65 ||

children.text: abhyantarāvasthitastvaṃ yadā bhavasi koṣṭhake /
children.translated_text: 'When you are situated inside a room,

children.text: bahiryadvartate tadvai na jānīṣe tvamalpadhīḥ // Saddhp_5.66 //
children.translated_text: you do not know what transpires outside, O you of small intelligence! || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.66 ||

children.text: yo 'bhyantare 'vasthitastu bahirjñātaṃ kṛtākṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'He who, though situated inside, knows what is done and not done outside —

children.text: so adyāpi na jānāti kutastvaṃ vetsyase 'lpadhīḥ // Saddhp_5.67 //
children.translated_text: even he does not know [everything] today — how then will you know, O you of small intelligence? || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.67 ||

children.text: pañcayojanamātraṃ tu yaḥ śabdo niścarediha /
children.translated_text: 'A sound that would emanate from merely five <s>yojanas</s> —

children.text: taṃ śrotuṃ na samartho 'si prāgevānyaṃ vidūrataḥ // Saddhp_5.68 //
children.translated_text: you are not able to hear that, let alone something else from afar! || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.68 ||

children.text: tvayi ye pāpacitta vā anunītāstathāpare /
children.translated_text: 'Those who are ill-disposed toward you, and likewise those who are well-disposed —

children.text: te na śakyaṃ tvayā jñātumabhimānaḥ kuto 'sti te // Saddhp_5.69 //
children.translated_text: they cannot be known by you — how can there be conceit in you? || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.69 ||

children.text: krośamātre 'pi gantavye padavīṃ na vinā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Even for a distance of a mere <s>krośa</s> to be traveled, there is no going without a guide;

children.text: mātuḥ kukṣau ca yadvṛttaṃ vismṛtaṃ tattadeva te // Saddhp_5.70 //
children.translated_text: and even what happened in your mother's womb — that you have forgotten entirely! || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.70 ||

children.text: abhijñā yasya pañcaitāḥ sa sarvajña ihocyate /
children.translated_text: 'One who has these five superknowledges is called omniscient in this world;

children.text: tvaṃ mohādapyakiṃcijjñaḥ sarvajño 'smīti bhāṣase // Saddhp_5.71 //
children.translated_text: you, through delusion, knowing nothing, declare: "I am omniscient!"' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.71 ||

children.text: sarvajñatvaṃ prārthayase yadyabhijñābhinirhareḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If you seek omniscience, you should produce the superknowledges;

children.text: taṃ cābhijñābhinirhāramaraṇyastho vicintaya /
children.translated_text: and dwelling in the forest, contemplate this production of the superknowledges —

children.text: dharmaṃ viśuddhaṃ tena tvamabhijñāḥ pratilapsyase // Saddhp_5.72 //
children.translated_text: the pure <s>Dharma</s>; by that you will obtain the superknowledges.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.72 ||

children.text: so 'rthaṃ gṛhya gato 'raṇyaṃ cintayet susamāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having grasped the meaning, he went to the forest and would contemplate, well-concentrated;

children.text: abhijñāḥ prāptavān pañca nacireṇa guṇānvitaḥ // Saddhp_5.73 //
children.translated_text: before long, endowed with qualities, he attained the five superknowledges. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.73 ||

children.text: tathaiva śrāvakāḥ sarve prāptanirvāṇasaṃjñinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, all <s>Śrāvakas</s>, thinking they have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> —

children.text: jino 'tha deśayettasmai viśrāmo 'yaṃ na nirvṛtiḥ // Saddhp_5.74 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jina</s> then teaches them: 'This is a resting-place, not cessation.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.74 ||

children.text: upāya eṣa buddhānāṃ vadanti yadimaṃ nayam /
children.translated_text: This is the skillful means of the Buddhas — they speak this method;

children.text: sarvajñatvamṛte nāsti nirvāṇaṃ tatsamārabha // Saddhp_5.75 //
children.translated_text: apart from omniscience, there is no <s>nirvāṇa</s> — strive for that! || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.75 ||

children.text: tryadhvajñānamanantaṃ ca ṣaṭ ca pāramitāḥ śubhāḥ /
children.translated_text: The infinite knowledge of the three times, and the six auspicious <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),

children.text: śūnyatāmanimittaṃ ca praṇidhānavivarjitam // Saddhp_5.76 //
children.translated_text: emptiness and signlessness, and freedom from aspiration, || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.76 ||

children.text: bodhicittaṃ ca ye cānye dharmā nirvāṇagāminaḥ /
children.translated_text: the thought of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>), and other <s>dharmas</s> leading to <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: sāsravānāsravāḥ śāntāḥ sarve gaganasaṃnibhāḥ // Saddhp_5.77 //
children.translated_text: with and without outflows, peaceful — all resembling space. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.77 ||

children.text: brahmavihārāścatvāraḥ saṃgrahā ye ca kīrtitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The four <s>brahmavihāras</s> (divine abidings) and those that are called <s>saṃgrahas</s> (means of gathering disciples) —

children.text: sattvānāṃ vinayārthāya kīrtitāḥ paramarṣibhiḥ // Saddhp_5.78 //
children.translated_text: are proclaimed by the supreme sages for the purpose of disciplining beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.78 ||

children.text: yaśca dharmān vijānāti māyāsvapnasvabhāvakān /
children.translated_text: And one who knows <s>dharmas</s> as having the nature of illusion, dream,

children.text: kadalīskandhaniḥsārān pratiśrutkāsamānakān // Saddhp_5.79 //
children.translated_text: essenceless like a plantain trunk, resembling an echo, || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.79 ||

children.text: tatsvabhāvaṃ ca jānāti traidhātukamaśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: and knows the true nature of the triple world in its entirety —

children.text: abaddhamavimuktaṃ ca na vijānāti nirvṛtim // Saddhp_5.80 //
children.translated_text: unbound and unfreed — he does not know cessation. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.80 ||

children.text: sarvadharmān samān śūnyānnirnānākaraṇātmakān /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are equal, empty, without distinction in nature;

children.text: na caitān prekṣate nāpi kiṃciddharmaṃ vipaśyati // Saddhp_5.81 //
children.translated_text: he does not examine these, nor does he see any <s>dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.81 ||

children.text: sa paśyati mahāprajño dharmakāyamaśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: He of great wisdom sees the <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body) in its entirety;

children.text: nāsti yānatrayaṃ kiṃcidekayānamihāsti tu // Saddhp_5.82 //
children.translated_text: there is no triple vehicle whatsoever — there is one vehicle here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.82 ||

children.text: sarvadharmāḥ samāḥ sarve samāḥ samasamāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are equal, all are equal, always equal and uniform;

children.text: evaṃ jñātvā vijānāti nirvāṇamamṛtaṃ śivam // Saddhp_5.83 //
children.translated_text: knowing thus and understanding — the immortal, auspicious <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 5.83 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye oṣadhīparivarto nāma pañcamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifth chapter, named the Chapter on Herbs (<s>Oṣadhīparivarta</s>), in the Noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_6: vyākaraṇaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 6: The Chapter on Prophecy (<s>Vyākaraṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimā gāthā bhāṣitvā sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - ārocayāmi vo bhikṣavaḥ, prativedayāmi | ayaṃ mama śrāvakaḥ kāśyapo bhikṣustriṃśato buddhakoṭīsahasrāṇāmantike satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati, teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saddharmaṃ dhārayiṣyati | sa paścime samucchraye avabhāsaprāptāyāṃ lokadhātau mahāvyūhe kalpe raśmiprabhāso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | dvādaśa cāsyāntarakalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | viṃśatiṃ cāsyāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | viṃśatimevāntarakalpān saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthāsyati | taccāsya buddhakṣetraṃ śuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati śuci apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhalyamapagataśvabhraprapātamapagatasyandanikāgūtholigallaṃ samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ vaiḍūryamayaṃ ratnavṛkṣapratimaṇḍitaṃ suvarṇasūtrāṣṭāpadanibaddhaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇam | bahūni ca tatra bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇyutpatsyante | aprameyāṇi ca tatra śrāvakakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bhaviṣyanti | na ca tatra māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraṃ lapsyate, na ca māraparṣat prajñāsyate | bhaviṣyanti tatra khalu punarmāraśca māraparṣadaśca | api tu khalu punastatra lokadhātau tasyaiva bhagavato raśmiprabhāsasya tathāgatasya śāsane saddharmaparigrahāyābhiyuktā bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having spoken these verses, addressed the entire assembly of monks: 'I declare to you, monks, I announce: this monk <s>Kāśyapa</s>, my <s>Śrāvaka</s>, will perform honor to thirty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, will perform respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem, and will uphold the true <s>Dharma</s> of those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. In his final birth, in the world-system called <s>Avabhāsaprāptā</s> (Radiance-Attained), in the great <s>Vyūha</s> (Adornment) <s>kalpa</s>, there will arise a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one in the world named <s>Raśmiprabhāsa</s> (Light of Radiance), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. And his lifespan will be twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. His true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, and the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And his <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field) will be pure, clean, free from stones, gravel, and roughness, free from chasms and precipices, free from drains and refuse, level, delightful, pleasing, beautiful to behold, made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), adorned with jewel-trees, bordered by golden cords in a chessboard pattern, strewn with flowers. And many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will arise there. And immeasurable <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundreds of thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s> will be there. And <s>Māra</s>, the evil one, will not gain entry there, nor will <s>Māra's</s> retinue be known. Yet there will be <s>Māra</s> and <s>Māra's</s> retinues there — but they will be devoted to upholding the true <s>Dharma</s> in the teaching of that Blessed One <s>Raśmiprabhāsa</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: paśyāmyahaṃ bhikṣava buddhacakṣuṣā sthaviro hyayaṃ kāśyapa buddha bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'I see with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, O monks — this elder <s>Kāśyapa</s> shall become a <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: anāgate 'dhvāni asaṃkhyakalpe kṛtvāna pūjāṃ dvipadottamānām // Saddhp_6.1 //
children.translated_text: in the future age, in incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, having made offerings to the supreme among bipeds. [Saddhp 6.1]

children.text: triṃśatsahasrāḥ paripūrṇakoṭyo jinānayaṃ drakṣyati kāśyapo hyayam /
children.translated_text: This <s>Kāśyapa</s> shall see <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) — thirty thousand full <s>koṭis</s> —

children.text: cariṣyatī tatra ca brahmacaryaṃ bauddhasya jñānasya kṛtena bhikṣavaḥ // Saddhp_6.2 //
children.translated_text: and there he shall practice the holy life, for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, O monks. [Saddhp 6.2]

children.text: kṛtvāna pūjāṃ dvipadottamānāṃ samudāniya jñānamidaṃ anuttaram /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the supreme among bipeds and gathered this unsurpassed knowledge,

children.text: sa paścime cocchrayi lokanātho bhaviṣyate apratimo maharṣiḥ // Saddhp_6.3 //
children.translated_text: in his final birth, he shall become a Lord of the World, an incomparable great seer. [Saddhp 6.3]

body.text: kṣetraṃ ca tasya pravaraṃ bhaviṣyati vicitra śuddhaṃ śubha darśanīyam /
body.translated_text: And his field shall be the finest — variegated, pure, auspicious, beautiful to behold,

body.text: manojñarūpaṃ sada premaṇīyaṃ suvarṇasūtraiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ ca // Saddhp_6.4 //
body.translated_text: of delightful form, always lovely, adorned with golden cords. [Saddhp 6.4]

children.text: ratnāmayā vṛkṣa tahiṃ vicitrā aṣṭāpadasmiṃ tahi ekameke /
children.translated_text: Variegated jewel-trees shall be there, each one on the chessboard [pattern],

children.text: manojñagandhaṃ ca vimuñcamānā bheṣyanti kṣetrasmi imasmi bhikṣo // Saddhp_6.5 //
children.translated_text: releasing delightful fragrance — they shall be in this field, O monk. [Saddhp 6.5]

children.text: puṣpaprakāraiḥ samalaṃkṛtaṃ ca vicitrapuṣpairupaśobhitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: And it shall be adorned with flower-displays, beautified with variegated flowers;

children.text: śvabhraprapātā na ca tatra santi samaṃ śivaṃ bheṣyati darśanīyam // Saddhp_6.6 //
children.translated_text: there shall be no chasms or precipices — it shall be level, auspicious, and beautiful to behold. [Saddhp 6.6]

children.text: tahi bodhisattvāna sahasrakoṭyaḥ sudāntacittāna maharddhikānām /
children.translated_text: There shall be thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, well-tamed in mind, of great supernatural power,

children.text: vaipulyasūtrāntadharāṇa tāyināṃ bahū bhaviṣyanti sahasra neke // Saddhp_6.7 //
children.translated_text: bearers of <s>vaipulya</s>-sūtras of the Protectors — many, in unnumbered thousands. [Saddhp 6.7]

children.text: anāsravā antimadehadhāriṇo bheṣyanti ye śrāvaka dharmarājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from outflows, bearers of their final bodies — these shall be the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of that <s>Dharma</s>-king;

children.text: pramāṇu teṣāṃ na kadāci vidyate divyena jñānena gaṇitva kalpān // Saddhp_6.8 //
children.translated_text: their measure shall never be found, even counting for <s>kalpas</s> with divine knowledge. [Saddhp 6.8]

children.text: so dvādaśa antarakalpa sthāsyati saddharma viṃśāntarakalpa sthāsyati /
children.translated_text: He shall endure for twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>; the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: pratirūpakaścāntarakalpa viṃśatiṃ raśmiprabhāsasya viyūha bheṣyati // Saddhp_6.9 //
children.translated_text: and the semblance shall endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> — the arrangement of <s>Raśmiprabhāsa</s>. [Saddhp 6.9]'

body.text:
atha khalvāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ sthavira āyuṣmāṃśca subhūtirāyuṣmāṃśca mahākātyāyanaḥ pravepamānaiḥ kāyairbhagavantamanimiṣairnetrairvyavalokayanti sma |
tasyāṃ ca velāyāṃ pṛthak pṛthaṅamanaḥsaṃgītyā imā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, the venerable <s>Subhūti</s>, and the venerable <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, with trembling bodies, gazed upon the Blessed One with unblinking eyes. And at that moment, each separately, in unison of thought, spoke these verses:

children.text: arhanta he mahāvīra śākyasiṃha narottama /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Arhat</s>, O great hero, O Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, O best of men!

children.text: asmākamanukampāya buddhaśabdamudīraya // Saddhp_6.10 //
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for us, proclaim the word "<s>Buddha</s>!" [Saddhp 6.10]

children.text: avaśyamavasaraṃ jñātvā asmākaṃ pi narottama /
children.translated_text: Knowing the right occasion for us too, O best of men,

children.text: amṛteneva siñcitvā vyākuruṣva vibhojana // Saddhp_6.11 //
children.translated_text: sprinkle us as if with nectar — prophesy [for us], O bountiful one! [Saddhp 6.11]

children.text: durbhikṣādāgataḥ kaścinnaro labdhvā subhojanam /
children.translated_text: As a man who has come from a famine, upon finding good food,

children.text: pratīkṣa bhūya ucyeta hastaprāptasmi bhojane // Saddhp_6.12 //
children.translated_text: would still look forward [anxiously], being told: "Food is at hand!" — [Saddhp 6.12]

children.text: evamevotsukā asmo hīnayānaṃ vicintaya /
children.translated_text: just so, we are eager, reflecting on the inferior vehicle;

children.text: duṣkālabhuktasattvā vā buddhajñānaṃ labhāmahe // Saddhp_6.13 //
children.translated_text: like beings who have eaten in a time of scarcity, may we obtain <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! [Saddhp 6.13]

children.text: na tāvadasmān saṃbuddho vyākaroti mahāmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: The perfectly enlightened one, the great sage, does not yet prophesy for us;

children.text: yathā hastasmi prakṣiptaṃ na tadbhuñjīta bhojanam // Saddhp_6.14 //
children.translated_text: it is as though food placed in [one's] hand is not eaten. [Saddhp 6.14]

children.text: evaṃ ca utsukā vīra śrutvā ghoṣamanuttaram /
children.translated_text: Thus eager, O hero, having heard the unsurpassed proclamation —

children.text: vyākṛtā yada bheṣyāmastadā bheṣyāma nirvṛtāḥ // Saddhp_6.15 //
children.translated_text: when we are prophesied, then we shall be at peace. [Saddhp 6.15]

children.text: vyākarohi mahāvīra hitaiṣī anukampakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Prophesy, O great hero, benevolent and compassionate one!

children.text: api dāridryacittānāṃ bhavedanto mahāmune // Saddhp_6.16 //
children.translated_text: May there be an end [to suffering] even for those of poverty-minds, O great sage!' [Saddhp 6.16]

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣā mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ sthavirāṇāmimamevaṃrūpaṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya punarapi sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - ayaṃ me bhikṣavo mahāśrāvakaḥ sthaviraḥ subhūtistriṃśata eva buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati | tatra ca brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyati, bodhiṃ ca samudānayiṣyati | evaṃrūpāṃścādhikārān kṛtvā paścime samucchraye śaśiketurnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | ratnasaṃbhavaṃ ca nāmāsya tad buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | ratnāvabhāsaśca nāma sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | samaṃ ca tad buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati, ramaṇīyaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ ratnavṛkṣavicitritamapagataśvabhraprapātamapagatagūtholigallaṃ manojñaṃ puṣpābhikīrṇam | kūṭāgāraparibhogeṣu cātra puruṣā vāsaṃ kalpayiṣyanti | bahavaścāsya śrāvakā bhaviṣyantyaparimāṇāḥ, yeṣāṃ na śakyaṃ gaṇanayā paryanto 'dhigantum | bahūni cātra bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bhaviḥyanti | tasya ca bhagavato dvādaśāntarakalpānāyuḥpramāṇaṃ bhaviḥyati | viṃśatiṃ cāntarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | viṃśatimevāntarakalpān saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthāsyati | sa ca bhagavān vaihāyasamantarīkḥe sthitvā abhīkḥṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayiḥyati, bahūni ca bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi bahūni ca śrāvakaśatasahasrāṇi vineḥyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having understood with his mind the mental deliberation of those elder great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, again addressed the entire assembly of monks: 'I declare to you, monks, I announce: this elder <s>Subhūti</s>, my great <s>Śrāvaka</s>, will perform honor to thirty <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, will perform respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem. He will practice the holy life there and will gather awakening. Having performed such preparations, in his final birth, there will arise a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one named <s>Śaśiketu</s> (Moon-Banner) in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. His <s>buddhakṣetra</s> will be called <s>Ratnasaṃbhava</s> (Jewel-Born). And his <s>kalpa</s> will be called <s>Ratnāvabhāsa</s> (Jewel-Radiance). His <s>buddhakṣetra</s> will be level, delightful, made of crystal, adorned with variegated jewel-trees, free from chasms and precipices, free from refuse, beautiful, strewn with flowers. And men there will dwell enjoying mansions. He will have many <s>Śrāvakas</s>, immeasurable, whose limit cannot be reached by calculation. And there will be many <s>koṭi-nayuta</s>-hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> there. And that Blessed One's lifespan will be twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. The true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, and the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. And that Blessed One, standing in mid-air, will frequently teach the <s>Dharma</s>, and will discipline many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and many hundreds of thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: ārocayāmi ahamadya bhikṣavaḥ prativedayāmyadya mamā śṛṇotha /
children.translated_text: 'I declare to you today, O monks; I announce — hear me now!

children.text: sthaviraḥ subhūtirmama śrāvako 'yaṃ bhaviṣyate buddha anāgate 'dhvani // Saddhp_6.17 //
children.translated_text: This elder <s>Subhūti</s>, my <s>Śrāvaka</s>, shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the future age. [Saddhp 6.17]

body.text: buddhāṃśca paśyitva mahānubhāvān triṃśacca pūrṇānayutāna koṭīḥ /
body.translated_text: Having seen <s>Buddhas</s> of great power — thirty full <s>nayuta koṭis</s> —

body.text: cariṣyate carya tadānulomikīmimasya jñānasya kṛtena caiṣaḥ // Saddhp_6.18 //
body.translated_text: he shall practice the conduct conforming to that, for the sake of this knowledge. [Saddhp 6.18]

children.text: sa paścime vīra samucchrayasmin dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhārī /
children.translated_text: In his final birth, that hero, bearing the form of the thirty-two marks,

children.text: suvarṇayūpapratimo maharṣirbhaviṣyate lokahitānukampī // Saddhp_6.19 //
children.translated_text: like a golden pillar, that great seer shall become a benefactor and compassionate one for the world. [Saddhp 6.19]

children.text: sudarśanīyaṃ ca sukṣetra bheṣyati iṣṭaṃ manojñaṃ ca mahājanasya /
children.translated_text: His field shall be beautiful, a fine field — desired, delightful, for the great multitude,

children.text: vihariṣyate yatra sa lokabandhustāritva prāṇīnayutāna koṭīḥ // Saddhp_6.20 //
children.translated_text: where that friend of the world shall dwell, having saved <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings. [Saddhp 6.20]

children.text: bahubodhisattvātra mahānubhāvā avivartyacakrasya pravartitāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great power shall be there, turners of the irreversible wheel,

children.text: tīkṣṇendriyāstasya jinasya śāsane ye śobhayiṣyanti ta buddhakṣetram // Saddhp_6.21 //
children.translated_text: of sharp faculties in the teaching of that <s>Jina</s> — they shall adorn that <s>Buddha</s>-field. [Saddhp 6.21]

children.text: bahuśrāvakāstasya na saṃkhya teṣāṃ pramāṇu naivāsti kadāci teṣām /
children.translated_text: Many <s>Śrāvakas</s> shall be his — their number is beyond count,

children.text: ṣaḍabhijña traividya maharddhikāśca aṣṭāvimokṣeṣu pratiṣṭhitāśca // Saddhp_6.22 //
children.translated_text: never is there a measure of them — endowed with the six superknowledges, the triple knowledge, great supernatural powers, and established in the eight liberations. [Saddhp 6.22]

children.text: acintiyaṃ ṛddhibalaṃ ca bheṣyati prakāśayantasyimamagrabodhim /
children.translated_text: Inconceivable shall be his power of supernatural ability, as he illuminates this supreme awakening;

children.text: devā manuṣyā yatha gaṅgavālikā bheṣyanti tasyo satataṃ kṛtāñjalī // Saddhp_6.23 //
children.translated_text: gods and humans, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, shall constantly stand before him with joined palms. [Saddhp 6.23]

children.text: so dvādaśo antarakalpa sthāsyapi saddharmu viṃśāntarakalpa sthāsyati /
children.translated_text: He shall endure for twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>; the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: pratirūpako viṃśatimeva sthāsyati  kalpāntarāṇi dvipadottamasya // Saddhp_6.24 //
children.translated_text: and the semblance shall endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> — of the supreme among bipeds. [Saddhp 6.24]'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - ārocayāmi vo bhikṣayaḥ, prativedayāmi | ayaṃ mama śrāvakaḥ sthaviro mahākātyāyano 'ṣṭānāṃ buddhakoṭīśatasahasrāṇāmantike satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati | parinirvṛtānāṃ ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāṃ stūpān kariṣyati yojanasahasraṃ samucchrayeṇa pañcāśad yojanāni pariṇāhena saptānāṃ ratnānām | tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmargabhasya musāragalvasya saptamasya ratnasya | teṣāṃ ca stūpānāṃ pūjāṃ kariṣyati puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantībhiśca
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the entire assembly of monks: 'I declare to you, monks, I announce: this elder <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, my <s>Śrāvaka</s>, will perform honor to eight hundred thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, will perform respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem. And he will build <s>stūpas</s> for those <s>Tathāgatas</s> who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, fifty <s>yojanas</s> in circumference, made of the seven jewels — namely, gold, silver, <s>vaidūrya</s>, crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (diamond), and <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), the seventh jewel. And he will make offerings to those <s>stūpas</s> with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-standards.

body.text: | tataśca bhūyaḥ pareṇa paratareṇa punarviśatīnāṃ buddhakoṭīnāmantike evarūpameva satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati | sa paścime samucchraye paścime ātmabhāvapratilambhe jāmbūnadaprabhāso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavan | pariśuddhaṃ cāsya buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ darśanīyaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ ratnavṛkṣābhivicitritaṃ suvarṇasūtrācchoḍitaṃ puṣpasaṃstarasaṃstṛtamapagatanirayatiryagyoniyamalokāsurakāyaṃ bahunaradevapratipūrṇaṃ bahuśrāvakaḥatasahasropaḥobhitaṃ bahubodhisattvaḥatasahasrālaṃkṛtam | dvādaḥa cāsya antarakalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | viṃḥatiṃ cāsya antarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | viṃḥatimevāntarakalpān saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthāsyati ||
body.translated_text: And then, further and further beyond, he will perform similar honor, respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem to twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. In his final birth, in his final acquisition of a bodily existence, there will arise a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one named <s>Jāmbūnadaprabhāsa</s> (Gold-of-Jambu-River Radiance) in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. His <s>buddhakṣetra</s> will be completely pure, level, delightful, pleasing, beautiful to behold, made of crystal, adorned with variegated jewel-trees, bordered by golden cords, covered with spreads of flowers, free from hells, animal realms, <s>Yama's</s> world, and <s>Asura</s> hosts, filled with many gods and humans, beautified with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, adorned with many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. His lifespan will be twelve intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. His true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, and the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: śṛṇotha me bhikṣava adya sarve udāharantasya girāmananyathām /
children.translated_text: 'Listen to me, all monks, today, as I utter a speech that is not otherwise:

children.text: kātyāyanaḥ sthaviru ayaṃ mi śrāvakaḥ kariṣyate pūja vināyakānām // Saddhp_6.25 //
children.translated_text: this elder <s>Kātyāyana</s> is my <s>Śrāvaka</s> — he shall make offerings to the Guides. [Saddhp 6.25]'

children.text: satkāru teṣāṃ ca bahuprakāraṃ bahūvidhaṃ lokavināyakānām /
children.translated_text: He will perform honor to them in many ways, of many kinds, to those Guides of the World,

children.text: stūpāṃśca kārāpayi nirvṛtānāṃ puṣpehi gandhehi ca pūjayiṣyati // Saddhp_6.26 //
children.translated_text: and will cause <s>stūpas</s> to be built for those who have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and will worship them with flowers and incense. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.26 ||

children.text: labhitva so paścimakaṃ samucchrayaṃ pariśuddhakṣetrasmi jino bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Having obtained that final exalted state, in a completely pure field he shall become a <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: paripūrayitvā imameva jñānaṃ deśeṣyate prāṇisahasrakoṭinām // Saddhp_6.27 //
children.translated_text: and having fulfilled this very knowledge, he shall teach thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.27 ||

children.text: sa satkṛto loki sadevakasmin prabhākaro buddha vibhurbhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: He, honored in the world with its gods, shall become a <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Prabhākara</s> (Light-Maker), mighty and sovereign,

children.text: jāmbūnadābhāsu sa cāpi nāmnā saṃtārako devamanuṣyakoṭinām // Saddhp_6.28 //
children.translated_text: and by the name <s>Jāmbūnadābhā</s> (Lustre of Jāmbūnada Gold), he shall be the liberator of <s>koṭis</s> of gods and humans. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.28 ||

children.text: bahubodhisattvāstatha śrāvakāśca amitā asaṃkhyā pi ca tatra kṣetre /
children.translated_text: Many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>, immeasurable and innumerable, in that field

children.text: upaśobhayiṣyanti ti buddhaśāsanaṃ bhavaprahīṇā vibhavāśca sarve // Saddhp_6.29 //
children.translated_text: shall beautify the teaching of the <s>Buddha</s> — all having abandoned existence and possessions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.29 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - ārocayāmi vo bhikṣavaḥ, prativedayāmi | ayaṃ mama śrāvakaḥ sthaviro mahāmaudgalyāyano 'ṣṭāviṃśatibuddhasahasrāṇyārāgayiṣyati, teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ vividhaṃ satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati | parinirvṛtānāṃ ca teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ stūpān kārayiṣyati saptaratnamayān | tadyathā suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaidūryasya sphaṭikasya lohitamukteraśmagarbhasya musāragalvasya | yojanasahasraṃ samucchrayeṇa pañcayojanaśatāni pariṇāhena | teṣāṃ ca stūpānāṃ vividhāṃ pūjāṃ kariṣyati puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantībhiḥ | tataśca bhūyaḥ pareṇa paratareṇa viṃśaterbuddhakoṭīśatasahasrāṇāmevaṃrūpameva satkāraṃ kariṣyati, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyati | paścime ca ātmabhāvapratilambhe tamālapatracandanagandho nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | manobhirāmaṃ ca nāmāsya tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | ratiprapūrṇaśca nāma sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | pariśuddhaṃ cāsya tadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati, samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ sudarśanīyaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ ratnavṛkṣābhivicitritaṃ muktakusumābhikīrṇaṃ bahunaradevapratipūrṇamṛṣiśatasahasraniṣevitaṃ yaduta śrāvakaiśca bodhisattvaiśca | caturviśatiṃ cāsya antarakalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | catvāriṃśacca antarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | catvāriṃśadeva antarakalpān saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthāsyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the entire assembly of monks: 'I declare to you, monks, I announce: this elder <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, my <s>Śrāvaka</s>, will pay homage to twenty-eight thousand <s>Buddhas</s>, and will perform varied honor, respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem to those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. And he will cause <s>stūpas</s> to be built for those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, made of the seven jewels — namely, gold, silver, <s>vaidūrya</s>, crystal, red pearl, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (diamond), and <s>musāragalva</s> (coral) — a thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in circumference. And he will perform various offerings to those <s>stūpas</s> with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-standards. And then, further and further beyond, he will perform similar honor, respect, reverence, veneration, worship, and esteem to twenty <s>koṭi</s> hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. In his final acquisition of a bodily existence, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one named <s>Tamālapatracandanagandha</s> (Fragrance of Tamāla-leaf Sandalwood) shall arise in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. His <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be named <s>Manobhirāma</s> (Delighting the Mind), and his <s>kalpa</s> shall be named <s>Ratiprapūrṇa</s> (Full of Delight). His <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be completely pure, level, delightful, pleasing, beautiful to behold, made of crystal, adorned with jewel-trees, strewn with loose flowers, filled with many gods and humans, frequented by hundreds of thousands of <s>ṛṣis</s> — namely, <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. His lifespan shall be twenty-four intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. The true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for forty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, and the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for forty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: maudgalyagotro mama śrāvako 'yaṃ jahitva mānuṣyakamātmabhāvam /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Maudgalyagotra</s> (one of <s>Maudgalya</s> lineage), my <s>Śrāvaka</s>, having abandoned this human bodily existence,

children.text: viṃśatsahasrāṇi jināna tāyināmanyāṃśca aṣṭau virajāna drakṣyati // Saddhp_6.30 //
children.translated_text: shall behold twenty-eight thousand <s>Jinas</s>, Protectors, and others who are free from defilement. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.30 ||

children.text: cariṣyate tatra ca brahmacaryaṃ bauddhaṃ imaṃ jñāna gaveṣamāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: He shall practice the holy life there, this Buddhist path, seeking this knowledge,

children.text: satkāru teṣāṃ dvipadottamānāṃ vividhaṃ tadā kāhi vināyakānām // Saddhp_6.31 //
children.translated_text: and shall perform varied honor to those supreme among bipeds, the Guides, at that time. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.31 ||

children.text: saddharmu teṣāṃ vipulaṃ praṇītaṃ dhāretva kalpāna sahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having upheld their vast and excellent true <s>Dharma</s> for thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: pūjāṃ ca stūpeṣu kariṣyate tadā parinirvṛtānāṃ sugatāna teṣām // Saddhp_6.32 //
children.translated_text: he shall then make offerings at the <s>stūpas</s> of those <s>Sugatas</s> who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.32 ||

body.text: ratnāmayān stūpa savaijayantān kariṣyate teṣa jinottamānām /
body.translated_text: He shall build <s>stūpas</s> made of jewels, with victory-banners, for those supreme <s>Jinas</s>,

body.text: puṣpehi gandhehi ca pūjayanto vādyehi vā lokahitānukampinām // Saddhp_6.33 //
body.translated_text: worshipping them with flowers and incense, and with music, those who have compassion for the welfare of the world. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.33 ||

children.text: tatpaścime caiva samucchrayasmin priyadarśane tatra manojñakṣetre /
children.translated_text: And in that final exalted state, in that beautiful and pleasing field,

children.text: bhaviṣyate lokahitānukampī tamālapatracandanagandha nāmnā // Saddhp_6.34 //
children.translated_text: he shall become one with compassion for the welfare of the world, named <s>Tamālapatracandanagandha</s> (Fragrance of Tamāla-leaf Sandalwood). || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.34 ||

children.text: caturviśapūrṇāntarakalpa tasya āyuṣpramāṇaṃ sugatasya bheṣyati /
children.translated_text: The lifespan of that <s>Sugata</s> shall be a full twenty-four intermediate <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: prakāśayantasyima buddhanetrīṃ manujeṣu deveṣu ca nityakālam // Saddhp_6.35 //
children.translated_text: illuminating this guide-eye of the <s>Buddha</s> for humans and gods constantly and at all times. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.35 ||

children.text: bahuśrāvakātasya jinasya tatra koṭī sahasrā yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Jina</s> shall have many <s>Śrāvakas</s> there — <s>koṭis</s> of thousands, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍabhijña traividya maharddhikāśca abhijñaprāptāḥ sugatasya śāsane // Saddhp_6.36 //
children.translated_text: possessing the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges), the threefold knowledge, and great miraculous powers, having attained <s>abhijñā</s> in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.36 ||

children.text: avaivartikāśco bahubodhisattvā ārabdhavīryāḥ sada saṃprajānāḥ /
children.translated_text: And many irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, of aroused vigor, always fully aware,

children.text: abhiyuktarūpāḥ sugatasya śāsane teṣāṃ sahasrāṇi bahūni tatra // Saddhp_6.37 //
children.translated_text: devoted to the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> — there shall be many thousands of them there. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.37 ||

children.text: parinirvṛtasyāpi jinasya tasya saddharmu saṃsthāsyati tasmi kāle /
children.translated_text: Even after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Jina</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure at that time,

children.text: viṃśacca viṃśāntarakalpa pūrṇā etatpramāṇaṃ pratirūpakasya // Saddhp_6.38 //
children.translated_text: for a full twenty and twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> — that is the measure of the semblance [<s>Dharma</s>]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.38 ||

children.text: maharddhikāḥ pañca mi śrāvakā ye nirdiṣṭa ye te maya agrabodhaye /
children.translated_text: These five <s>Śrāvakas</s> of mine, of great miraculous power, have been designated by me for supreme awakening;

children.text: anāgate 'dhvāni jināḥ svayaṃbhuvasteṣāṃ ca caryāṃ śṛṇuthā mamāntikāt // Saddhp_6.39 //
children.translated_text: in the future course they shall become self-arisen <s>Jinas</s> — hear from me the account of their conduct! || <s>Saddhp</s> 6.39 ||'

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye vyākaraṇaparivarto nāma ṣaṣṭhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Chapter on Prophecies,' in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>Dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_7: pūrvayogaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 7: The Chapter on the Former Connection (<s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s>).

body.text: bhūtapūrva bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani asaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairvipulairaprameyairacintyairaparimitairapramāṇaistataḥ pareṇa paratareṇa yadāsīt - tena kālena tena samayena mahābhijñājñānābhibhūrnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstāḥ devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān saṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau mahārūpe kalpe | kiyaccirotpannaḥ sa bhikṣavastathāgato 'bhūt | tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavo yāvāniha trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau pṛthivīdhātuḥ, taṃ kaścideva puruṣaḥ sarvaṃ cūrṇīkuryāt, maṣiṃ kuryāt | atha khalu sa puruṣastasmāllokadhātorekaṃ paramāṇurajo gṛhītvā pūrvasyāṃ diśi lokadhātusahasramatikramya tadekaṃ paramāṇuraja upanikṣipet | atha sa puruṣo dvitīyaṃ ca paramāṇurajo gṛhītvā tataḥ pareṇa parataraṃ lokadhātusahasramatikramya dvitīyaṃ paramāṇuraja upanikṣipet | anena paryāyeṇa sa puruṣaḥ sarvāvantaṃ pṛthivīdhātumupanikṣipet pūrvasyāṃ diśi | tatkiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ śakyaṃ teṣāṃ lokadhātūnāmanto vā paryanto vā gaṇanayādhigantum? ta āhuḥ - no hīdaṃ bhagavan, no hīdaṃ sugata | bhagavānāha - śakyaṃ punarbhikṣavasteṣāṃ lokadhātūnāṃ kenacid gaṇakena vā gaṇakamahāmātreṇa vā gaṇanayā paryanto 'dhigantum, yeṣu vopanikṣiptāni tāni paramāṇurajāṃsi, yeṣu vā nopanikṣiptāni | na tveva teṣāṃ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ śakyaṃ gaṇanāyogena paryanto 'dhigantum | yāvantaḥ kalpāstasya bhagavato mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya, etāvān sa kālo 'bhūdevamacintyaḥ, evamapramāṇaḥ | taṃ cāhaṃ bhikṣavastathāgataṃ tāvacciraṃ parinirvṛtamanena tathāgatajñānadarśanabalādhānena yathādya śvo vā parinirvṛtamanusmarāmi ||
body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O monks, in the past course, incalculable <s>kalpas</s> ago — more incalculable, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, unlimited, beyond measure, further and further beyond — at that time, in that era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly enlightened one named <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s> (Great One Overpowering through Superknowledge and Wisdom), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in a world-system called <s>Saṃbhavā</s>, in a <s>kalpa</s> called <s>Mahārūpa</s> (Great Form). How long ago did that <s>Tathāgata</s> arise, O monks? Suppose, O monks, a man were to grind into powder all the earth-element in this three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, reducing it to ink. Then that man, taking a single atom of dust from that world-system and going eastward, crossing a thousand world-systems, would deposit that single atom of dust. Then that man, taking a second atom of dust and going further and further beyond, crossing another thousand world-systems, would deposit the second atom of dust. In this manner, that man would deposit all that earth-element in the eastern direction. What do you think, O monks — is it possible to reach the end or limit of those world-systems by counting? They replied: 'No indeed, Blessed One! No indeed, <s>Sugata</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'Moreover, O monks, whether by some accountant or chief accountant, is it possible to reach the end by counting of those world-systems — both those where atoms of dust were deposited and those where they were not deposited? Even the end of the <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> cannot be reached by any method of counting. So many <s>kalpas</s> have passed since the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s> — so inconceivable, so immeasurable was that time. Yet I, O monks, by the power of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> knowledge, vision, and strength, remember that <s>Tathāgata</s>, though so long since passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, as if it were yesterday or today.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: abhū atītā bahu kalpakoṭyo anusmarāmi dvipadānamuttamam /
children.translated_text: 'There were in the past many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — I remember the supreme among bipeds,

children.text: abhijñajñānābhibhūvaṃ mahāmunimabhūṣi tatkālamanuttamo jinaḥ // Saddhp_7.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhijñajñānābhibhū</s> (Overpowering through Superknowledge and Wisdom), the great sage — at that time he was the unsurpassed <s>Jina</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.1 ||

children.text: yathā trisāhasrima lokadhātuṃ kaścid rajaṃ kurya aṇupramāṇam /
children.translated_text: Suppose someone were to grind this three-thousand world-system into dust of atomic measure,

children.text: paramāṇumekaṃ ca tato gṛhītvā kṣetraṃ sahasraṃ gamiyāna nikṣipet // Saddhp_7.2 //
children.translated_text: and taking a single atom from it, would go a thousand fields away and deposit it; || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.2 ||

children.text: dvitīyaṃ tṛtīyaṃ pi ca eva nikṣipet sarvaṃ pi so nikṣipi taṃ rajogatam /
children.translated_text: he would deposit a second and a third likewise, and would deposit all that dust thus produced —

children.text: riktā bhavetā iya lokadhātuḥ sarvaśca so pāṃsu bhaveta kṣīṇaḥ // Saddhp_7.3 //
children.translated_text: this world-system would become empty, and all that powder would be exhausted. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.3 ||

children.text: yo lokadhātūṣu bhaveta tāsu pāṃsu rajo yasya pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: Whatever world-systems there would be in those — dust whose measure is without limit —

children.text: rajaṃ karitvāna aśeṣatastaṃ lakṣyaṃ dade kalpaśate gate ca // Saddhp_7.4 //
children.translated_text: reducing all of them to dust without remainder, he would give a mark for each hundred <s>kalpas</s> passed. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.4 ||

children.text: evāprameyā bahu kalpakoṭyaḥ parinirvṛtasya sugatasya tasya /
children.translated_text: Thus immeasurable are the many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> since the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Sugata</s> —

children.text: paramāṇu sarve na bhavanti lakṣyāstāvadbahu kṣīṇa bhavanti kalpāḥ // Saddhp_7.5 //
children.translated_text: all the atoms are not [sufficient as] marks, so many <s>kalpas</s> have been exhausted. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.5 ||

children.text: tāvacciraṃ nirvṛtu taṃ vināyakaṃ tān śrāvakāṃstāṃśca pi bodhisattvān /
children.translated_text: So long ago passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> that Guide, with his <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —

children.text: etādṛśaṃ jñānu tathāgatānāṃ smarāmi vṛttaṃ yatha adya śvo vā // Saddhp_7.6 //
children.translated_text: such is the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — I remember the past as if it were today or yesterday. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.6 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ bhikṣava jñānametadanantajñānaśca tathāgatasya /
children.translated_text: Such, O monks, is this knowledge — the infinite knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: buddhaṃ mayā kalpaśatairanekaiḥ smṛtīya sūkṣmāya anāsravāya // Saddhp_7.7 //
children.translated_text: through many hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, I have remembered the <s>Buddha</s> by means of this subtle, outflow-free recollection. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.7 ||'

body.text:
tasya khalu punarbhikṣavo mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya catuṣpañcāśatkalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt | pūrve ca sa bhagavān mahābhijñānābhibhūstathāgato 'nabhisaṃbuddho 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragrata eva sarvāṃ mārasenāṃ prābhañjīt parājaiṣīt | prabhañjayitvā parājayitvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyāmiti na ca tāvattasya te dharmā āmukhībhavanti sma | sa bodhivṛkṣamūle bodhimaṇḍe ekamantarakalpamasthāt | dvitīyamapyantarakalpasthāt | na ca tāvadanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate | tṛtīyamapi caturthamapi pañcamamapi ṣaṣṭhamapi saptamamapi aṣṭamamapi navamamapi daśamamapyantarakalpaṃ
bodhivṛkṣamūle bodhimaṇḍe 'sthāt sakṛdvartanena paryaṅkena antarādavyutthitaḥ | aniñjamānena cittena acalamānena avepamānena kāyenāsthāt | na ca tāvadasya te dharmā āmukhībhavanti sma ||
body.translated_text: Now, O monks, the lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was fifty-four <s>koṭi</s> <s>nayuta</s> hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. Before that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, had attained supreme perfect awakening, while still unawakened, seated at the supreme seat of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> (place of awakening), he had already vanquished and defeated the entire army of <s>Māra</s>. Having vanquished and defeated them, thinking 'I shall attain supreme perfect awakening,' yet those <s>dharmas</s> did not become manifest to him. He sat at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> for one intermediate <s>kalpa</s>. He sat for a second intermediate <s>kalpa</s> as well, yet did not attain supreme perfect awakening. He sat for a third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, and tenth intermediate <s>kalpa</s> at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, in a single sitting with legs crossed, without rising in between, with an unwavering mind, an unmoved and untrembling body. Yet those <s>dharmas</s> did not become manifest to him.

body.text: tasya khalu punarbhikṣavo bhagavato bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatasya devaistrāyastriṃśairmahāsiṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptamabhūd yojanaśatasahasraṃ samucchrayeṇa, yatra sa bhagavān niṣadya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | samanantaraniṣaṇṇasya ca khalu punastasya bhagavato bodhimaṇḍe, atha brahmakāyikā devaputrā divyaṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravarṣayāmāsuḥ | bodhimaṇḍasya parisāmantakena yojanaśatamantarikṣe ca vātān pramuñcanti, ye taṃ jīrṇapuṣpamavakarṣayanti | yathāpravarṣitaṃ ca tat puṣpavarṣaṃ tasya bhagavato bodhimaṇḍe niṣaṇṇasya avyucchinnaṃ pravarṣayanti | paripūrṇān daśāntarakalpān taṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti
body.translated_text: Now, O monks, for that Blessed One seated at the supreme seat of the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) heaven had prepared a great lion-throne, a hundred-thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height, upon which that Blessed One, having sat down, attained supreme perfect awakening. And immediately upon that Blessed One being seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods rained down a divine shower of flowers. And around the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s> for a hundred <s>yojanas</s>, winds were released in the sky that swept away the withered flowers. And that flower-shower, as it was rained down upon that Blessed One seated at the <s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>, was rained down uninterruptedly. For a full ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, they showered and covered that Blessed One

body.text: sma | tathā pravarṣitaṃ ca tatpuḥpavarḥaṃ pravarḥayanti yāvat parinirvāṇakālasamaye tasya bhagavatastaṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti | cāturmahārājakāyikāśca devaputrā divyāṃ devadundubhimabhipravādayāmāsuḥ | tasya bhagavato bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatasya satkārārthamavyucchinnaṃ pravādayāmāsuḥ paripūrṇān daśāntarakalpān tasya bhagavato niḥaṇṇasya | tata uttari tāni divyāṇi tūryāṇi satatasamitaṃ pravādayāmāsuryāvattasya bhagavato mahāparinirvāṇakālasamayāt ||
body.translated_text: they rained [flowers]. And they continued to rain that flower-shower until the time of the Blessed One's <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, showering upon that Blessed One. And the sons of the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> heaven sounded divine heavenly drums. They sounded them uninterruptedly for the honor of that Blessed One seated at the supreme seat of awakening, for the full ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> while that Blessed One was seated. Beyond that, those divine musical instruments were sounded continuously until the time of that Blessed One's great <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavo daśānāmantarakalpānāmatyayena sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | samanantarābhisaṃbuddhaṃ ca taṃ viditvā ye tasya bhagavataḥ kumārabhūtasya ṣoḍaśa putrā abhūvannaurasāḥ, jñānākaro nāma teṣāṃ jyeṣṭho 'bhūt | teṣāṃ ca khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ ṣoḍaśānāṃ rājakumārāṇāmekaikasya ca vividhāni krīḍanakāni rāmaṇīyakānyabhūvan vicitrāṇi darśanīyāni | atha khalu bhikṣavaste ṣoḍaśa rājakumārāstāni vividhāni krīḍanakāni rāmaṇīyakāni visarjayitvā, taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaṃ viditvā, mātṛbhirdhātrībhiśca rudantībhiḥ parivṛtāḥ puraskṛtāḥ tena ca mahārājñā cakravartinā āryakeṇa mahākośena rājāmātyaiśca bahubhiśca prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtāḥ puraskṛtāḥ yena bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataḥ, tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma | tasya bhagavataḥ satkārārthāya gurukārārthāya mānanārthāya pūjanārthāya arcanārthāya apacāyanārthāya upasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā taṃ bhagavantaṃ triṣpradakṣiṇīkṛtya añjaliṃ pragṛhya taṃ bhagavantaṃ saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhiḥ sārūpyābhirabhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, after the passing of ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, attained supreme perfect awakening. And immediately upon knowing him to have attained awakening, the sixteen sons who had been princes of that Blessed One when he was still a layman — of whom the eldest was named <s>Jñānākara</s> — and each of those sixteen princes, O monks, had various playthings, delightful and marvelous to behold. Then, O monks, those sixteen princes abandoned those various delightful playthings, and having learned that the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One had attained supreme perfect awakening, surrounded and attended by their weeping mothers and nurses, and by that great king, the wheel-turning monarch, their grandfather, together with his great treasury and ministers and many <s>koṭis</s>, <s>nayutas</s>, and hundred-thousands of beings, they approached the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who was seated at the supreme seat of awakening. They approached for the purpose of honoring, venerating, respecting, worshipping, paying homage to, and revering that Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of that Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and with palms joined together, praised that Blessed One face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: mahābhiṣaṭko 'si anuttaro 'si anantakalpaiḥ samudāgato 'si /
children.translated_text: You are the great anointed one, the unsurpassed one; you have come through infinite <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: uttāraṇārthāyiha sarvadehināṃ paripūrṇa saṃkalpu ayaṃ ti bhadrakaḥ // Saddhp_7.8 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of liberating all embodied beings here — your resolution is fulfilled; this is excellent! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.8 ||

children.text: suduṣkarā antarakalpimān daśa kṛtāni ekāsani saṃniṣadya /
children.translated_text: Most difficult [was your feat]: you have performed ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s> of single-seated sitting,

children.text: na ca te 'ntarā kāyu kadāci cālito na hastapādaṃ na pi cānyadaṅgam // Saddhp_7.9 //
children.translated_text: and your body was never stirred in the meantime — neither hand nor foot nor any other limb. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.9 ||

children.text: cittaṃ pi te śāntagataṃ susaṃsthitamaniñjyabhūtaṃ sada aprakampyam /
children.translated_text: Your mind also has gone to peace, well-established, immovable, always unshakable;

children.text: vikṣepu naivāsti kadāci pi tava atyantaśāntasthitu tvaṃ anāsravaḥ // Saddhp_7.10 //
children.translated_text: distraction is never found in you — you are established in ultimate peace, free from outflows. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.10 ||

children.text: diṣṭayāsi kṣemeṇa ca svastinā ca aviheṭhitaḥ prāpta imāgrabodhim /
children.translated_text: By good fortune, in safety and well-being, unharmed, you have attained this supreme awakening;

children.text: asmākamṛddhī iyamevarūpā diṣṭayā ca vardhāma narendrasiṃha // Saddhp_7.11 //
children.translated_text: this is our great fortune too — by good fortune we prosper, O lion among kings! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.11 ||

children.text: anāyikeyaṃ praja sarva duḥkhitā utpāṭitākṣī va nihīnasaukhyā /
children.translated_text: This leaderless multitude, all suffering, as if with eyes plucked out, devoid of happiness,

children.text: mārgaṃ na jānanti dukhāntagāminaṃ na mokṣahetorjanayanti vīryam // Saddhp_7.12 //
children.translated_text: does not know the path leading to the end of suffering, nor do they generate vigor for the sake of liberation. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.12 ||

children.text: apāya vardhanti ca dīrgharātraṃ divyāśca kāyāḥ parihāṇadharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: The lower realms increase through the long night, and the divine hosts are subject to decline;

children.text: na śrūyate jātu jināna śabdastamondhakāro ayu sarvalokaḥ // Saddhp_7.13 //
children.translated_text: never is the voice of the <s>Jinas</s> heard — this entire world is darkened by dense gloom. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.13 ||

children.text: prāptaṃ ca te lokavidū ihādya śivaṃ padaṃ uttama nāsravaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: You, the Knower of the World, have now attained here the auspicious, supreme, outflow-free state;

children.text: vayaṃ ca lokaśca anugṛhītaḥ śaraṇaṃ ca tvā eti vrajāma nātha // Saddhp_7.14 //
children.translated_text: we and the world are blessed — we go to you as refuge, O Protector! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.14 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste ṣoḍaśa rājakumārāḥ kumārabhūtā eva bālakāḥ, taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhimukhaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamābhiḥ sārūpyabhīrgāthābhiḥ saṃmukhamabhiṣṭutya taṃ bhagavantamadhyeṣante sma dharmacakrapravartanatāyai - deśayatu bhagavān dharmam, deśayatu sugato dharmaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca | tasyāṃ ca velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those sixteen princes, still being youths, boys, having praised the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One face to face with fitting verses, entreated that Blessed One to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel: 'May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s>! May the <s>Sugata</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of gods and humans!' And at that time they spoke these verses —

children.text: deśehi dharmaṃ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇā vināyakā apratimā maharṣe /
children.translated_text: Teach the <s>Dharma</s>, O you marked with a hundred merits, O incomparable guide, O great sage!

children.text: labdhaṃ ti jñānaṃ pravaraṃ viśiṣṭaṃ prakāśayā loki sadevakasmin // Saddhp_7.15 //
children.translated_text: You have obtained supreme, distinguished knowledge — illuminate it in this world with its gods! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.15 ||

children.text: asmāṃśca tārehi imāṃśca sattvān nidarśaya jñānu tathāgatānām /
children.translated_text: Liberate us and these beings! Reveal the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

children.text: yathā vayaṃ pi imamagrabodhiṃ anuprāpnuyāmo 'tha ime ca sattvāḥ // Saddhp_7.16 //
children.translated_text: so that we too may attain this supreme awakening, and these beings likewise! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.16 ||

body.text: caryāṃ ca jñānaṃ pi ca sarva jānasi adhyāśayaṃ pūrvakṛtaṃ ca puṇyam /
body.translated_text: You know both the conduct and all knowledge, and the aspiration and the merit previously accumulated;

body.text: adhimukti jānāsi ca sarvaprāṇināṃ pravartayā cakravaraṃ anuttaram // Saddhp_7.17 //
body.translated_text: you know the resolve of all living beings — turn the unsurpassed, supreme wheel! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.17 ||

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena tena bhagavatā mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyamānena daśasu dikṣvaikaikasyāṃ diśi pañcāśallokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitānyabhūīvan, mahatā cāvabhāsena sphuṭānyabhūvan | sarveṣu ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu yā lokāntarikāstāsu ye akṣaṇāḥ saṃvṛtā andhakāratamisrāḥ yatra imāvapi candrasūryau evaṃmaharddhikau evaṃmahānubhāvau evaṃmahaujaskau ābhayāpyābhāṃ nānubhavataḥ, varṇenāpi varṇaṃ tejasāpi tejo nānubhavataḥ, tāsvapi tasmin samaye mahato 'vabhāsasya prādurbhāvo 'bhūt | ye 'pi tāsu lokāntarikāsu sattvā upapannāḥ, te 'pyanyonyamevaṃ paśyanti anyonyamevaṃ saṃjānanti - anye 'pi bata bhoḥ sattvāḥ santīhopapannāḥ | anye 'pi bata bhoḥ sattvāḥ santīhopapannāḥ iti | sarveṣu ca teṣu lokadhātuṣu yāni devabhavanāni devavimānāni ca, yāvad brahmalokād ṣaḍvikāraṃ prakampitānyabhūvan, mahatā cāvabhāsena sphuṭānyabhūvan atikramya devānāṃ devānubhāvam | iti hi bhikṣavastasmin samaye teṣu lokadhātuṣu mahataḥ pṛthivīcālasya mahataśca audārikasyāvabhāsasya loke prādurbhāvo 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then at that time, O monks, when that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One was attaining supreme perfect awakening, in each of the ten directions, five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems trembled with a sixfold quaking, and were filled with a great radiance. And in all those world-systems, those inter-world darknesses, the unfavorable states shrouded in blind darkness where even these two — the moon and sun — of such great power, such great might, such great splendor, do not experience radiance with their radiance, nor do they experience color with their color or brilliance with their brilliance — even in those [inter-world spaces], at that time there arose the manifestation of a great radiance. And those beings who had been reborn in those inter-world spaces also saw one another and perceived one another, [saying]: 'Indeed, there are other beings reborn here too! Indeed, there are other beings reborn here too!' And in all those world-systems, whatever divine mansions and divine palaces there were, up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, trembled with a sixfold quaking and were filled with a great radiance surpassing the divine splendor of the gods. Thus, O monks, at that time, in those world-systems, there arose the manifestation of a great earthquake and a great, massive radiance in the world.

body.text: atha pūrvasyāṃ diśi teṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu yāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni, tānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti, śrīmanti aujasvīni ca | atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāmetadabhavat - imāni khalu punarbrāhmāṇi vimānānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti aujasvīni ca | kasya khalvidaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te sarve 'nyonyabhavanāni gatvā ārocayāmāsuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then, in the eastern direction, in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, the <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces shone, blazed, and glittered exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> had this thought: 'These <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces are shining, blazing, and glittering exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Of what will this be a portent?' Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems all went to one another's abodes and reported.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sarvasattvatrātā nāma mahābrahmā taṃ mahāntaṃ brahmagaṇaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, a <s>Mahābrahmā</s> named <s>Sarvasattvatrātā</s> (Protector of All Beings) addressed that great assembly of <s>Brahmās</s> with verses —

children.text: atīva no harṣita adya sarve vimānaśreṣṭhā imi prajvalanti /
children.translated_text: All of us are exceedingly overjoyed today — these supreme palaces are blazing;

children.text: śriyā dyutīyā ca manoramā ye kiṃ kāraṇaṃ īdṛśu bheṣyate 'dya // Saddhp_7.18 //
children.translated_text: beautiful with splendor and radiance and delightful — what will be the cause of such [a sight] today? || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.18 ||

children.text: sādhu gaveṣāmatha etamarthaṃ ko devaputro upapannu adya /
children.translated_text: Come, let us investigate this matter! What son of a god has been born today,

children.text: yasyānubhāvo ayamevarūpo abhūtapūrvo ayamadya dṛśyate // Saddhp_7.19 //
children.translated_text: whose power is of such a kind — something unprecedented is seen today? || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.19 ||

children.text: yadi vā bhaved buddha narendrarājā utpannu lokasmi kahiṃcidadya /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps a <s>Buddha</s>, a king among men, has arisen somewhere in the world today,

children.text: yasyo nimittaṃ imamevarūpaṃ śriyā daśo dikṣu jvalanti adya // Saddhp_7.20 //
children.translated_text: by whose portent of such a form the ten directions blaze with splendor today? || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.20 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te sarve sahitāḥ samagrāstāni divyāni svāni svāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyabhiruhya divyāṃśca sumerumātrān puṣpapuṭān gṛhītvā catasṛṣu dikṣvanucaṃkramanto 'nuvicarantaḥ paścimaṃ digbhāgaṃ prakrāntāḥ | adrākṣuḥ khalu punasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇaḥ paścime digbhāge taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ, taiśca putraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhī rājakumārairadhyeṣyamāṇaṃ dharmacakrapravartanatāyai | dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena sa bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taiśca sumerumātraiḥ puṣpapuṭaistaṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma, taṃ ca bodhivṛkṣaṃ daśayojanapramāṇam | abhyavakīrya tāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātayāmāsuḥ - parigṛhṇātu bhagavānimāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni asmākamanukampāmupādāya | paribhuñjatu sugata imāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyasmākamanukampāmupādāya ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, all united and assembled, ascended their own respective divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces, and taking divine flower-baskets as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, traversing and surveying in the four directions, proceeded toward the western direction. And those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, O monks, in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, saw in the western direction the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, seated at the supreme seat of awakening on a lion-throne at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, surrounded and attended by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and being entreated by those sixteen princes to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Having seen [him], they approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of that Blessed One, circumambulated him many hundred-thousands of times, and showered and sprinkled that Blessed One with those <s>Sumeru</s>-sized flower-baskets, [showering] also that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree which was ten <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Having showered [him], they offered those <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us! May the <s>Sugata</s> enjoy these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastāni svāni svāni vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ saṃmukhamābhirgāthābhiḥ sārūpyābhirabhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, having offered their own palaces to the Blessed One, at that time praised that Blessed One face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: āścaryabhūto jina aprameyo utpanna lokasmi hitānukampī /
children.translated_text: A wondrous, immeasurable <s>Jina</s> has arisen in the world — compassionate for the welfare [of all];

children.text: nātho 'si śāstāsi gurūsi jāto anugṛhītā daśimā diśo 'dya // Saddhp_7.21 //
children.translated_text: you are born as Protector, Teacher, and Guru — these ten directions are blessed today! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.21 ||

children.text: pañcāśatī koṭisahasra pūrṇā yā lokadhātūna ito bhavanti /
children.translated_text: From those world-systems that are a full five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of hundred-thousands from here,

children.text: yato vayaṃ vandana āgatā jinaṃ vimānaśreṣṭhān prajahitva sarvaśaḥ // Saddhp_7.22 //
children.translated_text: we have come for worship of the <s>Jina</s>, having abandoned all our supreme palaces. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.22 ||

children.text: pūrveṇa karmeṇa kṛtena asmin vicitracitrā hi ime vimānāḥ /
children.translated_text: By merit formerly accumulated, these varied and wondrous palaces of ours [were obtained];

children.text: pratigṛhya asmākamanugrahārthaṃ paribhuñjatāṃ lokavidū yatheṣṭam // Saddhp_7.23 //
children.translated_text: having accepted them for the sake of our blessing, may the Knower of the World enjoy them as he wishes! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.23 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānabhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya taṃ bhagavantametadūcuḥ - pravartayatu bhagavān dharmacakram, pravartayatu sugato dharmacakraṃ loke | deśayatu bhagavān nirvṛtim | tārayatu bhagavān sattvān | anugṛhṇātu bhagavānimaṃ lokam | deśayatu bhagavān dharmasvāmī dharmamasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ | tad bhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> praised that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, face to face with fitting verses, and said this to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel! May the <s>Sugata</s> turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel in the world! May the Blessed One teach <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation)! May the Blessed One liberate beings! May the Blessed One show grace to this world! May the Blessed One, the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, teach the <s>Dharma</s> to this world with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, to this generation with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>! That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of gods and humans!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastāni pañcāśad brahmakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyekasvareṇa samasaṃgītyā taṃ bhagavantamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>, with one voice, in unison, addressed that Blessed One with these fitting verses —

children.text: deśehi bhagavan dharmaṃ deśehi dvipadottama /
children.translated_text: Teach the <s>Dharma</s>, O Blessed One! Teach, O Supreme among Bipeds!

children.text: maitrībalaṃ ca deśehi sattvāṃstārehi duḥkhitān // Saddhp_7.24 //
children.translated_text: Show the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), and liberate beings who are suffering! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.24 ||

children.text: durlabho lokapradyotaḥ puṣpamaudumbaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Rare is the Illuminator of the World, like the <s>udumbara</s> flower;

children.text: utpanno 'si mahāvīra adhyeṣāmastathāgatam // Saddhp_7.25 //
children.translated_text: you have arisen, O Great Hero — we entreat the <s>Tathāgata</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.25 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayati sma ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One consented to those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> by his silence.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena pūrvadakṣiṇe digbhāge teṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu yāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni, tānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣāṃ brahmaṇāmetadabhavat - imāni khalu punarbrāhmāṇi vimānānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | kasya khalvidaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te 'pi sarve 'nyonyabhavanāni gatvā ārocayāmāsuḥ | atha khalu bhikṣavo 'dhimātrakāruṇiko nāma mahābrahmā taṃ mahāntaṃ brahmagaṇaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
