body.translated_text: Then again, O monks, at that time, in the southeastern direction, in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, the <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces shone, blazed, and glittered exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Then, O monks, those <s>Brahmās</s> had this thought: 'These <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces are shining, blazing, and glittering exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Of what will this be a portent?' Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems all went to one another's abodes and reported. Then, O monks, a <s>Mahābrahmā</s> named <s>Adhimātrakāruṇika</s> (Supremely Compassionate) addressed that great assembly of <s>Brahmās</s> with verses —

children.text: kasya pūrvanimittena māriṣā atha dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: By whose portent, O noble ones, is this now seen?

children.text: vimānāḥ sarvi bhrājanti adhimātraṃ yaśasvinaḥ // Saddhp_7.26 //
children.translated_text: All the palaces are blazing exceedingly, [belonging to those] endowed with glory! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.26 ||

children.text: yadi vā devaputro 'dya puṇyavanta ihāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Or has a meritorious son of a god come here today,

children.text: yasyeme anubhāvena vimānāḥ sarvi śobhitāḥ // Saddhp_7.27 //
children.translated_text: by whose power all these palaces are made resplendent? || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.27 ||

children.text: atha vā buddha loke 'sminnutpanno dvipadottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Or perhaps a <s>Buddha</s>, supreme among bipeds, has arisen in this world,

children.text: anubhāvena yasyādya vimānā imi īdṛśāḥ // Saddhp_7.28 //
children.translated_text: by whose power these palaces are of such a kind today? || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.28 ||

children.text: sahitāḥ sarvi mārgāmo naitat kāraṇamalpakam /
children.translated_text: Let us all go together — this is no small matter;

children.text: na khalvetādṛśaṃ pūrvaṃ nimittaṃ jātu dṛśyate // Saddhp_7.29 //
children.translated_text: indeed, such a portent has never before been seen! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.29 ||

children.text: caturdiśaṃ prapadyāmo añcāmaḥ kṣetrakoṭiyo /
children.translated_text: Let us go forth in the four directions, let us traverse <s>koṭis</s> of fields;

children.text: vyaktaṃ loke 'dya buddhasya prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyati // Saddhp_7.30 //
children.translated_text: clearly, the manifestation of a <s>Buddha</s> in the world will occur today! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.30 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastānyapi pañcāśad brahmakoṭīnayutaḥatasahasrāṇi tāni svāni svāni divyāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyabhiruhya divyāṃḥca sumerumātrān puṣpapuṭān gṛhītvā catasṛṣu dikṣvanucaṃkramanto 'nuvicaranta uttarapaḥcimaṃ digbhāgaṃ prakrāntāḥ | adrākṣuḥ khalu punarbhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇa uttarapaḥcime digbhāge taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanopaviṣṭa parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ, taiḥca putraiḥ ṣoḍaḥabhī rājakumārairadhyeṣyamāṇaṃ dharmacakrapravartanatāyai | dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastenopasaṃkrantāḥ | upasaṃkramya ca tasya bhagavataḥ pādau ḥirobhirvanditvā taṃ bhagavantamanekaḥatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taiḥ sumerumātraiḥ puṣpapuṭaistaṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma taṃ ca bodhivṛkṣaṃ daḥayojanapramāṇam | abhyavakīrya tāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātayāmāsuḥ - parigṛhṇātu bhagavānimāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyasmākamanukampāmupādāya | paribhuñjatu sugata imāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyasmākamanukampāmupādāya ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s> ascended their own respective divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces, and taking divine flower-baskets as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, traversing and surveying in the four directions, proceeded toward the northwestern direction. And those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, O monks, saw in the northwestern direction the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, seated at the supreme seat of awakening on a lion-throne at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, surrounded and attended by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and being entreated by those sixteen princes to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Having seen [him], they approached the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of that Blessed One, circumambulated him many hundred-thousands of times, and showered and sprinkled that Blessed One with those <s>Sumeru</s>-sized flower-baskets, [showering] also that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree which was ten <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Having showered [him], they offered those <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us! May the <s>Sugata</s> enjoy these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastāni svāni svāni vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, having offered their own palaces to the Blessed One, at that time praised that Blessed One face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: namo 'stu te apratimā maharṣe devātidevā kalaviṅkasusvarā /
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O incomparable great sage, god above gods, [whose voice is sweet] like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird!

children.text: vināyakā loki sadevakasmin vandāmi te lokahitānukampī // Saddhp_7.31 //
children.translated_text: O Guide in this world with its gods, I bow to you, compassionate one for the welfare of the world! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.31 ||

children.text: āścaryabhūto 'si kathaṃciloke utpannu adyo sucireṇa nātha /
children.translated_text: You are a wondrous being — after so long, you have arisen somehow in the world today, O Protector!

children.text: kalpāna pūrṇā śata śūnya āsīdaśīti buddhairayu jīvalokaḥ // Saddhp_7.32 //
children.translated_text: For full hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> it was empty — this living world was [deprived] of <s>Buddhas</s> for eighty [hundred <s>kalpas</s>]! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.32 ||

children.text: śūnyaśca āsīddvipadottamehi apāyabhūmī tada utsadāsi /
children.translated_text: It was empty of the supreme among bipeds; the lower realms increased at that time,

children.text: divyāśca kāyāḥ parihāyiṣū tadā aśīti kalpāna śatā supūrṇā // Saddhp_7.33 //
children.translated_text: and the divine hosts declined — for full eighty hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.33 ||

children.text: so dāni cakṣuśca gatiśca leṇaṃ trāṇaṃ pitā co tatha bandhubhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now he is the eye, the path, the shelter, the refuge, the father, and likewise the kinsman;

children.text: utpannu lokasmi hitānukampī asmāka puṇyairiha dharmarājā // Saddhp_7.34 //
children.translated_text: he has arisen in the world, compassionate for [its] welfare — this <s>Dharma</s>-king, [arisen] through our merits! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.34 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya taṃ bhagavantametadūcuḥ - pravartayatu bhagavān dharmacakram | pravartayatu sugato dharmacakraṃ loke | deśayatu bhagavān nirvṛtim | tārayatu bhagavān sattvān | anugṛhṇātu bhagavānimaṃ lokam | deśayatu bhagavān dharmamasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurayāḥ | tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> praised that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, face to face with fitting verses, and said this to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel! May the <s>Sugata</s> turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel in the world! May the Blessed One teach <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation)! May the Blessed One liberate beings! May the Blessed One show grace to this world! May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s> to this world with its <s>Māra</s>, with its <s>Brahmā</s>, to this generation with its <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>! That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of gods and humans!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastāni pañcāśad brahmakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ekasvareṇa samasaṃgītyā taṃ bhagavantamābhyāṃ sārūpyābhyāṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>, with one voice, in unison, addressed that Blessed One with these two fitting verses —

children.text: pravartayā cakravaraṃ mahāmune prakāśayā dharmu daśādiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Turn the supreme wheel, O Great Sage! Illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> in the ten directions!

children.text: tārehi sattvān dukhadharmapīḍitān prāmodya harṣaṃ janayasva dehinām // Saddhp_7.35 //
children.translated_text: Liberate beings afflicted by the torment of suffering! Generate joy and delight in embodied beings! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.35 ||

children.text: yaṃ śrutva bodhīya bhaveyu lābhino divyāni sthānāni vrajeyu cāpi /
children.translated_text: Having heard [it], they would become recipients of awakening, and would also go to divine stations;

children.text: hāyeyu co āsurakāya sarve śāntāśca dāntāśca sukhī bhaveyuḥ // Saddhp_7.36 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>asura</s> hosts would all decline — peaceful and tamed, they would become happy! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.36 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavāṃsteṣāmapi mahābrahmaṇāṃ tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsayati sma ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One consented to those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> also by his silence.

body.text:
tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi teṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu yāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni tānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti, śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāmetadabhavat - imāni khalu punarbrāhmāṇi vimānānyatīva
bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | kasya khalvidamevaṃrūpaṃ pūrvanimittaṃ bhaviṣyati? atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te sarve 'nyonyabhavanāni gatvā ārocayāmāsuḥ | atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sudharmo nāma mahābrahmā taṃ mahāntaṃ brahmagaṇaṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣata -

children.text: nāhetu nākāraṇamadya mārṣāḥ sarve vimānā iha jājvalanti /
children.translated_text: Not without cause, not without reason, O noble ones, do all the palaces blaze today;

children.text: nimitta darśenti ha kiṃ pi loke sādhu gaveṣāma tametamartham // Saddhp_7.37 //
children.translated_text: they show a portent of something in the world — let us investigate this matter well! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.37 ||

body.translated_text: Then again, O monks, at that time, in the southern direction, in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, the <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces shone, blazed, and glittered exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> had this thought: 'These <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces are shining, blazing, and glittering exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Of what will this be a portent of such a form?' Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems all went to one another's abodes and reported. Then, O monks, a <s>Mahābrahmā</s> named <s>Sudharma</s> addressed that great assembly of <s>Brahmās</s> with two verses —

body.text: anūna kalpāna śatā hyatītā naitādṛśaṃ jātu nimittamāsīt /
body.translated_text: Full hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> have passed without interruption — never has such a portent been seen;

body.text: yadi vopapanno iha devaputro utpannu loke yadi veha buddhaḥ // Saddhp_7.38 //
body.translated_text: either a son of a god has been born here, or a <s>Buddha</s> has arisen in the world! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.38 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ te sarve sahitāḥ samagrāstāni divyāni svāni svāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyabhiruhya divyāṃśca sumerumātrān puṣpapuṭān gṛhītvā catasṛṣu dikṣvanucaṃkramanto 'nuvicaranta uttaraṃ digbhāgaṃ prakrāntāḥ | adrākṣuḥ khalu punarbhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇa uttaraṃ digbhāgaṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ, taiśca putraiḥ ṣoḍaṣabhī rājakumārairadhyeṣyamāṇaṃ dharmacakrapravartanatāyai | dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena sa bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taiḥ sumerumātraiḥ puṣpapuṭaistaṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma taṃ ca bodhivṛkṣaṃ daśayojanapramāṇam | abhyavakīrya tāni brāhmāṇi divyāni vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātayāmāsuḥ - parigṛhṇātu bhagavānimāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni asmākamanukampāmupādāya | paribhuñjatu sugata imāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni asmākamanukampāmupādāya ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, all united and assembled, ascended their own respective divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces, and taking divine flower-baskets as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, traversing and surveying in the four directions, proceeded toward the northern direction. And those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, O monks, saw in the northern direction the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, seated at the supreme seat of awakening on a lion-throne at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, surrounded and attended by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and being entreated by those sixteen princes to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Having seen [him], they approached that Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of that Blessed One, circumambulated him many hundred-thousands of times, and showered and sprinkled that Blessed One with those <s>Sumeru</s>-sized flower-baskets, [showering] also that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree which was ten <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Having showered [him], they offered those divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us! May the <s>Sugata</s> enjoy these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste 'pi mahābrahmāṇastāni svāni svāni vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> also, having offered their own palaces to the Blessed One, at that time praised that Blessed One face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: sudurlabhaṃ darśana nāyakānāṃ svabhyāgataṃ te bhavarāgamardana /
children.translated_text: Most rare is the sight of the Guides! It has come of its own accord, O Crusher of attachment to existence!

children.text: sucirasya te darśanamadya loke paripūrṇa kalpāna śatebhi dṛśyase // Saddhp_7.39 //
children.translated_text: After so long you are seen today in the world — you appear after full hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.39 ||

children.text: tṛṣitāṃ prajāṃ tarpaya lokanātha adṛṣṭapūrvo 'si kathaṃci dṛśyase /
children.translated_text: Satisfy the thirsty generation, O Lord of the World! You who have never been seen before are somehow now visible;

children.text: audumbaraṃ puṣpa yathaiva durlabhaṃ tathaiva dṛṣṭo 'si kathaṃci nāyaka // Saddhp_7.40 //
children.translated_text: just as the <s>udumbara</s> flower is rare, so you are somehow seen, O Guide! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.40 ||

children.text: vimāna asmākamimā vināyaka tavānubhāvena viśobhitādya /
children.translated_text: These palaces of ours, O Guide, are adorned today by your power;

children.text: parigṛhya etāni samantacakṣuḥ paribhuñja cāsmākamanugrahārtham // Saddhp_7.41 //
children.translated_text: having accepted these, O All-Seeing One, enjoy them for the sake of our blessing! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.41 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyabhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya te bhagavantametadūcuḥ - pravartayatu bhagavān dharmacakraṃ loke | deśayatu bhagavān nirvṛtim | tārayatu bhagavān sattvān | anugṛhṇātu bhagavānimaṃ lokam | deśayatu bhagavān dharmamasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> praised that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, face to face with fitting verses, and said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel in the world! May the Blessed One teach the path to <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation)! May the Blessed One ferry across all beings! May the Blessed One show grace to this world! May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s> to this world with its <s>Māras</s>, with its <s>Brahmās</s>, to the multitude of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text: prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ | tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: to the multitude together with gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>. That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude, of gods and humans!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastāni pañcāśad brahmakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ekasvareṇa samasaṃgītyā taṃ bhagavantamābhyāṃ sārūpyābhyāṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>, with a single voice, in unison, addressed the Blessed One with these two fitting verses —

children.text: deśehi dharmaṃ bhagavan vināyaka pravartayā dharmamayaṃ ca cakram /
children.translated_text: 'Teach the <s>Dharma</s>, O Blessed One, O Guide! Turn the wheel made of <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: nirnādayā dharmamayaṃ ca dundubhiṃ taṃ dharmaśaṅkhaṃ ca prapūrayasva // Saddhp_7.42 //
children.translated_text: Sound the drum made of <s>Dharma</s>, and fill the <s>Dharma</s>-conch to the full! || Saddhp 7.42 ||

children.text: saddharmavarṣaṃ varṣayasva loke valgusvaraṃ bhāṣa subhāṣitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Rain the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> upon the world! Speak with a sweet voice, well-spoken words!

children.text: adhyeṣito dharmamudīrayasva mocehi sattvā nayutāna koṭyaḥ // Saddhp_7.43 //
children.translated_text: Being entreated, proclaim the <s>Dharma</s>! Liberate beings, <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s>! || Saddhp 7.43 ||'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsayati sma | peyālam | evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi, evaṃ paścimāyāṃ diśi, evaṃ paścimottarasyāṃ diśi, evamuttarasyāṃ diśi, evamuttarapūrvasyāṃ diśi, evamadhodiśi ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One assented to those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> by his silence. [Abbreviated.] Likewise in the south-western direction, likewise in the western direction, likewise in the north-western direction, likewise in the northern direction, likewise in the north-eastern direction, likewise in the downward direction.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣava ūrdhvāyāṃ diśi teṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu yāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni, tānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣāṃ mahābrahmaṇāmetadabhavat - imāni khalu punarbrāhmāṇi vimānānyatīva bhrājanti tapanti virājanti śrīmanti ojasvīni ca | kasya khalvidamevaṃrūpaṃ pūrvaṃnimittaṃ bhaviṣyatīti? atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te sarve 'nyonyabhavanāni gatvā ārocayāmāsuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, in the upward direction, in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, the <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces shone, blazed, and glittered exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s> had this thought: 'These <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces are shining, blazing, and glittering exceedingly — resplendent and radiant. Of what will this be a portent?' Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems all went to one another's abodes and reported.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ śikhī nāma mahābrahmā taṃ mahāntaṃ brahmagaṇaṃ gāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, a <s>Mahābrahmā</s> named <s>Śikhī</s> addressed that great assembly of <s>Brahmās</s> with verses —

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mārṣa idaṃ bhaviṣyati yenā vimānāni parisphuṭāni /
children.translated_text: 'What will be the cause of this, O sirs, that the palaces are shining forth,

children.text: ojena varṇena dyutīya cāpi adhimātra vṛddhāni kimatra kāraṇam // Saddhp_7.44 //
children.translated_text: with radiance, color, and splendor as well — grown exceedingly — what is the cause here? || Saddhp 7.44 ||

children.text: na īdṛśaṃ no abhidṛṣṭapūrvaṃ śrutaṃ ca keno tatha pūrva āsīt /
children.translated_text: Never has such [a sight] been seen by us before, nor has it been heard from anyone in the past;

children.text: oja 'sphuṭāni yatha adya etā adhimātra bhrājanti kimatra kāraṇam // Saddhp_7.45 //
children.translated_text: radiant with splendor, as they are today — they blaze exceedingly — what is the cause here? || Saddhp 7.45 ||

children.text: yadi vā nu kaścidbhavi devaputraḥ śubhena karmeṇa samanvito iha /
children.translated_text: Could it be that some son of a god has been born here, endowed with meritorious <s>karma</s>,

children.text: upapannu tasyo ayamānubhāvo yadi vā bhaved buddha kadāci loke // Saddhp_7.46 //
children.translated_text: whose power this might be — or perhaps a <s>Buddha</s> has appeared somewhere in the world?' || Saddhp 7.46 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavasteṣu pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye mahābrahmāṇaḥ, te sarve sahitāḥ samagrāstāni divyāni svāni svāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyabhiruhya divyāṃśca sumerumātrān puṣpapuṭān gṛhītvā catasṛṣu dikṣvanucaṃkramanto 'nuvicaranto yena adhodigbhāgastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | adrākṣuḥ khalu punarbhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇo 'dhodigbhāge taṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bodhimaṇḍavarāgragataṃ bodhivṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ parivṛtaṃ puraskṛtaṃ devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ, taiśca putraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhī rājakumārairadhyeṣyamāṇaṃ dharmacakrapravartanatāyai | dṛṣṭvā ca punaryena sa bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā taṃ bhagavantamanekaśatasahasrakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya taiḥ sumerumātraiḥ puṣpapuṭaistaṃ bhagavantamabhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma taṃ ca bodhivṛkṣaṃ daśayojanapramāṇam | abhyavakīrya tāni divyāni svāni svāni brāhmāṇi vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātayāmāsuḥ - pratigṛhṇātu bhagavānimāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyasmākamanukampāmupādāya | paribhuñjatu sugata imāni brāhmāṇi vimānānyasmākamanukampāmupādāyeti ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, the <s>Mahābrahmās</s> in those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, all united and assembled, ascended their own respective divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces, and taking divine flower-baskets as large as Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, traversing and surveying in the four directions, proceeded downward. And those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, O monks, saw in the downward direction the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, seated at the supreme seat of awakening on a lion-throne at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, surrounded and attended by gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and being entreated by those sixteen princes to turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Having seen [him], they approached that Blessed One. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him many hundred-thousands of times, and showered and sprinkled that Blessed One with those <s>Sumeru</s>-sized flower-baskets, [showering] also that <s>Bodhi</s>-tree which was ten <s>yojanas</s> in extent. Having showered [him], they offered their own respective divine <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One accept these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us! May the <s>Sugata</s> enjoy these <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces out of compassion for us!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste 'pi mahābrahmāṇastāni svāni svāni vimānāni tasya bhagavato niryātya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭuvanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, having offered their own palaces to the Blessed One, at that time praised that Blessed One face to face with fitting verses —

children.text: sādhu darśana buddhāna lokanāthāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: 'Good it is to see the <s>Buddhas</s>, the protectors of the world, the saviors,

children.text: tradhātukasmi buddhā vai sattvānāṃ ye pramocakāḥ // Saddhp_7.47 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Buddhas</s> in the triple world who are indeed the liberators of beings! || Saddhp 7.47 ||

children.text: samantacakṣu lokendrā vyavalokenti diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: The all-seeing lords of the world survey the ten directions;

children.text: vivaritvāmṛtadvāramotārenti bahūn janān // Saddhp_7.48 //
children.translated_text: having opened the door of the deathless, they ferry across many people. || Saddhp 7.48 ||

children.text: śūnyā acintiyāḥ kalpā atītāḥ pūrvi ye abhū /
children.translated_text: Empty and inconceivable were the <s>kalpas</s> that passed before,

children.text: adarśanājjinendrāṇāṃ andhā āsīddiśo daśa // Saddhp_7.49 //
children.translated_text: and from the absence of the lords of <s>Jinas</s>, the ten directions were in darkness. || Saddhp 7.49 ||

children.text: vardhanti narakāstīvrāstiryagyonistathāsurāḥ /
children.translated_text: The fierce hells increase, as do the animal births and the <s>asura</s> [realms];

children.text: preteṣu copapadyante prāṇikoṭyaḥ sahasraśaḥ // Saddhp_7.50 //
children.translated_text: and in the realm of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) are reborn <s>koṭis</s> of living beings by the thousands! || Saddhp 7.50 ||

children.text: divyāḥ kāyāśca hīyante cyutā gacchanti durgatim /
children.translated_text: The divine bodies also decline — having fallen, they go to lower rebirths,

children.text: aśrutvā dharma buddhānāṃ gatyeṣāṃ bhoti pāpikā // Saddhp_7.51 //
children.translated_text: not having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> — their destiny becomes wretched. || Saddhp 7.51 ||

children.text: caryāśuddhigatiprajñā hīyante sarvaprāṇinām /
children.translated_text: Purity of conduct, good destinies, and wisdom decline for all living beings;

children.text: sukhaṃ vinaśyatī teṣāṃ sukhasaṃjñā ca naśyati // Saddhp_7.52 //
children.translated_text: happiness perishes for them, and the perception of happiness is lost. || Saddhp 7.52 ||

children.text: anācārāśca te bhonti asaddharme pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: They become given to misconduct, established in false <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: adāntā lokanāthena durgatiṃ prapatanti te // Saddhp_7.53 //
children.translated_text: untamed by the Lord of the World, they fall into lower rebirths. || Saddhp 7.53 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭo 'si lokapradyota sucireṇāsi āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: You have been seen, O Light of the World! After a very long time you have come!

children.text: utpannu sarvasattvānāṃ kṛtena anukampakaḥ // Saddhp_7.54 //
children.translated_text: You have arisen for the sake of all beings, acting with compassion! || Saddhp 7.54 ||

children.text: diṣṭayā kṣemeṇa prāpto 'si buddhajñānamanuttaram /
children.translated_text: By good fortune, in safety, unharmed, you have attained this unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: vayaṃ te anumodāmo lokaścaiva sadevakaḥ // Saddhp_7.55 //
children.translated_text: we rejoice for you, as does the world together with its gods! || Saddhp 7.55 ||

children.text: vimānāni sucitrāṇi anubhāvena te vibho /
children.translated_text: These beautiful and variegated palaces, through your power, O Lord,

children.text: dadāma te mahāvīra pratigṛhṇa mahāmune // Saddhp_7.56 //
children.translated_text: we offer to you, O Great Hero! Accept [them], O Great Sage! || Saddhp 7.56 ||

children.text: asmākamanukampārthaṃ paribhuñja vināyaka /
children.translated_text: Out of compassion for us, enjoy [them], O Guide!

children.text: vayaṃ ca sarvasattvāśca agrāṃ bodhiṃ spṛśemahi // Saddhp_7.57 //
children.translated_text: May we and all beings attain the supreme awakening! || Saddhp 7.57 ||'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste mahābrahmāṇastaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ saṃmukhamābhiḥ sārūpyābhirgāthābhirabhiṣṭutya taṃ bhagavantametadūcuḥ - pravartayatu bhagavān dharmacakram | pravartayatu sugato dharmacakram | deśayatu bhagavān nirvṛtim | tārayatu bhagavān sarvasattvān | anugṛhṇātu bhagavānimaṃ lokam | deśayatu bhagavān | dharmamasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ | tadbhaviṣyati bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokanukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those <s>Mahābrahmās</s>, having praised the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, face to face with fitting verses, said this to that Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel! May the <s>Sugata</s> turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel! May the Blessed One teach the path to <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation)! May the Blessed One ferry across all beings! May the Blessed One show grace to this world! May the Blessed One teach the <s>Dharma</s> to this world with its <s>Māras</s>, with its <s>Brahmās</s>, to the multitude of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, to the multitude together with gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>! That will be for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude, of gods and humans!'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastāni pañcāśad brahmakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyekasvareṇa samasaṃgītyā taṃ bhagavantamābhyāṃ sārūpyābhyāṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>, with a single voice, in unison, addressed that Blessed One with these two fitting verses —

children.text: pravartayā cakravaramanuttaraṃ parāhanasvā amṛtasya dundubhim /
children.translated_text: 'Turn the unsurpassed, supreme wheel! Strike the drum of the deathless!

children.text: pramocayā duḥkhaśataiśca sattvān nirvāṇamārgaṃ ca pradarśayasva // Saddhp_7.58 //
children.translated_text: Liberate beings from hundreds of sufferings, and reveal the path to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>! || Saddhp 7.58 ||

children.text: asmābhiradhyeṣitu bhāṣa dharmamasmānanugṛhṇa imaṃ ca lokam /
children.translated_text: Entreated by us, speak the <s>Dharma</s>! Show grace to us and to this world!

children.text: valgusvaraṃ co madhuraṃ pramuñca samudānitaṃ kalpasahasrakoṭibhiḥ // Saddhp_7.59 //
children.translated_text: Release a sweet and melodious voice, accumulated through <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>! || Saddhp 7.59 ||'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhasteṣāṃ brahmakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmadhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā teṣāṃ ca ṣoḍaśānāṃ putrāṇāṃ rājakumārāṇām, tasyāṃ velāyāṃ dharmacakraṃ pravartayāmāsa triparivartaṃ dvādaśākāramapravartitaṃ śramaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā māreṇa vā brahmaṇā vā anyena vā kenacit punarloke saha dharmeṇa | yadidaṃ
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, having understood the entreaty of those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Brahmās</s>, and of those sixteen princes, at that time turned the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel — with three turnings and twelve aspects — not turned before by any <s>śramaṇa</s> or <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, god or <s>Māra</s> or <s>Brahmā</s>, or anyone else in the world together with the <s>Dharma</s>. That is to say:

body.text: duḥkham, ayaṃ duḥkhasamudayaḥ, ayaṃ duḥkhanirodhaḥ, iyaṃ duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipadāryasatyamiti | pratītyasamutpādapravṛttiṃ ca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayāmāsa - iti hi bhikṣavo 'vidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam, nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam, ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ, sparśapratyayā vedanā vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā, tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam, upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ, bhavapratyayā jātiḥ, jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | avidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ, saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodhaḥ, vijñānanirodhānnāmarūpanirodhaḥ, nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ, ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ, sparśanirodhād vedanānirodhaḥ, vedanānirodhāttṛṣṇānirodhaḥ, tṛṣṇānirodhādupādānanirodhaḥ, upādānanirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ, bhavanirodhājjātinirodhaḥ, jātinirodhājjarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati ||
body.translated_text: 'This is <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering); this is the arising of <s>duḥkha</s>; this is the cessation of <s>duḥkha</s>; this is the path leading to the cessation of <s>duḥkha</s> — the noble truth.' And he fully illuminated in detail the process of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination): 'Thus, O monks, from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as condition arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from <s>saṃskāras</s> as condition arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from <s>vijñāna</s> as condition arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); from <s>nāmarūpa</s> as condition arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> (six sense-bases); from the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> as condition arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); from <s>sparśa</s> as condition arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); from <s>vedanā</s> as condition arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); from <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as condition arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); from <s>upādāna</s> as condition arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); from <s>bhava</s> as condition arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); from <s>jāti</s> as condition arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. Thus arises this entire great mass of suffering. From the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>; from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> comes the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>; from the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> comes the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s>; from the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> comes the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s>; from the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> comes the cessation of <s>sparśa</s>; from the cessation of <s>sparśa</s> comes the cessation of <s>vedanā</s>; from the cessation of <s>vedanā</s> comes the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>; from the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s> comes the cessation of <s>upādāna</s>; from the cessation of <s>upādāna</s> comes the cessation of <s>bhava</s>; from the cessation of <s>bhava</s> comes the cessation of <s>jāti</s>; from the cessation of <s>jāti</s>, <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair cease. Thus comes the cessation of this entire great mass of suffering.'

body.text: sahapravartitaṃ cedaṃ bhikṣavastena bhagavatā mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena dharmacakraṃ sadevakasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ sadevamānuṣāsurāyāḥ parṣadaḥ purastāt, atha tasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte ṣaṣṭeḥ prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmanupādāya āsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni | sarve ca te traividyāḥ ṣaḍabhijñā aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyinaḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | punaranupūrveṇa bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho dvitīyāṃ dharmadeśanāmakārṣīt, tṛtīyāmapi dharmadeśanāmakārṣīt, caturthīmapi dharmadeśanāmakārṣīt ||
body.translated_text: And when this <s>Dharma</s>-wheel was turned by that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, before the assembly of the world with its <s>Māras</s>, with its <s>Brahmās</s>, the multitude of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, together with gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> — then, at that very instant, moment, and hour, the minds of sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings were liberated from the outflows without clinging. And all of them became endowed with the three knowledges, the six superknowledges, and were established in the eight liberations of meditation. Then, in due course, O monks, the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One gave a second teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and a third teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, and also a fourth teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavastasya bhagavato mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyaikaikasyāṃ dharmadeśanāyāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmanupādāya āsravebhyaścittāni vimuktāni | tataḥ paścād bhikṣavastasya bhagavato gaṇanāsamatikrāntaḥ śrāvakasaṃgho 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, during each and every teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> by that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, the minds of beings numbering as many as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river — <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands — were liberated from the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) through non-clinging. Thereafter, O monks, the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>Saṃgha</s> of that Blessed One became beyond reckoning.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena te ṣoḍaśa rājakumārāḥ kumārabhūtā eva samānāḥ śraddhayā agārādanāgārikāṃ pravrajitāḥ | sarve ca te śrāmaṇerā abhūvan paṇḍitā vyaktā medhāvinaḥ kuśalā bahubuddhaśatasahasracaritāvino 'rthinaścānuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | atha khalu bhikṣavaste ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerāstaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadūcuḥ - imāni khalu punarbhagavaṃstathāgatasya bahūni śrāvakakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi maharddhikāni mahānubhāvāni maheśākhyāni bhagavato dharmadeśanayā pariniṣpannāni | tat sādhu bhagavāṃstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'smākamanukampāmupādāya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya dharmaṃ deśayatu, yadvayamapi tathāgatasyānuśikṣemahi | arthino vayaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatajñānadarśanena | bhagavānevāsmākamasminnevārthe sākṣī | tvaṃ ca bhagavan sarvasattvāśayajño jānīṣe asmākamadhyāśayamiti ||
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, those sixteen princes, being still youths, went forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith. All of them became <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> (novice monks) — learned, skilled, wise, capable, and well-versed in the conduct under many hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, and seekers of supreme perfect awakening. Then, O monks, those sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> addressed that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, saying: 'Indeed, O Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, possessed of great supernatural powers, great might, and great sovereignty, who have been perfected through the Blessed One's teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, may the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, out of compassion for us, teach the <s>Dharma</s> concerning supreme perfect awakening, so that we too may train in the way of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. We desire, O Blessed One, the knowledge and vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. The Blessed One himself is our witness in this very matter. And you, O Blessed One, knower of the intentions of all beings, know our innermost aspirations.'

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena tān bālān dārakān rājakumārān pravrajitān śrāmaṇerān dṛṣṭvā yāvāṃstasya rājñaścakravartinaḥ parivāraḥ, tato 'rdhaḥ pravrajito 'bhūdaśītiprāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ||
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, seeing those young boys, the princes, who had gone forth as <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, half of all the retinue of that wheel-turning king also went forth — eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhasteṣāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāmadhyāśayaṃ viditvā viṃśateḥ kalpasahasrāṇāmatyayena saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayāmāsa tāsāṃ sarvāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadām ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, having perceived the innermost aspirations of those <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, after the lapse of twenty thousand <s>kalpas</s>, expounded in detail the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True <s>Dharma</s>) — a great extensive teaching, an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, upheld by all <s>Buddhas</s> — to all those four assemblies.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena tasya bhagavato bhāṣitaṃ te ṣodaśa rājakumārāḥ śrāmaṇerā udgṛhītavanto dhāritavanta ārādhitavantaḥ paryāptavantaḥ ||
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, those sixteen princes, the <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, received, retained, mastered, and comprehended the words spoken by that Blessed One.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastān ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerān vyākārṣīdanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | tasya khalu punarbhikṣavo mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyemaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣamāṇasya śrāvakāścādhimuktavantaḥ | te ca ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerā bahūni ca prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi vicikitsāprāptānyabhūvan ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, gave those sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> a prediction of supreme perfect awakening. And while that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Śrāvakas</s> accepted it with faith. But those sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> and many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings fell into doubt.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamaṣṭau kalpasahasrāṇyaviśrānto bhāṣitvā vihāraṃ praviṣṭaḥ pratisaṃlayanāya | tathā pratisaṃlīnaśca bhikṣavaḥ sa tathāgataścaturaśītikalpasahasrāṇi vihārasthita evāsīt ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, having spoken this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse without rest for eight thousand <s>kalpas</s>, entered his dwelling for solitary meditation. And that <s>Tathāgata</s>, O monks, remained thus in meditative absorption, dwelling in his abode for eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerāstaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgataṃ pratisaṃlīnaṃ viditvā pṛthak pṛthag dharmāsanāni siṃhāsanāni prajñāpya teṣu niṣaṇṇāstaṃ bhagavantaṃ mahābhijñājñānābhibhuvaṃ tathāgataṃ namaskṛtya taṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ vistareṇa catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ caturaśītikalpasahasrāṇi saṃprakāśitavantaḥ | tatra bhikṣava ekaikaḥ śrāmaṇero bodhisattvaḥ ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau paripācitavān samādāpitavān saṃharṣitavān samuttejitavān saṃpraharṣitavānavatāritavān ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, knowing that the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, had entered meditative absorption, each prepared separate <s>Dharma</s>-seats, lion-thrones, and seated upon them, having paid homage to the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, they expounded in detail that <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse to the four assemblies for eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s>. Therein, O monks, each <s>śrāmaṇera</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> ripened, inspired, gladdened, encouraged, delighted, and established in supreme perfect awakening as many as sixty times sixty <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings.

body.text:
atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhasteṣāṃ
caturaśīteḥ kalpasahasrāṇāmatyayena smṛtimān saṃprajānastasmāt samādhervyuttiṣṭhat | vyutthāya ca sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgato yena taddharmāsanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāmat | upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat | samanantaraniṣaṇṇaśca khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ sa bhagavān mahābhijñājñānābhibhūstathāgatastasmin dharmāsane, atha tāvadeva sarvāvantaṃ parṣanmaṇḍalamavalokya bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayāmāsaāścaryaprāptā bhikṣavo 'dbhutaprāptā ime ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerāḥ prajñāvanto bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraparyupāsitāścīrṇacaritā buddhajñānaparyupāsakā buddhajñānapratigrāhakā buddhājñānāvatārakā buddhajñānasaṃdarśakāḥ | paryupāsadhvaṃ bhikṣava etān ṣoḍaśa śrāmaṇerān punaḥ punaḥ | ye kecid bhikṣavaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, that Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, after the lapse of those eighty-four thousand <s>kalpas</s>, mindful and fully aware, arose from that <s>samādhi</s>. Having arisen, the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, approached that <s>Dharma</s>-seat; having approached, he sat down upon the prepared seat. And immediately upon sitting down, O monks, the Blessed One <s>Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, surveyed the entire assembly and addressed the community of monks: 'Wondrous and marvelous, O monks, are these sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>! They are wise, well-attended upon by many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, of practiced conduct, attendants upon <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, recipients of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, introducers to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, revealers of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. Attend upon these sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> again and again, O monks! Whoever among you, O monks —

body.text: śrāvakayānikā vā pratyekabuddhayānikā vā bodhisattvayānikā vā eṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ dharmadeśanāṃ na pratikṣepsyanti | na pratibādhiṣyante, sarve te kṣipramanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherlābhino bhaviṣyanti, sarve ca te tathāgatajñānamanuprāpsyanti ||
body.translated_text: — whether followers of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, or followers of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-vehicle, or followers of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle — whoever will not reject the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of these sons of good family, whoever will not obstruct it, all of them will quickly become attainers of supreme perfect awakening, and all of them will attain the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: taiḥ khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ kulaputraistasya bhagavataḥ śāsane 'yaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ saṃprakāśito 'bhūt | taiḥ khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ śrāmaṇerairbodhisattvairmahāsattvairyāni tānyekaikena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ṣaṣṭiṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bodhāya samādāpitānyabhūvan, sarvāṇi ca tāni taireva sārdhaṃ tāsu tāsu jātiṣvanupravrajitāni | tānyeva samanupaśyantasteṣāmevāntikāddharmamaśrauṣuḥ | taiścatvāriṃśad buddhakoṭīsahasrāṇyārāgitāni | kecidadyāpyārāgayanti ||
body.translated_text: Indeed, O monks, by those sixteen sons of good family, this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse was expounded again and again in the teaching of that Blessed One. Furthermore, O monks, by those sixteen <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings — as many as sixty times sixty <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sands — that had been inspired toward awakening by each <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, all of them went forth together with those very ones in birth after birth. They continued to see those very ones and heard the <s>Dharma</s> from them. They pleased forty thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>; some are still pleasing them even today.

body.text:
ārocayāmi vo bhikṣavaḥ, prativedayāmi vaḥ | ye te ṣoḍaśa rājakumārāḥ kumārabhūtā ye tasya bhagavataḥ śāsane śrāmaṇerā dharmabhāṇakā abhūvan, sarve te 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ | sarve ca ta etarhi tiṣṭhanti dhriyante yāpayanti | daśasu dikṣu nānābuddhakṣetreṣu bahūnāṃ śrāvakabodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti | yaduta pūrvasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavo 'bhiratyāṃ lokadhātāvakṣobhyo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho merukūṭaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavaḥ siṃhaghoṣaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ siṃhadhvajaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavaḥ ākāśapratiṣṭhitaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho nityaparinirvṛtaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi bhikṣava indradhvajaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho brahmadhvajaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ |
paścimāyāṃ diśi bhikṣavo 'mitāyuśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvalokadhātūpadravodvegapratyuttīrṇaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | paścimottarasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavastamālapatracandanagandhābhijñaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho merukalpaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | uttarasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavo meghasvaradīpaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho meghasvararājaśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | uttarapūrvasyāṃ diśi bhikṣavaḥ sarvalokabhayacchambhitatvavidhvaṃsanarakaraśca nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ | ahaṃ ca bhikṣavaḥ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ ṣoḍaśamo madhye khalvasyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ ||
body.translated_text: I declare to you, O monks, I announce: those sixteen princes who were youths, who became <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> and teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> in the teaching of that Blessed One — all of them have attained supreme perfect awakening. And all of them now abide, persist, and continue in various <s>buddhakṣetras</s> (buddha-fields) in the ten directions, teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Namely, in the eastern direction, O monks, in the world-system <s>Abhirati</s>, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Akṣobhya</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Merukūṭa</s>. In the east-southeastern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Siṃhaghoṣa</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Siṃhadhvaja</s>. In the southern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Ākāśapratiṣṭhita</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Nityaparinirvṛta</s>. In the southwestern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Indradhvaja</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Brahmadhvaja</s>. In the western direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Amitāyus</s>, and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Sarvalokadhātūpadravodvegapratyuttīrṇa</s> (One Who Has Crossed Beyond All Calamity and Agitation of World-Systems). In the northwestern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Tamālapatracandanagandhābhijña</s> (One Who Knows the Fragrance of Tamāla-leaf Sandalwood), and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Merukalpa</s>. In the northern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Meghasvaradīpa</s> (Cloud-Voice Lamp), and the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Meghasvararāja</s> (Cloud-Voice King). In the northeastern direction, O monks, there is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Sarvalokabhayacchambhitatvavidhvaṃsanakara</s> (One Who Destroys All Fear and Trembling of the World). And I, O monks, am the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the sixteenth, who has attained supreme perfect awakening here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system.

body.text: ye punaste bhikṣavastadā asmākaṃ śrāmaṇerabhūtānāṃ sattvāṃ dharmaṃ śrutavantaḥ tasya bhagavataḥ śāsana ekaikasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bahūni gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi yānyasmābhiḥ samādāpitānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, tānyetāni bhikṣavo 'dyāpi śrāvakabhūmāvevāvasthitāni | paripācyanta evānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | eṣaivaiṣāmānupūrvī anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherabhisaṃbodhanāya | tatkasya hetoḥ? evaṃ duradhimocyaṃ hi bhikṣavastathāgatajñānam
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O monks, those beings who heard the <s>Dharma</s> from us when we were <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> in that Blessed One's teaching — in the teaching of each <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, the many <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings whom we had inspired toward supreme perfect awakening — all those, O monks, even now still remain on the level of <s>Śrāvakas</s>. They are being gradually ripened toward supreme perfect awakening. This is their gradual course toward the realization of supreme perfect awakening. For what reason? Because, O monks, the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is so very difficult to comprehend —

body.text: | katame ca te bhikṣavaḥ sattvāḥ, ye mayā bodhisattvena tasya bhagavataḥ śāsane aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvajñatādharmamanuśrāvitāni? yūyaṃ te bhikṣavastena kālena tena samayena sattvā abhūvan ||
body.translated_text: And who are those beings, O monks, whom I, as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in that Blessed One's teaching, caused to hear the <s>Dharma</s> of omniscience — the immeasurable, incalculable, <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings? You, O monks, were those beings at that time, in that era!

body.text: ye ca mama parinirvṛtasya anāgate 'dhvani śrāvakā bhaviṣyanti, bodhisattvacaryāṃ ca śroṣyanti, na cāvabhotsyante bodhisattvā vayamiti, kiṃcāpi te bhikṣavaḥ sarve parinirvāṇasaṃjñinaḥ parinirvāsyanti, api tu khalu punarbhikṣavo yadahamanyāsu lokadhātuṣvanyonyairnāmadheyairviharāmi, tatra te punarutpatsyante tathāgatajñānaṃ paryeṣamāṇāḥ | tatra ca te punarevaitāṃ kriyāṃ śroṣyanti | ekameva tathāgatānāṃ parinirvāṇam | nāstyanyad dvitīyamito bahirnirvāṇam | tathāgatānāmetadbhikṣava upāyakauśalyaṃ veditavyaṃ dharmadeśanābhinirhāraśca | yasmin bhikṣavaḥ samaye tathāgataḥ parinirvāṇakālasamayamātmanaḥ samanupaśyati, pariśuddhaṃ ca parṣadaṃ paśyati adhimuktisārāṃ śūnyadharmagatiṃ gatāṃ dhyānavatīṃ mahādhyānavatīm, atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato 'yaṃ kāla iti viditvā sarvān bodhisattvān sarvaśrāvakāṃśca saṃnipātya paścādetamarthaṃ saṃśrāvayati | na bhikṣavaḥ kiṃcidasti loke dvitīyaṃ nāma yānaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ vā, kaḥ punarvādastṛtīyasya? upāyakauśalyaṃ khalvidaṃ bhikṣavastathāgatānāmarhatām - dūrapranaṣṭaṃ sattvadhātuṃ viditvā hīnābhiratān kāmapaṅkamagnān, tata eṣāṃ bhikṣavastathāgatastannirvāṇaṃ bhāṣate yadadhimucyante ||
body.translated_text: And those who, in the future time after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will be my <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and will hear of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct but will not understand 'We are <s>Bodhisattvas</s>' — even though those monks, all having the notion of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will pass into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — yet, O monks, when I dwell in other world-systems under different names, there they will be reborn again, seeking the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. And there again they will hear this very teaching: 'There is only one <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>; there is no other, second <s>nirvāṇa</s> beyond this.' O monks, this should be understood as the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' skill in means and their manner of teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. At that time, O monks, when the <s>Tathāgata</s> perceives that the moment of his own <s>parinirvāṇa</s> has come, and sees that the assembly is pure, firm in faith, gone to the course of the <s>Dharma</s> of emptiness, possessed of <s>dhyāna</s>, great in <s>dhyāna</s> — then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing 'This is the time,' gathers together all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and proclaims this matter: 'O monks, there is no such thing in the world as a second vehicle or a second <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — how much less a third! O monks, this is indeed the skill in means of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s> — having understood the being-realm to be far gone astray, delighting in the inferior, sunk in the mire of desires, therefore, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaches that <s>nirvāṇa</s> to which they are inclined.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣava iha syāt pañcayojanaśatikamaṭavīkāntāram | mahāṃścātra janakāyaḥ pratipanno bhaved ratnadīpaṃ gamanāya | deśikaścaiṣāmeko bhaved vyaktaḥ paṇḍito nipuṇo medhāvī kuśalaḥ khalvaṭavīdurgāṇām | sa ca taṃ sārthamaṭavīmavakrāmayet | atha khalu sa mahājanakāyaḥ śrāntaḥ klānto bhītastrastaḥ evaṃ vadet - yat khalvārya deśika pariṇāyaka jānīyāḥ - vayaṃ hi śrāntāḥ klāntā bhītāstrastā anirvṛtāḥ | punareva pratinivartayiṣyāmaḥ | atidūramito 'ṭavīkāntāramiti | atha khalu bhikṣavaḥ sa deśika upāyakuśalastān puruṣān pratinivartitukāmān viditvā evaṃ cintayet - mā khalvime tapasvinastādṛśaṃ mahāratnadvīpaṃ na gaccheyuriti | sa teṣāmanukampārthamupāyakauśalyaṃ prayojayet | tasyā aṭavyā madhye yojanaśataṃ vā dviyojanaśataṃ vā triyojanaśataṃ vā atikramya ṛddhimayaṃ nagaramabhinirmimīyāt | tatastān puruṣānevaṃ vadet - mā bhavanto bhaiṣṭa, mā nivartadhvam | ayamasau mahājanapadaḥ | atra viśrāmyata | atra vo yāni kānicit karaṇīyāni tāni sarvāṇi kurudhvam | atra nirvāṇaprāptā viharadhvamatra viśrāntāḥ | yasya punaḥ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyati, sa taṃ mahāratnadvīpaṃ gamiṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Just as, O monks, suppose there were a wilderness stretch of five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. And a great company of people had set out to travel to a jewel-island. And they had one guide who was competent, learned, skillful, wise, and well-versed in the hazards of the wilderness. And he led that caravan into the wilderness. Then that great company of people, weary, exhausted, frightened, and terrified, would say: 'O noble guide, leader, you should know — we are weary, exhausted, frightened, terrified, and distressed. Let us turn back! This wilderness stretch is far too long from here.' Then, O monks, that guide, skilled in means, knowing those men wished to turn back, thought thus: 'These wretches should not fail to reach such a great jewel-island!' Out of compassion for them, he would employ skill in means. In the middle of that wilderness, having traversed one hundred, two hundred, or three hundred <s>yojanas</s>, he would conjure up a magical city. Then he would say to those men: 'Do not fear, good people! Do not turn back! Here is this great settlement. Rest here. Here you may do whatever you need to do. Dwell here as those who have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, resting here. And whoever has further business to accomplish, he shall go on to the great jewel-island.'

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavaste kāntāraprāptāḥ sattvā āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā bhaveyuḥ - muktā vayamaṭavīkāntārāt | iha nirvāṇaprāptā vihariṣyāma iti | atha khalu bhikṣavaste puruṣāstadṛddhimayaṃ nagaraṃ praviśeyuḥ, āgatasaṃjñinaśca bhaveyuḥ, nistīrṇasaṃjñinaśca bhaveyuḥ | nirvṛtāḥ śītībhūtā sma iti manyeran | tatastān deśiko viśrāntān viditvā tadṛddhimayaṃ nagaramantardhāpayet | antardhāpayitvā ca tān puruṣānevaṃ vadet - āgacchantu bhavantaḥ sattvāḥ | abhyāsanna eṣa mahāratnadvīpaḥ | idaṃ tu mayā nagaraṃ yuṣmākaṃ viśrāmaṇārthamabhinirmitamiti ||
body.translated_text: Then, O monks, those beings who had reached the wilderness would be amazed and astonished, [thinking]: 'We are freed from the wilderness! We shall dwell here having attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' Then, O monks, those men would enter that conjured city, and would have the notion of having arrived and the notion of having crossed over. They would think: 'We are at peace, cooled.' Then, that guide, knowing them to be rested, would cause that conjured city to disappear. Having caused it to disappear, he would say to those men: 'Come, good beings! This great jewel-island is near. That city was conjured by me for your rest.'

body.text:
evameva bhikṣavastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yuṣmākaṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca deśikaḥ | atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha evaṃ
paśyati - mahadidaṃ kleśakāntāraṃ nirgantavyaṃ niṣkrāntavyaṃ prahātavyam | mā khalvime ekameva buddhajñānaṃ śrutvā draveṇaiva pratinivartayeyuḥ, naivopasaṃkrameyuḥ | bahuparikleśamidaṃ buddhajñānaṃ samudānayitavyamiti | tatra tathāgataḥ sattvān durbalāśayān viditvā yathā sa deśikastadṛddhimayaṃ nagaramabhinirmitīte teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ viśrāmaṇārtham, viśrāntānāṃ caiṣāmevaṃ kathayati - idaṃ khalu ṛddhimayaṃ nagaramiti, evameva bhikṣavastathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho mahopāyakauśalyena antarā dve nirvāṇabhūmī sattvānāṃ viśrāmaṇārthaṃ deśayati saṃprakāśayati yadidaṃ śrāvakabhūmiṃ pratyekabuddhabhūmiṃ ca | yasmiṃśca bhikṣavaḥ samaye te sattvāstatra sthitā bhavanti, atha khalu bhikṣavastathāgato 'pyevaṃ saṃśrāvayati - na khalu punarbhikṣavo yūyaṃ kṛtakṛtyāḥ kṛtakaraṇīyāḥ | api tu khalu punarbhikṣavo yuṣmākamabhyāsaḥ | itastathāgatajñānaṃ vyavalokayadhvaṃ bhikṣavo vyavacārayadhvam | yad yuṣmākaṃ nirvāṇaṃ naiva nirvāṇam, api tu khalu punarūpāyakauśalyametad bhikṣavastathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ yat trīṇi yānāni saṃprakāśayantīti ||
body.translated_text: Even so, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, is your guide and the guide of all beings. Then, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, sees thus: 'This great wilderness of afflictions must be escaped, departed from, abandoned. Let not these [beings], having heard of the one <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge alone, turn back in haste and never approach [it]. This <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge requires much effort to attain.' Thereupon, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing beings to be of weak resolve — just as that guide conjured that magical city for the rest of those beings — and to those who have rested he says: 'This indeed was a conjured city.' Even so, O monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, by his great skill in means, teaches and reveals two stages of <s>nirvāṇa</s> as resting places for beings, namely the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-stage and the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-stage. And, O monks, at the time when those beings are established there, the <s>Tathāgata</s> proclaims: 'O monks, you are not yet ones whose task is done, whose work is accomplished. Rather, O monks, your [goal] is near. From here, contemplate the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge, O monks, examine it. That which is your <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not truly <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Rather, O monks, this is the skill in means of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the <s>Arhats</s>, the Perfectly Awakened Ones, that they reveal three vehicles.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayopadarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, wishing to illustrate this very matter more fully, at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: abhijñajñānābhibhu lokanāyako yadbodhimaṇḍasmi niṣaṇṇa āsīt /
children.translated_text: When the Guide of the World, master of higher knowledge and wisdom, was seated at the seat of awakening,

children.text: daśeha so antarakalpa pūrṇān na lapsi bodhiṃ paramārthadarśī // Saddhp_7.60 //
children.translated_text: for ten full intermediate <s>kalpas</s> here, he did not attain awakening, that seer of ultimate truth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.60 ||

children.text: devātha nāgā asurātha guhyakā udyukta pūjārtha jinasya tasya /
children.translated_text: Gods and <s>Nāgas</s> and <s>Asuras</s> and <s>Guhyakas</s>, intent on worship of that <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: puṣpāṇa varṣaṃ pramumocu tatra buddhe ca bodhiṃ naranāyake 'smin // Saddhp_7.61 //
children.translated_text: rained showers of flowers there, upon the <s>Buddha</s> and the awakening of this Guide of Men. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.61 ||

children.text: upariṃ ca khe dundubhayo vineduḥ satkārapūjārtha jinasya tasya /
children.translated_text: And above in the sky, drums resounded for the honor and worship of that <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: suduḥkhitā cāpi jinena tatra cirabudhyamānena anuttaraṃ padam // Saddhp_7.62 //
children.translated_text: and they were greatly distressed that the <s>Jina</s> there was so long in awakening to the unsurpassed state. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.62 ||

children.text: daśāna co antarakalpa atyayāt spṛśe sa bodhiṃ bhagavānanābhibhūḥ /
children.translated_text: After the passing of ten intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the Blessed One, the unconquered, attained awakening;

children.text: hṛṣṭā udagrāstada āsu sarve devā manuṣyā bhujagāsurāśca // Saddhp_7.63 //
children.translated_text: then all were delighted and overjoyed — gods, humans, serpents, and <s>Asuras</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.63 ||

body.text: vīrāḥ kumārā atha tasya ṣoḍaśa putrā guṇāḍhyā naranāyakasya /
body.translated_text: The sixteen heroic princes, sons of that Guide of Men, endowed with virtues,

body.text: upasaṃkramī prāṇīsahasrakoṭibhiḥ puraskṛtāstaṃ dvipadendramagryam // Saddhp_7.64 //
body.translated_text: approached, attended by many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings, that supreme lord among bipeds. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.64 ||

children.text: vanditva pādau ca vināyakasya adhyeṣiṣū dharma prakāśayasva /
children.translated_text: Having bowed at the feet of the Guide, they entreated: 'Illuminate the <s>Dharma</s>!

children.text: asmāṃśca tarpehi imaṃ ca lokaṃ subhāṣiteneha narendrasiṃha // Saddhp_7.65 //
children.translated_text: Satisfy us and this world with well-spoken [words], O Lion among Kings!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.65 ||

children.text: cirasya lokasya daśaddiśe 'smin vidito 'si utpannu mahāvināyaka /
children.translated_text: After a long time, in these ten directions of the world, you are known to have arisen, O great Guide!

children.text: nimittasaṃcodanahetu prāṇināṃ brāhmā vimānāni prakampayantaḥ // Saddhp_7.66 //
children.translated_text: For the purpose of rousing and inspiring beings, the <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces are shaking. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.66 ||

children.text: diśāya pūrvāya sahasrakoṭyaḥ kṣetrāṇa pañcāśadabhūṣi kampitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In the eastern direction, five hundred <s>koṭis</s> of world-systems were shaken,

children.text: tatrāpi ye brāhma vimāna agrāste tejavanto adhimātramāsi // Saddhp_7.67 //
children.translated_text: and there too the supreme <s>Brahmā</s>-palaces became exceedingly radiant. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.67 ||

children.text: viditva te pūrvanimittamīdṛśamupasaṃkramī lokavināyakendram /
children.translated_text: Having perceived such a portent beforehand, they approached the Lord, the Guide of the World,

children.text: puṣpairihābhyokiriyāṇa nāyakamarpenti te sarva vimāna tasya // Saddhp_7.68 //
children.translated_text: showered the Guide here with flowers, and offered all their palaces to him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.68 ||

children.text: adhyeṣiṣū cakrapravartanāya gāthābhigītena abhisaṃstaviṃsu /
children.translated_text: They entreated [him] to turn the wheel, and praised [him] with verses of song;

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ ca so āsi narendrarājā na tāva kālo mama dharma bhāṣitum // Saddhp_7.69 //
children.translated_text: but he, the King among Kings, remained silent — 'Not yet is the time for me to teach the <s>Dharma</s>.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.69 ||

children.text: evaṃ diśi dakṣiṇiyāṃ pi tatra atha paścimā heṣṭima uttarasyām /
children.translated_text: Likewise in the southern direction, and in the western, the lower, and the northern,

children.text: upariṣṭimāyāṃ vidiśāsu caiva āgatya brahmāṇa sahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_7.70 //
children.translated_text: in the upper direction and in the intermediate directions too, thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Brahmās</s> came. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.70 ||

children.text: puṣpebhi abhyokiriyāṇa nāyakaṃ pādau ca vanditva vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: Showering the Guide with flowers, and bowing at the feet of the Guide,

children.text: niryātayitvā ca vimāna sarvānabhiṣṭavitvā punarabhyayāci // Saddhp_7.71 //
children.translated_text: having presented all their palaces and having praised [him], they again made their entreaty: || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.71 ||

children.text: pravartayā cakramanantacakṣuḥ sudurlabhastvaṃ bahukalpakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Turn the wheel, O Infinite-Eyed One! Most rare are you through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: darśehi maitrībala pūrvasevitamapāvṛṇohī amṛtasya dvāram // Saddhp_7.72 //
children.translated_text: show the power of loving-kindness cultivated in former [lives] — open the door of the deathless!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.72 ||

children.text: adhyeṣaṇāṃ jñātva anantacakṣuḥ prakāśate dharma bahuprakāram /
children.translated_text: Having understood the entreaty, the Infinite-Eyed One illuminated the <s>Dharma</s> in many ways,

children.text: catvāri satyāni ca vistareṇa pratītya sarve imi bhāva utthitāḥ // Saddhp_7.73 //
children.translated_text: and the four noble truths in detail — all these states arise through dependent origination. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.73 ||

children.text: avidya ādīkariyāṇa cakṣumān prabhāṣate sa maraṇāntaduḥkham /
children.translated_text: The Seer, beginning with ignorance, proclaimed the suffering that ends in death,

children.text: jātiprasūtā imi sarvadoṣā mṛtyuṃ ca mānuṣyamimeva jānatha // Saddhp_7.74 //
children.translated_text: all these faults are born from birth — know that death too belongs to this human [existence]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.74 ||

children.text: samanantaraṃ bhāṣitu dharma tena bahuprakārā vividhā anantāḥ /
children.translated_text: Immediately after he taught the <s>Dharma</s>, [beings became] many, varied, and countless;

children.text: śrutvānaśītī nayutāna koṭyaḥ sattvāḥ sthitāḥ śrāvaka bhūtale laghum // Saddhp_7.75 //
children.translated_text: having heard, eighty <s>nayutas</s> of <s>koṭis</s> of beings quickly attained the <s>Śrāvaka</s> stage. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.75 ||

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ dvitīyaṃ aparaṃ abhūṣi jinasya tasyo bahu dharma bhāṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Then a second occasion arose, when that <s>Jina</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> extensively;

children.text: viśuddhasattvā yatha gaṅgavālukāḥ kṣaṇena te śrāvakabhūta āsīt // Saddhp_7.76 //
children.translated_text: pure beings, [numberless] like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in an instant became <s>Śrāvakas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.76 ||

children.text: tatottarī agaṇiyu tasya āsīt saṃghastadā lokavināyakasya /
children.translated_text: Thereafter, the <s>saṃgha</s> of that Guide of the World was innumerable,

children.text: kalpāna koṭīnyayutā gaṇenta ekaika no cāntu labheya teṣām // Saddhp_7.77 //
children.translated_text: even counting through <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, one would not reach the end of them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.77 ||

children.text: ye cāpi te ṣoḍaśa rājaputrā ye aurasā cailakabhūta sarve /
children.translated_text: And those sixteen princes who were his own sons, all having become ascetics,

children.text: te śrāmaṇerā avaciṃsu taṃ jinaṃ prakāśayā nāyaka agradharmam // Saddhp_7.78 //
children.translated_text: as novice monks, addressed that <s>Jina</s>: 'Illuminate the foremost <s>Dharma</s>, O Guide!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.78 ||

body.text: yathā vayaṃ lokavidū bhavema yathaiva tvaṃ sarvajinānamuttama /
body.translated_text: 'That we may become Knowers of the World, just as you are, O Supreme among all <s>Jinas</s>!

body.text: ime ca sattvā bhavi sarvi eva yathaiva tvaṃ vīra viśuddhacakṣuḥ // Saddhp_7.79 //
body.translated_text: And may all these beings too become just as you, O Hero of Pure Vision!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.79 ||

children.text: so cā jino āṃśayu jñātva teṣāṃ kumārabhūtāna tathātmajānām /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Jina</s>, understanding the wish of those princes, his own sons,

children.text: prakāśayī uttamamagrabodhiṃ dṛṣṭāntakoṭīnayutairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_7.80 //
children.translated_text: illuminated the supreme, foremost awakening, with countless <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of illustrations. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.80 ||

children.text: hetūsahasrairupadarśayanto abhijñajñānaṃ ca pravartayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Demonstrating with thousands of causes, and setting forth the knowledge of higher powers,

children.text: bhūtāṃ cariṃ darśayi lokanātho yathā caranto vidu bodhisattvāḥ // Saddhp_7.81 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of the World showed the true course as practiced by the knowing <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.81 ||

children.text: idameva saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ vaipulyasūtraṃ bhagavānuvāca /
children.translated_text: This very <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma) <s>vaipulya-sūtra</s> the Blessed One proclaimed,

children.text: gāthāsahasrehi analpakehi yeṣāṃ pramāṇaṃ yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ // Saddhp_7.82 //
children.translated_text: with thousands of verses, not few, whose measure is like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.82 ||

children.text: so cā jino bhāṣiya sūtrametadvihāru praviśitva vilakṣayīta /
children.translated_text: And that <s>Jina</s>, having taught this <s>sūtra</s>, entered his dwelling and sat in meditation,

children.text: pūrṇānaśītiṃ caturaśca kalpān samāhitaikāsani lokanāthaḥ // Saddhp_7.83 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of the World, on one seat in <s>samādhi</s>, for eighty-four full <s>kalpas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.83 ||

children.text: te śrāmaṇerāśca viditva nāyakaṃ vihāri āsannamaniṣkramantam /
children.translated_text: Those novice monks, knowing the Guide to be dwelling in his abode without emerging,

children.text: saṃśrāvayiṃsu bahuprāṇikoṭināṃ bauddha imaṃ jñānamanāsravaṃ śivam // Saddhp_7.84 //
children.translated_text: proclaimed to many <s>koṭis</s> of beings this <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, outflow-free and auspicious. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.84 ||

children.text: pṛthak pṛthagāsana prajñapitvā abhāṣi teṣāmidameva sūtram /
children.translated_text: Each having arranged a separate seat, they taught this very <s>sūtra</s>;

children.text: sugatasya tasya tada śāsanasmin adhikāra kurvanti mamevarūpam // Saddhp_7.85 //
children.translated_text: in the teaching of that <s>Sugata</s>, they performed service of this very kind on my behalf. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.85 ||

children.text: gaṅgā yathā vāluka aprameyā sahasra ṣaṣṭiṃ tada śrāvayiṃsu /
children.translated_text: Immeasurable as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — sixty thousand they taught;

children.text: ekaiku tasya sugatasya putro vineti sattvāni analpakāni // Saddhp_7.86 //
children.translated_text: each son of that <s>Sugata</s> tamed beings not few in number. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.86 ||

children.text: tasyo jinasya parinirvṛtasya caritva te paśyisu buddhakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: After that <s>Jina</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having practiced, they beheld <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: tehī tadā śrāvitakehi sārdhaṃ kurvanti pūjāṃ dvipadottamānām // Saddhp_7.87 //
children.translated_text: together with those who had been taught by them, they performed worship of the Supreme among Bipeds. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.87 ||

children.text: caritva caryāṃ vipulāṃ viśiṣṭāṃ buddhā ca te bodhi daśaddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Having practiced the vast and distinguished conduct, those <s>Buddhas</s> [attained] awakening in the ten directions;

children.text: te ṣoḍaśā tasya jinasya putrā diśāsu sarvāsu dvayo dvayo jināḥ // Saddhp_7.88 //
children.translated_text: those sixteen sons of the <s>Jina</s> are <s>Jinas</s> in all the directions, two by two. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.88 ||

children.text: ye cāpi saṃśrāvitakā tadāsī te śrāvakā teṣa jināna sarve /
children.translated_text: And those who were the hearers [of the Dharma] at that time are all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of those <s>Jinas</s>;

children.text: imameva bodhiṃ upanāmayanti kramakrameṇa vividhairupāyaiḥ // Saddhp_7.89 //
children.translated_text: they are being led toward this very awakening, gradually, by various skillful means. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.89 ||

children.text: ahaṃ pi abhyantari teṣa āsīnmayāpi saṃśrāvita sarvi yūyam /
children.translated_text: I too was among them — by me also all of you were caused to hear [the Dharma];

children.text: teno mama śrāvaka yūyamadya bodhāvupāyeniha sarvi nemi // Saddhp_7.90 //
children.translated_text: therefore you are my <s>Śrāvakas</s> today — all of you I lead toward awakening by skillful means here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.90 ||

children.text: ayaṃ khu hetustada pūrva āsīdayaṃ pratyayo yena hu dharma bhāṣe /
children.translated_text: This was the cause formerly, this was the condition by which I teach the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: nayāmyahaṃ yena mamāgrabodhiṃ mā bhikṣavo utrasatheha sthāne // Saddhp_7.91 //
children.translated_text: I lead [you] to my supreme awakening — do not be frightened here, O monks, in this matter! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.91 ||

children.text: yathāṭavī ugra bhaveya dāruṇā śūnyā nirālamba nirāśrayā ca /
children.translated_text: Just as there might be a wilderness, fierce and terrible, empty, without support, without refuge,

children.text: bahuśvāpadā caiva apāniyā ca bālāna sā bhīṣaṇikā bhaveta // Saddhp_7.92 //
children.translated_text: full of many wild beasts, and waterless — that would be terrifying to the foolish. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.92 ||

children.text: purūṣāṇa co tatra sahasra nekā ye prasthitāstāmaṭavīṃ bhaveyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And many thousands of people might set out into that wilderness;
