children.text: aṭavī ca sā śūnya bhaveta dīrghā pūrṇāni pañcāśata yojanāni // Saddhp_7.93 //
children.translated_text: and that wilderness might be empty and long, a full five hundred <s>yojanas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.93 ||

children.text: puruṣaśca āḍhyaḥ smṛtimantu vyakto dhīro vinītaśca viśāradaśca /
children.translated_text: And there might be a man — wealthy, mindful, skilled, steadfast, disciplined, and confident —

children.text: yo deśikasteṣa bhaveta tatra aṭavīya durgāya subhairavāya // Saddhp_7.94 //
children.translated_text: who would be their guide there, in that difficult and dreadful wilderness. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.94 ||

children.text: te cāpi khinnā bahuprāṇikoṭya uvāca taṃ deśika tasmi kāle /
children.translated_text: And those many <s>koṭis</s> of beings, being exhausted, said to that guide at that time:

children.text: khinnā vayaṃ ārya na śaknuyāma nivartanaṃ adyiha rocate naḥ // Saddhp_7.95 //
children.translated_text: 'We are exhausted, O noble one, we cannot go on — turning back appeals to us now here.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.95 ||

children.text: kuśalaśca so pi tada paṇḍitaśca praṇāyakopāya tadā vicintayet /
children.translated_text: And that skillful and wise leader then devised a plan of skillful means:

children.text: dhikkaṣṭa ratnairimi sarvi bālā bhraśyanti ātmāna nivartayantaḥ // Saddhp_7.96 //
children.translated_text: 'Alas, what a pity! These foolish ones will lose the jewels if they turn themselves back!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.96 ||

children.text: yannūnahaṃ ṛddhibalena vādya nagaraṃ mahantaṃ abhinirmiṇeyam /
children.translated_text: 'Suppose I now, by the power of supernatural ability, were to conjure a great city,

children.text: pratimaṇḍitaṃ veśmasahasrakoṭibhirvihāraudyānupaśobhitaṃ ca // Saddhp_7.97 //
children.translated_text: adorned with thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of dwellings, beautified with parks and monasteries, || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.97 ||

children.text: vāpī nadīyo abhinirmiṇeyam ārāmapuṣpaiḥ pratimaṇḍitaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: and I were to conjure ponds and rivers, adorned with garden flowers,

children.text: prākāradvārairupaśobhitaṃ ca nārīnaraiścāpratimairupetam // Saddhp_7.98 //
children.translated_text: beautified with ramparts and gates, and filled with incomparable women and men.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.98 ||

children.text: nirmāṇu kṛtva iti tān vadeya mā bhāyathā harṣa karotha caiva /
children.translated_text: Having created that conjured [city], he would say to them: 'Do not be afraid, and rejoice!

children.text: prāptā bhavanto nagaraṃ variṣṭhaṃ praviśya kāryāṇi kuruṣva kṣipram // Saddhp_7.99 //
children.translated_text: You have reached the most excellent city — enter and attend to your tasks quickly! || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.99 ||

children.text: udagracittā bhaṇatheha nirvṛtā nistīrṇa sarvā aṭavī aśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: With uplifted minds, declare yourselves content and liberated — the entire wilderness has been crossed completely!'

children.text: āśvāsanārthāya vadeti vācaṃ kathaṃ na pratyāgata sarvi asyā // Saddhp_7.100 //
children.translated_text: He speaks words for the purpose of reassurance — 'How shall all these not turn back?' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.100 ||

children.text: viśrāntarūpāṃśca viditva sarvān samānayitvā ca punarbravīti /
children.translated_text: And having perceived that all have rested, he gathers them together and speaks again:

children.text: āgacchatha mahya śṛṇotha bhāṣato ṛddhīmayaṃ nagaramidaṃ vinirmitam // Saddhp_7.101 //
children.translated_text: 'Come, listen to me as I speak — this city is conjured by supernatural power. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.101 ||

children.text: yuṣmāka khedaṃ ca mayā vitdivā nivartanaṃ mā ca bhaviṣyatīti /
children.translated_text: Having known your weariness, and [knowing] that you might turn back,

children.text: upāyakauśalyamidaṃ mameti janetha vīryaṃ gamanāya dvīpam // Saddhp_7.102 //
children.translated_text: this is my skillful means — generate vigor for journeying to the island [of jewels]!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.102 ||

children.text: emeva haṃ bhikṣava deśiko vā praṇāyakaḥ prāṇisahasrakoṭinām /
children.translated_text: Even so, O monks, I am like a guide, a leader of <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of living beings;

children.text: khidyanta paśyāmi tathaiva prāṇinaḥ kleśāṇḍakośaṃ na prabhonti bhettum // Saddhp_7.103 //
children.translated_text: I see those living beings exhausted in the same way — they are unable to break through the shell of the egg of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.103 ||

children.text: tato mayā cintitu eṣa artho viśrāmabhūtā imi nirvṛtīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Then I considered this purpose: the state of <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) shall be their place of rest;

children.text: sarvasya duḥkhasya nirodha eṣa arhantabhūmau kṛtakṛtya yūyam // Saddhp_7.104 //
children.translated_text: 'This is the cessation of all suffering — you are ones whose task is done, on the level of <s>Arhats</s>.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.104 ||

children.text: samaye yadā tu sthita atra sthāne paśyāmi yūyāmarhanta tatra sarvān /
children.translated_text: When at that time I see all of you established here as <s>Arhats</s>,

children.text: tadā ca sarvāniha saṃnipātya bhūtārthamākhyāmi yathaiṣa dharmaḥ // Saddhp_7.105 //
children.translated_text: then, having gathered all here, I declare the true meaning of what this <s>Dharma</s> is. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.105 ||

children.text: upāyakauśalya vināyakānāṃ yad yāna deśenti trayo maharṣī /
children.translated_text: It is the skillful means of the guides, the great sages, that they teach three vehicles;

children.text: ekaṃ hi yānaṃ na dvitīyamasti viśrāmaṇārthaṃ tu dviyāna deśitā // Saddhp_7.106 //
children.translated_text: for there is only one vehicle, no second — [the teaching of] two vehicles was for the purpose of providing rest. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.106 ||

children.text: tato vademi ahamadya bhikṣavo janetha vīryaṃ paramaṃ udāram /
children.translated_text: Therefore I say to you today, O monks: generate the supreme and noble vigor!

children.text: sarvajñajñānena kṛtena yūyaṃ naitāvatā nirvṛti kāci bhoti // Saddhp_7.107 //
children.translated_text: By omniscient knowledge [you must strive] — not by this much alone is there any <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.107 ||

children.text: sarvajñajñānaṃ tu yadā spṛśiṣyatha daśo balā ye ca jināna dharmāḥ /
children.translated_text: When you shall attain omniscient knowledge, the ten powers and the qualities of the <s>Jinas</s>,

children.text: dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhārī buddhā bhavitvāna bhavetha nirvṛtāḥ // Saddhp_7.108 //
children.translated_text: bearing the form adorned with the thirty-two marks, having become <s>Buddhas</s>, you shall be [truly] liberated. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.108 ||

children.text: etādṛśī deśana nāyakānāṃ viśrāmahetoḥ pravadanti nirvṛtim /
children.translated_text: Such is the teaching of the guides — they proclaim <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) for the purpose of rest;

children.text: viśrānta jñātvāna ca nirvṛtīye sarvajñajñāne upanenti sarvān // Saddhp_7.109 //
children.translated_text: and having known them to be rested in [that] <s>nirvṛti</s>, they lead all toward omniscient knowledge. || <s>Saddhp</s> 7.109 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye pūrvayogaparivarto nāma saptamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter, named 'The Chapter on Former Connection' (<s>Pūrvayogaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_8: pañcabhikṣuśatavyākaraṇaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 8: The Chapter on the Prediction of the Five Hundred Monks (<s>Pañcabhikṣuśatavyākaraṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmān pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro bhagavato 'ntikādidamevaṃrūpamupāyakauśalyajñānadarśanaṃ saṃdhābhāṣitanirdeśaṃ śrutvā eṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā imāṃ ca pūrvayogapratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ śrutvā imāṃ ca bhagavato vṛṣabhatāṃ śrutvā āścaryaprāpto 'bhūdadbhutaprāpto 'bhūnnirāmiṣeṇa ca cittena prītiprāmodyena sphuṭo 'bhūt | mahatā ca prītiprāmodyena mahatā ca dharmagauraveṇa utthāyāsanād bhagavataścaraṇayoḥ praṇipatya evaṃ cittamutpāditavān - āścaryaṃ bhagavan, āścaryaṃ sugata | paramaduṣkaraṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ kurvanti, ya imaṃ nānādhātukaṃ lokamanuvartayante, bahubhiścopāyakauśalyajñānanidarśanaiḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti, tasmiṃstasmiṃśca sattvān vilagnānupāyakauśalyena pramocayanti | kimatra bhagavan asmābhiḥ śakyaṃ kartum? tathāgata evāsmākaṃ jānīte āśayaṃ pūrvayogacaryāṃ ca | sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte sthito 'bhūd bhagavantameva namaskurvan animiṣābhyāṃ ca netrābhyāṃ saṃprekṣamāṇaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, having heard from the Blessed One this very form of the display of the knowledge of skillful means, this teaching by indirect speech, and having heard the prediction of those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and having heard this discourse connected with former connections, and having heard of the Blessed One's bull-like preeminence, was struck with wonder and amazement, and his mind was filled with joyous delight free from material attachments. With great joyous delight and with great reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, he rose from his seat, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, and generated this thought: 'Wonderful, O Blessed One! Wonderful, O <s>Sugata</s>! Most difficult is what the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones accomplish — that they conform to this world of manifold dispositions, and teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings with many displays of the knowledge of skillful means, freeing beings who are attached to this and that through skillful means. What can we do here, O Blessed One? Only the <s>Tathāgata</s> knows our aspiration and our former conduct.' He then bowed his head to the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side, paying homage to the Blessed One, gazing with unblinking eyes.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaḥ pūrṇasya maitrāyaṇīputrasya cittāśayamavalokya sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - paśyatha bhikṣavo yūyamimaṃ śrāvakaṃ pūrṇaṃ maitrāyaṇīputraṃ yo mayāsya bhikṣusaṃghasya dharmakathikānāmagryo nirdiṣṭaḥ, bahubhiśca bhūtairguṇairabhiṣṭutaḥ, bahubhiśca prakārairasmin mama śāsane saddharmaparigrahāyābhiyuktaḥ | catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃharṣakaḥ samādāpakaḥ samuttejakaḥ saṃpraharṣako 'klānto dharmadeśanayā, alamasya dharmasyākhyātā, alamanugrahītā sabrahmacāriṇām | muktvā bhikṣavastathāgataṃ nānyaḥ śaktaḥ pūrṇaṃ maitrāyaṇīputramarthato vā vyañjanato vā paryādātum | tatkiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo mamaivāyaṃ saddharmaparigrāhaka iti? na khalu punarbhikṣavo yuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? abhijānāmyahaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani navanavatīnāṃ buddhakoṭīnām, yatra anenaiva teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsane saddharmaḥ parigṛhītaḥ | tadyathāpi nāma mama etarhi sarvatra cāgryo dharmakathikānāmabhūt, sarvatra ca śūnyatāgatiṃ gato 'bhūt | sarvatra ca pratisaṃvidāṃ lābhī abhūt, sarvatra ca bodhisattvābhijñāsu gatiṃ gato 'bhūt | suviniścitadharmadeśako nirvicikitsadharmadeśakaḥ pariśuddhadharmadeśakaścābhūt | teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ śāsane yāvadāyuṣpramāṇaṃ brahmacaryaṃ caritavān | sarvatra ca śrāvaka iti saṃjñāyate sma | sa khalvanenopāyena aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmarthamakārṣīt, aprameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃśca sattvān paripācitavānanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | sarvatra ca buddhakṛtyena sattvānāṃ pratyupasthito 'bhūt | sarvatra cātmano buddhakṣetraṃ pariśodhayati sma | sattvānāṃ ca paripākāyābhiyukto 'bhūt | eṣāmapi bhikṣavo vipaśyipramukhānāṃ saptānāṃ tathāgatānāṃ yeṣāmahaṃ saptamaḥ, eṣa evāgryo dharmakathikānāmabhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having perceived the mental aspiration of the venerable <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, addressed the entire community of monks: 'Do you see, O monks, this <s>Śrāvaka</s> <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s>, who has been declared by me as foremost among the Dharma-preachers of this community of monks, and who has been praised for his many genuine qualities, and who has been devoted in many ways to the preservation of the true <s>Dharma</s> in my teaching? He is the encourager, inspirer, uplifter, and delighter of the four assemblies, untiring in teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, fully capable of explaining this <s>Dharma</s>, and fully capable of benefiting his fellow practitioners in the holy life. Except for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O monks, no one else is able to surpass <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> in meaning or in letter. What do you think, O monks — is it only my true <s>Dharma</s> that he upholds? No indeed, O monks, you should not view it thus. For what reason? I recall, O monks, that in the past, under ninety-nine <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, he upheld the true <s>Dharma</s> in the teachings of those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. Just as now, so too everywhere he was foremost among the Dharma-preachers; everywhere he had penetrated the course of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness); everywhere he had attained the analytical knowledges; everywhere he had penetrated the superknowledges of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. He was a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> with well-determined certainty, a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> without doubt, a teacher of the <s>Dharma</s> who was completely pure. And in the teachings of those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, he practiced the holy life for as long as their lifespans. Everywhere he was known as a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. Yet by this skillful means, he served the welfare of immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings, and ripened immeasurable, incalculable beings toward supreme perfect awakening. Everywhere he attended to the work of a <s>Buddha</s> on behalf of beings. Everywhere he was purifying his own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). And he was devoted to the ripening of beings. Of these seven <s>Tathāgatas</s> beginning with <s>Vipaśyin</s>, of whom I am the seventh, he was everywhere foremost among the Dharma-preachers.'

body.text: yadapi tadbhikṣavo bhaviṣyatyanāgate 'dhvani asmin bhadrakalpe caturbhirbuddhairūnaṃ buddhasahasram, teṣāmapi śāsane eṣa eva pūrṇo maitrāyaṇīputro 'gryo dharmakathikānāṃ bhaviṣyati, saddharmaparigrāhakaśca bhaviṣyati | evamanāgate 'dhvani aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saddharmamādhārayiṣyati, aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaṃ kariṣyati, aprameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃśca sattvān paripācayiṣyatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | satatasamitaṃ cābhiyukto bhaviṣyatyātmano buddhakṣetrapariśuddhaye sattvaparipācanāya | sa imāmevaṃrūpāṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrya aprameyairasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyate | dharmaprabhāso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | asminneva buddhakṣetra utpatsyate ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O monks, in the future, in this <s>Bhadrakalpa</s> (Fortunate Aeon), there will be a thousand <s>Buddhas</s> minus four — in the teachings of all of those as well, this <s>Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra</s> will be foremost among the Dharma-preachers, and will be an upholder of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, in the future, he will uphold the true <s>Dharma</s> of immeasurable, incalculable Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, will serve the welfare of immeasurable, incalculable beings, and will ripen immeasurable, incalculable beings toward supreme perfect awakening. And he will be constantly devoted to the purification of his own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> and the ripening of beings. Having fulfilled this very form of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, after immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, he will attain supreme perfect awakening. He will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Dharmaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of Dharma) in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. He will arise in this very <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.

body.text: tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena gaṅgānadīvālukopamāstrisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātava ekaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | samaṃ pāṇitalajātaṃ saptaratnamayamapagataparvataṃ saptaratnamayaiḥ kūṭāgāraiḥ paripūrṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | devavimānāni cākāśasthitāni bhaviṣyanti | devā api manuṣyān drakṣyanti, manuṣyā api devān drakṣyanti | tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena idaṃ buddhakṣetramapagatapāpaṃ bhaviṣyati apagatamātṛgrāmaṃ ca | sarve ca te sattvā aupapādukā bhaviṣyanti brahmacāriṇo manomayairātmabhāvaiḥ svayaṃprabhā ṛddhimanto vaihāyasaṃgamā vīryavantaḥ smṛtimantaḥ prajñāvantaḥ suvarṇavarṇaiḥ samucchrayairdvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtavigrahāḥ | tena khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ samayena tasmin buddhakṣetre teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ dvāvāhārau bhaviṣyataḥ | katamau dvau? yaduta dharmaprītyāhāro dhyānaprītyāhāraśca | aprameyāṇi cāsaṃkhyeyāni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bhaviṣyanti sarveṣāṃ ca mahābhijñāprāptānāṃ pratisaṃvidgatiṃgatānāṃ sattvāvavādakuśalānām | gaṇanāsamatikrāntāścāsya śrāvakā bhaviṣyanti maharddhikā mahānubhāvā aṣṭavimokṣadhyāyinaḥ | evamaparimitaguṇasamanvāgataṃ tad buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati | ratnāvabhāsaśca nāma sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | suviśuddhā ca nāma sā lokadhāturbhaviṣyati | aprameyānasaṃkhyeyāṃścāsya kalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | parinirvṛtasya ca tasya bhagavato dharmaprabhāsasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya saddharmaścirasthāyī bhaviṣyati | ratnamayaiśca stūpaiḥ sā lokadhātuḥ sphuṭā bhaviṣyati | evamacintyaguṇasamanvāgataṃ bhikṣavastasya bhagavatastadbuddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: At that time, O monks, trichiliocosms (three-thousand-great-thousand world-systems) as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river shall become one <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). It shall be level, flat as the palm of the hand, made of the seven jewels, without mountains, filled with mansions made of the seven jewels. Divine palaces shall stand in the sky. Gods shall see humans, and humans shall see gods. At that time, O monks, that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be free from evil and free from womankind. All those beings shall be spontaneously born, celibate, with mind-made bodies, self-luminous, possessed of supernatural powers, traversing the sky, endowed with vigor, mindfulness, and wisdom, with golden-colored bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great being. At that time, O monks, in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, those beings shall have two kinds of nourishment — what are the two? Namely, the nourishment of delight in the <s>Dharma</s> and the nourishment of delight in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). And there shall be immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, all having attained the great superknowledges, having reached the level of the analytical knowledges, skilled in instructing beings. His <s>Śrāvakas</s> shall be beyond counting — possessed of great supernatural powers, great might, established in the eight liberations of meditation. Thus endowed with immeasurable qualities shall that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> be. The <s>kalpa</s> shall be called <s>Ratnāvabhāsa</s> (Jewel-Radiance), and that world-system shall be called <s>Suviśuddhā</s> (Perfectly Pure). His lifespan shall be immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s>. And after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that Blessed One <s>Dharmaprabhāsa</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, the true <s>Dharma</s> shall long endure. And that world-system shall be covered with <s>stūpas</s> made of jewels. Thus endowed with inconceivable qualities, O monks, shall that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of that Blessed One be.

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān | idaṃ vaditvā sugato hyathāparametaduvāca śāstā -
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having spoken thus, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, further spoke these [verses] —

children.text: śṛṇotha me bhikṣava etamarthaṃ yathā carī mahya sutena cīrṇā /
children.translated_text: 'Listen to me, O monks, to this matter: how the conduct was practiced by my son,

children.text: upāyakauśalyasuśikṣitena yathā ca cīrṇā iya bodhicaryā // Saddhp_8.1 //
children.translated_text: well-trained in <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), and how this <s>bodhicaryā</s> (conduct of awakening) was practiced. || Saddhp 8.1 ||

body.text: hīnādhimuktā ima sattva jñātvā udārayāne ca samuttrasanti /
body.translated_text: Knowing that these beings are of inferior aspirations and are terrified of the great vehicle,

body.text: tatu śrāvakā bhontimi bodhisattvāḥ pratyekabodhiṃ ca nidarśayanti // Saddhp_8.2 //
body.translated_text: the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> become <s>Śrāvakas</s> and also display <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). || Saddhp 8.2 ||

children.text: upāyakauśalyaśatairanekaiḥ paripācayanti bahubodhisattvān /
children.translated_text: With countless hundreds of kinds of <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means), they ripen many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>,

children.text: evaṃ ca bhāṣanti vayaṃ hi śrāvakā dūre vayaṃ uttamamagrabodhiyā // Saddhp_8.3 //
children.translated_text: and they speak thus: "We are but <s>Śrāvakas</s> — far are we from the supreme, highest awakening!" || Saddhp 8.3 ||

children.text: etāṃ cariṃ teṣvanuśikṣamāṇāḥ paripāku gacchanti hi sattvakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Learning this conduct from them, <s>koṭis</s> of beings come to maturity;

children.text: hīnādhimuktāśca kusīdarūpā anupūrva te sarvi bhavanti buddhāḥ // Saddhp_8.4 //
children.translated_text: even those of inferior aspirations and of lazy disposition gradually all become <s>Buddhas</s>. || Saddhp 8.4 ||

children.text: ajñānacaryāṃ ca caranti ete vayaṃ khalu śrāvaka alpakṛtyāḥ /
children.translated_text: They practice the conduct of the unknowing, [saying:] "We are merely <s>Śrāvakas</s>, of small tasks";

children.text: nirviṇṇa sarvāsu cyutopapattiṣu svakaṃ ca kṣetraṃ pariśodhayanti // Saddhp_8.5 //
children.translated_text: wearied of all births and deaths, they purify their own fields. || Saddhp 8.5 ||

children.text: sarāgatāmātmani darśayanti sadoṣatāṃ cāpi samohatāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: They display in themselves attachment, and also anger and delusion;

children.text: dṛṣṭīvilagnāṃśca viditva sattvāṃsteṣāṃ pi dṛṣṭiṃ samupāśrayanti // Saddhp_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and knowing beings who are entangled in [wrong] views, they also adopt those views [for their sake]. || Saddhp 8.6 ||

children.text: evaṃ caranto bahu mahya śrāvakāḥ sattvānupāyena vimocayanti /
children.translated_text: Thus practicing, my many <s>Śrāvakas</s> liberate beings through skillful means;

children.text: unmādu gaccheyu narā avidvasū sa caiva sarvaṃ caritaṃ prakāśayet // Saddhp_8.7 //
children.translated_text: the ignorant people would go mad [if the full truth were revealed] — but he shall make manifest the entire conduct. || Saddhp 8.7 ||

children.text: pūrṇo ayaṃ śrāvaka mahya bhikṣavaścarito purā buddhasahasrakoṭiṣu /
children.translated_text: This <s>Pūrṇa</s>, a <s>Śrāvaka</s> of mine, O monks, has practiced formerly under <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>;

children.text: teṣāṃ ca saddharma parigrahīṣīd bauddhaṃ idaṃ jñāna gaveṣamāṇaḥ // Saddhp_8.8 //
children.translated_text: and he upheld the true <s>Dharma</s> of those [<s>Buddhas</s>], seeking this <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. || Saddhp 8.8 ||

children.text: sarvatra caiṣo abhu agraśrāvako bahuśrutaścitrakathī viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: He was everywhere the foremost <s>Śrāvaka</s> — learned, a versatile speaker, confident;

children.text: saṃharṣakaścā akilāsi nityaṃ sada buddhakṛtyena ca pratyupasthitaḥ // Saddhp_8.9 //
children.translated_text: an encourager, never weary, always attending upon the work of the <s>Buddhas</s>. || Saddhp 8.9 ||

children.text: mahāabhijñāsu sadā gatiṃgataḥ pratisaṃvidānāṃ ca abhūṣi lābhī /
children.translated_text: Always having attained mastery of the great superknowledges, and being a recipient of the analytical knowledges,

children.text: sattvāna co indriyagocarajño dharmaṃ ca deśeti sadā viśuddham // Saddhp_8.10 //
children.translated_text: and knowing the faculties and dispositions of beings, he always teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in purity. || Saddhp 8.10 ||

children.text: saddharma śreṣṭhaṃ ca prakāśayantaḥ paripācayī sattvasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Illuminating the supreme true <s>Dharma</s>, he ripened <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of beings,

children.text: anuttarasminniha agrayāne kṣetraṃ svakaṃ śreṣṭhu viśodhayantaḥ // Saddhp_8.11 //
children.translated_text: in this unsurpassed, supreme vehicle, purifying his own excellent field. || Saddhp 8.11 ||

children.text: anāgate cāpi tathaiva adhve pūjeṣyatī buddhasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And in the future age likewise, he shall worship <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: saddharma śreṣṭhaṃ ca parigrahīṣyati svakaṃ ca kṣetraṃ pariśodhayiṣyati // Saddhp_8.12 //
children.translated_text: and he shall uphold the supreme true <s>Dharma</s> and shall purify his own field. || Saddhp 8.12 ||

children.text: deśeṣyatī dharma sadā viśārado upāyakauśalyasahasrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: He shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> always with confidence, with <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of skillful means,

children.text: bahūṃśca sattvān paripācayiṣyati sarvajñajñānasmi anāsravasmin // Saddhp_8.13 //
children.translated_text: and he shall ripen many beings in the all-knowing knowledge that is free from outflows. || Saddhp 8.13 ||

children.text: so pūja kṛtvā naranāyakānāṃ saddharma śreṣṭhaṃ sada dhārayitvā /
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the leaders of men and always upheld the supreme true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: bhaviṣyatī buddha svayaṃbhu loke dharmaprabhāso diśatāsu viśrutaḥ // Saddhp_8.14 //
children.translated_text: he shall become a self-arisen <s>Buddha</s> in the world — <s>Dharmaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of the <s>Dharma</s>), renowned in the ten directions. || Saddhp 8.14 ||

children.text: kṣetraṃ ca tasya suviśuddha bheṣyatī ratnāna saptāna sadā viśiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: His field shall be perfectly pure, always distinguished by the seven jewels;

children.text: ratnavabhāsaśca sa kalpu bheṣyatī suviśuddha so bheṣyati lokadhātuḥ // Saddhp_8.15 //
children.translated_text: that <s>kalpa</s> shall be <s>Ratnāvabhāsa</s> (Jewel-Radiance), and that world-system shall be perfectly pure. || Saddhp 8.15 ||

children.text: bahubodhisattvāna sahasrakoṭyo mahāabhijñāsu sukovidānām /
children.translated_text: Many <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, well-versed in the great superknowledges,

children.text: yehi sphuṭo bheṣyati lokadhātuḥ suviśuddha śuddhehi maharddhikehi // Saddhp_8.16 //
children.translated_text: with whom that world-system shall be filled — pure ones, purified, of great supernatural power. || Saddhp 8.16 ||

children.text: atha śrāvakāṇāṃ pi sahasrakoṭyaḥ saṃghastadā bheṣyati nāyakasya /
children.translated_text: And <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Śrāvakas</s> too — that shall be the <s>Saṅgha</s> of that Guide,

children.text: maharddhikānaṣṭavimokṣadhyāyināṃ pratisaṃvidāsū ca gatiṃgatānām // Saddhp_8.17 //
children.translated_text: possessed of great supernatural power, established in the eight liberations of meditation, and having attained mastery of the analytical knowledges. || Saddhp 8.17 ||

children.text: sarve ca sattvāstahi buddhakṣetre śuddhā bhaviṣyanti ca brahmacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: All beings in that <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be pure and celibate,

children.text: upapādukāḥ sarvi suvarṇavarṇā dvātriṃśatīlakṣaṇarūpadhāriṇaḥ // Saddhp_8.18 //
children.translated_text: all spontaneously born, golden-colored, bearing the form adorned with the thirty-two marks. || Saddhp 8.18 ||

children.text: āhārasaṃjñā ca na tatra bheṣyati anyatra dharme rati dhyānaprītiḥ /
children.translated_text: There shall be no notion of food, but only delight in the <s>Dharma</s> and the joy of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation);

children.text: na mātṛgrāmo 'pi ca tatra bheṣyati na cāpyapāyāna ca durgatībhayam // Saddhp_8.19 //
children.translated_text: there shall be no womankind, nor fear of the lower realms or evil destinies. || Saddhp 8.19 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ kṣetravaraṃ bhaviṣyati pūrṇasya saṃpūrṇaguṇānvitasya /
children.translated_text: Such shall be the supreme field of <s>Pūrṇa</s>, endowed with complete qualities —

children.text: ākīrṇa sattvehi subhadrakehi yatkiṃcimātraṃ pi idaṃ prakāśitam // Saddhp_8.20 //
children.translated_text: filled with blessed beings — only a small portion of this has been declared here. || Saddhp 8.20 ||'

body.text: atha khalu teṣāṃ dvādaśānāṃ vaśībhūtaśatānāmetadabhavat - āścaryaprāpta sma, adbhutaprāptāḥ sma | sacedasmākamapi bhagavān yatheme 'nye mahāśrāvakā vyākṛtāḥ, evamasmākamapi tathāgataḥ pṛthak pṛthag vyākuryāt | atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya āyuṣmantaṃ mahākāśyapamāmantrayate sma - imāni kāśyapa dvādaśa vaśībhūtaśatāni, yeṣāmahametarhi saṃmukhībhūtaḥ | sarvāṇyetānyahaṃ kāśyapa dvādaśa vaśībhūtaśatānyanantaraṃ vyākaromi | tatra kāśyapa kauṇḍinyo bhikṣurmahāśrāvako dvāṣaṣṭīnāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ pareṇa parataraṃ samantaprabhāso nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tatra kāśyapa anenaikena nāmadheyena pañca tathāgataśatāni bhaviṣyanti | ataḥ pañca mahāśrāvakaśatāni sarvāṇyanantaramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante | sarvāṇyeva samantaprabhāsanāmadheyāni bhaviṣyanti | tadyathā gayākāśyapo nadīkāśyapaḥ urubilvakāśyapaḥ kālaḥ kālodāyī aniruddho revataḥ kapphiṇo bakkulaścundaḥ svāgataḥ ityevaṃpramukhāni pañca vaśībhūtaśatāni ||
body.translated_text: Then those twelve hundred who had attained mastery had this thought: 'We are filled with wonder and amazement! If only the Blessed One would grant us predictions as those other great <s>Śrāvakas</s> have been predicted — if the <s>Tathāgata</s> would grant each of us separately a prediction!' Then the Blessed One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, addressed the venerable <s>Mahākāśyapa</s>: 'These twelve hundred who have attained mastery, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, I shall now face to face give them all a prediction. Here, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the monk <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, the great <s>Śrāvaka</s>, after passing beyond sixty-two <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One in the world, named <s>Samantaprabhāsa</s> (Universal Radiance), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. Here, O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, under that single name there shall be five hundred <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And then five hundred great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, all in succession, shall attain supreme perfect awakening. All shall bear the name <s>Samantaprabhāsa</s>. That is to say: <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s>, <s>Urubilvakāśyapa</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Kālodāyin</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Revata</s>, <s>Kapphiṇa</s>, <s>Bakkula</s>, <s>Cunda</s>, <s>Svāgata</s> — these and the rest, five hundred who have attained mastery.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: kauṇḍinyagotro mama śrāvako 'yaṃ tathāgato bheṣyati lokanāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>-gotra <s>Śrāvaka</s> of mine shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, a Lord of the World,

children.text: anāgate 'dhvāni anantakalpe vineṣyate prāṇisahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_8.21 //
children.translated_text: in the future age, after immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, and he shall guide <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of beings. || Saddhp 8.21 ||

body.text: samantaprabho nāma jino bhaviṣyati kṣetraṃ ca tasya pariśuddha bheṣyati /
body.translated_text: He shall become a <s>Jina</s> named <s>Samantaprabha</s> (Universal Radiance), and his field shall be perfectly pure,

body.text: anantakalpasmi anāgate 'dhvani dṛṣṭvāna buddhān bahavo hyanantān // Saddhp_8.22 //
body.translated_text: in the immeasurable <s>kalpa</s> in the future age, having seen many <s>Buddhas</s>, innumerable. || Saddhp 8.22 ||

children.text: prabhāsvaro buddhabalenupeto vighuṣṭaśabdo daśasu ddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Radiant, endowed with the power of the <s>Buddhas</s>, his fame resounding in the ten directions,

children.text: puraskṛtaḥ prāṇisahasrakoṭibhirdeśeṣyatī uttamamagrabodhim // Saddhp_8.23 //
children.translated_text: attended upon by <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of beings, he shall teach the supreme, highest awakening. || Saddhp 8.23 ||

children.text: tatu bodhisattvā abhiyuktarūpā vimānaśreṣṭhānyabhiruhya cāpi /
children.translated_text: There the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, diligently devoted, ascending the finest palaces,

children.text: viharanta tatra anucintayanti viśuddhaśīlā sada sādhuvṛttayaḥ // Saddhp_8.24 //
children.translated_text: shall dwell there in contemplation — ever pure in conduct, always of good behavior. || Saddhp 8.24 ||

children.text: śrutvāna dharmaṃ dvipadottamasya anyāni kṣetrāṇyapi co sadā te /
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of the Supreme among Bipeds, they shall also always [visit] other fields;

children.text: vrajanti te buddhasahasravandakāḥ pūjāṃ ca teṣāṃ vipulāṃ karonti // Saddhp_8.25 //
children.translated_text: they shall go to worship thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> and make abundant offerings to them. || Saddhp 8.25 ||

children.text: kṣeṇena te cāpi tadāsya kṣetraṃ pratyāgamiṣyanti vināyakasya /
children.translated_text: And in an instant they shall return to the field of that Guide,

children.text: prabhāsanāmasya narottamasya caryābalaṃ tādṛśakaṃ bhaviṣyati // Saddhp_8.26 //
children.translated_text: of <s>Prabhāsa</s>, the best of men — such shall be the power of his conduct. || Saddhp 8.26 ||

children.text: ṣaṣṭiḥ sahasrā paripūrṇakalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ sugatasya tasya /
children.translated_text: Sixty thousand fully complete <s>kalpas</s> shall be the lifespan of that <s>Sugata</s>;

children.text: tataśca bhūyo dviguṇena tāyinaḥ parinirvṛtasyeha sa dharma sthāsyati // Saddhp_8.27 //
children.translated_text: and then for twice as long after the Savior's <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, his <s>Dharma</s> shall endure here. || Saddhp 8.27 ||

children.text: pratirūpakaścāsya bhaviṣyate punastriguṇaṃ tato ettakameva kālam /
children.translated_text: And the semblance thereof shall endure for three times that same span of time;

children.text: saddharmabhraṣṭe tada tasya tāyino dukhitā bhaviṣyanti narā marū ca // Saddhp_8.28 //
children.translated_text: when the true <s>Dharma</s> of that Savior is lost, then humans and gods shall be sorrowful. || Saddhp 8.28 ||

children.text: jināna teṣāṃ samanāmakānāṃ samantaprabhāṇāṃ puruṣottamānām /
children.translated_text: Of those <s>Jinas</s> of the same name, <s>Samantaprabhā</s>, the best of men,

children.text: paripūrṇa pañcāśata nāyakānāṃ ete bhaviṣyanti paraṃparāya // Saddhp_8.29 //
children.translated_text: a full five hundred guides — these shall arise in succession. || Saddhp 8.29 ||

children.text: sarveṣa etādṛśakāśca vyūhā ṛddhibalaṃ ca tatha buddhakṣetram /
children.translated_text: The arrays of all of them shall be of such a kind, and their supernatural power and <s>buddhakṣetra</s> likewise;

children.text: gaṇaśca saddharma tathaiva īdṛśaḥ saddharmasthānaṃ ca samaṃ bhaviṣyati // Saddhp_8.30 //
children.translated_text: and their <s>Saṅgha</s> and true <s>Dharma</s> shall be just like this — and the duration of the true <s>Dharma</s> shall be equal. || Saddhp 8.30 ||

children.text: sarveṣametādṛśakaṃ bhaviṣyati nāmaṃ tadā loki sadevakasmin /
children.translated_text: For all of them such shall be their renown in the world together with its gods,

children.text: yathā mayā pūrvi prakīrtitāsīt samantaprabhāsasya narottamasya // Saddhp_8.31 //
children.translated_text: as was declared by me earlier concerning <s>Samantaprabhāsa</s>, the best of men. || Saddhp 8.31 ||

children.text: paraṃparā eva tathānyamanyaṃ te vyākariṣyanti hitānukampī /
children.translated_text: In succession, each one shall give a prediction to the next, compassionate and beneficent;

children.text: anantarāyaṃ mama adya bheṣyati yathaiva śāsāmyahu sarvalokam // Saddhp_8.32 //
children.translated_text: there shall be unbroken continuity from me today, just as I instruct the entire world. || Saddhp 8.32 ||

children.text: evaṃ khu ete tvamihādya kāśyapa dhārehi pañcāśatanūnakāni /
children.translated_text: Thus indeed these — O <s>Kāśyapa</s>, retain today these nearly five hundred

children.text: vaśibhūta ye cāpi mamānyaśrāvakāḥ kathayāhi cānyeṣvapi śrāvakeṣu // Saddhp_8.33 //
children.translated_text: who have attained mastery, and my other <s>Śrāvakas</s> — proclaim this also among the other <s>Śrāvakas</s>! || Saddhp 8.33 ||'

body.text: atha khalu tāni pañcārhacchatāni bhagavataḥ saṃmukhamātmano vyākaraṇāni śrutvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanasa pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā yena bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ śirobhirnipatya evamāhuḥ - atyayaṃ vayaṃ bhagavan deśayāmo yairasmābhirbhagavannevaṃ satatasamitaṃ cittaṃ paribhāvitam - idamasmākaṃ parinirvāṇam | parinirvṛtā vayamiti | yathāpīdaṃ bhagavan avyaktā akuśalā avidhijñāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? yairnāma asmābhirbhagavaṃstathāgatajñāne 'bhisaṃboddhavye evaṃrūpeṇa parīttena jñānena paritoṣaṃ gatāḥ sma | tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan kasyacideva puruṣasya kaṃcideva mitragṛhaṃ praviṣṭasya mattasya vā suptasya vā sa mitro 'narghamaṇiratnaṃ vastrānte badhnīyāt - asyedaṃ maṇiratnaṃ bhavatviti | atha khalu bhagavan sa puruṣa utthāyāsanāt prakāmet | so 'nyaṃ janapadapradeśaṃ prapadyeta | sa tatra kṛcchraprāpto bhavet | āhāracīvaraparyeṣṭihetoḥ kṛcchramāpadyeta | mahatā ca vyāyāmena kathaṃcit kaṃcidāhāraṃ pratilabheta | tena ca saṃtuṣṭo bhavedāttamanaskaḥ pramuditaḥ | atha khalu bhagavaṃstasya puruṣasya sa purāṇamitraḥ puruṣo yena tasya tadanargheyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ vastrānte baddham, sa taṃ punareva paśyet | tamevaṃ vadet - kiṃ tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa kṛcchramāpadyase āhāracīvaraparyeṣṭihetoḥ, yadā yāvad bhoḥ puruṣa mayā tava sukhavihārārthaṃ sarvakāmanivartakamanargheyaṃ maṇiratnaṃ vastrānte upanibaddham | niryātitaṃ te bhoḥ puruṣa mamaitanmaṇiratnam | tadevamupanibaddhameva bhoḥ puruṣa vastrānte maṇiratnam | na ca nāma tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa pratyavekṣase - kiṃ mama baddhaṃ yena vā baddhaṃ ko hetuḥ kiṃnidānaṃ vā
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred <s>Arhats</s>, having heard their own prophecies directly from the Blessed One, were satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness. They approached the Blessed One, and having approached, bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One and said: 'We confess our transgression, O Blessed One — we who constantly entertained this thought in our minds: "This is our <s>parinirvāṇa</s>! We have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!" Like dull, incompetent fools without knowledge! For what reason? Because we, who should have attained awakening in the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, became satisfied with such paltry knowledge. It is as if, Blessed One, a certain man were to enter the house of a friend, and while he was drunk or asleep, that friend would tie a priceless jewel in the hem of his garment, [thinking]: "Let this jewel be his." Then, Blessed One, that man, having risen from his seat, would depart. He would go to another region of the country. There he would fall into hardship. He would undergo difficulty in searching for food and clothing. With great effort he would somehow obtain some food, and with that he would be content, delighted, and pleased. Then, Blessed One, that former friend of the man — the one who had tied the priceless jewel in the hem of his garment — would see him again. He would say to him: "Why, good man, are you undergoing hardship for the sake of food and clothing, when, good man, I tied this priceless jewel in the hem of your garment for your comfort and for the fulfillment of all your desires? It was given to you, good man, this jewel of mine! And yet, good man, this jewel remains tied in the hem of your garment. Do you not, good man, examine [yourself to see]: 'What is tied to me, by whom was it tied, what is the cause, what is the condition'

body.text: baddhametat? bālajātīyastvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa yastvaṃ kṛcchreṇa āhāracīvaraṃ paryeṣamāṇastuṣṭimāpadyase | gaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa etanmaṇiratnaṃ grahāya mahānagaraṃ gatvā parivartayastva | tena ca dhanena sarvāṇi dhanakaraṇīyāni kuruṣveti ||
body.translated_text: 'by which it was tied?' You are a fool, good man, in that you, searching with hardship for food and clothing, become satisfied! Go, good man, take this jewel, go to a great city, and exchange it. With that wealth, do all that needs to be done with wealth!'

body.text: evameva bhagavan asmākamapi tathāgatena pūrvameva bodhisattvacaryāṃ caratā sarvajñatācittānyutpāditānyabhūvan | tāni ca vayaṃ bhagavan na jānīmo na budhyāmahe | te vayaṃ bhagavan arhadbhūmau nirvṛtāḥ sma iti saṃjānīmaḥ | vayaṃ kṛcchraṃ jīvāmaḥ, yadvayaṃ bhagavan evaṃ parīttena jñānena paritoṣamāpadyāmaḥ | sarvajñajñānapraṇidhānena sadā avinaṣṭena | te vayaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatena saṃbodhyamānāḥ - mā yūyaṃ bhikṣava etannirvāṇaṃ manyadhvam | saṃvidyante bhikṣavo yuṣmākaṃ saṃtāne kuśalamūlāni yāni mayā pūrvaṃ paripācitāni | etarhi ca mamaivedamupāyakauśalyaṃ dharmadeśanābhilāpena yad yūyametarhi nirvāṇamiti manyadhve | evaṃ ca vayaṃ bhagavatā saṃbodhayitvā adyānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just so, Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s> had previously, while we were still practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s> path, generated in us the aspiration for omniscience. But we, Blessed One, did not know it, did not understand it. We thought: 'We are <s>Arhats</s>, we have attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' We live in hardship, in that we, Blessed One, become satisfied with such paltry knowledge — [yet] the aspiration for omniscient knowledge was never lost. And we, Blessed One, are now being awakened by the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Do not, O monks, consider this to be <s>nirvāṇa</s>! There exist in your continuum wholesome roots that were previously ripened by me. And this is my own skillful means in the expression of the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching, that you now consider this to be <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' And thus, having been awakened by the Blessed One, we have today been given the prophecy of supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: atha khalu tāni pañca vaśībhūtaśatānyājñātakauṇḍinyapramukhāni tasyāṃ velāyamimā gāthā abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those five hundred who had attained mastery, led by <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, at that moment spoke these verses:

children.text: hṛṣṭā prahṛṣṭā sma śruṇitva etāṃ āśvāsanāmīdṛśikāmanuttarām /
children.translated_text: 'We are joyful and delighted, having heard this unsurpassed reassurance of such a kind,

children.text: yaṃ vyākṛtāḥ sma paramāgrabodhaye namo 'stu te nāyaka nantacakṣuḥ // Saddhp_8.34 //
children.translated_text: that we have been given the prophecy of supreme, foremost awakening — homage to you, O Guide of Infinite Vision! || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.34 ||

children.text: deśemahe atyayu tubhyamantike yathaiva bālā avidū ajānakāḥ /
children.translated_text: We confess our transgression before you — just like dull, ignorant fools,

children.text: yaṃ vai vayaṃ nirvṛtimātrakeṇa parituṣṭa āsīt sugatasya śāsane // Saddhp_8.35 //
children.translated_text: we were satisfied with mere <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.35 ||

children.text: yathāpi puruṣo bhavi kaścideva praviṣṭa sa syādiha mitraśālam /
children.translated_text: Just as a certain man might enter the house of a friend,

children.text: mitraṃ ca tasya dhanavantamāḍhyaṃ so tasya dadyād bahū khādyabhojyam // Saddhp_8.36 //
children.translated_text: and that friend, wealthy and prosperous, would give him much food and drink; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.36 ||

children.text: saṃtarpayitvāna ca bhojanena anekamūlyaṃ ratanaṃ ca dadyāt /
children.translated_text: and having satisfied him with food, would give him a jewel of immeasurable value,

children.text: baddhvāntarīye vasanānti granthiṃ datvā ca tasyeha bhaveta tuṣṭaḥ // Saddhp_8.37 //
children.translated_text: tying a knot in his undergarment, and having given it, would be pleased; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.37 ||

children.text: so cāpi prakrāntu bhaveta bālo utthāya so 'nyaṃ nagaraṃ vrajeta /
children.translated_text: and that [man] too, being a fool, would depart — having risen, he would go to another city,

children.text: so kṛcchraprāptaḥ kṛpaṇo gaveṣī āhāra paryeṣati khidyamānaḥ // Saddhp_8.38 //
children.translated_text: and fallen into hardship, miserable, searching, he would seek food in distress; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.38 ||

children.text: paryeṣitaḥ bhojananirvṛtaḥ syād bhaktaṃ udāraṃ avicintayantaḥ /
children.translated_text: after searching, he would be content with [whatever] food [he finds], not thinking of the excellent meal,

children.text: taṃ cāpi ratnaṃ hi bhaveta vismṛtaṃ baddhvāntarīye smṛtirasya nāsti // Saddhp_8.39 //
children.translated_text: and that jewel too would be forgotten — tied in his undergarment, he has no recollection of it; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.39 ||

children.text: tameva so paśyati pūrvamitro yenāsya dattaṃ ratanaṃ gṛhe sve /
children.translated_text: that same former friend would see him — the one who had given him the jewel in his own house —

children.text: tameva suṣṭhū paribhāṣayitvā darśeti ratnaṃ vasanāntarasmin // Saddhp_8.40 //
children.translated_text: and having reproved him well, would show him the jewel in the hem of his garment; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.40 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca so paramasukhaiḥ samarpito ratnasya tasyo anubhāva īdṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: and having seen it, he would be endowed with supreme happiness — such is the power of that jewel,

children.text: mahādhanī kośabalī ca so bhavet samarpitaḥ kāmaguṇehi pañcahi // Saddhp_8.41 //
children.translated_text: he would become greatly wealthy and powerful in treasury, endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure. || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.41 ||

children.text: emeva bhagavan vayamevarūpam ajānamānā praṇidhānapūrvakam /
children.translated_text: Just so, Blessed One, we, not knowing such a prior aspiration,

children.text: tathāgatenaiva idaṃ hi dattaṃ bhaveṣu pūrveṣviha dīrgharātram // Saddhp_8.42 //
children.translated_text: which was given by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself in former existences throughout the long night [of <s>saṃsāra</s>]; || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.42 ||

children.text: vayaṃ ca bhagavanniha bālabuddhayo ajānakāḥ smo sugatasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: and we, Blessed One, of childish understanding here, not knowing, in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: nirvāṇamātreṇa vayaṃ hi tuṣṭā na uttarī prārthayi nāpi cintayī // Saddhp_8.43 //
children.translated_text: were satisfied with mere <s>nirvāṇa</s> — we neither sought nor contemplated anything higher. || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.43 ||

children.text: vayaṃ ca saṃbodhita lokabandhunā na eṣa etādṛśa kāci nirvṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: And we have been awakened by the Kinsman of the World: "This is no true <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation) of such a kind;

children.text: jñānaṃ praṇītaṃ puruṣottamānāṃ yā nirvṛtīyaṃ paramaṃ ca saukhyam // Saddhp_8.44 //
children.translated_text: the excellent knowledge of the supreme among men — that is the supreme <s>nirvṛti</s> and highest bliss." || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.44 ||

children.text: idaṃ cudāraṃ vipulaṃ bahūvidhaṃ anuttaraṃ vyākaraṇaṃ ca śrutvā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this excellent, vast, manifold, unsurpassed prophecy,

children.text: prītā udagrā vipulā sma jātāḥ parasparaṃ vyākaraṇāya nātha // Saddhp_8.45 //
children.translated_text: we have become joyful, elated, and greatly [delighted] — for the prophecy of one another, O Protector! || <s>Saddhp</s> 8.45 ||'

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye pañcabhikṣuśatavyākaraṇaparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter, named 'The Prophecy of the Five Hundred Monks,' in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>Dharmaparyāya</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_9: ānandādivyākaraṇaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 9: The Chapter on the Prophecy of <s>Ānanda</s> and Others (<s>Ānandādivyākaraṇaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandastasyāṃ velāyāmevaṃ cintayāmāsa - apyeva nāma vayamevaṃrūpaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabhemahi | evaṃ ca cintayitvā anuvicintya prārthayitvā utthāyāsanād bhagavataḥ pādayornipatya, āyuṣmāṃśca rāhulo 'pyevaṃ cintayitvā anuvicintya prārthayitvā bhagavataḥ pādayornipatya evaṃ vācamabhāṣata - asmākamapi tāvad bhagavan avasaro bhavatu | asmākamapi tāvat sugata avasaro bhavatu | asmākaṃ hi bhagavān pitā janako layanaṃ trāṇaṃ ca | vayaṃ hi bhagavan sadevamānuṣāsure loke 'tīva citrīkṛtāḥ - bhagavataścaite putraḥ bhagavataścopasthāyakāḥ bhagavataśca dharmakośaṃ dhārayantīti | tannāma bhagavan kṣiprameva pratirūpaṃ bhaved yad bhagavānasmākaṃ vyākuryādanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, at that moment, thought thus: 'Perhaps we too might obtain such a prophecy!' Having thought, reflected, and wished thus, he rose from his seat and bowed at the feet of the Blessed One. And the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> too, having thought, reflected, and wished thus, bowed at the feet of the Blessed One and spoke these words: 'May there be an opportunity for us too, Blessed One! May there be an opportunity for us too, <s>Sugata</s>! For the Blessed One is our father, progenitor, refuge, and protector. We, Blessed One, are greatly renowned in the world with its gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>: "These are the sons of the Blessed One, the attendants of the Blessed One, and they bear the <s>Dharma</s>-treasury of the Blessed One." Therefore, Blessed One, it would be fitting if the Blessed One were to quickly give us the prophecy of supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: anye ca dve bhikṣusahasre sātireke śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ śrāvakāṇāmutthāyāsanebhya ekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā añjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavato 'bhimukhaṃ bhagavantamullokayamāne tasthatuḥ etāmeva cintāmanuvicintayamāne yaduta idameva buddhajñānam - apyeva nāma vayamapi vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabhemahi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti ||
body.translated_text: And two thousand other monks, both learners and adepts among the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, rose from their seats, arranged their upper robes over one shoulder, and stood facing the Blessed One with palms joined, gazing at the Blessed One, contemplating and reflecting on this very thought — that is, this <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge: 'Perhaps we too might obtain the prophecy of supreme perfect awakening.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - bhaviṣyasi tvamānanda anāgate 'dhvani sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijño nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | dvāṣaṣṭīnāṃ buddhakoṭīnāṃ satkāraṃ kṛtvā, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāṃ ca kṛtvā, teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saddharmaṃ dhārayitvā, śāsanaparigrahaṃ ca kṛtvā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyasi | sa tvamānanda anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ saṃbuddhaḥ samāno viṃśatigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi paripācayiṣyasyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | samṛddhaṃ ca te buddhakṣetraṃ bhaviṣyati vaiḍūryamayaṃ ca | anavanāmitavaijayantī ca nāma sā lokadhāturbhaviṣyati | manojñaśabdābhigarjitaśca nāma sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | aparimitāṃśca kalpāṃstasya bhagavataḥ sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, yeṣāṃ kalpānāṃ na śakyaṃ gaṇanayā paryanto 'dhigantum | tāvadasaṃkhyeyāni tāni kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi tasya bhagavata āyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | yāvacca ānanda tasya bhagavataḥ sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, taddviguṇaṃ parinirvṛtasya saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | yāvāṃstasya bhagavataḥ saddharmaḥ sthāsyati, taddviguṇaḥ saddharmapratirūpakaṃ sthāsyati | tasya khalu punarānanda sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñasya tathāgatasya daśasu dikṣu bahūni gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi varṇaṃ bhāṣiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'You, <s>Ānanda</s>, shall become in a future age a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s> (One Whose Superknowledge Plays with the Wisdom of the Foremost Ocean-Bearer), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. Having performed honor to sixty-two <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, having performed respect, reverence, and worship, having upheld the true <s>Dharma</s> of those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, and having maintained their teaching, you shall attain supreme perfect awakening. You, <s>Ānanda</s>, having attained supreme perfect awakening, shall ripen twenty times the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> River in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> for supreme perfect awakening. Your <s>buddhakṣetra</s> shall be prosperous and made of <s>vaidūrya</s>. That world-system shall be named <s>Anavanāmitavaijayantī</s> (Unbowed Victory-Banner). That <s>kalpa</s> shall be named <s>Manojñaśabdābhigarjita</s> (Thundering with Pleasing Sound). The lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, shall be immeasurable <s>kalpas</s>, whose end cannot be reached by counting — so innumerable shall be those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> as the lifespan of that Blessed One. And, <s>Ānanda</s>, for however long the lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One shall be, the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for twice that long after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. And for however long the true <s>Dharma</s> of that Blessed One shall endure, the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for twice that. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s> shall be praised by many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, in the ten directions.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

body.text: ārocayāmi ahu bhikṣusaṃghe ānandabhadro mama dharmadhārakaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'I declare to the assembly of monks: <s>Ānandabhadra</s> (the auspicious <s>Ānanda</s>), my <s>Dharma</s>-bearer,

body.text: anāgate 'dhvāni jino bhaviṣyati pūjitva ṣaṣṭiṃ sugatāna koṭyaḥ // Saddhp_9.1 //
body.translated_text: shall become a <s>Jina</s> in a future age, having worshipped sixty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Sugatas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.1 ||

children.text: nāmena so sāgarabuddhidhārī abhijñaprāpto iti tatra viśrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: By name he shall be <s>Sāgarabuddhidhārī</s> (Bearer of Ocean-Wisdom), having attained <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge), renowned there,

children.text: pariśuddhakṣetrasmi sudarśanīye anonatāyāṃ dhvajavaijayantyām // Saddhp_9.2 //
children.translated_text: in a completely pure field, beautiful to behold, [a world-system named] <s>Anonatā Dhvajavaijayantyām</s> (Unbowed Victory-Banner). || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.2 ||

children.text: tahi bodhisattvā yathā gaṅgavālikāstataśca bhūyo paripācayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: There <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [shall be as numerous] as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and he shall ripen even more than those;

children.text: maharddhikaśco sa jino bhaviṣyati daśaddiśe lokavighuṣṭaśabdaḥ // Saddhp_9.3 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Jina</s> shall be of great miraculous power, his fame resounding in the ten directions throughout the world. || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.3 ||

children.text: amitaṃ ca tasyāyu tadā bhaviṣyati yaḥ sthāsyate lokahitānukampakaḥ /
children.translated_text: His lifespan then shall be immeasurable — he shall abide with compassion for the welfare of the world;

children.text: parinirvṛtasyāpi jinasya tāyino dviguṇaṃ ca saddharmu sa tasya sthāsyati // Saddhp_9.4 //
children.translated_text: and after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Jina</s>, the Protector, the true <s>Dharma</s> shall endure for twice [his lifespan]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.4 ||

children.text: pratirūpakaṃ taddviguṇena bhūyaḥ saṃsthāsyate tasya jinasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: The semblance [of the <s>Dharma</s>] shall endure for twice more in the teaching of that <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: tadāpi sattvā yathā gaṅgavālikā hetuṃ janeṣyantiha buddhabodhau // Saddhp_9.5 //
children.translated_text: and even then, beings [as numerous] as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> shall generate the cause for <s>Buddha</s>-awakening here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.5 ||'

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ parṣadi navayānasaṃprasthitānāmaṣṭānāṃ bodhisattvasahasrāṇāmetadabhavat - na bodhisattvānāmapi tāvadasmābhirevamudāraṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutapūrvam, kaḥ punarvādaḥ śrāvakāṇām? kaḥ khalvatra heturbhaviṣyati, kaḥ pratyaya iti? atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥ parivitarkamājñāya tān bodhisattvānāmantrayāmāsa - samamasmābhiḥ kulaputrā ekakṣaṇe ekamuhūrte mayā ca ānandena ca anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpāditaṃ dharmagaganābhyudgatarājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya saṃmukham | tatraiṣa kulaputrā bāhuśrutye ca satatasamitamabhiyukto 'bhūt, ahaṃ ca vīryārambhe 'bhiyuktaḥ | tena mayā kṣiprataramanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā | ayaṃ punarānandabhadro buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ saddharmakośadhara eva bhavati sma - yaduta bodhisattvānāṃ pariniṣpattihetoḥ praṇidhānametatkulaputrā asya kulaputrasyeti ||
body.translated_text: Then, in that assembly, the eight thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had newly set forth on the Vehicle had this thought: "We have never before heard even of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> receiving such an exalted prophecy, let alone <s>Śrāvakas</s>! What will be the cause here, what the condition?" Then the Blessed One, knowing the mental deliberation of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with his own mind, addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: "Together with us, O sons of good family, at the same instant, at the same moment, both I and <s>Ānanda</s> generated the thought of supreme perfect awakening in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Dharmagaganābhyudgatarāja</s>. Therein, O sons of good family, this one was constantly and continuously devoted to great learning, while I was devoted to the exertion of vigor. Therefore I attained supreme perfect awakening more quickly. But this worthy <s>Ānanda</s> was always the guardian of the treasury of the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones — that is, for the purpose of the complete development of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. This, O sons of good family, was the vow of this son of good family."

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānando bhagavato 'ntikādātmano vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, ātmanaśca buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān śrutvā, pūrvapraṇidhānacaryāṃ ca śrutvā, tuṣṭa udagra āttamanaskaḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto 'bhūt | tasmiṃśca samaye bahūnāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ saddharmamanusmarati sma, ātmanaśca purvapraṇidhānam ||
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having heard his own prophecy from the Blessed One regarding supreme perfect awakening, and having heard of the excellent qualities and adornments of his own <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (Buddha-field), and having heard of his former vow and conduct, was satisfied, elated, uplifted, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness. And at that time, he remembered the true <s>Dharma</s> of many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and his own former vow.

body.text: atha khalvāyuṣmānānandastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: āścaryabhūtā jina aprameyā ye smārayanti mama dharmadeśanām /
children.translated_text: Wondrous are the <s>Jinas</s>, immeasurable, who remind me of the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching;

children.text: parinirvṛtānāṃ hi jināna tāyināṃ samanusmarāmī yatha adya śvo vā // Saddhp_9.6 //
children.translated_text: I remember the true <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Jinas</s>, the Protectors, who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, as if it were today or yesterday! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.6 ||

children.text: niṣkāṅkṣaprāpto 'smi sthito 'smi bodhaye upāyakauśalya mamedamīddaśam /
children.translated_text: I have become free from doubt, I am established in awakening; such is my skill in means —

children.text: paricārako 'haṃ sugatasya bhomi saddharma dhāremi ca bodhikāraṇāt // Saddhp_9.7 //
children.translated_text: I am a servant of the <s>Sugata</s>, and I uphold the true <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.7 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānāyuṣmantaṃ rāhulabhadramāmantrayate sma - bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ rāhulabhadra anāgate 'dhvani saptaratnapadmavikrāntagāmī nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān daśalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā arcayitvā | sadā teṣāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ jyeṣṭhaputro bhaviṣyasi tadyathāpi nāma mamaitarhi | tasya khalu punā rāhulabhadra bhagavataḥ saptaratnapadmavikrāntagāminastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya evaṃrūpamevāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati, evaṃ rūpaiva sarvākāraguṇasaṃpad bhaviṣyati tadyathāpi nāma tasya bhagavataḥ sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sarvākāraguṇopetā buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā bhaviṣyanti | tasyāpi rāhula sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tvameva jyeṣṭhaputro bhaviṣyasi | tataḥ paścāt pareṇānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyasīti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>: "You, <s>Rāhulabhadra</s>, in the future, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Saptaratnapadmavikrāntagāmin</s> (He Who Treads on Lotuses of Seven Jewels), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, having honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, and venerated <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones equal in number to the atoms of dust of ten world-systems. You will always be the eldest son of those <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, just as you are now of me. And the lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Saptaratnapadmavikrāntagāmin</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, will be of just such a measure, and his perfection of all qualities will be of just such a form, as the excellent qualities and adornments of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the Blessed One <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with all manner of qualities. And of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sāgaravaradharabuddhivikrīḍitābhijña</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, you, <s>Rāhula</s>, will be the eldest son. Thereafter, you will attain supreme perfect awakening."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: ayaṃ mamā rāhula jyeṣṭhaputro yo auraso āsi kumārabhāve /
children.translated_text: This <s>Rāhula</s> is my eldest son, who was my own [son] in his princely youth;

children.text: bodhiṃ pi prāptasya mamaiṣa putro dharmasya dāyādyadharo maharṣiḥ // Saddhp_9.8 //
children.translated_text: even after I attained awakening, he is [still] my son — a great sage, heir and bearer of the <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.8 ||

children.text: anāgate 'dhve bahubuddhakoṭyo yān drakṣyase yeṣa pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: In the future, many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, whose number is without measure, you shall behold;

children.text: sarveṣa teṣāṃ hi jināna putro bhaviṣyatī bodhi gaveṣamāṇaḥ // Saddhp_9.9 //
children.translated_text: of all those <s>Jinas</s>, he will be the son, seeking awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.9 ||

children.text: ajñātacaryā iya rāhulasya praṇidhānametasya ahaṃ prajānami /
children.translated_text: Unknown is this conduct of <s>Rāhula</s> — but I know his vow;

children.text: karoti saṃvarṇana lokabandhuṣu ahaṃ kilā putra tathāgatasya // Saddhp_9.10 //
children.translated_text: he proclaims the praise of the Kinsmen of the World: "I am indeed the son of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!" || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.10 ||

children.text: guṇāna koṭīnayutāprameyāḥ pramāṇu yeṣāṃ na kadācidasti /
children.translated_text: <s>Koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of qualities, immeasurable, whose measure is never [exhausted] —

children.text: ye rāhulasyeha mamaurasatya tathā hi eṣo sthitu bodhikāraṇāt // Saddhp_9.11 //
children.translated_text: these belong to <s>Rāhula</s>, my own [son]; for thus he is established for the sake of awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.11 ||

body.text: adrākṣītkhalu punarbhagavāṃste dve śrāvakasahasre śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ bhagavantamavalokayamāne abhimukhaṃ prasannacitte mṛducitte mārdavacitte | atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmāyuṣmantamānandamāmantrayate sma - paśyasi tvamānanda ete dve śrāvakasahasre śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ śrāvakāṇām? āha - paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata | bhagavānāha - sarva evaite ānanda dve bhikṣu sahasre samaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ samudānayiṣyanti, pañcāśallokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāṃśca buddhān bhagavataḥ satkṛtya gurukṛtya mānayitvā pūjayitvā arcayitvā apacāyitvā saddharma ca dhārayitvā paścime samucchraye ekakṣaṇenaikamuhūrtenaikalavenaikasaṃnipātena daśasu dikṣvanyonyāsu lokadhātuṣu sveṣu sveṣu buddhakṣetreṣvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbhotsyante | ratnaketurājā nāma tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bhaviṣyanti | paripūrṇaṃ caiṣāṃ kalpamāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | samāścaiṣāṃ buddhakṣetraguṇavyūhā bhaviṣyanti | samaḥ śrāvakagaṇo bodhisattvagaṇaśca bhaviṣyati | samaṃ caiṣāṃ parinirvāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | samaścaiṣāṃ saddharmaḥ sthāsyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One beheld those two thousand <s>Śrāvakas</s>, both trainees and those beyond training, who were looking toward the Blessed One with serene, gentle, and tender minds. Then the Blessed One, at that time, addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Do you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, these two thousand <s>Śrāvakas</s>, both trainees and those beyond training?" He said: "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, <s>Sugata</s>." The Blessed One said: "All these, <s>Ānanda</s>, these two thousand monks, having equally fulfilled the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-practice, and having honored, revered, esteemed, worshipped, venerated, and paid respect to <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, equal in number to the atoms of dust of fifty world-systems, and having upheld the true <s>Dharma</s>, in their final rising, at the same instant, at the same moment, at the same time, at the same gathering, in the ten directions, in their respective <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in different world-systems, they will all attain supreme perfect awakening. They will be <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones named <s>Ratnaketurāja</s> (King of Jewel Banners). Their lifespan will be a full <s>kalpa</s>. The excellent qualities and adornments of their <s>buddhakṣetras</s> will be equal. Their assemblies of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> will be equal. Their <s>parinirvāṇa</s> will be at the same time. And their true <s>Dharma</s> will endure equally."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: dve vai sahasre ime śrāvakāṇāṃ ānanda ye te mama agrataḥ sthitāḥ /
children.translated_text: These two thousand <s>Śrāvakas</s>, O <s>Ānanda</s>, who stand before me,

children.text: tān vyākaromī ahamadya paṇḍitānanāgate 'dhvāni tathāgatatve // Saddhp_9.12 //
children.translated_text: I prophesy for them today, the wise ones — in the future they shall attain <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.12 ||

children.text: ananta aupamyanidarśanehi buddhāna agryāṃ kariyāṇa pūjām /
children.translated_text: With infinite incomparable illustrations, having made the supreme worship of <s>Buddhas</s>,

children.text: ārāgayiṣyanti mamāgrabodhiṃ sthihitva carimasmi samucchrayasmin // Saddhp_9.13 //
children.translated_text: they will reach my foremost awakening, abiding in their final rising! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.13 ||

body.text: ekena nāmena daśaddiśāsu kṣaṇasmi ekasmi tathā muhūrte /
body.translated_text: With a single name, in the ten directions, at one instant, at one moment,

body.text: niṣadya ca drumapravarāṇa mūle buddhā bhaviṣyanti spṛśitva jñānam // Saddhp_9.14 //
body.translated_text: seated at the feet of the most excellent trees, they will become <s>Buddhas</s>, having touched knowledge! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.14 ||

children.text: ekaṃ ca teṣāmiti nāma bheṣyati ratnasya ketūtiha loki viśrutāḥ /
children.translated_text: One and the same name shall be theirs — "Banner of Jewels" — renowned in this world;

children.text: samāni kṣetrāṇi varāṇi teṣāṃ samo gaṇaḥ śrāvakabodhisattvāḥ // Saddhp_9.15 //
children.translated_text: equal and excellent will be their fields, equal their assemblies of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.15 ||

children.text: ṛddhiprabhūtā iha sarvi loke samantataste daśasu ddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: Mighty in supernatural power, all of them in this world, in all the ten directions,

children.text: dharmaṃ prakāśetva yadāpi nirvṛtāḥ saddharmu teṣāṃ samameva sthāsyati // Saddhp_9.16 //
children.translated_text: having illuminated the <s>Dharma</s> and then attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s> of all of them will endure equally! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.16 ||

body.text: atha khalu te śaikṣāśaikṣāḥ śrāvakā bhagavato 'ntikāt saṃmukhaṃ svāni svāni vyākaraṇāni śrutvā tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanaskāḥ pramuditāḥ prītisaumanasyajātā bhagavantaṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Śrāvakas</s>, both trainees and those beyond training, having heard their own respective prophecies face to face from the Blessed One, were satisfied, elated, uplifted, joyful, and filled with delight and happiness, and they addressed the Blessed One with two verses —

children.text: tṛptāḥ sma lokapradyota śrutvā vyākaraṇaṃ idam /
children.translated_text: We are satisfied, O Illuminator of the World, having heard this prophecy;

children.text: amṛtena yathā siktāḥ sukhitāḥ sama tathāgata // Saddhp_9.17 //
children.translated_text: as if sprinkled with nectar, we are made happy, O <s>Tathāgata</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.17 ||

children.text: nāsmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vimatirna bheṣyāma narottamāḥ /
children.translated_text: We shall have no doubt or uncertainty, O Best of Men!

children.text: adyāsmābhiḥ sukhaṃ prāptaṃ śrutvā vyākaraṇaṃ idam // Saddhp_9.18 //
children.translated_text: Today we have obtained happiness, having heard this prophecy! || <s>Saddhp</s> 9.18 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye ānandarāhulābhyāmanyābhyāṃ ca dvābhyāṃ bhikṣusahasrābhyāṃ vyākaraṇaparivarto nāma navamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma), the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Prophecy Chapter for <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Rāhula</s>, and the Other Two Thousand Monks.

body.text: Saddhp_10: dharmabhāṇakaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 10: The Chapter on the Preachers of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavan bhaiṣajyarājaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamārabhya tānyaśītiṃ bodhisattvasahasrāṇyāmantrayate sma - paśyasi tvaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja asyāṃ parṣadi bahudevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyān bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ śrāvakayānīyān pratyekabuddhayāniyān bodhisattvayānīyāṃśca, yairayaṃ dharmaparyāyastathāgatasya saṃmukhaṃ śrutaḥ? āha - paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata | bhagavānāha - sarve svalvete bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, yairasyāṃ parṣadi antaśaḥ ekāpi gāthā śrutā, ekapadamapi śrutam, yairvā punarantaśa ekacittotpādenāpyanumoditamidaṃ sūtram | sarvā etā ahaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja catasraḥ parṣado vyākaromyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | ye 'pi kecid bhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti, antaśa ekagāthāmapi śrutvā, antaśa ekenāpi cittotpādena abhyamumodayiṣyanti, tānapyahaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputrān va kuladuhitṛrvā vyākaromyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | paripūrṇabuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraparyupāsitāvinaste bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā bhaiṣyanti | buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrakṛtapraṇidhānāste bhaiṣajyarājakulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā bhaviṣyanti | sattvānāmanukampārthamasmin jambudvīpe manuṣyeṣu pratyājātā veditavyāḥ, ya ito dharmaparyāyādantaśa ekagāthāmapi dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti prakāśayiṣyanti saṃgrāhayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti, likhitvā cānusmariṣyanti, kālena ca kālaṃ vyavalokayiṣyanti | tasmiṃśca pustake tathāgatagauravamutpādayiṣyanti, śāstṛgauraveṇa satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti | taṃ ca pustakaṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvādyādibhirnamaskārāñjalikarmabhiśca pūjayiṣyanti | ye kecid bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā ito dharmaparyāyādantaśa ekagāthāmapi dhārayiṣyanti anumodayiṣyanti vā, sarvāṃstānahaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja vyākaromyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, addressing the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> and those eighty thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, spoke thus: "Do you see, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, in this assembly the many gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, non-humans, monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>-followers, <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>-followers, and <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s>-followers, by whom this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) has been heard in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?" He said: "I see them, Blessed One; I see them, <s>Sugata</s>." The Blessed One said: "All these, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, are <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — those who in this assembly have heard even a single verse, or heard even a single word, or even those who have rejoiced in this <s>sūtra</s> with even a single arising of thought. All of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> — the fourfold assembly — I prophesy for supreme perfect awakening. And whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, and having heard even a single verse, will rejoice with even a single arising of thought — them too, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, whether sons or daughters of good family, I prophesy for supreme perfect awakening. Those sons or daughters of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, will have fully served many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. Those sons or daughters of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, will have made vows before many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. They should be understood as having been reborn among humans in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> out of compassion for beings — those who will uphold, recite, illuminate, collect, or write even a single verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, and having written it, will remember it, and will examine it from time to time. And in that manuscript they will generate reverence for the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and with respect for the Teacher, they will honor, revere, esteem, and worship it. And they will worship that manuscript with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, victory-standards, musical instruments, and with acts of homage and joined palms. Whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, whether sons or daughters of good family, will uphold even a single verse from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, or will rejoice in it — all of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, I prophesy for supreme perfect awakening."

body.text: tatra bhaiṣajyarāja yaḥ kaścidanyataraḥ puruṣo vā strī vā evaṃ vadet - kīdṛśāḥ khalvapi te sattvā bhaviṣyantyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā iti? tasya bhaiṣajyarāja puruṣasya vā striyā vā sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā darśayitavyaḥ, ya ito dharmaparyāyādantaśaścatuṣpādikāmapi gāthāṃ dhārayitā śrāvayitā vā deśayitā vā sagauravo veha dharmaparyāye | ayaṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, yo hyanāgate 'dhvani tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati | evaṃ paśya | tatkasya hetoḥ? sa hi bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā va tathāgato veditavyaḥ sadevakena lokena | tasya ca tathāgatasyaivaṃ satkāraḥ kartavyaḥ, yaḥ khalvasmāddharmaparyāyādantaśa ekagāthāmapi dhārayet, kaḥ punarvādo ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāpta mudgṛhṇīyād dhārayedvā vācayedvā paryavāpnuyādvā prakāśayedvā likhedvā likhāpayedvā, likhitvā cānusmaret | tatra ca pustake satkāraṃ kuryāt gurukāraṃ kuryāt mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvādyāñjalinamaskāraiḥ praṇāmaiḥ | pariniṣpannaḥ
body.translated_text: In this regard, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, if any man or woman should say: 'What kind of beings will become <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the future?' — to that man or woman, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family should be pointed out, who retains, recites, teaches, or shows reverence for even a single four-line verse from this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. This is the son of good family or daughter of good family who in the future will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One. See it thus! For what reason? That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be known as a <s>Tathāgata</s> by the world with its gods. And such honor should be rendered to that <s>Tathāgata</s> — one who retains even a single verse from this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — how much more so one who takes up, retains, recites, masters, illuminates, writes, or causes to be written this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse complete and whole, and who, having written it, remembers it, and performs honor to that book, performs reverence, respect, worship, veneration, and homage with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, music, salutations, and prostrations. Accomplished

body.text:
sa bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau veditavyaḥ | tathāgatadarśī ca veditavyaḥ | lokasya hitānukampakaḥ praṇidhānavaśenopapanno 'smin jambudvīpe manuṣyeṣu asya dharmaparyāyasya saṃprakāśanatāyaiḥ | yaḥ svayamudāraṃ dharmābhisaṃskāramudārāṃ ca buddhakṣetropapattiṃ sthāpayitvā asya dharmaparyāyasya saṃprakāśanahetormayi parinirvṛte sattvānāṃ hitārthamanukampārthaṃ ca ihopapanno veditavyaḥ | tathāgatadūtaḥ sa
