bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā veditavyaḥ | tathāgatakṛtyakarastathāgatasaṃpreṣitaḥ sa bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā saṃjñātavyaḥ, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya saṃprakāśayet, antaśo rahasi cauryeṇāpi kasyacidekasattvasyāpi saṃprakāśayedācakṣīta vā ||
body.translated_text: that son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be known as one who is accomplished in supreme perfect awakening, and should be known as one who has seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>, as one who is compassionate for the welfare of the world, born by the power of his vow in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> among humans, for the purpose of illuminating this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. One who, setting aside his own exalted <s>Dharma</s>-accumulation and exalted rebirth in a <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, has been born here after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> for the benefit and compassion of beings, for the purpose of illuminating this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — that son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be known as a messenger of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be understood as one who performs the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s work, one sent by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — one who, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, illuminates this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, even secretly, even stealthily to a single being, or declares it.

body.text: yaḥ khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja kaścideva sattvo duṣṭacittaḥ pāpacitto raudracittastathāgatasya saṃmukhaṃ kalpamavarṇaṃ bhāṣet, yaśca teṣāṃ tathārūpāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmasya sūtrāntasya dhārakāṇāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ vā pravrajitānāṃ vā ekāmapi vācamapriyāṃ saṃśrāvayed bhūtāṃ vā abhūtāṃ vā, ida māgāḍhataraṃ pāpakaṃ karmeti vadāmi | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathāgatabhāraṇapratimaṇḍitaḥ sa bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā veditavyaḥ | tathāgataṃ sa bhaiṣajyarāja aṃsena pariharati, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhitvā pustakagataṃ kṛtvā aṃsena pariharati | sa yena yenaiva prakrāmet, tena tenaiva sattvairañjalīkaraṇīyaḥ satkartavyo gurukartavyo mānayitavyaḥ pūjayitavyo 'rcayitavyo 'pacāyitavyo divyamānuṣyakaiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvādyakhādyabhojyānnapānayānairagraprāptaiśca divyai ratnarāśibhiḥ | sa dharmabhāṇakaḥ satkartavyo gurukartavyo mānayitavyaḥ pūjayitavyaḥ, divyāśca ratnarāśayastasya dharmabhāṇakasyopanāmayitavyāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? apyeva nāma ekavāramapi imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃśrāvayet, yaṃ śrutvā aprameyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ sattvāḥ kṣipramanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariniṣpadyeyuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, if any being with a hostile mind, an evil mind, a cruel mind, were to speak abuse of the <s>Tathāgata</s> face to face for a full <s>kalpa</s>, and another were to address even a single unpleasant word — whether true or false — to those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, holders of this <s>sūtra</s>, whether householders or renunciants, I declare this to be the more grievous evil deed. For what reason? That son of good family or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be known as one adorned with the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s adornments. He carries the <s>Tathāgata</s> on his shoulder, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, who, having written this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse and made it into a book, carries it on his shoulder. Wherever he goes, there beings should salute him with joined palms, honor him, revere him, respect him, worship him, venerate him, pay homage to him with divine and human flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, music, foods, drinks, meals, beverages, vehicles, and with the choicest divine heaps of jewels. That <s>Dharma</s>-preacher should be honored, revered, respected, and worshipped, and divine heaps of jewels should be offered to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher. For what reason? Because perhaps even by hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse just once, immeasurable, innumerable beings may swiftly be accomplished in supreme perfect awakening.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: buddhatve sthātukāmena svayaṃbhūjñānamicchatā /
children.translated_text: By one who wishes to abide in Buddhahood, who desires the knowledge of the Self-Existent,

children.text: satkartavyāśca te sattvā ye dhārenti imaṃ nayam // Saddhp_10.1 //
children.translated_text: those beings who uphold this teaching should be honored. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.1 ||

children.text: sarvajñatvaṃ ca yo icchet kathaṃ śīrghaṃ bhavediti /
children.translated_text: And whoever desires omniscience, [thinking] 'How may it quickly come to be?'

children.text: sa imaṃ dhārayet sūtraṃ satkuryādvāpi dhārakam // Saddhp_10.2 //
children.translated_text: he should uphold this <s>sūtra</s> or honor its upholder. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.2 ||

children.text: preṣito lokanāthena sattvavaineyakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: Sent by the Lord of the World for the sake of taming beings,

children.text: sattvānāmanukampārthaṃ sūtraṃ yo vācayedidam // Saddhp_10.3 //
children.translated_text: for the compassion of beings — he who recites this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.3 ||

children.text: upapattiṃ śūbhāṃ tyaktvā sa dhīra iha āgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned a blessed rebirth, that steadfast one has come here,

children.text: sattvānāmanukampārthaṃ sūtraṃ yo dhārayedidam // Saddhp_10.4 //
children.translated_text: for the compassion of beings — he who upholds this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.4 ||

children.text: upapatti vaśā tasya yena so dṛśyate tahi /
children.translated_text: By the power of his [chosen] rebirth, he appears there,

children.text: paścime kāli bhāṣanto idaṃ sūtraṃ niruttaram // Saddhp_10.5 //
children.translated_text: in the final age, teaching this unsurpassed <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.5 ||

children.text: divyehi puṣpehi ca satkareta mānuṣyakaiścāpi hi sarvagandhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: With divine flowers one should honor him, and with all human perfumes too,

children.text: divyehi vastrehi ca chādayeyā ratnehi abhyokiri dharmabhāṇakam // Saddhp_10.6 //
children.translated_text: with divine garments one should cover him, and shower the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher with jewels. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.6 ||

children.text: kṛtāñjalī tasya bhaveta nityaṃ yathā jinendrasya svayaṃbhuvastathā /
children.translated_text: One should always stand before him with joined palms, as before the Self-Existent Lord of <s>Jinas</s> —

children.text: yaḥ paścime kāli subhairave 'smin parinirvṛtasya ida sutra dhārayet // Saddhp_10.7 //
children.translated_text: whoever, in the final age, in this fearsome [time], upholds this <s>sūtra</s> of the one who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.7 ||

children.text: khādyaṃ ca bhojyaṃ ca tathānnapānaṃ vihāraśayyāsanavastrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Foods and meals, and likewise drinks, lodgings, beds, seats, and <s>koṭis</s> of garments

children.text: dadeya pūjārtha jinātmajasya apyekavāraṃ pi vadeta sūtram // Saddhp_10.8 //
children.translated_text: one should give for the worship of the son of the <s>Jina</s> — even if he teaches the <s>sūtra</s> but once. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.8 ||

children.text: tathāgatānāṃ karaṇīya kurvate mayā ca so preṣita mānuṣaṃ bhavam /
children.translated_text: He performs the work of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and has been sent by me to the human realm —

children.text: yaḥ sūtrametaccarimasmi kāle likheya dhāreya śruṇeya vāpi // Saddhp_10.9 //
children.translated_text: whoever, in this final age, would write, uphold, or hear this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.9 ||

children.text: yaścaiva sthitveha jinasya saṃmukhaṃ śrāvedavarṇaṃ paripūrṇakalpam /
children.translated_text: And whoever, standing face to face with the <s>Jina</s>, would speak abuse for a full <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: praduṣṭacitto bhṛkuṭiṃ karitvā bahuṃ naro 'sau prasaveta pāpam // Saddhp_10.10 //
children.translated_text: with a hostile mind, knitting his brow — that man would produce much evil. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.10 ||

children.text: yaścāpi sūtrāntadharāṇa teṣāṃ prakāśayantāniha sūtrametat /
children.translated_text: But whoever, to those holders of the <s>sūtra</s>, who illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> here,

children.text: avarṇamākrośa vadeya teṣāṃ bahūtaraṃ tasya vadāmi pāpam // Saddhp_10.11 //
children.translated_text: would speak abuse and reproach to them — I declare his evil to be far greater. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.11 ||

children.text: naraśca yo saṃmukha saṃstaveyā kṛtāñjalī māṃ paripūrṇakalpam /
children.translated_text: And the man who, face to face, would praise me with joined palms for a full <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: gāthāna koṭīnayutairanekaiḥ paryeṣamāṇo imamagrabodhim // Saddhp_10.12 //
children.translated_text: with many <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of verses, seeking this supreme awakening — || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.12 ||

body.text: bahuṃ khu so tatra labheta puṇyaṃ māṃ saṃstavitvāna praharṣajātaḥ /
body.translated_text: he indeed would obtain much merit thereby, having praised me, filled with joy;

body.text: ataśca so bahutarakaṃ labheta yo varṇa teṣāṃ pravadenmanuṣyaḥ // Saddhp_10.13 //
body.translated_text: but far greater [merit] would that man obtain who speaks praise of those [preachers]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.13 ||

children.text: aṣṭādaśa kalpasahasrakoṭyo yasteṣu pusteṣu karoti pūjām /
children.translated_text: For eighteen thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, whoever performs worship to those books,

children.text: śabdehi rūpehi rasehi cāpi divyaiśca gandhaiśca sparśaiśca divyaiḥ // Saddhp_10.14 //
children.translated_text: with sounds and forms and tastes, and with divine perfumes and divine touches — || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.14 ||

children.text: karitva pustāna tathaiva pūjāṃ aṣṭādaśa kalpasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: having performed such worship to the books for eighteen thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: yadi śruṇo ekaśa eta sūtraṃ āścaryalābho 'sya bhavenmahāniti // Saddhp_10.15 //
children.translated_text: if he then hears this <s>sūtra</s> even once — his gain would be marvelous and great! || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.15 ||

body.text: ārocayāmi te bhaiṣajyarāja, prativedayāmi te | bahavo hi mayā bhaiṣajyarāja dharmaparyāyā bhāṣitāḥ, bhāṣāmi bhāṣiṣye ca | sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ bhaiṣajyarāja dharmaparyāyāṇāmayameva dharmaparyāyaḥ sarvalokavipratyanīkaḥ sarvalokāśraddadhanīyaḥ | tathāgatasyāpyetad bhaiṣajyarāja ādhyātmikadharmarahasyaṃ tathāgatabalasaṃrakṣitamapratibhinnapūrvamanācakṣitapūrvamanākhyātamidaṃ sthānam | bahujanapratikṣipto 'yaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja dharmaparyāyastiṣṭhato 'pi tathāgatasya, kaḥ punarvādaḥ parinirvṛtasya ||
body.translated_text: I announce to you, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, I declare to you: many <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, have been taught by me, are being taught, and will be taught. And among all those <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, this very <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is opposed by the entire world, disbelieved by the entire world. This, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the innermost secret of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharma</s>, guarded by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s power, never before penetrated, never before declared, never before proclaimed. This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is rejected by the many even while the <s>Tathāgata</s> is present — how much more so after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!

body.text: api tu khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatacīvaracchannāste kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā veditavyāḥ | anyalokadhātusthitaiśca tathāgatairavalokitāśca adhiṣṭhitāśca | pratyātmikaṃ ca teṣāṃ śraddhābalaṃ bhaviṣyati, kuśalamūlabalaṃ ca praṇidhānabalaṃ ca | tathāgatavihāraikasthānanivāsinaśca te bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā bhaviṣyanti, tathāgatapāṇiparimārjitamūrdhānaśca te bhaviṣyanti, ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya śraddadhiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti likhiṣyanti satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti pareṣāṃ ca saṃśrāvayiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, those sons of good family or daughters of good family should be known as covered by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s robe, as watched over and sustained by <s>Tathāgatas</s> dwelling in other world-systems. And they will possess the power of personal faith, the power of roots of merit, and the power of vows. Those sons of good family or daughters of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, will dwell together with the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the same abode, and will have their heads stroked by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s hand — those who, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will have faith in, recite, write, honor, revere, and proclaim to others this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: yasmin khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja pṛthivīpradeśe 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhāṣyeta vā deśyeta vā likhyeta vā svādhyāyeta vā saṃgāyeta vā, tasmin bhaiṣajyarāja pṛthivīpradeśe tathāgatacaityaṃ kārayitavyaṃ mahantaṃ ratnamayamuccaṃ pragṛhītam | na ca tasminnavaśyaṃ tathāgataśarīrāṇi pratiṣṭhāpayitavyāni | tatkasya hetoḥ? ekaghanameva tasmiṃstathāgataśarīramupanikṣiptaṃ bhavati, yasmin pṛthivīpradeśe 'yaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhāṣyeta vā deśyeta vā paṭhyeta vā saṃgāyeta vā likhyeta vā likhito vā pustakagatastiṣṭhet | tasmiṃśca stūpe satkāro gurukāro mānanā pūjanā arcanā karaṇīyā sarvapuṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantībhiḥ | sarvagītavādyanṛtyatūryatālāvacarasaṃgītisaṃpravāditaiḥ pūjā karaṇīyā | ye ca khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja sattvāstaṃ tathāgatacaityaṃ labheran vandanāya pūjanāya darśanāya vā, sarve te bhaiṣajyarāja abhyāsannībhūtā veditavyā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? bahavo bhaiṣajyarāja gṛhasthāḥ pravrajitāśca
body.translated_text: Moreover, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, in whatever place on earth this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is spoken, taught, written, studied, or chanted, in that place, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine should be erected — great, made of jewels, lofty, and grand. And it is not necessary to place <s>Tathāgata</s>-relics therein. For what reason? Because in that place on earth where this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is spoken, taught, recited, chanted, written, or stands written in a book, there the entire body of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is deposited. And that <s>stūpa</s> should be honored, revered, respected, worshipped, and venerated with all flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-standards. Worship should be performed with all songs, instrumental music, dances, drums, rhythmic accompaniments, and musical ensembles. And those beings, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, who might come to that <s>Tathāgata</s>-shrine for salutation, worship, or viewing — all of them, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be known as having drawn near to supreme perfect awakening. For what reason? Many, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, householders and renunciants

body.text: bodhisattvacaryāṃ caranti, na ca punarimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ labhante darśanāya vā śravaṇāya vā likhanāya vā pūjanāya vā | na tāvatte bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ kuśalā bhavanti, yāvannemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇvanti | ye tvimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇvanti, śrutvā cādhimucyanti avataranti vijānanti parigṛhṇanti, tasmin samaye te āsannasthāyino bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, abhyāśībhūtāḥ ||
body.translated_text: practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, yet do not obtain this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse for seeing, hearing, writing, or worshipping. Those [practitioners], <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, are not yet skilled in the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct so long as they do not hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. But those who hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and having heard it, believe in it, penetrate it, understand it, and embrace it — at that moment they will stand close to supreme perfect awakening, having drawn near [to it].

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhaiṣajyarāja kaścideva puruṣo bhavedudakārthī udakagaveṣī | sa udakārthamujjaṅgale pṛthivīpradeśe udapānaṃ khānayet | sa yāvat paśyecchuṣkaṃ pāṇḍaraṃ pāṃsuṃ nirvāhyamānam, tāvajjānīyāt, dūra itastāvadūdakamiti | atha pareṇa samayena sa puruṣa ārdrapaṃsumudakasaṃniśraṃ kardamapaṅkabhutamudakabindubhiḥ sravadbhirnirvāhyamānaṃ paśyet, tāṃśca puruṣānudapānakhānakān kardamapaṅkadigdhāṅgān, atha khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja sa puruṣastatpūrvanimittaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣkāṅkṣo bhavennirvicikitsaḥ - āsannamidaṃ khalūdakamiti | evameva bhaiṣajyarāja dūre te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yāvannemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇvanti, nodgṛhṇanti nāvataranti nāvagāhante na cintayanti | yadā khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇvanti udgṛhṇanti dhārayanti vācayanti avataranti svādhyāyanti cintayanti bhavayanti, tadā te 'bhyāśībhūtā bhaviṣyantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | sattvānāmito bhaiṣajyarāja dharmaparyāyādanuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirājāyate | tatkasya hetoḥ? paramasaṃdhābhāṣitavivaraṇo hyayaṃ dharmaparyāyastathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ | dharmanigūḍhasthānamākhyātaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pariniṣpattihetoḥ | yaḥ kaścid bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvo 'sya dharmaparyāyasyotraset saṃtraset saṃtrāsamāpadyet, navayānasaṃprasthitaḥ sa bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvo mahāsattvo veditavyaḥ | sacet punaḥ śrāvakayānīyo 'sya dharmaparyāyasyotraset saṃtraset saṃtrāsamāpadyeta, adhimānikaḥ sa bhaiṣajyarāja śrāvakayānikaḥ pudgalo veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Just as, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, some man might be thirsty, seeking water. He would dig a well on arid ground for the sake of water. As long as he sees dry, white dust being brought up, so long he would know: 'Water is still far from here.' But then, at another time, that man would see moist soil, water-soaked, with mud and clay, with drops of water dripping as it is brought up, and those men who dig the well with their limbs smeared with mud and clay. Then, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, that man, having seen these preliminary signs, would become free from doubt and uncertainty: 'Water is indeed near!' Even so, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> are far from supreme perfect awakening so long as they do not hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, do not receive it, do not penetrate it, do not plunge into it, do not contemplate it. But when, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, receive it, retain it, recite it, penetrate it, study it, contemplate it, and cultivate it, then they will be near to supreme perfect awakening. From this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, supreme perfect awakening arises for beings. For what reason? Because this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> is the supreme revelation of the indirect teaching by the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. It declares the hidden ground of the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of the complete perfection of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is frightened, terrified, or falls into alarm at this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be understood as one who has newly set out on the [<s>Bodhisattva</s>] vehicle. And if a follower of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle is frightened, terrified, or falls into alarm at this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, that person following the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, should be understood as one of inflated pride.

body.text: yaḥ kaścid bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle paścime samaye imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃprakāśayet, tena bhaiṣajyarāja bodhisattvena mahāsattvena tathāgatalayanaṃ praviśya tathāgatacīvaraṃ prāvṛtya tathāgatasyāsane niṣadya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | katamaśca bhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatalayanam? sarvasattvamaitrīvihāraḥ svalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatalayanam | tatra tena kulaputreṇa praveṣṭavyam | katamacca bhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatacīvaram? mahākṣāntisauratyaṃ khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatacīvaram | tattena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā prāvaritavyam | katamacca bhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatasya dharmāsanam? sarvadharmaśūnyatāpraveśaḥ khalu punarbhaiṣajyarāja tathāgatasya dharmāsanam | tatra tena kulaputreṇa niṣattavyam, niṣadya cāyaṃ dharmaparyāyaścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | anavalīnacittena bodhisattvena purastādbodhisattvagaṇasya bodhisattvayānasaṃprasthitānāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | anyalokadhātusthitaścāhaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja tasya kulaputrasya nirmitaiḥ
body.translated_text: Whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who, in the last time, the last period after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, will illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> for the four assemblies — that <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, having entered the abode of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having put on the robe of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and having sat upon the seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, should illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> for the four assemblies. And what, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the abode of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? The dwelling in loving-kindness toward all beings — that, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the abode of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. There that son of good family should enter. And what, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the robe of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? Great patience and gentleness — that, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the robe of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. That, that son or daughter of good family should put on. And what, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s>? The entry into the emptiness of all <s>dharmas</s> — that, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, is the <s>Dharma</s>-seat of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. There that son of good family should sit, and having sat, should illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> for the four assemblies. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with unshrunken mind, should illuminate it before the assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the four assemblies who have set forth on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle. And I, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, even while abiding in another world-system, will bring to that son of good family, by means of emanations —

body.text: parṣadaḥ samāvartayiṣyāmi | nirmitāṃśca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ saṃpreṣayiṣyāmi dharmaśravaṇāya | te tasya dharmabhāṇakasya bhāṣitaṃ na pratibādhiṣyanti, na pratikṣepsyanti | sacetkhalu punararaṇyagato bhaviṣyati, tatrāpyahamasya bahudevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragān saṃpreṣayiṣyāmi dharmaśravaṇāya | anyalokadhātusthitaścāhaṃ bhaiṣajyarāja tasya kulaputrasya mukhamupadarśayiṣyāmi | yāni ca asya asmāddharmaparyāyāt padavyañjanāni paribhraṣṭāni bhaviṣyanti, tāni tasya svādhyāyataḥ pratyuccārayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: — assemblies. And I will send emanated monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. They will not obstruct or reject the words of that Dharma-preacher. And if he should be dwelling in the wilderness, there too I will send to him many gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, and <s>mahoragas</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. And I, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, while abiding in another world-system, will show my face to that son of good family. And whatever words and syllables from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> he may have lost, those I will prompt him to utter correctly while he is reciting.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: līyanāṃ sarva varjitvā śṛṇuyāt sūtramīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned all laziness, one should hear a <s>sūtra</s> such as this;

children.text: durlabho vai śravo hyasya adhimuktī pi durlabhā // Saddhp_10.16 //
children.translated_text: for rare indeed is the hearing of it, and faith in it is also rare. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.16 ||

children.text: udakārthī yathā kaścit khānayet kūpa jaṅgale /
children.translated_text: Just as one seeking water would dig a well on barren ground,

children.text: śuṣkaṃ ca pāṃsu paśyeta khānyamāne punaḥ punaḥ // Saddhp_10.17 //
children.translated_text: and would see dry dust as it is dug, again and again — || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.17 ||

children.text: so dṛṣṭvā cintayettatra dūre vāri ito bhavet /
children.translated_text: seeing that, he would think there: 'Water must be far from here;'

children.text: idaṃ nimittaṃ dūre syāt śuṣkapāṃsuritotsṛtaḥ // Saddhp_10.18 //
children.translated_text: this is the sign that it is distant — dry dust issuing from here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.18 ||

children.text: yadā tu ārdraṃ paśyeta pāṃsuṃ snigdhaṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when he sees moist soil, moist and oily, again and again,

children.text: niṣṭhā tasya bhavettatra nāsti dūre jalaṃ iha // Saddhp_10.19 //
children.translated_text: he would have certainty there: 'Water is not far from here.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.19 ||

children.text: evameva tu te dūre buddhajñānasya tādṛśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, those who are far from <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge are of such a kind —

children.text: aśṛṇvanta idaṃ sūtramabhāvitvā punaḥ punaḥ // Saddhp_10.20 //
children.translated_text: not hearing this <s>sūtra</s>, not cultivating it again and again. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.20 ||

children.text: yadā tu gambhīramidaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ viniścayam /
children.translated_text: But when they hear this profound [<s>sūtra</s>], the decisive [teaching] for <s>Śrāvakas</s>,

children.text: sūtrarājaṃ śruṇiṣyanti cintayiṣyanti vā sakṛt // Saddhp_10.21 //
children.translated_text: this king of <s>sūtras</s>, and contemplate it even once — || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.21 ||

children.text: te bhonti saṃnikṛṣṭā vai buddhajñānasya paṇḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: those wise ones are indeed near to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge,

children.text: yathaiva cārdre pāṃsusmin āsannaṃ jalamucyate // Saddhp_10.22 //
children.translated_text: just as when moist soil [is found], it is said that water is near. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.22 ||

children.text: jinasya lenaṃ praviśitvā prāvaritvā mi cīvaram /
children.translated_text: Having entered the abode of the <s>Jina</s>, having put on my robe,

children.text: mamāsane niṣīditvā abhīto bhāṣi paṇḍitaḥ // Saddhp_10.23 //
children.translated_text: having sat on my seat, the wise one should teach fearlessly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.23 ||

children.text: maitrībalaṃ ca layanaṃ kṣāntisauratya cīvaram /
children.translated_text: The power of loving-kindness is the abode, patience and gentleness is the robe,

children.text: śūnyatā cāsanaṃ mahyamatra sthitvā hi deśayet // Saddhp_10.24 //
children.translated_text: and emptiness is my seat — established there, one should teach. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.24 ||

children.text: loṣṭaṃ daṇḍaṃ vātha śaktī ākrośa tarjanātha vā /
children.translated_text: If clods, sticks, or spears, or abuse and threats

children.text: bhāṣantasya bhavettatra smaranto mama tā sahet // Saddhp_10.25 //
children.translated_text: should befall the one who teaches — remembering me, one should endure them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.25 ||

children.text: kṣetrakoṭīsahasresu ātmabhāvo dṛḍho mama /
children.translated_text: In thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields, my form is firm;

children.text: deśemi dharma sattvānāṃ kalpakoṭīracintiyāḥ // Saddhp_10.26 //
children.translated_text: I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings for inconceivable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.26 ||

children.text: ahaṃ pi tasya vīrasya yo mahya parinirvṛte /
children.translated_text: I too [will help] that hero who, after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśeyā preṣeṣye bahu nirmitān // Saddhp_10.27 //
children.translated_text: illuminates this <s>sūtra</s> — I shall send many emanations. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.27 ||

children.text: bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇīyā ca upāsakā upāsikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen

children.text: tasya pūjāṃ kariṣyanti parṣadaśca samā api // Saddhp_10.28 //
children.translated_text: will perform worship for him, as well as equal assemblies. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.28 ||

children.text: loṣṭaṃ daṇḍāṃstathākrośāṃstarjanāṃ paribhāṣaṇām /
children.translated_text: And those who would hurl clods, sticks, abuse, threats, and harsh words

children.text: ye cāpi tasya dāsyanti vāreṣyanti sma nirmitāḥ // Saddhp_10.29 //
children.translated_text: at him — emanations will ward them off. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.29 ||

children.text: yadāpi caiko viharan svādhyāyanto bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And even when one is dwelling alone, reciting [this sūtra],

children.text: narairvirahite deśe aṭavyāṃ parvateṣu vā // Saddhp_10.30 //
children.translated_text: in a deserted place, in a wilderness or on mountains — || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.30 ||

children.text: tato 'sya ahaṃ darśiṣye ātmabhāva prabhāsvaram /
children.translated_text: then I shall show him my radiant form,

children.text: skhalitaṃ cāsya svādhyāyamuccāriṣye punaḥ punaḥ // Saddhp_10.31 //
children.translated_text: and when he stumbles in his recitation, I will correct it again and again. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.31 ||

children.text: tahiṃ ca sya viharato ekasya vanacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when he dwells there, wandering alone in the forest,

children.text: devān yakṣāṃśca preṣiṣye sahāyāṃstasya naikaśaḥ // Saddhp_10.32 //
children.translated_text: I will send gods and <s>yakṣas</s> as his numerous companions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.32 ||

children.text: etādṛśāstasya guṇā bhavanti caturṇa parṣāṇa prakāśakasya /
children.translated_text: Such are the merits of one who illuminates [this sūtra] before the four assemblies;

children.text: eko vihāre vanakandareṣu svādhyāya kurvantu mamāhi paśyet // Saddhp_10.33 //
children.translated_text: dwelling alone in a monastery or in forest caves, reciting, one should see me. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.33 ||

children.text: pratibhāna tasya bhavatī asaṅgaṃ nirukti dharmāṇa bahū prajānāti /
children.translated_text: His eloquence becomes unimpeded — he comprehends many etymologies and meanings of <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: toṣeti so prāṇisahasrakoṭyaḥ yathāpi buddhena adhiṣṭhitatvāt // Saddhp_10.34 //
children.translated_text: he delights thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of living beings, as if empowered by the <s>Buddha</s> himself. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.34 ||

children.text: ye cāpi tasyāśrita bhonti sattvāste bodhisattvā laghu bhonti sarve /
children.translated_text: And those beings who rely upon him — they all quickly become <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;

children.text: tatsaṃgatiṃ cāpi niṣevamāṇāḥ paśyanti buddhāna yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ // Saddhp_10.35 //
children.translated_text: and cultivating his companionship, they behold <s>Buddhas</s> [as numerous] as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 10.35 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye dharmabhāṇakaparivarto nāma daśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the tenth chapter, named 'The Chapter on Dharma-Preachers' (<s>Dharmabhāṇakaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_11: stūpasaṃdarśanaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 11: The Chapter on the Manifestation of the <s>Stūpa</s> (<s>Stūpasaṃdarśanaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavataḥ purastāttataḥ pṛthivīpradeśāt parṣanmadhyāt saptaratnamayaḥ stūpo 'bhyudgataḥ pañcayojanaśatānyuccaistvena tadanurūpeṇa ca pariṇāhena | abhyudgamya vaihāyasamantarīkṣe samavātiṣṭhaccitro darśanīyaḥ pañcabhiḥ puṣpagrahaṇīyavedikāsahasraiḥ svabhyalaṃkṛto bahutoraṇasahasraiḥ pratimaṇḍitaḥ patākāvaijayantīsahasrābhiḥ pralambito ratnadāmasahasrābhiḥ pralambitaḥ paṭṭaghaṇṭāsahasraiḥ pralambitaḥ tamālapatracandanagandhaṃ pramuñcamānaḥ | tena ca gandhena sarvāvatīyaṃ lokadhātuḥ saṃmūrcchitābhūt | chatrāvalī cāsya yāvaccāturmahārājakāyikadevabhavanāni samucchritābhūt saptaratnamayī, tadyathā - suvarṇasya rūpyasya vaiḍūryasya musāragalvasyāśmagarbhasya lohitamukteḥ karketanasya | tasmiṃśca stūpe trāyastriṃśatkāyikā devaputrā divyairmāndāravamahāmāndāravaiḥ puṣpaistaṃ ratnastūpamavakiranti adhyavakiranti abhiprakiranti | tasmācca ratnastūpādevaṃrūpaḥ śabdo niścarati sma - sādhu sādhu bhagavan śākyamune | subhāṣitaste 'yaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ | evametat bhagavan, evametat sugata ||
body.translated_text: Then, before the Blessed One, from that very spot of earth, from the midst of the assembly, a <s>stūpa</s> made of seven jewels rose up — five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height and of proportionate circumference. Having risen, it stood suspended in the sky, in mid-air, wonderful to behold, adorned with five thousand flower-receiving balustrades, beautified with many thousands of gateways, hung with thousands of pennants and victory-banners, draped with thousands of jewel garlands, draped with thousands of small bells with silken streamers, releasing the fragrance of <s>tamāla</s>-leaf sandalwood. And with that fragrance, this entire world-system was pervaded. Its row of parasols rose as high as the palaces of the <s>Cāturmahārājakāyika</s> gods, made of the seven jewels — namely, gold, silver, <s>vaidūrya</s>, <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), <s>aśmagarbha</s> (diamond), red pearl, and <s>karketana</s>. And at that <s>stūpa</s>, the sons of the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> heaven scattered and showered and rained down divine <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers upon that jeweled <s>stūpa</s>. And from that jeweled <s>stūpa</s> issued forth a voice of this kind: 'Excellent, excellent, O Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>! Well spoken is this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> of yours! So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu tāścatasraḥ parṣadastaṃ mahāntaṃ ratnastūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā vaihāyasamantarīkṣe sthitaṃ saṃjātaharṣāḥ prītiprāmodyaprasādaprāptāḥ tasyāṃ velāyāmutthāya āsanebhyo 'ñjaliṃ pragṛhyāvasthitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then those four assemblies, seeing that great jeweled <s>stūpa</s> standing suspended in mid-air, arose with joy, filled with delight, gladness, and serenity, and at that time stood up from their seats with palms joined.

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāpratibhāno nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sadevamānuṣāsuraṃ lokaṃ kautūhalaprāptaṃ viditvā bhagavantametadavocat - ko bhagavan hetuḥ, kaḥ pratyayaḥ, asyaivaṃrūpasya mahāratnastūpasya loke prādurbhāvāya? ko vā bhagavan asmānmahāratnastūpādevaṃrūpaṃ śabdaṃ niścārayati? evamukte bhagavān mahāpratibhānaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - asmin mahāpratibhāna mahāratnastūpe tathāgatasyātmabhāvastiṣṭhati ekaghanaḥ | tasyaiṣa stūpaḥ | sa eṣa śabdaṃ niścārayati | asti mahāpratibhāna adhastāyāṃ diśi asaṃkhyeyāni lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya ratnaviśuddhā nāma lokadhātuḥ | tasyāṃ prabhūtaratno nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'bhūt | tasyaitadbhagavataḥ purvapraṇidhānamabhūt - ahaṃ khalu pūrvaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caramāṇo na tāvanniryāto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, yāvanmayāyaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo bodhisattvāvavādo na śruto 'bhūt | yadā tu mayā ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ śrutaḥ, tadā paścādahaṃ pariniṣpanno 'bhūvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | tena khalu punarmahāpratibhāna bhagavatā prabhūtaratnena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena parinirvāṇakālasamaye sadevakasya lokasya samārakasya sabrahmakasya saśramaṇabrāhmaṇikāyāḥ prajāyāḥ purastādevamārocitam - mama khalu bhikṣavaḥ parinirvṛtasya asya tathāgatātmabhāvavigrahasya eko mahāratnastūpaḥ kartavyaḥ | śeṣāḥ punaḥ stūpā mamoddiśya kartavyāḥ | tasya khalu punarmahāpratibhāna bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyaitadadhiṣṭhānamabhūt - ayaṃ mama stūpo daśasu dikṣu sarvalokadhātuṣu yeṣu buddhakṣetreṣvayaṃ
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s> (Great Eloquence), knowing that the world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s> had become curious, said this to the Blessed One: 'What is the cause, O Blessed One, what is the condition for the appearance of this great jeweled <s>stūpa</s> in the world? And who, O Blessed One, utters such a sound from within this great jeweled <s>stūpa</s>?' Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>: 'In this great jeweled <s>stūpa</s>, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, there rests the body of a <s>Tathāgata</s>, entire and undivided. This is his <s>stūpa</s>. He is the one who utters that sound. There is, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, in the downward direction, beyond innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, a world-system called <s>Ratnaviśuddhā</s> (Jewel-Pure). In that world, there was a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> (Abundant Treasures). That Blessed One had this former vow: "While I was formerly practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, I shall not attain final accomplishment in supreme perfect awakening until I have heard this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. But when I have heard this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, then afterward I shall be fully accomplished in supreme perfect awakening." Furthermore, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, at the time of <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, announced before the world with its gods, its <s>Māras</s>, its <s>Brahmās</s>, and the multitude of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: "After my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O monks, one great jeweled <s>stūpa</s> should be made for the body of this <s>Tathāgata</s>. The remaining <s>stūpas</s> should be made in my name." Furthermore, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, made this resolution: "This <s>stūpa</s> of mine — in whatever <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions this

body.text:
saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ saṃprakāśyeta, teṣu teṣvayaṃ mamātmabhāvavigrahastūpaḥ samabhyudgacchet | taistairbuddhairbhagavadbhirasmin saddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe parṣanmaṇḍalasyopari vaihāyasaṃ tiṣṭhet | teṣāṃ ca buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmimaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣamāṇānāmayaṃ mamātmabhāvavigrahastūpaḥ sādhukāraṃ dadyāt | tadayaṃ mahāpratibhāna tasya bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya
tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya śarīrastūpaḥ | asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau asmin saddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye mayā bhāṣyamāṇe 'smāt parṣanmaṇḍalamadhyādabhyudgamya uparyantarīkṣe vaihāyasaṃ sthitvā sādhukāraṃ dadāti sma ||
body.translated_text: <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse is being proclaimed — in each of those, this <s>stūpa</s> containing my bodily remains shall arise. When those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, are teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, it shall stand suspended in the sky above the assembly. And to those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, while they are teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, this <s>stūpa</s> containing my bodily remains shall give its approval." Now this, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, is the bodily <s>stūpa</s> of that Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. While I am teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, it has arisen from the midst of this assembly, and standing suspended in the sky above, has given its approval.

body.text: atha khalu mahāpratibhāno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - paśyāma vayaṃ bhagavan etaṃ tathāgatavigrahaṃ bhagavato 'nubhāvena | evamukte bhagavān mahāpratibhānaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - tasya khalu punarmahāpratibhāna bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya praṇidhānaṃ gurukamabhūt | etadasya praṇidhānam - yadā khalvanyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu buddhā bhagavanta imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣeyuḥ, tadāyaṃ mamātmabhāvavigrahastūpo 'sya saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya śravaṇāya gacchet tathāgatānāmantikam | yadā punaste buddhā bhagavanto mamātmabhāvavigrahamuddhāṭya darśayitukāmā bhaveyuścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadām, atha taistathāgatairdaśasu dikṣvanyonyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu ya ātmabhāvanirmitāstathāgatavigrahā anyānyanāmadheyāḥ, teṣu teṣu buddhakṣetreṣu sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti, tān sarvān saṃnipātya tairātmabhāvanirmitaistathāgatavigrahaiḥ sārdhaṃ paścādayaṃ mamātmabhāvavigrahastūpaḥ samuddhāṭya upadarśayitavyaścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadām | tanmayāpi mahāpratibhāna bahavastathāgatavigrahā nirmitāḥ, ye daśasu dikṣvanyonyeṣu buddhakṣetreṣu lokadhātusahasreṣu sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti | te sarve khalvihānayitavyā bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Let us see, O Blessed One, the body of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, by the Blessed One's power.' Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>: 'The vow of that Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was a weighty one. This was his vow: "When <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> are teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, then this <s>stūpa</s> containing my bodily remains shall go to the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s> for the hearing of this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. But when those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, wish to open [this <s>stūpa</s>] and display my bodily form to the four assemblies, then those <s>Tathāgatas</s> must first gather together all the <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanations created from their own being, bearing various names, who are teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions. Only after gathering those emanation-<s>Tathāgatas</s> together should this <s>stūpa</s> containing my bodily remains be opened and displayed to the four assemblies." Therefore, O <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, I too have created many <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanations who are teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in other <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions, in thousands of world-systems. All of them must now be brought here.'

body.text: atha khalu mahāpratibhāno bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - tānapi tāvad bhagavaṃstathāgatātmabhāvāṃstathāgatanirmitān sarvān vandāmahai ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Let us indeed, O Blessed One, worship all those <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanations created by the <s>Tathāgata</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmūrṇākośādraśmiṃ prāmuñcat, yayā raśmyā samanantarapramuktayā pūrvasyāṃ diśi pañcāśatsu gaṅgānadīvālukāsameṣu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye buddhā bhagavanto viharanti sma, te sarve saṃdṛśyante sma | tāni ca buddhakṣetrāṇi sphaṭikamayāni saṃdṛśyante sma, ratnavṛkṣaiśca citrāṇi saṃdṛśyante sma, dūṣyapaṭṭadāmasamalaṃkṛtāni bahubodhisattvaśatasahasraparipūrṇāni vitānavitatāni saptaratnahemajālapraticchannāni | teṣu teṣu buddhā bhagavanto madhureṇa valgunā svareṇa sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayamānāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma | bodhisattvaśatasahasraiśca paripūrṇāni tāni buddhakṣetrāṇi saṃdṛśyante sma | evaṃ pūrvadakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi | evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi | evaṃ dakṣiṇapaścimāyāṃ diśi | evaṃ paścimāyāṃ diśi | evaṃ paścimottarāyāṃ diśi | evamuttarāyāṃ diśi | evamuttarapūrvasyāṃ diśi | evamadhastāyāṃ diśi | evamūrdhvāyāṃ diśi | evaṃ samantāddaśasu dikṣu ekaikasyāṃ diśi bahūni gaṅgānadīvālukopamāni buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bahuṣu gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye buddhā bhagavantastiṣṭhanti, te sarve saṃdṛśyante sma ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One at that time released a ray of light from his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows). As soon as that ray was released, in the eastern direction, in fifty <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, all the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who were dwelling [there] became visible. And those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> became visible, made of crystal, adorned with variegated jewel-trees, decorated with silk and cloth banners, filled with many hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, spread with canopies, covered with nets of golden threads and the seven jewels. In those [fields], the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, were seen teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings with sweet, melodious voices. And those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> were seen filled with hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Likewise in the east-southeastern direction, likewise in the southern direction, likewise in the southwestern direction, likewise in the western direction, likewise in the northwestern direction, likewise in the northern direction, likewise in the northeastern direction, likewise in the downward direction, likewise in the upward direction. Thus, on all sides in the ten directions, in each and every direction, many <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, in many <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-like <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, all the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, who dwell there became visible.

body.text: atha khalu te daśasu dikṣu tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ svān svān bodhisattvagaṇānāmantrayanti sma - gantavyaṃ khalu punaḥ kulaputrā bhaviṣyati asmābhiḥ sahāṃ lokadhātum, bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāntikam, prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya śarīrastūpavandanāya | atha khalu te buddhā bhagavantaḥ svaiḥ svairupasthāyakaiḥ sārdhamātmadvitīyā ātmatṛtīyā imāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātumāgacchanti sma | iti hi tasmin samaye iyaṃ sarvāvatī lokadhātū ratnavṛkṣapratimaṇḍitābhūd vaiḍūryamayī saptaratnahemajālasaṃchannā mahāratnagandhadhūpanadhūpitā māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpasaṃstīrṇā kiṅkiṇījālālaṃkṛtā suvarṇasūtrāṣṭāpadanibaddhā apagatagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānī apagatakālaparvatā apagatamucilindamahāmucilindaparvatā apagatacakravālamahācakravālaparvatā apagatasumeruparvatā apagatatadanyamahāparvatā apagatamahāsamudrā apagatanadīmahānadīparisaṃsthitābhūt, apagatedavamanuṣyāsurakāyā apagatanirayatiryagyoniyamalokā | iti hi tasmin samaye ye 'syāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau ṣaḍgatyupapannāḥ sattvāḥ, te sarve 'nyeṣu lokadhātuṣūpanikṣiptā abhūvan, sthāpayitvā ye tasyāṃ parṣadi saṃnipatitā abhūvan | atha khalu te buddhā bhagavanta upasthāyakadvitīyā upasthāyakatṛtīyā imāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātumāgacchanti sma | āgatāgatāśca te tathāgatā ratnavṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanamupaniśritya viharanti sma | ekaikaśca ratnavṛkṣaḥ pañcayojanaśatānyuccaistvenābhūt anupūrvaśākhāpatrapalāśapariṇāhaḥ puṣpaphalapratimaṇḍitaḥ | ekaikasmiṃśca ratnavṛkṣamūle siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptamabhūt pañcayojanaśatānyuccaistvena mahāratnapratimaṇḍitam | tasminnekaikastathāgataḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā niṣaṇṇo 'bhūt | anena paryāyeṇa sarvasyāṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sarvaratnavṛkṣamūleṣu tathāgatāḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā niṣaṇṇā abhūvan ||
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones in the ten directions addressed their own respective assemblies of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'We must now go, O sons of good family, to the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, to the presence of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, for the worship of the bodily <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.' Then those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, together with their own attendants — each with one or two companions — came to this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. At that time, this entire world-system became adorned with jewel-trees, made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), covered with nets of golden threads and the seven jewels, perfumed with the smoke of great jeweled incense, strewn with <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers, decorated with nets of tinkling bells, bordered with golden cords in an eight-fold pattern, devoid of villages, cities, towns, hamlets, kingdoms, and capital cities, devoid of <s>Kāla</s> mountains, devoid of <s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Mahāmucilinda</s> mountains, devoid of <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> mountains, devoid of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, devoid of other great mountains, devoid of great oceans, devoid of rivers and great rivers. At that time, all the beings who had been reborn in the six destinies in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system were transferred to other world-systems, except for those who had gathered in that assembly. Then those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, each with one or two attendants, came to this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. And as each <s>Tathāgata</s> arrived, he sat upon a lion-throne at the foot of a jewel-tree. Each jewel-tree was five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height, with proportionate branches, leaves, and foliage, adorned with flowers and fruits. At the foot of each jewel-tree, a lion-throne was prepared, five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height, decorated with great jewels. Upon each one, a <s>Tathāgata</s> sat cross-legged. In this manner, at the foot of every jewel-tree throughout the entire trichiliocosm, <s>Tathāgatas</s> sat cross-legged.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena iyaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasrī lokadhātustathāgataparipūrṇābhūt | na tāvad bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyātmabhāvanirmitā ekasmādapi digbhāgāt sarva āgatā abhūvan | atha khalu punarbhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhasteṣāṃ tathāgatavigrahāṇāmāgatāgatānāmavakāśaṃ nirmimīte sma | samantādaṣṭabhyo digbhyo viṃśatibuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvāṇi vaiḍūryamayāni saptaratnahemajālasaṃchannāni kiṅkiṇījālālaṃkṛtāni māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpasaṃstīrṇāni divyavitānavitatāni divyapuṣpadāmābhipralambitāni divyagandhadhūpanadhūpitāni | sarvāṇi ca tāni viṃśatibuddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyapagatagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīni apagatakālaparvatāni apagatamucilindamahāmucilindaparvatāni apagatacakravālamahācakravālaparvatāni apagatasumeruparvatāni apagatatadanyamahāparvatāni apagatamahāsamudrāṇi apagatanadīmahānadīni parisaṃsthāpayati apagatadevamanuṣyāsurakāyāni apagatanirayatiryagyoniyamalokāni | tāni ca sarvāṇi bahubuddhakṣetrāṇi ekameva buddhakṣetramekameva pṛthivīpradeśaṃ parisaṃsthāpayāmāsa samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ saptaratnamayaiśca
body.translated_text: At that time, this trichiliocosm was filled with <s>Tathāgatas</s>. But the emanations of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> from even a single direction had not yet all arrived. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, created space for those <s>Tathāgata</s>-emanations as each arrived. On all sides, in the eight directions, twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, all made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), covered with nets of golden threads and the seven jewels, decorated with nets of tinkling bells, strewn with <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mahāmāndārava</s> flowers, spread with divine canopies, hung with divine flower-garlands, perfumed with the smoke of divine incense — all those twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, devoid of villages, cities, towns, hamlets, kingdoms, and capital cities, devoid of <s>Kāla</s> mountains, devoid of <s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Mahāmucilinda</s> mountains, devoid of <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> mountains, devoid of Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, devoid of other great mountains, devoid of great oceans, devoid of rivers and great rivers — he established them, devoid of gods, humans, and <s>asura</s> hosts, devoid of hells, animal realms, and <s>Yama's</s> world. And all those many <s>buddhakṣetras</s> he arranged as a single <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, a single expanse of earth — level, delightful, made of the seven jewels, and with

body.text:
vṛkṣaiścitritam | teṣāṃ ca ratnavṛkṣāṇāṃ pañcayojanaśatānyārohapariṇāho 'nupūrvaśākhāpatrapuṣpaphalopetaḥ | sarvasmiṃśca ratnavṛkṣamūle pañcayojanaśatānyārohapariṇāhaṃ divyaratnamayaṃ vicitraṃ darśanīyaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptamabhūt | teṣu ratnavṛkṣamūleṣvāgatāgatāstathāgatāḥ siṃhāsaneṣu paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā niṣīdante sma | anena paryāyeṇa punaraparāṇi viṃśatilokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyekaikasyāṃ diśi śākyamunistathāgataḥ pariśodhayati sma teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmāgatānāmavakāśārtham | tānyapi viṃśatilokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyaikaikasyāṃ diśi apagatagrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānīni apagatakālaparvatāni apagatamucilindamahāmucilindaparvatāni apagatacakravālamahācakravālaparvatāni apagatasumeruparvatāni apagatatadanyamahāparvatāni apagatamahāsamudrāṇi apagatanadīmahānadīni parisaṃsthāpayati apagatadevamanuṣyāsurakāyāni apagatanirayatiryagyoniyamalokāni |
te ca sarvasattvā anyeṣu lokadhātuṣūpanikṣiptāḥ | tānyapi buddhakṣetrāṇi vaiḍūryamayāni saptaratnahemajālapraticchannāni kiṅkiṇījālālaṃkṛtāni māndāravamahāmāndāravapuṣpasaṃstīrṇāni divyavitānavitatāni divyapuṣpadāmābhipralambitāni divyagandhadhūpanadhūpitāni ratnavṛkṣopaśobhitāni | sarve ca te ratnavṛkṣāḥ pañcayojanaśatapramāṇāḥ | pañcayojanapramāṇāni ca siṃhāsanānyabhinirmitāni | tataste tathāgatā niṣīdante sma pṛthak pṛthak siṃhāsaneṣu ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā ||
body.translated_text: adorned with jewel-trees. Those jewel-trees were five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height and circumference, furnished with orderly branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits. At the base of every jewel-tree, a divine lion-throne made of jewels was arranged, five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in height and circumference, variegated and beautiful to behold. On those lion-thrones at the bases of the jewel-trees, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> who had arrived sat down with legs crossed. In this same manner, the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> purified twenty further <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems in each direction, to make room for those <s>Tathāgatas</s> who had arrived. Those twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems in each direction were cleared of villages, cities, market towns, districts, kingdoms, and capitals; cleared of black mountains; cleared of <s>Mucilinda</s> and <s>Mahāmucilinda</s> mountains; cleared of <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> mountains; cleared of <s>Sumeru</s> mountains; cleared of all other great mountains; cleared of great oceans; cleared of rivers and great rivers; made free of the hosts of gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>; free of hells, animal realms, and the realm of <s>Yama</s>. All those beings were transferred to other world-systems. Those <s>buddhakṣetras</s> too were made of <s>vaidūrya</s>, covered with golden nets of the seven jewels, adorned with nets of bells, strewn with <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s> flowers, spread with divine canopies, hung with garlands of divine flowers, perfumed with divine incense and fragrant smoke, beautified with jewel-trees. All those jewel-trees were five hundred <s>yojanas</s> in measure, and lion-thrones of five <s>yojanas</s> in measure were magically created. Then those <s>Tathāgatas</s> sat down, each upon a separate lion-throne at the base of a jewel-tree, with legs crossed.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavatā śākyamuninā ye nirmitāstathāgatāḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti sma gaṅgānadīvālukopameṣu buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu, te sarve samāgatā daśabhyo digbhyaḥ | te cāgatā aṣṭāsu dikṣu niṣaṇṇā abhūvan | tena khalu punaḥ samayenaikaikasyāṃ diśi triṃśallokadhātukoṭīśatasahasrāṇyaṣṭabhyo digbhyaḥ samantāttaistathāgatairākrāntā abhūvan | atha khalu te tathāgatāḥ sveṣu sveṣu siṃhāsaneṣūpaviṣṭāḥ svān svānupasthāyakān saṃpreṣayanti sma bhagavataḥ śākyamunerantikam | ratnapuṣpapuṭān datvā evaṃ vadanti sma - gacchata yūyaṃ gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam | gatvā ca punastasmiṃstaṃ bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ vanditvā asmadvacanādalpābādhatāṃ mandaglānatāṃ ca balaṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca paripṛcchadhvaṃ sārdhaṃ bodhisattvagaṇena śrāvakagaṇena | anena ca ratnarāśinā abhyavakiradhvam, evaṃ ca vadadhvam - dadāti khalu punarbhagavāṃstathāgataśchandamasya mahāratnastūpasya samuddhāṭane | evaṃ te tathāgatāḥ sarve svān svānupasthāyakān saṃpreṣayāmāsuḥ ||
body.translated_text: At that time, those emanation-<s>Tathāgatas</s> created by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, who had been teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the eastern direction in <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — they all assembled from the ten directions. And those who had arrived were seated in the eight directions. At that time, thirty <s>koṭi</s> hundred-thousands of world-systems in each of the eight directions were entirely occupied by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Then those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, seated upon their respective lion-thrones, each dispatched their own attendants to the presence of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>. Giving them baskets of jewel-flowers, they spoke thus: 'Go to <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain. Having gone, salute that Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and on our behalf inquire about his health, his freedom from illness, his strength, and his comfortable abiding, together with his assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Śrāvakas</s>. And shower him with this heap of jewels, and speak thus: "The Blessed One <s>Tathāgata</s> gives his consent for the opening of this great jewel-<s>stūpa</s>."' Thus all those <s>Tathāgatas</s> dispatched their own respective attendants.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgatastasyāṃ velāyāṃ svānnirmitānaśeṣataḥ samāgatān viditvā, pṛthakpṛthak siṃhāsaneṣu niṣaṇṇāṃśca viditvā, tāṃścopasthāyakāṃsteṣāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmāgatān viditvā, chandaṃ ca taistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairārocitaṃ viditvā, tasyāṃ velāyāṃ svakāddharmāsanādutthāya vaihāyasamantarīkṣe 'tiṣṭhat | tāśca sarvāścatasraḥ pariṣadaḥ utthāyāsanebhyo 'ñjalīḥ parigṛhya bhagavato mukhamullokayantyastasthuḥ | atha khalu bhagavāṃstaṃ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, at that moment, knowing that his emanations had all arrived without exception, and knowing them to be seated each upon separate lion-thrones, and knowing that those attendants of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones had arrived, and knowing that the consent had been conveyed by those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — at that moment, he rose from his own <s>Dharma</s>-seat and stood in the sky, in mid-air. And all those four assemblies, rising from their seats, stood with palms joined, gazing at the face of the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, with the finger of his right hand, opened that

body.text: mahāntaṃ ratnastūpaṃ vaihāyasaṃ sthitaṃ dakṣiṇayā hastāṅgulyā madhye samuddhāṭayati sma | samuddhāṭya ca dve bhittī pravisārayati sma | tadyathāpi nāma mahānagaradvāreṣu mahākapāṭasaṃpuṭāvargalavimuktau pravisāryete, evameva bhagavāṃstaṃ mahāntaṃ ratnastūpaṃ vaihāyasaṃ sthitaṃ dakṣiṇayā hastāṅgulyā madhye samuddhāṭya apāvṛṇoti sma | samanantaravivṛtasya khalu punastasya mahāratnastūpasya, atha khalu bhagavān prabhūtaratnastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaḥ paryaṅkaṃ baddvā pariśuṣkagātraḥ saṃghaṭitakāyo yathā samādhisamāpannastathā saṃdṛśyate sma | evaṃ ca vācamabhāṣata - sādhu sādhu bhagavan śākyamune | subhāṣitaste 'yaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ | sādhu khalu punastvaṃ bhagavan śākyamune yastvamimaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ parṣanmadhye bhāṣase | asyaivāhaṃ bhagavan saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya śravaṇāyehāgataḥ ||
body.translated_text: great jewel-<s>stūpa</s> standing in the sky, right in the middle. Having opened it, he pushed apart the two panels — just as the great door-panels of a great city gate are pushed apart when the bolt is released — even so the Blessed One, with the finger of his right hand, opened in the middle and uncovered that great jewel-<s>stūpa</s> standing in the sky. And immediately upon that great jewel-<s>stūpa</s> being opened, the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> (Many Jewels), <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was seen seated on a lion-throne with legs crossed, his body withered and shrunken, appearing as if absorbed in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration). And he spoke these words: 'Excellent, excellent, Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>! Well spoken is this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma) discourse by you! Well done indeed, Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, that you teach this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> discourse in the midst of the assembly! It is for the sake of hearing this very <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> discourse that I have come here, Blessed One.'

body.text: atha khalu tāścatasraḥ parṣadastaṃ bhagavantaṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bahukalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraparinirvṛtaṃ tathā bhāṣamāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā abhūvan | tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddha taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ divyamānuṣyakai ratnarāśibhirabhyavakiranti sma | atha khalu bhagavān prabhūtaratnastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tasminneva siṃhāsane 'rdhāsanamadāsīt, tasyaiva mahāratnastūpābhyantare, evaṃ ca vadati - ihaiva bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato niṣīdatu | atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgatastasminnardhāsane niṣasāda tenaiva tathāgatena sārdham | ubhau ca tau tathāgatau tasya mahāratnastūpasya madhye siṃhāsanopaviṣṭau vaihāyasamantarīkṣasthau saṃdṛśyete ||
body.translated_text: Then those four assemblies, seeing the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One — who had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> ago — speaking in such a manner, were struck with wonder and amazement. At that moment they showered the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, with heaps of divine and human jewels. Then the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, offered the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, half of his lion-seat within that very great jewel-<s>stūpa</s>, and said: 'Let the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, sit down right here.' Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, sat down on that half-seat together with that <s>Tathāgata</s>. And both those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, seated on the lion-throne within that great jewel-<s>stūpa</s>, were seen [suspended] in the sky, in mid-air.

body.text: atha khalu tāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāmetadabhavat - dūrasthā vayamābhyāṃ tathāgatābhyām | yannūnaṃ vayamapi tathāgatānubhāvena vaihāyasamabhyudgacchema iti | atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgatastāsāṃ catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya tasyāṃ velāyāmṛddhibalena tāścatasraḥ parṣado vaihāyasamuparyantarīkṣe pratiṣṭhāpayati sma | atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgatastasyāṃ velāyāṃ tāścatasraḥ parṣada āmantrayate sma - ko bhikṣavo yuṣmākamutsahate tasyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayitum? ayaṃ sa kālaḥ, ayaṃ sa samayaḥ | saṃmukhībhūtastathāgataḥ | parinirvāyitukābho bhikṣavastathāgata imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamupanikṣipya ||
body.translated_text: Then the thought arose in those four assemblies: 'We are far from those two <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Surely, by the power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, we too could rise up into the sky!' Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing with his mind the thoughts in the minds of those four assemblies, at that moment, by the power of his <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power), established those four assemblies up in the sky above. Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, at that moment addressed those four assemblies: 'Who among you, O monks, is capable of illuminating this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> discourse in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system? This is the time, this is the moment! The <s>Tathāgata</s> is present face to face! The <s>Tathāgata</s> wishes to enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, O monks, having entrusted this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> discourse.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: ayamāgato nirvṛtako maharṣī ratanāmayaṃ stūpa praviśya nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This great sage who has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> has come, entering the jewel-<s>stūpa</s>, this Guide —

children.text: śravaṇārtha dharmasya imasya bhikṣavaḥ ko dharmahetorna janeta vīryam // Saddhp_11.1 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of hearing this <s>Dharma</s>, O monks! Who would not generate vigor for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>? || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.1 ||

children.text: bahukalpakoṭīparinirvṛto 'pi so nāma adyāpi śṛṇoti dharmam /
children.translated_text: Though he passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> ago, he still even now hears the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: tahiṃ tahiṃ gacchati dharmahetoḥ sudurlabho dharma yamevarūpaḥ // Saddhp_11.2 //
children.translated_text: he goes here and there for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> — so rare indeed is a <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.2 ||

children.text: praṇidhānametasya vināyakasya niṣevitaṃ pūrvabhave yadāsīt /
children.translated_text: This was the vow of that Guide, cultivated in a former existence:

children.text: parinirvṛto 'pī imu sarvalokaṃ paryeṣatī sarvadaśaddiśāsu // Saddhp_11.3 //
children.translated_text: even after <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, he seeks throughout this entire world, in all ten directions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.3 ||

children.text: ime ca sarve mama ātmabhāvāḥ sahasrakoṭyo yatha gaṅgavālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: And all these are my own emanation-bodies, thousands of <s>koṭis</s>, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>;

children.text: te dharmakṛtyasya kṛtena āgatāḥ parinirvṛtaṃ ca imu draṣṭu nātham // Saddhp_11.4 //
children.translated_text: they have come for the sake of performing the <s>Dharma</s>-task, and to see this Protector who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.4 ||

children.text: choritva kṣetrāṇi svakasvakāni tatha śrāvakāntara marutaśca sarvān /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned their own respective fields, and likewise all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and celestial beings,

children.text: saddharmasaṃrakṣaṇahetu sarve kathaṃ ciraṃ tiṣṭhiya dharmanetrī // Saddhp_11.5 //
children.translated_text: all for the sake of preserving the true <s>Dharma</s> — that the <s>Dharma</s>-eye may endure long! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.5 ||

children.text: eteṣu buddhāna niṣīdanārthaṃ bahulokadhātūna sahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: For the seating of these <s>Buddhas</s>, thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of many world-systems

children.text: saṃkrāmitā me tatha sarvasattvā ṛddhībalena pariśodhitāśca // Saddhp_11.6 //
children.translated_text: have been transformed by me, and all beings transferred and [those fields] purified by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power). || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.6 ||

children.text: etādṛśī utsukatā iyaṃ me kathaṃ prakāśediya dharmanetrī /
children.translated_text: Such is my earnest desire — how may this <s>Dharma</s>-eye be illuminated!

children.text: ime ca buddhā sthita aprameyā drumāṇa mūle yatha padmarāśiḥ // Saddhp_11.7 //
children.translated_text: And these <s>Buddhas</s> stand here, immeasurable, like heaps of lotuses at the bases of trees. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.7 ||

children.text: drumamūlakoṭīya analpakāyo siṃhāsanasthehi vināyakehi /
children.translated_text: Innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of tree-bases, with the Guides standing upon lion-thrones,

children.text: śobhanti tiṣṭhanti ca nityakālaṃ hutāśaneneva yathāndhakāram // Saddhp_11.8 //
children.translated_text: they shine and abide constantly, like [dispelling] darkness with blazing fire. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.8 ||

body.text: gandho manojño daśasū diśāsu pravāyate lokavināyakānām /
body.translated_text: A delightful fragrance wafts in the ten directions from the Guides of the World,

body.text: yenā ime mūrcchita sarvasattvā vāte pravāte iha nityakālam // Saddhp_11.9 //
body.translated_text: by which all these beings are enraptured, as the wind blows here constantly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.9 ||

children.text: mayi nirvṛte yo etaṃ dharmaparyāyu dhārayet /
children.translated_text: Whoever, after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>, would uphold this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse,

children.text: kṣipraṃ vyāharatāṃ vācaṃ lokanāthāna saṃmukham // Saddhp_11.10 //
children.translated_text: let him quickly speak out, in the presence of the Lords of the World! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.10 ||

children.text: parinirvṛto hi saṃbuddhaḥ prabhūtaratano muniḥ /
children.translated_text: The fully awakened sage <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, who has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: siṃhanādaṃ śruṇe tasya vyavasāyaṃ karoti yaḥ // Saddhp_11.11 //
children.translated_text: will hear the lion's roar of whoever makes the resolute vow! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.11 ||

children.text: ahaṃ dvitīyo bahavo ime ca ye koṭiyo āgata nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: I, the second one, and these many <s>koṭis</s> of Guides who have come —

children.text: vyavasāya śroṣyāmi jinasya putrāt yo utsaheddharmamimaṃ prakāśitum // Saddhp_11.12 //
children.translated_text: we shall hear the resolute vow of the son of the <s>Jina</s> who is capable of illuminating this <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.12 ||

children.text: ahaṃ ca tena bhavi pūjitaḥ sadā prabhūtaratnaśca jinaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ /
children.translated_text: And by that [vow], I shall be honored always, and <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, the self-arisen <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: yo gacchate diśavidiśāsu nityaṃ śravaṇāya dharmaṃ imamevarūpam // Saddhp_11.13 //
children.translated_text: who goes constantly in all directions, for the sake of hearing this very <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.13 ||

children.text: ime ca ye āgata lokanāthā vicitritā yairiya śobhitā bhūḥ /
children.translated_text: and these World-Protectors who have come, by whom this earth has been made resplendent and adorned,

children.text: teṣāṃ pi pūjā vipula analpakā kṛtā bhavetsūtraprakāśanena // Saddhp_11.14 //
children.translated_text: they too will be given vast and abundant worship through the illumination of this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.14 ||

children.text: ahaṃ ca dṛṣṭo iha āsanasmin bhagavāṃśca yo 'yaṃ sthitu stūpamadhye /
children.translated_text: I am seen here on this seat, and the Blessed One who stands within this <s>stūpa</s>,

children.text: ime ca anye bahulokanāthā ye āgatāḥ kṣetraśatairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_11.15 //
children.translated_text: and these other many World-Protectors who have come from hundreds of many fields — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.15 ||

children.text: cintetha kulaputrāho sarvasatvānukampayā /
children.translated_text: consider, O sons of good family, out of compassion for all beings —

children.text: suduṣkaramidaṃ sthānamutsahanti vināyakāḥ // Saddhp_11.16 //
children.translated_text: the Guides are capable of what is extremely difficult to accomplish! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.16 ||

children.text: bahusūtrasahasrāṇi yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ /
children.translated_text: One might illuminate many thousands of <s>sūtras</s>, as [numerous] as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: tāni kaścitprakāśeta na tadbhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.17 //
children.translated_text: that would not be difficult. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.17 ||

children.text: sumeruṃ yaśca hastena adhyālambitva muṣṭinā /
children.translated_text: One might seize <s>Sumeru</s> in his hand, grasping it with his fist,

children.text: kṣipeta kṣetrakoṭīyo na tadbhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.18 //
children.translated_text: and hurl it across <s>koṭis</s> of fields — that would not be difficult. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.18 ||

children.text: yaśca imāṃ trisāhasrīṃ pādāṅguṣṭhena kampayet /
children.translated_text: One might shake this three-thousand [world-system] with the tip of his great toe,

children.text: kṣipeta kṣetrakoṭīyo na tadbhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.19 //
children.translated_text: and hurl it across <s>koṭis</s> of fields — that would not be difficult. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.19 ||

children.text: bhavāgre yaśca tiṣṭhitvā dharmaṃ bhāṣennaro iha /
children.translated_text: One might stand at the summit of existence and preach the <s>Dharma</s> here,

children.text: anyasūtrasahasrāṇi na tadbhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.20 //
children.translated_text: and teach thousands of other <s>sūtras</s> — that would not be difficult. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.20 ||

children.text: nirvṛtasmiṃstu lokendre paścātkāle sudāruṇe /
children.translated_text: But after the Lord of the World has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, in the latter age, the dreadful [time],

children.text: ya idaṃ dhārayet sūtraṃ bhāṣedvā tatsuduṣkaram // Saddhp_11.21 //
children.translated_text: one who would uphold or teach this <s>sūtra</s> — that is most difficult! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.21 ||

children.text: ākāśadhātuṃ yaḥ sarvāmekamuṣṭiṃ tu nikṣipet /
children.translated_text: One who would compress the entire realm of space into a single fist

children.text: prakṣipitvā ca gaccheta na tadbhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.22 //
children.translated_text: and, having hurled it, go on — that would not be difficult! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.22 ||

children.text: yastu īdṛśakaṃ sūtraṃ nirvṛtasmiṃstadā mayi /
children.translated_text: But one who, when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, in such a <s>sūtra</s> as this,

children.text: paścātkāle likheccāpi idaṃ bhavati duṣkaram // Saddhp_11.23 //
children.translated_text: in the final age would even write it — that is difficult! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.23 ||

children.text: pṛthivīdhātuṃ ca yaḥ sarvaṃ nakhāgre saṃpraveśayet /
children.translated_text: One who would place the entire earth-element on the tip of his nail

children.text: prakṣipitvā ca gaccheta brahmalokaṃ pi āruhet // Saddhp_11.24 //
children.translated_text: and, having hurled it, ascend even to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.24 ||

children.text: na duṣkaraṃ hi so kuryānna ca vīryasya tattakam /
children.translated_text: he would not be performing a difficult feat, nor would that require great vigor;

children.text: taṃ duṣkaraṃ karitvāna sarvalokasyihāgrataḥ // Saddhp_11.25 //
children.translated_text: but having performed this difficult deed before all the world — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.25 ||

children.text: ato 'pi duṣkarataraṃ nirvṛtasya tadā mama /
children.translated_text: even more difficult than that, when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: paścātkāle idaṃ sūtraṃ vadeyā yo muhūrtakam // Saddhp_11.26 //
children.translated_text: would be one who teaches this <s>sūtra</s> even for a moment! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.26 ||

children.text: na duṣkaramidaṃ loke kalpadāhasmi yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: This would not be difficult in the world — a man who, during the conflagration at the end of a <s>kalpa</s>,

children.text: madhye gacchedadahyantastṛṇabhāraṃ vaheta ca // Saddhp_11.27 //
children.translated_text: walks through the midst of the blaze unburned, carrying a load of hay; || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.27 ||

children.text: ato 'pi duṣkarataraṃ nirvṛtasya tadā mama /
children.translated_text: even more difficult than that, when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: dhārayitvā idaṃ sūtramekasattvaṃ pi śrāvayet // Saddhp_11.28 //
children.translated_text: would be one who, having upheld this <s>sūtra</s>, teaches it to even one being! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.28 ||

children.text: dharmaskandhasahasrāṇi caturaśīti dhārayet /
children.translated_text: One who would uphold eighty-four thousand aggregates of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: sopadeśān yathāproktān deśayet prāṇikoṭinām // Saddhp_11.29 //
children.translated_text: with their explanations, as they were proclaimed, and teach them to <s>koṭis</s> of beings — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.29 ||

children.text: na hyetaṃ duṣkaraṃ bhoti tasmin kālasmi bhikṣuṇām /
children.translated_text: this would not be difficult for monks at that time;

children.text: vinayecchrāvakān mahyaṃ pañcābhijñāsu sthāpayet // Saddhp_11.30 //
children.translated_text: one who would discipline <s>Śrāvakas</s> for me and establish them in the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.30 ||

children.text: tasyedaṃ duṣkarataraṃ idaṃ sūtraṃ ca dhārayet /
children.translated_text: more difficult than that would it be for one who upholds this <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: śraddadhedadhimucyedvā bhāṣedvāpi punaḥ punaḥ // Saddhp_11.31 //
children.translated_text: and has faith in it, resolves upon it, or teaches it again and again! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.31 ||

children.text: koṭīsahasrān bahavaḥ arhattve yo 'pi sthāpayet /
children.translated_text: Even one who would establish many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> in <s>Arhatship</s>,

children.text: ṣaḍabhijñān mahābhāgān yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // Saddhp_11.32 //
children.translated_text: endowed with the six <s>abhijñās</s>, fortunate ones, [numerous] like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.32 ||

children.text: ato bahutaraṃ karma karoti sa narottamaḥ /
children.translated_text: far greater is the deed of that best of men

children.text: nirvṛtasya hi yo mahyaṃ sūtraṃ dhārayate varam // Saddhp_11.33 //
children.translated_text: who, when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, upholds this supreme <s>sūtra</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.33 ||

children.text: lokadhātusahasreṣu bahu me dharma bhāṣitāḥ /
children.translated_text: In thousands of world-systems, much <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by me;

children.text: adyāpi cāhaṃ bhāṣāmi buddhajñānasya kāraṇāt // Saddhp_11.34 //
children.translated_text: and even now I teach, for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.34 ||

children.text: idaṃ tu sarvasūtreṣu sūtramagraṃ pravucyate /
children.translated_text: But among all <s>sūtras</s>, this <s>sūtra</s> is declared the foremost;

children.text: dhāreti yo idaṃ sūtraṃ sa dhāre jinavigraham // Saddhp_11.35 //
children.translated_text: whoever upholds this <s>sūtra</s>, upholds the body of the <s>Jina</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.35 ||

children.text: bhāṣadhvaṃ kulaputrāho saṃmukhaṃ vastathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Speak, O sons of good family, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

children.text: ya utsahati vaḥ kaścit paścātkālasmi dhāraṇam // Saddhp_11.36 //
children.translated_text: who among you is able to uphold [this <s>sūtra</s>] in the final age? || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.36 ||

children.text: mahatpriyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhoti lokanāthāna sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: A great act of devotion is performed to all the Lords of the World

children.text: durādhāramidaṃ sutraṃ dhārayedyo muhūrtakam // Saddhp_11.37 //
children.translated_text: by one who upholds this difficult-to-uphold <s>sūtra</s> even for a moment! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.37 ||

children.text: saṃvarṇitaśca so bhoti lokanāthehi sarvadā /
children.translated_text: He is praised always by the Lords of the World —

children.text: śūraḥ śauṭīryavāṃścāpi kṣiprābhijñaśca bodhaye // Saddhp_11.38 //
children.translated_text: a hero, valiant, and swift in <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) toward awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.38 ||

children.text: dhurāvāhaśca so bhoti lokanāthāna aurasaḥ /
