children.translated_text: He is a bearer of burdens, a true son of the Lords of the World,

children.text: dāntabhūmimanuprāptaḥ sūtraṃ dhāreti yo idam // Saddhp_11.39 //
children.translated_text: who has attained the stage of self-mastery — one who upholds this <s>sūtra</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.39 ||

children.text: cakṣubhūtaśca so bhoti loke sāmaramānuṣe /
children.translated_text: He becomes the eye of the world with its gods and humans,

children.text: idaṃ sutraṃ prakāśitvā nirvṛte naranāyake // Saddhp_11.40 //
children.translated_text: one who illuminates this <s>sūtra</s> when the Guide of Men has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.40 ||

children.text: vandanīyaśca so bhoti sarvasattvāna paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Worthy of veneration by all beings, that wise one

children.text: paścime kāli yo bhāṣet sūtramekaṃ muhūrtakam // Saddhp_11.41 //
children.translated_text: who, in the final age, teaches this <s>sūtra</s> even for a moment! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.41 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān kṛtsnaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ sasurāsuraṃ ca lokamāmantraya etadavocat - bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ahamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyān kalpān saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ sūtraṃ paryeṣitavānakhinno 'viśrāntaḥ | pūrvaṃ ca ahamanekān kalpānanekāni kalpaśatasahasrāṇi rājābhūvamanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ | na ca me cittavyāvṛttirabhūt | ṣaṇṇāṃ ca pāramitānāṃ paripūryā udyukto 'bhūvamaprameyadānapradaḥ suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaidūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālajātarūparajatāśmagarbham usāragalvalohitamuktāgrāmanagaranigamajanapadarāṣṭrarājadhānībhāryāputraduhitṛdāsīdāsakarmakarapauruṣeyahastyaśvarathaṃ yāvadātmaśarīraparityāgī karacaraṇaśirottamāṅgapratyaṅgajīvitadātā | na ca me kadācidāgrahacittamutpannam | tena ca samayena ayaṃ loko dīrghāyurabhat | anekavarṣaśatasahasrajīvitena ca ahaṃ kālena dharmārthaṃ rājyaṃ kāritavān, na viṣayārtham | so 'haṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ kumāraṃ rājye 'bhiṣicya caturdiśaṃ jyeṣṭhadharmagaveṣaṇāya udyukto 'bhūvam | evaṃ ghaṇṭayā ghoṣāpayitavān - yo me jyeṣṭhaṃ dharmamanupradāsyati, arthaṃ cākhyāsyati, tasyāhaṃ dāso bhūyāsam | tena ca kālena ṛṣirabhūt | sa māmetadavocat - asti mahārāja saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma sutraṃ jyeṣṭhadharmanirdeśakam | tadyadi dāsyamabhyupagacchasi, tataste 'haṃ taṃ dharmaṃ śrāvayiṣyāmi | so 'haṃ śrutvā tasyarṣervacanaṃ hṛṣṭastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ prītisaumanasyajāto yena sa ṛṣistenopeyivān | upetyāvocat - yatte dāsena karma karaṇīyaṃ tatkaromi | so 'haṃ tasyarṣerdāsabhāvamabhyupetya tṛṇakāṣṭhapānīyakandamūlaphalādīni preṣyakarmāṇi kṛtavān, yāvad dvārādhyakṣo 'pyahamāsam | divasaṃ caivaṃvidhaṃ karma kṛtvā rātrau śayānasya mañcake pādān dhārayāmi | na ca me kāyaklamo na cetasi klamo 'bhūt | evaṃ ca me kurvataḥ paripūrṇaṃ varṣāsahasraṃ gatam ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the world with its gods and <s>asuras</s>, and said this: "O monks, in the past, in a former age, I sought the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra</s> for immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, unwearied and without rest. And formerly, for many <s>kalpas</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, I was a king who had made a vow for supreme perfect awakening. And my mind never turned back. Being diligent in fulfilling the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), I was a giver of immeasurable gifts — gold, gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, refined gold, silver, diamonds, <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), red pearls, villages, cities, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, capitals, wives, sons, daughters, female and male servants, workers, attendants, elephants, horses, chariots, and even the sacrifice of my own body — giving my hands, feet, head, and limbs, and even my life. Never once did a thought of attachment arise in me. At that time, the world had long lifespans, and with a lifespan of many hundreds of thousands of years, I exercised kingship for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, not for the sake of sense-pleasures. Then I anointed my eldest prince as king, and became diligent in seeking the supreme <s>Dharma</s> in the four directions. Thus I had it proclaimed by bell: 'Whoever teaches me the supreme <s>Dharma</s> and explains its meaning — I shall become his servant!' At that time there was a <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer). He said to me: 'O great king, there is a <s>sūtra</s> named the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, an exposition of the supreme <s>Dharma</s>. If you accept servitude, I will teach you that <s>Dharma</s>.' Having heard the words of that <s>ṛṣi</s>, I was delighted, elated, uplifted, and filled with joy and happiness. I approached that <s>ṛṣi</s> and said: 'Whatever work is to be done by a servant, that I shall do.' Then, having undertaken servitude to that <s>ṛṣi</s>, I performed the tasks of a servant — [gathering] grass, firewood, water, roots, fruits, and such. I even became the doorkeeper. By day I performed such work, and at night I supported the feet of [the <s>ṛṣi</s>] lying on his couch. Neither weariness of body nor weariness of mind came upon me. And thus, while I served, a full thousand years passed."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmetamevārthaṃ paridyotayannimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, illuminating this very meaning, spoke these verses —

children.text: kalpānatītān samanusmarāmi yadāhamāsaṃ dhārmiko dharmarājā /
children.translated_text: I remember past <s>kalpas</s>, when I was a righteous <s>Dharma</s>-king;

children.text: rājyaṃ came dharmahetoḥ kṛtaṃ tanna ca kāmahetorjyeṣṭhadharmahetoḥ // Saddhp_11.42 //
children.translated_text: my kingship was exercised for the sake of <s>Dharma</s>, not for the sake of desire — for the sake of the supreme <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.42 ||

children.text: caturdiśaṃ me kṛta ghoṣaṇo 'yaṃ dharmaṃ vadedyastasya dāsyaṃ vrajeyam /
children.translated_text: I had this proclamation made in the four directions: "Whoever teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, I shall enter his service!";

children.text: āsīdṛṣistena kālena dhīmān sūtrasya saddharmanāmnaḥ pravaktāḥ // Saddhp_11.43 //
children.translated_text: at that time there was a wise <s>ṛṣi</s>, a proclaimer of the <s>sūtra</s> named the True <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.43 ||

children.text: sa māmavocadyadi te dharmakāṅkṣā upehi dāsyaṃ dharmamataḥ pravakṣye /
children.translated_text: He said to me: "If you desire the <s>Dharma</s>, enter servitude — I shall then teach the <s>Dharma</s>";

children.text: tuṣṭaścāhaṃ vacanaṃ taṃ niśāmya karmākaroddāsayogyaṃ tadā yam // Saddhp_11.44 //
children.translated_text: and I was delighted, hearing that speech, and performed the work fit for a servant at that time! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.44 ||

children.text: na kāyacittaklamatho spṛśenmāṃ saddharmahetordāsamāgatasya /
children.translated_text: Neither weariness of body nor of mind touched me, who had entered servitude for the sake of the true <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: praṇidhistadā me bhavi sattvahetornātmānamuddiśya na kāmahetoḥ // Saddhp_11.45 //
children.translated_text: my vow at that time was for the sake of beings, not directed toward myself, nor for the sake of desire! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.45 ||

children.text: sa rāja āsīttadā abdhavīryo ananyakarmāṇi daśaddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: That king was of tireless vigor, performing no other works in the ten directions;

children.text: paripūrṇa kalpāna sahasrakhinno yāvatsūtraṃ labdhavān dharmanāmam // Saddhp_11.46 //
children.translated_text: unwearied for a full thousand <s>kalpas</s>, until he obtained the <s>sūtra</s> named the [True] <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.46 ||

body.text: tatkiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājābhūt? na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? ahaṃ sa tena kālena tena samayena rājābhūvam | syātkhalu punarbhikṣavo 'nyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayenarṣirabhūt? na khalu punarevaṃ draṣṭavyam | ayameva sa tena kālena tena samayena devadatto bhikṣurṛṣirabhut | devadatto hi bhikṣavo mama kalyāṇamitram | devadattameva cāgamya mayā ṣaṭū pāramitāḥ paripūritāḥ, mahāmaitrī mahākaruṇā mahāmuditā mahopekṣā | dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni aśītyanuvyañjanāni suvarṇavarṇacchavitā daśa balāni catvāri vaiśāradyāni catvāri saṃgrahavastūni aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmā maharddhibalatā daśadiksattvanistāraṇatā, sarvametaddevadattamāgasya | ārocayāmi vo bhikṣavaḥ, prativedayāmi - eṣa devadatto bhikṣuranāgate 'dhvani aprameyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyairdevarājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho
body.translated_text: "What do you think, O monks? Was it someone else who was the king at that time, at that occasion? It should not be seen thus. For what reason? I myself was the king at that time, at that occasion. And, O monks, do you think it was someone else who was the <s>ṛṣi</s> at that time, at that occasion? It should not be seen thus. It was this very monk <s>Devadatta</s> who was the <s>ṛṣi</s> at that time, at that occasion. For, O monks, <s>Devadatta</s> was my <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend). It was through <s>Devadatta</s> that I fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> — great <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), great <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), great <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), great <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), the thirty-two marks of a great being, the eighty subsidiary marks, golden-colored skin, the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the four means of attracting [beings], the eighteen special qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>, the power of great supernatural ability, and the deliverance of beings in the ten directions — all this came about through <s>Devadatta</s>. I declare to you, O monks, I announce: this monk <s>Devadatta</s>, in the future, after immeasurable, incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Devarāja</s> (King of Gods),

body.text:
bhaviṣyati vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca bhagavān devasopānāyāṃ lokadhātau | devarājasya khalu punarbhikṣavastathāgatasya viṃśatyantarakalpānāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati | vistareṇa ca dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati | gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāśca sattvāḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti | aneke ca sattvāḥ pratyekabodhau cittamutpādayiṣyanti | gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāśca sattvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayiṣyanti, avaivartikakṣāntipratilabdhāśca bhaviṣyanti | devarājasya khalu punarbhikṣavastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya viṃśatyantarakalpān saddharmaḥ sthāsyati | na ca śarīraṃ dhātubhedena bhetsyate | ekaghanaṃ cāsya śarīraṃ bhaviṣyati saptaratnastūpaṃ praviṣṭam | sa ca stūpaḥ ṣaṣṭiyojanaśatānyuccaistvena bhaviṣyati, catvāriṃśadyojanānyāyāmena | sarve ca tatra devamanuṣyāḥ pūjāṃ kariṣyanti puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākābhirgāthābhiḥ | tena cābhiṣṭoṣyanti | ye ca taṃ stūpaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kariṣyanti praṇāmaṃ vā, teṣāṃ kecidagraphalamarhattvaṃ sākṣātkariṣyanti kecit pratyekabodhimanuprāpsyante acintyācāścāprameyā devamanuṣyā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau
cittānyutpādya avinivartanīyā bhaviṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a Blessed One, in the world-system called <s>Devasopānā</s> (Stairway of the Gods). The lifespan of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Devarāja</s>, O monks, will be twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. He will teach the <s>Dharma</s> extensively. Beings equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> will realize <s>Arhatship</s> through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). Many beings will generate the aspiration for <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). Beings equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> will generate the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening and will attain the <s>avaivartika</s> (irreversible) stage of patient acceptance. After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Devarāja</s>, O monks, the true <s>Dharma</s> will endure for twenty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. His body will not be divided into relics. His body will remain as a single solid mass, enshrined in a <s>stūpa</s> made of the seven jewels. That <s>stūpa</s> will be six thousand <s>yojanas</s> in height and forty <s>yojanas</s> in breadth. And there, all gods and humans will perform worship with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and verses of praise. Those who circumambulate that <s>stūpa</s> or bow before it — some will realize the supreme fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>, some will attain <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>, and inconceivable, immeasurable gods and humans will generate the thought of supreme perfect awakening and become irreversible."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān punareva bhikṣusaṃghamāmantrayate sma - yaḥ kaścit bhikṣavo 'nāgate 'dhvani kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ sūtraparivartaṃ śroṣyati, śrutvā ca na kāṅkṣiṣyati na vicikitsiṣyati, viśuddhacittaścādhimokṣyate, tena tisṛṇāṃ durgatīnāṃ dvāraṃ pithitaṃ bhaviṣyati ḥ narakatiryagyoniyamalokopapattiṣu na patiṣyati | daśadigbuddhakṣetropapannaścedameva sūtraṃ janmani janmani śroṣyati | devamanuṣyalokopapannasya cāsya viśiṣṭasthānaprāptirbhaviṣyati | yasmiṃśca buddhakṣetra upapatsyate, tasminnaupapāduke saptaratnamaye padme upapatsyate tathāgatasya saṃmukham ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One again addressed the assembly of monks: "Whoever, O monks, in the future — whether a son of good family or a daughter of good family — will hear this chapter of the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra</s>, and having heard it, will not doubt or waver, but will resolve upon it with a purified mind — for that person the door to the three lower destinies will be closed: he will not fall into the hells, the animal realm, or the realm of <s>Yama</s>. He will be reborn in the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of the ten directions and will hear this very <s>sūtra</s> in birth after birth. When reborn in the realm of gods or humans, he will obtain an excellent station. And in whatever <s>buddhakṣetra</s> he is reborn, there he will be born miraculously, on a lotus of seven jewels, in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāmadhastāddiśaḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādāgataḥ prajñākūṭo nāma bodhisattvaḥ | sa taṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatametadavocat - gacchāmo bhagavan svakaṃ buddhakṣetram | atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgataḥ prajñākūṭaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - muhūrtaṃ tāvat kulaputra āgamayasva yāvanmadīyena bodhisattvena mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena sārdhaṃ kaṃcideva dharmaviniścayaṃ kṛtvā paścāt svakaṃ buddhakṣetraṃ gamiṣyasi | atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sahasrapatre padme śakaṭacakrapramāṇamātre niṣaṇṇo 'nekabodhisattvaparivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ samudramadhyāt sāgaranāgarājabhavanādabhyudgamya upari vaihāyasaṃ khagapathena gṛdhrakūṭe parvate bhagavato 'ntikamupasaṃkrāntaḥ | atha mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ padmādavatīrya bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ prabhūtaratnasya ca tathāgatasya pādau śirasābhivanditvā yena prajñākūṭo bodhisattvastenopasaṃkrāntaḥ | upasaṃkramya prajñākūṭena bodhisattvena sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāmupasaṃgṛhya ekānte nyaṣīdat | atha khalu prajñākūṭo bodhisattvo mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - samudramadhyagatena tvayā mañjuśrīḥ kiyān sattvadhāturvinītaḥ? mañjuśrīrāha - anekānyaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni sattvāni vinītāni | tāvadaprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni yāvadvācā na śakyaṃ vijñāpayituṃ cittena vā cintayitum
body.translated_text: Then at that time, from the lower direction, from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, there came a <s>Bodhisattva</s> named <s>Prajñākūṭa</s>. He said to that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>: 'Let us go, Blessed One, to our own <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.' Then the Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s>: 'Wait a moment, son of good family, until you have a certain discussion of the <s>Dharma</s> with my <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, and then you may go to your own <s>buddhakṣetra</s>.' Then at that time, <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince, seated upon a thousand-petaled lotus as large as a chariot wheel, surrounded and attended by many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, rose up from the midst of the ocean, from the palace of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King, and traversing the sky above by the aerial path, approached the Blessed One on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince descended from the lotus, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> and of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, and approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s>. Having approached, he exchanged various cordial and pleasant words of greeting with the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> and sat down to one side. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> said to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince: 'While you were in the midst of the ocean, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, how many beings did you convert?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'Many, immeasurable, innumerable beings were converted — so many immeasurable and innumerable that they cannot be made known by speech nor conceived by the mind.

body.text:
| muhūrtaṃ tāvat kulaputra āgamayasva yāvat pūrvanimittaṃ drakṣyasi | samanantarabhāṣitā ceyaṃ mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena vāk, tasyāṃ velāyāmanekāni padmasahasrāṇi samudramadhyādabhyudgatāni upari vaihāyasam | teṣu ca padmeṣvanekāni bodhisattvasahasrāṇi saṃniṣaṇṇāni | atha te bodhisattvāstenaiva khagapathena yena gṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvatastenopasaṃkrāntāḥ | upasaṃkramya tataścopari vaihāyasaṃ sthitāḥ saṃdṛśyante sma | sarve ca te mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena vinītā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | tatra ye bodhisattvā mahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ pūrvamabhūvan, te mahāyānaguṇān ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ saṃvarṇayanti | ye śrāvakapūrvā bodhisattvāste śrāvakayānameva saṃvarṇayanti | sarve ca te sarvadharmān śūnyāniti
saṃjānanti sma, mahāyānagūṇāṃśca | atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ prajñākūṭaṃ bodhisattvametadavocat - sarvo 'yaṃ kulaputra mayā samudramadhyagatena sattvavinayaḥ kṛtaḥ | sa cāyaṃ saṃdṛśyate | atha khalu prajñākūṭo bodhisattvo mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtaṃ gāthābhigītena paripṛcchati -
body.translated_text: Wait a moment, son of good family, and you will see the evidence.' No sooner had <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince spoken these words than, at that time, many thousands of lotuses rose from the midst of the ocean up into the sky, and upon those lotuses sat many thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Then those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> traversed by that very aerial path to <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> Mountain. Having arrived, they were seen standing above in the sky. All of them had been converted by <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince to supreme perfect awakening. Among them, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had previously set out upon the <s>Mahāyāna</s> praised the virtues of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> and the six <s>pāramitās</s>. Those who had previously been <s>Śrāvakas</s> praised only the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>. But all of them understood all <s>dharmas</s> to be empty, and [also understood] the virtues of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s>: 'All this, son of good family, is the work of converting beings that I performed while in the midst of the ocean. And it is now visible.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> questioned <s>Mañjuśrī</s> the Prince with a verse:

children.text: mahābhadra prajñayā sūranāman asaṃkhyeyā ye vinītāstvayādya /
children.translated_text: O greatly auspicious one, heroic in wisdom — you by whom innumerable [beings] have now been converted,

children.text: sattvā amī kasya cāyaṃ prabhāvastadbūhi pṛṣṭo naradeva tvametat // Saddhp_11.47 //
children.translated_text: these beings — whose power is this? Tell us, O Lord of Men, when asked! || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.47 ||

children.text: kaṃ vā dharmaṃ deśitavānasi tvaṃ kiṃ vā sūtraṃ bodhimārgopadeśam /
children.translated_text: And what <s>Dharma</s> did you teach? What <s>sūtra</s>, what instruction on the path to awakening,

children.text: yacchrutvāmī bodhaye jātacittāḥ sarvajñatve niścitaṃ labdhagādhāḥ // Saddhp_11.48 //
children.translated_text: hearing which these [beings] have set their minds on awakening, firmly established in omniscience? || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.48 ||

body.text: mañjuśrīrāha - samudramadhye saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ sūtraṃ bhāṣitavān, na cānyat | prajñākūṭa āha - idaṃ sūtraṃ gambhīraṃ sūkṣmaṃ durdṛśam, na cānena sutreṇa kiṃcidanyat sūtraṃ samamasti | asti kaścit sattvo ya idaṃ sūtraratnaṃ satkuryādavaboddhumanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum? mañjuśrīrāha - asti kulaputra sāgarasya nāgarājño duhitā aṣṭavarṣā jātyā mahāprajñā tīkṣṇendriyā jñānapūrvaṃgamena kāyavāṅmanaskarmaṇā samanvāgatā sarvatathāgatabhāṣitavyañjanārthodgrahaṇe dhāraṇīpratilabdhā sarvadharmasattvasamādhānasamādhisahasraikakṣaṇapratilābhinī | bodhicittāvinivartinī vistīrṇapraṇidhānā sarvasattveṣvātmapremānugatā guṇotpādane ca samarthā | na ca tebhyaḥ parihīyate | smitamukhī paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā maitracittā karuṇāṃ ca vācaṃ bhāṣate | sā samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ samarthāṃ | prajñākūṭo bodhisattva āha - dṛṣṭo mayā bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato bodhāya ghaṭamāno bodhisattvabhūto 'nekāni puṇyāni kṛtavān | anekāni ca kalpasahasrāṇi na kadācid vīryaṃ sraṃsitavān | trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau nāsti kaścidantaśaḥ sarṣapamātro 'pi pṛthivīpradeśaḥ yatrānena śarīraṃ na nikṣiptaṃ sattvahitahetoḥ | paścād bodhimabhisaṃbuddha | ka evaṃ śraddadhyāt, yadanayā śakyaṃ muhūrtena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃboddhum?
body.translated_text: <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'In the midst of the ocean I taught the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra</s>, and nothing else.' <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> said: 'This <s>sūtra</s> is profound, subtle, and difficult to perceive, and there is no other <s>sūtra</s> equal to it. Is there any being who, honoring this jewel among <s>sūtras</s>, can comprehend and attain supreme perfect awakening?' <s>Mañjuśrī</s> replied: 'There is, son of good family — the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King, eight years old, of noble birth, of great wisdom, with sharp faculties, endowed with bodily, verbal, and mental actions preceded by knowledge, who has attained <s>dhāraṇī</s> in grasping the letters and meaning of all that the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have spoken, who in a single instant attains thousands of <s>samādhis</s> of composure regarding all <s>dharmas</s> and beings. She is irreversible in the awakening mind, of vast vows, regards all beings with love as she would herself, and is capable of producing virtues without falling away from them. With a smiling face, endowed with supreme beauty and loveliness, with a mind of loving-kindness, she speaks words of compassion. She is capable of attaining supreme perfect awakening.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> said: 'I have seen the Blessed One, <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, while a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, striving for awakening, performing countless merits, and through countless thousands of <s>kalpas</s> never once relaxing his effort. In this great trichiliocosm, there is not even a spot as small as a mustard seed where he has not laid down his body for the welfare of beings — only afterward did he attain awakening. Who could believe that this [girl] is able to attain supreme perfect awakening in an instant?'

body.text:
atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sāgaranāgarājaduhitā agrataḥ sthitā saṃdṛśyate sma | sā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya ekānte 'sthāt |
tasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King appeared standing before [them]. She bowed her head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side. At that time she spoke these verses:

children.text: puṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ gabhīraṃ ca diśaḥ sphurati sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Merit upon merit, deep, radiating in all directions,

children.text: sūkṣmaṃ śarīraṃ dvātriṃśallakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam // Saddhp_11.49 //
children.translated_text: a subtle body adorned with the thirty-two marks. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.49 ||

children.text: anuvyajanayuktaṃ ca sarvasattvanamaskṛtam /
children.translated_text: Endowed with the secondary characteristics, saluted by all beings,

children.text: sarvasattvābhigamyaṃ ca antarāpaṇavadyathā // Saddhp_11.50 //
children.translated_text: approachable by all beings, like a marketplace. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.50 ||

children.text: yathecchayā me saṃbodhiḥ sākṣī me 'tra tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: My awakening is as I wish — the <s>Tathāgata</s> is my witness here;

children.text: vistīrṇaṃ deśayiṣyāmi dharmaṃ duḥkhapramocanam // Saddhp_11.51 //
children.translated_text: I shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> extensively, [the <s>Dharma</s>] that liberates from suffering. || <s>Saddhp</s> 11.51 ||

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāmāyuṣmān śāriputrastāṃ sāgaranāgarājaduhitarametadavocat - kevalaṃ kulaputri bodhāya cittamutpannam | avivartyāprameyaprajñā cāsi | samyaksaṃbuddhatvaṃ tu durlabham | asti kulaputri strī na ca vīryaṃ sraṃsayati, anekāni ca kalpaśatānyanekāni ca kalpasahasrāṇi puṇyāni karoti, ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrayati, na cādyāpi buddhatvaṃ prāpnoti | kiṃ kāraṇam? pañca sthānāni strī adyāpi na prāpnoti | katamāni pañca? prathamaṃ brahmasthānaṃ dvitīyaṃ śakrasthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ mahārājasthānaṃ caturthaṃ cakravartisthānaṃ pañcamamavaivartikabodhisattvasthānam ||
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said to the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King: 'You have merely generated the mind for awakening, O noble girl. You are of irreversible and immeasurable wisdom. Yet <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>-hood is difficult to attain. There are, O noble girl, women who do not relax their effort, who perform merits for many hundreds and many thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, who fulfill the six <s>pāramitās</s>, and yet even now do not attain Buddhahood. For what reason? There are five stations that a woman even now cannot attain. Which five? First, the station of <s>Brahmā</s>; second, the station of <s>Śakra</s>; third, the station of a Great King; fourth, the station of a <s>Cakravartin</s>; fifth, the station of an irreversible <s>Bodhisattva</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sāgaranāgarājaduhitureko maṇirasti, yaḥ kṛtsnāṃ mahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātuṃ mūlyaṃ kṣamate | sa ca maṇistayā sāgaranāgarājaduhitrā bhagavate dattaḥ | sa bhagavatā ca anukampāmupādāya pratigṛhītaḥ | atha sāgaranāgarājaduhitā prajñākūṭaṃ bodhisattvaṃ sthaviraṃ ca śāriputrametadavocat - yo 'yaṃ maṇirmayā bhagavato dattaḥ, sa ca bhagavatā śīrghraṃ pratigṛhīto veti? sthavira āha - tvayā ca śīghraṃ datto bhagavatā ca śīghraṃ pratigṛhītaḥ | sāgaranāgarājaduhitā āha - yadyahaṃ bhadanta śāriputra maharddhikī syām, śīghrataraṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyeyam | na cāsya maṇeḥ pratigrāhakaḥ syāt ||
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King had a single jewel whose value was equal to the entire great trichiliocosm. That jewel was given by the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King to the Blessed One, and out of compassion, the Blessed One accepted it. Then the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> and the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'This jewel that I gave to the Blessed One — was it not quickly accepted by the Blessed One?' The elder said: 'It was quickly given by you, and quickly accepted by the Blessed One.' The daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King said: 'If I, venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, were to be of great supernatural power, I would attain supreme perfect awakening even more swiftly — and there would be no one to accept this jewel!'

body.text: atha tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sāgaranāgarājaduhitā sarvalokapratyakṣaṃ sthavirasya ca śāriputrasya pratyakṣaṃ tat strīndriyamantarhitaṃ puruṣendriyaṃ ca prādurbhūtaṃ bodhisattvabhūtaṃ cātmānaṃ saṃdarśayati | tasyāṃ velāyāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ prakrāntaḥ | atha dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi vimalā nāma lokadhātuḥ | tatra saptaratnamaye bodhivṛkṣamūle niṣaṇṇamabhisaṃbuddhamātmānaṃ saṃdarśayati sma, dvātriṃśallakṣaṇadharaṃ sarvānuvyajanarūpaṃ prabhayā ca daśadiśaṃ sphuritvā dharmadeśanāṃ kurvāṇam | ye ca sahāyāṃ lokadhātau sattvāḥ, te sarve taṃ tathāgataṃ paśyanti sma, sarvaiśca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramanuṣyāmanuṣyairnamasyamānaṃ dharmadeśanāṃ ca kurvantam | ye ca sattvāstasya tathāgatasya dharmadeśanāṃ śṛṇvanti, sarve te 'vinivartanīyā bhavantyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | sā ca vimalā lokadhātuḥ, iyaṃ ca sahā lokadhātuḥ ṣaḍvikāraṃ prākampat | bhagavataśca śākyamuneḥ parṣanmaṇḍalānāṃ trayāṇāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilābho 'bhūt | trayāṇāṃ ca prāṇiśatasahasrāṇāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākaraṇapratilābho 'bhūt | atha prajñākūṭo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sthaviraśca śāriputrastūṣṇīmabhūtām ||
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the daughter of <s>Sāgara</s> the <s>Nāga</s> King, in full view of the entire world and in the sight of the elder <s>Śāriputra</s>, caused her female faculties to disappear and her male faculties to appear, and showed herself as having become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. At that moment, she proceeded toward the southern direction. In the southern direction there was a world-system named <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless). There, at the foot of a <s>Bodhi</s>-tree made of the seven jewels, she showed herself as having attained supreme perfect awakening, bearing the thirty-two marks, endowed with all the secondary characteristics, radiating light in the ten directions, and teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And the beings in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system all beheld that <s>Tathāgata</s>, being worshipped by all gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, humans, and non-humans, and teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And all beings who heard the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of that <s>Tathāgata</s> became irreversible in supreme perfect awakening. And that <s>Vimalā</s> world-system and this <s>Sahā</s> world-system trembled with a sixfold quaking. And three thousand beings in the assembly of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). And three hundred thousand beings obtained the prophecy of supreme perfect awakening. Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Prajñākūṭa</s> and the elder <s>Śāriputra</s> fell silent.

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye stūpasaṃdarśanaparivarto nāmaikādaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma), the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on the Manifestation of the <s>Stūpa</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_12: utsāhaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 12: The Chapter on Exhortation.

body.text: atha khalu bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo mahāpratibhānaśca bodhisattvo mahāsattvo viṃśatibodhisattvaśatasahasraparivāro bhagavataḥ saṃmukhamimāṃ vācamabhāṣetām - alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatvasminnarthe | vayamimaṃ bhagavan dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya sattvānāṃ deśayiṣyāmaḥ saṃprakāśayiṣyāmaḥ | kiṃcāpi bhagavan śaṭhakāḥ sattvāstasmin kāle bhaviṣyanti, parīttakuśalamūlā adhimānikā lābhasatkārasaṃniśritā akuśalamūlapratipannā durdamā adhimuktivirahitā anadhimuktibahulāḥ, api tu khalu punarvayaṃ bhagavan kṣāntibalamupadarśayitvā tasmin kāle idaṃ sūtramuddekṣyāmo dhārayiṣyāmo deśayiṣyāmo likhiṣyāmaḥ satkariṣyāmo gurukariṣyāmo mānayiṣyāmaḥ pūjayiṣyāmaḥ | kāyajīvitaṃ ca vayaṃ bhagavan utsṛjya idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśayiṣyāmaḥ | alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatviti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāpratibhāna</s>, together with a retinue of two hundred thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, spoke this word in the presence of the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One be without concern in this matter! We, O Blessed One, will teach and illuminate this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse to beings after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Even though, Blessed One, beings in that time will be deceitful, with few roots of merit, presumptuous, attached to gain and honor, planted in unwholesome roots, difficult to tame, devoid of faith, and mostly lacking in devotion — yet we, O Blessed One, showing the power of patience, will in that time recite, uphold, teach, write, honor, revere, respect, and worship this <s>sūtra</s>. And even at the cost of our bodies and lives, O Blessed One, we will illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>. May the Blessed One be without concern!'

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ parṣadi śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ pañcamātrāṇi bhikṣuśatāni bhagavanta metadūcuḥ - vayamapi bhagavan utsahāmahe imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayitum, api tu khalu punarbhagavan anyāsu lokadhātuṣviti | atha khalu yāvantaste bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ śaikṣāśaikṣā bhagavatā vyākṛtā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, aṣṭau bhikṣusahasrāṇi, sarvāṇi tāni yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantametadūcuḥ - alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu | vayamapīmaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyāmastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle paścime samaye api tvanyāsu lokadhātuṣu | tatkasya hetoḥ? asyāṃ bhagavan sahāyāṃ lokadhātau adhimānikāḥ sattvā alpakuśalamūlā nityaṃ vyāpannacittāḥ śaṭhā vaṅkajātīyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then in that assembly, five hundred monks among the trainers and those beyond training said this to the Blessed One: 'We too, O Blessed One, are able to proclaim this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, but only in other world-systems.' Then all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> of the Blessed One, trainers and those beyond training, whom the Blessed One had predicted for supreme perfect awakening — eight thousand monks — all of them, joining their palms toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'May the Blessed One be free from concern! We too shall proclaim this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in the final time, in the final age — but in other world-systems. For what reason? Because in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, O Blessed One, beings are arrogant, of few roots of merit, always of hostile minds, deceitful, and of crooked nature.'

body.text: atha khalu mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhagavato mātṛbhaginī ṣaḍbhirbhikṣuṇīsahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ śaikṣāśaikṣābhirbhikṣuṇībhiḥ utthāyāsanād yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantamullokayantī sthitābhūt | atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ mahāprajāpatīṃ gautamīmāmantrayāmāsa - kiṃ tvaṃ gautami durmanasvinī sthitā tathāgataṃ vyavalokayasi? nāhaṃ parikīrtitā vyākṛtā ca anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | api tu khalu punargautami sarvaparṣadvayākaraṇena vyākṛtāsi | api tu khalu punastvaṃ gautami ita upādāya aṣṭātriṃśatāṃ buddhakoṭīniyutaśatasahasrāṇāmantike satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kṛtvā bodhisattvā mahāsattvo dharmabhāṇako bhaviṣyasi | imānyapi ṣaḍ bhikṣuṇīsahasrāṇi śaikṣāśaikṣāṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnāṃ tvayaiva sārdhaṃ teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantike bodhisattvā dharmabhāṇakā bhaviṣyanti | tataḥ pareṇa paratareṇa bodhisattvacaryāṃ paripūrya sarvasattvapriyadarśano nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyasi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | sa ca gautami sarvasattvapriyadarśanastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastāni ṣaḍ bodhisattvasahasrāṇi paraṃparāvyākaraṇena vyākariṣyatyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>, the maternal aunt of the Blessed One, together with six thousand nuns — both trainers and those beyond training — rose from her seat and, joining her palms toward the Blessed One, stood gazing up at the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One at that time addressed <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>: 'Why do you stand, O <s>Gautamī</s>, looking dejected at the <s>Tathāgata</s>? [You are thinking:] "I have not been named or given a prediction for supreme perfect awakening." But indeed, O <s>Gautamī</s>, by the general prediction for the entire assembly, you have been predicted. Furthermore, O <s>Gautamī</s>, from now onward, having performed honor, respect, reverence, worship, veneration, and homage in the presence of thirty-eight <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, you shall become a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, a preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. These six thousand nuns also — both trainers and those beyond training — together with you, shall become <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Dharma</s>-preachers in the presence of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. Then, further and further beyond, having fulfilled the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, you shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One in the world named <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> (Delightful to All Beings), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. And that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O <s>Gautamī</s>, shall give those six thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> predictions of supreme perfect awakening in succession.'

body.text: atha khalu rāhulamāturyaśodharāyā bhikṣuṇyā etadabhavat - na me bhagavatā nāmadheyaṃ parikīrtitam | atha khalu bhagavān yaśodharāyā bhikṣuṇyāścetasaiva cetaḥparivitarkamājñāya yaśodharāṃ bhikṣuṇīmetadavocat - ārocayāmi te yaśodhare, prativedayāmi te | tvamapi daśānāṃ buddhakoṭīsahasrāṇāmantike satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kṛtvā bodhisattvo dharmabhāṇako bhaviṣyasi | bodhisattvacaryāṃ ca anupūrveṇa paripūrya raśmiśatasahasraparipūrṇadhvajo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyasi vidhācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugatolokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān bhadrāyāṃ lokadhātau | aparimitaṃ ca tasya bhagavato raśmiśatasahasraparipūrṇadhvajasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasyāyuṣpramāṇaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the nun <s>Yaśodharā</s>, mother of <s>Rāhula</s>, had this thought: 'The Blessed One has not mentioned my name.' Then the Blessed One, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the nun <s>Yaśodharā</s>, said this to the nun <s>Yaśodharā</s>: 'I announce to you, <s>Yaśodharā</s>, I declare to you: You too, having performed honor, respect, reverence, worship, veneration, and homage in the presence of ten <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, shall become a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a preacher of the <s>Dharma</s>. And having gradually fulfilled the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, you shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One in the world named <s>Raśmiśatasahasraparipūrṇadhvaja</s> (Banner Filled with a Hundred Thousand Rays), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in the world-system <s>Bhadrā</s> (Auspicious). And the lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Raśmiśatasahasraparipūrṇadhvaja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, shall be immeasurable.'

body.text: atha khalu mahāprajāpatī gautamī bhikṣuṇī ṣaḍbhikṣuṇīsahasraparivārā yaśodharā ca bhikṣuṇī caturbhikṣuṇīsahasraparivārā bhagavato 'ntikāt svakaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptāśca tasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī</s>, the nun, together with her retinue of six thousand nuns, and <s>Yaśodharā</s>, the nun, together with her retinue of four thousand nuns, having heard their own predictions for supreme perfect awakening from the Blessed One, were filled with wonder and amazement, and at that time spoke this verse —

children.text: bhagavan vinetāsi vināyako 'si śāstāsi lokasya sadevakasya /
children.translated_text: 'O Blessed One, you are the tamer, you are the Guide, you are the Teacher of the world with its gods;

children.text: āśvāsadātā naradevapūjito vayaṃ pi saṃtoṣita adya nātha // Saddhp_12.1 //
children.translated_text: you are the giver of comfort, worshipped by gods and humans — we too are satisfied today, O Protector! || Saddhp 12.1 ||'

body.text: atha khalu tā bhikṣuṇyaḥ imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣitvā bhagavantametadūcuḥ - vayamapi bhagavan samutsahāmahe imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayituṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye, api tvanyāsu lokadhātuṣviti ||
body.translated_text: Then those nuns, having spoken this verse, said this to the Blessed One: 'We too, O Blessed One, are able to proclaim this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the final time, in the final age — but in other world-systems.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān yena tānyaśītibodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi dhāraṇīpratilabdhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmavaivartikadharmacakrapravartakānāṃ tenāvalokayāmāsa | atha khalu te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ samanantarāvalokitā bhagavatā utthāyāsanebhyo yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇāmyaivaṃ cintayāmāsuḥ - asmākaṃ bhagavān adhyeṣati asya dharmaparyāyasya saṃprakāśanatāyai | te khalvevamanuvicintya saṃprakampitāḥ parasparamūcuḥ - kathaṃ vayaṃ kulaputrāḥ kariṣyāmo yad bhagavānadhyeṣati asya dharmaparyāyasyānāgate 'dhvani saṃprakāśanatāyai? atha khalu te kulaputrā bhagavato gauraveṇa ātmanaśca purvacaryāpraṇidhānena bhagavato 'bhimukhaṃ siṃhanādaṃ nadante sma - vayaṃ bhagavan anāgate 'dhvani imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgate parinirvṛte daśasu dikṣu gatvā sarvasattvāṃllekhayiṣyāmaḥ pāṭhayiṣyāmaścintāpayiṣyāmaḥ prakāśayiṣyāmo bhagavata evānubhāvena | bhagavāṃśca asmākamanyalokadhātusthito rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One looked toward those eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who had attained <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (powers of retention), who were turners of the irreversible <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Then those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, immediately upon being looked at by the Blessed One, rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Blessed One, and thought thus: 'The Blessed One is requesting us to proclaim this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.' Thinking thus, they were stirred and said to one another: 'How shall we, O sons of good family, do what the Blessed One requests — the proclamation of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the future age?' Then those sons of good family, out of reverence for the Blessed One and in accordance with their own former conduct and vows, roared a lion's roar before the Blessed One: 'We, O Blessed One, in the future age, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, going in the ten directions, shall cause all beings to write, recite, contemplate, and proclaim [this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse], by the Blessed One's own power. And may the Blessed One, abiding in another world-system, grant us protection, shelter, and guardianship.'

body.text: atha khalu te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ samasaṃgītyā bhagavantamābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, in unison, addressed the Blessed One with these verses —

children.text: alpotsukastvaṃ bhagavan bhavasva vayaṃ tadā te parinirvṛtasya /
children.translated_text: 'May you be free from concern, O Blessed One! We, after your <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: svaṃ paścime kāli subhairavasmin prakāśayiṣyāmida sūtramuttamam // Saddhp_12.2 //
children.translated_text: in the final age, in this fearsome [time], shall proclaim this supreme <s>sūtra</s>. || Saddhp 12.2 ||

children.text: ākrośāṃstarjanāṃścaiva daṇḍa-udgūraṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: Insults, threats, and even blows with sticks and clubs —

children.text: bālānāṃ saṃsahiṣyāmo 'dhivāsiṣyāma nāyaka // Saddhp_12.3 //
children.translated_text: from fools we shall endure; we shall bear [all], O Guide! || Saddhp 12.3 ||

children.text: durbuddhinaśca vaṅkāśca śaṭhā bālādhimāninaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of wicked minds, crooked, deceitful, foolish, and arrogant,

children.text: aprāpte prāptasaṃjñī ca ghore kālasmi paścime // Saddhp_12.4 //
children.translated_text: who imagine themselves to have attained what they have not attained — in the terrible final age, || Saddhp 12.4 ||

children.text: araṇyavṛttakāścaiva kanthāṃ prāvariyāṇa ca /
children.translated_text: those dwelling in forests, wearing patched robes,

children.text: saṃlekhavṛtticāri sma evaṃ vakṣyanti durmatī // Saddhp_12.5 //
children.translated_text: practicing austerity — those of evil minds will say thus: || Saddhp 12.5 ||

children.text: raseṣu gṛddha saktāśca gṛhīṇāṃ dharma deśayī /
children.translated_text: "Greedy for tastes, attached, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> to householders;

children.text: satkṛtāśca bhaviṣyanti ṣaḍabhijñā yathā tathā // Saddhp_12.6 //
children.translated_text: they are honored as though they were endowed with the six superknowledges." || Saddhp 12.6 ||

children.text: raudracittāśca duṣṭāśca gṛhavittavicintakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of cruel minds, corrupt, thinking only of household wealth,

children.text: araṇyaguptiṃ praviśitvā asmākaṃ parivādakāḥ // Saddhp_12.7 //
children.translated_text: having entered a forest retreat, shall be our slanderers, || Saddhp 12.7 ||

children.text: asmākaṃ caiva vakṣyanti lābhasatkāraniśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: and they shall say of us, dependent on gain and honor:

children.text: tīrthikā batime bhikṣū svāni kāvyāni deśayuḥ // Saddhp_12.8 //
children.translated_text: "These monks are heretics — they teach their own compositions!" || Saddhp 12.8 ||

children.text: svayaṃ sūtrāṇi granthitvā lābhasatkārahetavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having composed <s>sūtras</s> themselves, for the sake of gain and honor,

children.text: parṣāya madhye bhāṣante asmākamanukuṭṭakāḥ // Saddhp_12.9 //
children.translated_text: they speak in the midst of the assembly — our detractors! || Saddhp 12.9 ||

children.text: rājeṣu rājaputreṣu rājāmātyeṣu vā tathā /
children.translated_text: Before kings, before princes, before royal ministers,

children.text: viprāṇāṃ gṛhapatīnāṃ ca anyeṣāṃ cāpi bhikṣuṇām // Saddhp_12.10 //
children.translated_text: before <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, and also other monks, || Saddhp 12.10 ||

children.text: vakṣyantyavarṇamasmākaṃ tīrthyavādaṃ ca kārayī /
children.translated_text: they shall speak ill of us, claiming we teach heretical doctrines;

children.text: sarvaṃ vayaṃ kṣamiṣyāmo gauraveṇa maharṣiṇām // Saddhp_12.11 //
children.translated_text: all this we shall endure, out of reverence for the Great Sages! || Saddhp 12.11 ||

children.text: ye cāsmān kutsayiṣyanti tasmin kālasmi durmatī /
children.translated_text: And those of evil minds who shall revile us at that time —

children.text: ime buddhā bhaviṣyanti kṣamiṣyāmatha sarvaśaḥ // Saddhp_12.12 //
children.translated_text: "These will become <s>Buddhas</s>!" — we shall endure everything! || Saddhp 12.12 ||

children.text: kalpasaṃkṣobhamīṣmasmin dāruṇasmi mahābhaye /
children.translated_text: In this turbulent <s>kalpa</s>, in this terrible, great danger,

children.text: yakṣarūpā bahu bhikṣū asmākaṃ paribhāṣakāḥ // Saddhp_12.13 //
children.translated_text: many monks in the guise of <s>yakṣas</s> shall be our revilers. || Saddhp 12.13 ||

children.text: gauraveṇeha lokendre utsahāma suduṣkaram /
children.translated_text: Out of reverence for the Lord of the World, we shall undertake what is most difficult;

children.text: kṣāntīya kakṣyāṃ bandhitvā sūtrametaṃ prakāśaye // Saddhp_12.14 //
children.translated_text: girding on the armor of patience, we shall proclaim this <s>sūtra</s>. || Saddhp 12.14 ||

children.text: anarthikāḥ sma kāyena jīvitena ca nāyaka /
children.translated_text: We are unconcerned with our bodies and with life itself, O Guide;

children.text: arthikāśca sma bodhīya tava nikṣepadhārakāḥ // Saddhp_12.15 //
children.translated_text: we care only for awakening, as bearers of your trust! || Saddhp 12.15 ||

children.text: bhagavāneva jānīte yādṛśāḥ pāpabhikṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Blessed One himself knows what manner of evil monks

children.text: paścime kāli bheṣyanti saṃdhābhāṣyamajānakāḥ // Saddhp_12.16 //
children.translated_text: shall exist in the final age — those who do not understand the hidden meaning. || Saddhp 12.16 ||

children.text: bhṛkuṭī sarva soḍhavyā aprajñaptiḥ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Frowns must all be endured, and banishments again and again,

children.text: niṣkāsanaṃ vihārebhyo bandhakuṭṭī bahūvidhā // Saddhp_12.17 //
children.translated_text: expulsion from monasteries, and imprisonment of many kinds. || Saddhp 12.17 ||

children.text: ājñaptiṃ lokanāthasya smarantā kāli paścime /
children.translated_text: Remembering the command of the Lord of the World, in the final age

children.text: bhāṣiṣyāma idaṃ sūtraṃ parṣanmadhye viśāradāḥ // Saddhp_12.18 //
children.translated_text: we shall speak this <s>sūtra</s> fearlessly in the midst of the assembly. || Saddhp 12.18 ||

children.text: nagareṣvatha grāmeṣu ye bheṣyanti ihārthikāḥ /
children.translated_text: In cities and in villages, wherever there are those who seek [the <s>Dharma</s>],

children.text: gatvā gatvāsya dāsyāmo nikṣepaṃ tava nāyaka // Saddhp_12.19 //
children.translated_text: going forth again and again, we shall deliver your trust, O Guide! || Saddhp 12.19 ||

children.text: preṣaṇaṃ tava lokendra kariṣyāmo mahāmune /
children.translated_text: We shall carry out your mission, O Lord of the World, O Great Sage!

children.text: alpotsuko bhava tvaṃ hi śāntiprāpto sunirvṛtaḥ // Saddhp_12.20 //
children.translated_text: Be free from concern — you who have attained peace and supreme <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). || Saddhp 12.20 ||

children.text: sarve ca lokapradyotā āgatā ye diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: All the Lights of the World who have come from the ten directions —

children.text: satyāṃ vācaṃ prabhāṣāmo adhimuktiṃ vijānasi // Saddhp_12.21 //
children.translated_text: we speak a true word; you know our aspiration! || Saddhp 12.21 ||'

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye utsāhaparivarto nāma dvādaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the twelfth chapter, named 'The Chapter on Exertion' (<s>Utsāhaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_13: sukhavihāraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: Saddhp 13: The Chapter on Dwelling in Ease (<s>Sukhavihāraparivarta</s>).

body.text:
atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto bhagavantametadavocata - duṣkaraṃ bhagavan paramaduṣkaramebhirbodhisattvairmahāsattvairutsoḍhaṃ bhagavato gauraveṇa | kathaṃ bhagavan ebhirbodhisattvairmahāsattvairayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ? evamukte bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtametadavocat - caturṣu mañjuśrīrdharmeṣu pratiṣṭhitena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ paścime kāle paścime samaye saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | katameṣu caturṣu? iha mañjuśrīrbodhisattvena mahāsattvena ācāragocarapratiṣṭhitena ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye saṃprakāśayitavyaḥ | kathaṃ ca mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattva ācāragocarapratiṣṭhito bhavati? yadā ca mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ kṣānto bhavati, dānto dāntabhūmimanuprāpto 'nutrastāsaṃtrastamanā anabhyasūyakaḥ, yadā ca mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvo na kasmiṃściddharme carati, yathābhūtaṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇaṃ vyavalokayati |
yā khalveṣu dharmeṣvavicāraṇā avikalpanā, ayamucyate mañjuśrīrbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyācāraḥ | katamaśca mañjuśrīrbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gocaraḥ? yadā ca mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvo na rājānaṃ saṃsevate, na rājaputrān na rājamahāmātrān na rājapuruṣān saṃsevate na bhajate na paryupāste nopasaṃkrāmati, nānyatīrthyāścarakaparivrājakājīvakanirgranthān na kāvyaśāstraprasṛtān sattvān saṃsevate, na bhajate na paryupāste, na ca lokāyatamantradhārakān na lokāyatikān sevate na bhajate na paryupāste, na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti | na cāṇḍalān na mauṣṭikān na saukarikān na kaukkuṭikān na mṛgalubdhakān na māṃsikān na naṭanṛttakān na jhallān na mallān | anyāni pareṣāṃ ratikrīḍāsthānāni tāni nopasaṃkrāmati | na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti | anyatropasaṃkrāntānāṃ kālena kālaṃ dharmaṃ bhāṣate, taṃ cāniśrito bhāṣate | śrāvakayānīyāṃśca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā na sevate na bhajate na paryupāste, na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti | na ca taiḥ saha samavadhānagocaro bhavati caṃkrame vā vihāre vā | anyatropasaṃkrāntānāṃ caiṣāṃ kālena kālaṃ dharmaṃ bhāṣate, taṃ cāniśrito bhāṣate | ayaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gocaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince, said this to the Blessed One: 'Difficult, O Blessed One, supremely difficult is what these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> have borne out of reverence for the Blessed One. How, O Blessed One, should these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in the last time, the last period?' Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the prince: 'A <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, established in four <s>dharmas</s>, should illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in the last time, the last period. In which four? Here, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, established in proper conduct and proper range, should illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in the last time, the last period. And how, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> established in proper conduct and proper range? When, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is patient, tamed, having attained the ground of self-control, unfrightened and unterrified in mind, free from envy, and when, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not engage in any <s>dharma</s>, and perceives the own-characteristic of <s>dharmas</s> as they truly are — the non-investigation, non-conceptualization regarding those <s>dharmas</s> — this, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is called the conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>. And what, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the range of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>? When, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not associate with kings, does not associate with, attend upon, serve, or approach princes, royal ministers, or royal servants; does not associate with, attend upon, or serve followers of other doctrines — wandering ascetics, mendicants, <s>Ājīvakas</s>, <s>Nirgranthas</s> — or beings devoted to poetry and secular treatises; does not associate with, attend upon, or serve those who uphold worldly incantations or <s>Lokāyatikas</s> (materialists), nor engage in familiar conversation with them; does not [associate with] <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, boxers, pig-keepers, chicken-keepers, deer-hunters, butchers, actors, dancers, wrestlers, or combatants; does not approach the various places of entertainment and amusement of others, nor engage in familiar conversation with them; but when others approach, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> from time to time, and teaches it without attachment; and he does not associate with, attend upon, or serve monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen who are followers of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, nor engage in familiar conversation with them, nor share the same walking-space or dwelling with them; but when these others approach, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> from time to time, and teaches it without attachment. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the range of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvo na mātṛgrāmasya anyatarānyataramanunayanimittamudgṛhya abhīkṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati, na ca mātṛgrāmasya abhīkṣṇaṃ darśanakāmo bhavati | na ca kulānyupasaṃkramati, na ca dārikāṃ vā kanyāṃ vā vadhukāṃ vā abhīkṣṇamābhāṣitavyāṃ manyate, na pratisaṃmodayati | na ca paṇḍakasya dharmaṃ deśayati, na ca tena sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti, na ca pratisaṃmodayati | na caikākī bhikṣārthamantargṛhaṃ praviśati anyatra tathāgatānusmṛtiṃ bhāvayamānaḥ | sacetpunarmātṛgrāmasya dharmaṃ deśayati, sa nāntaśo dharmasaṃrāgeṇāpi dharmaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> does not, having seized any sign of attraction, teach the <s>Dharma</s> frequently to women, nor is he eager to see women frequently. He does not visit families, nor does he think it fitting to converse frequently with girls, maidens, or young brides, nor does he exchange greetings [with them]. He does not teach the <s>Dharma</s> to a <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch), nor engage in familiar conversation with him, nor exchange greetings. He does not enter a household alone for alms, except while cultivating recollection of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And if he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to women, he does not teach the <s>Dharma</s> with even so much as a passion for the <s>Dharma</s> —

body.text: deśayati, kaḥ punarvādaḥ strīsaṃrāgeṇa | nāntaśo dantāvalīmapyupadarśayati, kaḥ punarvāda audārikamukhavikāram | na ca śrāmaṇeraṃ na ca śrāmaṇerīṃ na bhikṣuṃ na bhikṣuṇīṃ na kumārakaṃ na kumārikāṃ sātīyati, na ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃstavaṃ karoti, na ca saṃlāpaṃ karoti | sa ca pratisaṃlayanaguruko bhavati, abhīkṣṇaṃ ca pratisaṃlayanaṃ sevate | ayamucyate mañjuśrīrbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prathamo gocaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: — let alone with passion for women. He does not even display his row of teeth, let alone make a broad facial expression. He does not take pleasure in a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, or a <s>śrāmaṇerī</s>, or a monk, or a nun, or a boy, or a girl, nor engage in familiar conversation with them, nor enter into discourse [with them]. He is devoted to solitary retreat and frequently resorts to solitary meditation. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is called the first range of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sarvadharmān śūnyān vyavalokayati, yathāvat pratiṣṭhitān dharmān aviparītasthāyino yathābhūtasthitānacalānakampyānavivartyānaparivartān sadā yathābhūtasthitānākāśasvabhāvānniruktivyavahāravivarjitānajātānabhutān anasaṃbhūtān asaṃskṛtān asaṃtānān asattābhilāpapravyāhṛtānasaṅgasthānasthitān saṃjñāviparyāsaprādurbhūtān | evaṃ hi mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhīkṣṇaṃ sarvadharmān vyavalokayan viharati anena vihāreṇa viharan bodhisattvo mahāsattvo gocare sthito bhavati | ayaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvasya dvitīyo gocaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> perceives all <s>dharmas</s> as empty — as they truly are: established, standing without inversion, standing as they truly are, unmoved, unshakable, irreversible, non-revolving, always standing as they truly are, of the nature of space, devoid of etymological convention and linguistic designation, unborn, non-existent, unarisen, unconditioned, without continuation, designated as non-existent, unobstructed in their standing-place, arisen from the distortion of perception. Thus indeed, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> frequently abides perceiving all <s>dharmas</s>. Abiding by this mode of abiding, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> is established in the [proper] range. This, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is the second range of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānetamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, further illustrating this very meaning to a greater extent, at that time spoke these verses:

children.text: yo bodhisattva iccheyā paścātkāle sudāruṇe /
children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> who would wish, in the last time, the terrible [age],

children.text: idaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśetuṃ anolīno viśāradaḥ // Saddhp_13.1 //
children.translated_text: to illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> — unshrinking and confident — || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.1 ||

children.text: ācāragocaraṃ rakṣedasaṃsṛṣṭaḥ śucirbhavet /
children.translated_text: should guard his conduct and range, be unattached and pure,

children.text: varjayetsaṃstavaṃ nityaṃ rājaputrehi rājabhiḥ // Saddhp_13.2 //
children.translated_text: and always avoid familiar conversation with kings and princes. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.2 ||

children.text: ye cāpiṃ rājapuruṣāḥ kuryāttehi na saṃstavam /
children.translated_text: And with those who are servants of kings — he should have no familiar conversation with them,

children.text: caṇḍālamuṣṭikaiḥ śauṇḍaistīrthikaiścāpi sarvaśaḥ // Saddhp_13.3 //
children.translated_text: nor with <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, boxers, drunkards, and followers of other doctrines of every kind. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.3 ||

children.text: adhimānīnna seveta vinaye cāgame sthitān /
children.translated_text: He should not frequent those of inflated pride who are established in the <s>Vinaya</s> and the tradition,

children.text: arhantasaṃmatān bhikṣūn duḥśīlāṃścaiva varjayet // Saddhp_13.4 //
children.translated_text: nor monks reputed to be <s>Arhats</s> — and he should avoid those of bad conduct. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.4 ||

children.text: bhikṣuṇīṃ varjayennityaṃ hāsyasaṃlāpagocarām /
children.translated_text: He should always avoid nuns given to laughter and gossip,

children.text: upāsikāśca varjeta prākaṭā yā avasthitāḥ // Saddhp_13.5 //
children.translated_text: and he should avoid laywomen who are forward in their ways. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.5 ||

children.text: yā nirvṛtiṃ gaveṣanti dṛṣṭe dharme upāsikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those laywomen who seek <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation) in the present life —

children.text: varjayet saṃstavaṃ tābhiḥ ācāro ayamucyate // Saddhp_13.6 //
children.translated_text: he should avoid familiar conversation with them. This is called [proper] conduct. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.6 ||

children.text: yaścainamupasaṃkramya dharmaṃ pṛcche 'grabodhaye /
children.translated_text: And whoever approaches him asking about the <s>Dharma</s> concerning supreme awakening,

children.text: tasya bhāṣet sadā dhīro anolīno aniśritaḥ // Saddhp_13.7 //
children.translated_text: to that person the wise one should always speak — unshrinking and unattached. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.7 ||

children.text: strīpaṇḍakāśca ye sattvāḥ saṃstavaṃ tairvivarjayet /
children.translated_text: Women, <s>paṇḍakas</s> (eunuchs), and such beings — he should avoid familiar conversation with them;

children.text: kuleṣu cāpi vadhukāṃ kumāryaśca vivarjayet // Saddhp_13.8 //
children.translated_text: and also in families, he should avoid young brides and maidens. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.8 ||

children.text: na tā saṃmodayejjātu kauśalyaṃ hāsa pṛcchitum /
children.translated_text: He should never greet them, nor should he inquire about their skillfulness or amusements;

children.text: saṃstavaṃ tehi varjeta saukaraurabhrikaiḥ saha // Saddhp_13.9 //
children.translated_text: he should avoid familiar conversation with them, as well as with pig-keepers and sheep-slaughterers. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.9 ||

children.text: ye cāpi vividhān prāṇīn hiṃseyurbhogakāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: And those who would harm various beings for the sake of profit,

children.text: māṃsaṃ sūnāya vikrenti saṃstavaṃ tairvivarjayet // Saddhp_13.10 //
children.translated_text: and who sell meat at slaughterhouses — he should avoid familiar conversation with them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.10 ||

children.text: strīpoṣakāśca ye sattvā varjayettehi saṃstavam /
children.translated_text: And those beings who maintain women for profit — he should avoid familiar conversation with them,

children.text: naṭebhirjhallamallebhirye cānye tādṛśā janāḥ // Saddhp_13.11 //
children.translated_text: as with actors, wrestlers, combatants, and other such people. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.11 ||

children.text: vāramukhyā na seveta ye cānye bhogavṛttinaḥ /
children.translated_text: He should not frequent leading courtesans or others who live by sensual trade;

children.text: pratisaṃmodanaṃ tebhiḥ sarvaśaḥ parivarjayet // Saddhp_13.12 //
children.translated_text: he should completely avoid greeting them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.12 ||

children.text: yadā ca dharmaṃ deśeyā mātṛgrāmasya paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when the wise one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to women,

children.text: na caikaḥ praviśettatra nāpi hāsyasthito bhavet // Saddhp_13.13 //
children.translated_text: he should not enter there alone, nor should he stand in a laughing manner. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.13 ||

children.text: yadāpi praviśed grāmaṃ bhojanārthī punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: And when he enters a village repeatedly for the sake of food,

children.text: dvitīyaṃ bhikṣu mārgeta buddhaṃ vā samanusmaret // Saddhp_13.14 //
children.translated_text: he should seek a second monk [as companion], or recollect the <s>Buddha</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.14 ||

children.text: ācāragocaro hyeṣa prathamo me nidarśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the first conduct and range that I have set forth;

children.text: viharanti yena saprajñā dhārentā sūtramīdṛśam // Saddhp_13.15 //
children.translated_text: abiding by which, the wise ones who uphold a <s>sūtra</s> such as this dwell [in peace]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.15 ||

children.text: yadā na carate dharmaṃ hīnautkṛṣṭamadhyame /
children.translated_text: When one does not engage in <s>dharmas</s> as inferior, superior, or middling,

children.text: saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛte cāpi bhūtābhūte ca sarvaśaḥ // Saddhp_13.16 //
children.translated_text: nor in conditioned or unconditioned, nor in real or unreal, in any way — || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.16 ||

children.text: strīti nācarate dhīro puruṣeti na kalpayet /
children.translated_text: the wise one does not engage [in things] as 'woman,' nor does he conceive of 'man';

children.text: sarvadharma ajātatvād gaveṣanto na paśyati // Saddhp_13.17 //
children.translated_text: seeking all <s>dharmas</s>, since they are unborn, he does not see [any of them]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.17 ||

children.text: ācāro hi ayaṃ ukto bodhisattvāna sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: This indeed is called the conduct of all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>;

children.text: gocaro yādṛśasteṣāṃ taṃ śṛṇotha prakāśataḥ // Saddhp_13.18 //
children.translated_text: hear openly what their range is like. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.18 ||

children.text: asantakā dharma ime prakāśitā aprādubhūtāśca ajāta sarve /
children.translated_text: These <s>dharmas</s> are proclaimed as non-existent, not having appeared, all unborn,

children.text: śūnyā nirīhā sthita nityakālaṃ ayaṃ gocaro ucyati paṇḍitānām // Saddhp_13.19 //
children.translated_text: empty, without activity, standing for all time — this is called the range of the wise. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.19 ||

body.text: viparītasaṃjñīhi ime vikalpitā asantasantā hi abhūtabhūtataḥ /
body.translated_text: By those of distorted perception, these are conceptualized as existent though non-existent, as real though unreal;

body.text: anutthitāścāpi ajātadharmā jātātha bhūtā viparītakalpitāḥ // Saddhp_13.20 //
body.translated_text: and also as unarisen, as <s>dharmas</s> that are unborn, [yet] conceived in distortion as born and real. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.20 ||

children.text: ekāgracitto hi samāhitaḥ sadā sumerukūṭo yatha susthitaśca /
children.translated_text: One-pointed in mind, always composed, steady as the peak of <s>Sumeru</s>,

children.text: evaṃ sthitaścāpi hi tān nirīkṣedākāśabhūtānima sarvadharmān // Saddhp_13.21 //
children.translated_text: and so established, one should regard all these <s>dharmas</s> as being like space. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.21 ||

children.text: sadāpi ākāśasamānasārakān aniñjitān manyanavarjitāṃśca /
children.translated_text: Always of the same essence as space, unmoved, free from conceptual thinking —

children.text: sthitā hi dharmā iti nityakālaṃ ayu gocaro ucyati paṇḍitānām // Saddhp_13.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>dharmas</s> stand thus for all time: this is called the range of the wise. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.22 ||

children.text: īryāpathaṃ yo mama rakṣamāṇo bhaveta bhikṣū mama nirvṛtasya /
children.translated_text: The monk who guards my conduct, after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: prakāśayet sūtramidaṃ hi loke na cāpi saṃlīyana tasya kācit // Saddhp_13.23 //
children.translated_text: should illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> in the world — and no shrinking shall be his. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.23 ||

children.text: kālena vā cintayamānu paṇḍitaḥ praviśya lenaṃ tatha ghaṭṭayitvā /
children.translated_text: At the right time, the wise one, contemplating, having entered his dwelling and exerted himself,

children.text: vipaśya dharmaṃ imu sarva yoniśo utthāya deśeta alīnacittaḥ // Saddhp_13.24 //
children.translated_text: should investigate all these <s>dharmas</s> thoroughly, and rising, should teach with unshrinking mind. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.24 ||

children.text: rājāna tasyeha karonti rakṣāṃ ye rājaputrāśca śṛṇonti dharmam /
children.translated_text: Kings will provide protection for him here, and princes will hear the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: anye 'pi co gṛhapati brāhmaṇāśca parivārya sarve 'sya sthitā bhavanti // Saddhp_13.25 //
children.translated_text: and other householders and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> too will all stand around him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.25 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrirbodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle paścime samaye saddharmavipralope vartamāne imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayitukāmaḥ sukhasthito bhavati | sa sukhasthitaśca dharmaṃ bhāṣate kāyagataṃ vā pustakagataṃ vā | pareṣāṃ ca deśayamāno nādhimātramupālambhajātīyo bhavati, na cānyān dharmabhāṇakān bhikṣūn parivadati, na cāvarṇaṃ bhāṣate, na cāvarṇaṃ niścārayati, na cānyeṣāṃ śrāvakayānīyānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ nāma gṛhītvā avarṇa bhāṣate, na cāvarṇaṃ cārayati, na ca teṣāmantike pratyarthikasaṃjñī bhavati | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpīdaṃ sukhasthānavasthitatvāt | sa āgatāgatānāṃ dhārmaśrāvaṇikānāmanuparigrāhikayā anabhyasūyayā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> who, in the last time, the last period after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, during the decline of the true <s>Dharma</s>, wishes to illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, should dwell in comfort. And dwelling in comfort, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, whether memorized or from a manuscript. And when teaching others, he does not excessively find fault [with them], nor does he disparage other Dharma-preaching monks, nor speak ill [of them], nor utter censure. Nor does he, having taken the names of other monks who are followers of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle, speak ill [of them], nor propagate censure, nor generate the perception of adversary toward them. For what reason? Because he is established in the state of dwelling in comfort. When those who come to hear the <s>Dharma</s> arrive, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> with a spirit of hospitality and without envy —

body.text: dharmaṃ deśayati | avivadamāno na ca praśnaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ śrāvakayānena visarjayati | api tu khalu punastathā visarjayati, yathā buddhajñānamabhisaṃbudhyate ||
body.translated_text: — and without quarreling. And when asked a question, he does not answer by means of the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-vehicle; but rather he answers in such a way that [the questioner] awakens to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: sukhasthito bhoti sadā vicakṣaṇaḥ sukhaṃ niṣaṇṇastatha dharmu bhāṣate /
children.translated_text: The discerning one always dwells in comfort; seated comfortably, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: udāra prajñapta karitva āsanaṃ caukṣe manojñe pṛthivīpradeśe // Saddhp_13.26 //
children.translated_text: having prepared a noble and lofty seat, on a pure and pleasant spot of ground. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.26 ||

children.text: caukṣaṃ cāsau cīvara prāvaritvā suraktaraṅgaṃ supraśastaraṅgaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having put on a clean robe, well-dyed and of excellent hue,

children.text: āsevakāṃ kṛṣṇa tathādaditvā mahāpramāṇaṃ ca nivāsayitvā // Saddhp_13.27 //
children.translated_text: and having put on a black inner garment and a lower robe of great dimensions — || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.27 ||

children.text: sapādapīṭhasmi niṣadya āsane vicitradūṣyehi susaṃstṛtasmin /
children.translated_text: seated on a seat with a footstool, well-spread with variegated covers,

children.text: sudhautapādaśca upāruhitvā snigdhena śīrṣeṇa mukhena cāpi // Saddhp_13.28 //
children.translated_text: having ascended with washed feet, with an anointed head and face also — || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.28 ||

children.text: dharmāsane cātra niṣīdiyāna ekāgrasattveṣu samāgateṣu /
children.translated_text: and sitting upon the <s>Dharma</s>-seat there, when beings of single-minded intent have gathered,

children.text: upasaṃhareccitrakathā bahūśca bhikṣūṇa co bhikṣūṇikāna caiva // Saddhp_13.29 //
children.translated_text: he should present manifold and varied discourses to monks and nuns, || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.29 ||

children.text: upāsakānāṃ ca upāsikānāṃ rājñāṃ tathā rājasutāna caiva /
children.translated_text: and to laymen and laywomen, to kings and likewise to princes —

children.text: vicitritārthāṃ madhurāṃ katheyā anabhyasūyantu sadā sa paṇḍitaḥ // Saddhp_13.30 //
children.translated_text: he should tell stories of varied meaning, sweet; that wise one should never harbor envy. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.30 ||

children.text: pṛṣṭo 'pi cāsau tada praśna tehi anulomamarthaṃ punarnirdiśeta /
children.translated_text: And when asked questions by them, he should expound the meaning in accordance [with the <s>Dharma</s>],

children.text: tathā ca deśeya tamarthajātaṃ yatha śrutva bodhīya bhaveyu lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_13.31 //
children.translated_text: and he should teach that body of meaning in such a way that, having heard, they may become attainers of awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.31 ||

body.text: kilāsitāṃ cāpi vivarjayitvā na cāpi utpādayi khedasaṃjñām /
body.translated_text: And having abandoned laziness too, he should not generate the perception of weariness;

body.text: aratiṃ ca sarvāṃ vijaheta paṇḍito maitrībalaṃ cā pariṣāya bhāvayet // Saddhp_13.32 //
body.translated_text: the wise one should abandon all discontent and cultivate the power of loving-kindness toward the assembly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.32 ||

children.text: bhāṣecca rātriṃdivamagradharmaṃ dṛṣṭāntakoṭīnayutaiḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ /
children.translated_text: That wise one should preach the supreme <s>Dharma</s> day and night, with <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of illustrations,

children.text: saṃharṣayetparṣa tathaiva toṣayenna cāpi kiṃcittatu jātu prārthayet // Saddhp_13.33 //
children.translated_text: delighting and satisfying the assembly — yet he should never seek anything for himself. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.33 ||

children.text: khādyaṃ ca bhojyaṃ ca tathānnapānaṃ vastrāṇi śayyāsana cīvaraṃ vā /
children.translated_text: He should not think of food and drink, nor of meals and beverages,

children.text: gilānabhaiṣajya na cintayeta na vijñapeyā pariṣāya kiṃcit // Saddhp_13.34 //
children.translated_text: nor of clothing, bedding, seats, or robes, nor of medicine for illness — he should make no requests of the assembly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.34 ||

children.text: anyatra cinteya sadā vicakṣaṇo bhaveya buddho 'hamime ca sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Rather, the discerning one should always think: 'May I become a <s>Buddha</s>, and may these beings [too]!

children.text: etanmamo sarvasukhopadhānaṃ yaṃ dharma śrāvemi hitāya loke // Saddhp_13.35 //
children.translated_text: This is my provision for all happiness — that I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the welfare of the world.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.35 ||

children.text: yaścāpi bhikṣū mama nirvṛtasya anīrṣuko eta prakāśayeyā /
children.translated_text: And whatever monk, after my <s>nirvāṇa</s>, without envy, would illuminate this [<s>sūtra</s>],

children.text: na tasya duḥkhaṃ na ca antarāyo śokopayāsā na bhavetkadācit // Saddhp_13.36 //
children.translated_text: for him there shall be no suffering, no obstacle — neither grief nor distress shall ever arise. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.36 ||

children.text: na tasya saṃtrāsana kaści kuryānna tāḍanāṃ nāpi avarṇa bhāṣet /
children.translated_text: No one shall cause him fear, nor strike him, nor speak reproach of him,

children.text: na cāpi nipkāsana jātu tasya tathā hi so kṣāntibale pratiṣṭhitaḥ // Saddhp_13.37 //
children.translated_text: nor shall he ever be expelled — for he is established in the power of patience. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.37 ||

children.text: sukhasthitasyo tada paṇḍitasya evaṃ sthitasyo yatha bhāṣitaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: When that wise one abides in happiness, dwelling as I have declared,

children.text: guṇāna koṭīśata bhontyaneke na śakyate kalpaśate hi vaktum // Saddhp_13.38 //
children.translated_text: his hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of virtues are many and beyond reckoning — they cannot be told in a hundred <s>kalpas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.38 ||'

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmakṣayāntakāle vartamāne idaṃ sūtraṃ dhārayamāṇo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'nīrṣuko bhavatyaśaṭho 'māyāvī, na cānyeṣāṃ bodhisattvayānīyānāṃ pudgalānāmavarṇaṃ bhāṣate, nāpavadati nāvasādayati | na cānyeṣāṃ bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ śrāvakayānīyānāṃ vā pratyekabuddhayānīyānāṃ vā bodhisattvayānīyānāṃ vā kaukṛtyamupasaṃharati - dūre yūyaṃ kulaputrā anuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheḥ, na tasyāṃ yūyaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who upholds this <s>sūtra</s> in the time of the decay of the true <s>Dharma</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> should be without envy, without deceit, without guile. He should not speak reproach of other persons who follow the <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s>, nor disparage them, nor belittle them. He should not cause remorse in other monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen — whether followers of the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s>, or <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s> — [saying]: 'You, sons of good family, are far from supreme perfect awakening! You are not fit for it! You dwell in utter heedlessness! You are not capable of attaining that knowledge!' Thus he should not cause remorse in any follower of the <s>Bodhisattvayāna</s>.

body.text: sadṛśyadhve | atyantapramādavihāriṇo yūyam | na yūyaṃ pratibalāstaṃ jñānamabhisaṃboddhum | ityevaṃ na kasyacid bodhisattvayānīyasya kaukṛtyamupasaṃharati | na ca dharmavivādābhirato bhavati, na ca dharmavivādaṃ karoti, sarvasattvānāṃ cāntike maitrībalaṃ na vijahāti | sarvatathāgatānāṃ cāntike pitṛsaṃjñāmutpādayati, sarvabodhisattvānāṃ cāntike śāstṛsaṃjñāmutpādayati | ye ca daśasu dikṣu loke bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, tānabhīkṣṇamadhyāśayena gauraveṇa ca namaskurute | dharmaṃ ca deśayamāno 'nūnamanadhikaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati samena dharmapremṇā, na ca kasyacidantaśo dharmapremṇāpyadhikataramanugrahaṃ karoti imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamānaḥ ||
body.translated_text: He should not take delight in <s>Dharma</s>-disputes, nor engage in <s>Dharma</s>-disputes. He should not abandon the power of loving-kindness toward all beings. He should generate the perception of a father toward all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and the perception of a teacher toward all <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And he should constantly pay homage with sincere reverence to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> of the ten directions. When teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, he should teach it neither deficiently nor excessively, with equal love for the <s>Dharma</s>, and he should not show special favor to anyone, even out of love for the <s>Dharma</s>, while illuminating this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text:
anena mañjuśrīstṛtīyena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmaparikṣayāntakāle vartamāne imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamānaḥ sukhasparśaṃ viharati, aviheṭhitaścemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayati | bhavanti cāsya
