dharmasaṃgītyāṃ sahāyakāḥ | utpatsyante cāsya dhārmaśrāvaṇikāḥ, ye 'syemaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śroṣyanti śraddhāsyanti, pattīyiṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti likhiṣyanti likhāpayiṣyanti, pustakagataṃ ca kṛtvā satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti mānayiṣyanti pūjayiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Endowed with this third quality, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who illuminates this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the time of the decay of the true <s>Dharma</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> dwells in comfortable ease and teaches this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse without being harassed. He shall have companions in his <s>Dharma</s>-recitation. There shall arise for him <s>Dharma</s>-hearers who will hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, believe in it, trust it, uphold it, master it, write it, cause it to be written, and having made it into a book, will honor it, respect it, revere it, and worship it.

body.text: idamavocad bhagavān | idaṃ vaditvā sugato hyathāparametaduvāca śāstā -
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, further spoke thus:

children.text: śāṭhyaṃ ca mānaṃ tatha kūṭanāṃ ca aśeṣato ujjhiya dharmabhāṇakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Having completely abandoned deceit, pride, and dishonesty, the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher

children.text: īrṣyāṃ na kuryāttatha jātu paṇḍito ya icchate sūtramidaṃ prakāśitum // Saddhp_13.39 //
children.translated_text: should never harbor envy — the wise one who wishes to illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.39 ||

children.text: avarṇa jātū na vadeya kasyaciddṛṣṭīvivādaṃ ca na jātu kuryāt /
children.translated_text: He should never speak reproach of anyone, nor ever engage in disputes over views;

children.text: kaukṛtyasthānaṃ ca na jātu kuryānna lapsyase jñānamanuttara tvam // Saddhp_13.40 //
children.translated_text: he should never cause remorse [saying]: "You shall not attain unsurpassed knowledge." || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.40 ||

children.text: sadā ca so ārjavu mardāvaśca kṣāntaśca bhotī sugatasya putraḥ /
children.translated_text: And that son of the <s>Sugata</s> should always be upright, gentle, and patient;

children.text: dharmaṃ prakāśetuḥ punaḥ punaścimaṃ na tasya khedo bhavatī kadācit // Saddhp_13.41 //
children.translated_text: he should illuminate this <s>Dharma</s> again and again — weariness shall never touch him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.41 ||

children.text: ye bodhisattvā daśasū diśāsu sattvānukampāya caranti loke /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who in the ten directions practice in the world out of compassion for beings,

children.text: te sarvi śāstāra bhavanti mahyaṃ gurugauravaṃ teṣu janeta paṇḍitaḥ // Saddhp_13.42 //
children.translated_text: they are all teachers to me — the wise one should generate respect and reverence toward them. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.42 ||

children.text: smaritva buddhāna dvipadānamuttamān jineṣu nityaṃ pitṛsaṃjña kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Remembering the <s>Buddhas</s>, supreme among bipeds, he should constantly regard the <s>Jinas</s> with the perception of a father;

children.text: adhimānasaṃjñāṃ ca vihāya sarvāṃ na tasya bhotī tada antarāyaḥ // Saddhp_13.43 //
children.translated_text: and having abandoned all perceptions of conceit, no obstacle shall then arise for him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.43 ||

children.text: śruṇitva dharmaṃ imamevarūpaṃ sa rakṣitavyastada paṇḍitena /
children.translated_text: Having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind, it should be guarded by that wise one;

children.text: sukhaṃ vihārāya samāhitaśca surakṣito bhoti ca prāṇikoṭibhiḥ // Saddhp_13.44 //
children.translated_text: concentrated, for the sake of comfortable abiding, he becomes well-guarded by <s>koṭis</s> of beings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.44 ||'

body.text: punaraparaṃ mañjuśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmapratikṣayāntakāle vartamāne imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayitukāmastena bhikṣuṇā gṛhasthapravrajitānāmantikād dūreṇa dūraṃ vihartavyam, maitrīvihāreṇa ca vihartavyam | ye ca sattvā bodhāya saṃprasthitā bhavanti, teṣāṃ sarveṣāmantike spṛhotpādayitavyā | evaṃ cānena cittamutpādayitavyam | mahāduṣprajñajātīyā bateme sattvāḥ, ye tathāgatasyopāyakauśalyaṃ saṃdhābhāṣitaṃ na śṛṇvanti na jānanti na budhyante na pṛcchanti na śraddadhanti nādhimucyante | kiṃcāpyete sattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ nāvataranti, na budhyante, api tu khalu punarahametāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya yo yasmin sthito bhaviṣyati, taṃ tasminneva ṛddhibalenāvarjayiṣyāmi pattīyāpayiṣyāmi avatārayiṣyāmi paripācayiṣyāmi ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who wishes to uphold this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the time of the decay of the true <s>Dharma</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> should dwell far away from householders and renunciants, and should dwell in the abiding of loving-kindness. With regard to all beings who have set out toward awakening, he should generate aspiration toward them all. And he should generate this thought: 'Alas, these beings are of greatly deficient wisdom, for they do not hear, know, understand, ask about, believe in, or resolve upon the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s skillful means, his hidden meaning. Although these beings do not enter into this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, do not understand it, nevertheless, when I have attained supreme perfect awakening, whatever being is established wherever, I shall draw him in by the power of <s>ṛddhi</s> (miraculous power) in that very place, cause him to trust, cause him to enter, ripen him.'

body.text: anenāpi mañjuśrīścaturthena dharmeṇa samanvāgato bodhisattvo mahāsattvastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamāno 'vyābādho bhavati, satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikānāṃ rājñā rajaputrāṇāṃ rājāmātyānāṃ rājamahāmātrāṇāṃ naigamajānapadānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām | antarīkṣāvacarāścāsya devatāḥ śrāddhāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhā bhaviṣyanti dharmaśravaṇāya | devaputrāścāsya sadānubaddhā bhaviṣyantyārakṣāyai grāmagatasya vā vihāragatasya vā | upasaṃkramiṣyanti rātriṃdivaṃ dharmaṃ paripṛcchakāḥ | tasya ca vyākaraṇenaṃ tuṣṭā udagrā āttamanaskā bhaviṣyanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhito 'yaṃ mañjuśrīrdharmaparyāyaḥ | atītānāgatapratyutpannairmañjuśrīstathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairayaṃ dharmaparyāyo nityādhiṣṭhitaḥ | durlabho 'sya mañjuśrīrdharmaparyāyasya bahuṣu lokadhātuṣu śabdo vā ghoṣo vā nāmaśravo vā ||
body.translated_text: Endowed with this fourth quality too, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, a <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who illuminates this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> shall be unharmed, honored, respected, revered, and worshipped by monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, kings, princes, royal ministers, royal chief ministers, townspeople, countryfolk, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and householders. And the sky-dwelling deities, faithful, shall follow behind him for the sake of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. The sons of the gods shall constantly attend upon him for his protection, whether he is in a village or in a monastery. They shall approach day and night as questioners of the <s>Dharma</s>. And by his exposition, they shall be satisfied, elated, and delighted. For what reason? This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is sustained by all <s>Buddhas</s>. This <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is constantly sustained by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones of the past, future, and present. Rare, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, is even the sound or voice or mention of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in many world-systems.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma mañjuśrī rājā bhavati balacakravartī, balena taṃ svakaṃ rājyaṃ nirjināti | tato 'sya pratyarthikāḥ pratyamitrāḥ pratirājānastena sārdhaṃ vigrahamāpannā bhavanti | atha tasya rājño balacakravartino vividhā yodhā bhavanti | te taiḥ śatrubhiḥ sārdhaṃ yudhyante | atha sa rājā tān yodhān yudhyamānān dṛṣṭvā teṣāṃ yodhānāṃ prīto bhavatyāttamanaskaḥ | sa prīta āttamanāḥ samānasteṣāṃ yodhānāṃ vividhāni dānāni dadāti | tadyathā grāmaṃ vā grāmakṣetrāṇi
body.translated_text: It is as if, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, there were a king, a powerful wheel-turning sovereign, who conquers his own kingdom by force. Then his adversaries, enemies, and rival kings enter into conflict with him. Now that king, the powerful wheel-turning sovereign, has various warriors. Those warriors fight with those enemies. Then that king, seeing those warriors fighting, is pleased and delighted. Being pleased and delighted, he gives various gifts to those warriors — such as a village or village-fields,

body.text:
vā dadāti, nagaraṃ nagarakṣetrāṇi vā dadāti, vastrāṇi dadāti, veṣṭanāni hastābharaṇāni pādābharaṇāni kaṇṭhābharaṇāni karṇābharaṇāni sauvarṇasūtrāṇi hārārdhahārāṇi hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālānyapi dadāti, hastyaśvarathapattidāsīdāsānapi dadāti, yānāni śibikāśca dadāti | na punaḥ kasyaciccūḍāmaṇiṃ dadāti | tatkasya hetoḥ? eka eva hi sa cūḍāmaṇī rājño mūrdhasthāyī | yadā punarmañjuśrī rājā tamapi cūḍāmaṇiṃ dadāti, tadā sa sarvo rājñaścaturaṅgabalakāya āścaryaprāpto bhavatyadbhutaprāptaḥ | evameva mañjuśrīstathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho dharmasvāmī dharmarājā svena bāhubalanirjitena puṇyabalanirjitena traidhātuke dharmeṇa dharmarājyaṃ kārayati | tasya māraḥ pāpīyāṃstraidhātukamākrāmati | atha khalu tathāgatasyāpi āryā yodhā māreṇa sārdhaṃ yudhyante | atha khalu mañjuśrīstathāgato 'pyarhan samyaksaṃbuddho dharmasvāmī dharmarājā teṣāmāryāṇāṃ yodhānāṃ yudhyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā vividhāni sūtraśatasahasrāṇi bhāṣate sma catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ saṃharṣaṇārtham | nirvāṇanagaraṃ caiṣāṃ mahādharmanagaraṃ dadāti | nirvṛtyā cainān pralobhayati sma | na punarimamevaṃrūpaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhāṣate sma | tatra mañjuśrīryathā sa rājā balacakravartī teṣāṃ yodhānāṃ yudhyatāṃ mahatā puruṣakāreṇa vismāpitaḥ samānaḥ paścāttaṃ sarvasvabhūtaṃ paścimaṃ cūḍāmaṇiṃ dadāti sarvalokāśraddheyaṃ vismayabhūtam | yathā mañjuśrīstasya rājñaḥ sa cūḍāmaṇiścirarakṣito mūrdhasthāyī, evameva mañjuśrīstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastraidhātuke dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayamāṇo yasmin samaye
paśyati śrāvakāṃśca bodhisattvāṃśca skandhamāreṇa vā kleśamāreṇa vā sārdhaṃ yudhyamānān, taiśca sārdhaṃ yudhyamānairyadā rāgadveṣamohakṣayaḥ sarvatraidhātukānniḥsaraṇaṃ sarvamāranirghātanaṃ mahāpuruṣakāraḥ kṛto bhavati, tadā tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'pyārāgitaḥ samānasteṣāmāryḥṇḥṃ yodhḥnḥmimamevaṃrūpaṃ sarvalokavipratyanīkaṃ sarvalokḥśraddheyamabhḥṣitapūrvamanirdiṣṭapūrvaṃ dharmaparyḥyaṃ bhḥṣate sma | sarveṣḥṃ sarvajñatḥhḥrakaṃ mahḥcūḍḥmaṇiprakhyaṃ tathḥgataḥ śrḥvakebhyo 'nuprayacchati sma | eṣḥ hi mañjuśrīstathḥgatḥnḥṃ paramḥ dharmadeśanḥ, ayaṃ paścimastathḥgatḥnḥṃ dharmaparyḥyaḥ | sarveṣḥṃ dharmaparyḥyḥṇḥmayaṃ dharmaparyḥyaḥ sarvagambhīraḥ sarvalokavipratyanīkaḥ, yo 'yaṃ mañjuśrīstathḥgatena adya tenaiva rḥjñḥ balacakravartinḥ ciraparirakṣitaścūḍḥmaṇiravamucya yodhebhyo dattaḥ | evameva mañjuśrīstathḥgato 'pīmaṃ dharmaguhyaṃ cirḥnurakṣitaṃ sarvadharmaparyḥyḥṇḥṃ mūrdhasthḥyi tathḥgatavijñeyam | tadidaṃ tathḥgatenḥdya saṃprakḥśitamiti ||
body.translated_text: he gives cities and city-territories, he gives garments, turbans, hand-ornaments, foot-ornaments, neck-ornaments, ear-ornaments, golden threads, necklaces and half-necklaces, gold, silver, gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s>, conch, crystal, and coral — he also gives elephants, horses, chariots, infantry, female and male servants, and he gives vehicles and palanquins. But he does not give to anyone the <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel). For what reason? Because that single <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> rests upon the king's head. But when, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the king gives even that <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s>, then the king's entire fourfold army is struck with wonder and amazement. In just the same way, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dharma</s>-king, exercises his <s>Dharma</s>-kingship over the triple world, conquered by the power of his own arms and the power of his merit. <s>Māra</s>, the evil one, attacks the triple world. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s noble warriors fight with <s>Māra</s>. Then, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dharma</s>-king, seeing those noble warriors fighting, taught many hundreds of thousands of <s>sūtras</s> to gladden the fourfold assembly. He gives them the great <s>Dharma</s>-city of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. He entices them with <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But he does not yet teach this kind of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. Just as, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that king, the mighty wheel-turner, being amazed by the great heroism of those warriors who fought, finally gives that last <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s>, his greatest possession, unbelievable to all the world and wondrous — just as, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, that king's <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s>, long guarded, resting on his head — in the same way, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, the <s>Dharma</s>-king in the triple world, exercising his kingship through <s>Dharma</s>, when he sees <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> fighting with <s>Skandhamāra</s> (the demon of the aggregates) or <s>Kleśamāra</s> (the demon of afflictions), and when those fighting ones have accomplished the great heroism of destroying attachment, aversion, and delusion, emerging from the entire triple world, and defeating all <s>Māras</s> — then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, being pleased, teaches to those noble warriors this kind of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, opposed by all the world, unbelievable to all the world, never before proclaimed or declared —

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānetamevārthaṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, further illustrating this very meaning to a greater extent, at that time spoke these verses —

children.text: maitrībalaṃ co sada darśayantaḥ kṛpāyamāṇaḥ sada sarvasattvān /
children.translated_text: Always showing the power of <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), being compassionate always toward all beings,

children.text: prakāśayeddharmamimevarūpaṃ sūtraṃ viśiṣṭaṃ sugatehi varṇitam // Saddhp_13.45 //
children.translated_text: one should illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> of such a form — this distinguished <s>sūtra</s> praised by the <s>Sugatas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.45 ||

children.text: gṛhastha ye pravrajitāśca ye syuratha bodhisattvāstada kāli paścime /
children.translated_text: Whether householders or renunciants, and also <s>Bodhisattvas</s> in that final age —

children.text: sarveṣu maitrībala so hi darśayī mā haiva kṣepsyanti śruṇitva dharmam // Saddhp_13.46 //
children.translated_text: he should show the power of loving-kindness to all of them, lest they should scorn [him] upon hearing the <s>Dharma</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.46 ||

children.text: ahaṃ tu bodhimanuprāpuṇitvā yadā sthito bheṣyi tathāgatatve /
children.translated_text: When I have attained awakening and am established in <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood,

children.text: tato upāneṣyi upāyi sthitvā saṃśrāvayiṣye imamagrabodhim // Saddhp_13.47 //
children.translated_text: then, standing in skillful means, I shall bring [them] near and cause them to hear this supreme awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.47 ||

children.text: yathāpi rājā balacakravartī yodhāna dadyādvividhaṃ hiraṇyam /
children.translated_text: Just as a king, a mighty wheel-turner, gives to his warriors various gold,

children.text: hastīṃśca aśvāṃśca rathān padātīn nagarāṇi grāmāṃśca dadāti tuṣṭaḥ // Saddhp_13.48 //
children.translated_text: elephants and horses and chariots and infantry, cities and villages — he gives, delighted! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.48 ||

children.text: keṣāṃci hastābharaṇāni prīto dadāti rūpyaṃ ca suvarṇasūtram /
children.translated_text: To some, pleased, he gives hand-ornaments, silver, and golden threads,

children.text: muktāmaṇiṃ śaṅkhaśilāpravālaṃ vividhāṃśca dāsān sa dadāti prītaḥ // Saddhp_13.49 //
children.translated_text: pearls, gems, conch, crystal, and coral — various servants too he gives, delighted! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.49 ||

children.text: yadā tu so uttamasāṃhasena vismāpito kenaci tatra bhoti /
children.translated_text: But when he is amazed by some supreme heroic deed there,

children.text: vijñāya āścaryamidaṃ kṛtaṃ ti mukuṭaṃ sa muñcitva maṇiṃ dadāti // Saddhp_13.50 //
children.translated_text: recognizing 'This is a wonderful deed!' — he removes his crown and gives the jewel! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.50 ||

children.text: tathaiva buddho ahu dharmarājā kṣāntībalaḥ prajñaprabhūtakośaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so am I, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>-king, rich in the power of patience and the treasury of wisdom,

children.text: dharmeṇa śāsāmimu sarvalokaṃ hitānukampī karūṇāyamānaḥ // Saddhp_13.51 //
children.translated_text: I govern this entire world through <s>Dharma</s>, compassionate and full of kindness! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.51 ||

children.text: sattvāṃśca dṛṣṭvātha vihanyamānān bhāṣāmi sūtrāntasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing beings being struck down, I teach hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>sūtras</s>,

children.text: parākramaṃ jāniya teṣa prāṇināṃ ye śuddhasattvā iha kleśaghātinaḥ // Saddhp_13.52 //
children.translated_text: knowing the heroic effort of those beings who are pure beings here, destroyers of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.52 ||

body.text: atha dharmarājāpi mahābhiṣaṭkaḥ paryāyakoṭīśata bhāṣamāṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Dharma</s>-king too, the great champion, having taught <s>koṭis</s> and hundreds of discourses,

body.text: jñātvā ca sattvān balavantu jñānī cūḍāmaṇiṃ vā ima sūtra deśayī // Saddhp_13.53 //
body.translated_text: knowing the beings to be strong and wise, teaches this <s>sūtra</s> [which is like] the <s>cūḍāmaṇi</s> (crest-jewel)! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.53 ||

children.text: imu paścimu loki vadāmi sūtraṃ sūtrāṇa sarveṣa mamāgrabhūtam /
children.translated_text: I teach this, the last <s>sūtra</s> in the world, the foremost of all my <s>sūtras</s>;

children.text: saṃrakṣitaṃ me na ca jātu proktaṃ taṃ śrāvayāmyadya śṛṇotha sarve // Saddhp_13.54 //
children.translated_text: guarded by me and never before proclaimed — I now cause it to be heard; listen, all of you! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.54 ||

children.text: catvāri dharmā imi evarūpāḥ mayi nirvṛte ye ca niṣevitavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: These are the four practices of such a form that should be cultivated when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: ye cārthikā uttamamagrabodhau vyāpāraṇaṃ ye ca karonti mahyam // Saddhp_13.55 //
children.translated_text: by those who desire the supreme, foremost awakening, and who carry out the work on my behalf! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.55 ||

children.text: na tasya śoko na pi cāntarāyo daurvarṇikaṃ nāpi gilānakatvam /
children.translated_text: For him there is no grief, no obstacles, no ill-complexion, no sickness,

children.text: na ca cchavī kṛṣṇika tasya bhoti na cāpi hīne nagarasmi vāsaḥ // Saddhp_13.56 //
children.translated_text: nor does his skin become dark — nor does he dwell in a lowly city! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.56 ||

children.text: priyadarśano 'sau satataṃ maharṣī  tathāgato vā yatha pūjya bhoti /
children.translated_text: Pleasant to behold always is that great sage — he becomes worthy of worship like a <s>Tathāgata</s>;

children.text: upasthāyakāstasya bhavanti nityaṃ ye devaputrā daharā bhavanti // Saddhp_13.57 //
children.translated_text: his constant attendants are young sons of the gods! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.57 ||

children.text: na tasya śastraṃ na viṣaṃ kadācit kāye krame nāpi ca daṇḍaloṣṭam /
children.translated_text: Never do weapons or poison [harm] his body, nor stick nor stone;

children.text: saṃmīlitaṃ tasya mukhaṃ bhaveya yo tasya ākrośamapī vadeyā // Saddhp_13.58 //
children.translated_text: but the mouth of one who would speak abuse to him would be sealed shut! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.58 ||

children.text: so bandhubhūto bhavatīha prāṇināmālokajāto vicarantu medinīm /
children.translated_text: He becomes a kinsman of beings here, a light arisen, wandering the earth,

children.text: timiraṃ haranto bahuprāṇakoṭināṃ yo sūtradhāre imu nirvṛte mayi // Saddhp_13.59 //
children.translated_text: dispelling the darkness for many <s>koṭis</s> of beings — one who upholds this <s>sūtra</s> when I have passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.59 ||

children.text: supinasmi so paśyati bhadrarūpaṃ bhikṣūṃśca so paśyati bhikṣuṇīśca /
children.translated_text: In his dreams he sees auspicious visions — monks and nuns,

children.text: sihāsanasthaṃ ca tathātmabhāvaṃ dharmaṃ prakāśentu bahuprakāram // Saddhp_13.60 //
children.translated_text: and himself seated upon a lion-throne, illuminating the <s>Dharma</s> in many ways! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.60 ||

children.text: devāṃśca yakṣān yatha gaṅgāvālikā asurāṃśca nāgāṃśca bahuprakārān /
children.translated_text: Gods and <s>yakṣas</s>, [numerous] like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>asuras</s> and <s>nāgas</s> of many kinds —

children.text: teṣāṃ ca so bhāṣati agradharmaṃ supinasmi sarveṣa kṛtāñjalīnām // Saddhp_13.61 //
children.translated_text: he teaches the supreme <s>Dharma</s> to all of them in his dreams, all standing with joined palms! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.61 ||

children.text: tathāgataṃ so supinasmi paśyati deśenta dharmaṃ bahuprāṇikoṭinām /
children.translated_text: In his dreams he sees the <s>Tathāgata</s> teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to many <s>koṭis</s> of beings,

children.text: raśmīsahasrāṇi pramuñcamānaṃ valgusvaraṃ kāñcanavarṇanātham // Saddhp_13.62 //
children.translated_text: emitting thousands of rays of light, the Lord of golden hue with a beautiful voice! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.62 ||

children.text: so cā tahī bhoti kṛtāñjalisthito abhiṣṭuvanto dvipaduttamaṃ munim /
children.translated_text: And he stands there with joined palms, praising the Supreme among Bipeds, the sage;

children.text: so cā jino bhāṣati agradharmaṃ caturṇa parṣāṇa mahābhiṣaṭūkaḥ // Saddhp_13.63 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Jina</s>, the great champion, teaches the supreme <s>Dharma</s> to the fourfold assembly! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.63 ||

children.text: so ca prahṛṣṭo bhavatī śruṇitvā prāmodyajātaśca karoti pūjām /
children.translated_text: He becomes joyful upon hearing, and filled with gladness he performs worship;

children.text: supine ca so dhāraṇi prāpuṇoti avivartiyaṃ jñāna spṛśitva kṣipram // Saddhp_13.64 //
children.translated_text: in his dream he attains <s>dhāraṇī</s> (mystic formulae), quickly touching irreversible knowledge! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.64 ||

children.text: jñātvā ca so āśayu lokanāthastaṃ vyākarotī puruṣarṣabhatve /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the World, knowing his aspiration, prophesies him for the state of a bull among men:

children.text: kulaputra tvaṃ pīha anuttaraṃ śivaṃ spṛśiṣyasi jñānamanāgate 'dhvani // Saddhp_13.65 //
children.translated_text: 'O son of good family, you too here will touch the unsurpassed, blessed knowledge in the future!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.65 ||

children.text: tavāpi kṣetraṃ vipulaṃ bhaviṣyati parṣāśca catvāri yathaiva mahyam /
children.translated_text: 'Your field too will be vast, and the fourfold assembly just as mine;

children.text: śroṣyanti dharmaṃ vipulaṃ anāsravaṃ sagauravā bhūtva kṛtāñjalī ca // Saddhp_13.66 //
children.translated_text: they will hear the vast, outflow-free <s>Dharma</s>, having become reverential and standing with joined palms!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.66 ||

children.text: punaśca so paśyati ātmabhāvaṃ bhāventa dharmaṃ girikandareṣu /
children.translated_text: And again he sees himself practicing the <s>Dharma</s> in mountain caves,

children.text: bhāvitva dharmaṃ ca spṛśitva dharmatāṃ samādhi so labdhu jinaṃ ca paśyati // Saddhp_13.67 //
children.translated_text: and having practiced the <s>Dharma</s> and touched the true nature of reality, he attains <s>samādhi</s> and beholds the <s>Jina</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.67 ||

body.text: suvarṇavarṇaṃ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇaṃ supinasmi dṛṣṭvā ca śṛṇoti dharmam /
body.translated_text: In his dream, having seen [the <s>Buddha</s>] of golden hue, marked with a hundred merits, he hears the <s>Dharma</s>;

body.text: śrutvā ca taṃ parṣadi saṃprakāśayī supino khu tasyo ayamevarūpaḥ // Saddhp_13.68 //
body.translated_text: having heard it, he illuminates it in the assembly — such indeed are his dreams! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.68 ||

children.text: svapne 'pi sarvaṃ prajahitva rājyamantaḥpuraṃ jñātigaṇaṃ tathaiva /
children.translated_text: Even in dreams he renounces all kingship, the inner palace, and his host of kinsmen,

children.text: abhiniṣkramī sarva jahitva kāmānupasaṃkramī yena ca bodhimaṇḍam // Saddhp_13.69 //
children.translated_text: and goes forth, abandoning all pleasures, approaching the seat of awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.69 ||

children.text: siṃhāsane tatra niṣīdiyāno drumasya mūle tahi bodhiarthikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Sitting there on a lion-throne at the foot of a tree, seeking awakening,

children.text: divasāna saptāna tathātyayena anuprāpsyate jñānu tathāgatānām // Saddhp_13.70 //
children.translated_text: after the passing of seven days, he will attain the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.70 ||

children.text: bodhiṃ ca prāptastatu vyutthahitvā pravartayī cakramanāsravaṃ hi /
children.translated_text: Having attained awakening and risen from that [seat], he will turn the outflow-free wheel,

children.text: caturṇa parṣāṇa sa dharma deśayī acintiyā kalpasahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_13.71 //
children.translated_text: and he will teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the fourfold assembly, the great champion, for inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.71 ||

children.text: prakāśayitvā tahi dharma nāsravaṃ nirvāpayitvā bahu prāṇikoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having illuminated the outflow-free <s>Dharma</s> there, and having brought many <s>koṭis</s> of beings to <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

children.text: nirvāyatī hetukṣaye va dīpaḥ supino ayaṃ so bhavatevarūpaḥ // Saddhp_13.72 //
children.translated_text: he passes into <s>nirvāṇa</s> like a lamp when its fuel is exhausted — such is his dream of this kind! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.72 ||

children.text: bahu ānuśaṃsāśca anantakāśca ye mañjughoṣā sada tasya bhonti /
children.translated_text: Many and endless are the blessings, O <s>Mañjughoṣa</s>, that always belong to that one

children.text: yo paścime kāli iamamagradharmaṃ sūtraṃ prakāśeya mayā sudeśitam // Saddhp_13.73 //
children.translated_text: who, in the final age, would illuminate this foremost <s>Dharma</s>, this <s>sūtra</s> well-taught by me! || <s>Saddhp</s> 13.73 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye sukhavihāraparivarto nāma trayodaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma), the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on Peaceful Abiding (<s>Sukhavihāra</s>).

body.text: Saddhp_14: bodhisattvapṛthivīvirasamudgamaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 14: The Chapter on the Emergence of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> from the Fissure of the Earth.

body.text: atha khalu anyalokadhātvāgatānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmaṣṭau gaṅgānadīvālukāsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstasmin samaye tataḥ parṣanmaṇḍalādabhyutthitā abhūvan | te 'ñjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavato 'bhimukhā bhagavantaṃ namasyamānā bhagavantametadūcuḥ - saced bhagavānasmākamanujānīyāt, vayamapi bhagavan imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya tasyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau saṃprakāśeyama vācayema lekhayema pūjayema, asmiṃśca dharmaparyāye yogamāpadyemahi | tatsādhu bhagavānasmākamapīmaṃ dharmaparyāyamanujānātu | atha khalu bhagavāṃstān bodhisattvānetadavocat - alaṃ kulaputrāḥ | kiṃ yuṣmākamanena kṛtyena? santi kulaputrā iha mamaivāsyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau ṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni bodhisattvasahasrāṇi ekasya bodhisattvasya parivāraḥ | evaṃrūpāṇāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ ṣaṣṭyeva gaṅgānadīvālukāsamāni bodhisattvasahasrāṇi, yeṣāmekaikasya bodhisattvasya iyāneva parivāraḥ ye mama parinirvṛtasya paścime kāle paścime samaye imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti saṃprakāśayiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then, at that time, from among those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who had come from other world-systems, eight [times as many] <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> [as the number of] sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> rose from the midst of that assembly-circle. Having joined their palms facing the Blessed One, saluting the Blessed One, they said this to the Blessed One: 'If the Blessed One would give us permission, we too, O Blessed One,

body.text: samanantarabhāṣitā ceyaṃ bhagavatā vāk, atheyaṃ sahā lokadhātuḥ samantāt sphuṭitā visphuṭitā abhūt | tebhyaśca sphoṭāntarebhyo bahūni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyuttiṣṭhante sma suvarṇavarṇaiḥ kāyairdvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ, ye 'syāṃ mahāpṛthivyāmadha ākāśadhātau viharanti sma | imāmeva sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ niśritya te khalvimamevaṃrūpaṃ bhagavataḥ śabdaṃ śrutvā pṛthivyā adhaṃ samutthitāḥ, yeṣāmekaiko bodhisattvaḥ ṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivāro gaṇī mahāgaṇī gaṇācaryaḥ | tādṛśānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ gaṇīnāṃ mahāgaṇīnāṃ gaṇācāryāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukopamāni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi, ye itaḥ sahāyā lokadhātordharaṇīvivarebhyaḥ samunmajjante sma | kaḥ punarvādaḥ pañcāśadgaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaścatvāriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādastriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādo viṃśatibodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādo daśagaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ pañcacatustridvigaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvāda ekagaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādo 'rdhagaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaścaturbhāga-ṣaḍbhāgāṣṭabhāga-daśabhāga-viṃśatibhāga-triṃśadbhāga-catvāriṃśadbhāga-pañcāśadbhāgaśatabhāgasahasrabhāgaśatasahasrabhāgakoṭībhāgakoṭīśatabhāgakoṭīsahasrabhāgakoṭīśatasahasrabhāgakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrabhāgagaṅgānadīvālukopamabodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām?
body.translated_text: No sooner had the Blessed One spoken this word than this <s>Sahā</s> world-system split open and burst apart on all sides. And from those crevices arose many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with bodies of golden hue, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, who had been dwelling in the space beneath this great earth. Having heard this utterance of the Blessed One, they rose up from below the earth, all relying upon this very <s>Sahā</s> world-system. Each one of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> was a leader, a great leader, a chief of a company, with a retinue of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of sixty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers. Of such <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, leaders, great leaders, and chiefs of companies, there were <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of sixty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, who emerged from the crevices of the earth of this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. How much more so of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> with retinues of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal to the sands of fifty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of forty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of thirty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! How much more so of those with retinues of twenty <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of ten <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of five, four, three, or two <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of one <s>Gaṅgā</s> river! How much more so of those with retinues equal to the sands of half a <s>Gaṅgā</s> river! How much more so of those with retinues equal to a fourth, a sixth, an eighth, a tenth, a twentieth, a thirtieth, a fortieth, a fiftieth, a hundredth, a thousandth, a hundred-thousandth, a <s>koṭi</s>th, a hundred-<s>koṭi</s>th, a thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, a hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th, a <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousandth part of the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river!

body.text:
kaḥ punarvādo bahubodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām?
kaḥ punarvādaḥ koṭīparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ śatasahasraparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ sahasraparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ pañcaśataparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaścatuḥśatatriśatadviśataparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ ekaśataparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādaḥ pañcāśadbodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? peyālam | kaḥ punarvādaścatvāriṃśatriṃśadviṃśatidaśapañcacatustridvibodhisattvaparivārāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvāda ātmadvitīyānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? kaḥ punarvādo 'parivārāṇāmekavihāriṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānām? na teṣāṃ saṃkhyā vā gaṇanā vā upamā vā upaniṣadvā upalabhyate, ya iha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau dharaṇīvivarebhyo bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ samunmajjante sma | te ca unmajjyonmajjya yena sa mahāratnastūpo vaihāyasamantarīkṣe sthitaḥ, yasmin sa bhagavān prabhūtaratnastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ, bhagavatā śākyamuninā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena sārdhaṃ siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāmanti sma | upasaṃkramya ca ubhayayostathāgatayorarhatoḥ samyaksaṃbuddhayoḥ pādau śirobhirvanditvā sarvāṃśca tān bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyātmīyān nirmitāṃstathāgatavigrahān ye te samantato daśasu dikṣvanyonyāsu lokadhātuṣu saṃnipatitāḥ, nānāratnavṛkṣamūleṣu siṃhāsanopaviṣṭāḥ, tān sarvānabhivandya namaskṛtya ca anekaśatasahasrakṛtvastāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān pradakṣiṇīkṛtya nānāprakārairbodhisattvastavairabhiṣṭutya ekānte tasthuḥ | añjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ ca prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamabhisaṃmukhaṃ namaskurvanti sma ||
body.translated_text: How much more so of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> with retinues of many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! How much more so of those with retinues of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! How much more so of those with retinues of hundreds of thousands! How much more so of those with retinues of thousands! How much more so of those with retinues of five hundred! How much more so of those with retinues of four hundred, three hundred, or two hundred! How much more so of those with retinues of one hundred! How much more so of those with retinues of fifty <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! And so on in abbreviated form — how much more so of those with retinues of forty, thirty, twenty, ten, five, four, three, or two <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! How much more so of those accompanied by a single companion! How much more so of those without retinues, solitary <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>! Their number, count, comparison, or approximation could not be found — those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who emerged from the crevices of the earth in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. And having emerged, they approached the great jeweled <s>stūpa</s> standing in the sky, in which the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, was seated together with the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, on the lion-throne. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of both <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. And all those emanation-bodies of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, who had gathered from other world-systems in all ten directions and were seated on lion-thrones at the feet of various jewel-trees — to all of them they bowed and paid homage, circumambulating those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones many hundreds of thousands of times, praising them with various kinds of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-praises, and stood to one side. With joined palms, they paid homage face to face to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and to the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena teṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ pṛthivīvivarebhya unmajjatāṃ tathāgatāṃśca vandamānānāṃ nānāprakārairbodhisattvastavairabhiṣṭuvatāṃ paripūrṇāḥ pañcāśadantarakalpā gacchanti sma | tāṃśca pañcāśadantarakalpān sa bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastūṣṇīmabhūt | tāścatasraḥ parṣadastāneva pañcāśadantakalpāṃstūṣṇīṃbhāvenāvasthitā abhūvan | atha khalu bhagavāṃstathārūpamṛddhyabhisaṃskāramakarot, yathārūpeṇa ṛddhyabhisaṃskāreṇābhisaṃskṛtena tāścatasraḥ parṣadastamevaikaṃ paścādbhaktaṃ saṃjānante sma | imāṃ ca sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ śatasahasrākāśaparigṛhītāṃ bodhisattvaparipūrṇāmadrākṣuḥ | tasya khalu punarmahato bodhisattvagaṇasya mahato bodhisattvarāśeścatvāro bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, ye pramukhā abhūvan, tadyathā viśiṣṭacāritraśca nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, anantacāritraśca nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, viśuddhacāritraśca nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ, supratiṣṭhitacāritraśca nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ | ime catvāro bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstasya mahato bodhisattvagaṇasya mahato bodhisattvarāśeḥ pramukhā abhūvan | atha khalu catvāro bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstasya mahato
body.translated_text: Now at that time, while those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> were emerging from the crevices of the earth and paying homage to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and praising them with various kinds of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-praises, a full fifty intermediate <s>kalpas</s> passed. And for those fifty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>, the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, remained silent. And the four assemblies remained in silence for those very fifty intermediate <s>kalpas</s>. Then the Blessed One performed such an exercise of supernatural power that, by such an exercise of supernatural power, the four assemblies perceived it as merely one afternoon. And they saw this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, encompassing a hundred thousand spaces, filled with <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Now, of that great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, there were four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who were the leaders, namely: the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Viśiṣṭacāritra</s> (Superior Conduct), the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Anantacāritra</s> (Infinite Conduct), the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Viśuddhacāritra</s> (Pure Conduct), and the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Supratiṣṭhitacāritra</s> (Firmly Established Conduct). These four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> were the leaders of that great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Then those four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, standing before that great

body.text: bodhisattvagaṇasya mahato bodhisattvarāśeragrataḥ sthitvā bhagavato 'bhimukhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantametadūcuḥ - kaccid bhagavato 'lpābādhatā mandaglānatā sukhasaṃsparśavihāratā ca? kaccid bhagavan sattvāḥ svākārāḥ suvijñāpakāḥ suvineyāḥ suviśodhakāḥ? mā haiva bhagavataḥ khedamutpādayanti ||
body.translated_text: company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with joined palms facing the Blessed One, said to the Blessed One: 'Is the Blessed One in good health, with few ailments, with slight indisposition, dwelling in comfort? Are the beings, O Blessed One, amenable, easy to instruct, easy to tame, easy to purify? Do they not cause fatigue to the Blessed One?'

body.text: atha khalu te catvāro bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhagavantāmābhyāṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> addressed the Blessed One with these two verses:

children.text: kaccit sukhaṃ viharasi lokanātha prabhaṃkara /
children.translated_text: Are you dwelling in happiness, O Lord of the World, O Radiant One?

children.text: ābādhavipramukto 'si sparśaḥ kāye tavānagha // Saddhp_14.1 //
children.translated_text: Are you free from ailments? Is there comfort in your body, O Faultless One? || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.1 ||

children.text: svākārāścaiva te sattvāḥ suvineyāḥ suśodhakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Are your beings amenable, easy to tame, easy to purify?

children.text: mā haiva khedaṃ janayanti lokanāthasya bhāṣataḥ // Saddhp_14.2 //
children.translated_text: May they not cause fatigue to the Lord of the World as he teaches! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.2 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasya mahato bodhisattvagaṇasya mahato bodhisattvarāśeḥ pramukhāṃścaturo bodhisattvān mahāsattvānetadavocat - evametat kulaputrāḥ, evametat | sukhasaṃsparśavihāro 'smi alpābādho mandaglānaḥ | svākārāśca mamaiva te sattvāḥ suvijñāpakāḥ suvineyāḥ suviśodhakāḥ | na ca me khedaṃ janayanti viśodhyamānāḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? mamaiva hyete kulaputrāḥ sattvāḥ paurvakeṣu samyaksaṃbuddheṣu kṛtaparikarmāṇaḥ | darśanādeva hi kulaputrāḥ śravaṇācca mamādhimucyante, buddhajñānamavataranti avagāhante | yatra ye 'pi śrāvakabhūmau vā pratekabuddhabhūmau vā kṛtaparicaryā abhuvan, te 'pi mayaiva etarhi buddhadharmajñānamavatāritāḥ saṃśrāvitāśca paramārtham ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said to the four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who were the leaders of that great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'So it is, sons of good family, so it is. I am dwelling in comfort, with few ailments, with slight indisposition. And those beings of mine are indeed amenable, easy to instruct, easy to tame, easy to purify. And they do not cause me fatigue while being purified. For what reason? For these beings, sons of good family, have been prepared under former Perfectly Awakened Ones. Indeed, sons of good family, merely upon seeing me, merely upon hearing me, they have faith, they penetrate the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, they enter into it. Even those who previously had practiced on the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-stage or the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>-stage — they too have now been brought by me to enter the knowledge of <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharma</s> and have been taught the ultimate truth.'

body.text: atha khalu te bodhisattvā mahāsattvāstasyāṃ velāyāmime gāthe abhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: sādhu sādhu mahāvīra anumodāmahe vayam /
children.translated_text: Excellent, excellent, O Great Hero! We rejoice

children.text: svākārā yena te sattvāḥ suvineyāḥ suśodhakāḥ // Saddhp_14.3 //
children.translated_text: that your beings are amenable, easy to tame, easy to purify. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.3 ||

children.text: ye cedaṃ jñāna gambhīraṃ śṛṇvanti tava nāyaka /
children.translated_text: Those who hear this profound knowledge of yours, O Guide,

children.text: śrutvā ca adhimucyante uttaranti ca nāyaka // Saddhp_14.4 //
children.translated_text: and having heard, have faith in it and penetrate it, O Guide! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.4 ||

body.text: evamukte bhagavāṃstasya mahato bodhisattvagaṇasya mahato bodhisattvarāśeḥ pramukhebhyaścaturbhyo bodhisattvebhyo mahāsattvebhyaḥ sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu kulaputrāḥ, ye yūyaṃ tathāgatamabhinandatha iti ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One gave his approval to those four <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who were the leaders of that great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, sons of good family, that you rejoice in the <s>Tathāgata</s>!'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena maitreyasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya anyeṣāṃ cāṣṭānāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukopamānāṃ bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmetadabhavat - adṛṣṭapūrvo 'yamasmābhirmahābodhisattvagaṇo mahābodhisattvarāśiḥ | aśrutapūrvaśca yo 'yaṃ pṛthivīvivarebhyaḥ samunmajya bhagavataḥ purataḥ sthitvā bhagavantaṃ satkurvanti gurukurvanti mānayanti pūjayanti bhagavantaṃ ca pratisaṃmodante | kutaḥ khalvime bodhisattvā mahāsattvā āgatā iti?
body.translated_text: At that time, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and the other eight <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-numbered <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> had this thought: 'Never before have we seen or heard of this great company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, this great host of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, who, having emerged from the crevices of the earth, stand before the Blessed One and honor, revere, respect, and worship the Blessed One, and exchange greetings with the Blessed One. From where have these <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> come?'

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattva ātmanā vicikitsāṃ kathaṃkathāṃ viditvā teṣāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukopamānāṃ bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ cetasaiva cetaḥ parivitarkamājñāya tasyāṃ velāyāmañjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantaṃ gāthābhigītenaitamevārthaṃ paripṛcchanti sma -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, knowing his own doubt and uncertainty, and understanding through his mind the thoughts of those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, at that time, with joined palms, questioned the Blessed One on this very matter with verses:

children.text: bahusahasrā nayutāḥ koṭīyo ca anantakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Many thousands, <s>nayutas</s>, and <s>koṭis</s>, endless,

children.text: apūrvā bodhisattvānāmakhyāhi dvipadottama // Saddhp_14.5 //
children.translated_text: unprecedented — these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! Declare [their origin], O Supreme among Bipeds! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.5 ||

children.text: kuto ime kathaṃ vāpi āgacchanti maharddhikāḥ /
children.translated_text: From where and how have these mighty ones come?

children.text: mahātmabhāvā rūpeṇa kuta eteṣa āgamaḥ // Saddhp_14.6 //
children.translated_text: Great of nature and form — from where is their coming? || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.6 ||

children.text: dhṛtimantāścime sarve smṛtimanto maharṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All of them are steadfast, mindful, great seers,

children.text: priyadarśanāśca rūpeṇa kuta eteṣa āgamaḥ // Saddhp_14.7 //
children.translated_text: pleasing to behold in form — from where is their coming? || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.7 ||

children.text: ekaikasya ca lokendra bodhisattvasya vijñinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of each wise <s>Bodhisattva</s>, O Lord of the World,

children.text: aprameyaḥ parivāro yathā gaṅgāya vālikāḥ // Saddhp_14.8 //
children.translated_text: the retinue is immeasurable, like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.8 ||

children.text: gaṅgāvālikasamā ṣaṣṭi paripūrṇā yaśasvinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Full sixty, equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, of the illustrious ones,

children.text: parivāro bodhisattvasya sarve bodhāya prasthitāḥ // Saddhp_14.9 //
children.translated_text: is the retinue of each <s>Bodhisattva</s> — all set forth toward awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.9 ||

children.text: evaṃrūpāṇa vīrāṇāṃ parṣavantāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: Of such heroes, possessed of assemblies, protectors,

children.text: ṣaṣṭireva pramāṇena gaṅgāvālikayā ime // Saddhp_14.10 //
children.translated_text: these [number] sixty in measure, by the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.10 ||

children.text: ato bahutarāścānye parivārairanantakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And even more than these, with endless retinues,

children.text: pañcāśatīya gaṅgāya catvāriṃśacca triṃśati // Saddhp_14.11 //
children.translated_text: of fifty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, and forty, and thirty, || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.11 ||

children.text: samo viṃśati gaṅgāyā parivāraḥ samantataḥ /
children.translated_text: and retinues equal to twenty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, on every side —

children.text: ato bahutarāścānye yeṣāṃ daśa ca pañca ca // Saddhp_14.12 //
children.translated_text: And still more numerous are others, whose [retinues number] ten, or five — || Saddhp 14.12 ||

children.text: ekaikasya parīvāro buddhaputrasya tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: as the retinue of each son of the <s>Buddha</s>, each Savior;

children.text: kuto 'yamīdṛśī parṣadāgatādya vināyaka // Saddhp_14.13 //
children.translated_text: whence has such an assembly come today, O Guide? || Saddhp 14.13 ||

children.text: catvāri trīṇi dve cāpi gaṅgāvālikayā samāḥ /
children.translated_text: Four, three, two, or even equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> —

children.text: ekaikasya parīvārā ye 'nuśikṣā sahāyakāḥ // Saddhp_14.14 //
children.translated_text: the retinue of each, who are companions in training! || Saddhp 14.14 ||

children.text: ato bahutarāścānye gaṇanā yeṣvanantikā /
children.translated_text: And still more numerous are others, whose count is endless;

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasreṣu upametuṃ na śaknuyāt // Saddhp_14.15 //
children.translated_text: even in <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> one could not reckon them. || Saddhp 14.15 ||

children.text: ardhagaṅgā tribhāgaśca daśaviṃśatibhāgikaḥ /
children.translated_text: Half a <s>Gaṅgā</s>, a third, a tenth, a twentieth —

children.text: parivāro 'tha vīrāṇāṃ bodhisattvāna tāyinām // Saddhp_14.16 //
children.translated_text: such is the retinue of those heroes, those <s>Bodhisattva</s> Saviors. || Saddhp 14.16 ||

children.text: ato bahutarāścānye pramāṇaiṣāṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And still more numerous are others — their measure cannot be found,

children.text: ekaikaṃ gaṇayantena kalpakoṭīśatairapi // Saddhp_14.17 //
children.translated_text: even reckoning each one individually for hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. || Saddhp 14.17 ||

children.text: ato bahutarāścānye parivārairanantakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And still more numerous are others, with infinite retinues —

children.text: koṭī koṭī ca koṭī ca ardhakoṭī tathaiva ca // Saddhp_14.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>koṭis</s> upon <s>koṭis</s> upon <s>koṭis</s>, and half a <s>koṭi</s> as well! || Saddhp 14.18 ||

children.text: gaṇanāvyativṛttāśca anye bhūyo maharṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: Beyond all counting, and still more of the Great Sages —

children.text: bodhisattvā mahāprajñāḥ sthitāḥ sarve sagauravāḥ // Saddhp_14.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of great wisdom, all standing reverently! || Saddhp 14.19 ||

children.text: parivārasahasraṃ ca śatapañcāśadeva ca /
children.translated_text: A thousand, or a hundred and fifty retinues —

children.text: gaṇanā nāsti eteṣāṃ kalpakoṭīśatairapi // Saddhp_14.20 //
children.translated_text: their count does not exist, even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>! || Saddhp 14.20 ||

children.text: viṃśatiddaśa pañcātha catvāri trīṇi dve tathā /
children.translated_text: Twenty, ten, five, and four, three, two likewise —

children.text: parivāro 'tha vīrāṇāṃ gaṇanaiṣāṃ na vidyate // Saddhp_14.21 //
children.translated_text: these are the retinues of the heroes — their count cannot be found! || Saddhp 14.21 ||

children.text: carantyekātmakā ye ca śāntiṃ vindanti caikakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who wander alone and find peace in solitude —

children.text: gaṇanā teṣa naivāsti ye ihādya samāgatāḥ // Saddhp_14.22 //
children.translated_text: the count of those who have gathered here today cannot be found! || Saddhp 14.22 ||

children.text: gaṅgāvālikāsamān kalpān gaṇayeta yadī naraḥ /
children.translated_text: If a man were to count <s>kalpas</s> equal to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

children.text: śalākāṃ gṛhya hastena paryantaṃ naiva so labhet // Saddhp_14.23 //
children.translated_text: taking a tally-stick in hand — he would never reach the limit! || Saddhp 14.23 ||

children.text: mahātmanāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ vīryantāna tāyinām /
children.translated_text: Of all these great beings, these heroes of vigor, these Saviors,

children.text: bodhisattvāna vīrāṇāṃ kuta eteṣa saṃbhavaḥ // Saddhp_14.24 //
children.translated_text: these <s>Bodhisattva</s> heroes — whence is their origin? || Saddhp 14.24 ||

children.text: kenaiṣāṃ deśito dharmaḥ kena bodhīya sthāpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: By whom was the <s>Dharma</s> taught to them? By whom were they established in awakening?

children.text: rocanti śāsanaṃ kasya kasya śāsanadhārakāḥ // Saddhp_14.25 //
children.translated_text: Whose teaching delights them? Whose teaching do they uphold? || Saddhp 14.25 ||

children.text: bhittvā hi pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ samantena caturdiśam /
children.translated_text: Having split open the entire earth, on all four sides,

children.text: unmajjanti mahāprajñā ṛddhimantā vicakṣaṇāḥ // Saddhp_14.26 //
children.translated_text: they emerge — those of great wisdom, possessed of supernatural powers, discerning! || Saddhp 14.26 ||

children.text: jarjarā lokadhātveyaṃ samantena kṛtā mune /
children.translated_text: This world-system is shaken to pieces, O Sage, on every side,

children.text: unmajjamānairetairhi bodhisattvairviśāradaiḥ // Saddhp_14.27 //
children.translated_text: by these confident <s>Bodhisattvas</s> as they emerge! || Saddhp 14.27 ||

children.text: na hyete jātu asmābhirdṛṣṭapūrvāḥ kadācana /
children.translated_text: Never before have these been seen by us at any time;

children.text: ākhyāhi no tasya nāma lokadhātorvināyaka // Saddhp_14.28 //
children.translated_text: tell us the name of their world-system, O Guide! || Saddhp 14.28 ||

children.text: daśādiśā hi asmābhirañcitāyo punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: We have indeed traversed the ten directions again and again,

children.text: na ca dṛṣṭā ime 'smābhirbodhisattvāḥ kadācana // Saddhp_14.29 //
children.translated_text: yet never have we seen these <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! || Saddhp 14.29 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭo na jāturasmābhireko 'pi tanayastava /
children.translated_text: Never have we seen even a single son of yours;

children.text: ime 'dya sahasā dṛṣṭā ākhyāhi caritaṃ mune // Saddhp_14.30 //
children.translated_text: yet today they are suddenly seen — tell us of their conduct, O Sage! || Saddhp 14.30 ||

children.text: bodhisattvasahasrāṇi śatāni nayutāni ca /
children.translated_text: Thousands, hundreds, <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> —

children.text: sarve kautūhalaprāptāḥ paśyanti dvipadottamam // Saddhp_14.31 //
children.translated_text: all have become curious, gazing at the Supreme among Bipeds. || Saddhp 14.31 ||

children.text: vyākuruṣva mahāvīra aprameya niropadhe /
children.translated_text: Explain, O Great Hero, O Immeasurable One, free from substrate!

children.text: kuta enti ime śūrā bodhisattvā viśāradaḥ // Saddhp_14.32 //
children.translated_text: Whence come these bold, confident <s>Bodhisattvas</s>? || Saddhp 14.32 ||'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena ye te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anyebhyo lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrebhyo 'bhyāgatā bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya nirmitāḥ, ye 'nyeṣu lokadhātuṣu sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayanti sma, ye bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya samantādaṣṭabhyo digbhyo ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu mahāratnasiṃhāsaneṣūpaviṣṭāḥ paryaṅkabaddhāḥ, teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ ye svakasvakā upasthāyakāḥ, te 'pi taṃ mahāntaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ bodhisattvarāśiṃ dṛṣṭvā samantāt pṛthivīvivarebhya unmajjantamākāśadhātupratiṣṭhitam, te 'pyāścaryaprāptāstān svān svāṃstathāgatānetadūcuḥ - kuto bhagavan iyanto bodhisattvā mahāsattvā āgacchantyaprameyā asaṃkhyeyāḥ? evamuktāste tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstān svān svānupasthāyakānetadūcuḥ - āgamayadhvaṃ yūyaṃ kulaputrā muhūrtam | eṣa maitreyo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ śākyamuneranantaraṃ vyākṛto 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau, sa etaṃ bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametamarthaṃ paripṛcchati | eṣa ca bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vyākariṣyati | tato yūyaṃ śroṣyatheti ||
body.translated_text: At that time, those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — the emanations of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> — who had come from <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of other world-systems, who were teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in other world-systems, who were seated cross-legged on great jeweled lion-thrones at the foot of jewel-trees on all sides in the eight directions — their attendants, of those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, they too, upon seeing that great assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, that mass of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, emerging from the crevices of the earth on all sides and standing in the realm of space, were filled with wonder and said this to their respective <s>Tathāgatas</s>: 'Whence, O Blessed One, do so many immeasurable, incalculable <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> come?' Thus addressed, those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones said this to their respective attendants: 'Wait a moment, O sons of good family! This <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Maitreya</s> has been given a prediction of supreme perfect awakening by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> as his immediate successor. He is asking the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, about this matter. And the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, will answer. Then you will hear.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - sādhu sādhu ajita | udārametadajita sthānaṃ yattvaṃ māṃ paripṛcchasi | atha khalu bhagavān sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇamāmantrayate sma - tena hi kulaputrāḥ sarva eva prayatā bhavadhvam | susaṃnaddhā dṛḍhasthāmāśca bhavadhvam, sarvaścāyaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaḥ | tathāgatajñānadarśanaṃ kulaputrāstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sāṃprataṃ saṃprakāśayati, tathāgatavṛṣabhitaṃ tathāgatakarma tathāgatavikrīḍitaṃ tathāgatavijṛmbhitaṃ tathāgataparākramamiti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Ajita</s>! It is a great matter, <s>Ajita</s>, that you ask me about.' Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Therefore, O sons of good family, all of you be attentive! Be well-armored and firm in strength — all this assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O sons of good family, will now reveal the knowledge and vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — the heroic might of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the work of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the sport of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the prowess of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the valor of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: prayatā bhavadhvaṃ kulaputra sarva imāṃ pramuñcāmi girāmananyathām /
children.translated_text: 'Be attentive, all sons of good family! I shall utter this speech that is not otherwise;

children.text: mā khū viṣādaṃ kurutheha paṇḍitā acintiyaṃ jñānu tathāgatānām // Saddhp_14.33 //
children.translated_text: do not, O wise ones, fall into despondency here — inconceivable is the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! || Saddhp 14.33 ||

children.text: dhṛtimanta bhūtvā smṛtimanta sarve samāhitāḥ sarviḥ sthitā bhavadhvam /
children.translated_text: Be all steadfast, mindful, and concentrated — all of you stand [ready]!

children.text: apūrvadharmo śruṇitavyu adya āścaryabhūto hi tathāgatānām // Saddhp_14.34 //
children.translated_text: An unprecedented <s>Dharma</s> is to be heard today — a wonder of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>! || Saddhp 14.34 ||

children.text: vicikitsa mā jātu kurudhva sarve ahaṃ hi yuṣmān parisaṃsthapemi /
children.translated_text: Never entertain doubts, all of you! I shall firmly establish you;

children.text: ananyathāvādirahaṃ vināyako jñānaṃ ca me yasya na kāci saṃkhyā // Saddhp_14.35 //
children.translated_text: I am a Guide whose speech is never otherwise, and my knowledge is beyond all reckoning. || Saddhp 14.35 ||

body.text: gambhīra dharmāḥ sugatena buddhā atarkiyā yeṣa premāṇu nāsti /
body.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> understood by the <s>Sugata</s> are profound, beyond reasoning, without measure;

body.text: tānadya haṃ dharma prakāśayiṣye śṛṇotha me yādṛśakā yathā ca te // Saddhp_14.36 //
body.translated_text: those <s>dharmas</s> I shall now illuminate — listen to me, [and learn] of what nature and how they are! || Saddhp 14.36 ||'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimā gāthā bhāṣitvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ maitrayaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - ārocayāmi te ajita, prativedayāmi | ya ime ajita bodhisattvā aprameyā asaṃkhyeyā acintyā atulyā agaṇanīyāḥ, ye yuṣmābhiradṛṣṭapūrvāḥ, ya etarhi pṛthivīvirebhyo niṣkrāntāḥ, mayaite ajita sarve bodhisattvā mahāsattvā asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya samādāpitāḥ samuttejitāḥ saṃpraharṣitāḥ, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau pariṇāmitāḥ | mayā caite kulaputrā asmin bodhisattvadharme paripācitāḥ pratiṣṭhāpitā niveśitāḥ parisaṃsthāpitā avatāritāḥ paribodhitāḥ pariśodhitāḥ | ete ca ajita bodhisattvā mahāsattvā asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau adhastādākāśadhātuparigrahe prativasanti | svādhyāyoddeśacintāyoniśomanasikārapravṛttā ete kulaputrā asaṃgaṇikārāmā asaṃsargābhiratā anikṣiptadhurā ārabdhavīryāḥ | ete ajita kulaputrā vivekārāmā vivekābhiratāḥ | naite kulaputrā devamanuṣyānupaniśrāya viharanti asaṃsargacaryābhiratāḥ | ete kulaputrā dharmārāmābhiratā buddhajñāne 'bhiyuktāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having spoken these verses, at that time addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'I announce to you, <s>Ajita</s>, I declare to you: These <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O <s>Ajita</s>, immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, incomparable, beyond counting — whom you have never seen before, who have now emerged from the crevices of the earth — all these <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, O <s>Ajita</s>, were in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system inspired, encouraged, gladdened, and directed toward supreme perfect awakening by me, after I had attained supreme perfect awakening. And these sons of good family were by me ripened, established, settled, confirmed, introduced, awakened, and purified in this <s>Bodhisattva Dharma</s>. And these <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, O <s>Ajita</s>, dwell beneath the space-realm of this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. These sons of good family are engaged in self-study, exposition, reflection, and proper attention — they delight in non-association, they rejoice in non-mixing, they have not laid down the burden, they are of aroused vigor. These sons of good family, O <s>Ajita</s>, delight in seclusion and rejoice in seclusion. These sons of good family do not dwell depending on gods or humans — they rejoice in the practice of non-mixing. These sons of good family delight in the <s>Dharma</s> and are devoted to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: ye bodhisattvā ime aprameyā acintiyā yeṣa pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: 'These <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are immeasurable, inconceivable, beyond all measure,

children.text: ṛddhīya prajñāya śrutenupetā bahukalpakoṭīcaritāśca jñāne // Saddhp_14.37 //
children.translated_text: endowed with supernatural power, wisdom, and learning — their conduct in knowledge spans many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. || Saddhp 14.37 ||

children.text: paripācitāḥ sarvi mayaiti bodhaye mamaiva kṣetrasmi vasanti caite /
children.translated_text: All of them were ripened by me toward awakening, and they dwell in my very field;

children.text: paripācitāḥ sarvi mayaiva ete mamaiva putrāścimi bodhisattvāḥ // Saddhp_14.38 //
children.translated_text: all of them were ripened by me alone — these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are my very sons! || Saddhp 14.38 ||

children.text: sarve ti āraṇyadhutābhiyuktāḥ saṃsargabhūmiṃ sada varjayanti /
children.translated_text: All are devoted to forest-dwelling and ascetic practices; they always avoid the grounds of mixing;

children.text: asaṅgacārī ca mamaiti putrā mamottamāṃ caryanuśikṣamāṇāḥ // Saddhp_14.39 //
children.translated_text: they wander free from attachment, these sons of mine — training in my supreme conduct! || Saddhp 14.39 ||

children.text: vasanti ākāśaparigrahe 'smin kṣetrasya heṣṭhā paricāri vīrāḥ /
children.translated_text: They dwell in this spatial realm, beneath the field, wandering as heroes;

children.text: samudānayantā imamagrabodhiṃ udyukta rātriṃdivamapramattāḥ // Saddhp_14.40 //
children.translated_text: accumulating this supreme awakening — striving day and night, unwearied! || Saddhp 14.40 ||

children.text: ārabdhavīryāḥ smṛtimanta sarve prajñābalasmin sthita aprameye /
children.translated_text: All are of aroused vigor, mindful, established in immeasurable power of wisdom;

children.text: viśāradā dharmu kathenti caite prabhāsvarā putra mamaiti sarve // Saddhp_14.41 //
children.translated_text: confident, they teach the <s>Dharma</s> — radiant, all of them are my sons! || Saddhp 14.41 ||

children.text: mayā ca prāpya imamagrabodhiṃ nagare gayāyāṃ drumamūli tatra /
children.translated_text: Having attained this supreme awakening in the city of <s>Gayā</s>, at the foot of the tree,

children.text: anuttaraṃ vartiya dharmacakraṃ paripācitāḥ sarvi ihāgrabodhau // Saddhp_14.42 //
children.translated_text: and having turned the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-wheel — all were ripened here in supreme awakening! || Saddhp 14.42 ||

children.text: anāsravā bhūta iyaṃ mi vācā śruṇitva sarve mama śraddadhadhvam /
children.translated_text: This word of mine is free from outflows — listen, all of you, and have faith in me!

children.text: evaṃ ciraṃ prāpta mayāgrabodhi paripācitāścaiti mayaiva sarve // Saddhp_14.43 //
children.translated_text: Thus for a long time I have attained supreme awakening, and all these were ripened by me alone! || Saddhp 14.43 ||'

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastāni ca saṃbahulāni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyāścaryaprāptānyabhūvan, adbhutaprāptāni vismayaprāptāni - kathaṃ nāma bhagavatā anena kṣaṇavihāreṇa alpena kālāntareṇa amī etāvanto bodhisattvā mahāsattvā asaṃkhyeyāḥ samādāpitāḥ, paripācitāśca anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kathamidānīṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatena kumārabhūtena kapilavastunaḥ śākyanagarānniṣkasya gayānagarānnātidūre bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddhā? tasyādya bhagavan kālasya sātiriṃkāṇi catvāriṃśadvarṣāṇi | tatkathaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatena iyatā kālāntareṇedamaparimitaṃ tathāgatakṛtyaṃ kṛtam, tathāgatena tathāgatavṛṣabhitā tathāgataparākramaḥ kṛtaḥ, yo 'yaṃ bodhisattvagaṇo bodhisattvarāśiriyatā bhagavan kālāntareṇa anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitaḥ paripācitaśca? asya bhagavan bodhisattvagaṇasya bodhisattvarāśergaṇyamānasya kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairapyanto nopalabhyate | evamaprameyā bhagavan ime bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ, evamasaṃkhyeyāściracaritabrahmacaryā bahubuddhaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlā bahukalpaśatasahasrapariniṣpannāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and those many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> were filled with wonder, amazement, and astonishment: 'How indeed did the Blessed One, in such a brief stay, in such a short interval of time, inspire and ripen so many incalculable <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> in supreme perfect awakening?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'How then, O Blessed One, did the <s>Tathāgata</s>, while still a prince, having departed from the <s>Śākya</s> city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and having gone to the supreme seat of awakening not far from the city of <s>Gayā</s>, attain supreme perfect awakening? Barely forty years and a little more have passed since then, O Blessed One. How then, O Blessed One, has the <s>Tathāgata</s> accomplished such immeasurable work of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in such a short interval of time — the heroic might of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the valor of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — that this assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, this mass of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, was in such a short time, O Blessed One, inspired and ripened in supreme perfect awakening? This assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, this mass of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O Blessed One, even when counted for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, their limit cannot be found. So immeasurable, O Blessed One, are these <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> — so incalculable, having practiced celibacy for a long time, having planted roots of merit under many hundred-thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>, having been perfected over many hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>!'

body.text:
tadyathāpi nāma bhagavan kaścideva puruṣo navo daharaḥ śiśuḥ kṛṣṇakeśaḥ prathamena vayasā samanvāgataḥ pañcaviṃśativarṣo jātyā bhavet | sa varṣaśatikān putrānādarśayet, evaṃ ca vadet - ete kulaputrā mama putrā iti | te ca varṣaśatikāḥ puruṣā evaṃ ca vadeyuḥ - eṣo 'smākaṃ pitā janaka iti | tasya ca puruṣasya bhagavaṃstadvacanamaśraddheyaṃ bhavellokasya duḥśraddheyam | evameva bhagavānacirābhisaṃbuddho 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim, ime ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bahvaprameyā
bahukalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasracīrṇacaritabrahmacaryāḥ, dīrgharātraṃ hi kṛtaniścayāḥ, buddhajñāne samādhimukhaśatasahasrasamāpadyanavyutthānakuśalāḥ mahābhijñāparikarmaniryātāḥ mahābhijñākṛtaparikarmāṇaḥ
body.translated_text: It is as if, O Blessed One, some man were new, young, a child with black hair, endowed with the first [bloom of] youth, twenty-five years old by birth. And he were to point out hundred-year-old sons, and say thus: 'These, sons of good family, are my sons.' And those hundred-year-old men would say thus: 'This is our father, our progenitor.' And that man's statement, O Blessed One, would be incredible and difficult to believe for the world. Even so, the Blessed One has only recently attained supreme perfect awakening, while these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, immeasurably many, have practiced the holy life for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>; for a long time they have been firmly resolved, they are skilled in entering and emerging from hundreds of thousands of <s>samādhi</s> doors in <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, they have completed the preparatory practices of the great superknowledges, they have accomplished the preparatory practices of the great superknowledges —

body.text: paṇḍitā buddhabhūmau, saṃgītakuśalāstathāgatadharmāṇām, āścaryādbhutā lokasya mahāvīryabalasthāmaprāptāḥ | tāṃśca bhagavānevaṃ vadati - mayaite ādita eva samādāpitāḥ samuttejitāḥ paripācitāḥ, pariṇāmitāśca asyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāviti | anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhena mayaiṣa sarvavīryaparākramaḥ kṛta iti | kiṃcāpi vayaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatasya vacanaṃ śraddhayāgamiṣyāmaḥ - ananyathāvādī tathāgata iti | tathāgata evaitamarthaṃ jānīyāt | navayānasaṃprasthitāḥ khalu punarbhagavan bodhisattvā mahāsattvā vicikitsāmāpadyante | atra sthāne parinirvṛte tathāgate imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā na pattīyiṣyanti na śraddhāsyanti nādhimokṣyanti | tataste bhagavan dharmavyasanasaṃvartanīyena karmābhisaṃskāreṇa samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti | tatsādhu bhagavan etamevārtha deśaya, yadvayaṃ niḥsaṃśayā asmin dharme bhavema, anāgate 'dhvani bodhisattvayānīyāḥ kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā śrutvā na vicikitsāmāpadyeranniti ||
body.translated_text: — wise on the ground of the <s>Buddhas</s>, skilled in rehearsing the <s>dharmas</s> of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, wondrous and marvelous to the world, endowed with great vigor, strength, and firmness. And the Blessed One says of them: 'These were from the very beginning inspired, encouraged, ripened, and brought to maturity by me on this <s>Bodhisattva</s> ground.' And [he says]: 'Having attained supreme perfect awakening, I made this entire effort of vigor.' Though we, O Blessed One, will accept the word of the <s>Tathāgata</s> on faith — that the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks without contradiction — yet the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself should know this matter [best]. But <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> who have newly set forth on the vehicle will fall into doubt. In this matter, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, they will not trust it, will not believe it, will not have confidence in it. And those, O Blessed One, will become endowed with <s>karmic</s> formations leading to the destruction of the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, O Blessed One, please teach this very matter, so that we may be free from doubt regarding this <s>Dharma</s>, and so that in the future, sons or daughters of good family following the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle, having heard this, may not fall into doubt.

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantamābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, at that time, addressed the Blessed One with these verses:

children.text: yadāsi jāto kapilāhvayasmin śākyādhivāse abhiniṣkramitvā /
children.translated_text: When you were born in [the city] called <s>Kapila</s>, the dwelling of the <s>Śākyas</s>, having gone forth,

children.text: prāpto 'si bodhiṃ nagare gayāhvaye kālo 'yamalpo 'tra tu lokanātha // Saddhp_14.44 //
children.translated_text: you attained awakening in the city called <s>Gayā</s> — this time is but brief, O Lord of the World! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.44 ||

children.text: ime ca te ārya viśāradā bahū ye kalpakoṭīcaritā mahāgaṇī /
children.translated_text: But these noble ones, confident and many, whose great assembly has practiced for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: ṛddhībale ca sthita aprakampitāḥ suśikṣitāḥ prajñabale gatiṃgatāḥ // Saddhp_14.45 //
children.translated_text: established in the power of supernatural ability, unshakable, well-trained, having penetrated the power of wisdom — || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.45 ||

children.text: anūpaliptāḥ padumaṃ va vāriṇā bhittvā mahīṃ ye iha adya āgatāḥ /
children.translated_text: unstained like a lotus by water, having burst through the earth, they have come here today,

children.text: kṛtāñjalī sarvi sthitāḥ sagauravāḥ smṛtimanta lokādhipatisya putrāḥ // Saddhp_14.46 //
children.translated_text: all standing with palms joined, respectful, mindful — the sons of the Lord of the World! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.46 ||

children.text: kathaṃ imaṃ adbhutamīdṛśaṃ te taṃ śraddadhiṣyantimi bodhisattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: How will these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> believe this wondrous thing of such a kind?

children.text: vicikitsanirghātanahetu bhāṣa taṃ tvaṃ caiva deśehi yathaiva arthaḥ // Saddhp_14.47 //
children.translated_text: Speak that which will destroy [their] doubts — and do you teach it exactly as it is! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.47 ||

children.text: yathā hi puruṣo iha kaścideva daharo bhaveyā śiśu kṛṣṇakeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is as if some man here were young, a child with black hair,

children.text: jātyā ca so viṃśatiruttare vā darśeti putrān śatavarṣajātān // Saddhp_14.48 //
children.translated_text: twenty or a little more in age — and he points out hundred-year-old sons. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.48 ||

children.text: valīhi palitehi ca te upetā eṣo ca no dehakaro ti brūyuḥ /
children.translated_text: And they, endowed with wrinkles and gray hair, would say: 'This one is our progenitor!'

children.text: duḥśraddadhaṃ tadbhavi lokanātha daharasya putrā imi evarūpāḥ // Saddhp_14.49 //
children.translated_text: That is incredible, O Lord of the World — that sons of such a kind belong to one so young! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.49 ||

children.text: emeva bhagavāṃśca navo vayasthaḥ ime ca vijñā bahubodhisattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, the Blessed One is new and youthful, and these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are wise and many,

children.text: smṛtimanta prajñāya viśāradāśca suśikṣitāḥ kalpasahasrakoṭiṣu // Saddhp_14.50 //
children.translated_text: mindful and confident in wisdom, well-trained through thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.50 ||

children.text: dhṛtimanta prajñāya vicakṣaṇāśca prāsādikā darśaniyāśca sarve /
children.translated_text: steadfast, discerning in wisdom, beautiful and comely to behold — all of them

children.text: viśāradā dharmaviniścayeṣu parisaṃstutā lokavināyakehi // Saddhp_14.51 //
children.translated_text: confident in determinations of the <s>Dharma</s>, praised by the guides of the world! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.51 ||

children.text: asaṅgacārī pavaneva santi ākāśadhātau satataṃ aniśritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Wandering unattached like the wind, always unattached in the realm of space,

children.text: jānenti vīryaṃ sugatasya putrāḥ paryeṣamāṇā ima buddhabhūmim // Saddhp_14.52 //
children.translated_text: these sons of the <s>Sugata</s> know vigor — seeking this <s>Buddha</s>-ground! || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.52 ||

children.text: kathaṃ nu śraddheyamidaṃ bhaveyā parinirvṛte lokavināyakasmin /
children.translated_text: How could this be believed, when the Guide of the World has passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>?

children.text: vicikitsa asmāka na kācidasti śṛṇomathā saṃmukha lokanāthā // Saddhp_14.53 //
children.translated_text: We have no doubt — we hear it face to face from the Lord of the World. || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.53 ||

children.text: vicikitsa kṛtvāna imasmi sthāne gaccheyu mā durgati bodhisattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: But lest, having generated doubt in this matter, the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> go to an unfortunate destiny,

children.text: tvaṃ vyākuruṣvā bhagavan yathāvat katha bodhisattvāḥ paripācitā ime // Saddhp_14.54 //
children.translated_text: please do explain, O Blessed One, as it truly is — how were these <s>Bodhisattvas</s> ripened? || <s>Saddhp</s> 14.54 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye bodhisattvapṛthivīvivarasamudgamaparivarto nāma caturdaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fourteenth chapter, named 'The Chapter on the Emergence of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> from the Crevices of the Earth' (<s>Bodhisattvapṛthivīvivarasamudgamaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_15: tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 15: The Chapter on the Measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Lifespan (<s>Tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇaparivarta</s>).
