body.text: atha khalu bhagavān sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇamāmantrayate sma - avakalpayadhvaṃ me kulaputrāḥ, abhiśraddadhadhvaṃ tathāgatasya bhūtāṃ vācaṃ vyāharataḥ | dvitīyakamapi bhagavāṃstān bodhisattvānāmantrayate sma - avakalpayadhvaṃ me kulaputrāḥ, abhiśraddadhadhvaṃ tathāgatasya bhutāṃ vācaṃ vyāharataḥ | tṛtīyakamapi bhagavāṃstan bodhisattvānāmantrayate sma - avakalpayadhvaṃ me kulaputrāḥ, abhiśraddadhadhvaṃ tathāgatasya bhūtāṃ vācaṃ vyāharataḥ | atha khalu sa sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇo maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamagrataḥ sthāpayitvā añjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantametadavocat - bhāṣatu bhagavānetamevārtham, bhāṣatu sugataḥ | vayaṃ tathāgatasya bhāṣitamabhiśraddhāsyāmaḥ | dvitīyakamapi sa sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇo bhagavantametadavocat - bhāṣatu bhagavānetamevārtham, bhāṣatu sugataḥ | vayaṃ tathāgatasya bhāṣitamabhiśraddhāsyāmaḥ | tṛtīyakamapi sa sarvāṃvān bodhisattvagaṇo bhagavantametadavocat - bhāṣatu bhagavānetamevārtham, bhāṣatu sugataḥ | vayaṃ tathāgatasya bhāṣitamabhiśraddhāsyāma iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Believe me, O sons of good family! Trust the truthful words that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is about to speak!' A second time the Blessed One addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Believe me, O sons of good family! Trust the truthful words that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is about to speak!' A third time the Blessed One addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Believe me, O sons of good family! Trust the truthful words that the <s>Tathāgata</s> is about to speak!' Then that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, placing the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> at their head, with palms joined, said this to the Blessed One: 'Speak, O Blessed One, this very matter! Speak, O <s>Sugata</s>! We will trust the words of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!' A second time that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Speak, O Blessed One, this very matter! Speak, O <s>Sugata</s>! We will trust the words of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!' A third time that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Speak, O Blessed One, this very matter! Speak, O <s>Sugata</s>! We will trust the words of the <s>Tathāgata</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃsteṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ yāvattṛtīyakamapyadhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā tān bodhisattvānāmantrayate sma - tena hi kulaputrāḥ śṛṇudhvamidamevaṃrūpaṃ mamādhiṣṭhānabalādhānam, yadayaṃ kulaputrāḥ sadevamānuṣāsuro loka evaṃ saṃjānīte - sāṃprataṃ bhagavatā śākyamuninā tathāgatena śākyakulādabhiniṣkramya gayāhvaye mahānagare bodhimaṇḍavarāgragatena anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddheti | naivaṃ draṣṭavyam | api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ bahūni mama kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya | tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ pañcāśatsu lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu ye pṛthivīdhātuparamāṇavaḥ, atha khalu kaścideva puruṣa utpadyate | sa ekaṃ paramāṇurajaṃ gṛhītvā pūrvasyāṃ diśi pañcāśallokadhātvasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya tadekaṃ paramāṇurajaḥ samupanikṣipet | anena paryāyeṇa kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sa puruṣaḥ sarvāṃstāṃllokadhātūna vyapagatapṛthivīdhātūn kuryāt, sarvāṇi ca tāni pṛthivīdhātuparamāṇurajāṃsi anena paryāyeṇa anena ca lakṣanikṣepeṇa pūrvasyāṃ diśyupanikṣipet | tatkiṃ manyadhve kulaputrāḥ śakyaṃ te lokadhātavaḥ kenaciccintayituṃ vā gaṇayituṃ vā tulayituṃ vā upalakṣayituṃ vā? evamukte maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sa ca sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇo bodhisattvarāśirbhagavantametadavocat - asaṃkhyeyāste bhagavaṃllokadhātavaḥ, agaṇanīyāścittabhūmisamatikrāntāḥ | sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairapi bhagavan āryeṇa jñānena na śakyaṃ cintayituṃ vā gaṇayituṃ vā tulayituṃ vā upalakṣayituṃ vā | asmākamapi tāvad bhagavan avaivartyabhūmisthitānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmasmin sthāne cittagocaro na pravartate | tāvadaprameyā bhagavaṃste lokadhātavo bhaveyuriti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing the entreaty of those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> even to the third time, addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Then listen, O sons of good family, to the power of the sustaining authority of this kind of mine. This world with its gods, humans, and <s>asuras</s>, O sons of good family, understands thus: "The Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, having gone forth from the <s>Śākya</s> clan, having gone to the supreme seat of awakening in the great city called <s>Gayā</s>, has attained supreme perfect awakening." But it should not be seen thus. Rather, O sons of good family, many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> have passed since I attained supreme perfect awakening. Suppose, O sons of good family, in fifty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, there were atoms of earth-substance. Then some man might arise. He would take one atom and, proceeding in the eastern direction, traversing fifty incalculable hundred-thousands of world-systems, would deposit that one atom. In this manner, over <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, that man would cause all those world-systems to be deprived of earth-substance, and all those atoms of earth-substance, by this method and this manner of depositing markers, he would deposit in the eastern direction. What do you think, O sons of good family — can those world-systems be conceived of, or counted, or estimated, or discerned by anyone?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> and that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the multitude of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, said this to the Blessed One: 'Those world-systems, O Blessed One, are incalculable, innumerable, beyond the reach of thought. Not even with noble wisdom, O Blessed One, would all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> be able to conceive of, count, estimate, or discern them. For us too, O Blessed One, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> established on the irreversible stage — in this matter, the range of thought does not extend. So immeasurable, O Blessed One, would those world-systems be.'

body.text:
evamukte bhagavāṃstān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānetadavocat - ārocayāmi vaḥ kulaputrāḥ, prativedayāmi vaḥ | yāvantaḥ kulaputrāste lokadhātavo yeṣu tena puruṣeṇa tāni paramāṇurajāṃsyupanikṣiptāni, yeṣu ca nopanikṣiptāni, sarveṣu teṣu kulaputra lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu na tāvanti paramāṇurajāṃsi saṃvidyante, yāvanti mama kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhasya | yataḥprabhṛtyahaṃ kulaputrā asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayāmi, anyeṣu ca lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu, ye ca mayā kulaputrā atrāntarā tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ parikīrtitā dīpaṃkaratathāgataprabhṛtayaḥ, teṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ parinirvāṇāni, mayaiva tāni kulaputrā upāyakauśalyadharmadeśanābhinirhāranirmitāni | api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ, tathāgata āgatāgatānāṃ sattvānāmindriyavīryavaimātratāṃ vyavalokya tasmiṃstasminnātmano nāma vyāharati | tasmiṃstasmiṃścātmanaḥ parinirvāṇaṃ vyāharati, tathā tathā ca sattvān paritoṣayati nānāvidhairdharmaparyāyaiḥ | tatra kulaputrāstathāgato nānādhimuktānāṃ sattvānāmalpakuśalamūlānāṃ bahūpakleśānāmevaṃ vadati - daharo 'hamasmi bhikṣavo jātyābhiniṣkrāntaḥ | acirābhisaṃbuddho 'smi bhikṣavo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim | yatkhalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ, tathāgata evaṃ cirābhisaṃbuddha evaṃ vyāharati - acirābhisaṃbuddho 'hamasmīti, nānyatra sattvānāṃ paripācanārtham | avatāraṇārthamete dharmaparyāyā bhāṣitāḥ | sarve ca te kulaputrā dharmaparyāyāstathāgatena sattvānāṃ vinayārthāya bhāṣitāḥ |
yāṃ ca kulaputrāstathāgataḥ sattvānāṃ vinayārthavācaṃ bhāṣate ātmopadarśanena vā paropadarśanena vā, ātmārambaṇena vā parārambanena vā yatkiṃcittathāgato vyāharati, sarve te dharmaparyāyāḥ satyāstathāgatena bhāṣitāḥ | nāstyatra tathāgatasya mṛṣāvādaḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? dṛṣṭaṃ hi tathāgatena traidhātukaṃ yathābhūtam | na jāyate na mriyate na cyavate nopapadyate na saṃsarati na parinirvāti, na bhūtaṃ nābhūtaṃ na santaṃ nāsantaṃ na tathā nānyathā na vitathā nāvitathā | na tathā traidhātukaṃ tathāgatena dṛṣṭaṃ yathā bālapṛthagjanāḥ paśyanti | pratyakṣadharmā tathāgataḥ khalvasmin sthāne 'saṃpramoṣadharmā | tatra tathāgato yāṃ kāṃcidvācaṃ vyāharati, sarvaṃ tatsatyaṃ na mṛṣā nānyathā | api tu khalu punaḥ sattvānāṃ nānācaritānāṃ nānābhiprāyāṇāṃ saṃjñāvikalpacaritānāṃ kuśalamūlasaṃjananārthaṃ vividhān dharmaparyāyān vividhairārambaṇairvyāharati | yaddhi kulaputrāstathāgatena kartavyaṃ tattathāgataḥ karoti | tāvaccirābhisaṃbuddho 'parimitāyuṣpramāṇastathāgataḥ sadā sthitaḥ | aparinirvṛtastathāgataḥ parinirvāṇamādarśayati vaineyavaśena | na ca tāvanme kulaputrā adyāpi paurvikī bodhisattvacaryāṃ pariniṣpāditā | āyuṣpramāṇamapyaparipūrṇam | api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputrā adyāpi taddviguṇena me kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi bhaviṣyanti āyuṣpramāṇasyāparipūrṇatvāt | idānīṃ
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One spoke thus to those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>: 'I declare to you, sons of good family, I announce: as many world-systems as there are, sons of good family, in which that man deposited those atoms of dust, and in which he did not deposit them — in all those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, there are not as many atoms of dust as there are <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> since I attained supreme perfect awakening. From the time, sons of good family, that I have been teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system and in other <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems — and those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones whom I mentioned in between, beginning with <s>Dīpaṃkara</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, and [those whom I declared to have had] <s>parinirvāṇas</s> — all of those, sons of good family, were produced by me through skillful means in <s>Dharma</s>-teaching. Moreover, sons of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, examining the varying faculties and vigor of beings who come and come [to him], announces different names for himself in each case, and announces his own <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in each case, and satisfies beings in various ways with various <s>Dharma</s>-discourses. In this regard, sons of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> says to beings of different inclinations, with few wholesome roots, with many defilements: "I am young, O monks! I went forth in my youth. I have recently attained supreme perfect awakening, O monks." But, sons of good family, when the <s>Tathāgata</s>, who has attained awakening so long ago, declares thus: "I have recently attained awakening" — it is for no other purpose than the ripening of beings. These <s>Dharma</s>-discourses are spoken for the purpose of leading [beings] in. All those <s>Dharma</s>-discourses, sons of good family, are spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> for the purpose of disciplining beings. Whatever word the <s>Tathāgata</s> speaks for the purpose of disciplining beings — whether by showing himself or by showing others, whether taking himself as the object or others as the object — whatever the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares, all those <s>Dharma</s>-discourses are true, spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. There is no false speech by the <s>Tathāgata</s> in this regard. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgata</s> has seen the triple world as it truly is: it is not born, does not die, does not decease, is not reborn, does not transmigrate, does not enter <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; it is neither real nor unreal, neither existent nor non-existent, neither thus nor otherwise, neither false nor not false. The <s>Tathāgata</s> does not see the triple world as ordinary foolish beings see it. The <s>Tathāgata</s> is indeed one who directly perceives <s>dharmas</s> in this matter, one whose perception is unfailing. In this regard, whatever word the <s>Tathāgata</s> declares, all of it is true, not false, not otherwise. However, sons of good family, for beings of varied conduct, varied intentions, who act through conceptions and discriminations, for the purpose of generating wholesome roots, he declares various <s>Dharma</s>-discourses with various objects. What the <s>Tathāgata</s> must do, that the <s>Tathāgata</s> does. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, who attained awakening so long ago, whose lifespan is immeasurable, always abides. The <s>Tathāgata</s> has not entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — he displays <s>parinirvāṇa</s> according to the needs of those to be disciplined. Moreover, sons of good family, even now my former <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career has not been completed. My lifespan too is not yet fulfilled. Furthermore, sons of good family, even now twice that many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> shall remain of my lifespan that is not yet fulfilled. Now,

body.text:
khalu punarahaṃ kulaputrā aparinirvāyamāṇa eva parinirvāṇamārocayāmi | tatkasya hetoḥ? sattvānahaṃ kulaputrā anena paryāyeṇa paripācayāmi - mā haiva me 'ticiraṃ tiṣṭhato 'bhīkṣṇadarśanena akṛtakuśalamūlāḥ sattvāḥ puṇyavirahitā daridrabhūtāḥ kāmalolupā andhā dṛṣṭijālasaṃchannāḥ tiṣṭhati tathāgata iti viditvā kilīkṛtasaṃjñā bhaveyuḥ, na ca tathāgate durlabhasaṃjñāmutpādayeyuḥ - āsannā vayaṃ tathāgatasyeti | vīryaṃ nārabheyustraidhātukānniḥsaraṇārtham, na ca tathāgate durlabhasaṃjñāmutpādayeyuḥ | tataḥ kulaputrāḥ tathāgataḥ upāyakauśalyena teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ durlabhaprādurbhāvo bhikṣavastathāgata iti vācaṃ vyāharati sma | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ bahubhiḥ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairapi tathāgatadarśanaṃ
bhavati vā na vā | tataḥ khalvahaṃ kulaputrāstadārambaṇaṃ kṛtvaivaṃ vadāmi - durlabhaprādurbhāvā hi bhikṣavastathāgatā iti | te bhūyasyā mātrayā durlabhaprādurbhāvāṃstathāgatān viditvā āścaryasaṃjñāmutpādayiṣyanti, śokasaṃjñāmutpādayiṣyanti | apaśyantaśca tathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhān tṛṣitā bhaviṣyanti tathāgatadarśanāya | teṣāṃ tāni tathāgatārambaṇamanaskārakuśalamūlāni dīrgharātramarthāya hitāya sukhāya ca bhaviṣyanti | etamarthaṃ viditvā tathāgato 'parinirvāyanneva parinirvāṇamārocayati sattvānāṃ vaineyavaśamupādāya | tathāgatasyaiṣa kulaputrā dharmaparyāyo yadevaṃ vyāharati | nāstyatra tathāgatasya mṛṣāvādaḥ ||
body.translated_text: sons of good family, even though I am not actually entering <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I announce <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? By this method, sons of good family, I ripen beings — lest beings, through seeing me constantly present for too long, beings who have not cultivated wholesome roots, who are devoid of merit, who have become impoverished, who are greedy for sensual pleasures, who are blind, covered by a net of wrong views — knowing that the <s>Tathāgata</s> abides, might develop a perception of triviality and not generate a perception of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as rare [thinking]: "We are near the <s>Tathāgata</s>" — they might not generate vigor for escape from the triple world, and might not generate a perception of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as rare. Therefore, sons of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, by skillful means, declares to those beings: "Rare is the appearance of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, O monks!" For what reason? Indeed, for those beings, even through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, they may or may not obtain a vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Therefore, sons of good family, taking that as the basis, I say thus: "Rare is the appearance of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O monks!" Those [beings], having known to a greater degree that <s>Tathāgatas</s> are rare in appearance, will generate a perception of wonder and a perception of sorrow. Not seeing the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, they will become thirsty for a vision of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Their wholesome roots, arising from mental attention directed toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>, will be for their benefit, welfare, and happiness through the long night [of <s>saṃsāra</s>]. Understanding this purpose, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, even though not actually entering <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, announces <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, taking into account the needs of those to be disciplined. This, sons of good family, is the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, when he declares thus. There is no false speech by the <s>Tathāgata</s> herein.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma kulaputrāḥ kaścideva vaidyapuruṣo bhavet paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī sukuśalaḥ sarvavyādhipraśamanāya | tasya ca puruṣasya bahavaḥ putrā bhaveyurdaśa vā viṃśatirvā triṃśadvā catvāriṃśadvā pañcāśadvā śataṃ vā | sa ca vaidyaḥ pravāsagato bhavet, te cāsya sarve putrā garapīḍā vā viṣapīḍā vā bhaveyuḥ | tena gareṇa vā viṣeṇa vā duḥkhābhirvedanābhirabhitūrṇā bhaveyuḥ | te tena gareṇa vā viṣeṇa vā dahyamānāḥ pṛthivyāṃ prapateyuḥ | atha sa teṣāṃ vaidyaḥ pitā pravāsādāgacchet | te cāsya putrāstena gareṇa vā viṣeṇa vā duḥkhābhirvedanābhirārtāḥ | kecidviparītasaṃjñino bhaveyuḥ, kecidaviparītasaṃjñino bhaveyuḥ | sarve ca te tenaiva duḥkhenārtāstaṃ pitaraṃ dṛṣṭvābhinandeyuḥ, evaṃ cainaṃ vadeyuḥ - diṣṭyāsi tāta kṣemasvastibhyāmāgataḥ | tadasmākamasmādātmoparodhād garādvā viṣādvā parimocayasva | dadasva nastāta jīvitamiti | atha khalu sa vaidyastān putrān duḥkhārtān dṛṣṭvā vedanābhibhūtān dahyataḥ pṛthivyāṃ pariveṣṭamānān, tato mahābhaiṣajyaṃ samudānayitvā varṇasaṃpannaṃ gandhasaṃpannaṃ rasasaṃpannaṃ ca, śilāyāṃ piṣṭvā teṣāṃ putrāṇāṃ pānāya dadyāt, evaṃ cainān vadet - pibatha putrā idaṃ mahābhaiṣajyaṃ varṇasaṃpannaṃ gandhasaṃpannaṃ rasasaṃpannam | idaṃ yūyaṃ putrā mahābhaiṣajyaṃ pītvā kṣipramevāsmād garādvā viṣādvā parimokṣyadhve, svasthā bhaviṣyatha arogāśca | tatra ye tasya vaidyasya putrā aviparītasaṃjñinaḥ te bhaiṣajyasya varṇaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā gandhaṃ cāghrāya rasaṃ cāsvādya kṣipramevābhyavahareyuḥ | te cābhyavaharantastasmādābādhāt sarveṇa sarvaṃ vimuktā bhaveyuḥ | ye punastasya putrā viparītasaṃjñinaḥ te taṃ pitaramabhinandeyuḥ, enaṃ caivaṃ vadeyuḥ - diṣṭayāsi tāta kṣemasvastibhyāmāgato yastvamasmākaṃ cikitsaka iti |
body.translated_text: 'It is as if, sons of good family, there were a physician, a wise, learned, intelligent man, skilled in the pacification of all diseases. That man might have many sons — ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or a hundred. That physician might go abroad, and all his sons might become afflicted by poison or venom. Tormented by painful sensations from that poison or venom, burning with that poison or venom, they would fall writhing on the ground. Then that physician, their father, would return from abroad. Those sons of his would be suffering, tormented by painful sensations from that poison or venom. Some might have deranged perceptions, and some might have underanged perceptions. All of them, tormented by that very suffering, upon seeing their father, would rejoice and say to him: "It is fortunate that you, father, have arrived safely and in good health! Deliver us from this self-destruction caused by poison or venom! Give us life, father!" Then that physician, seeing those sons in pain, overcome by sensations, burning and writhing on the ground, having prepared from that a great medicine — perfect in color, perfect in smell, and perfect in taste — ground it on a stone and gave it to those sons to drink, saying: "Drink, my sons, this great medicine, perfect in color, smell, and taste. Having drunk this great medicine, you, my sons, will quickly be freed from this poison or venom; you will be healthy and free from disease." Then those sons of the physician who had underanged perceptions, seeing the color of the medicine, smelling its scent, and tasting its flavor, would quickly consume it. And upon consuming it, they would be completely freed from that ailment. But those sons of his who had deranged perceptions would rejoice at their father and say to him: "It is fortunate that you, father, have arrived safely and in good health, you who are our healer!"

body.text:
te caivaṃ vācaṃ bhāṣeran, tacca bhaiṣajyamupanāmitaṃ na pibeyuḥ | tatkasya hetoḥ? tathā hi teṣāṃ tayā viparītasaṃjñyā tad bhaiṣajyamupanāmitaṃ varṇenāpi na rocate, gandhenāpi rasenāpi na rocate | atha khalu sa vaidyapuruṣa evaṃ cintayet - ime mama putrā anena gareṇa vā viṣeṇa vā viparītasaṃjñinaḥ | te khalvidaṃ mahābhaiṣajyaṃ
na pibanti, māṃ cābhinandanti | yannavahamimān putrānupāyakauśalyena idaṃ bhaiṣajyaṃ pāyayeyamiti | atha khalu sa vaidyastān putrānupāyakauśalyena tadbhaiṣajyaṃ pāyayitukāma evaṃ vadet - jīrṇo 'hamasmi kulaputrāḥ, vṛddho mahallakaḥ | kālakriyā ca me pratyupasthitā | mā ca yūyaṃ putrāḥ śociṣṭha, mā ca klamamāpadhvam | idaṃ vo mayā mahābhaiṣajyamupanītam | sacedākāṅkṣadhve, tadeva bhaiṣajyaṃ pibadhvam | sa evaṃ tān putrānupāyakauśalyena anuśiṣya anyataraṃ janapadapradeśaṃ prakrāntaḥ | tatra gatvā kālagatamātmānaṃ yeṣāṃ glānānāṃ putrāṇāmārocayet, te tasmin samaye 'tīva śocayeyuḥ, atīva parideveyuḥ - yo hyasmākaṃ pitā nātho janako 'nukampakaḥ so 'pi nāmaikaḥ kālagataḥ, te 'dya vayamanāthāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ | te khalvanāthabhūtamātmānaṃ samanupaśyanto 'śaraṇamātmānaṃ samanupaśyanto 'bhīkṣṇaṃ śokārtā bhaveyuḥ | teṣāṃ ca tayābhīkṣṇaṃ śokārtatayā sā viparītasaṃjñā aviparītasaṃjñā bhavet | yacca tad bhaiṣajyaṃ varṇagandharasopetaṃ tadvarṇagandharasopetameva saṃjānīyuḥ | tatastasmin samaye tadbhaiṣajyamabhyavahareyuḥ | te cābhyavaharantastasmādābādhāt parimuktā bhaveyuḥ | atha khalu sa vaidyastān putrānābādhavimuktān viditvā punarevātmānamupadarśayet | tatkiṃ manyadhve kulaputrā mā haiva tasya vaidyasya tadupāyakauśalyaṃ kurvataḥ kaścinmṛṣāvādena saṃcodayet? āhuḥ - no hīdaṃ bhagavan, no hīdaṃ sugata | āha - evameva kulaputrāḥ ahamapyaprameyāsaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrābhisaṃbuddha imāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim | api tu khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ ahamantarāntaramevaṃrūpāṇyupāyakauśalyāni sattvānāmupadarśayāmi vinayārtham | na ca me kaścidatra sthāne mṛṣāvādo bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Yet, though they spoke such words, they would not drink the medicine that was offered. For what reason? Because, with their deranged perceptions, that medicine offered to them was neither pleasing in color, nor in smell, nor in taste. Then that physician might think: "These sons of mine have deranged perceptions from this poison or venom. They do not drink this great medicine, yet they rejoice at me. Surely I should, by skillful means, cause these sons to drink this medicine." Then that physician, wishing to make those sons drink that medicine by skillful means, would say: "I am old, sons of good family, aged and decrepit. My death is approaching. Do not grieve, sons, do not be distressed! This great medicine has been prepared by me for you. If you wish, drink this medicine." Having thus instructed those sons by skillful means, he departed to another region of the country. Having gone there, he would send word to those sick sons that he had died. At that time they would grieve exceedingly, lament exceedingly: "He who was our father, protector, progenitor, and compassionate one — he alone has died! Now we have become fatherless!" Perceiving themselves as fatherless, perceiving themselves as without refuge, they would become constantly afflicted by grief. And through that constant affliction of grief, their deranged perceptions would become underanged. They would perceive the medicine endowed with color, smell, and taste as truly endowed with color, smell, and taste. At that time they would consume that medicine, and upon consuming it, they would be freed from their ailment. Then that physician, knowing those sons to be freed from their ailment, would show himself again. What do you think, sons of good family — could anyone accuse that physician of false speech for performing such skillful means?' They replied: 'No indeed, Blessed One! No indeed, <s>Sugata</s>!' He said: 'Just so, sons of good family, I too, immeasurable, innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> ago, attained this supreme perfect awakening. However, sons of good family, from time to time I display such skillful means to beings for the purpose of disciplining them. And there is no false speech by me in this matter.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavānimāmeva arthagatiṃ bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃdarśayamānastasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, displaying this very meaning to an even greater degree, at that moment spoke these verses:

children.text: acintiyā kalpasahasrakoṭyo yāsāṃ pramāṇaṃ na kadāci vidyate /
children.translated_text: 'Inconceivable are the thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> whose measure is never found;

children.text: prāptā mayā eṣa tadāgrabodhirdharmaṃ ca deśemyahu nityakālam // Saddhp_15.1 //
children.translated_text: I attained that supreme awakening, and I teach the <s>Dharma</s> constantly and always. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.1 ||

children.text: samādapemī bahubodhisattvān bauddhasmi jñānasmi sthapemi caiva /
children.translated_text: I exhort many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and establish them in the <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.

children.text: sattvāna koṭīnayutānanekān paripācayāmī bahukalpakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_15.2 //
children.translated_text: I ripen <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings, many, through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.2 ||

children.text: nirvāṇabhūmiṃ cupadarśayāmi vinayārtha sattvāna vadāmyupāyam /
children.translated_text: I show the stage of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and for the sake of taming beings I teach skill in means,

children.text: na cāpi nirvāmyahu tasmi kāle ihaiva co dharmu prakāśayāmi // Saddhp_15.3 //
children.translated_text: yet I do not pass into <s>nirvāṇa</s> at that time — right here I illuminate the <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.3 ||

children.text: tatrāpi cātmānamadhiṣṭhahāmi sarvāṃśca sattvāna tathaiva cāham /
children.translated_text: There too I sustain myself and likewise all beings,

children.text: viparītabuddhī ca narā vimūḍhāḥ tatraiva tiṣṭhantu na paśyiṣū mām // Saddhp_15.4 //
children.translated_text: but people of perverted understanding, deluded, though I stand right there, do not see me. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.4 ||

children.text: parinirvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭva mamātmabhāvaṃ dhātūṣu pūjāṃ vividhāṃ karonti /
children.translated_text: Seeing my bodily form as having passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, they perform various worship to the relics,

children.text: māṃ cā apaśyanti janenti tṛṣṇāṃ tatorjukaṃ citta prabhoti teṣām // Saddhp_15.5 //
children.translated_text: and not seeing me, they develop longing — thereupon their minds become straightforward. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.5 ||

children.text: ṛjū yadā te mṛdumārdavāśca utsṛṣṭakāmāśca bhavanti sattvāḥ /
children.translated_text: When those beings become straightforward, gentle, tender,

children.text: tato ahaṃ śrāvakasaṃgha kṛtvāḥ ātmāna darśemyahu gṛdhrakūṭe // Saddhp_15.6 //
children.translated_text: and have abandoned desires, then I, having assembled the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>saṃgha</s>, show myself on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.6 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca haṃ teṣa vadāmi paścāt ihaiva nāhaṃ tada āsi nirvṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus I say to them afterward: 'I was not then passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> here;

children.text: upāyakauśalya mameti bhikṣavaḥ punaḥ puno bhomyahu jīvaloke // Saddhp_15.7 //
children.translated_text: this is my skill in means, O monks — again and again I am born in the world of the living.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.7 ||

children.text: anyehi sattvehi puraskṛto 'haṃ teṣāṃ prakāśemi mamāgrabodhim /
children.translated_text: Attended by other beings, I illuminate to them my supreme awakening,

children.text: yūyaṃ ca śabdaṃ na śṛṇotha mahyaṃ anyatra so nirvṛtu lokanāthaḥ // Saddhp_15.8 //
children.translated_text: but you do not hear my voice, [thinking] 'Elsewhere that Lord of the World has passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.8 ||

children.text: paśyāmyahaṃ sattva vihanyamānān na cāhu darśemi tadātmabhāvam /
children.translated_text: I see beings afflicted, yet I do not show them my bodily form;

children.text: spṛhentu tāvanmama darśanasya tṛṣitāna saddharmu prakāśayiṣye // Saddhp_15.9 //
children.translated_text: let them first long for the sight of me — then I shall illuminate the true <s>Dharma</s> to those who thirst. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.9 ||

body.text: sadādhiṣṭhānaṃ mama etadīdṛśaṃ acintiyā kalpasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Such is my supernatural sustaining power always — for inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

body.text: na ca cyavāmī itu gṛdhrakūṭāt anyāsu śayyāsanakoṭibhiśca // Saddhp_15.10 //
body.translated_text: I never depart from this <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, nor from the other <s>koṭis</s> of seats and resting places. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.10 ||

children.text: yadāpi sattvā ima lokadhātuṃ paśyanti kalpenti ca dahyamānam /
children.translated_text: Even when beings see this world-system burning, considering it to be consumed by fire,

children.text: tadāpi cedaṃ mama buddhakṣetraṃ paripūrṇa bhotī marumānuṣāṇām // Saddhp_15.11 //
children.translated_text: even then this <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of mine is filled with gods and humans. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.11 ||

children.text: krīḍā ratī teṣa vicitra bhoti udyānaprāsādavimānakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Their play and delight are varied — <s>koṭis</s> of gardens, palaces, and celestial mansions,

children.text: pratimaṇḍitaṃ ratnamayaiśca parvatairdrumaistathā puṣpaphalairupetaiḥ // Saddhp_15.12 //
children.translated_text: adorned with mountains made of jewels, and trees endowed with flowers and fruits. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.12 ||

children.text: upariṃ ca devābhihananti tūryān mandāravarṣaṃ ca visarjayanti /
children.translated_text: Above, the gods strike their instruments and rain showers of <s>Māndārava</s> flowers,

children.text: mamaṃ ca abhyokiri śrāvakāṃśca ye cānya bodhāviha prasthitā vidū // Saddhp_15.13 //
children.translated_text: showering me and the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and those others who are wise and set forth toward awakening here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.13 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca me kṣetramidaṃ sadā sthitaṃ anye ca kalpentimu dahyamānam /
children.translated_text: Thus this field of mine always abides, while others consider it to be burning,

children.text: subhairavaṃ paśyiṣu lokadhātuṃ upadrutaṃ śokaśatābhikīrṇam // Saddhp_15.14 //
children.translated_text: and see a fearsome world-system, beset and strewn with hundreds of sorrows. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.14 ||

children.text: na cāpi me nāma śṛṇonti jātu tathāgatānāṃ bahukalpakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: They never hear my name, nor [the names] of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: dharmasya vā mahya gaṇasya cāpi pāpasya karmasya phalevarūpam // Saddhp_15.15 //
children.translated_text: nor of the <s>Dharma</s>, nor of my <s>saṃgha</s> — such is the fruit of evil <s>karma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.15 ||

children.text: lyadā tu sattvā mṛdu mārdavāśca utpanna bhontīha manuṣyaloke /
children.translated_text: But when beings, gentle and tender, are born here in the human world,

children.text: utpannamātrāśca śubhena karmaṇā paśyanti māṃ dharmu prakāśayantam // Saddhp_15.16 //
children.translated_text: no sooner are they born, through wholesome <s>karma</s>, than they see me illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.16 ||

children.text: na cāhu bhāṣāmi kadāci teṣāṃ imāṃ kriyāmīdṛśikīmanuttarām /
children.translated_text: Yet I never tell them of this, of this unsurpassed activity of such a kind;

children.text: teno ahaṃ dṛṣṭa cirasya bhomi tato 'sya bhāṣāmi sudurlabhā jināḥ // Saddhp_15.17 //
children.translated_text: therefore I am seen after a long time, and therefore I declare: 'Rare are the <s>Jinas</s>!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.17 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ jñānabalaṃ mayedaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ yasya na kaścidantaḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is this power of my knowledge, radiant, of which there is no end;

children.text: āyuśca me dīrghamanantakalpaṃ samupārjitaṃ pūrva caritva caryām // Saddhp_15.18 //
children.translated_text: and my lifespan is long, of infinite <s>kalpas</s>, acquired through having practiced the course of conduct in the past. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.18 ||

children.text: mā saṃśayaṃ atra kurudhva paṇḍitā vicikitsitaṃ co jahathā aśeṣam /
children.translated_text: Do not harbor doubt in this, O wise ones, and abandon all uncertainty entirely!

children.text: bhūtāṃ prabhāṣāmyahameta vācaṃ mṛṣā mamā naiva kadāci vāg bhavet // Saddhp_15.19 //
children.translated_text: I speak this word truthfully — never would my speech be false! || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.19 ||

children.text: yathā hi so vaidya upāyaśikṣito viparītasaṃjñīna sutāna hetoḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as that physician, skilled in means, for the sake of his sons of perverted perception,

children.text: jīvantamātmāna mṛteti brūyāt taṃ vaidyu vijño na mṛṣeṇa codayet // Saddhp_15.20 //
children.translated_text: though alive, would declare himself dead — no wise person would accuse that physician of falsehood. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.20 ||

children.text: yameva haṃ lokapitā svayaṃbhūḥ cikitsakaḥ sarvaprajāna nāthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even so, I am the father of the world, the Self-Existent, the healer, the protector of all creatures;

children.text: viparīta mūḍhāṃśca viditva bālān anirvṛto nirvṛta darśayāmi // Saddhp_15.21 //
children.translated_text: knowing them to be perverted, deluded, and foolish, though not passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>, I show myself as having passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.21 ||

children.text: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mahyamabhīkṣṇadarśanād viśraddha bhontī abudhā ajānakāḥ /
children.translated_text: For what reason? Because of seeing me constantly, they would become faithless, unwise, ignorant,

children.text: viśvasta kāmeṣu pramatta bhontī pramādahetoḥ prapatanti durgatim // Saddhp_15.22 //
children.translated_text: and heedlessly attached to sense-pleasures, they would fall into lower destinies through heedlessness. || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.22 ||

children.text: cariṃ cariṃ jāniya nityakālaṃ vadāmi sattvāna tathā tathāham /
children.translated_text: Knowing always the conduct and course [of beings], I say to beings thus and thus:

children.text: kathaṃ nu bodhāvupanāmayeyaṃ katha buddhadharmāṇa bhaveyu lābhinaḥ // Saddhp_15.23 //
children.translated_text: 'How may I lead them toward awakening? How may they become attainers of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>?' || <s>Saddhp</s> 15.23 ||

body.text: ityāryasaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇaparivarto nāma pañcadaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Dharma), the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on the Measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s Lifespan.

body.text: Saddhp_16: puṇyaparyāyaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 16: The Chapter on the Distribution of Merit.

body.text:
asmin khalu punastathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśe nirdiśyamāne aprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ sattvānāmarthaḥ kṛto 'bhūt | atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - asmin khalu punarajita tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśadharmaparyāye nirdiśyamāne aṣṭaṣaṣṭigaṅgānadīvālukāsamānāṃ bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntirutpannā | ebhyaḥ sahasraguṇena yeṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dhāraṇīpratilambho 'bhūt | anyeṣāṃ ca sāhasrikalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā asaṅgapratibhānatāpratilambho 'bhūt | anyeṣāṃ ca dvisāhasrikalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ koṭīnayutaśatasahasraparivartāyā dhāraṇyāḥ pratilambho 'bhūt | anye ca trisāhasrikalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā avaivartyadharmacakraṃ pravartayāmāsuḥ | anye ca madhyamakalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā vimalanirbhāsacakraṃ pravartayāmāsuḥ | anye ca kṣudrakalokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā aṣṭajāti[prati]baddhā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | anye ca catuścāturdvīpikā lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā caturjātipratibaddhā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | anye ca tricāturdvīpikā lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā trijātipratibaddhā abhūvan anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | anye ca dvicāturdvīpikā lokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamā bodhisattvḥ mahḥsattvḥ imaṃ dharmaparyḥyaṃ śrutvḥ dvijḥtipratibaddhḥ abhūvannanuttarḥyḥṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | anye caikacḥturdvīpikḥ lokadhḥtuparamḥṇurajaḥsamḥ bodhisattvḥ mahḥsattvḥ imaṃ dharmaparyḥyaṃ śrutvḥ ekajḥtipratibaddhḥ abhūvannanuttarḥyḥṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | aṣṭatrisḥhasramahḥsḥhasralokadhḥtuparamḥṇurajaḥsamaiśca bodhisattvairmahḥsattvairimaṃ dharmaparyḥyaṃ śrutvḥ anuttarḥyḥṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittḥnyutpḥditḥni
||
body.translated_text: When this teaching on the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan was being expounded, immeasurable, innumerable beings were benefited. Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'When this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse on the measure of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan was being expounded, O <s>Ajita</s>, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of sixty-eight <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas). A thousand times more <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> than these obtained <s>dhāraṇī</s>. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a thousand-fold world-system, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, attained unobstructed eloquence. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a two-thousand-fold world-system, attained the <s>dhāraṇī</s> of a <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousand revolutions. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a three-thousand-fold world-system, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, set turning the irreversible <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a medium world-system, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, set turning the stainless, radiant wheel. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a minor world-system, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, became bound to eight more births before supreme perfect awakening. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a world-system of four continents, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, became bound to four more births before supreme perfect awakening. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a world-system of three four-continent-groups, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, became bound to three more births before supreme perfect awakening. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a world-system of two four-continent-groups, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, became bound to two more births before supreme perfect awakening. Other <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of a world-system of one four-continent-group, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, became bound to one more birth before supreme perfect awakening. And <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of eight trichiliocosms, upon hearing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, generated the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening.

body.text: atha samanantaranirdiṣṭe bhagavataiṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ dharmābhisamaye pratiṣṭhāne, atha tāvadevoparivaihāyasādantarīkṣānmāndāravamahāmāndāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravṛṣṭam | teṣu ca lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasreṣu yāni tāni buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyāgatya ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu siṃhāsanopaviṣṭāni, tāni sarvāṇi cāvakiranti sma, abhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma | bhagavantaṃ ca śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ parinirvṛtaṃ siṃhāsanopaviṣṭamavakiranti sma, abhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma | taṃ ca sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ tāścatasraḥ parṣado 'vakiranti sma, abhyavakiranti sma, abhiprakiranti sma | divyāni ca candanāgarucūrṇānyantarīkṣāt pravarṣanti sma | upariṣṭāccāntarīkṣe vaihāyasaṃ mahādundubhayo 'ghaṭṭitāḥ praṇedurmanojñamadhuragambhīranirghoṣāḥ
body.translated_text: Then, immediately after the Blessed One had thus expounded the establishment of those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> in the realization of the <s>Dharma</s>, a rain of <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s> flowers fell from above, from the sky. And upon all those many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s> who had come from those world-systems and were seated on lion-thrones at the feet of jewel-trees — upon all of them they scattered, showered, and sprinkled [flowers]. And upon the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and upon the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who had passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, seated on the lion-throne — upon them they scattered, showered, and sprinkled [flowers]. And upon the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the four assemblies they scattered, showered, and sprinkled [flowers]. And divine sandalwood and agaru powders rained from the sky. And above in the sky, great drums, unbeaten, resounded with sweet, pleasant, and deep tones.

body.text: | divyāni ca dūṣyayugmaśatasahasrāṇyupariṣṭādantarīkṣāt prapatanti sma | hārārdhahāramuktāhāramaṇiratnamahāratnāni copariṣṭādvaihāyasamantarīkṣe samantāt savāsu dikṣu pralambanti sma | samantācca anarghaprāptasya dhūpasya ghaṭikāsahasrāṇi ratnamayāni svayameva pravicaranti sma | ekaikasya ca tathāgatasya ratnamayīṃ chatrāvalīṃ yāvad brahmalokādupari vaihāyasamantarīkṣe bodhisattvā mahāsattvā dhārayāmāsuḥ | anena paryāyeṇa sarveṣāṃ teṣāmaprameyāṇāmasaṃkhyeyānāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ te bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ratnamayīṃ chatrāvalīṃ yāvadbrahmalokādupari vaihāyasamantarīkṣe dhārayāmāsuḥ | pṛthak pṛthag gāthābhinirhārairbhūtairbuddhastavaistāṃstathāgatānābhiṣṭuvanti sma ||
body.translated_text: And divine pairs of cloths, in hundreds of thousands, fell from above, from the sky. And necklaces, half-necklaces, pearl necklaces, jewels, and great jewels hung suspended from above, in the sky, in all directions. And thousands of jeweled censers of priceless incense moved about of their own accord on all sides. And <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> held aloft jeweled rows of canopies, above in the sky, up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, over each <s>Tathāgata</s>. In this manner, those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> held jeweled rows of canopies, above in the sky up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, over all those immeasurable, innumerable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. And they praised those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, each individually, with genuine <s>Bodhisattva</s>-praises expressed in verses.

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: āścarya dharmaḥ sugatena śrāvito na jātu asmābhiḥ śrutaiṣa pūrvam /
children.translated_text: A wondrous <s>Dharma</s> has been taught by the <s>Sugata</s>, such as we have never heard before —

children.text: mahātmatā yādṛśi nāyakānāṃ āyuṣpramāṇaṃ ca yathā anantam // Saddhp_16.1 //
children.translated_text: how great is the nature of the Guides, and how their lifespan is infinite! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.1 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca dharmaṃ śruṇiyāna adya vibhajyamānaṃ sugatena saṃmukham /
children.translated_text: And hearing this <s>Dharma</s> today, expounded by the <s>Sugata</s> face to face,

children.text: prītisphuṭāḥ prāṇasahasrakoṭyo ya aurasā lokavināyakasya // Saddhp_16.2 //
children.translated_text: thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings burst with joy — they are the true sons of the Guide of the World! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.2 ||

children.text: avivartiyā keci sthitāgrabodhau keci sthitā dhāraṇiye varāyām /
children.translated_text: Some stand irreversible in the supreme awakening, some established in the highest <s>dhāraṇī</s>,

children.text: asaṅgapratibhāṇi sthitāśca kecit koṭīsahasrāya ca dhāraṇīye // Saddhp_16.3 //
children.translated_text: and some stand in unobstructed eloquence, and in <s>dhāraṇī</s> of thousands of <s>koṭis</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.3 ||

children.text: paramāṇukṣetrasya tathaiva cānye ye prasthitā uttamabuddhajñāne /
children.translated_text: And others, equal to the atoms of world-systems, have set forth toward the supreme <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge;

children.text: kecicca jātībhi tathaiva cāṣṭabhi jinā bhaviṣyanti anantadarśinaḥ // Saddhp_16.4 //
children.translated_text: some, with eight births [remaining], shall become <s>Jinas</s>, seers of the infinite! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.4 ||

children.text: kecittu catvāri atikramitvā kecitribhiścaiva dvibhiśca anye /
children.translated_text: Some, having passed beyond four births, and others with three or two,

children.text: lapsyanti bodhiṃ paramārthadarśinaḥ śruṇitva dharmaṃ imu nāyakasya // Saddhp_16.5 //
children.translated_text: shall attain awakening, seers of ultimate truth, having heard this <s>Dharma</s> of the Guide! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.5 ||

children.text: ke cāpi ekāya sthihitva jātyā sarvajña bhoṣyanti bhavāntareṇa /
children.translated_text: Some, abiding with just one birth remaining, shall become omniscient in their next existence,

children.text: śruṇitva āyu imu nāyakasya etādṛśaṃ labdhu phalaṃ anāsravam // Saddhp_16.6 //
children.translated_text: having heard of this lifespan of the Guide — such is the attainment of the outflow-free fruit! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.6 ||

children.text: aṣṭāna kṣetrāṇa yathā rajo bhavet evāpramāṇā gaṇanāya tattakāḥ /
children.translated_text: As many atoms as there are in eight world-systems — equally immeasurable and incalculable are

children.text: yāḥ sattvakoṭyo hi śruṇitva dharmaṃ utpādayiṃsū varabodhicittam // Saddhp_16.7 //
children.translated_text: those <s>koṭis</s> of beings who, having heard the <s>Dharma</s>, generated the supreme awakening-mind! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.7 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ karma kṛtaṃ maharṣiṇā prakāśayantenima buddhabodhim /
children.translated_text: Such is the work performed by the Great Seer, illuminating this <s>Buddha</s>-awakening,

children.text: anantakaṃ yasya pramāṇu nāsti ākāśadhātū ca yathāprameyaḥ // Saddhp_16.8 //
children.translated_text: infinite, of which there is no measure — like the immeasurable realm of space! || <s>Saddhp</s> 16.8 ||

children.text: māndāravāṇāṃ ca pravarṣi varṣaṃ bahudevaputrāṇa sahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: and many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of sons of the gods rained a shower of <s>māndārava</s> flowers;

children.text: śakrāśca brahmā yathā gaṅgavālikā ye āgatā kṣetrasahasrakoṭibhiḥ // Saddhp_16.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>, [numberless] like the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, came from thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of fields! || Saddhp 16.9 ||

children.text: sugandhacūrṇāni ca candanasya agarusya cūrṇāni ca muñcamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Releasing fragrant powders of sandalwood and aloe-wood powders,

children.text: caranti ākāśi yathaiva pakṣī abhyokirantā vidhivajjinendrān // Saddhp_16.10 //
children.translated_text: they move through the sky like birds, showering the Lords of <s>Jinas</s> in proper fashion! || Saddhp 16.10 ||

children.text: upariṃ ca vaihāyasu dundubhīyo ninādayanto madhurā aghaṭṭitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Above, in the sky, drums sounded sweetly, untouched;

children.text: divyāna dūṣyāṇa sahasrakoṭyaḥ kṣipanti bhrāmenti ca nāyakānām // Saddhp_16.11 //
children.translated_text: thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of divine silken garments they hurl and whirl [in offering] to the Guides! || Saddhp 16.11 ||

children.text: anarghamūlyasya ca dhūpanasya ratnāmayī ghaṭikasahasrakoṭyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of jeweled censers of priceless incense

children.text: svayaṃ samantena viceru tatra pūjārtha lokādhipatisya tāyinaḥ // Saddhp_16.12 //
children.translated_text: moved about of their own accord on all sides, for the worship of the Lord of the World, the Protector! || Saddhp 16.12 ||

children.text: uccān mahantān ratanāmayāṃśca chatrāṇa koṭīnayutānanantān /
children.translated_text: Lofty, great, jeweled parasols, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s>, endless,

children.text: dhārantime paṇḍita bodhisattvāḥ avataṃsakān yāvat brahmalokāt // Saddhp_16.13 //
children.translated_text: the wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s> hold aloft, along with garlands reaching up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>! || Saddhp 16.13 ||

children.text: savaijayantāṃśca sudarśanīyān dhvajāṃśca oropayi nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: And beautiful victory-banners and flags they lower [in offering] to the Guides;

children.text: gāthāsahasraiśca abhiṣṭuvanti prahṛṣṭacittāḥ sugatasya putrāḥ // Saddhp_16.14 //
children.translated_text: and with thousands of verses of praise, the joyful sons of the <s>Sugata</s> extol [him]! || Saddhp 16.14 ||

children.text: etādṛśāścaryaviśiṣṭa adbhutā vicitra dṛśyantimi adya nāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Such wondrous, distinguished, and marvelous [sights] — varied, are seen today, O Guides!

children.text: āyuṣpramāṇasya nidarśanena prāmodyalabdhā imi sarvasattvāḥ // Saddhp_16.15 //
children.translated_text: By the declaration of [his] lifespan-measure, all these beings have obtained great joy! || Saddhp 16.15 ||

children.text: vipulo 'dya artho daśasū diśāsu ghoṣaśca abhyudgatu nāyakānām /
children.translated_text: Vast today is the benefit in the ten directions, and the proclamation of the Guides has gone forth;

children.text: saṃtarpitāḥ prāṇasahasrakoṭyaḥ kuśalena bodhāya samanvitāśca // Saddhp_16.16 //
children.translated_text: thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of beings are satisfied and endowed with merit leading to awakening! || Saddhp 16.16 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - yairajita asmiṃstathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśadharmaparyāye nirdiśyamāne sattvairekacittotpādikāpyadhimuktirutpāditā, abhiśraddadhānatā vā kṛtā, kiyatte kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro vā puṇyaṃ prasavantīti tacchṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ yāvat puṇyaṃ prasavantīti | tadyathāpi nāma ajitakaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhikāṅkṣamāṇaḥ pañcasu pāramitāsvaṣṭau kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi caret | tadyathā dānapāramitāyāṃ śīlapāramitāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ vīryapāramitāyāṃ dhyānapāramitāyāṃ virahitaḥ prajñāpāramitayā, yena ca ajita kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā imaṃ tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā ekacittotpādikāpyadhimuktirutpāditā abhiśraddadhānatā vā kṛtā, asya puṇyābhisaṃskārasya kuśalābhisaṃskārasya asau paurvakaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ kuśalābhisaṃskāraḥ pañcapāramitāpratisaṃyukto 'ṣṭakalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrapariniṣpannaḥ śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopayāti, sahasratamīmapi śatasahasratamīmapi koṭīśatasahasratamīmapi koṭīnayutasahasratamīmapi koṭīnayutaśatasahasratamīmapi kalāṃ nopayāti, saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi upamāmapi upanisāmapi na kṣamate | evaṃrūpeṇa ajita puṇyābhisaṃskāreṇa samanvāgataḥ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā vivartate 'nuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheriti naitat sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: "O <s>Ajita</s>, those sons of good family or daughters of good family who, when this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse) on the exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan-measure was being taught, generated even a single moment's thought of faith or resolution, or produced belief — how much merit do they generate? Listen, and pay careful, thorough attention! I shall tell you how much merit they generate. Suppose, O <s>Ajita</s>, some son of good family or daughter of good family, aspiring to supreme perfect awakening, were to practice the five <s>pāramitās</s> for eight thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> — namely, the <s>pāramitā</s> of giving, the <s>pāramitā</s> of moral conduct, the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience, the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor, and the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation — but lacking the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom. And suppose, O <s>Ajita</s>, a son of good family or daughter of good family, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan-measure, generates even a single moment's thought of faith or resolution, or produces belief — compared to this merit-formation, this wholesome formation, that former merit-formation, that wholesome formation, connected with five <s>pāramitās</s>, accomplished over eight thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, does not approach even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, a hundred-thousandth part, a <s>koṭi</s>-hundred-thousandth part, or a <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousandth part. It does not bear comparison in number, in fraction, in calculation, in simile, or in approximation. With such a merit-formation endowed, O <s>Ajita</s>, it is impossible that a son of good family or daughter of good family would turn back from supreme perfect awakening."

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: yaśca pāramitāḥ pañca samādāyehi vartate /
children.translated_text: Whoever would undertake and practice the five <s>pāramitās</s>,

children.text: idaṃ jñānaṃ gaveṣanto buddhajñānamanuttaram // Saddhp_16.17 //
children.translated_text: seeking this knowledge, the unsurpassed <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, || Saddhp 16.17 ||

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi aṣṭau pūrṇāni yujyate /
children.translated_text: for full eight thousand <s>koṭis</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: dānaṃ dadanto buddhebhyaḥ śrāvakebhyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ // Saddhp_16.18 //
children.translated_text: giving gifts again and again to <s>Buddhas</s> and to <s>Śrāvakas</s>, || Saddhp 16.18 ||

children.text: pratyekabuddhāṃstarpento bodhisattvāna koṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: satisfying <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> and <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>

children.text: khādyabhojyānnapānehi vastraśayyāsanehi ca // Saddhp_16.19 //
children.translated_text: with food, drink, meals, beverages, garments, bedding, and seats, || Saddhp 16.19 ||

children.text: pratiśrayān vihārāṃśca candanasyeha kārayet /
children.translated_text: and would build shelters and monasteries of sandalwood here,

children.text: ārāmān ramaṇīyāṃśca caṃkramasthānaśobhitān // Saddhp_16.20 //
children.translated_text: and delightful gardens adorned with walking-paths, || Saddhp 16.20 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ daditvāna dānaṃ citra bahūvidham /
children.translated_text: having given such gifts, varied and manifold,

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi datvā bodhāya nāmayet // Saddhp_16.21 //
children.translated_text: for thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, and dedicating [them] to awakening — || Saddhp 16.21 ||

children.text: punaśca śīlaṃ rakṣeta śuddhaṃ saṃbuddhavarṇitam /
children.translated_text: and would further guard morality, pure, praised by the Perfectly Awakened Ones,

children.text: akhaṇḍaṃ saṃstutaṃ vijñairbuddhajñānasya kāraṇāt // Saddhp_16.22 //
children.translated_text: unbroken, commended by the wise, for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, || Saddhp 16.22 ||

children.text: punaśca kṣānti bhāveta dāntabhūmau pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: and would further cultivate patience, established on the stage of self-mastery,

children.text: dhṛtimān smṛtimāṃścaiva paribhāṣāḥ kṣame bahūḥ // Saddhp_16.23 //
children.translated_text: steadfast and mindful, enduring many insults, || Saddhp 16.23 ||

children.text: ye copalambhikāḥ sattvā adhimāne pratiṣṭhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: and those beings who hold to views of substantialism, established in conceit —

children.text: kutsanaṃ ca sahetteṣāṃ buddhajñānasya kāraṇāt // Saddhp_16.24 //
children.translated_text: he would bear their reproach, for the sake of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! || Saddhp 16.24 ||

children.text: nityodyuktaśca vīryasmin abhiyukto dṛḍhasmṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Always diligent in vigor, devoted, firm in mindfulness,

children.text: ananyamanasaṃkalpo bhaveyā kalpakoṭiyaḥ // Saddhp_16.25 //
children.translated_text: with a mind of single purpose, for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, || Saddhp 16.25 ||

children.text: araṇyavāsi tiṣṭhanto caṃkramaṃ abhiruhya ca /
children.translated_text: dwelling in the forest, undertaking walking meditation,

children.text: styānamiddhaṃ ca varjitvā kalpakoṭyo hi yaścaret // Saddhp_16.26 //
children.translated_text: avoiding sloth and torpor, for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> one would practice thus, || Saddhp 16.26 ||

children.text: yaśca dhyāyī mahādhyāyī dhyānārāmaḥ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: and one who meditates, a great meditator, delighting in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), absorbed,

children.text: kalpakoṭyaḥ sthito dhyāyet sahasrāṇyaṣṭanūnakāḥ // Saddhp_16.27 //
children.translated_text: for eight thousand <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> would remain established in meditation, || Saddhp 16.27 ||

children.text: tena dhyānena so vīraḥ prārthayed bodhimuttamām /
children.translated_text: and by that meditation, that hero would aspire to the supreme awakening,

children.text: ahaṃ syāmiti sarvajño dhyānapāramitāṃ gataḥ // Saddhp_16.28 //
children.translated_text: 'May I become omniscient!' — having reached the perfection of meditation; || Saddhp 16.28 ||

children.text: yacca puṇyaṃ bhavetteṣāṃ niṣevitvā imāṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: whatever merit would accrue to those from practicing such deeds

children.text: kalpakoṭīsahasrāṇi ye pūrvaṃ parikīrtitāḥ // Saddhp_16.29 //
children.translated_text: for the thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s> previously described — || Saddhp 16.29 ||

children.text: āyuṃ ca mama yo śrutvā strī vāpi puruṣo 'pi vā /
children.translated_text: whoever, man or woman, hearing of my lifespan,

children.text: ekakṣaṇaṃ pi śraddhāti idaṃ puṇyamanantakam // Saddhp_16.30 //
children.translated_text: has faith even for a single instant — that merit is endless! || Saddhp 16.30 ||

children.text: vicikitsāṃ ca varjitvā iñjitā manyitāni ca /
children.translated_text: Having abandoned doubt, wavering, and hesitation,

children.text: adhimucyenmuhūrtaṃ pi phalaṃ tasyedamīdṛśam // Saddhp_16.31 //
children.translated_text: if one resolves [to believe] even for a moment — such is the fruit thereof! || Saddhp 16.31 ||

children.text: bodhisattvāśca ye bhonti caritāḥ kalpakoṭiyaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have practiced for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>

children.text: na te trasanti śrutvedaṃ mama āyuracintiyam // Saddhp_16.32 //
children.translated_text: do not tremble upon hearing this — my lifespan is inconceivable! || Saddhp 16.32 ||

children.text: mūrdhena ca namasyanti ahamapyedṛśo bhavet /
children.translated_text: They bow with their heads, [aspiring]: 'May I too become like this',

children.text: anāgatasminnadhvāni tāreyaṃ prāṇikoṭiyaḥ // Saddhp_16.33 //
children.translated_text: in the future, may I liberate <s>koṭis</s> of beings! || Saddhp 16.33 ||

children.text: yathā śākyamunirnāthaḥ śākyasiṃho mahāmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the Lord, the lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the great sage,

children.text: bodhimaṇḍe niṣīditvā siṃhanādamidaṃ nadet // Saddhp_16.34 //
children.translated_text: seated at the seat of awakening, lets out this lion's roar — || Saddhp 16.34 ||

children.text: ahamapyanāgate 'dhvāni satkṛtaḥ sarvadehinām /
children.translated_text: 'I too, in the future, honored by all embodied beings,

children.text: bodhimaṇḍe niṣīditvā āyuṃ deśeṣyamīdṛśam // Saddhp_16.35 //
children.translated_text: seated at the seat of awakening, will teach such a lifespan!' || Saddhp 16.35 ||

children.text: adhyāśayena saṃpannāḥ śrutādhārāśca ye narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those men who are endowed with superior aspiration and are holders of what they have heard,

children.text: saṃdhābhāṣyaṃ vijānanti kāṅkṣā teṣāṃ na vidyate // Saddhp_16.36 //
children.translated_text: understand the intentional speech [of the <s>Buddha</s>] — no doubt exists for them! || Saddhp 16.36 ||

body.text: punaraparamajita ya imaṃ tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā avataredadhimucyeta avagāheta avabudhyeta, so 'smādaprameyataraṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ prasaved buddhajñānasaṃvartanīyam | kaḥ punarvādo ya imamevaṃrūpaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇuyācchrāvayeta vācayeda dhārayedvā likhedvā likhāpayedvā pustakagataṃ vā satkuryāt, gurukuryānmānayet pūjayet satkārayedvā puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapātakābhistailapradīpairvā ghṛtapradīpairvā gandhatailapradīpairvā, bahutaraṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ prasaved buddhajñānasaṃvartanīyam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Ajita</s>, whoever, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan-measure, penetrates it, resolves upon it, fathoms it, and comprehends it — that one would generate an even more immeasurable merit-formation leading to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge. How much more so one who would hear, cause others to hear, recite, uphold, write, or cause to be written this kind of <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, or who would honor, revere, esteem, and worship that book, performing veneration with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, oil-lamps, ghee-lamps, or perfumed-oil-lamps — that one would generate an even greater merit-formation leading to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge.

body.text: yadā ca ajita sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ tathāgatāyuṣpramāṇanirdeśaṃ dharmaparyāya śrutvā adhyāśayenādhimucyate, tadā tasyedamadhyāśayalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam - yaduta gṛdhrakūṭaparvatagataṃ māṃ dharmaṃ nirdeśayantaṃ drakṣyati bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaṃ bodhisattvagaṇapuraskṛtaṃ śrāvakasaṃghamadhyagatam | idaṃ ca me buddhakṣetraṃ sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ vaiḍūryamayīṃ samaprastarāṃ drakṣyati suvarṇasūtrāṣṭāpadavinaddhāṃ ratnavṛkṣairvicitritām | kūṭāgāraparibhogeṣu ca atra bodhisattvān nivasato drakṣyati | idamajita adhyāśayenādhimuktasya kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā adhyāśayalakṣaṇaṃ veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: And when, O <s>Ajita</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> on the exposition of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s lifespan-measure, resolves upon it with superior aspiration — then the following should be known as the sign of that superior aspiration: he will see me on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, surrounded and attended by a company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in the midst of the assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s>. And he will see this <s>buddhakṣetra</s>, this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, as made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), level and even, interlaced with golden cords in an eightfold pattern, adorned with jeweled trees. And he will see <s>Bodhisattvas</s> dwelling in tower-chambers here. This, O <s>Ajita</s>, should be known as the sign of superior aspiration of the son of good family or daughter of good family who resolves with superior aspiration.

body.text: api tu khalu punarajita tānapyahamadhyāśayādhimuktān kulaputrān vadāmi, ye tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śrutvā na pratikṣepsyanti uttari cābhyanumodayiṣyanti | kaṃḥ punarvādo ye dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti | tatastathāgataṃ soṃ 'sena pariharati ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pustakagataṃ kṛtvā aṃsena pariharati | na me tenājita kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā stūpāḥ kartavyāḥ, na vihārā kartavyāḥ, na bhikṣusaṃghāya glānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāstenānupradeyā bhavanti | tatkasya hetoḥ? kṛtā me tena ajita kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā śarīreṣu śarīrapūjā, saptaratnamayāśca stūpāḥ kāritāḥ, yāvad brahmalokamuccaistvena anupūrvapariṇāhena sacchatraparigrahāḥ savaijayantīkā ghaṇṭāsamudgānuratāḥ, teṣāṃ ca śarīrastūpānāṃ vividhāḥ satkārāḥ kṛtā nānāvidhairdivyairmānuṣyakaiḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantībhirvividhamadhuramanojñapaṭupaṭahadundubhimahādundubhibhirvādyatālaninādarnirghoṣaśabdairnānāvidhaiśca gītanṛtyalāsyaprakārairbahubhiraparimitairbahvaprameyāṇi kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi satkāraḥ kṛto bhavati | imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ mama parinirvṛtasya dhārayitvā vācayitvā likhitvā
body.translated_text: Moreover, O <s>Ajita</s>, I also call those sons of good family who resolve with superior aspiration — those who, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, having heard this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, will not reject it but will further rejoice in it. How much more so those who will uphold, recite it! That one carries the <s>Tathāgata</s> on his shoulder who, having made this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> into a book, carries it on his shoulder. For that son of good family or daughter of good family, O <s>Ajita</s>, it is not necessary to build <s>stūpas</s>, nor monasteries, nor to give medicines and requisites for the sick to the community of monks. For what reason? Because, O <s>Ajita</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family has already performed worship to the relics, has already caused <s>stūpas</s> to be built of the seven jewels, reaching up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s> in height, tapering gradually, with parasol-crowns and victory-banners adorned with bell-networks — and various acts of honor have been performed to those relic-<s>stūpas</s>, with manifold divine and human flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-banners, with various sweet, pleasant, clear drums, great drums, musical instruments, rhythms, sounds, echoes, and tones, and with manifold songs, dances, and dramatic performances — many, unlimited — for many immeasurable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, such worship has been performed. Having upheld, recited, and written this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>,

body.text:
prakāśayitvā vihārā api tena ajita kṛtā bhavanti vipulā vistīrṇāḥ | pragṛhītāśca lohitacandanamayā dvātriṃśatprāsādā aṣṭatalā bhikṣusahasrāvāsāḥ | ārāmapuṣpopaśobhitāścaṃkramavanopetāḥ śayanāsanopastabdhāḥ khādyabhojyānnapānaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraparipūrṇāḥ sarvasukhopadhānapratimaṇḍitāḥ | te ca bahvaprameyā yaduta śataṃ vā sahasraṃ vā śatasahasraṃ vā koṭī vā koṭīśataṃ vā koṭīsahasraṃ vā koṭiśatasahasraṃ vā koṭīnayutaśatasahasraṃ vā | te ca mama saṃmukhaṃ śrāvakasaṃghasya niryātitāḥ, te ca mayā paribhuktā veditavyāḥ | ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya dhārayedvā vācayedvā deśayedvā likhedvā lekhayedvā, tadanenāhamajitaparyāyeṇa evaṃ vadāmi - na me tena parinirvṛtasya dhātustūpāḥ kārayitavyāḥ, na saṃghapūjā | kaḥ punarvādo 'jita ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayan dānena vā saṃpādayecchīlena vā kṣāntyā vā vīryeṇa vā dhyānena
vā prajñayā vā saṃpādayet, bahutaraṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā prasaved buddhajñānasaṃvartanīyamaprameyamasaṃkhyeyamaparyantam | tadyathāpi nāma ajita ākāśa dhāturaparyantaḥ pūrvadakṣiṇapaścimottarādharordhvāsu dikṣu vidikṣu, evamaprameyāsaṃkhyeyān sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā puṇyābhisaṃskārān prasaved buddhajñānasaṃvartanīyān ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayedvā vācayedvā deśayedvā likhedvā likhāpayedvā | tathāgatacaityasatkārārthaṃ ca abhiyukto bhavet, tathāgataśrāvakāṇāṃ ca varṇaṃ bhāṣeta, bodhisattvānāṃ ca mahāsattvānāṃ guṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi parikīrtayet, pareṣāṃ ca saṃprakāśayet, kṣāntyā ca saṃpādayet, śīlavāṃśca bhavet, kalyāṇadharmaḥ sukhasaṃvāsaḥ kṣāntaśca bhavet, dāntaśca bhavedanabhyasūyakaśca, apagatakrodhamanaskāro 'vyāpannamanaskāraḥ smṛtimāṃśca sthāmavāṃśca bhavet, vīryavāṃśca nityābhiyuktaśca bhavet, buddhadharmaparyeṣṭyā dhyāyī ca bhavet, pratisaṃlayanagurukaḥ pratisaṃlayanabahulaśca praśnaprabhedakuśalaśca bhavet, praśnakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ visarjayitā | yasya kasyacidajita bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya dhārayataḥ ime evaṃrūpā guṇā bhaveyurye mayā parikīrtitāḥ, so 'jita kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā evaṃ veditavyaḥ - bodhimaṇḍasaṃprasthito 'yaṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā bodhimabhisaṃboddhuṃ bodhivṛkṣamūlaṃ gacchati | yatra ca ajita sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tiṣṭhedvā niṣīdedvā caṃkramedvā, tatra ajita tathāgatamuddiśya caityaṃ kartavyam, tathāgatastūpo 'yamiti ca sa vaktavyaḥ sadevakena lokeneti ||
body.translated_text: having illuminated [the Dharma], and monasteries too, O <s>Ajita</s>, are built by that one — vast and extensive. Mansions made of red sandalwood, thirty-two in number, of eight stories, each housing a thousand monks, are presented. They are beautified with garden flowers, equipped with walking paths, furnished with beds and seats, stocked with snacks, food, rice, drinks, medicines for the sick, and all requisites — adorned with every comfort. And they are many and immeasurable — a hundred, or a thousand, or a hundred-thousand, or a <s>koṭi</s>, or a hundred <s>koṭis</s>, or a thousand <s>koṭis</s>, or a hundred-thousand <s>koṭis</s>, or <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands. And those are presented in my presence to the <s>Śrāvaka</s>-<s>Saṅgha</s>, and should be understood as enjoyed by me. Whoever retains, recites, teaches, writes, or causes to be written this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — by this method, O <s>Ajita</s>, I say thus: it is not necessary for that person to build relic-<s>stūpas</s> for me who have passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, nor to make offerings to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. How much more, O <s>Ajita</s>, if a person who retains this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse accomplishes it through generosity, or through morality, or through patience, or through vigor, or through meditation, or through wisdom — that son of good family or daughter of good family would produce an immeasurable, incalculable, unlimited accumulation of merit leading to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge! Just as, O <s>Ajita</s>, the spatial realm is unlimited in the eastern, southern, western, northern, downward, and upward directions and intermediate directions, even so immeasurable and incalculable are the merit-accumulations leading to <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge that a son of good family or daughter of good family would produce who retains, recites, teaches, writes, or causes to be written this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and who is devoted to honoring the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s shrines, and who praises the qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and who celebrates <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of qualities of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, and who proclaims [this] to others, and who accomplishes patience, and who is virtuous, of good character, agreeable to live with, patient, tamed, free from envy, with mind free from anger and hostility, mindful, firm, vigorous, always diligent, meditating in seeking <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>, one who values seclusion, who practices seclusion extensively, who is skilled in analyzing questions, and who resolves <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of questions. If any <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, O <s>Ajita</s>, while retaining this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, possesses such qualities as I have described, that son of good family or daughter of good family should be known thus: 'This son of good family or daughter of good family is one who has set forth toward the seat of awakening, who is proceeding to the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s>-tree to attain awakening.' And wherever, O <s>Ajita</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family stands, or sits, or walks — there, O <s>Ajita</s>, a shrine should be made dedicated to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and it should be proclaimed by the world with its gods: 'This is a <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>stūpa</s>!'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: puṇyaskandho aparyanto varṇito me punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The mass of merit is boundless — described by me again and again —

children.text: ya idaṃ dhārayetsūtraṃ nirvṛte naranāyake // Saddhp_16.37 //
children.translated_text: for one who retains this <s>sūtra</s> when the Leader of Men has entered <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation). || Saddhp 16.37 ||

children.text: pūjāśca me kṛtāstena dhātustūpāśca kāritāḥ /
children.translated_text: Worship has been performed by that one for me, and relic-<s>stūpas</s> have been built —

children.text: ratnāmayā vicitrāśca darśanīyaḥ suśobhanāḥ // Saddhp_16.38 //
children.translated_text: made of jewels, variegated, beautiful and resplendent to behold! || Saddhp 16.38 ||

children.text: brahmalokasamā uccā chatrāvalibhiranvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: As high as the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, furnished with rows of parasols,

children.text: pariṇāhavantaḥ śrīmanto vaijayantīsamanvitāḥ // Saddhp_16.39 //
children.translated_text: of great circumference, glorious, adorned with victory-banners! || Saddhp 16.39 ||

children.text: paṭughaṇṭā raṇantaśca paṭṭadāmopaśobhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Sharp-toned bells ringing, adorned with silk banners,

children.text: vāteritāstathā ghaṇṭā śobhanti jinadhātuṣu // Saddhp_16.40 //
children.translated_text: bells stirred by the wind — they shine at the shrines of the <s>Jina</s>! || Saddhp 16.40 ||

children.text: pūjā ca vipulā teṣāṃ puṣpagandhavilepanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Abundant worship to those [shrines] with flowers, perfumes, and ointments

children.text: kṛtā vādyaiśca vastraiśca dundubhībhiḥ punaḥ puna // Saddhp_16.41 //
children.translated_text: has been performed, and with music, garments, and drums, again and again! || Saddhp 16.41 ||

children.text: madhurā vādyabhāṇḍā ca vāditā teṣu dhātuṣu /
children.translated_text: Sweet musical instruments have been played at those relic-shrines,

children.text: gandhatailapradīpāśca dattāste 'pi samantataḥ // Saddhp_16.42 //
children.translated_text: and lamps filled with perfumed oil have been offered on all sides! || Saddhp 16.42 ||

children.text: ya idaṃ dhārayet sūtraṃ kṣayakāli ca deśayet /
children.translated_text: Whoever retains this <s>sūtra</s> and teaches it in the time of decline —

children.text: īdṛśī me kṛtā tena vividhā pūjanantikā // Saddhp_16.43 //
children.translated_text: such varied worship has been performed by that one for me! || Saddhp 16.43 ||

children.text: agrā vihārakoṭyo 'pi bahuścandanakāritāḥ /
children.translated_text: The finest <s>koṭis</s> of monasteries, many, built of sandalwood,

children.text: dvātriṃśatī ca prāsādā uccaistvenāṣṭavattalāḥ // Saddhp_16.44 //
children.translated_text: and thirty-two mansions, of eight stories high! || Saddhp 16.44 ||

children.text: śayyāsanairupastabdhāḥ khādyabhojyaiḥ samanvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Furnished with beds and seats, stocked with snacks and foods,

children.text: praveṇī praṇīta prajñaptā āvāsāśca sahasraśaḥ // Saddhp_16.45 //
children.translated_text: arranged in rows, of excellent quality — and lodgings by the thousands! || Saddhp 16.45 ||

children.text: ārāmāścaṃkramā dattāḥ puṣpārāmopaśobhitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Gardens and walking paths have been given, beautified with flower-gardens,

children.text: bahu ucchadakāścaiva bahurūpavicitritāḥ // Saddhp_16.46 //
children.translated_text: many canopied walkways, variously adorned! || Saddhp 16.46 ||

children.text: saṃghasya vividhā pūjā kṛtā me tena saṃmukham /
children.translated_text: Varied worship of the <s>Saṅgha</s> has been performed by that one in my presence —

children.text: ya idaṃ dhārayetsūtraṃ nirvṛtasmin vināyake // Saddhp_16.47 //
children.translated_text: one who retains this <s>sūtra</s> when this Guide has entered <s>nirvṛti</s>! || Saddhp 16.47 ||

children.text: adhimuktisāro yo syādato bahutaraṃ hi saḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever is of resolute faith — far greater still

children.text: puṇyaṃ labheta yo etatsūtraṃ vācellikheta vā // Saddhp_16.48 //
children.translated_text: is the merit obtained by one who recites or writes this <s>sūtra</s>! || Saddhp 16.48 ||

children.text: likhāpayennaraḥ kaścit suniruktaṃ ca pustake /
children.translated_text: If some man were to cause it to be written, well-composed, in a manuscript,

children.text: pustakaṃ pūjayettacca gandhamālyavilepanaiḥ // Saddhp_16.49 //
children.translated_text: and were to worship that manuscript with perfumes, garlands, and ointments, || Saddhp 16.49 ||

children.text: dīpaṃ ca dadyādyo nityaṃ gandhatailasya pūritam /
children.translated_text: and were to give a lamp always filled with perfumed oil,

children.text: jātyutpalātimuktaiśca prakaraiścampakasya ca // Saddhp_16.50 //
children.translated_text: and [offerings of] jasmine, <s>atimuktaka</s>, and <s>campaka</s> blossoms — || Saddhp 16.50 ||

children.text: kuryādetādṛśīṃ pūjāṃ pustakeṣu ca yo naraḥ /
children.translated_text: the man who performs such worship to those manuscripts

children.text: bahu prasavate puṇyaṃ pramāṇaṃ yasya no bhavet // Saddhp_16.51 //
children.translated_text: produces abundant merit, whose measure cannot be found! || Saddhp 16.51 ||

children.text: yathaivākāśadhātau hi pramāṇaṃ nopalabhyate /
children.translated_text: Just as in the spatial realm no measure can be found

children.text: diśāsu daśasū nityaṃ puṇyaskandho 'yamīdṛśaḥ // Saddhp_16.52 //
children.translated_text: in the ten directions, always — such is this mass of merit! || Saddhp 16.52 ||

children.text: kaḥ punarvādo yaśca syāt kṣānto dāntaḥ samāhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: How much more so for one who is patient, tamed, concentrated,

children.text: śīlavāṃścaiva dhyāyī ca pratisaṃlānagocaraḥ // Saddhp_16.53 //
children.translated_text: virtuous, and meditative, devoted to seclusion! || Saddhp 16.53 ||

children.text: akrodhano apiśunaścaityasmin gaurave sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from anger, free from slander, established in reverence for this shrine,

children.text: bhikṣūṇāṃ praṇato nityaṃ nādhimānī na cālasaḥ // Saddhp_16.54 //
children.translated_text: always humble before monks, neither arrogant nor lazy! || Saddhp 16.54 ||

children.text: prajñavāṃścaiva dhīraśca praśnaṃ pṛṣṭo na kupyati /
children.translated_text: Wise, steadfast, not angered when asked a question,

children.text: anulomaṃ ca deśeti kṛpābuddhī ca prāṇiṣu // Saddhp_16.55 //
children.translated_text: teaching in accordance [with the questioner's needs], having a mind of compassion toward beings! || Saddhp 16.55 ||

children.text: ya īdṛśo bhavetkaścid yaḥ sūtraṃ dhārayedidam /
children.translated_text: Whoever would be of such a kind, and would retain this <s>sūtra</s> —

children.text: na tasya puṇyaskandhasya pramāṇamupalabhyate // Saddhp_16.56 //
children.translated_text: the measure of that one's mass of merit cannot be found! || Saddhp 16.56 ||

children.text: yadi kaścinnaraḥ paśyedīdṛśaṃ dharmabhāṇakam /
children.translated_text: If some man were to see such a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher,

children.text: dhārayantamidaṃ sūtraṃ kuryādvai tasya satkriyām // Saddhp_16.57 //
children.translated_text: one who retains this <s>sūtra</s>, he should indeed honor him: || Saddhp 16.57 ||

children.text: divyaiśca puṣpaistatha okireta divyaiśca vastrairabhicchādayeta /
children.translated_text: he should shower him with divine flowers and cover him with divine garments,

children.text: mūrdhena vanditva ca tasya pādau tathāgato 'yaṃ janayeta saṃjñām // Saddhp_16.58 //
