children.translated_text: and bowing his head to his feet, should generate the perception: "This is a <s>Tathāgata</s>!" || Saddhp 16.58 ||

children.text: dṛṣṭvā ca taṃ cintayi tasmi kāle gamiṣyate eṣa drumasya mūlam /
children.translated_text: And seeing him, one should think at that time: "This one will go to the foot of the tree;

children.text: budhyiṣyate bodhimanuttarāṃ śivāṃ hitāya lokasya sadevakasya // Saddhp_16.59 //
children.translated_text: he will attain the unsurpassed, auspicious awakening, for the welfare of the world with its gods!" || Saddhp 16.59 ||

children.text: yasmiṃśca so caṃkrami tādṛśo viduḥ tiṣṭheta vā yatra niṣīdayedvā /
children.translated_text: And wherever that wise one walks, or stands, or sits,

children.text: śayyāṃ ca kalpeya kahiṃci dhīro bhāṣantu gāthāṃ pi tu ekasūtrāt // Saddhp_16.60 //
children.translated_text: or lies down, or even recites a single verse from this <s>sūtra</s> — || Saddhp 16.60 ||

children.text: yasmiṃśca stūpaṃ puruṣottamasya kārāpayeccitrasudarśanīyam /
children.translated_text: there one should cause to be built a <s>stūpa</s> of the Supreme among Men, variegated and beautiful to behold,

children.text: uddiśya buddhaṃ bhagavanta nāyakaṃ pūjāṃ ca citrāṃ tahi kārayettathā // Saddhp_16.61 //
children.translated_text: dedicated to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the Guide — and varied worship should be performed there! || Saddhp 16.61 ||

children.text: mayā sa bhuktaḥ pṛthivīpradeśo mayā svayaṃ caṃkramitaṃ ca tatraṃ /
children.translated_text: That spot of earth has been used by me; I myself have walked there;

children.text: tatropaviṣṭo ahameva ca syāṃ yatra sthitaḥ so bhavi buddhaputraḥ // Saddhp_16.62 //
children.translated_text: I myself would be seated there — where that son of the <s>Buddha</s> stands! || Saddhp 16.62 ||'

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye puṇyaparyāyaparivarto nāma ṣoḍaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixteenth chapter, named 'The Chapter on the Measure of Merit' (<s>Puṇyaparyāyaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_17: anumodanāpuṇyanirdeśaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: Saddhp 17: The Chapter on the Instruction Regarding the Merit of Rejoicing (<s>Anumodanāpuṇyanirdeśaparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - yo bhagavan imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ deśyamānaṃ śrutvā anumodet kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā, kiyantaṃ sa bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā puṇyaṃ prasavediti?
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'If, O Blessed One, a son of good family or daughter of good family, having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse being taught, should rejoice [in it] — how much merit, O Blessed One, would that son of good family or daughter of good family produce?'

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāmimāṃ gāthāmabhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, at that time, spoke this verse:

children.text: yo nirvṛte mahāvīre śṛṇuyātsūtramīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever, when the Great Hero has entered <s>nirvṛti</s>, would hear such a <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: śrutvā cābhyanumodeyā kiyantaṃ kuśalaṃ bhavet // Saddhp_17.1 //
children.translated_text: and having heard it, would rejoice — how much merit would there be?' || Saddhp 17.1 ||

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān maitreyaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - yaḥ kaścidajita kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya imaṃ dharmaparyāya deśyamānaṃ saṃprakāśyamānaṃ śṛṇuyād bhikṣurvā bhikṣuṇī vā upāsako vā upāsikā vā vijñapuruṣo vā kumārako vā, kumārikā vā, śrutvā ca abhyanumodeta, sacettato dharmaśravaṇādutthāya prakrāmet, sa ca vihāragato vā gṛhagato vā araṇyagato vā vīthīgato vā grāmagato vā janapadagato vā tān hetūṃstāni kāraṇāni taṃ dharmaṃ yathāśrutaṃ yathodgṛhītaṃ yathābalamaparasya sattvasyācakṣīta māturvā piturvā jñātervā, saṃmoditasya vā anyasya vā saṃstutasya kasyacit, so 'pi yadi śrutvā anumodeta, anumodya ca punaranyasmai ācakṣīta | so 'pi yadi śrutvānumodeta, anumodya ca so 'pyaparasmai ācakṣīta, so 'pi taṃ śrutvānumodeta | ityanena paryāyeṇa yāvat pañcāśat paraṃparayā | atha khalvajita yo 'sau pañcāśattamaḥ puruṣo bhavet paraṃparāśravānumodakaḥ, tasyāpi tāvadahamajita kulaputrasya vā kuladuhiturvā anumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāramabhinirdekṣyāmi | taṃ śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuru | bhāṣiṣye 'haṃ te ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>: 'If, O <s>Ajita</s>, any son of good family or daughter of good family, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, would hear this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse being taught and proclaimed — whether a monk, a nun, a layman, a laywoman, a learned man, a boy, or a girl — and having heard it, would rejoice, and then, rising from that <s>Dharma</s>-hearing, would depart, and being in a monastery, or in a house, or in a wilderness, or on a road, or in a village, or in the countryside, would tell those reasons, those causes, that <s>Dharma</s>, as heard, as understood, according to ability, to another being — whether to a mother, a father, a relative, a friend, or to any acquaintance — and if that person too, having heard, would rejoice, and having rejoiced, would tell yet another; and if that person too, having heard, would rejoice, and having rejoiced, would in turn tell yet another, and that person too, having heard, would rejoice — in this manner, up to the fiftieth in succession. Then, O <s>Ajita</s>, I shall describe the merit-accumulation associated with the rejoicing of even that fiftieth person, that son of good family or daughter of good family, who has heard and rejoiced through successive transmission. Listen to that, well and carefully! I shall speak it to you.'

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma ajita caturṣu lokadhātuṣvasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasreṣu ye sattvāḥ santaḥ saṃvidyamānāḥ ṣaṭsu gatiṣūpapannāḥ, aṇḍajā vā jarāyujā vā saṃsvedajā vā aupapādukā vā rūpiṇo vā arūpiṇo vā saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino vā nāsaṃjñino vā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuṣpadā vā bahupadā vā yāvadeva sattvāḥ sattvadhātau saṃgrahasamavasaraṇaṃ gacchanti | atha kaścideva puruṣaḥ samutpadyeta puṇyakāmo hitakāmastasya sattvakāyasya sarvakāmakrīḍāratiparibhogāniṣṭān kāntān priyān manāpān dadyāt | ekaikasya sattvasya jambudvīpaṃ paripūrṇaṃ dadyāt kāmakrīḍāratiparibhogāya, hiraṇyasuvarṇarūpyamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālānaśvarathagorathahastirathān dadyāt prāsādān kūṭāgārān | anena paryāyeṇa ajita sa puruṣo dānapatirmahādānapatiḥ paripūrṇānyaśītiṃ varṣāṇi dānaṃ dadyāt | atha khalvajita sa puruṣo dānapatirmahādānapatirevaṃ cintayet - ime khalu sattvāḥ sarve mayā krīḍāpitā ramāpitāḥ sukhaṃ jivāpitāḥ | ime ca te bhavantaḥ sattvā balinaḥ palitaśiraso jīrṇavṛddhā mahallakā
body.translated_text: Suppose, <s>Ajita</s>, in four incalculable hundred-thousands of world-systems, whatever beings exist and are found, reborn in the six destinies — whether egg-born, womb-born, moisture-born, or spontaneously born; whether with form or formless; whether with perception, without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception; whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed — as many beings as are comprised in the realm of beings. And then some man might arise, desiring merit, desiring benefit for that multitude of beings, and would give all of them desirable, lovely, dear, and agreeable enjoyments, pleasures, amusements, and provisions. To each and every being he would give a <s>Jambudvīpa</s> full of enjoyments, pleasures, amusements, and provisions — gold, silver, gems, pearls, <s>vaidūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, horse-chariots, ox-chariots, elephant-chariots, palaces, and mansions. In this manner, <s>Ajita</s>, that man, the great donor, the great lord of giving, would give gifts for a full eighty years. Then, <s>Ajita</s>, that great donor, the great lord of giving, might think: 'All these beings have been entertained, delighted, and made to live happily by me. But these beings have become aged, gray-haired, worn, old, and decrepit —

body.text:
aśītivarṣikā jātyā | abhyāśībhūtāścaite kālakriyāyāḥ | yannvahametāṃstathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye 'vatārayeyamanuśāsayeyam | atha khalvajita sa puruṣastān sarvasattvān samādāpayet | samādāpayitvā ca tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye 'vatārayed grāhayet | tasya te sattvāstaṃ ca dharmaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ | śrutvā ca ekakṣaṇena ekamuhūrtena ekalavena sarve srotaāpannāḥ syuḥ, sakṛdāgāmino 'nāgāmino 'nāgāmiphalaṃ prāpnuyuryāvadarhanto bhaveyuḥ, kṣīṇāsravā dhyāyino mahādhyāyino 'ṣṭavimokṣadhyāyinaḥ | tatkiṃ manyase ajita api nu sa puruṣo dānapatirmahādānapatistatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavedaprameyamasaṃkhyeyam? evamukte maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - evametat bhagavan, evametat sugata | anenaiva tāvad bhagavan kāraṇena sa puruṣo dānapatirmahādānapatirbahu puṇyaṃ prasavet, yastāvatāṃ sattvānāṃ sarvasukhopadhānaṃ dadyāt | kaḥ punarvādo
yaduttariarhattve pratiṣṭhāpayet ||
body.translated_text: — eighty years old by birth. Their death is approaching. Surely I should train and instruct them in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then, <s>Ajita</s>, that man would inspire all those beings. Having inspired them, he would introduce and instruct them in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Those beings would hear that <s>Dharma</s>. Having heard it, in one instant, one moment, one flash, all would become stream-enterers, once-returners, non-returners — they would attain the fruit of non-returning — and finally become <s>Arhats</s>, with outflows destroyed, meditators, great meditators, meditators in the eight liberations. What do you think, <s>Ajita</s> — would that man, the great donor, the great lord of giving, thereby generate much merit, immeasurable and incalculable?' Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Indeed so, Blessed One! Indeed so, <s>Sugata</s>! Even by this much alone, O Blessed One, that man, the great donor, the great lord of giving, would generate much merit — that he gave the provision of all happiness to so many beings. How much more so that he established them in <s>Arhatship</s>!'

body.text: evamukte bhagavānajitaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - ārocayāmi te ajita, prativedayāmi | yaśca sa dānapatirmahādānapatiḥ puruṣaścaturṣu lokadhātuṣvasaṃkhyeyaśatasahasreṣu sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasukhopadhānaiḥ paripūrya arhattve pratiṣṭhāpya puṇyaṃ prasavet, yaśca pañcāśattamaḥ puruṣaḥ paraṃparāśravānugataḥ śravaṇena ito dharmaparyāyādekāmapi gāthāmekapadamapi śrutvā anumodeta | yaccaitasya puruṣasyānumodanāsahagataṃ puṇyakriyāvastu, yacca tasya puruṣasya dānapatermahādānapaterdānasahagatamarhattvaṃ pratiṣṭhāpanāsahagatapuṇyakriyāvastu, idameva tato bahutaram | yo 'yaṃ puruṣaḥ pañcāśattamaḥ, tataḥ puruṣaparaṃparāta ito dharmaparyāyādekāmapi gāthāmekapadamapi śrutvā anumodet | asya anumodanāsahagatasya ajita puṇyābhisaṃskārasya kuśalamūlābhisaṃskārasya anumodanāsahagatasya agrataḥasau paurviko dānasahagataśca arhattvapratiṣṭhāpanāsahagataśca puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ śatatamīmapi kalāṃ nopayāti, sahasratamīmapi śatasahasratamīmapi koṭītamīmapi koṭīśatatamīmapi koṭīsahasratamīmapi koṭīśatasahasratamīmapi koṭīniyutaśatasahasratamīmapi kalāṃ nopayāti | saṃkhyāmapi kalāmapi gaṇanāmapi upamāmapi upaniḥadamapi na kḥamate | evamaprameyamasaṃkhyeyamajita so 'pi tāvat pañcāśattamaḥ paraṃparāśravaṇe puruḥa ito dharmaparyāyādantaśa ekagāthāmapi ekapadamapi anumodya ca puṇyaṃ prasavati | kaḥ punarvādo 'jita yo 'yaṃ mama saṃmukhamimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇuyāt, śrutvā cābhyanumodet, aprameyataramasaṃkhyayetaraṃ tasyāhamajita taṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ vadāmi ||
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Ajita</s>: 'I declare to you, <s>Ajita</s>, I announce: that great donor, the great lord of giving, who, having fully satisfied all beings in four incalculable hundred-thousands of world-systems with the provision of all happiness, established them in <s>Arhatship</s> and generated merit — and the fiftieth person in the chain of successive hearers who, through successive hearing, having heard even one verse, even one word from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, rejoices — the meritorious act accompanied by that person's rejoicing is far greater than the meritorious act accompanied by giving and by establishing in <s>Arhatship</s> of that great donor, the great lord of giving. The fiftieth person in the chain of successive hearers, <s>Ajita</s>, who, from the succession of persons, having heard even one verse, even one word from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, rejoices — of his meritorious formation accompanied by rejoicing, of his wholesome root formation accompanied by rejoicing, the former meritorious formation accompanied by giving and accompanied by establishing in <s>Arhatship</s> does not reach even a hundredth part, nor a thousandth part, nor a hundred-thousandth part, nor a <s>koṭi</s>th part, nor a hundred-<s>koṭi</s>th part, nor a thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th part, nor a hundred-thousand-<s>koṭi</s>th part, nor a <s>koṭi</s>-<s>nayuta</s>-hundred-thousand-th part. It does not bear comparison by number, by fraction, by counting, by analogy, or by approximation. So immeasurable, so incalculable, <s>Ajita</s>, is the merit generated by even the fiftieth person in the chain of successive hearers who rejoices at even one verse, even one word from this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. How much more so, <s>Ajita</s>, for one who hears this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> face to face before me, and having heard it, rejoices — I declare that person's meritorious formation to be even more immeasurable and incalculable!'

body.text: yaḥ khalu punarajita asya dharmaparyāyasya śravāṇārthaṃ kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā svagṛhānniṣkramya vihāraṃ gacchet | sa ca gattvā tasminnimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ muhūrtakamapi śṛṇuyāt sthito vā niṣaṇṇo vā | sa sattvastanmātreṇa puṇyābhisaṃskāreṇa kṛtenopacitena jātivinivṛtto dvitīye samucchraye dvitīye ātmabhāvapratilambhe gorathānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati, aśvarathānāṃ hastirathānāṃ śibikānāṃ goyanānāmṛṣabhayānānāṃ divyānāṃ ca vimānānāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyati | sacet punastatra dharmaśravaṇe muhūrtamātramapi niṣadya idaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇuyāt,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Ajita</s>, if any son or daughter of good family, for the purpose of hearing this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, should leave their home and go to a monastery, and having gone there, should hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> even for a moment, whether standing or seated — that being, by that much meritorious formation alone, having created and accumulated it, upon turning from this birth to the next acquisition of a bodily existence, will become the possessor of ox-chariots, horse-chariots, elephant-chariots, palanquins, ox-yokes, bull-vehicles, and divine aerial carriages. And if, furthermore, in that <s>Dharma</s>-hearing, he should sit even for a moment and hear this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> —

body.text:
paraṃ vā niṣādayet, āsanasaṃvibhāgaṃ vā kuryādaparasya sattvasya, tena sa puṇyābhisaṃskāreṇa lābhī bhaviṣyati śakrāsanānāṃ brahmāsanānāṃ cakravartisaṃhāsanānām | sacet punarajita kaścideva kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā aparaṃ puruṣamevaṃ vadet - āgaccha tvaṃ bhoḥ puruṣa | saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ śṛṇuṣva | sa ca puruṣastasya tāṃ protsāhanāmāgamya yadi muhūrtamātramapi śṛṇuyāt, sa sattvastena protsāhena kuśalamūlenābhisaṃskṛtena dhāraṇīpratilabdhairbodhisattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ samavadhānaṃ pratilabhate | ajaḍaśca bhavati, tīkṣṇendriyaḥ prajñāvān | na tasya jātiśatasahasrairapi pūti mukhaṃ bhavati na durgandhi | nāpyasya jihvārogo bhavati, na mukharogo bhavati | na ca śyāmadanto bhavati, na viṣamadanto bhavati, na pītadanto bhavati, na duḥsaṃsthitadanto na khaṇḍadanto na patitadanto na vakradanto na lamboṣṭho bhavati, nābhyantaroṣṭho na prasāritoṣṭho na khaṇḍoṣṭho na vaṅkoṣṭho na kṛṣṇoṣṭho na bībhatsoṣṭho bhavati | na cipīṭanāso bhavati, na vakranāso bhavati | na dīrghamukho bhavati, na vaṅkamukho bhavati, na kṛṣṇamukho bhavati, nāpriyadarśanamukhaḥ | api tu khalvajita sūkṣmasujātajihvādantoṣṭho bhavati āyatanāsaḥ | praṇītamukhamaṇḍalaḥ subhrūḥ suparinikṣiptalalāṭo bhavati | suparipūrṇapuruṣavyañjanapratilābhī ca bhavati | tathāgataṃ ca avavādānuśāsakaṃ pratilabhate | kṣipraṃ ca buddhairbhagavadbhiḥ saha samavadhānaṃ pratilabhate | paśya ajita ekasattvamapi nāma utsāhayitvā iyat puṇyaṃ prasavati | kaḥ punarvādo yaḥ satkṛtya śṛṇuyāt, satkṛtya vācayet, satkṛtya
deśayet, satkṛtya prakāśayediti ||
body.translated_text: — or should cause another to sit, or should share his seat with another being — by that meritorious formation he will become the possessor of the seats of <s>Śakra</s>, the seats of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the thrones of wheel-turning kings. And furthermore, <s>Ajita</s>, if any son or daughter of good family should say to another person: 'Come, good sir! There is a <s>dharmaparyāya</s> called the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> — listen to it!' And if that person, through that encouragement, should hear it even for a moment — that being, by the wholesome root formed through that encouragement, will obtain association with <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained <s>dhāraṇī</s>. He will be not dull but sharp in faculties and wise. For hundreds of thousands of births his mouth will not be foul or ill-smelling. Nor will he have any disease of the tongue, or disease of the mouth. His teeth will not be dark, nor uneven, nor yellow, nor badly set, nor broken, nor fallen, nor crooked. His lips will not be drooping, nor turned inward, nor protruding, nor cleft, nor crooked, nor dark, nor repulsive. His nose will not be flat, nor crooked. His face will not be long, nor crooked, nor dark, nor unpleasant to look at. Rather, <s>Ajita</s>, his tongue, teeth, and lips will be delicate and well-formed; his nose will be long and handsome; his facial contour will be excellent; his eyebrows will be fine; his forehead will be well-shaped. He will attain the full characteristics of a man. And he will obtain a <s>Tathāgata</s> as his admonisher and instructor. Quickly he will obtain association with <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones. See, <s>Ajita</s>, even by encouraging one single being, one generates this much merit. How much more so for one who respectfully hears, respectfully recites, respectfully teaches, and respectfully illuminates [this sūtra]!

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: pañcāśimo yaśca paraṃparāyāṃ sūtrasyimasyo śṛṇutekagāthām /
children.translated_text: The fiftieth person in the chain of successive [hearers] who hears one verse of this <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: anumodayitvā ca prasannacittaḥ śṛṇuṣva puṇyaṃ bhavi yattakaṃ tat // Saddhp_17.2 //
children.translated_text: and having rejoiced with a serene mind — hear what merit shall be his! || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.2 ||

children.text: sa caiva puruṣo bhavi dānadātā sattvān koṭīnayuteṣu nityam /
children.translated_text: And that very man who is a giver of gifts, constantly, to <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of beings —

children.text: ye pūrvamaupamyakṛtā mayā vai tān sarvi tarpeya aśīti varṣān // Saddhp_17.3 //
children.translated_text: those whom I formerly described by comparison — he would satisfy all of them for eighty years. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.3 ||

children.text: so dṛṣṭva teṣāṃ ca jarāmupasthitāṃ valī ca khaṇḍaṃ ca śiraśca pāṇḍaram /
children.translated_text: Seeing old age approaching them, their wrinkles and gray heads and decayed [state],

children.text: hāhādhimucyanti hi sarvasattvā yannūna dharmeṇa hu ovadeyam // Saddhp_17.4 //
children.translated_text: he would be deeply moved [thinking]: 'Alas! All these beings — surely I should instruct them in the <s>Dharma</s>!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.4 ||

children.text: so teṣa dharmaṃ vadatīha paścānnirvāṇabhūmiṃ ca prakāśayeta /
children.translated_text: He would then teach them the <s>Dharma</s>, and would illuminate the ground of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>:

children.text: sarve bhavāḥ phenamarīcikalpā nirvidyathā sarvabhaveṣu kṣipram // Saddhp_17.5 //
children.translated_text: 'All existences are like foam and mirages — be quickly disenchanted with all existences!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.5 ||

children.text: te sarvasattvāśca śruṇitva dharmaṃ tasyaiva dātuḥ puruṣasya antikāt /
children.translated_text: And all those beings, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from that very donor, that man,

children.text: arhantabhūtā bhavi ekakāle kṣīṇāsravā antimadehadhāriṇaḥ // Saddhp_17.6 //
children.translated_text: would become <s>Arhats</s> at one time — with outflows destroyed, bearing their final bodies. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.6 ||

children.text: puṇyaṃ tato bahutaru tasya hi syat paraṃparātaḥ śruṇi ekagāthām /
children.translated_text: Far more merit than that would he have who hears one verse through the chain of succession,

children.text: anumodi vā yattaku tasya puṇyaṃ kala puṇyaskandhaḥ purimo na bhoti // Saddhp_17.7 //
children.translated_text: or who rejoices — that much is his merit. The former heap of merit does not equal [even a fraction]. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.7 ||

children.text: evaṃ bahu tasya bhaveta puṇyaṃ anantakaṃ yasya pramāṇu nāsti /
children.translated_text: Thus much merit would be his — infinite, whose measure does not exist —

children.text: gāthāṃ pi śrutvaika paraṃparāya kiṃ vā punaḥ saṃmukha yo śruṇeyā // Saddhp_17.8 //
children.translated_text: even from hearing one verse through the chain of succession. How much more so for one who hears it face to face! || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.8 ||

children.text: yaścaikasattvaṃ pi vadeya tatra protsāhaye gaccha śṛṇuṣva dharmam /
children.translated_text: And whoever would say to even one being: 'Go, encouraged, and hear the <s>Dharma</s>!' —

children.text: sudurlabhaṃ sutramidaṃ hi bhoti kalpāna koṭīnayutairanekaiḥ // Saddhp_17.9 //
children.translated_text: [knowing that] this <s>sūtra</s> is indeed extremely rare, [appearing] through many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s> — || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.9 ||

children.text: sa cāpi protsāhitu tena sattvaḥ śruṇeya sūtrema muhūrtakaṃ pi /
children.translated_text: and that being, thus encouraged by him, would hear this <s>sūtra</s> even for a moment —

children.text: tasyāpi dharmasya phalaṃ śṛṇohi mukharoga tasya na kadāci bhoti // Saddhp_17.10 //
children.translated_text: hear the fruit of that <s>Dharma</s> [act] too: disease of the mouth shall never be his! || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.10 ||

children.text: jihvāpi tasya na kadāci duḥkhati na tasya dantā patitā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: His tongue too shall never ail, nor shall his teeth ever fall out;

children.text: śyāmātha pītā viṣamā ca jātu bībhatsitoṣṭho na ca jātu bhoti // Saddhp_17.11 //
children.translated_text: dark, yellow, or uneven [teeth shall he never have] — nor shall his lips ever be repulsive. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.11 ||

body.text: kuṭilaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca na jātu dīrghaṃ mukhaṃ na cipiṭaṃ sya kadāci bhoti /
body.translated_text: Neither crooked, nor dry, nor long — his face shall never be flat;

body.text: susaṃsthitā nāsa tathā lalāṭaṃ dantā ca oṣṭho mukhamaṇḍalaṃ ca // Saddhp_17.12 //
body.translated_text: well-formed shall be his nose, and likewise his forehead, his teeth, his lips, and his facial contour. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.12 ||

children.text: priyadarśano bhoti sadā narāṇāṃ pūrtiṃ ca vakraṃ na kadāci bhoti /
children.translated_text: He shall always be pleasant to behold for people; his [face] shall never be swollen or crooked;

children.text: yathotpalasyeha sadā sugandhiḥ pravāyate tasya mukhasya gandhaḥ // Saddhp_17.13 //
children.translated_text: just as the fragrance of a blue lotus always wafts, so shall the fragrance of his mouth. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.13 ||

children.text: gṛhādvihāraṃ hi vrajitva dhīro gaccheta sūtraṃ śravaṇāya etat /
children.translated_text: The wise one, having gone from home to a monastery, would go to hear this <s>sūtra</s>;

children.text: gatvā ca so tatra śṛṇe muhūrtaṃ prasannacittasya phalaṃ śṛṇotha // Saddhp_17.14 //
children.translated_text: and having gone there, he hears it for a moment — hear the fruit for one with a serene mind! || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.14 ||

children.text: sugauru tasyo bhavatetmabhāvaḥ pariyāti co aśvarathehi dhīraḥ /
children.translated_text: His bodily existence shall become very excellent; that steadfast one shall travel in horse-chariots,

children.text: hastīrathāṃśco abhiruhya uccān ratanehi citrānanucaṃkrameyā // Saddhp_17.15 //
children.translated_text: and shall mount lofty elephant-chariots, and shall ride variegated vehicles adorned with jewels. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.15 ||

children.text: vibhūṣitāṃ so śibikāṃ labheta narairanekairiha vāhyamānām /
children.translated_text: He shall obtain an adorned palanquin, carried by many men here;

children.text: gatvāpi dharmaṃ śravaṇāya tasya phalaṃ śubhaṃ bhoti ca evarūpam // Saddhp_17.16 //
children.translated_text: even from going to hear the <s>Dharma</s>, his auspicious fruit shall be of such a kind. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.16 ||

children.text: niṣadya cāsau pariṣāya tatra śuklena karmeṇa kṛtena tena /
children.translated_text: And by sitting there in the assembly, through that bright <s>karma</s> that was done,

children.text: śakrāsanānāṃ bhavate sa lābhī brahmāsanānāṃ ca nṛpāsanānām // Saddhp_17.17 //
children.translated_text: he shall become the possessor of the seats of <s>Śakra</s>, the seats of <s>Brahmā</s>, and the thrones of kings. || <s>Saddhp</s> 17.17 ||

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye anumodanāpuṇyanirdeśaparivarto nāma saptadaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventeenth chapter, named 'The Chapter on the Teaching of the Merit of Rejoicing' (<s>Anumodanāpuṇyanirdeśaparivarta</s>), in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_18: dharmabhāṇakānuśaṃsāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 18: The Chapter on the Merits of the Dharma-Preacher (<s>Dharmabhāṇakānuśaṃsāparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān satatasamitābhiyuktaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayāmāsa - yaḥ kaścit kulaputra imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayiṣyati vācayiṣyati vā deśayiṣyati vā likhiṣyati va, sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā va aṣṭau cakṣurguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate, dvādaśa śrotraguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate, aṣṭau ghrāṇaguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate, dvādaśa jihvāguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate, aṣṭau kāyaguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate, dvādaśa manoguṇaśatāni pratilapsyate | tasyaibhirbahubhirguṇaśataiḥ ṣaḍindriyagrāmaḥ pariśuddhaḥ supariśuddho bhaviṣyati | sa evaṃ pariśuddhena cakṣurindriyeṇa prākṛtena māṃsacakṣuṣā mātāpitṛsaṃbhavena trisāhasramahāsāhasrāṃ lokadhātuṃ sāntarbahiḥ saśailavanaṣaṇḍāmadho yāvadavīcimahānirayamupādāya upari ca yāvat bhavāgraṃ tat sarvaṃ drakṣyati prākṛtena māṃsacakṣuṣā | ye ca tasmin sattvā upapannāḥ, tān sarvān drakṣyati, karmavipākaṃ ca teṣāṃ jñāsyatīti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s> (Ever-Diligent): 'Whoever, son of good family, will uphold, recite, teach, or write this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — that son of good family or daughter of good family will obtain eight hundred qualities of the eye, twelve hundred qualities of the ear, eight hundred qualities of the nose, twelve hundred qualities of the tongue, eight hundred qualities of the body, and twelve hundred qualities of the mind. With these many hundreds of qualities, the group of six sense-faculties will become pure, completely pure. With such a purified eye-faculty — the natural, fleshly eye, born of mother and father — he will see the entire three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, inside and out, with its mountains and forests, down to the <s>Avīci</s> great hell and up to the summit of existence — he will see all of this with the natural, fleshly eye. And whatever beings have been reborn therein, he will see them all and will know the ripening of their <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that moment, spoke these verses:

children.text: ya imaṃ sūtra bhāṣeta parṣāsu ca viśāradaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever would teach this <s>sūtra</s> in assemblies, confident,

children.text: anolīnaḥ prakāśeyā guṇāṃstasya śṛṇuṣva me // Saddhp_18.1 //
children.translated_text: undaunted, illuminating it — hear from me his qualities: || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.1 ||

children.text: aṣṭau guṇaśatāastasya cakṣuṣo bhonti sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: He obtains eight hundred qualities of the eye in every respect,

children.text: yenāsya vimalaṃ bhoti śuddhaṃ cakṣuranāvilam // Saddhp_18.2 //
children.translated_text: whereby his eye becomes immaculate, pure, and unclouded. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.2 ||

children.text: sa māṃsacakṣuṣā tena mātāpitṛkasaṃbhunā /
children.translated_text: With that fleshly eye, born of mother and father,

children.text: paśyate lokadhātvemāṃ saśailavanakānanām // Saddhp_18.3 //
children.translated_text: he sees this world-system with its mountains, forests, and groves; || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.3 ||

children.text: meruṃ sumeru sarvā ca cakravālā sa paśyati /
children.translated_text: <s>Meru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, and all the <s>Cakravālas</s> he sees,

children.text: ye cānye parvatāḥ khaṇḍāḥ samudrāṃścāpi paśyati // Saddhp_18.4 //
children.translated_text: and all other mountain ranges, and oceans too he sees. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.4 ||

children.text: yāvānavīci heṣṭhena bhavāgraṃ copariṣṭataḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Avīci</s> below to the summit of existence above,

children.text: sarvaṃ sa paśyate dhīro māṃsacakṣusya īdṛśam // Saddhp_18.5 //
children.translated_text: the wise one sees everything — such is [the power of] the fleshly eye! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.5 ||

children.text: na tāva divyacakṣu sya bhoti no cāpi jāyate /
children.translated_text: Not yet has the divine eye arisen in him, nor has it been produced;

children.text: viṣayo māṃsacakṣusya bhavettasyāyamīdṛśaḥ // Saddhp_18.6 //
children.translated_text: the range of the fleshly eye becomes of such a kind for him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.6 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ satatasamitābhiyukta sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayamānaḥ pareṣāṃ ca saṃśrāvayamānastairdvādaśabhiḥ śrotraguṇaśataiḥ samanvāgataḥ ye trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau vividhāḥ śabdā niścaranti yāvadavīcirmahānirayo yāvacca bhavāgraṃ sāntarbahiḥ, tadyathā - hastiśabdā vā aśvaśabdā vā uṣṭraśabdā vā gośabdā vā ajaśabdā vā janapadaśabdā vā rathaśabdā vā ruditaśabdā vā śokaśabdā vā bhairavaśabdā vā śaṅkhaśabdā vā ghaṇṭāśabdā vā paṭahaśabdā vā bherīśabdā vā krīḍāśabdā vā gītaśabdā vā nṛtyaśabdā vā tūryaśabdā vā vādyaśabdā vā strīśabdā vā puruṣaśabdā vā dārakaśabdā vā
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s>, that son of good family or daughter of good family who illuminates this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse and causes others to hear it, endowed with those twelve hundred qualities of the ear — whatever various sounds issue forth in the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, from <s>Avīci</s> great hell up to the summit of existence, inside and out — such as the sounds of elephants, horses, camels, cattle, goats, sounds of the countryside, sounds of chariots, sounds of weeping, sounds of grief, sounds of terror, sounds of conch-shells, sounds of bells, sounds of kettledrums, sounds of large drums, sounds of play, sounds of singing, sounds of dancing, sounds of musical instruments, sounds of music, sounds of women, sounds of men, sounds of boys,

body.text: dārikāśabdā vā dharmaśabdā vā adharmaśabdā vā sukhaśabdā vā duḥkhaśabdā vā bālaśabdā vā āryaśabdā vā manojñaśabdā vā amanojñaśabdā vā devaśabdā vā nāgaśabdā vā yakṣaśabdā vā rākṣasaśabdā vā gandharvaśabdā vā asuraśabdā vā garuḍaśabdā vā kinnaraśabdā vā mahoragaśabdā vā manuṣyaśabdā vā amanuṣyaśabdā vā agniśabdā vā vāyuśabdā vā udakaśabdā vā grāmaśabdā vā nagaraśabdā vā bhikṣuśabdā vā śrāvakaśabdā vā pratyekabuddhaśabdā vā bodhisattvaśabdā vā tathāgataśabdā vā, yāvantaḥ kecitrisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sāntarbahiḥ śabdā niścaranti, tān śabdāṃstena prākṛtena pariśuddhena śrotrendriyeṇa śṛṇoti | na ca tāvaddivyaṃ śrotramabhinirharati | teṣāṃ teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ rutānyavabudhyate, vibhāvayati vibhajati tena ca prākṛtena śrotrendriyeṇa | teṣāṃ teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ rutāni śṛṇvatastasya taiḥ sarvaśabdaiḥ śrotrendriyaṃ nābhibhūyate | evaṃrūpaḥ satatasamitābhiyukta tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya śrotrendriyapratilambho bhavati, na ca tāvaddivyaṃ śrotramabhinirharati ||
body.translated_text: sounds of girls, sounds of <s>Dharma</s>, sounds of non-<s>Dharma</s>, sounds of happiness, sounds of suffering, sounds of the foolish, sounds of the noble, pleasant sounds, unpleasant sounds, sounds of gods, sounds of <s>nāgas</s>, sounds of <s>yakṣas</s>, sounds of <s>rākṣasas</s>, sounds of <s>gandharvas</s>, sounds of <s>asuras</s>, sounds of <s>garuḍas</s>, sounds of <s>kinnaras</s>, sounds of <s>mahoragas</s>, sounds of humans, sounds of non-humans, sounds of fire, sounds of wind, sounds of water, sounds of villages, sounds of cities, sounds of monks, sounds of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, sounds of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, sounds of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, sounds of <s>Tathāgatas</s> — whatever sounds issue forth in the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, inside and out — he hears all those sounds with that natural, purified ear-faculty. Yet he has not produced the divine ear. He understands, distinguishes, and discerns the voices of those various beings with that natural ear-faculty. And though hearing the voices of those various beings, his ear-faculty is not overwhelmed by all those sounds. Such is the attainment of the ear-faculty of that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s> (Ever-Diligent), yet he has not produced the divine ear.

body.text: idamavocadbhagavān | idaṃ vaditvā sugato hyathāparametaduvāca śāstā -
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, further spoke thus:

children.text: śrotrendriyaṃ tasya viśuddhu bhoti anāvilaṃ prākṛtakaṃ ca tāvat /
children.translated_text: 'His ear-faculty becomes pure, immaculate, and natural as before;

children.text: vividhān hi yeneha śṛṇoti śabdāniha lokadhātau hi aśeṣato 'yam // Saddhp_18.7 //
children.translated_text: by which he hears various sounds here, in this world-system, completely and without remainder. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.7 ||

children.text: hastīna aśvāna śṛṇoti śabdān rathāna goṇāna ajaiḍakānām /
children.translated_text: He hears the sounds of elephants and horses, of chariots, of cattle, and of sheep and goats,

children.text: bherīmṛdaṅgāna sughoṣakānāṃ vīṇāna veṇūnatha vallakīnām // Saddhp_18.8 //
children.translated_text: of drums and <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, of those that produce beautiful sounds, of <s>vīṇās</s>, flutes, and lutes. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.8 ||

children.text: gītaṃ manojñaṃ madhuraṃ śṛṇoti na cāpi so sajjati tatra dhīraḥ /
children.translated_text: He hears sweet and delightful singing, yet that wise one does not become attached to it;

children.text: manuṣyakoṭīna śṛṇoti śabdān bhāṣanti yaṃ yaṃ ca yahiṃ yahiṃ te // Saddhp_18.9 //
children.translated_text: he hears the sounds of <s>koṭis</s> of humans — whatever they speak, wherever they are. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.9 ||

children.text: devāna co nitya śṛṇoti śabdān gītasvaraṃ ca madhuraṃ manojñam /
children.translated_text: He constantly hears the sounds of gods — sweet and delightful singing voices,

children.text: puruṣāṇa istrīṇa rutāni cāpi tatha dārakāṇāmatha dārikāṇām // Saddhp_18.10 //
children.translated_text: and the voices of men and women, and likewise of boys and girls. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.10 ||

body.text: ye parvateṣveva guhānivāsī kalaviṅkakā kokila barhiṇaśca /
body.translated_text: Those who dwell in caves in the mountains — the <s>kalaviṅka</s> birds, the cuckoos, and the peacocks,

body.text: pakṣīṇa ye jīvakajīvakā hi teṣāṃ ca valgū śṛṇute hi śabdān // Saddhp_18.11 //
body.translated_text: and those birds called <s>jīvaka</s> and <s>jīvajīvaka</s> — he hears their beautiful sounds too. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.11 ||

children.text: narakeṣu ye vedana vedayanti sudāruṇāṃścāpi karonti śabdān /
children.translated_text: Those in the hells who experience sensations and make sounds most dreadful,

children.text: āhāraduḥkhairavapīḍitānāṃ yān preta kurvanti tathaiva śabdān // Saddhp_18.12 //
children.translated_text: and those sounds that <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) make, tormented by the suffering of hunger — || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.12 ||

children.text: asurāśca ye sāgaramadhyavāsino muñcanti ghoṣāṃstatha cānyamanyān /
children.translated_text: and the <s>Asuras</s> who dwell in the midst of the ocean, who utter cries among one another —

children.text: sarvānihastho sa hi dharmabhāṇakaḥ śṛṇoti śabdānna ca ostarīyati // Saddhp_18.13 //
children.translated_text: all those sounds that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher hears while standing here, and his [faculties] are not impaired. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.13 ||

children.text: tiryāṇa yonīṣu rutāni yāni anyonyasaṃbhāṣaṇatāṃ karonti /
children.translated_text: Whatever voices are in the animal realms, those who converse with one another —

children.text: iha sthitastānapi so śṛṇoti vividhāni śabdāni bahūvidhāni // Saddhp_18.14 //
children.translated_text: standing here, he hears those too — sounds of various and many kinds. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.14 ||

children.text: ye brahmaloke nivasanti devā akaniṣṭha ābhāsvara ye ca devāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those gods who dwell in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, and the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods,

children.text: ye cānyamanyasya karonti ghoṣān śṛṇoti tatsarvamaśeṣato 'sau // Saddhp_18.15 //
children.translated_text: and those who make sounds among one another — he hears all of that, completely and without remainder. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.15 ||

children.text: svādhyāya kurvantiha ye ca bhikṣavaḥ sugatāniha śāsani pravrajitvā /
children.translated_text: And those monks here who practice study, having gone forth in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s>,

children.text: parṣāsu ye deśayate ca dharmaṃ teṣāṃ pi śabdaṃ śṛṇute sa nityam // Saddhp_18.16 //
children.translated_text: and those who teach the <s>Dharma</s> in assemblies — he constantly hears their sounds too. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.16 ||

children.text: ye bodhisattvāściha lokadhātau svādhyāya kurvanti paraspareṇa /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> here in this world-system who practice study among one another,

children.text: saṃgīti dharmeṣu ca ye karonti śṛṇoti śabdān vividhāṃśca teṣām // Saddhp_18.17 //
children.translated_text: and those who make recitations of the <s>Dharma</s> — he hears their various sounds. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.17 ||

children.text: bhagavān pi buddho naradamyasārathiḥ parṣāsu dharmaṃ bruvate yamagram /
children.translated_text: The Blessed <s>Buddha</s> too, the tamer of men to be tamed, speaks the <s>Dharma</s> in assemblies — the supreme one —

children.text: taṃ cāpi so śṛṇvanti ekakāle yo bodhisattvo imu sūtra dhārayet // Saddhp_18.18 //
children.translated_text: and that too he hears at the same time — whoever, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, upholds this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.18 ||

children.text: sarve trisāhasri imasmi kṣetre ye sattva kurvanti bahūṃ pi śabdān /
children.translated_text: All the beings in this three-thousand field who make even many sounds,

children.text: abhyantareṇāpi ca bāhireṇa avīciparyanta bhavāgramūrdhvam // Saddhp_18.19 //
children.translated_text: both inside and outside, from <s>Avīci</s> to the summit of existence above — || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.19 ||

children.text: sarveṣa sattvāna śṛṇoti śabdān naṃ cāpi kṣetraṃ uparudhyate 'sya /
children.translated_text: he hears the sounds of all beings, yet his field [of hearing] is not impeded;

children.text: paṭvindriyo jānati sthānasthānaṃ śrotrendriyaṃ prākṛtakaṃ hi tāvat // Saddhp_18.20 //
children.translated_text: with sharp faculties he knows what is fitting and unfitting — the ear-faculty being natural as before. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.20 ||

children.text: na ca tāva divyasmi karoti yatnaṃ prakṛtya saṃtiṣṭhati śrotrametat /
children.translated_text: Not yet does he make effort for the divine [ear]; the ear remains in its natural [state];

children.text: sūtraṃ hi yo dhārayate viśārado guṇā sya etādṛśakā bhavanti // Saddhp_18.21 //
children.translated_text: such are the qualities of whoever, confident, upholds this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.21 ||'

body.text: punaraparaṃ satatasamitābhiyukta asya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayataḥ prakāśayataḥ svādhyāyato likhato 'ṣṭābhirguṇaśataiḥ samanvāgataṃ ghrāṇendriyaṃ pariśuddhaṃ bhavati | sa tena pariśuddhena ghrāṇendriyeṇa ye trisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau sāntarbahirvividhagandhāḥ saṃvidyante, tadyathā - pūtigandhā vā manojñagandhā vā nānāprakārāṇāṃ sumanasāṃ gandhāḥ, tadyathā - jātimallikācampakapāṭalagandhāḥ, tān gandhān ghrāyati | jalajānāmapi puṣpāṇāṃ vividhān gandhān ghrāyati, tadyathā - utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkāṇāṃ gandhān ghrāyati | vividhānāṃ puṣpaphalavṛkṣāṇāṃ puṣpaphalagandhān ghrāyati, tadyathā - candanatamālapatratagarāgarusurabhigandhān ghrāyati | nānāvikārāṇi gandhavikṛtiśatasahasrāṇi yānyekasthānasthitaḥ sarvāṇi ghrāyati | sattvānāmapi vividhān gandhān ghrāyati, tadyathā - hastyaśvagaveḍakapaśugandhān ghrāyati | vividhānāṃ ca tiryagyonigatānāṃ prāṇināmātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | strīpuruṣātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | dārakadārikātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | dūrasthānāmapi tṛṇagulmauṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ gandhān ghrāyati | bhūtān gandhān vandati, na ca tairgandhaiḥ saṃhriyate, na saṃmuhyati | sa ihasthita eva devānāmapi gandhān ghrāyati, tadyathā - pārijātakasya kovidārasya māndāravamahāmāndāravamañjūṣakamahāmañjūṣakānāṃ divyānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ gandhān ghrāyati | divyānāmagarucūrṇacandanacūrṇānāṃ gandhān ghrāyati | divyānāṃ ca nānāvidhānāṃ puṣpavikṛtiśatasahasrāṇāṃ gandhān ghrāyati, nāmāni caiṣāṃ saṃjānīte | devaputrātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati, tadyathā - śakrasya devānāmindrasya ātmabhāvagandhaṃ ghrāyati | taṃ ca jānīte yadi vā vaijayante prāsāde krīḍantaṃ ramantaṃ paricārayantaṃ yadi vā sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ devānāṃ trāyastriṃśānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayantaṃ yadi vā udyānabhūmau niryāntaṃ krīḍanāya | anyeṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇāṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Satatasamitābhiyukta</s>, the nose-faculty of that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> who upholds, illuminates, studies, and writes this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse becomes endowed with eight hundred qualities and becomes pure. With that purified nose-faculty, whatever various fragrances there are in the three-thousand-great-thousand world-system, inside and out — such as foul odors or pleasant odors, the scents of various kinds of flowers — such as the scents of jasmine, <s>mallikā</s>, champaka, and <s>pāṭala</s> — he smells those scents. He smells the various fragrances of water-born flowers too — such as the scents of <s>utpala</s> (blue lotus), <s>padma</s> (lotus), <s>kumuda</s> (white lily), and <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus). He smells the fragrances of the flowers and fruits of various flower-and-fruit-bearing trees — such as the scents of sandalwood, <s>tamālapatra</s>, <s>tagara</s>, <s>agaru</s> (aloe), and <s>surabhi</s> (fragrant wood). He smells the fragrances of hundreds of thousands of variously compounded perfume preparations, all while standing in one place. He smells the various fragrances of beings too — such as the scents of elephants, horses, cattle, goats, and other animals. He smells the fragrances of the bodies of various beings born in the animal realm. He smells the fragrances of the bodies of women and men. He smells the fragrances of the bodies of boys and girls. He smells the scents of grasses, shrubs, herbs, and forest trees even from afar. He smells the actual fragrances, yet is not captivated or confused by those fragrances. Standing right here, he also smells the fragrances of the gods — such as the scents of the divine flowers <s>Pārijātaka</s>, <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Māndārava</s>, great <s>Māndārava</s>, <s>Mañjūṣaka</s>, and great <s>Mañjūṣaka</s>. He smells the scents of divine aloe powder and sandalwood powder. He smells the scents of hundreds of thousands of various divine flower preparations, and he knows their names. He smells the fragrances of the bodies of the sons of the gods — such as the body-fragrance of <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods — and he knows whether he is playing, enjoying, and amusing himself in the <s>Vaijayanta</s> Palace, or teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the gods of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) in the <s>Sudharmā</s> divine assembly hall, or going out to the pleasure-grounds for recreation. And the individual body-fragrances of the other sons of the gods,

body.text:
pṛthakpṛthagātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | devakanyānāmapi devavadhūnāmapi ātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | devakumārāṇāmapi ātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | devakumārikāṇāmapi ātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati |
na ca tairgandhaiḥ saṃhriyate | anena paryāyeṇa yāvad bhavāgropapannānāmapi sattvānāmātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | brahmakāyikānāmapi devaputrāṇāṃ mahābrahmaṇāmapi cātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | anena paryāyeṇa sarvadevanikāyānāmapi ātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | śrāvakapratyekabuddhabodhisattvatathāgatātmabhāvagandhān ghrāyati | tathāgatāsanānāmapi gandhān ghrāyati | yasmiṃśca sthāne te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā viharanti, tacca prajānāti | na cāsya tad ghrāṇendiyaṃ taistairvividhairgandhaiḥ pratihanyate, nopahanyate, na saṃpīḍyate | ākāṅkṣamāṇaśca tāṃstān gandhān pareṣāmapi vyākaroti | na cāsya smṛtirupahanyate ||
body.translated_text: he smells them individually. He smells the body-fragrances of divine maidens and divine consorts too. He smells the body-fragrances of divine youths and divine young women too. He is not captivated by those fragrances. In this manner, he smells the body-fragrances of beings reborn even up to the summit of existence. He smells the body-fragrances of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> gods and of the great <s>Brahmas</s> too. In this manner, he smells the body-fragrances of all classes of gods. He smells the body-fragrances of <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>. He smells the fragrances of the seats of <s>Tathāgatas</s> too. And the place where those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, dwell — that too he recognizes. Yet his nose-faculty is not struck, injured, or oppressed by those various fragrances. And if he wishes, he can distinguish those various fragrances for others as well. And his mindfulness is not impaired.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: ghrāṇendriyaṃ tasya viśuddha bhoti vividhāṃśca gandhān bahu ghrāyate 'sau /
children.translated_text: His sense of smell becomes purified, and he smells the various scents,

children.text: ye lokadhātau hi imasmi sarve sugandha durgandha bhavanti kecit // Saddhp_18.22 //
children.translated_text: all that exist in this world-system — fragrant and foul alike! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.22 ||

children.text: jātīya gandho atha mallikāyā tamālapatrasya ca candanasya /
children.translated_text: The scent of jasmine and of <s>mallikā</s> (Arabian jasmine), of <s>tamālapatra</s> (bay-leaf) and sandalwood,

children.text: tagarasya gandho agarusya cāpi vividhāna puṣpāṇa phalāna cāpi // Saddhp_18.23 //
children.translated_text: the scent of <s>tagara</s> (valerian) and of aloe-wood, and of various flowers and fruits as well! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.23 ||

children.text: sattvāna gandhān pi tathaiva jānati narāṇa nārīṇa ca dūrataḥ sthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: He knows the scents of beings likewise — of men and women, though standing far away,

children.text: kumārakāṇāṃ ca kumārikāṇāṃ gandhena so jānati teṣa sthānam // Saddhp_18.24 //
children.translated_text: and of boys and girls — by their scent he knows their location! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.24 ||

children.text: rājñāṃ pi so jānati cakravartināṃ balacakravartīnatha maṇḍalīnām /
children.translated_text: He knows also of kings — wheel-turners, mighty wheel-turners, and territorial lords,

children.text: kumārakāmātya tathaiva teṣāṃ gandhena cāntaḥpura sarva jānati // Saddhp_18.25 //
children.translated_text: their princes and ministers likewise — and by scent he knows the entire inner palace! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.25 ||

children.text: paribhogaratnāni bahūvidhāni kupyāni bhūmau nihitāni yāni /
children.translated_text: Jewels of enjoyment of many kinds, and goods deposited in the earth,

children.text: strīratnabhūtāni bhavanti yāpi gandhena so jānati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.26 //
children.translated_text: and those who are jewels among women — by scent that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows [them all]! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.26 ||

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yā ābharaṇā bhavanti kāyasmi āmukta vicitrarūpā /
children.translated_text: And whatever ornaments they wear, adorning their bodies in variegated forms,

children.text: vastraṃ ca mālyaṃ ca vilepanaṃ ca gandhena so jānati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.27 //
children.translated_text: garments, garlands, and ointments — by scent that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.27 ||

children.text: sthitāṃ niṣaṇṇāṃ śayitāṃ tathaiva krīḍāratiṃ ṛddhibalaṃ ca sarvam /
children.translated_text: Standing, sitting, lying down, and likewise all play, delight, and supernatural powers —

children.text: so jānatī ghrāṇabalena dhīro yo dhārayet sūtramidaṃ variṣṭham // Saddhp_18.28 //
children.translated_text: that wise one knows [all this] by the power of smell — whoever upholds this supreme <s>sūtra</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.28 ||

children.text: sugandhatailāna tathaiva gandhān nānāvidhān puṣpaphalāna gandhān /
children.translated_text: And likewise the scents of fragrant oils, the manifold scents of flowers and fruits —

children.text: sakṛtasthito jānati ghrāyate ca amukasmi deśasmi imasmi gandhān // Saddhp_18.29 //
children.translated_text: standing in one place, he knows and smells: 'In such-and-such a region are these scents!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.29 ||

children.text: ye parvatānāṃ vivarāntareṣu bahu candanā puṣpita tatra santi /
children.translated_text: In the crevices between mountains, where many sandalwood trees bloom,

children.text: ye cāpi tasminnivasanti sattvāḥ sarveṣa gandhena vidurvijānati // Saddhp_18.30 //
children.translated_text: and whatever beings dwell therein — by scent he knows [them] all with understanding! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.30 ||

children.text: ye cakravālasya bhavanti pārśve ye sāgarasyo nivasanti madhye /
children.translated_text: Those who dwell on the slopes of the <s>Cakravāla</s> (world-rim mountains), those who dwell in the midst of the ocean,

children.text: pṛthivīya ye madhyi vasanti sattvāḥ sarvān sa gandhena vidurvijānati // Saddhp_18.31 //
children.translated_text: those beings who dwell inside the earth — he knows them all by scent with understanding! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.31 ||

children.text: surāṃśca jānāti tathāsurāṃśca asurāṇa kanyāśca vijānate 'sau /
children.translated_text: He knows the gods and likewise the <s>asuras</s>, and he discerns the daughters of the <s>asuras</s>,

children.text: asurāṇa krīḍāśca ratiṃ ca jānati ghrāṇasya tasyedṛśakaṃ balaṃ hi // Saddhp_18.32 //
children.translated_text: and he knows the play and delight of the <s>asuras</s> — such is the power of his sense of smell! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.32 ||

children.text: aṭavīṣu ye keci catuṣpadāsti siṃhāśca vyāghrāstatha hastināgāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever four-legged creatures are in the forests — lions, tigers, and elephant-lords,

children.text: mahiṣā gavā ye gavayaśca tatra ghrāṇena so jānati teṣa vāsam // Saddhp_18.33 //
children.translated_text: buffaloes, cattle, and wild oxen there — by smell he knows their dwelling place! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.33 ||

children.text: striyaśca yā gurviṇikā bhavanti kumārakāṃ vāpi kumārikāṃ vā /
children.translated_text: And women who are pregnant, whether carrying a boy or a girl,

children.text: dhārenti kukṣau hi kilāntakāyā gandhena so jānati yaṃ tahiṃ syāt // Saddhp_18.34 //
children.translated_text: bearing [the child] in the womb within their bodies — by scent he knows what is there! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.34 ||

children.text: āpannasattvāṃ pi vijānate 'sau vināśadharmāṃ pi vijānate 'sau /
children.translated_text: He discerns those who have conceived, and he discerns those destined for destruction;

children.text: iyaṃ pi nārī vyapanītaduḥkhā prasaviṣyate puṇyamayaṃ kumāram // Saddhp_18.35 //
children.translated_text: 'This woman too, her suffering removed, will give birth to a meritorious boy!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.35 ||

children.text: puruṣāṇa abhiprāyu bahuṃ vijānate abhiprāyagandhaṃ ca tathaiva ghrāyate /
children.translated_text: He discerns the many intentions of men, and likewise smells the scent of intention;

children.text: raktāna duṣṭāna tathaiva mrakṣiṇāṃ upaśāntacittāna ca gandha ghrāyate // Saddhp_18.36 //
children.translated_text: he smells the scent of those attached, those hostile, those deceitful, and those with calmed minds! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.36 ||

children.text: pṛthivīya ye cāpi nidhāna santi ghanaṃ hiraṇyaṃ ca suvarṇarūpyam /
children.translated_text: And whatever treasures are within the earth — solid gold, silver, and gold-ore,

children.text: mañjūṣa lohī ca tathā supūrṇā gandhena so ghrāyati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.37 //
children.translated_text: well-filled copper caskets — by scent that <s>Bodhisattva</s> smells [them]! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.37 ||

children.text: hārārdhahārān maṇimuktikāśca anarghaprāptā vividhā ca ratnā /
children.translated_text: Necklaces and half-necklaces, gems, and pearls,

children.text: gandhena so jānati tāni sarvā anarghanāmaṃ dyutisaṃsthitaṃ ca // Saddhp_18.38 //
children.translated_text: various jewels of priceless value — by scent he knows them all, their priceless names and radiant natures! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.38 ||

children.text: upariṃ ca deveṣu tathaiva puṣpā mandāravāṃścaiva mañjūṣakāṃśca /
children.translated_text: And above, among the gods likewise, the flowers — <s>māndārava</s> and <s>mañjūṣaka</s>,

children.text: yā pārijātasya ca santi puṣpā iha sthito ghrāyati tā sa dhīraḥ // Saddhp_18.39 //
children.translated_text: and whatever flowers of the <s>pārijāta</s> tree exist — standing here, that wise one smells them! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.39 ||

children.text: vimāna ye yādṛśakāśca yasya udāra hīnāstatha madhyamāśca /
children.translated_text: The palaces of whatever kind and of whomever — exalted, lowly, or middling,

children.text: vicitrarūpāśca bhavanti yatra iha sthito ghrāṇabalena ghrāyati // Saddhp_18.40 //
children.translated_text: and variegated in form wherever they may be — standing here, he smells them by the power of smell! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.40 ||

children.text: udyānabhūmiṃ ca tathā prajānate sudharma devāsani vaijayante /
children.translated_text: And likewise he knows the garden grounds, the <s>Sudharmā</s> (assembly hall of the gods), and the <s>Vaijayanta</s> (palace of <s>Indra</s>),

children.text: prāsādaśreṣṭhe ca tathā vijānate ye co ramante tahi devaputrāḥ // Saddhp_18.41 //
children.translated_text: and likewise he knows the finest mansions, and the sons of the gods who delight therein! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.41 ||

body.text: iha sthito ghrāyati gandhu teṣāṃ gandhena so jānati devaputrān /
body.translated_text: Standing here, he smells their scent; by scent he knows the sons of the gods —

body.text: yo yatra karmā kurute sthito vā śete vā gacchati yatra vāpi // Saddhp_18.42 //
body.translated_text: who performs what activity, or stands, or sleeps, or goes wherever! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.42 ||

children.text: yā devakanyā bahupuṣpamaṇḍitā āmuktamālyābharaṇā alaṃkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: The daughters of the gods, adorned with many flowers, wearing garlands and ornaments, bedecked —

children.text: ramanti gacchanti ca yatra yatra gandhena so jānati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.43 //
children.translated_text: wherever they delight and go — by scent that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.43 ||

children.text: yāvadbhavāgrādupariṃ ca devā brahmā mahābrahma vimānacāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Up to the summit of existence, above, the gods — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Mahābrahmā</s>, those who move in palaces —

children.text: tāṃścāpi gandhena tahiṃ prajānate sthitāṃśca dhyāne atha vyutthitān vā // Saddhp_18.44 //
children.translated_text: even them he knows there by scent, whether established in meditation or risen from it! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.44 ||

children.text: ābhāsvarān jānati devaputrān cyutopapannāṃśca apūrvakāṃśca /
children.translated_text: He knows the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) gods, those who have died and been reborn, and those newly arisen;

children.text: ghrāṇendriyaṃ īdṛśa tasya bhoti yo bodhisattvo imu sūtra dhārayet // Saddhp_18.45 //
children.translated_text: such is the sense of smell of that <s>Bodhisattva</s> who upholds this <s>sūtra</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.45 ||

children.text: ya keci bhikṣū sugatasya śāsane abhiyuktarūpā sthita cakrameṣu /
children.translated_text: All monks in the teaching of the <s>Sugata</s> who are devoted in practice and stand on the walking-paths,

children.text: uddeśasvādhyāyaratāśca bhikṣavo sarvān hi so jānati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.46 //
children.translated_text: and those monks delighting in recitation and study — that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows them all! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.46 ||

children.text: ye śrāvakā bhonti jinasya putrā viharanti kecit sada vṛkṣamūle /
children.translated_text: Those who are <s>Śrāvakas</s>, sons of the <s>Jina</s>, some always dwelling at the foot of trees —

children.text: gandhena sarvān vidu jānate tān amutra bhikṣū amuko sthito ti // Saddhp_18.47 //
children.translated_text: by scent he knows them all with understanding: 'In such a place, such a monk is standing!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.47 ||

children.text: ye bodhisattvāḥ smṛtimanta dhyāyino uddeśasvādhyāyaratāśca ye sadā /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who are mindful and meditative, always delighting in recitation and study,

children.text: parṣāsu dharmaṃ ca prakāśayanti gandhena tān jānati bodhisattvaḥ // Saddhp_18.48 //
children.translated_text: and who illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> in assemblies — by scent that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows them! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.48 ||

children.text: yasyāṃ diśāyāṃ sugato mahāmunirdharmaṃ prakāśeti hitānukampakaḥ /
children.translated_text: In whatever direction the <s>Sugata</s>, the great sage, illuminates the <s>Dharma</s>, compassionate for welfare,

children.text: puraskṛtaḥ śrāvakasaṃghamadhye gandhena so jānati lokanātham // Saddhp_18.49 //
children.translated_text: attended in the midst of the assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> — by scent he knows the Lord of the World! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.49 ||

children.text: ye cāpi sattvā sya śṛṇoti dharmaṃ śrutvā ca ye prītamanā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: And those beings who hear his <s>Dharma</s>, and having heard, become joyful in mind —

children.text: iha sthito jānati bodhisattvo jinasya parṣāmapui tatra sarvām // Saddhp_18.50 //
children.translated_text: standing here, that <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows, and also the entire assembly of the <s>Jina</s> there! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.50 ||

children.text: etādṛśaṃ ghrāṇabalaṃ sya bhoti na ca tāva divyaṃ bhavate sya ghrāṇam /
children.translated_text: Such is the power of his sense of smell, yet his sense of smell has not yet become divine;

children.text: pūrvaṃgamaṃ tasya tu eta bhoti divyasya ghrāṇasya anāsravasya // Saddhp_18.51 //
children.translated_text: but this is the forerunner of that divine, outflow-free sense of smell! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.51 ||

body.text:
punaraparaṃ satatasamitābhiyukta sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayamāṇo deśayamānaḥ prakāśayamāno likhamānastairdvādaśabhirjihvāguṇaśataiḥ samanvāgataṃ jihvendriyaṃ pratilapsyate | sa tathārūpeṇa jihvendriyeṇa yān yān rasānāsvādayati, yān yān rasān jihvendriye upanikṣepsati, sarve te divyaṃ mahārasaṃ mokṣyante | tathā ca āsvādayiṣyati yathā na kaṃcid rasamamanaāpamāsvādayiṣyati | ye 'pi amanaāpā rasāste 'pi tasya jihvendriye samupanikṣiptāḥ divyaṃ rasaṃ mokṣyante | yaṃ ca dharmaṃ vyāhariṣyati parṣanmadhyagataḥ, tena tasya te sattvāḥ prīṇitendriyā bhaviṣyanti tuṣṭāḥ paramatuṣṭāḥ prāmodyajātāḥ | madhuraścāsya valgumanojñasvaro gambhīro niścariṣyati hṛdayaṃgamaḥ premaṇīyaḥ | tenāsya te sattvāstuṣṭā udagracittā bhaviṣyanti | yeṣāṃ ca dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati, te cāsya madhuranirghoṣaṃ śrutvā valgumanojñaṃ devā apyupasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravanāya ca | devaputrā api devakanyā api upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | śakrā api brahmāṇo 'pi brahmakāyikā api devaputrā upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | nāgā nāgakanyā api upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | asurā asurakanyā api upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | garūḍā garūḍakanyā api upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | kinnarāḥ kinnarakanyā api, mahoragā mahoragakanyā api, yakṣā yakṣakanyā api, piśācāḥ piśācakanyā api upasaṃkramitavyaṃ maṃsyante darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya ca | te cāsya satkāraṃ kariṣyanti, gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kariṣyanti | bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā api darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti | rājāno 'pi rājaputrā api rājāmātyā api rājamahāmātrā api darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti | balacakravartino 'pi rājānaḥ, cakravartino 'pi saptaratnasamanvāgatāḥ sakumārāḥ sāmātyāḥ sāntaḥpuraparivārā darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti
satkārārthinaḥ | tāvanmadhuraṃ sa dharmabhāṇako dharmaṃ bhāṣiṣyate yathābhūtaṃ yathoktaṃ tathāgatena | anye 'pi brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo naigamajānapadāstasya dharmabhāṇakasya
body.translated_text: Furthermore, that son of good family or daughter of good family, constantly and continuously devoted, who upholds, teaches, illuminates, or writes this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, will obtain a tongue-faculty endowed with twelve hundred qualities. Whatever tastes he savors, whatever tastes he places upon his tongue-faculty — all of them will release a divine, great flavor. And he will savor them in such a way that he will not taste any unpleasant flavor. Even those unpleasant flavors, placed upon his tongue-faculty, will release a divine flavor. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> he proclaims in the midst of the assembly — by that, the sense-faculties of those beings will be gladdened; they will be satisfied, supremely satisfied, and filled with joy. His voice will emerge sweet, pleasant, agreeable, deep, and heart-stirring, lovable. By it, those beings will be satisfied and elated in mind. And those to whom he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>, upon hearing his sweet tone, pleasant and agreeable — even gods will think it worth approaching, for the purpose of seeing, saluting, attending, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Sons of the gods and daughters of the gods too will think it worth approaching. <s>Śakras</s> too, <s>Brahmās</s> too, sons of the gods of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> heaven too will think it worth approaching. <s>Nāgas</s> and <s>nāga</s>-maidens too, <s>asuras</s> and <s>asura</s>-maidens too, <s>garuḍas</s> and <s>garuḍa</s>-maidens too, <s>kinnaras</s> and <s>kinnara</s>-maidens too, <s>mahoragas</s> and <s>mahoraga</s>-maidens too, <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>yakṣa</s>-maidens too, <s>piśācas</s> and <s>piśāca</s>-maidens too — all will think it worth approaching, for the purpose of seeing, saluting, attending, and hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. And they will perform honor, reverence, respect, worship, veneration, and homage to him. Monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen too will desire to see him. Kings too, princes too, royal ministers and great officers too will desire to see him. Mighty wheel-turning kings too, and wheel-turning kings endowed with the seven jewels, together with their princes, ministers, and inner-palace retinues, will desire to see him, seeking to pay honor. So sweet will that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher teach the <s>Dharma</s>, in accordance with truth, in accordance with what has been spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. And other <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, householders, townspeople, and country-folk will constantly follow that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher

body.text: satatasamitaṃ samanubaddhā bhaviṣyanti yāvadāyuṣparyavasānam | tathāgataśrāvakā api asya darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti | pratyekabuddhā apyasya darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti | buddhā apyasya bhagavanto darśanakāmā bhaviṣyanti | yasyāṃ ca diśi sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā vihariṣyati, tasyāṃ diśi tathāgatābhimukhaṃ dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati, buddhadharmāṇāṃ ca bhājanabhūto bhaviṣyati | evaṃ manojñastasya gambhīro dharmaśabdo niścariṣyati ||
body.translated_text: uninterruptedly for their entire lifespan. The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Śrāvakas</s> too will desire to see him. <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> too will desire to see him. <s>Buddhas</s>, the Blessed Ones, too will desire to see him. And in whatever direction that son of good family or daughter of good family abides, in that direction he will teach the <s>Dharma</s> facing the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and will become a vessel worthy of the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>dharmas</s>. So pleasant and deep will his sound of <s>Dharma</s> emerge.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses —

children.text: jihvendriyaṃ tasya viśiṣṭu bhoti na jātu hīnaṃ rasa svādayeta /
children.translated_text: His tongue-faculty becomes distinguished; never will he taste a bad flavor;

children.text: nikṣiptamātrāśca bhavanti divyā rasena divyena samanvitāśca // Saddhp_18.52 //
children.translated_text: the moment [flavors are] placed [upon it], they become divine, endowed with divine taste! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.52 ||

children.text: valgusvarāṃ madhura prabhāṣate girāṃ śravaṇīyamiṣṭāṃ ca manoramāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: He speaks with a pleasant, sweet voice, a speech that is agreeable, desired, and delightful;

children.text: parṣāya madhyasmi ha premaṇīyaṃ gambhīraghoṣaṃ ca sadā prabhāṣate // Saddhp_18.53 //
children.translated_text: in the midst of the assembly, he always utters a deep-toned, lovable [sound]! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.53 ||

children.text: yaścāpi dharmaṃ śṛṇute 'sya bhāṣato dṛṣṭāntakoṭīnayutairanekaiḥ /
children.translated_text: And whoever hears the <s>Dharma</s> as he speaks, with countless <s>koṭis</s> and <s>nayutas</s> of illustrations —

children.text: prāmodya tatrāpi janeti so 'graṃ pūjāṃ ca tasya kurute 'prameyām // Saddhp_18.54 //
children.translated_text: there too he generates supreme joy, and performs immeasurable worship to him! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.54 ||

children.text: devā pi nāgāsuraguhyakāśca draṣṭuṃ tamicchanti ca nityakālam /
children.translated_text: Gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>guhyakas</s> (secret ones) desire to see him at all times,

children.text: śṛṇvanti dharmaṃ ca sagauravāśca ime guṇāstasya bhavanti sarve // Saddhp_18.55 //
children.translated_text: and hear the <s>Dharma</s> reverentially — all these are his qualities! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.55 ||

children.text: ākāṅkṣamāṇaśca ima lokadhātuṃ svareṇa sarvāmabhivijñapeyā /
children.translated_text: And if he desired, he could make this entire world-system hear with his voice;

children.text: snigdhaḥ svaro 'sya madhuraśca bhoti gambhīra valguśca supremaṇīyaḥ // Saddhp_18.56 //
children.translated_text: his voice is smooth, sweet, deep, pleasant, and supremely lovable! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.56 ||

children.text: rājāna ye kṣitipati cakravartinaḥ pūjārthikāstasyupasaṃkramanti /
children.translated_text: Kings, lords of the earth, and wheel-turners approach him seeking to worship,

children.text: saputradārā kariyāṇa añjaliṃ śṛṇvanti dharmasya ca nityakālam // Saddhp_18.57 //
children.translated_text: with their sons and wives, paying homage with joined palms, and they hear the <s>Dharma</s> at all times! || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.57 ||

children.text: yakṣāṇa co bhoti sadā puraskṛto nāgāna gandharvagaṇāna caiva /
children.translated_text: He is always attended by <s>Yakṣas</s>, and by <s>Nāgas</s> and hosts of <s>Gandharvas</s>,

children.text: piśācakānāṃ ca piśācikānāṃ susatkṛto mānitu pūjitaśca // Saddhp_18.58 //
children.translated_text: and by male and female <s>Piśācas</s> — well-honored, respected, and worshipped. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.58 ||

children.text: brahmāpi tasya vaśavarti bhoti maheśvaro īśvara devaputraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> himself becomes subject to his command, as do <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>, and the sons of the gods;

children.text: śakrastathānye 'pi ca devaputrā bahudevakanyāścupasaṃkramanti // Saddhp_18.59 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> likewise, and other sons of the gods, and many divine maidens approach him. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.59 ||

children.text: buddhāśca ye lokahitānukampakāḥ saśrāvakāstasya niśāmya ghoṣam /
children.translated_text: And the <s>Buddhas</s>, compassionate for the welfare of the world, together with their <s>Śrāvakas</s>, hearing his voice,

children.text: karonti rakṣāṃ mukhadarśanāya tuṣṭāśca bhonti bruvato 'sya dharmam // Saddhp_18.60 //
children.translated_text: protect him and show him their faces, and are pleased when he teaches the <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.60 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ satatasamitābhiyukta sa bodhisattvo mahāsattva imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayamāṇo vā vācayamāno vā prakāśayamāno vā deśayamāno vā likhamāno vā aṣṭau kāyaguṇaśatāni pratilapsyati | tasya kāyaḥ śuddhaḥ pariśuddho vaiḍūryapariśuddhacchavivarṇo bhaviṣyati, priyadarśanaḥ sattvānām | sa tasminnātmabhāve pariśuddhe sarvaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuṃ drakṣyati | ye ca trisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātau sattvāścyavanti upapadyante ca, hīnāḥ praṇītāśca, suvarṇā durvarṇāḥ, sugatau durgatau, ye ca cakravālamahācakravāleṣu merusumeruṣu ca parvatarājeṣu sattvāḥ prativasanti, ye ca adhastādavīcyāmūrdhvaṃ ca yāvad bhavāgraṃ sattvāḥ prativasanti, tān sarvān sva ātmabhāve drakṣyati | ye cāpi kecidasmiṃstrisāhasramahāsāhasre lokadhātrau śrāvakā vā pratyekabuddhā vā bodhisattvā vā tathāgatā vā prativasanti, yaṃ ca te tathāgatā dharmaṃ deśayanti, ye ca sattvāstāṃstathāgatān paryupāsante, sarveṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāmātmabhāvapratilambhān sva ātmabhāve drakṣyati | tatkasya hetoḥ? yathāpīdaṃ pariśuddhatvādātmabhāvasyeti ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, constantly and diligently engaged in upholding, reciting, illuminating, teaching, or writing this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, will obtain eight hundred bodily virtues. His body will be pure, thoroughly pure, with a complexion as pure as <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl), pleasing to behold by beings. In that pure body of his, he will see the entire great trichiliocosm. The beings in the great trichiliocosm who die and are reborn — the lowly and the exalted, the beautiful and the ugly, those in fortunate and unfortunate destinies, and those dwelling on <s>Cakravāla</s> and <s>Mahācakravāla</s> mountains and on the king of mountains <s>Meru</s> and <s>Sumeru</s>, and those dwelling below in <s>Avīci</s> and above up to the summit of existence — all of them he will see in his own body. And whatever <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, or <s>Tathāgatas</s> dwell in this great trichiliocosm, and whatever <s>Dharma</s> those <s>Tathāgatas</s> teach, and whatever beings attend upon those <s>Tathāgatas</s> — the bodily forms of all those beings he will see in his own body. For what reason? Because of the purity of his body.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: pariśuddha tasyo bhavatetmabhāvo yathāpi vaiḍūryamayo viśuddhaḥ /
children.translated_text: His body becomes pure, as if made of <s>vaidūrya</s>, brilliant,

children.text: sattvāna nityaṃ priyadarśanaśca yaḥ sūtra dhāreti idaṃ udāram // Saddhp_18.61 //
children.translated_text: always pleasing to behold by beings — one who upholds this noble <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.61 ||

body.text: ādarśapṛṣṭhe yatha vimbu paśyet loko 'sya kāye ayu dṛśyate tathā /
body.translated_text: As on the surface of a mirror one sees a reflection, so the world is seen in his body;

body.text: svayaṃbhu so paśyati nānyi sattvāḥ pariśuddhi kāyasmi ima evarūpā // Saddhp_18.62 //
body.translated_text: he alone, the Self-Existent, sees — no other beings — such is the purity in this body. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.62 ||

children.text: ye lokadhātau hi ihāsti sattvā manuṣya devāsura guhyakā vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever beings exist here in this world-system — humans, gods, <s>Asuras</s>, or <s>Guhyakas</s>,

children.text: narakeṣu preteṣu tiraścayoniṣu pratibimbu saṃdṛśyati tatra kāye // Saddhp_18.63 //
children.translated_text: in the hells, among hungry ghosts, in animal wombs — their reflections appear in that body. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.63 ||

children.text: vimāna devāna bhavāgra yāvacchailaṃ pi co parvatacakravālam /
children.translated_text: The palaces of the gods, up to the summit of existence, and the mountains and the <s>Cakravāla</s> range,

children.text: himavān sumeruśca mahāṃśca meruḥ kāyasmi dṛśyantimi sarvathaiva // Saddhp_18.64 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Himavān</s>, <s>Sumeru</s>, and the great <s>Meru</s> — all these are seen entirely in his body. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.64 ||

children.text: buddhān pi so paśyati ātmabhāve saśrāvakān buddhasutāṃstathānyān /
children.translated_text: He also sees <s>Buddhas</s> in his body, together with their <s>Śrāvakas</s> and other sons of the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.text: ye bodhisattvā viharanti caikakā gaṇe ca ye dharma prakāśayanti // Saddhp_18.65 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who dwell in solitude, and those who illuminate the <s>Dharma</s> in assemblies. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.65 ||

children.text: etādṛśī kāyaviśuddhi tasya yahi dṛśyate sarviya lokadhātuḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is the purity of his body, in which the entire world-system is seen,

children.text: na ca tāva so divya na prāpuṇoti prakṛtīya kāyasyiyamīdṛśī bhavet // Saddhp_18.66 //
children.translated_text: yet he has not yet attained the divine [eye] — this is merely the natural condition of his body. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.66 ||

body.text: punaraparaṃ satatasamitābhiyukta asya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tathāgate parinirvṛte imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayato deśayataḥ saṃprakāśayato likhato vācayatastairdvādaśabhirmanaskāraguṇaśataiḥ samanvāgataṃ manaindriyaṃ pariśuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati | sa tena pariśuddhena manaindriyeṇa yadyekagāthāmapyantaśaḥ śroṣyati, tasya bahvarthamājñāsyati | sa tāvamabudhya tannidānaṃ māsamapi dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati, caturmāsamapi saṃvatsaramapi dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati | yaṃ ca dharmaṃ bhāṣiṣyati, so 'sya smṛto na sa saṃpramoṣaṃ yāsyati | ye kecillaukikā lokavyavahārā bhāṣyāṇi vā mantrā vā, sarvāṃstān dharmanayena saṃsyandayiṣyati | yāvantaśca kecitrisāhasramahāsāhasrāyāṃ lokadhātau ṣaṭsu gatiṣūpapannāḥ sattvāḥ saṃsaranti, sarveṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ cittacaritavispanditāni jñāsyati | iñjitamanyitaprapañcitāni jñāsyati praviciniṣyati | apratilabdhe ca tāvadāryajñāne evaṃrūpaṃ cāsya manaindriyaṃ pariśuddhaṃ bhaviṣyati || yāṃ yāṃ ca dharmaniruktimanuvicintya dharmaṃ deśayiṣyati, sarvaṃ tad bhūtaṃ deśayiṣyati | sarvaṃ tattathāgatabhāṣitaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvajinasūtraparyāyanirdiṣṭaṃ bhāṣati ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, for this <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, constantly and diligently engaged, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in upholding, teaching, illuminating, writing, or reciting this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — his mind-faculty will be pure, endowed with twelve hundred qualities of mental attentiveness. With that purified mind-faculty, upon hearing even a single verse, he will understand its manifold meaning. Having comprehended that, he will be able to teach the <s>Dharma</s> based on it for a month, or for four months, or even for a year. And whatever <s>Dharma</s> he teaches, he will remember it and it will not be forgotten. All worldly matters, worldly conventions, sayings, or incantations — all of these he will harmonize with the principles of the <s>Dharma</s>. And he will know the mental activities, thoughts, and impulses of all beings reborn in the six destinies throughout the great trichiliocosm. He will know their movements, thoughts, and conceptual elaborations, and will discern them. And even though he has not yet attained the noble knowledge, his mind-faculty will be pure in this manner. Whatever <s>Dharma</s>-exposition he contemplates and teaches, all of it he will teach truthfully. All of it is spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, all of it is expounded in the <s>sūtra</s>-discourses of former <s>Jinas</s>.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: manaindriyaṃ tasya viśuddha bhoti prabhāsvaraṃ śuddhamanāvilaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: His mind-faculty becomes pure, radiant, clear, and unclouded;

children.text: so tena dharmān vividhān prajānati hīnānathotkṛṣṭa tathaiva madhyamān // Saddhp_18.67 //
children.translated_text: with it he discerns various <s>dharmas</s> — the inferior, the exalted, and likewise the middling. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.67 ||

children.text: ekāmapi gātha śruṇitva dhīro artha bahuṃ jānati tasya tatra /
children.translated_text: Even hearing a single verse, the wise one understands its manifold meaning therein,

children.text: samitaṃ ca bhūtaṃ ca sadā prabhāṣate māsān pi catvāri tathāpi varṣam // Saddhp_18.68 //
children.translated_text: and always teaches what is consistent and true — for months and even for four months, and even a year. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.68 ||

children.text: ye cāpi sattvā iha lokadhātau abhyantare bāhiri ye vasanti /
children.translated_text: Whatever beings exist here in this world-system, those dwelling within and without,

children.text: devā manuṣyāsuraguhyakāśca nāgāśca ye cāpi tiraścayoniṣu // Saddhp_18.69 //
children.translated_text: gods, humans, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Guhyakas</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, and those in animal wombs — || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.69 ||

children.text: ṣaṭsu gatīṣu nivasanti sattvā vicintitaṃ teṣa bhaveta yaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: the beings dwelling in the six destinies, whatever their thoughts may be,

children.text: ekakṣaṇe sarvi vidurvijānate dhāretva sūtraṃ ima ānuśaṃsāḥ // Saddhp_18.70 //
children.translated_text: in a single instant he knows and understands them all — these are the benefits of upholding this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.70 ||

children.text: yaṃ cāpi buddhaḥ śatapuṇyalakṣaṇo dharmaṃ prakāśedida sarvaloke /
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>Dharma</s> the <s>Buddha</s> marked by a hundred merits would illuminate in all this world,

children.text: tasyāpi śabdaṃ śṛṇute viśuddhaṃ yaṃ cāpi so bhāṣati gṛhyate tat // Saddhp_18.71 //
children.translated_text: his voice he hears, pure, and whatever he teaches is grasped. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.71 ||

children.text: bahūn vicinteti ca agradharmān bahūṃśca so bhāṣati nityakālam /
children.translated_text: He contemplates many supreme <s>dharmas</s> and always teaches abundantly,

children.text: na cāsya saṃmoha kadāci bhoti dhāretva sūtraṃ imi ānuśaṃsāḥ // Saddhp_18.72 //
