children.translated_text: and never does delusion arise in him — these are the benefits of upholding this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.72 ||

children.text: saṃdhiṃ visaṃdhiṃ ca vijānate 'sau sarveṣu dharmeṣu vilakṣaṇāni /
children.translated_text: He understands the connected and the disconnected, the distinguishing features in all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: prajānate artha niruktayaśca yathā ca taṃ jānati bhāṣate tathā // Saddhp_18.73 //
children.translated_text: he discerns meanings and etymologies, and as he knows, so he teaches. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.73 ||

children.text: yaṃ bhāṣitaṃ bhotiha dīrgharātraṃ pūrvehi lokācariyehi sūtram /
children.translated_text: The <s>sūtra</s> that was taught here through the long night by the former teachers of the world —

children.text: taṃ dharma so bhāṣati nityakālaṃ asaṃtrasanto pariṣāya madhye // Saddhp_18.74 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Dharma</s> he teaches constantly, without trembling in the midst of the assembly. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.74 ||

children.text: manaindriyaṃ īdṛśamasya bhoti dhāretva sūtraṃ imu vācayitvā /
children.translated_text: Such is his mind-faculty, one who upholds and recites this <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: na ca tāva asaṅgaṃ labhate ha jñānaṃ pūrvaṃgamaṃ tasya imaṃ tu bhoti // Saddhp_18.75 //
children.translated_text: yet he has not yet attained unobstructed knowledge — this [purification] is merely a forerunner of it. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.75 ||

children.text: ācāryabhūmau hi sthitaśca bhoti sarveṣa sattvāna katheya dharmam /
children.translated_text: He stands on the stage of a teacher, able to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings,

children.text: niruktikoṭīkuśalaśca bhoti imu dhārayanto sugatasya sutram // Saddhp_18.76 //
children.translated_text: skilled in <s>koṭis</s> of etymologies — one who upholds this <s>sūtra</s> of the <s>Sugata</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 18.76 ||

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye dharmabhāṇakānuśaṃsāparivarto nāmāṣṭādaśamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on the Benefits of the <s>Dharma</s>-Preacher.

body.text: Saddhp_19: sadāparibhūtaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 19: The Chapter on <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> (Never Disparaging).

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān mahāsthāmaprāptaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamāmantrayate sma - anenāpi tāvanmahāsthāmaprāpta paryāyeṇa evaṃ veditavyam - yathā ya imamevaṃrūpaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ pratikṣepsyanti, evaṃrūpāṃśca sūtrāntadhārakāṃśca bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā ākrośiṣyanti, paribhāṣiṣyanti, asatyayā paruṣayā vācā samudācariṣyanti, teṣāmevamaniṣṭo vipāko bhaviṣyati, yo na śakyaṃ vācā parikīrtayitum | ye ca imamaevaṃrūpaṃ sūtrāntaṃ dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti deśayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti, parebhyaśca vistareṇa saṃprakāśayiṣyanti, teṣāmevamiṣṭo vipāko bhaviṣyati yādṛśo mayā pūrvaṃ parikīrtitaḥ | evaṃrūpāṃ ca cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥ - pariśuddhimadhigamiṣyanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>: 'By this very method, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, it should be understood as follows: those who will reject this kind of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, and who will revile and abuse such holders of the <s>sūtra</s> — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — who will address them with false and harsh words, for them the result will be so undesirable that it cannot be fully described in words. And those who will uphold, recite, teach, master, and extensively illuminate to others this kind of <s>sūtra</s> — for them the result will be as desirable as I have previously described: they will attain such purity of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.'

body.text:
bhūtapūrvaṃ mahāsthāmaprāpta atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairvipulairaprameyairacintyaistebhyaḥ pareṇa paratareṇa yadāsīt - tena kālena samayena bhīṣmagarjitasvararājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān vinirbhoge kalpe mahāsaṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau | sa khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta bhagavān bhīṣmagarjitasvararājastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastasyāṃ mahāsaṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau sadevamānuṣāsurasya lokasya purato dharmaṃ deśayati sma | yadidaṃ śrāvakāṇāṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprayuktaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsasamatikramāya nirvāṇaparyavasānaṃ pratītyasamutpādapravṛttim | bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktānāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimārabhya tathāgatajñānadarśanaparyavasānaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati sma | tasya khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta bhagavato bhīṣmagarjitasvararājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya catvāriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt | parinirvṛtasya jambudvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamāni kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi saddharmaḥ sthito 'bhūt | caturdvīpaparamāṇurajaḥsamāni kalpakoṭīnayutasahasrāṇi saddharmapratirūpakaḥ sthito 'bhūt | tasyāṃ khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta mahāsaṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau bhagavato bhīṣmagarjitasvararājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya saddharmapratirūpake ca antarhite aparo 'pi bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja eva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | anayā mahāsthāmaprāpta paraṃparayā tasyāṃ mahāsaṃbhavāyāṃ lokadhātau bhīṣmagarjitasvararājanāmnāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ viṃśatikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyabhūvan | tatra mahāsthāmaprāpta yo 'sau tathāgataḥ sarvapūrvako 'bhūd bhīṣmagarjitasvararājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato
lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān, tasya bhagavataḥ parinirvṛtasya saddharme 'ntarhite saddharmapratirūpake ca antardhīyamāne tasmin śāsane 'dhimānikabhikṣvadhyākrānte
body.translated_text: In the past, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, in a former age, beyond incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, more incalculable still, vast, immeasurable, inconceivable, and far beyond even that — at that time, in that era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s> (King of Fearsome-Thundering Voice), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in a <s>kalpa</s> named <s>Vinirbhoga</s> (Distinction), in a world-system named <s>Mahāsaṃbhavā</s> (Great Arising). That Blessed One <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, in that <s>Mahāsaṃbhavā</s> world-system, taught the <s>Dharma</s> before the world with its gods, humans, and <s>Asuras</s>. For the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the four noble truths, for crossing beyond birth, old age, sickness, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, grief, and despair, culminating in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, [based on] the arising of dependent origination. For the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, he taught the <s>Dharma</s> connected with the six <s>pāramitās</s>, beginning with supreme perfect awakening, culminating in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge and vision. The lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was forty <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-numbered <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s>. After his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, the true <s>Dharma</s> endured for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. The semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> endured for <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of thousands of <s>kalpas</s> equal in number to the atoms of the four continents. In that <s>Mahāsaṃbhavā</s> world-system, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the Blessed One <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and after the disappearance of the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, another <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s> appeared in the world. In this succession, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones bearing the name <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s> arose in that <s>Mahāsaṃbhavā</s> world-system. Of those, <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, the very first <s>Tathāgata</s> was named <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. After that Blessed One's <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, after the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and while the semblance of the true <s>Dharma</s> was disappearing, in that dispensation dominated by presumptuous monks,

body.text: sadāparibhūto nāma bodhisattvo bhikṣurabhūt | kena kāraṇena mahāsthāmaprāpta sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sadāparibhūta ityucyate? sa khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta bodhisattvo mahāsattvo yaṃ yameva paśyati bhikṣuṃ vā bhikṣūṇīṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikāṃ vā, taṃ tamupasaṃkramya eva vadati - nāhamāyuṣmanto yuṣmākaṃ paribhavāmi | aparibhūtā yūyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarve hi bhavanto bodhisattvacaryāṃ carantu | bhaviṣyatha yūyaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā iti | anena mahāsthāmaprāpta paryāyeṇa sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhikṣubhūto noddeśaṃ karoti, na svādhyāya karoti, anyatra yaṃ yameva paśyati dūragatamapi, sarvaṃ tamupaṃsakramya evaṃ saṃśrāvayati bhikṣuṃ vā bhikṣuṇīṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikāṃ vā, taṃ tamupasaṃkramyaivaṃ vadati - nāhaṃ bhaginyo yuṣmākaṃ paribhavāmi | aparibhūtā yūyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvā yūyaṃ bodhisattvacaryāṃ caradhvam | bhaviṣyatha yūyaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | yaṃ yameva mahāsthāmaprāpta sa bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasmin samaye bhikṣuṃ vā bhikṣuṇīṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikāṃ vā evaṃ saṃśrāvayati, sarve 'sya yadbhūyastvena krudhyanti, vyāpādanti aprasādamutpādayanti ākrośanti paribhāṣante - kuto 'yamapṛṣṭo bhikṣuraparibhavacittamityasmākamupadarśayati? paribhūtamātmānaṃ karoti yadasmākaṃ vyākarotyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau asantamanākāṅkṣitaṃ ca | atha khalu mahāsthāmaprāpta tasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya bahūni varṣāṇi tathā ākruśyataḥ paribhāṣyamāṇasya gacchanti | na ca kasyacit krudhyati, na vyāpādacittamutpādayati | ye cāsya evaṃ saṃśrāvayato loṣṭaṃ vā daṇḍaṃ vā kṣipanti, sa teṣāṃ dūrata eva uccaiḥsvaraṃ kṛtvā saṃśrāvayati sma - nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ paribhavāmīti | tasya tābhirabhimānikabhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikābhiḥ satatasamitaṃ saṃśrāvyamāṇābhiḥ sadāparibhūta iti nāma kṛtamabhūt ||
body.translated_text: there was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> monk named <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> (Never Disparaged). For what reason, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, was that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> called <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>? Indeed, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, whoever he saw — whether a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman — would approach each one and say: 'I do not disparage you, O venerable ones! You are not to be disparaged! For what reason? Because all of you are practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct. You will become <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones!' By this method, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, being a monk, did not give expositions, did not recite — but rather, whoever he saw, even one gone far away, he would approach each one and proclaim thus — whether a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman, he would approach each one and say: 'I do not disparage you, sisters! You are not to be disparaged! For what reason? Because all of you are practicing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct. You will become <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones!' Whenever, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>, at that time, proclaimed thus to a monk, or a nun, or a layman, or a laywoman, all of them for the most part became angry, hostile, and displeased, and would revile and abuse him: 'Whence has this unasked monk come, displaying [his notion of] "non-disparagement" to us? He makes a fool of himself when he gives us a prediction of supreme perfect awakening — something unreal and undesired!' But, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, though many years passed while that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> was thus reviled and abused, he never became angry, nor did he generate a hostile thought. And those who, when he thus proclaimed, would hurl clods or sticks at him — he would stand at a distance from them, and raising his voice aloud, would proclaim: 'I do not disparage you!' And those arrogant monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, who were constantly addressed thus, gave him the name <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> (Never Disparaged).

body.text: tena khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta sadāparibhūtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena kālakriyāyāṃ pratyupasthitāyāṃ maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ śruto 'bhūt | tena ca bhagavatā bhīṣmagarjitasvararājena tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo viṃśatibhirgāthāviṃśatikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairbhāṣito 'bhūt | sa ca sadāparibhūto bodhisattvo mahāsattvo maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite antarīkṣanirghoṣādimaṃ dharmaparyāyamaśrauṣīt | yena kenacid bhāṣitamantarīkṣānnirghoṣaṃ śrutvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyamudgṛhītavān, imāṃ caivaṃrūpāṃ cakṣurviśuddhiṃ śrotraviśuddhiṃ ghrāṇaviśuddhiṃ jihvāviśuddhiṃ kāyaviśuddhiṃ manoviśuddhiṃ ca pratilabdhavān | sahapratilabdhābhirviśuddhibhiḥ punaranyāni viṃśativarṣakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ātmano jīvitasaṃskāramadhiṣṭhāya imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśitavān | ye ca te 'bhimānikāḥ sattvā bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāḥ, ye pūrvaṃ nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ paribhavāmīti saṃśrāvitāḥ, yairasyedaṃ sadāparibhūta iti nāma kṛtamabhūt, tasyodārarddhibalasthāmaṃ pratijñāpratibhānabalasthāmaṃ prajñābalasthāmaṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, when the time of death approached for that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, at the moment when death was near, he heard this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. That Blessed One <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, had taught this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of twenty-line verses. And that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, at the moment when death was near, heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse as a sound from the sky. Having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — this sound issued from the sky by someone — he retained it and obtained purification of the eye, purification of the ear, purification of the nose, purification of the tongue, purification of the body, and purification of the mind. Having obtained those purifications, he further sustained his life-forces for twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of years, and proclaimed this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. And all those arrogant beings — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen — who had previously been told 'I do not disparage you,' and who had given him the name <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, upon seeing his great power of supernatural ability, his power of eloquence and confident speech, his power of wisdom,

body.text: ca dṛṣṭvā sarve 'nusahāyībhūtā abhūvan dharmaśravaṇāya | sarve tena anyāni ca bahūni prāṇikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau samādāpitānyabhūvan ||
body.translated_text: all became his followers for the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>. All of them, and many other <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of beings, were inspired by him toward supreme perfect awakening.

body.text: sa khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta bodhisattvo mahāsattvastataścyavitvā candrasvararājasahanāmnāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ viṃśatikoṭīśatānyārāgitavān, sarveṣu ca imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayāmāsa | so 'nupūrveṇa tenaiva pūrvakeṇa kuśalamūlena punarapyanupūrveṇa dundubhisvararājasahanāmnāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ viṃśatimeva tathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyārāgitavān | sarveṣu ca imameva saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamārāgitavān, saṃprakāśitavāṃścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadām | so 'nenaiva pūrvakeṇa kuśalamūlena punarapyapūrveṇa meghasvararājasahanāmnāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ viṃśatimeva tathāgatakoṭīśatasahasrāṇyārāgitavān, sarveṣu ca imameva saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamāragitavān, saṃprakāśitavāṃścatasṛṇāṃ parṣadām | sarveṣu ca evaṃrūpayā cakṣuḥpariśuddhayā samanvāgato 'bhūt, śrotrapariśuddhyā ghrāṇapariśuddhayā jihvāpariśuddhayā kāyapariśuddhayā manaḥpariśuddhayā samanvāgato 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, having departed from that [life], pleased twenty hundred <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones bearing the same name <s>Candrasvararāja</s> (Moon-Voice King), and under all of them he proclaimed this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. Then, gradually, by those same former roots of merit, he again gradually pleased twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones bearing the same name <s>Dundubhisvararāja</s> (Drum-Voice King). Under all of them he pleased [them] with this very <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse and proclaimed it to the four assemblies. Then, by those same former roots of merit, he again gradually pleased twenty <s>koṭis</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones bearing the same name <s>Meghasvararāja</s> (Cloud-Voice King), under all of them he pleased [them] with this very <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse and proclaimed it to the four assemblies. Under all of them, he was endowed with such purification of the eye, purification of the ear, purification of the nose, purification of the tongue, purification of the body, and purification of the mind.

body.text: sa khalu punarmahāsthāmaprāpta sadāparibhūto bodhisattvo mahāsattva iyatāṃ tathāgata koṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kṛtvā anyeṣāṃ ca bahūnāṃ buddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ satkāraṃ gurukāraṃ mānanāṃ pūjanāmarcanāmapacāyanāṃ kṛtvā, sarveṣu ca teṣu imameva saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamārāgitavān, ārāgayitvā sa tenaiva pūrvakeṇa kuśalamūlena paripakvena anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | syātkhalu punaste mahāsthāmaprāpta evaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena sadāparibhūto nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhūt, yastasya bhagavato bhīṣmagarjitasvararājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya śāsane catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ sadāparibhūtaḥ saṃmato 'bhūt, yena te tāvantastathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā ārāgitā abhūvan? na khalu punaste mahāsthāmaprāpta evaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? ahameva sa mahāsthāmaprāpta tena kālena tena samayena sadāparibhūto nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'bhūvam | yadā mayā mahāsthāmaprāpta pūrvamayaṃ dharmaparyāyo nodgṛhīto 'bhaviṣyat, na dhāritaḥ, nāhamevaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddho 'bhaviṣyam | yataścāhaṃ mahāsthāmaprāpta paurvikāṇāṃ tathāgatānāmarhatāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmantikādimaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhāritavān vācitavān deśitavān, tato 'hamevaṃ kṣipramanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhaḥ | yānyapi tāni mahāsthāmaprāpta tena sadāparibhūtena bodhisattvena mahāsattvena bhikṣuśatāni bhikṣuṇīśatāni ca upāsakaśatāni upāsikāśatāni ca tasya bhagavataḥ śāsane imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃśrāvitānyabhūvan - nāhaṃ yuṣmākaṃ paribhavāmīti | sarve bhavanto bodhisattvacaryāṃ carantu | bhaviṣyatha yūyaṃ tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | yaistasya bodhisattvasyāntike vyāpādacittamutpāditamabhūt,
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, having performed honor, respect, reverence, worship, veneration, and homage to so many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and having performed similar honors to many other hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>, and having pleased [them] under all of them with this very <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — having pleased [them], by those very former roots of merit, now fully ripened, he attained supreme perfect awakening. Would you perhaps, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, have doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity [thinking]: 'The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> at that time, in that era — who was regarded as <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> by the four assemblies in the teaching of that Blessed One <s>Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and who pleased so many <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — was someone other [than me]?' Do not see it thus, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>! For what reason? I myself, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, was at that time, in that era, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>. If I, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, had not formerly taken up, retained, and held this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, I would not have so quickly attained supreme perfect awakening. Because, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, I retained, recited, and taught this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in the presence of those former <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones — therefore I so quickly attained supreme perfect awakening. And those hundreds of monks, hundreds of nuns, hundreds of laymen, and hundreds of laywomen, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, who in that Blessed One's teaching were told by that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sadāparibhūta</s>, 'I do not disparage you — all of you, practice the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct! You will become <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones!' — those who had generated hostile thoughts toward that <s>Bodhisattva</s>,

body.text:
tairviśatikalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi na jātu tathāgato dṛṣṭo 'bhūt, nāpi dharmaśabdo na saṃghaśabdaḥ śruto 'bhūt | daśa ca kalpasahasrāṇyavīcau mahānarake dāruṇāṃ vedanāṃ vedayāmāsuḥ | te ca sarve tasmāt karmāvaraṇāt parimuktāḥ
| tenaiva bodhisattvena mahāsattvena paripācitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | syātkhalu punaste mahāsthāmaprāpta kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - katame tena kālena tena samayena te sattvā abhūvan ye te taṃ bodhisattvaṃ ptahāsattvamullāpitavanta uccagghitavantaḥ? asyāmeva mahāsthāmaprāpta parṣadi bhadrapālapramukhāṇi pañca bodhisattvaśatāni siṃhacandrāpramukhāni pañcabhikṣuṇīśatāni sugatacetanāpramukhāni pañcopāsikāśatāni sarvāṇyavaivartikāni kṛtāni anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | evamiyaṃ mahāsthāmaprāpta mahārthasya dharmaparyāyasya dhāraṇā vācanā deśanā bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāmanuttarāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodherāhārikā saṃvartate | tasmāttarhi mahāsthāmaprāpta ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo bodhisattvairmahāsattvaistathāgate parinirvṛte abhīkṣṇaṃ dhārayitavyo vācayitavyo deśayitavyaḥ saṃprakāśayitavya iti ||
body.translated_text: for twenty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s> they never saw a <s>Tathāgata</s>, nor heard the word '<s>Dharma</s>,' nor the word '<s>Saṅgha</s>.' For ten thousand <s>kalpas</s> they experienced dreadful sensations in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell. And all of them, freed from that <s>karmic</s> obstruction, were ripened by that very <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> in supreme perfect awakening. Would you perhaps, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, have doubt, uncertainty, or perplexity [thinking]: 'Who were those beings at that time, in that era, who mocked and ridiculed that <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>?' In this very assembly, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, [they are] the five hundred <s>Bodhisattvas</s> headed by <s>Bhadrapāla</s>, the five hundred nuns headed by <s>Siṃhacandrā</s>, and the five hundred laywomen headed by <s>Sugatacetanā</s> — all of them have been made irreversible in supreme perfect awakening. Thus, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, the retaining, reciting, and teaching of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of great import brings about supreme perfect awakening for <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>. Therefore, O <s>Mahāsthāmaprāpta</s>, this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse should be constantly retained, recited, taught, and proclaimed by <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: atītamadhvānamanusmarāmi bhīṣmasvaro rāja jino yadāsi /
children.translated_text: 'I recall the past age, when <s>Bhīṣmasvararāja</s> (Fearsome-Voice King), the <s>Jina</s>, existed —

children.text: mahānubhāvo naradevapūjitaḥ praṇāyako naramaruyakṣarakṣasām // Saddhp_19.1 //
children.translated_text: of great might, worshipped by gods and humans, the guide of humans, <s>Māras</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s>. || Saddhp 19.1 ||

children.text: tasya jinasya parinirvṛtasya saddharma saṃkṣobha vrajanti paścime /
children.translated_text: After the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of that <s>Jina</s>, when the true <s>Dharma</s> was in turmoil, in the final [age],

children.text: bhikṣū abhūṣī tada bodhisattvo nāmena so sadaparibhūta ucyate // Saddhp_19.2 //
children.translated_text: there was a monk who was a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — by name he was called <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> (Never Disparaged). || Saddhp 19.2 ||

children.text: upasaṃkramitvā tada bhikṣu anyān upalambhadṛṣṭīna tathaiva bhikṣuṇī /
children.translated_text: Having approached other monks and likewise nuns, who held the view of reification,

children.text: paribhāva mahyaṃ na kadācidasti yūyaṃ hi caryāṃ carathāgrabodhaye // Saddhp_19.3 //
children.translated_text: [he said:] "Disparagement of you is never mine — for you are all practicing the conduct for supreme awakening!" || Saddhp 19.3 ||

children.text: evaṃ ca saṃśrāvayi nityakālaṃ ākrośa paribhāṣa sahantu teṣām /
children.translated_text: Thus he proclaimed constantly, enduring their insults and abuse;

children.text: kālakriyāyāṃ samupasthitāyāṃ śrutaṃ idaṃ sūtramabhūṣi tena // Saddhp_19.4 //
children.translated_text: when the time of death approached, this <s>sūtra</s> was heard by him. || Saddhp 19.4 ||

children.text: akṛtva kālaṃ tada paṇḍitena adhiṣṭhihitvā ca sudīrghamāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Not dying at that time, the wise one, having sustained a very long life,

children.text: prakāśitaṃ sūtramidaṃ tadāsīt tahi śāsane tasya vināyakasya // Saddhp_19.5 //
children.translated_text: proclaimed this <s>sūtra</s> then, in the teaching of that Guide. || Saddhp 19.5 ||

children.text: te cāpi sarve bahu opalambhikā bodhīya tena paripācitāsīt /
children.translated_text: All those of reifying views were ripened by him toward awakening;

children.text: tataścyavitvāna sa bodhisattvo ārāgayī buddhasahasrakoṭyaḥ // Saddhp_19.6 //
children.translated_text: then, departing from that [life], that <s>Bodhisattva</s> pleased <s>koṭis</s> of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. || Saddhp 19.6 ||

children.text: anupūrva puṇyena kṛtena tena prakāśayitvā imu sūtra nityam /
children.translated_text: Gradually, by that merit formerly acquired, constantly illuminating this <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text: bodhiṃ sa saṃprāpta jinasya putro ahameva so śākyamunistadāsīt // Saddhp_19.7 //
children.translated_text: he attained the awakening of a son of the <s>Jina</s> — I myself was that <s>Śākyamuni</s> at that time! || Saddhp 19.7 ||

children.text: ye cāpi bhikṣū tada opalambhikā yā bhikṣuṇī ye ca upāsakā vā /
children.translated_text: And those monks at that time who held reifying views, and those nuns, and those laymen,

children.text: upāsikāstatra ca yā tadāsīd ye bodhi saṃśrāvita paṇḍitena // Saddhp_19.8 //
children.translated_text: and those laywomen who were there at that time — who were told of awakening by the wise one — || Saddhp 19.8 ||

children.text: te cāpi dṛṣṭvā bahubuddhakoṭya ime ca te pañcaśatā anūnakāḥ /
children.translated_text: they too, having seen many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> — these are those very five hundred, no fewer!

children.text: tathaiva bhikṣūṇa ca bhikṣuṇī ca upāsikāścāpi mi mahya saṃmukham // Saddhp_19.9 //
children.translated_text: and likewise the monks and nuns and the laywomen too, [all] before me, face to face. || <s>Saddhp</s> 19.9 ||

children.text: sarve mayā śrāvita agradharmā te caiva sarve paripācitā me /
children.translated_text: All of them were caused to hear the supreme <s>Dharma</s> by me, and all of them were ripened by me;

children.text: mayi nirvṛte cāpimi sarvi dhīrā imu dhārayiṣyanti ha sūtramagram // Saddhp_19.10 //
children.translated_text: and after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, all these steadfast ones will uphold this supreme <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 19.10 ||

children.text: kalpāna koṭyo bahubhīracintyairna kadācidetādṛśa dharma śrūyate /
children.translated_text: Through many inconceivable thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, never is such a <s>Dharma</s> heard;

children.text: buddhāna koṭīśata caiva bhonti na ca te pimaṃ sūtra prakāśayanti // Saddhp_19.11 //
children.translated_text: and even though hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s> may arise, they do not illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 19.11 ||

children.text: tasmācchrūṇitvā idamevarūpaṃ parikīrtitaṃ dharmu svayaṃ svayaṃbhūvā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, having heard this <s>Dharma</s> of such a kind, proclaimed by the Self-Existent One himself,

children.text: ārāgayitvā ca punaḥ punaścimaṃ prakāśayet sūtra mayīha nirvṛte // Saddhp_19.12 //
children.translated_text: and having pleased [him] again and again, one should illuminate this <s>sūtra</s> after my <s>parinirvāṇa</s> here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 19.12 ||

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye sadāparibhūtaparivarto nāmaikonaviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Chapter on [the Bodhisattva] <s>Sadāparibhūta</s> (Never Despising),' in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text: Saddhp_20: tathāgataddharyabhisaṃskāraparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 20: The Chapter on the Supernatural Display of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (<s>Tathāgataddharyabhisaṃskāraparivarta</s>).

body.text: atha khalu yāni tāni sāhasralokadhātuparamāṇurajaḥsamāni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi pṛthivīvivarebhyo niṣkrāntāni, tāni sarvāṇi bhagavato 'bhimukhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya bhagavantametadūcuḥ - vayaṃ bhagavan imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ tathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu yāni yāni bhagavato buddhakṣetrāṇi, yatra yatra bhagavān parinirvṛto bhaviṣyati, tatra tatra saṃprakāśayiṣyāmaḥ | arthino vayaṃ bhagavan anenaikavamudāreṇa dharmaparyāyeṇa dhāraṇāya vācanāya deśanāya saṃprakāśanāya vā likhanāya ||
body.translated_text: Then those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, equal in number to the atoms of dust of a trichiliocosm, who had emerged from the crevices of the earth — all of them, with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'We, O Blessed One, will illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, in all the <s>buddhakṣetras</s> of the Blessed One — in whatever <s>buddhakṣetras</s> the Blessed One will have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, there we will illuminate it. We desire, O Blessed One, this one supremely noble <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — to uphold it, recite it, teach it, illuminate it, and write it.'

body.text: atha khalu mañjuśrīpramukhāni bahūni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi yāni asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau vāstavyāni, bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikā devanāgayakṣāgandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ, bahavaśca gaṅgānadīvālikopamā bodhisattvā mahāsattvā bhagavantametadūcuḥ - vayamapi bhagavan imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ saṃprakāśayiṣyāmastathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya addaṣṭenātmabhāvena, bhagavan antarīkṣe sthitā ghoṣaṃ saṃśrāvayiṣyāmaḥ, anavaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ ca sattvānāṃ kuśalamūlānyavaropayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> headed by <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, who were residents of this <s>Sahā</s> world-system — together with monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans, and many <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — said this to the Blessed One: 'We too, O Blessed One, will illuminate this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. With unseen bodily forms, O Blessed One, standing in the sky, we will send forth a sound, and we will plant wholesome roots in beings who have not yet planted wholesome roots.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāṃ teṣāṃ paurvikāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ gaṇināṃ mahāgaṇināṃ gaṇācāryāṇāmekaṃ pramukhaṃ viśiṣṭacāritraṃ nāma bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ mahāgaṇinaṃ gaṇācāryamāmantrayāmāsa - sādhu sādhu viśiṣṭacāritra | evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ karaṇīyamasya dharmaparyāyasyārthe | yūyaṃ tathāgatena paripācitāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, addressed the foremost <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> among those earlier <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, the assembly leaders, the great assembly leaders, the great teachers of assemblies — the one named <s>Viśiṣṭacāritra</s> (Distinguished Conduct), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s>, great assembly leader and teacher: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Viśiṣṭacāritra</s>! Thus should you act for the sake of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. You have been ripened by the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgataḥ sa ca bhagavān prabhūtaratnastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ stūpamadhye | siṃhāsanopaviṣṭau dvāvapi smitaṃ prāduṣkṛrutaḥ, mukhavivarāntarābhyāṃ ca jihvendriyaṃ nirṇāmayataḥ | tābhyāṃ ca jihvendriyābhyāṃ yāvad brahmalokamanuprāpnutaḥ | tābhyāṃ ca jihvendriyābhyāṃ bahūni raśmikoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi niścaranti sma | tāsu ca raśmiṣvekaikasyā raśmerbahūni bodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi niśceruḥ | suvarṇavarṇāḥ kāyairdvātriṃśadbhirmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatāḥ padmagarbhe siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇāḥ | te ca bodhisattvā digvidikṣu lokadhātuśatasahasreṣu visṛtāḥ, sarvāsu digvidikṣvantarīkṣe sthitā dharmaṃ deśayāmāsuḥ | yathaiva bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho jihvendriyeṇa ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ karoti prabhūtaratnaśca tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ tathaiva te sarve tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ, ye te 'nyalokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrebhyo 'bhyāgatā ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu pṛthak pṛthak siṃhāsanopaviṣṭā jihvendriyeṇa ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ kurvanti ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s> and the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, [seated] within the <s>stūpa</s> — both seated upon lion-thrones — displayed a smile, and from between their open mouths they extended their tongue-faculties. With those tongue-faculties they reached up to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>. And from those tongue-faculties issued forth many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of rays. And upon each of those rays appeared many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> — golden-bodied, endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, seated upon lion-thrones within lotus-receptacles. Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> spread out in all the directions and intermediate directions, in hundreds of thousands of world-systems, and standing in mid-air in all directions and intermediate directions, they taught the <s>Dharma</s>. Just as the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, performed a supernatural wonder with his tongue-faculty, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, [likewise], so too all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, who had come from other <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, seated separately upon lion-thrones at the feet of jeweled trees — they too performed supernatural wonders with their tongue-faculties.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ te ca sarve tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ tamṛddhayabhisaṃskāraṃ paripūrṇaṃ varśaśatasahasraṃ kṛtavantaḥ | atha khalu varṣaśatasahasrasyātyayena te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāstāni jihvendriyāṇi punarevopasaṃhṛtya ekasminneva kṣaṇalavamuhūrte samakālaṃ sarvairmahāsiṃhotkāsanaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ, ekaścācchaṭāsaṃghātaśabdaḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, performed that supernatural display for a full hundred thousand years. Then, at the end of those hundred thousand years, those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, withdrew those tongue-faculties, and in a single instant, moment, and hour, simultaneously, all of them produced the sound of a great lion's roar, and a single snapping of the fingers

body.text: kṛtaḥ | tena ca mahotkāsanaśabdena mahācchaṭāsaṃghātaśabdena yāvanti daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi, tāni sarvāṇyākampitānyabhūvan, prakampitāni saṃprakampitāni calitāni pracalitāni saṃpracalitāni vedhitāni pravedhitāni saṃpravedhitāni | teṣu ca sarveṣu buddhakṣetreṣu yāvantaḥ sarvasattvā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāḥ, te 'pi sarve buddhānubhāvena tatrasthā evamimāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātuṃ paśyanti sma | tāni ca sarvatathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu pṛthak pṛthak siṃhāsanopaviṣṭāni bhagavantaṃ ca śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ parinirvṛtaṃ tasya mahāratnastūpasya madhye siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaṃ bhagavatā śākyamuninā tathāgatena sārdhaṃ niṣaṇṇāṃ tāśca tisraḥ parṣadaḥ paśyanti sma | dṛṣṭvā ca āścaryaprāptā adbhutaprāptā audbilyaprāptā abhūvan | evaṃ ca antarīkṣād ghoṣamaśrauṣuḥ - eṣa mārṣā aprameyāṇyasaṃkhyeyāni lokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇyatikramya sahā nāma lokadhātuḥ | tasyāṃ śākyamunirnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | sa etarhi saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ sūtrāntaṃ mahāvaipulyaṃ bodhisattvāvavādaṃ sarvabuddhaparigrahaṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ saṃprakāśayati | taṃ yūyamadhyāśayena anumodadhvam, taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ taṃ ca bhagavantaṃ prabhūtaratnaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ namaskurudhvam ||
body.translated_text: was produced. By the sound of that great lion's roar and the sound of the snapping of the fingers, all the <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>buddhakṣetras</s> in the ten directions trembled — trembled, shook and greatly shook, quaked and greatly quaked, vibrated, strongly vibrated, and violently vibrated. And in all those <s>buddhakṣetras</s>, whatever beings there were — gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — all of them, through the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, remaining right where they were, beheld this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. And they saw all those <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s> seated separately upon lion-thrones at the feet of jeweled trees, and the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who had entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, seated upon a lion-throne within that great jeweled <s>stūpa</s>, sitting together with the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, and those three assemblies. Seeing this, they were filled with wonder, amazement, and exaltation. And they heard a voice from the sky thus: 'Beyond immeasurable, incalculable <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems, O noble ones, there is a world-system called <s>Sahā</s>. In it there is a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>. He is now illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the great extensive teaching, an instruction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, upheld by all <s>Buddhas</s>, for the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s>. Rejoice in it with your innermost intention, and pay homage to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and to the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One!'

body.text: atha khalu te sarvasattvā imamevaṃrūpamantarīkṣānnirghoṣaṃ śrutvā tatrasthā eva namo bhagavate śākyamunaye tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāyeti vācaṃ bhāṣante sma añjaliṃ pragṛhya | vividhāśca puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantyo yeneyaṃ sahā lokadhātustena kṣipanti sma, nānavidhāni cābharaṇāni pindhāṇi hārārdhahāramaṇiratnānyapi kṣipanti sma, bhagavataḥ śākyamuneḥ prabhūtaratnasya ca tathāgatasya pūjākarmaṇe, asya ca saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya | tāśca puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantyastāni ca hārārdhahāramaṇiratnāni kṣiptāni imāṃ sahāṃ lokadhātumāgacchanti sma | taiśca puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantīrāśibhirhārārdhahārairmaṇiratnaiśca asyāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau sārdhaṃ tairanyarlokadhātukoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairekībhūtairye teṣu tathāgatāḥ saṃniṣaṇṇāḥ, teṣu sarveṣu vaihāyase 'ntarīkṣe samantānmahāpuṣpavitānaṃ parisaṃsthitamabhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then all those beings, having heard that voice of such a kind from the sky, remaining right where they were, said the words: 'Homage to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One!' — with palms joined. And they cast various flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, and victory-standards toward this <s>Sahā</s> world-system; and they also cast various ornaments, necklaces, half-necklaces, jewels, and gems — for the worship of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> and the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, and of this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. Those flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, victory-standards, and those half-necklaces, jewels, and gems, having been cast, came to this <s>Sahā</s> world-system. And those heaps of flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, victory-standards, and the half-necklaces, jewels, and gems — in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, together with those other <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of world-systems merged into one, wherever those <s>Tathāgatas</s> were seated — in all of them, in the sky above, a great canopy of flowers formed all around.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstān viśiṣṭacāritrapramukhān bodhisattvān mahāsattvānāmantrayāmāsa - acintyaprabhāvāḥ kulaputrāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ | bahūnyapyahaṃ kulaputrāḥ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi asya dharmaparyāyasya parīndanārthaṃ nānādharmapramukhairbahūnānuśaṃsān bhāṣeyam | na cāhaṃ guṇānāṃ pāraṃ gaccheyamasya dharmaparyāyasya bhāṣamāṇaḥ | saṃkṣepeṇa kulaputrāḥ sarvabuddhavṛṣabhitā sarvabuddharahasyaṃ sarvabuddhagambhīrasthānaṃ mayā asmin dharmaparyāye deśitam | tasmāttarhi kulaputrā yuṣmābhistathāgatasya parinirvṛtasya satkṛtya ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo dhārayitavyo deśayitavyo likhitavyo vācayitavyaḥ prakāśayitavyo bhāvayitavyaḥ pūjayitavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> <s>Mahāsattvas</s> headed by <s>Viśiṣṭacāritra</s>: 'Inconceivable, O sons of good family, is the power of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. Even if I, O sons of good family, were to speak for many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>kalpas</s>, by way of various <s>Dharma</s>-teachings, of the many merits of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> for the purpose of entrusting it, I could not reach the limit of the merits of this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> while speaking of it. In brief, O sons of good family, all the bull-like eminence of the <s>Buddhas</s>, all the secret [treasure] of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the deep ground of the <s>Buddhas</s> — all of this has been taught by me in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Therefore, O sons of good family, after the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> should be respectfully upheld, taught, written, recited, illuminated, cultivated, and worshipped by you.'

body.text: yasmiṃśca kulaputrāḥ pṛthivīpradeśe ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo vācyeta vā prakāśyeta vā deśyeta vā likhyeta vā cintyeta vā bhāṣyeta vā svādhyāyeta vā pustakagato vā tiṣṭhat ārāme vā vihāre vā gṛhe vā vane vā nagare vā vṛkṣamūle vā prāsāde vā layane vā guhāyāṃ vā, tasmin pṛthivīpradeśe tathāgatamudiśya caityaṃ kartavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? sarvatathāgatānāṃ hi sa pṛthivīpradeśo bodhimaṇḍo veditavyaḥ | tasmiṃśca pṛthivīpradeśe sarvatathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhā iti veditavyam | tasmiṃśca pṛthivīpradeśe sarvatathāgatairdharmacakraṃ pravartitam, tasmiṃścapṛthivīpradeśe sarvatathāgatāḥ parinirvṛtā iti veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: 'And in whatever spot of ground, O sons of good family, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> is recited, or illuminated, or taught, or written, or contemplated, or spoken of, or studied, or exists in manuscript form — whether in a park, a monastery, a house, a forest, a city, at the foot of a tree, in a palace, in a hut, or in a cave — in that spot of ground, a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) should be made in honor of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For what reason? That spot of ground should be understood as the <s>bodhimaṇḍa</s> (seat of awakening) of all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In that spot of ground, it should be understood that all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, have attained supreme perfect awakening. In that spot of ground, the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel has been turned by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>. In that spot of ground, it should be understood that all <s>Tathāgatas</s> have entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

children.text: acintiyā lokahitāna dharmatā abhijñajñānasmi pratiṣṭhitānām /
children.translated_text: Inconceivable is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of reality) of those who benefit the world, of those established in superknowledge and wisdom;

children.text: ye ṛddhi darśenti anantacakṣuṣaḥ prāmodyahetoriha sarvadehinām // Saddhp_20.1 //
children.translated_text: they display supernatural wonders, those of boundless vision, for the purpose of delighting all embodied beings here. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.1 ||

children.text: jihvendriyaṃ prāpiya brahmalokaṃ raśmīsahasrāṇi pramuñcamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Extending their tongue-faculties to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, sending forth thousands of rays —

children.text: āścaryabhūtā iha ṛddhidarśitāḥ te sarvi ye prasthita agrabodhau // Saddhp_20.2 //
children.translated_text: marvelous are the supernatural displays shown here by all those who have set forth toward supreme awakening! || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.2 ||

children.text: utkāsitaṃ cāpi karonti buddhā ekācchaṭā ye ca karonti śabdam /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> also produce a great lion's roar, and produce a single snapping sound;

children.text: te vijñapentī imu sarvalokaṃ daśo diśāyāṃ ima lokadhātum // Saddhp_20.3 //
children.translated_text: they make this entire world in the ten directions, this world-system, aware. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.3 ||

children.text: etāni cānyāni ca prātihāryā guṇānnidarśenti hitānukampakāḥ /
children.translated_text: These and other supernatural wonders they show — those who are compassionate and benevolent — displaying their merits;

children.text: kathaṃ nu te harṣita tasmi kāle dhāreyu sūtraṃ sugatasya nirvṛte // Saddhp_20.4 //
children.translated_text: how delighted they were at that time! [Thinking:] 'May they uphold this <s>sūtra</s> after the <s>Sugata</s>'s <s>parinirvāṇa</s>!' || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.4 ||

children.text: bahū pi kalpāna sahasrakoṭyo vadeya varṇaṃ sugatātmajānām /
children.translated_text: Even through many thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, I might praise the merits of the sons of the <s>Sugata</s>

children.text: ye dhārayiṣyantima sūtramagraṃ parinirvṛte lokavināyakasmin // Saddhp_20.5 //
children.translated_text: who will uphold this supreme <s>sūtra</s> after the Lord of the World has entered <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.5 ||

children.text: na teṣa paryanta bhavedguṇānāṃ ākāśadhātau hi yathā diśāsu /
children.translated_text: There would be no end to their merits, as in the realm of space there [is no end] in the directions;

children.text: acintiyā teṣā guṇā bhavanti ye sūtra dhārenti idaṃ śubhaṃ sadā // Saddhp_20.6 //
children.translated_text: Inconceivable are the virtues of those who always uphold this auspicious <s>sūtra</s>! || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.6 ||

body.text: dṛṣṭo ahaṃ sarva ime ca nāyakā ayaṃ ca yo nirvṛtu lokanāyakaḥ /
body.translated_text: I have been seen, and all these Guides, and he who is the departed World-Protector,

body.text: ime ca sarve bahubodhisattvāḥ parṣāśca catvāri anena dṛṣṭāḥ // Saddhp_20.7 //
body.translated_text: and all these many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and the four assemblies have been seen by this one. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.7 ||

children.text: ahaṃ ca ārāgitu tenihādya ime ca ārāgita sarvi nāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: And I have been pleased by him here today, and all these Guides have been pleased,

children.text: ayaṃ ca yo nirvṛtako jinendro ye cāpi anye daśasū diśāsu // Saddhp_20.8 //
children.translated_text: and he who is the departed Lord of <s>Jinas</s>, and those others too in the ten directions. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.8 ||

children.text: anāgatātīta tathā ca buddhāḥ tiṣṭhanti ye cāpi daśasu ddiśāsu /
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddhas</s> of the future, the past, and likewise those who abide in the ten directions —

children.text: te sarvi dṛṣṭāśca supūjitāśca bhaveyu yo dhārayi sūtrametat // Saddhp_20.9 //
children.translated_text: all of them would be seen and well-worshipped by one who upholds this <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.9 ||

children.text: rahasyajñānaṃ puruṣottamānāṃ yaṃ bodhimaṇḍasmi vicintitāsīt /
children.translated_text: The secret knowledge of the supreme among men, which was contemplated at the seat of awakening —

children.text: anucintayetso pi tu kṣiprameva yo dhārayet sūtrimu bhūtadharmam // Saddhp_20.10 //
children.translated_text: he too would quickly contemplate it, who upholds this <s>sūtra</s> of the true <s>Dharma</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.10 ||

children.text: pratibhānu tasyāpi bhavedanantaṃ yathāpi vāyurna kahiṃci sajjati /
children.translated_text: His eloquence too would be infinite, just as the wind is unobstructed anywhere;

children.text: dharme 'pi cārthe ca nirukti jānati yo dhārayet sutramidaṃ viśiṣṭam // Saddhp_20.11 //
children.translated_text: he knows both <s>Dharma</s>, meaning, and etymology — whoever upholds this distinguished <s>sūtra</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.11 ||

children.text: anusaṃdhisūtrāṇa sadā prajānati saṃdhāya yaṃ bhāṣitu nāyakehi /
children.translated_text: He always knows the connections between <s>sūtras</s>, the hidden meaning spoken by the Guides;

children.text: parinirvṛtasyāpi vināyakasya sūtrāṇa so jānati bhutamartham // Saddhp_20.12 //
children.translated_text: even after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the Guide, he knows the true meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.12 ||

children.text: candropamaḥ sūryasamaḥ sa bhāti ālokapradyotakaraḥ sa bhoti /
children.translated_text: He shines like the moon, like the sun; he becomes a giver of light and radiance;

children.text: vicarantu so medini tena tena samādapetī bahubodhisattvān // Saddhp_20.13 //
children.translated_text: wandering here and there over the earth, he inspires many <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.13 ||

children.text: tasmāddhi ye paṇḍita bodhisattvāḥ śrutvānimānīddaśa ānuśaṃsān /
children.translated_text: Therefore, those wise <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, having heard these ten advantages,

children.text: dhāreyu sūtraṃ mama nirvṛtasya na teṣa bodhāya bhaveta saṃśayaḥ // Saddhp_20.14 //
children.translated_text: should uphold this <s>sūtra</s> of mine [spoken while I have] passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s> — there shall be no doubt for them regarding awakening. || <s>Saddhp</s> 20.14 ||'

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye tathāgataddharyabhisaṃskāraparivarto nāma viṃśatitamaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, named 'The Chapter on the Miraculous Power of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,' in the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse.

body.text:
Saddhp_21: dhāraṇīparivartaḥ |
atha khalu bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantametadavocat kiyad bhagavan sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā puṇyaṃ prasavet, ya imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ dhārayet, kāyagataṃ vā pustakagataṃ vā kṛtvā? evamukte bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - yaḥ kaścid bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā aśītigaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni tathāgatakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi satkuryād gurukuryānmānayet pūjayet, takiṃ manyase bhaiṣajyarāja kiyatkulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahu puṇyaṃ prasavet? bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattva āha - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata | bhagavānāha - ārocayāmi te bhaiṣajyarāja, prativedayāmi | yaḥ kaścid bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā asmāt saddharmapuṇḍarīkāddharmaparyāyādantaśa ekāmapi catuṣpadīgāthāṃ dhārayet, vācayet, paryavāpnuyāt, pratipattyā ca saṃpādayet, ataḥ sa bhaiṣajyarāja kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahutaraṃ puṇyaṃ prasavet ||
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 21: The Chapter on <s>Dhāraṇī</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, having risen from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'How much merit, Blessed One, would a son of good family or daughter of good family generate, who upholds this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse — whether memorized or written in a book?' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>: 'Whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, whether a son or daughter of good family, were to honor, revere, respect, and worship eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — what do you think, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, would that son or daughter of good family generate much merit from that cause?' The <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> replied: 'Much, Blessed One! Much, <s>Sugata</s>!' The Blessed One said: 'I declare to you, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, I announce: whoever, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, whether a son or daughter of good family, upholds even a single four-line verse from this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, recites it, masters it, and practices it — that son or daughter of good family, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, would generate even greater merit from that cause.'

body.text: atha khalu bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavantametadavocat - dāsyāmo vayaṃ bhagavaṃsteṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ vā yeṣāmayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ kāyagato vā syāt, pustakagato vā, rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye dhāraṇīmantrapadāni | tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, at that moment, said this to the Blessed One: 'We shall give, Blessed One, to those sons of good family or daughters of good family for whom this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse has become memorized or written in a book, <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables for their protection, guarding, and safekeeping.' Namely:

body.text: anye manye mane mamane citte carite same samitā viśānte mukte muktatame same aviṣame samasame jaye kṣaye akṣaye akṣiṇe śānte samite dhāraṇi ālokabhāṣe pratyavekṣaṇi nidhiru abhyantaraniviṣṭe abhyantarapāriśuddhimutkule araḍe paraḍe sukāṅkṣi asamasame buddhavilokite dharmaparīkṣite saṃghanirghoṣaṇi nirghoṇi bhayābhayaviśodhani mantre mantrākṣayate rute rutakauśalye akṣaye akṣayavanatāye vakkule valoḍra amanyanatāye svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>anye manye mane mamane citte carite same samitā viśānte mukte muktatame same aviṣame samasame jaye kṣaye akṣaye akṣiṇe śānte samite dhāraṇi ālokabhāṣe pratyavekṣaṇi nidhiru abhyantaraniviṣṭe abhyantarapāriśuddhimutkule araḍe paraḍe sukāṅkṣi asamasame buddhavilokite dharmaparīkṣite saṃghanirghoṣaṇi nirghoṇi bhayābhayaviśodhani mantre mantrākṣayate rute rutakauśalye akṣaye akṣayavanatāye vakkule valoḍra amanyanatāye svāhā</s>.

body.text: imāni bhagavan mantradhāraṇīpadāni dvāṣaṣṭibhirgaṅgānadīvālikāsamairbuddhairbhagavadbhirbhāṣitāni | te sarve buddhā bhagavantastena drugdhāḥ syuḥ, ya evaṃrupān dharmabhāṇakānevaṃrūpān sūtrāntadhārakānatikrāmet ||
body.translated_text: 'These <s>mantra</s>-<s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables, Blessed One, have been spoken by <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, as numerous as the sands of sixty-two <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers. All those Blessed <s>Buddhas</s> would be wronged by anyone who would violate such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, such holders of <s>sūtras</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān bhaiṣajyarājāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya sādhukāramadāt sādhu sādhu bhaiṣajyarāja, sattvānāmarthaḥ kṛtaḥ | dhāraṇīpadāni bhāṣitāni sattvānāmanukampāmupādaya | rakṣāvaraṇaguptiḥ kṛtā ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One gave his approval to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>! The welfare of beings has been accomplished. <s>Dhāraṇī</s> syllables have been spoken out of compassion for beings. Protection, guarding, and safekeeping have been provided.'

body.text: atha khalu pradānaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ahamapi bhagavan evaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmarthāya dhāraṇīpadāni dāsyāmi, yatteṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ na kaścidavatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ lapsyate | tadyathā yakṣo vā rākṣaso vā pūtano vā kṛtyo vā kumbhāṇḍo vā preto vā avatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ na lapsyata iti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Pradānaśūra</s> (Hero of Giving) said this to the Blessed One: 'I too, Blessed One, shall give <s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables for the sake of such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, so that for such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, no one seeking an opportunity, searching for an opening, shall find an opening — neither a <s>yakṣa</s>, nor a <s>rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>pūtana</s>, nor a <s>kṛtyā</s>, nor a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>, nor a <s>preta</s> seeking an opportunity, searching for an opening, shall find an opening.'

body.text: atha khalu pradānaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasyāṃ velāyāmimāni dhāraṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣate sma | tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Pradānaśūra</s>, at that moment, spoke these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables. Namely:

body.text: jvale mahājvale ukke tukke mukke aḍe aḍāvati nṛtye nṛtyāvati iṭṭini viṭṭini ciṭṭini nṛtyani nṛtyāvati svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>jvale mahājvale ukke tukke mukke aḍe aḍāvati nṛtye nṛtyāvati iṭṭini viṭṭini ciṭṭini nṛtyani nṛtyāvati svāhā</s>.

body.text: imāni bhagavan dhāraṇīpadāni gaṅgānadīvālikāsamaistathāgatairarhadbhiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhairbhāṣitāni, anumoditāni ca | te sarve tathāgatāstena drugdhāḥ syuḥ, yastānevaṃrūpān dharmabhāṇakānatikrameta ||
body.translated_text: 'These <s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables, Blessed One, have been spoken by <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, as numerous as the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and approved by them. All those <s>Tathāgatas</s> would be wronged by anyone who would violate such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers.'

body.text: atha khalu vaiśravaṇo mahārājo bhagavantametadavocat - ahamapi bhagavan dhāraṇīpadāni bhāṣiṣye teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ hitāya sukhāya anukampāyai rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye || tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then the great king <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'I too, Blessed One, shall speak <s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables for the welfare, happiness, and compassionate protection, guarding, and safekeeping of those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers.' Namely:

body.text: aṭṭe taṭṭe naṭṭe vanaṭṭe anaḍe nāḍi kunaḍi svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>aṭṭe taṭṭe naṭṭe vanaṭṭe anaḍe nāḍi kunaḍi svāhā</s>.

body.text: ebhirbhagavan dhāraṇīpadaisteṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ pudgalānāṃ rakṣāṃ karomi, yojanaśatāccāhaṃ teṣāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ ca evaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ rakṣā kṛtā bhaviṣyati, svastyayanaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: 'With these <s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables, Blessed One, I make the protection of those <s>Dharma</s>-preacher individuals. And for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> around, I shall provide protection and safety for those sons of good family and daughters of good family who are holders of such <s>sūtras</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu virūḍhako mahārājo tasyāmeva parṣadi saṃnipatito 'bhūt saṃniṣaṇṇaśca kumbhāṇḍakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ | sa utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat - ahamapi bhagavan dhāraṇīpadāni bhāṣiṣye bahujanahitāya | teṣāṃ ca tathārūpāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye dhāraṇīmantrapadāni | tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then the great king <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, who was present and seated in that very assembly, surrounded and attended by <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundred-thousands of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, having risen from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, and with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'I too, Blessed One, shall speak <s>dhāraṇī</s> syllables for the welfare of the many, and for the protection, guarding, and safekeeping of such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers and holders of such <s>sūtras</s>.' Namely:

body.text: agaṇe gaṇe gauri gandhāri caṇḍāli mātaṅgi pukkasi saṃkule vrūsali sisi svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>agaṇe gaṇe gauri gandhāri caṇḍāli mātaṅgi pukkasi saṃkule vrūsali sisi svāhā</s>.

body.text: imāni tāni bhagavan dhāraṇīmantrapadāni, yāni dvācatvāriṃśadbhirbuddhakoṭībhirbhāṣitāni | te sarve tena drugdhāḥ syuḥ, yastānevaṃrūpān dharmabhāṇakānatikrameta ||
body.translated_text: 'These, Blessed One, are <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables that have been spoken by forty-two <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Buddhas</s>. All of them would be wronged by anyone who would violate such <s>Dharma</s>-preachers.'

body.text: atha khalu lambā ca nāma rākṣasī vilambā ca nāma rākṣasī kūṭadantī ca nāma rākṣasī puṣpadantī ca nāma rākṣasī makuṭadantī ca nāma rākṣasī keśinī ca nāma rākṣasī acalā ca nāma rākṣasī mālādhārī ca nāma rākṣasī kuntī ca nāma rākṣasī sarvasattvojohārī ca nāma rākṣasī hḥrītī ca nḥma rḥkṣasī saputraparivḥrḥ etḥḥ sarvḥ rḥkṣasyo yena bhagavḥṃstenopasaṃkrḥntḥḥ | upasaṃkramya sarvḥstḥ rḥkṣasya ekasvareṇa bhagavantametadavocan - vayamapi bhagavaṃsteṣḥmevaṃrūpḥṇḥṃ sūtrḥntadhḥrakḥṇḥṃ dharmabhḥṇakḥnḥṃ rakṣḥvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyḥmaḥ, svastyayanaṃ ca kariṣyḥmaḥ | yathḥ teṣḥṃ dharmabhḥṇakḥnḥṃ na kaścidavatḥraprekṣī avatḥragaveṣī avatḥraṃ lapsyatīti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>rākṣasīs</s> (demonesses) named <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Vilambā</s>, <s>Kūṭadantī</s> (Fang-Tooth), <s>Puṣpadantī</s> (Flower-Tooth), <s>Makuṭadantī</s> (Crown-Tooth), <s>Keśinī</s> (Long-Haired), <s>Acalā</s> (Unshakable), <s>Mālādhārī</s> (Garland-Bearer), <s>Kuntī</s>, <s>Sarvasattvojohārī</s> (Stealer of All Beings), and <s>Hārītī</s>, together with her sons and retinue — all these <s>rākṣasīs</s> approached the Blessed One. Having approached, all those <s>rākṣasīs</s> with one voice said this to the Blessed One: 'We too, Blessed One, shall provide protection, guarding, and safekeeping for such holders of <s>sūtras</s> and <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, and shall provide safety — so that no one seeking an opportunity, searching for an opening, shall find an opening against those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers.'

body.text: atha khalu tāḥ sarvā rākṣasya ekasvareṇa samaṃ saṃgītyā bhagavata imāni dhāraṇīmantrapadāni prayacchanti sma | tadyathā -
body.translated_text: Then all those <s>rākṣasīs</s>, with one voice, in unison, offered these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-<s>mantra</s> syllables to the Blessed One. Namely:

body.text: iti me iti me iti me iti me iti me | nime nime nime nime nime | ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe | stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>iti me iti me iti me iti me iti me | nime nime nime nime nime | ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe ruhe | stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe stuhe svāhā</s>.

body.text: imaṃ śīrṣaṃ samāruhya mā kaścid drohī bhavatu dharmabhāṇakānāṃ yakṣo vā rākṣaso vā preto vā piśāco vā pūtano vā kṛtyo va vetālo vā kumbhāṇḍo vā stabdho vā omārako vā ostārako vā apasmārako vā yakṣakṛtyo vā amanuṣyakṛtyo vā manuṣyakṛtyo vā ekāhiko vā dvaitīyako vā traitīyako vā caturthako vā nityajvaro vā viṣamajvaro vā | antaśaḥ svapnāntaragatasyāpi strīrūpāṇi vā puruṣarūpāṇi vā dārakarūpāṇi vā dārikārūpāṇi vā viheṭhāṃ kuryuḥ, nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Let no one climbing upon this head be hostile to the <s>Dharma</s>-preachers — neither a <s>yakṣa</s>, nor a <s>rākṣasa</s>, nor a <s>preta</s>, nor a <s>piśāca</s>, nor a <s>pūtana</s>, nor a <s>kṛtyā</s>, nor a <s>vetāla</s>, nor a <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>, nor a <s>stabdha</s> (paralysis spirit), nor an <s>omāraka</s> (vomiting spirit), nor an <s>ostāraka</s> (casting-down spirit), nor an <s>apasmāraka</s> (epilepsy spirit), nor a <s>yakṣa</s>-made affliction, nor a non-human-made affliction, nor a human-made affliction, nor a one-day fever, nor a two-day fever, nor a three-day fever, nor a four-day fever, nor a constant fever, nor an irregular fever. Even in the interval of dreams, whether in the form of a woman, a man, a boy, or a girl — let none cause harm! This situation is not possible!'

body.text: atha khalu tā rākṣasya evasvareṇa samaṃ saṃgītyā bhagavantamābhirgāthābhiradhyabhāṣanta -
body.translated_text: Then those <s>rākṣasīs</s>, with one voice, in unison, addressed the Blessed One with these verses:

children.text: saptadhāsya sphuṭenmūrdhā arjakasyeva mañjarī /
children.translated_text: 'May his head be split into seven parts, like the flower-cluster of an <s>arjaka</s> plant,

children.text: ya imaṃ mantra śrutvā vai atikrameddharmabhāṇakam // Saddhp_21.1 //
children.translated_text: of whoever, having heard this <s>mantra</s>, would violate the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher! || <s>Saddhp</s> 21.1 ||

children.text: yā gatirmātṛghātīnāṃ pitṛghātīna yā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the destiny of matricides, whatever is the destiny of patricides,

children.text: tāṃ gatiṃ pratigacchedyo dharmabhāṇakamatikramet // Saddhp_21.2 //
children.translated_text: that destiny shall befall whoever would violate the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher! || <s>Saddhp</s> 21.2 ||

children.text: yā gatistilapīḍānāṃ tilakūṭānāṃ ca yā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the destiny of sesame-oil pressers, whatever is the destiny of sesame-cheaters,

children.text: tāṃ gatiṃ pratigacchedyo dharmabhāṇakamatikramet // Saddhp_21.3 //
children.translated_text: that destiny shall befall whoever would violate the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher! || <s>Saddhp</s> 21.3 ||

children.text: yā gatistulakūṭānāṃ kāṃsyakūṭāna yā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the destiny of scale-cheaters, whatever is the destiny of bronze-cheaters,

children.text: tāṃ gatiṃ pratigacchedyo dharmabhāṇakamatikramet // Saddhp_21.4 //
children.translated_text: that destiny shall befall whoever would violate the <s>Dharma</s>-preacher! || <s>Saddhp</s> 21.4 ||'

body.text: evamuktvā tāḥ kuntipramukhā rākṣasyo bhagavantametadūcuḥ - vayamapi bhagavaṃsteṣāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ viṣadūṣaṇaṃ kariṣyāma iti | evamukte bhagavāṃstā rākṣasya etadavocat - sādhu sādhu bhaginyaḥ | yad yūyaṃ teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptiṃ kariṣyadhve ye 'sya dharmaparyāyasya antaśo nāmadheyamātramapi dhārayiṣyanti | kaḥ punarvādo ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ sakalasamāptaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, pustakagataṃ vā satkuryuḥ puṣpadhūpagandhamālyavilepanacūrṇacīvaracchatradhvajapatākāvaijayantībhistailapradīpairvā ghṛtapradīpairvā gandhatailapradīpairvā campakatailapradīpairvā vārṣikatailapradīpairvā utpalatailapradīpairvā sumanātailapradīpairvā īddaśairbahuvidhaiḥ pūjāvidhānaśatasahasraiḥ satkariṣyanti gurukariṣyanti, te tvayā kunti saparivārayā rakṣitavyāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having said this, those <s>Rākṣasīs</s> led by <s>Kuntī</s> said to the Blessed One: 'We too, Blessed One, will protect those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers of such a kind. We will bring them safety, protection from punishment, and neutralization of poison.' Having said this, the Blessed One said to those <s>Rākṣasīs</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, sisters! May you provide protection, shelter, and guardianship for those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers who will uphold even the mere name of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. How much more so for those who will uphold this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse complete and whole, or who will honor the book with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, flags, victory-standards, oil-lamps, ghee-lamps, perfumed-oil-lamps, campaka-oil-lamps, vārṣika-oil-lamps, utpala-oil-lamps, sumanā-oil-lamps, and with such manifold hundreds of thousands of forms of worship — they, O <s>Kuntī</s>, together with your retinue, are to be protected!'

body.text: asmin khalu punardhāraṇīparivarte nirdiśyamāne aṣṭāṣaṣṭīnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilābho 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: When this <s>Dhāraṇī</s> chapter was being expounded, sixty-eight thousand beings attained <s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (acceptance of the non-arising of dharmas).

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye dhāraṇīparivarto nāmaikaviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the <s>Dhāraṇī</s> Chapter.

body.text: Saddhp_22: bhaiṣajyarājapūrvayogaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 22: The Chapter on the Former Yoga of <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>.

body.text: atha khalu nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijño bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kena kāreṇena bhagavan bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'syāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau pravicarati, bahūni cāsya bhagavan duṣkarakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi saṃdṛśyante? tatsādhu bhagavān deśayatu tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhaiṣajyarājasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya yat kiṃciccaryāpradeśamātram, yacchrutvā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāstadanyalokadhātvāgatāśca bodhisattvā mahāsattvā ime ca mahāśrāvakāḥ śrutvā sarve prītāstuṣṭā udagrā āttamanaso bhaveyuriti ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s> (Star-King-Flower-Superknowledge) said to the Blessed One: 'For what reason, Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> wander in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system? And many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of difficult deeds of his are seen, O Blessed One. Please, may the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, teach even a small portion of the conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, hearing which gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, non-humans, and <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who have come from other world-systems, and these great <s>Śrāvakas</s> — may all of them, having heard, be gladdened, satisfied, uplifted, and delighted.'

body.text:
atha khalu bhagavān nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya adhyeṣaṇāṃ viditvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - bhūtapurvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvani gaṅgānadīvālikāsamaiḥ kalpairyadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrīrnāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādividyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān | tasya khalu punarnakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña bhagavataścandrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya aśītikoṭyo bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ mahāsaṃnipāto 'bhūt dvāsaptatigaṅgānadīvālikāsamāścāsya śrāvakasaṃnipāto 'bhūt | apagamātṛgrāmaṃ ca tatpravacanamabhūt, apagatanirayatiryagyonipretāsurakāyaṃ samaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ pāṇitalajātaṃ ca tadbuddhakṣetramabhūt, divyavaiḍūryamayabhūmibhāgaṃ ratnacandanavṛkṣasamalakṛtaṃ ca ratnajālasamīritaṃ ca avasaktapaṭṭadāmābhipralambitaṃ ca ratnagandhaghaṭikānirdhūpitaṃ ca | sarveṣu ca ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu iṣukṣepamānamātre ratnavyomakāni saṃsthitānyabhūvan | sarveṣu ca ratnavyomakamūrdhneṣu koṭīśataṃ devaputrāṇāṃ tūryatālāvacarasaṃgītisaṃprabhāṇitena avasthitamabhūt tasya bhagavataścandrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjākarmaṇe | sa ca bhagavānimaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ teṣāṃ mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati sma, sarvasattvapriyadarśanaṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamadhiṣṭhānaṃ kṛtvā | tasya khalu punarnakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña bhagavataścandrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya dvācatvāriṃśatkalpasahasrāṇyāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt, teṣāṃ ca bodhisattvanāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ tāvadevāyuṣpramāṇamabhūt | sa ca sarvasattvapriyadarśano bodhisattvo mahāsattvastasya bhagavataḥ pravacane duṣkaracaryābhiyukto 'bhūt | sa dvādaśavarṣasahasrāṇi caṃkramābhiruḍho 'bhūt, mahāvīryārambheṇa yogābhiyukto
'bhūt | sa dvādaśānāṃ varṣasahasrāṇāmatyayena sarvarūpasaṃdarśanaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate sma | sahapratilambhācca tasya samādheḥ sa sarvasattvapriyadarśano bodhisattvo mahāsattvastuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātastasyāṃ velāyāmevaṃ cintayāmāsa - imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyamāgamya ayaṃ mayā sarvarūpasaṃdarśanaḥ
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having understood the request of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, at that time said to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>: 'In the past, son of good family, in a former age, <s>kalpas</s> ago equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, at that time, in that era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī</s> (Splendor of Pure Radiance of Moon and Sun), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. That Blessed One <s>Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, had a great assembly of eighty <s>koṭis</s> of <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, and a <s>Śrāvaka</s>-assembly of seventy-two <s>Gaṅgā</s>-river-sand-numbered [monks]. And his dispensation was free from women, free from the hells, the animal realm, the hungry-ghost realm, and the <s>Asura</s> host. That <s>buddhakṣetra</s> was level, delightful, smooth as the palm of the hand, with ground made of divine <s>vaidūrya</s>, adorned with jeweled sandalwood trees, draped with nets of jewels, overhung with festoons of silk ribbons, perfumed with censers of jeweled incense. And at the foot of every jewel-tree, jeweled platforms were set up at a distance of a bowshot apart. And on every jewel-platform summit, a hundred <s>koṭis</s> of sons of the gods stood, performing worship to that Blessed One <s>Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, with an ensemble of instrumental music, rhythms, and songs. And that Blessed One extensively illuminated this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> to those great <s>Śrāvakas</s> and those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, having appointed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> (Beloved-Sight-of-All-Beings) [as the principal]. The lifespan of that Blessed One <s>Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, O <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, was forty-two thousand <s>kalpas</s>, and the lifespan of those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> and those great <s>Śrāvakas</s> was the same. That <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> devoted himself to difficult practices in that Blessed One's dispensation. For twelve thousand years he engaged in walking meditation, devoted to yoga with great effort and vigor. At the end of those twelve thousand years, he attained a <s>samādhi</s> called <s>Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana</s> (Vision-of-All-Forms). And immediately upon attaining that <s>samādhi</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>, satisfied, uplifted, delighted, filled with joy and happiness, thought at that time: 'It is through this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> that I have attained this <s>Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana</s>

body.text: samādhiḥ pratilabdhaḥ | tasyāṃ velāyāṃ sa sarvasattvapriyadarśano bodhisattvo mahāsattva evaṃ cintayati sma - yannvahaṃ bhagavataścandrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśriyastathāgatasya pūjāṃ kuryāmū, asya ca saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya | sa tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ yasya samādheḥ samanantarasamāpannasya sarvasattvapriyadarśanasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya, adya tāvadevoparyandarīkṣānmāndāravamahāmāndāravāṇāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ mahantaṃ puṣpavarṣamabhipravṛṣḥam | kālānusāricandanameghaḥ kṛtaḥ | uragasāracandanavarṣanabhipravṛṣḥam | tādṛśī ca nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña sā gandhajātiḥ, yasyā ekaḥ karṣa imāṃ sahālokadhātuṃ mūlyena kṣamati ||
body.translated_text: <s>samādhi</s>.' At that time, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s> thought: 'Let me now perform worship to the Blessed One <s>Candrasūryavimalaprabhāsaśrī</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, and to this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>.' At that time he entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, immediately upon his entering it, from above in the sky there rained a great shower of <s>Māndārava</s> and great <s>Māndārava</s> flowers upon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>. A cloud of <s>kālānusāri</s> (black aloe) sandalwood arose, and a rain of <s>uragasāra</s> (serpent-essence) sandalwood fell. And that fragrance, O <s>Nakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, was such that a single <s>karṣa</s> (unit of weight) was worth the entire <s>Sahā</s> world-system in value.
