body.text: atha khalu gadgadasvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tasya ca bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya dhātustūpe vipulāṃ vistīrṇāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā punarapi saptaratnamaye kūṭāgāre 'bhiruhya prakampadbhiḥ kṣetraiḥ pravarṣadbhiḥ padmaiḥ pravādyamānaistūryakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ taiścaturaśītibodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ punarapi svaṃ buddhakṣetramabhigataḥ | samabhigamya ca taṃ bhagavantaṃ kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadavocat - kṛto me bhagavan sahāyāṃ lokadhātau sattvārthaḥ | tasya ca bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya dhātustūpo dṛṣṭaḥ vanditaśca | sa ca bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato dṛṣṭo vanditaśca | sa ca mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto dṛṣṭaḥ | sa ca bhaiṣajyarājo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo vīryabalabegaprāptaḥ, sa ca pradānaśūro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dṛṣṭaḥ | sarveṣāṃ ca teṣāṃ caturaśītibodhisattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ sarvarūpasaṃdarśanasya samādheḥ pratilambho 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Gadgadasvara</s>, having performed extensive worship to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, and to the relic-<s>stūpa</s> of that Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, ascended again into the seven-jeweled tower-chamber, and surrounded and attended by those eighty-four <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, amidst trembling fields, raining lotuses, and the playing of hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of musical instruments, returned to his own <s>buddhakṣetra</s>. Having returned, he said this to the Blessed One <s>Kamaladalavimalanakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One: 'I have accomplished the benefit of beings in the <s>Sahā</s> world-system, O Blessed One. The relic-<s>stūpa</s> of that Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, was seen and saluted. And the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, was seen and saluted. And the prince <s>Mañjuśrī</s> was seen. And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s>, who has attained the force and speed of vigor, was seen. And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Pradānaśūra</s> (Hero of Giving) was seen. And all those eighty-four <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attained the <s>Sarvarūpasaṃdarśana Samādhi</s>.'

body.text: asmin khalu punargadgadasvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya gamanāgamanaparivarte bhāṣyamāṇe dvācatvāriṃśatāṃ bodhisattvasahasrāṇāmanutpattikadharmakṣāntipratilambho 'bhūt | padmaśriyaśca bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya samādheḥ pratilambho 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Now, while this chapter on the coming and going of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Gadgadasvara</s> was being taught, forty-two thousand <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attained the <s>Anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s> (Patient Acceptance of the Non-Arising of Dharmas). And the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Padmaśrī</s> attained the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Samādhi</s>.

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye gadgadasvaraparivarto nāma trayoviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on <s>Gadgadasvara</s> (Wonderful Voice).

body.text: Saddhp_24: samantamukhaparivartaḥ ||
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 24: The Chapter on <s>Samantamukha</s> (Universal Gateway).

body.text: atha khalu akṣayamatirbodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat - kena kāraṇena bhagavan avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'valokiteśvara ityucyate? evamukte bhagavānakṣayamatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - iha kulaputra yāvanti sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi yāni duḥkhāni pratyuanubhavanti, tāni sacedavalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmadheyaṃ śṛṇuyuḥ, te sarve tasmādduḥkhaskandhād parimucyeran | ye ca kulaputra sattvā avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmadheyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, sacette mahatyagniskandhe prapateyuḥ, sarve te avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tejasā tasmānmahato 'gniskandhāt parimucyeran | sacet punaḥ kulaputra sattvā nadībhiruhyamānā avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyākrandaṃ kuryuḥ, sarvāstā nadyasteṣāṃ sattvānāṃ gādhaṃ dadyuḥ | sacet punaḥ kulaputra sāgaramadhye vahanābhirūḍhānāṃ sattvakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇāṃ hiraṇyasuvarṇamaṇimuktāvajravaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravālāśmagarbhamusāragalvalohitamuktādīnāṃ kṛtanidhīnāṃ sa potasteṣāṃ kālikāvātena rākṣasīdvīpe kṣiptaḥ syāt, tasmiṃśca kaścidevaikaḥ sattvaḥ syāt yo 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyākrandaṃ kuryāt, sarve te parimucyeraṃstasmād rākṣasīdvīpāt | anena khalu punaḥ kulaputra kāraṇena avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'valokiteśvara iti saṃjñāyate ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> (Inexhaustible Intention) rose from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and joining his palms facing the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'For what reason, O Blessed One, is the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> called <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> (Lord Who Looks Down)?' When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s>: 'Here, O son of good family, as many as there are hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of beings who experience suffering — if they should hear the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, all of them would be freed from that mass of suffering. And those beings, O son of good family, who will hold the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — if they should fall into a great mass of fire, all of them, by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, would be freed from that great mass of fire. And if, O son of good family, beings being swept away by rivers were to call upon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, all those rivers would give those beings a place to stand. And if, O son of good family, hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of beings, having boarded ships in the midst of the ocean, laden with precious treasures — gold, silver, gems, pearls, diamonds, <s>vaidūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (diamond), <s>musāragalva</s> (coral), and red pearls — and that vessel were cast by a <s>kālikā</s>-wind onto a <s>rākṣasī</s>-island, and if among them even a single being were to call upon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, all of them would be freed from that <s>rākṣasī</s>-island. For this reason, O son of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is called <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.'

body.text: sacet kulaputra kaścideva vadhyotsṛṣṭo 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyākrandaṃ kuryāt, tāni teṣāṃ vadhyaghātakānāṃ śastrāṇi vikīryeran | sacet khalu punaḥ kulaputra ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturyakṣarākṣasaiḥ paripūrṇo bhavet, te 'valokiteśvarasya mahāsattvasya nāmadheyagrahaṇena duṣṭacittā draṣṭumapyaśaktāḥ syuḥ | sacetkhalu punaḥ kulaputra kaścideva sattvo dārvāyasmayairhaḍinigaḍabandhanairbaddho bhavet, aparādhyanaparādhī vā, tasyāvalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmadheyagrahaṇena kṣipraṃ tāni haḍinigaḍabandhanāni vivaramanuprayacchanti | īdṛśaḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'If, O son of good family, anyone condemned to execution were to call upon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the weapons of those executioners would be scattered. If, O son of good family, this great trichiliocosm were filled with <s>yakṣas</s> and <s>rākṣasas</s>, they, by the mere holding of the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, would be unable even to look upon [that being] with hostile eyes. If, O son of good family, any being were bound with fetters, shackles, and chains of wood or iron, whether guilty or innocent, by the mere holding of the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, those fetters, shackles, and chains would quickly fall open. Such, O son of good family, is the power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.'

body.text: sacetkulaputra ayaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhāturdhūrtairamitraiścauraiśca śastrapāṇibhiḥ paripūrṇo bhavet, tasmiṃścaikaḥ sārthavāho mahāntaṃ sārthaṃ ratnāḍhyamanardhyaṃ gṛhītvā gacchet | te gacchantastāṃścaurān dhūrtān śatrūṃśca śastrahastān paśyeyuḥ | dṛṣṭvā ca punarbhītāstrastā aśaraṇamātmānaṃ saṃjānīyuḥ | sa ca sārthavāhastaṃ sārthamevaṃ brūyāt - mā bhaiṣṭa kulaputrāḥ, mā bhaiṣṭa, abhayaṃdadamavalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvamekasvareṇa sarve samākrandadhvam | tato yūyamasmāccaurabhayādamitrabhayāt kṣiprameva parimokṣyadhve | atha khalu sarva eva sa sārthaḥ ekasvareṇa avalokiteśvaramākrandet - namo namastasmai abhayaṃdadāyāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāyeti
body.translated_text: 'If, O son of good family, this great trichiliocosm were filled with rogues, enemies, and bandits armed with weapons, and if in it a single caravan-leader were traveling with a great caravan laden with priceless treasures, and those [travelers], going along, were to see those bandits, rogues, and enemies armed with weapons, and seeing them became frightened, terrified, and recognized themselves as without refuge — and that caravan-leader were to say to the caravan: "Do not be afraid, sons of good family, do not be afraid! Call upon the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the giver of fearlessness, with a single voice, all of you! Then you will quickly be freed from this danger of bandits and enemies!" Then that entire caravan, with a single voice, would call upon <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: "Homage, homage to that giver of fearlessness, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!"

body.text: | sahanāmagrahaṇenaiva sa sārthaḥ sarvabhayebhyaḥ parimukto bhavet | īdṛśaḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: By the mere holding of his name, that caravan would be freed from all fears. Such, O son of good family, is the power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.'

body.text: ye kulaputra rāgacaritāḥ sattvāḥ, te 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kṛtvā vigatarāgā bhavanti | ye dveṣacaritāḥ sattvāḥ, te 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kṛtvā vigatadveṣā bhavanti | ye mohacaritāḥ sattvāḥ, te 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kṛtvā vigatamohā bhavanti | evaṃ maharddhikaḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Those beings, O son of good family, who are of the nature of passion — by paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they become free from passion. Those beings who are of the nature of hatred — by paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they become free from hatred. Those beings who are of the nature of delusion — by paying homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they become free from delusion. So great in supernatural power, O son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.'

body.text: yaśca kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya putrakāmo mātṛgrāmo namaskāraṃ karoti, tasya putraḥ prajāyate abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ | putralakṣaṇasamanvāgato bahujanapriyo manāpo 'varopitakuśalamūlaśca bhavati | yo dārikāmabhinandati, tasya dārikā prajāyate abhirūpā prāsādikā darśanīyā paramayā śubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgatā dārikā - lakṣaṇasamanvāgatā bahujanapriyā manāpā avaropitakuśalabhūlā ca bhavati | īdṛśaḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya prabhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'And, O son of good family, if a woman who desires a son pays homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, a son will be born to her — handsome, attractive, pleasant to behold, endowed with the marks of a son, dear to many people, agreeable, and one who has planted roots of merit. And if she desires a daughter, a daughter will be born to her — handsome, attractive, pleasant to behold, endowed with the highest excellence of beautiful complexion, endowed with the marks of a daughter, dear to many people, agreeable, and one who has planted roots of merit. Such, O son of good family, is the power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.'

body.text: ye ca kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kariṣyanti, nāmadheyaṃ ca dhārayiṣyanti, teṣāmamoghaphalaṃ bhavati | yaśca kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kariṣyati, nāmadheyaṃ ca dhārayiṣyati, yaśca dvāṣaṣṭīnāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ namaskāraṃ kuryāt, nāmadheyāni ca dhārayet, yaśca tāvatāmeva buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ tiṣṭhatāṃ dhriyatāṃ yāpayatāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ pūjāṃ kuryāt, tatkiṃ manyase kulaputra kiyantaṃ sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ prasavet? evamukte akṣayamatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - bahu bhagavan, bahu sugata sa kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā tatonidānaṃ bahuṃ puṇyābhisaṃskāraṃ prasavet | bhagavānāha - yaśca kulaputra tāvatāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ satkāraṃ kṛtvā puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ, yaśca avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya antaśa ekamapi namaskāraṃ kuryāt nāmadheyaṃ ca dhārayet, samo 'nadhiko 'natirekaḥ puṇyābhisaṃskāraḥ ubhayato bhavet | yaśca teṣāṃ dvāṣaṣṭīnāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ satkāraṃ kuryāt nāmadheyāni ca dhārayet, yaśca avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya namaskāraṃ kuryāt nāmadheyaṃ ca dhārayet, etāvubhau puṇyaskandhau na sukarau kṣapayituṃ kalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrairapi | evamaprameyaṃ kulaputra avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmadhāraṇāt puṇyam ||
body.translated_text: 'And those, O son of good family, who will pay homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> and hold his name — their merit will not be in vain. If, O son of good family, one were to pay homage to and hold the names of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, equal in number to the sands of sixty-two <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, and were to perform worship to all those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, while they dwell, sustain, and continue, with robes, alms-food, bedding, seats, medicines and requisites for the sick — what do you think, O son of good family, how much merit would that son of good family or daughter of good family generate thereby?' When this was said, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Much, O Blessed One, much, O <s>Sugata</s> — that son of good family or daughter of good family would generate much merit thereby.' The Blessed One said: 'The merit generated by performing such honor to all those <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, and the merit of one who pays even a single homage to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> and holds his name — the two merit-formations would be equal, neither greater nor lesser. And the two heaps of merit — that of honoring and holding the names of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, equal to the sands of sixty-two <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, and that of paying homage to and holding the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — could not easily be exhausted even in hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. So immeasurable, O son of good family, is the merit from holding the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.''

body.text: atha khalvakṣayamatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - kathaṃ bhagavan avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'syāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātau pravicarati? kathaṃ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati? kīdṛśaścāvalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyopāyakauśalyaviṣayaḥ? evamukte bhagavānakṣayamatiṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - santi kulaputra lokadhātavaḥ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> (Inexhaustible Intention) said this to the Blessed One: 'How, O Blessed One, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> move about in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system? How does he teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings? And what is the sphere of <s>upāyakauśalya</s> (skillful means) of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>?' Thus addressed, the Blessed One said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s>: 'There are world-systems, O son of good family,

body.text: yeṣvavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo buddharūpeṇa sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | santi lokadhātavaḥ, yeṣvavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bodhisattvarūpeṇa sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcit pratyekabuddharūpeṇa avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcicchrāvakarūpeṇa avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcid brahmarūpeṇāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcicchakrarūpeṇāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcid gandharvarūpeṇāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | keṣāṃcid gandharvarūpeṇāvalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ sattvānāṃ dharmaṃ deśayati | yakṣavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ yakṣarūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | īśvaravaineyānāṃ sattvānāmīśvararūpeṇa, maheśvaravaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ maheśvararūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | cakravartirājavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ cakravartirājarūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | piśācavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ piśācarūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | vaiśravaṇavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vaiśravaṇarūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | senāpativaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ senāpatirūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | brāhmaṇavaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ brāhmaṇarūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | vajrapāṇivaineyānāṃ sattvānāṃ vajrapāṇirūpeṇa dharmaṃ deśayati | evamacintyaguṇasamanvāgataḥ kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ | tasmāttarhi kulaputra avalokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvaṃ pūjayadhvam | eṣa kulaputra avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhītānāṃ sattvānāmabhayaṃ dadāti | anena kāraṇena abhayaṃdada iti saṃjñāyate iha sahāyāṃ lokadhātau ||
body.translated_text: in which the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the form of a <s>Buddha</s>. There are world-systems in which the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings in the form of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>. To some, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>. To some, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Śrāvaka</s>. To some, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of <s>Brahmā</s>. To some, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of <s>Śakra</s>. To some, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>Gandharva</s>. To beings to be disciplined through <s>yakṣas</s>, he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> in the form of a <s>yakṣa</s>. To beings to be disciplined through <s>Īśvara</s>, he teaches in the form of <s>Īśvara</s>; to beings to be disciplined through <s>Maheśvara</s>, he teaches in the form of <s>Maheśvara</s>. To beings to be disciplined through a wheel-turning king, he teaches in the form of a wheel-turning king. To beings to be disciplined through <s>piśācas</s>, he teaches in the form of a <s>piśāca</s>. To beings to be disciplined through <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, he teaches in the form of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. To beings to be disciplined through a general, he teaches in the form of a general. To beings to be disciplined through a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, he teaches in the form of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. To beings to be disciplined through <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, he teaches in the form of <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>. Thus endowed with inconceivable qualities, O son of good family, is the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>. Therefore, O son of good family, worship the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! This <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, O son of good family, bestows fearlessness upon beings who are afraid. For this reason, in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, he is known as <s>Abhayaṃdada</s> (Giver of Fearlessness).'

body.text: atha khalvakṣayamatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - dāsyāmo vayaṃ bhagavan avalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya dharmaprābhṛtaṃ dharmācchādam | bhagavānāhayasyedānīṃ kulaputra kālaṃ manyase | atha khalvakṣayamatirbodhasattvo mahāsattvaḥ svakaṇṭhādavartāya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāramavalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya dharmācchādamanuprayacchati sma - pratīccha satpuruṣa imaṃ dharmācchādaṃ mamāntikāt | sa na pratīcchati sma | atha khalvakṣayamatirbodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'valokiteśvaraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - pratigṛhāṇa tvaṃ kulaputra imaṃ muktāhāramasmākamanukampāmupādāya | atha khalvavalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'kṣayamaterbodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyāntikāt taṃ muktāhāraṃ pratigṛhṇāti sma akṣayamaterbodhisattvasya mahasattvasyānukampāmupādāya, tāsāṃ ca catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ teṣāṃ ca devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyāṇāmanukampāmupādāya | pratigṛhya ca dvau pratyaṃśau kṛtavān | kṛtvā caikaṃ pratyaṃśaṃ bhagavate śākyamunaye dadāti sma, dvitīyaṃ pratyaṃśaṃ bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya ratnastūpe samupanāmayāyāsa | īdṛśyā kulaputra vikurvayā avalokiteśvaro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo 'syāṃ sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvanuvicarati ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Let us, O Blessed One, give to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> a <s>Dharma</s>-offering, a <s>Dharma</s>-covering.' The Blessed One said: 'Let it be as you think fit now, O son of good family.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> removed from his own neck a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [coins] and offered it to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> as a <s>Dharma</s>-covering: 'Accept, O noble one, this <s>Dharma</s>-covering from me.' He did not accept it. Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s> said this to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>: 'Accept, O son of good family, this pearl necklace, out of compassion for us.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> accepted that pearl necklace from the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s>, out of compassion for the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Akṣayamati</s>, and out of compassion for the four assemblies and for the gods, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans. Having accepted it, he divided it into two portions. Having done so, he offered one portion to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, and presented the second portion to the jeweled <s>stūpa</s> of the Blessed One <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. With such a display of miraculous power, O son of good family, does the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> move about in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃstasyāṃ velāyāmimā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, at that time, spoke these verses:

body.text: citradhvaja akṣayomatī etamarthaṃ paripṛcchi kāraṇāt /
body.translated_text: '<s>Citradhvaja</s>, <s>Akṣayamati</s> asked this matter for a reason:

body.text: kenā jinaputra hetunā ucyate hi avalokiteśvaraḥ // Saddhp_24.1 //
body.translated_text: "By what cause, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, is he called <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>?" || Saddhp 24.1 ||

children.text: atha sa diśatā vilokiyā praṇidhīsāgaru akṣayomati /
children.translated_text: Then the Seer, <s>Citradhvaja</s>, possessing an ocean of vows, addressed <s>Akṣayamati</s>:

children.text: citradhvajo 'dhyabhāṣata śṛṇu caryāmavalokiteśvare // Saddhp_24.2 //
children.translated_text: "Listen to the conduct of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! || Saddhp 24.2 ||

children.text: kalpaśata nekakoṭyacintiyā bahubuddhāna sahasrakoṭibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, countless <s>koṭis</s>, inconceivable — under thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of many <s>Buddhas</s>

children.text: praṇidhāna yathā viśodhitaṃ statha śṛṇvāhi mama pradeśataḥ // Saddhp_24.3 //
children.translated_text: was his vow purified — listen to me as I describe it in part. || Saddhp 24.3 ||

children.text: śravaṇo atha darśano 'pi ca anupūrvaṃ ca tathā anusmṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing and seeing, and gradually also mindful recollection [of his name] —

children.text: bhavatīha amogha prāṇināṃ sarvaduḥkhabhavaśokanāśakaḥ // Saddhp_24.4 //
children.translated_text: these are never fruitless for living beings; he is the destroyer of all suffering, existence, and sorrow. || Saddhp 24.4 ||

children.text: saci agnikhadāya pātayed ghatanārthāya praduṣṭamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one with a hostile mind were to cast [you] into a fire-pit for the purpose of killing —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ abhisikto iva agni śāmyati // Saddhp_24.5 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the fire is quenched as if sprinkled [with water]. || Saddhp 24.5 ||

children.text: saci sāgaradurgi pātayennāgamakarasurabhūta-ālaye /
children.translated_text: If one were cast into the perilous ocean, the abode of <s>nāgas</s>, <s>makaras</s>, and <s>asura</s>-beings —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ jalarāje na kadācisīdati // Saddhp_24.6 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, one never sinks in the king of waters. || Saddhp 24.6 ||

children.text: saci merutalātu pātayed ghatanārthāya praduṣṭamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one with a hostile mind were to hurl [you] from the peak of <s>Meru</s> for the purpose of killing —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ sūryabhūto va nabhe pratiṣṭhati // Saddhp_24.7 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, one remains suspended in the sky like the sun. || Saddhp 24.7 ||

children.text: vajrāmaya parvato yadi ghatanārthāya hi mūrdhni oṣaret /
children.translated_text: If an adamantine mountain were to fall on one's head for the purpose of killing —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ romakūpa na prabhonti hiṃsitum // Saddhp_24.8 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, not a hair-pore can they harm. || Saddhp 24.8 ||

children.text: saci śatrugaṇaiḥ parīvṛtaḥ śastrahastairvihiṃsacetasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were surrounded by a host of enemies, weapons in hand, with murderous intent —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ maitracitta tada bhonti tatkṣaṇam // Saddhp_24.9 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, their minds become friendly at that very instant. || Saddhp 24.9 ||

children.text: saci āghatane upasthito vadhyaghātanavaśaṃgato bhavet /
children.translated_text: If one were brought to the execution-ground, subject to the executioner's power —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ khaṇḍakhaṇḍa tada śastra gacchiyuḥ // Saddhp_24.10 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the swords would shatter into pieces! || Saddhp 24.10 ||

children.text: saci dārumayairayomayairhaḍinigaḍairiha baddhabandhanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were bound with fetters of wood and iron, shackled and chained —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ kṣiprameva vipaṭanti bandhanā // Saddhp_24.11 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the bonds are quickly sundered! || Saddhp 24.11 ||

children.text: mantrā bala vidya oṣadhī bhūta vetāla śarīranāśakā /
children.translated_text: Spells, powers, magical arts, and herbs, beings who destroy bodies — <s>bhūtas</s> and <s>vetālas</s> —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ tān gacchanti yataḥ pravartitāḥ // Saddhp_24.12 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they return to whence they came. || Saddhp 24.12 ||

children.text: saci ojaharaiḥ parīvṛto nāgayakṣasurabhūtarākṣasaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were surrounded by vitality-stealers — <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>bhūtas</s>, and <s>rākṣasas</s> —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ romakūpa na prabhonti hiṃsitum // Saddhp_24.13 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, not a hair-pore can they harm. || Saddhp 24.13 ||

children.text: saci vyālamṛgaiḥ parīvṛtastīkṣṇadaṃṣṭranakharairmahābhayaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were surrounded by fierce wild beasts with sharp fangs and claws, most fearsome —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ kṣipra gacchanti diśā anantataḥ // Saddhp_24.14 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they quickly flee to the boundless directions. || Saddhp 24.14 ||

children.text: saci dṛṣṭiviṣaiḥ parīvṛto jvalanārciśikhiduṣṭadāruṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: If one were surrounded by venomous serpents, with blazing flames and terrifying glares —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ kṣiprameva te bhonti nirviṣāḥ // Saddhp_24.15 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they quickly become venom-free. || Saddhp 24.15 ||

children.text: gambhīra savidyu niścarī meghavajrāśani vāriprasravāḥ /
children.translated_text: If a deep [cloud] comes forth with lightning, thunder, vajra-bolts, and torrents of rain —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ kṣiprameva praśamanti tatkṣaṇam // Saddhp_24.16 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, they quickly subside at that very instant. || Saddhp 24.16 ||

children.text: bahuduḥkhaśatairupadrutān sattva dṛṣṭva bahuduḥkhapīḍitān /
children.translated_text: Seeing beings afflicted by hundreds of sufferings, oppressed by many sorrows —

children.text: śubhajñānabalo vilokiyā tena trātaru gaje sadevake // Saddhp_24.17 //
children.translated_text: with the power of auspicious knowledge, that Seer becomes their savior in the world with its gods. || Saddhp 24.17 ||

children.text: ṛddhībalapāramiṃgato vipulajñāna upāyaśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the perfection of supernatural powers and vast wisdom, trained in skillful means,

children.text: sarvatra daśaddiśī jage sarvakṣetreṣu aśeṣa dṛśyate // Saddhp_24.18 //
children.translated_text: in all ten directions of the world, in all fields without remainder, he is seen. || Saddhp 24.18 ||

children.text: ye ca akṣaṇadurgatī bhayā narakatiryagyamasya śāsane /
children.translated_text: The fears of the unfavorable states and lower destinies — in the hells, in the animal realm, in <s>Yama</s>'s dominion,

children.text: jātījaravyādhipīḍitā anupūrvaṃ praśamanti prāṇinām // Saddhp_24.19 //
children.translated_text: and the afflictions of birth, old age, and disease — gradually subside for living beings [who remember him]. || Saddhp 24.19 ||'

body.text: atha khalu akṣamatirhṛṣṭatuṣṭamanā imā gāthā abhāṣata -
body.translated_text: Then <s>Akṣayamati</s>, delighted and satisfied in mind, spoke these verses:

children.text: śubhalocana maitralocanā prajñājñānaviśiṣṭalocanā /
children.translated_text: 'O one of auspicious eyes, of compassionate eyes, of eyes distinguished by wisdom and knowledge,

children.text: kṛpalocana śuddhalocanā premaṇīya sumukhā sulocanā // Saddhp_24.20 //
children.translated_text: of merciful eyes, of pure eyes — lovely one, beautiful-faced, beautiful-eyed! || Saddhp 24.20 ||

children.text: amalāmalanirmalaprabhā vitimira jñānadivākaraprabhā /
children.translated_text: Stainless, with immaculate radiance of purity, with darkness dispelled — the radiance of the sun of knowledge —

children.text: apahṛtānilajvalaprabhā pratapanto jagatī virocase // Saddhp_24.21 //
children.translated_text: having subdued the radiance of wind and fire, you shine, warming the world! || Saddhp 24.21 ||

children.text: kṛpasadguṇamaitragarjitā śubhaguṇa maitramanā mahāghanā /
children.translated_text: Your thunder is compassion, good qualities, and loving-kindness; your mind of loving-kindness and auspicious qualities is a great cloud;

children.text: kleśāgni śamesi prāṇināṃ dharmavarṣaṃ amṛtaṃ pravarṣasi // Saddhp_24.22 //
children.translated_text: you quench the fire of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) for living beings, and you rain the <s>Dharma</s>-rain of the deathless! || Saddhp 24.22 ||

children.text: kalahe ca vivādavigrahe narasaṃgrāmagate mahābhaye /
children.translated_text: In quarrels, disputes, and conflicts, in fearsome battles and great dangers —

children.text: smarato avalokiteśvaraṃ praśameyā arisaṃgha pāpakā // Saddhp_24.23 //
children.translated_text: by remembering <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the evil host of enemies is pacified. || Saddhp 24.23 ||

children.text: meghasvara dundubhisvaro jaladharagarjita brahmasusvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: His voice is like a cloud, a drum, like the rumbling of the ocean, like the sweet voice of <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: svaramaṇḍalapāramiṃgataḥ smaraṇīyo avalokiteśvaraḥ // Saddhp_24.24 //
children.translated_text: having gone to the perfection of all tones of voice — <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is to be remembered! || Saddhp 24.24 ||

children.text: smarathā smarathā sa kāṅkṣathā śuddhasattvaṃ avalokiteśvaram /
children.translated_text: Remember! Remember! And do not doubt the pure being <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>!

children.text: maraṇe vyasane upadrave trāṇu bhoti śaraṇaṃ parāyaṇam // Saddhp_24.25 //
children.translated_text: In death, in calamity, in misfortune, he becomes a refuge, a shelter, a final resort! || Saddhp 24.25 ||

children.text: sarvaguṇasya pāramiṃgataḥ sarvasattvakṛpamaitralocano /
children.translated_text: Having gone to the perfection of all qualities, gazing with eyes of compassion and loving-kindness upon all beings,

children.text: guṇabhūta mahāguṇodadhī vandanīyo avalokiteśvaraḥ // Saddhp_24.26 //
children.translated_text: an ocean of great qualities, a treasury of virtues — <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> is to be worshipped! || Saddhp 24.26 ||

children.text: yo 'sau anukampako jage buddha bheṣyati anāgate 'dhvani /
children.translated_text: He who has compassion for the world, who shall become a <s>Buddha</s> in the future age,

children.text: sarvaduḥkhabhayaśokanāśakaṃ praṇamāmī avalokiteśvaram // Saddhp_24.27 //
children.translated_text: the destroyer of all suffering, fear, and sorrow — I bow down to <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>! || Saddhp 24.27 ||

children.text: lokeśvara rājanāyako bhikṣudharmākaru lokapūjito /
children.translated_text: Lord of the World, king and guide, storehouse of the monks' <s>Dharma</s>, worshipped by the world,

children.text: bahukalpaśatāṃścaritva ca prāptu bodhi virajāṃ anuttarām // Saddhp_24.28 //
children.translated_text: having practiced for hundreds of <s>kalpas</s>, he has attained the stainless, unsurpassed awakening. || Saddhp 24.28 ||

children.text: sthita dakṣiṇavāmatastathā vījayanta amitābhanāyakam /
children.translated_text: Standing at the right and left [of <s>Amitābha</s>], fanning the Guide <s>Amitābha</s>,

children.text: māyopamatā samādhinā sarvakṣetre jina gatva pūjiṣu // Saddhp_24.29 //
children.translated_text: through illusion-like <s>samādhis</s>, he has gone to all fields and worshipped the <s>Jinas</s>. || Saddhp 24.29 ||

body.text: diśi paścimataḥ sukhākarā lokadhātu virajā sukhāvatī /
body.translated_text: In the western direction, the world-system called the producer of bliss — the stainless <s>Sukhāvatī</s>,

body.text: yatra eṣa amitābhanāyakaḥ saṃprati tiṣṭhati sattvasārathiḥ // Saddhp_24.30 //
body.translated_text: where that Guide <s>Amitābha</s> presently abides, the Charioteer of beings — || Saddhp 24.30 ||

children.text: na ca istriṇa tatra saṃbhavo nāpi ca maithunadharma sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: there is no birth of women there, nor sexual intercourse of any kind;

children.text: upapāduka te jinorasāḥ padmagarbheṣu niṣaṇṇa nirmalāḥ // Saddhp_24.31 //
children.translated_text: spontaneously born, those sons of the <s>Jina</s>, immaculate, sit in lotus calyxes. || Saddhp 24.31 ||

children.text: so caiva amitābhanāyakaḥ padmagarbhe viraje manorame /
children.translated_text: And that Guide <s>Amitābha</s> himself, in a stainless, delightful lotus-calyx,

children.text: siṃhāsani saṃniṣaṇṇako śālarajo va yathā virājate // Saddhp_24.32 //
children.translated_text: seated upon a lion-throne, shines like the king of <s>Śāla</s>-trees. || Saddhp 24.32 ||

children.text: so 'pi tathā lokanāyako yasya nāsti tribhavesmi sādṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: That Lord of the World too, who has no equal in the triple world —

children.text: yanme puṇya stavitva saṃcitaṃ kṣipra bhomi yatha tvaṃ narottama // Saddhp_24.33 //
children.translated_text: whatever merit I have accumulated by praising [you], may I quickly become like you, O Best of Men! || Saddhp 24.33 ||'

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: atha khalu dharaṇiṃdharo bodhisattvo mahāsattva utthāyāsanādekāṃsamuttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃstenāñjaliṃ praṇāmya bhagavantametadavocat - na te bhagavan sattvāḥ avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgatā bhaviṣyanti, ye 'valokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyemaṃ dharmaparyāyaparivartaṃ śroṣyanti avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya vikurvānirdeśaṃ samantamukhaparivartaṃ nāma avalokiteśvarasya bodhisattvasya vikurvaṇaprātihāryam ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Dharaṇiṃdhara</s> (Earth-Holder), having risen from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, placed his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Blessed One, said this to the Blessed One: 'Those beings who will hear this chapter of the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — the exposition of the miraculous transformations of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the chapter named <s>Samantamukha</s> (Universal Gate), the display of miraculous transformations of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Avalokiteśvara</s> — those beings, Blessed One, will not be endowed with inferior wholesome roots!'

body.text: asmin khalu punaḥ samantamukhaparivarte bhagavatā nirdeśyamāne tasyāḥ parṣadaścaturaśītināṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāmasamasamāyāmanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittānyutpannānyabhūvan ||
body.translated_text: While this <s>Samantamukha</s> chapter was being expounded by the Blessed One, in that assembly, eighty-four thousand beings generated the mind of supreme, incomparable, perfect awakening.

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye samantamukhaparivarto nāmāvalokiteśvaravikurvaṇanirdeśaścaturviśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, named the <s>Samantamukha</s> chapter, the exposition of the miraculous transformations of <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_25: śubhavyūharājapūrvayogaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 25: The Chapter on the Former Connection of King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>.

body.text:
atha khalu bhagavān sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇamāmantrayāmāsa - bhūtapūrvaṃ kulaputra atīte 'dhvanyasaṃkhyeyaiḥ kalpairasaṃkhyeyatarairyadāsīt | tena kālena tena samayena jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijño nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān priyadarśane kalpe vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitāyāṃ lokadhātau | tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputrā jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasya pravacane śubhavyūho nāma rājābhūt | tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputrā rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasya vimaladattā nāma bhāryābhūt | tasya khalu punaḥ kulaputrā rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasya dvau putrāvabhūtām - eko vimalagarbho nāma, dvitīyo vimalanetro nāma | tau ca dvau dārakāvṛddhimantau cābhūtām, prajñāvantau ca puṇyavantau ca jñānavantau ca bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ ca abhiyuktāvabhūtām | tadyathā - dānapāramitāyāmabhiyuktāvabhūtām, śīlapāramitāyāṃ kṣāntipāramitāyāṃ vīryapāramitāyāṃ dhyānapāramitāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāmupāyakauśalyapāramitāyāṃ maitryāṃ karuṇāyāṃ muditāyāmupekṣāyāṃ yāvat saptatriṃśatsu bodhipakṣikeṣu dharmeṣu | sarvatra pāraṃgatāvabhūtām, vimalasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatau, nakṣatrarājādityasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatau, vimalanirbhāsasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatau, vimalabhāsasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatau, alaṃkāraśubhasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatau, mahātejogarbhasya samādheḥ pāraṃgatāvabhūtām | sa ca bhagavāṃstena kālena tena samayena imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayāmāsa teṣāṃ sattvānāmanukampāyai, tasya ca rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasyānukampāyai | atha khalu kulaputrā vimalagarbho dārako vimalanetraśca dārako yena svamātā janayitrī, tenopasaṃkrāmatām | upasaṃkramya daśanakhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya janayitrīmetadavocatām ehyamba gamiṣyāvastasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśam taṃ bhagavantaṃ jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ darśanāya vandanāya
paryupāsanāya | tatkasya hetoḥ? eṣa hyamba sa bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sadevakasya lokasya purataḥ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ visteraṇa saṃprakāśayati, taṃ śravaṇāya gamiṣyāvaḥ | evamukte kulaputrā vimaladattā rājabhāryā vimalagarbhaṃ dārakaṃ vimalanetraṃ ca dārakametadavocat - eṣa khalu kulaputrau yuvayoḥ pitā rājā śubhavyūho brāhmaṇeṣvabhiprasannaḥ | tasmānna lapsyatha taṃ tathāgataṃ darśanāyābhigantum | atha khalu kulaputrā vimalagarbho dārako vimalanetraśca dārako daśanakhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya tāṃ svamātaraṃ janayitrīmetadavocatām - mithyādṛṣṭikule 'sminnāvāṃ jātau? āvāṃ punardharmarājaputrāviti | atha khalu kulaputrā vimaladattā rājabhāryā tau dvau dārakāvetadavocat - sādhu sādhu kulaputrau
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>: 'Once upon a time, sons of good family, in a former age, in incalculable <s>kalpas</s>, more incalculable still — at that time, in that era, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s> (Superknowledge Blossoming like the Constellation King with the Beautiful Voice of Thundering Cloud-Sound), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in the <s>kalpa</s> <s>Priyadarśana</s> (Pleasing to See), in the world-system <s>Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitā</s>. Now, sons of good family, in the dispensation of that <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, there was a king named <s>Śubhavyūha</s> (Splendid Array). That king <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, sons of good family, had a wife named <s>Vimaladattā</s>. And that king <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, sons of good family, had two sons — one named <s>Vimalagarbha</s> (Womb of Purity), the second named <s>Vimalanetra</s> (Pure Eye). Those two boys were mighty, wise, meritorious, knowledgeable, and devoted to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-career — devoted to the <s>pāramitā</s> of giving, the <s>pāramitā</s> of morality, the <s>pāramitā</s> of patience, the <s>pāramitā</s> of vigor, the <s>pāramitā</s> of meditation, the <s>pāramitā</s> of wisdom, the <s>pāramitā</s> of skillful means, in loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, equanimity, and up to the thirty-seven factors of awakening. They had gone beyond in all, having reached the other shore of the <s>Vimala</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Purity), the <s>Nakṣatrarājāditya</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Constellation King Sun), the <s>Vimalanirbhāsa</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Pure Radiance), the <s>Vimalabhāsa</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Pure Splendor), the <s>Alaṃkāraśubha</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Ornament of Beauty), and the <s>Mahātejogarbha</s>-<s>samādhi</s> (Great Splendor-Womb). At that time, in that era, that Blessed One was teaching this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>Dharma</s>-discourse out of compassion for those beings and for that king <s>Śubhavyūha</s>. Then, sons of good family, the boy <s>Vimalagarbha</s> and the boy <s>Vimalanetra</s> approached their mother. Having approached, with palms joined with all ten fingers, they said this to their mother: 'Come, mother! Let us go to the presence of that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, to see, salute, and attend upon that Blessed One. For what reason? For, mother, that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, is extensively illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> before the world with its gods. Let us go to hear it!' When this was said, sons of good family, the queen <s>Vimaladattā</s> said this to the boys <s>Vimalagarbha</s> and <s>Vimalanetra</s>: 'Your father, sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, is devoted to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. Therefore you will not obtain permission to go for the sight of that <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then, sons of good family, the boy <s>Vimalagarbha</s> and the boy <s>Vimalanetra</s>, with palms joined with all ten fingers, said this to their mother: 'Are we born in a family of wrong views? Yet we are sons of the <s>Dharma</s>-King!' Then, sons of good family, the queen <s>Vimaladattā</s> said this to those two boys: 'Excellent, excellent, sons of good family!

body.text: | yuvāṃ tasya svapitū rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasyānukampāyai kiṃcideva prātihāryaṃ saṃdarśayatam | apyeva nāma yuvayorantike prasādaṃ kuryāt | prasannacittaśca asmākamanujānīyāt tasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhamabhigantum ||
body.translated_text: Show some miracle to your father, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, out of compassion for him. Perhaps he may generate faith in your presence. And with a trusting mind, may he give us permission to go to that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One.'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrā vimalagarbho dārako vimalanetraśca dārakastasyāṃ velāyāṃ saptatālamātraṃ vaihāyasamabhyudgamya tasya pitū rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasyānukampāyai buddhānujñātāni yamakāni prātihāryāṇyakurutām | tau tatraivāntarīkṣe gatau śayyāmakalpayatām | tatraivāntarīkṣe caṃkramataḥ, tatraivāntarīkṣe rajo vyadhunītām, tatraivāntarīkṣe 'dhaḥkāyādvāridhārāṃ pramumocatuḥ, ūrdhvakāyādagniskandhaṃ prajvālayataḥ sma | ūrdhvakāyādvāridhārāṃ pramumocatuḥ, adhaḥkāyādagniskandhaṃ prajvālayataḥ sma | tau tasminnevākāśe mahāntau bhūtvā khuḍḍakau bhavataḥ, khuḍḍakau bhūtvā mahāntau bhavataḥ | tasminnevāntarīkṣe 'ntardhāyataḥ | pṛthivyāmunmajjataḥ | pṛthivyāmunmajjitvā ākāśaunmajjataḥ | iyadbhiḥ khalu punaḥ kulaputrā ṛddhiprātihāryaistābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dārakābhyāṃ sa śubhavyūho rājā svapitā vinītaḥ | atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rājā śubhavyūhastayordārakayostamṛddhiprātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto daśanakhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya tau dārakāvetadavocat - ko yuvayoḥ kulaputrau śāstā, kasya vā yuvāṃ śiṣyāviti? atha khalu kulaputrāstau dvau dārakau taṃ rājānaṃ śubhavyūhametadavocat - eṣa sa mahārāja bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati ratnamaye bodhivṛkṣamūle dharmāsanopaviṣṭaḥ | sadevakasya lokasya purataḥ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati | sa āvayorbhagavān śāstā | tasyāvāṃ mahārāja śiṣyau | atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rājā śubhavyūhastau dārakāvetadavocat - paśyāmo vayaṃ kulaputrau taṃ yuvayoḥ śāstāram | gamiṣyāmo vayaṃ tasya bhagavataḥ sakāśam ||
body.translated_text: Then, sons of good family, the boy <s>Vimalagarbha</s> and the boy <s>Vimalanetra</s>, at that moment, rose up into the sky to a height of seven palm-trees, and out of compassion for their father, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, performed miraculous feats of paired displays as authorized by the <s>Buddha</s>. While up there in the sky, they reclined; while up there in the sky, they walked about; while up there in the sky, they shook off the dust; while up there in the sky, from the lower half of their bodies they released a stream of water, and from the upper half they blazed forth a mass of fire; from the upper half of their bodies they released a stream of water, and from the lower half they blazed forth a mass of fire. In that very sky, having become large they became small; having become small they became large. In that very sky, they disappeared; on the earth they emerged; having emerged on the earth, they emerged in the sky. With these miraculous feats, sons of good family, those two boys converted their father, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>. Then, sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, having seen those miraculous feats of those two boys, at that moment was satisfied, elated, delighted, joyful, and filled with gladness. With palms joined with all ten fingers, he said this to those two boys: 'Who is your teacher, sons of good family? Whose disciples are you?' Then, sons of good family, those two boys said this to King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>: 'This, O great king, is that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, who abides, sustains, and endures, seated on the <s>Dharma</s>-seat at the foot of a jeweled <s>Bodhi</s>-tree, extensively illuminating the <s>Dharma</s>-discourse called the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> before the world with its gods. He, O great king, is our teacher. We are his disciples.' Then, sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> said this to those two boys: 'Let us see your teacher, sons of good family! We shall go to the presence of that Blessed One.'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāstau dvau dārakau tato 'ntarīkṣādavatīrya yena svamātā janayitrī tenopasaṃkrāmatām | upasaṃkramya daśanakhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya svamātaraṃ janayitrīmetadavocatām - eṣa āvābhyāmamba vinītaḥ svapitā anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau | kṛtamāvābhyāṃ pituḥ śāstṛkṛtyam | tadidānīmutsraṣṭumarhasi | āvāṃ tasya bhagavataḥ sakāśe pravrajiṣyāva iti ||
body.translated_text: Then, sons of good family, those two boys descended from the sky and approached their mother. Having approached, with palms joined with all ten fingers, they said this to their mother: 'Our own father has been converted by us in supreme perfect awakening! The work of a teacher has been done by us for our father. Therefore now, please give us permission. We shall go forth into the renunciant life in the presence of that Blessed One.'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrā vimalagarbho dārako vimalanetraśca dārakastasyāṃ velāyāṃ svamātaraṃ janayitrīṃ gāthābhyāmadhyabhāṣatām -
body.translated_text: Then, sons of good family, the boy <s>Vimalagarbha</s> and the boy <s>Vimalanetra</s>, at that moment, addressed their mother with these two verses:

children.text: anujānīhyāvayoramba pravrajyāmanagārikām /
children.translated_text: 'Give us permission, mother, for the homeless renunciant life;

children.text: āvāṃ vai pravrajiṣyāvo durlabho hi tathāgataḥ // Saddhp_25.1 //
children.translated_text: we shall indeed go forth, for the <s>Tathāgata</s> is rare to encounter! || <s>Saddhp</s> 25.1 ||

children.text: audumbaraṃ yathā puṣpaṃ sudurlabhataro jinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Like the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree, even more rare is the <s>Jina</s>;

children.text: utsṛjya pravrajiṣyāvo durlabhā kṣaṇasaṃpadā // Saddhp_25.2 //
children.translated_text: having let go, we shall go forth — rare is the attainment of the right moment! || <s>Saddhp</s> 25.2 ||'

body.text: vimaladattā rājabhāryā āha -
body.translated_text: The queen <s>Vimaladattā</s> said:

children.text: utsṛjāmi yuvāmadya gacchathā sādhu dārakau /
children.translated_text: 'I release you both today — go in goodness, dear boys!

children.text: vayaṃ pi pravrajiṣyāmo durlabho hi tathāgataḥ // Saddhp_25.3 //
children.translated_text: We too shall go forth, for the <s>Tathāgata</s> is rare to encounter! || <s>Saddhp</s> 25.3 ||'

body.text: iti ||
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāstau dvau dārakāvime gāthe bhāṣitvā tau mātāpitarāvetadavocatām - sādhu amba tāta eta | vayaṃ sarve sahitā bhūtvā gamiṣyāmastasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśam | upasaṃkramiṣyāmastaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāya vandanāya paryupāsanāya dharmaśravaṇāya | tatkasya hetoḥ? durlabho hyamba tāta buddhotpādaḥ, udumbarapuṣpasadṛśo mahārṇavyugacchidrakūrmagrīvāpraveśavat | durlabhaprādurbhāvā amba buddhā bhagavantaḥ | tasmāttarhi amba tāta paramapuṇyopastabdhā vayamīdṛśe pravacane upapannāḥ | tat sādhu amba tāta utsṛjadhvam | āvāṃ gamiṣyāvaḥ | tasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśe pravrajiṣyāvaḥ | durlabhaṃ hi amba tāta tathāgatānāṃ darśanam | durlabho hyadya kālaḥ | īdṛśo dharmarājā | paramadurlabhedṛśī kṣaṇasaṃpat ||
body.translated_text: Then, sons of good family, those two boys, having spoken these verses, said this to both their parents: 'Come then, mother, father! Let us all go together to the presence of that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. We shall approach that Blessed One for seeing, saluting, and attending upon him, and for hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. For what reason? For, mother, father, rare is the arising of a <s>Buddha</s> — like the flower of the <s>udumbara</s> tree, like the entry of a turtle's neck into the hole of a yoke floating in the great ocean! Rare indeed is the appearance of <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones, mother! Therefore, mother, father, sustained by supreme merit, we have been reborn in such a dispensation. Therefore please, mother, father, give us permission! We shall go forth in the presence of that Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One. For rare, mother, father, is the sight of <s>Tathāgatas</s>. Rare indeed is the present time. Such a <s>Dharma</s>-King [is rare]. Supremely rare is such an attainment of the right moment!'

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ samayena tasya rājñaḥ śūbhavyūhasya antaḥpurāccaturaśītirantaḥpurikāsahasrāṇi asya saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya bhājanabhutānyabhūvan | vimalanetraśca dārako 'smin dharmaparyāye caritāvī | vimalagarbhaśca dārako bahukalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāṇi sarvasattvapāpajahane samādhau carito 'bhūt kimiti sarvasattvāḥ sarvapāpaṃ jaheyuriti | sā ca tayordārakayormātā vimaladattā rājabhāryā sarvabuddhasaṃgītiṃ sarvabuddhadharmaguhyasthānāni ca saṃjānīte sma | atha khalu kulaputrā rājā śubhavyūhastābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dārakābhyāṃ tathāgataśāsane vinītaḥ, avatāritaśca, paripācitaśca sarvasvajanaparivāraḥ | sā ca vimaladattā rājabhāryā sarvasvajanaparivārā tau ca dvau dārakau rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasya putrau dvācatvāriṃśadbhiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ sāntapurau sāmātyau sarve sahitāḥ samagrāḥ yena bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ, tenopasaṃkrāman | upasaṃkramya tasya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya taṃ bhagavantaṃ triṣkṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte tasthuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, O sons of good family, at that time, eighty-four thousand women of King <s>Śubhavyūha's</s> inner palace became worthy vessels of this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Law). And the boy <s>Vimalanetra</s> became accomplished in this <s>dharma</s>-discourse. And the boy <s>Vimalagarbha</s> practiced the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Abandonment of All Evil by All Beings' for many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>, [thinking:] 'How may all beings abandon all evil?' And the mother of those two boys, <s>Vimaladattā</s>, the queen, came to know the collected discourses of all <s>Buddhas</s> and the secret repositories of the <s>dharma</s> of all <s>Buddhas</s>. Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> was disciplined in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s> by those two boys, and was brought down [from his wrong views], and was matured, together with all his family and retinue. And <s>Vimaladattā</s>, the queen, together with all her family and retinue, and those two boys, the sons of King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, together with forty-two thousand beings, including the inner palace and the ministers — all of them together, as one body — approached the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s> (He Whose Superknowledge is Adorned with the King of Constellations, Having the Sweet Voice of Thundering Clouds). Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and stood to one side.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho rājānaṃ śubhavyūhaṃ saparivāramupasaṃkrāntaṃ viditvā dhārmyā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati | atha khalu kulaputrā rājā śubhavyūhastena bhagavatā dhārmyā kathayā sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca saṃdarśitaḥ samādāpitaḥ samuttejitaḥ
body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, having perceived that King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> with his retinue had approached, instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, having been well and thoroughly instructed, encouraged, and inspired by the Blessed One with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> —

body.text: saṃpraharṣitastasyāṃ velāyāṃ tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajātaḥ kanīyaso bhrātuḥ paṭṭaṃ baddhvā rājye pratiṣṭhāpya saputrasvajanaparivāraḥ, sā ca vimaladattā rājabhāryā sarvastrīgaṇaparivārā, tau ca dvau dārakau sārdhaṃ tairdvācatvāriṃśadbhiḥ prāṇisahasraiḥ, sarve sahitāḥ samagrāstasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pravacane śraddhayā agārādanagārikāṃ pravrajitāḥ | pravrajitvā ca rājā śubhavyūhaḥ saparivāraścaturaśītivarṣasahasrāṇyabhiyukto vijahāra imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ cintayan bhāvayan paryavadāpayan | atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rājā śubhavyūhasteṣāṃ caturaśītīnāṃ varṣasahasrāṇāmatyayena sarvaguṇālaṃkāravyūhaṃ nāma samādhiṃ pratilabhate sma | sahapratilabdhāccāsya samādheḥ, atha tāvadeva saptatālamātraṃ vaihāyasamabhyudgacchati sma ||
body.translated_text: — was gladdened. At that time, being satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with happiness and gladness, he tied the royal turban-cloth upon his younger brother, establishing him in the kingdom; and together with his sons and his own family and retinue, and <s>Vimaladattā</s> the queen together with all her company of women, and those two boys together with those forty-two thousand beings — all of them together, as one body — went forth from home into homelessness in the teaching of the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, with faith. And having gone forth, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> with his retinue dwelt for eighty-four thousand years, devoted to contemplating, cultivating, and mastering this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>. Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, after the passage of those eighty-four thousand years, attained the <s>samādhi</s> called 'Array of All Meritorious Qualities' (<s>Sarvaguṇālaṃkāravyūha</s>). And as soon as he attained that <s>samādhi</s>, he immediately rose up into the air to the height of seven palm trees.

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rājāḥ śubhavyūho gaganatale sthitastaṃ bhagavantaṃ jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadavocat - imau bhagavan mama putrau śāstārau bhavataḥ | yadahamābhyāmṛddhiprātihāryeṇa tasmānmahato dṛṣṭigatādvinivartitaḥ, tathāgataśāsane ca pratiṣṭhapitaḥ, paripācitaśca avatāritaśca, tathāgatadarśanāya ca saṃcoditaḥ | kalyāṇamitrau bhagavan mama tau dvau dārakau putrarūpeṇa mama gṛha upapannau, yaduta pūrvakuśalamūlasmaraṇārtham ||
body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, standing in the sky, said this to the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: 'O Blessed One, these two sons of mine are my teachers! For I was turned away from that great [thicket of] wrong views by means of their display of miraculous powers, and was established in the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and was matured and brought down [from error], and was urged to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. O Blessed One, these two boys are my spiritual friends (<s>kalyāṇamitra</s>) who were born in the form of sons in my house — for the purpose of recalling my former roots of merit.'

body.text: evamukte bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhastaṃ rājānaṃ śubhavyūhametadavocat - evametanmahārāja, evametad yathā vadasi | avaropitakuśalamūlānāṃ hi mahārāja kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ ca sarveṣu bhavagaticyutyupapattyāyataneṣūpapannānāṃ sulabhāni bhavanti kalyāṇamitrāṇi, yāni śāstṛkṛtyena pratyupasthitāni bhavanti, yānyanuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau śāsakānyavatārakāṇi paripācakāni bhavanti | udārametanmahārāja sthānaṃ yaduta kalyāṇamitraparigrahastathāgatadarśanasamādāpakaḥ | paśyasi tvaṃ mahārāja etau dvau dārakau? āha - paśyāmi bhagavan, paśyāmi sugata | bhagavānāha - etau khalu punarmahārāja kulaputrau pañcaṣṭīnāṃ gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānḥṃ tathḥgatḥnḥmarhatḥṃ samyaksaṃbuddhḥnḥmantike pūjḥṃ kariṣyataḥ, imaṃ ca saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyḥyaṃ dhḥrayiṣyataḥ sattvḥnḥmanukampḥyai, mithyḥdṛṣṭīnḥṃ ca sattvḥnḥṃ samyagdṛṣṭaye vīryasaṃjananḥrtham ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, said this to King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>: 'It is so, great king, it is so, as you say. For, great king, sons of good family and daughters of good family who have planted roots of merit — wherever they are born among the various courses of existence, departure, and rebirth — for them, spiritual friends are easily found, who stand present performing the function of a teacher, who instruct, bring down, and mature [beings] in the supreme, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). This is a sublime matter, great king — namely, the association with spiritual friends who urge one to see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Do you see, great king, these two boys?' He said: 'I see them, Blessed One; I see them, Well-Gone One.' The Blessed One said: 'These two sons of good family, great king, will make offerings in the presence of <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones as numerous as the sands of sixty-five <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, and will uphold this <s>dharma</s>-discourse, the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, out of compassion for beings and for the purpose of generating vigor in beings of wrong views [so that they may attain] right views.'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rājā śubhavyūhastato gaganatalādavatīrya daśanakhamañjaliṃ pragṛhya taṃ bhagavantaṃ jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadavocat - tatsādhu bhagavan | nirdiśatu tathāgataḥ - kīdṛśena jñānena samanvāgatastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho yena mūrdhni uṣṇīṣo vibhāti, vimalanetraśca bhagavān, bhruvormadhye corṇā vibhāti śaśiśaṅkhapāṇḍarābhā, sā ca samasahitā dantāvalī vadanāntare virājati, bimboṣṭhaśca bhagavāṃścārunetraśca sugataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, having descended from the sky, and having joined his palms with all ten nails [touching], said this to the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One: 'Excellent, Blessed One! May the <s>Tathāgata</s> declare — with what kind of knowledge is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One endowed, that the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) shines upon his head, and the Blessed One has pure eyes, and between his eyebrows the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft of hair) shines, radiant as the moon and conch-shell, and that even, well-arranged row of teeth gleams within his mouth, and the Blessed One has <s>bimba</s>-red lips, and the Well-Gone One has beautiful eyes!'

body.text: atha khalu kulaputrāḥ sa rāja śubhavyūha iyadbhirguṇaistaṃ bhagavantaṃ jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhamabhiṣṭutya anyaiśca guṇakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraistaṃ bhagavantamabhiṣṭutya tasyāṃ velāyāṃ taṃ bhagavantaṃ jaladharagarjitabhoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñaṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadavocat - āścaryaṃ bhagavan yāvanmahārthamidaṃ tathāgataśāsanam, acintyaguṇasamanvāgataśca tathāgatapravedito dharmavinayaḥ, yāvat suprajñaptā ca tathāgataśikṣā | adyāgreṇa vayaṃ bhagavanna bhūyaścittasya vaśagā bhaviṣyāmaḥ, na bhūyo mithyādṛṣṭervaśagā bhaviṣyāmaḥ, na bhūyaḥ krodhasya vaśagā bhaviṣyāmaḥ, na bhūyaḥ pāpakānāṃ cittotpādānāṃ vaśagā bhaviṣyāmaḥ | ebhirahaṃ bhagavan iyadbhirakuśalaidharmaiḥ samanvāgato necchāmi bhagavato 'ntikamupasaṃkramitum | sa tasya bhagavato jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrajasaṃkusumitābhijñasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasābhivandya antarīkṣagata evāsthāt ||
body.translated_text: Then, O sons of good family, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, having praised the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, with these many qualities, and having further praised that Blessed One with many hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of qualities, at that time said this to the Blessed One: 'Wondrous, O Blessed One, how supremely meaningful is this teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! And endowed with inconceivable qualities is the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and how well-established is the training of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! From this day forward, O Blessed One, we shall no longer be subject to the power of the mind; we shall no longer be subject to the power of wrong views; we shall no longer be subject to the power of anger; we shall no longer be subject to the power of evil mental intentions. O Blessed One, I who am endowed with these many unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> do not wish to approach close to the Blessed One.' He bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, and remained standing in the sky.

body.text: atha khalu sa rājā śubhavyūhaḥ sā ca vimaladattā rājabhāryā śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ bhagavata uparyantarīkṣe 'kṣaipsīt | samanantarakṣiptaśca sa muktāhārastasya bhagavato mūrdhni muktāhāraḥ kūṭāgāraḥ saṃsthito 'bhūccaturasraścatuḥsthūṇaḥ samabhāgaḥ suvibhakto darśanīyaḥ | tasmiṃśca kūṭāgāre paryaṅkaḥ prādurbhūto 'nekadūṣyaśatasahasrasaṃstṛtaḥ | tasmiṃśca paryaṅke tathāgatavigrahaḥ paryaṅkabaddhaṃ saṃdṛśyate sma | atha khalu rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasyaitadabhavat - mahānubhāvamidaṃ buddhajñānam, acintyaguṇasamanvāgataśca tathāgataḥ | yatra hi nāma ayaṃ tathāgatavigrahaḥ kūṭāgāramadhyagataḥ saṃdṛśyate prāsādiko darśanīyaḥ paramaśubhavarṇapuṣkaratayā samanvāgataḥ ||
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> and <s>Vimaladattā</s> the queen cast upward into the sky above the Blessed One a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces]. And as soon as that pearl necklace was cast, it stood above the Blessed One as a pavilion (<s>kūṭāgāra</s>) — four-cornered, with four pillars, well-proportioned, beautifully divided, and pleasant to behold. And in that pavilion there appeared a couch spread with many hundreds of thousands of coverings. And on that couch, the image of a <s>Tathāgata</s> was seen sitting cross-legged. Then the thought occurred to King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>: 'Of great power is the knowledge of a <s>Buddha</s>, and endowed with inconceivable qualities is the <s>Tathāgata</s> — since this image of a <s>Tathāgata</s> is seen within this pavilion, graceful, beautiful to behold, endowed with the supreme beauty of a golden lotus.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijñastathāgataścatasraḥ parṣadaḥ āmantrayate sma - paśyatha bhikṣavo yūyaṃ śubhavyūhaṃ rājānaṃ gaganatalasthaṃ siṃhanādaṃ nadantam? āhuḥ - paśyāmo bhagavan | bhagavānāha - eṣa khalu bhikṣavaḥ śubhavyūho rājā mama śāsane bhikṣubhāvaṃ kṛtvā śālendrarājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho loke bhaviṣyati, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavidanuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān vistīrṇavatyāṃ lokadhātau | abhyudgatarājo nāma sa kalpo bhaviṣyati | tasya khalu punarbhikṣavaḥ śālendrarājasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya aprameyo bodhisattvasaṃgho bhaviṣyati, aprameyaḥ śrāvakasaṃghaḥ | samā pāṇitalajātā ca vaidūryamayī sā vistīrṇavatī lokadhāturbhaviṣyati | evamacintyaḥ sa tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati | syāt khalu punaḥ kulaputrāḥ yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyaḥ sa tena kālena tena samayena śubhavyūho nāma rājābhūt? na khalu punaḥ kulaputrā yuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? ayameva sa padmaśrīrbodhisattvo mahāsattvastena kālena tena samayena śubhavyūho nāma rājābhut | syātkhalu punaḥ kulaputrā yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyā sā tena kālena tena samayena vimaladattā nāma
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Jaladharagarjitaghoṣasusvaranakṣatrarājasaṃkusumitābhijña</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, addressed the four assemblies: 'Do you see, O monks, King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> standing in the sky, uttering a lion's roar?' They said: 'We see him, Blessed One.' The Blessed One said: 'This King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, O monks, having attained the state of a monk in my teaching, will become in the future a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One in the world, named <s>Śālendrarāja</s> (King of the Foremost Śāla Trees), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Well-Gone One, a Knower of the World, an Unsurpassed One, a Tamer of Men to Be Tamed, a Teacher of Gods and Humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One, in the world-system called <s>Vistīrṇavatī</s> (the Extensive). That <s>kalpa</s> will be called <s>Abhyudgatarāja</s> (King of Exalted Ones). That <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One <s>Śālendrarāja</s> will have an immeasurable assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and an immeasurable assembly of <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers). That world-system <s>Vistīrṇavatī</s> will be level like the palm of a hand and made of <s>vaidūrya</s> (beryl). Thus inconceivable will that <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One be. Now, O sons of good family, perhaps you may have doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation [thinking:] 'Was that King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> at that time and on that occasion someone other [than a person known to you]?' You should not view it thus, O sons of good family. Why? This very <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Padmaśrī</s> was at that time and on that occasion the king named <s>Śubhavyūha</s>. And perhaps, O sons of good family, you may have doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation [thinking:] 'Was <s>Vimaladattā</s> at that time and on that occasion someone other —'

body.text:
rājabhāryābhūt? na khalu punaḥ kulaputrā yuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? ayaṃ sa vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitadhvajarājo nāma bodhisattvo mahāsattvastena kālena tena samayena vimaladattā nāma rājabhāryābhut | tasya rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasyānukampāyai teṣāṃ ca sattvānāṃ rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasya bhāryātvamabhyupagato 'bhūt | syātkhalu punaḥ kulaputrā yuṣmākaṃ kāṅkṣā vā vimatirvā vicikitsā vā - anyau tau tena kālena tena samayena dvau dārakāvabhūtām? na khalu punaḥ kulaputrā yuṣmābhirevaṃ draṣṭavyam | tatkasya hetoḥ? imau tau bhaiṣajyarājaśca bhaiṣajyasamundataśca tena kālena tena samayena tasya rājñaḥ śubhavyūhasya putrāvabhūtām | evamacintyaguṇasamanvāgatau kulaputrā bhaiṣajyarājo bhaiṣajyasamudgataśca bodhisattvau mahāsattvau, bahubuddhakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrāvaropitakuśalamūlau
etāvubhāvapi satpuruṣāvacintyadharmasamanvāgatau | ye ca etayoḥ satpuruṣayornāmadheyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, te sarve namaskaraṇīyā bhaviṣyanti sadevakena lokena ||
body.translated_text: was the queen? You should not see it thus, sons of good family. For what reason? This <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> named <s>Vairocanaraśmipratimaṇḍitadhvajarāja</s> was the queen named <s>Vimaladattā</s> at that time, on that occasion. He had assumed the role of wife to that King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> out of compassion for him and for those beings. Perhaps you might have doubt, hesitation, or uncertainty, sons of good family — thinking 'Were they some other two boys at that time, on that occasion?' You should not see it thus, sons of good family. For what reason? These very <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> and <s>Bhaiṣajyasamudgata</s> were the two sons of that King <s>Śubhavyūha</s> at that time, on that occasion. Endowed with such inconceivable virtues, sons of good family, are the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> <s>Bhaiṣajyarāja</s> and <s>Bhaiṣajyasamudgata</s> — having planted roots of merit under many <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of <s>Buddhas</s>. Both of these noble beings are endowed with inconceivable qualities. And those who will hold the names of these two noble beings — all of them will be worthy of salutation by the world with its gods.

body.text: asmin khalu punaḥ pūrvayogaparivarte bhāṣyamāṇe caturaśītīnāṃ prāṇisahasrāṇāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣurviśuddham ||
body.translated_text: While this chapter on the Former Deeds [of King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>] was being taught, eighty-four thousand beings purified the pure, stainless, immaculate Dharma-eye regarding all dharmas.

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye śubhavyūharājapūrvayogaparivarto nāma pañcaviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on the Former Deeds of King <s>Śubhavyūha</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_26: samantabhadrotsāhanaparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 26: The Chapter on <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s Encouragement.

body.text:
atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi gaṇanāsamatikrāntairbodhisattvairmahāsattvaiḥ sārdhaṃ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ prakampadbhiḥ kṣetrai pravarṣadbhiḥ padmaiḥ pravādyamānaistūryakoṭīnayutaśatasahasraiḥ, mahatā bodhisattvānubhāvena mahatyā bodhisattvavikurvayā mahatyā bodhisattvaddharyā mahata bodhisattvamāhātmyena mahatā bodhisattvasamāhitena mahatā bodhisattvatejasā jājvalyamānena, mahatā bodhisattvayānena, mahatā bodhisattvaprātihāryeṇa, mahadbhirdevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragarūḍakinnaramahoragamanuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ evamacintyairṛddhiprātihāryaiḥ samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattva imāṃ lokadhātuṃ saṃprāptaḥ | sa yenagṛdhrakūṭaḥ parvatarājaḥ yena ca bhagavāṃstenopasaṃkrāmat | upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya saptakṛtvaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavantametadavocat - ahaṃ bhagavaṃstasya bhagavato ratnatejobhyudgatarājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetrādihāgataḥ iha bhagavan sahāyāṃ lokadhātāvayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo deśyata iti | tamahaṃ śravaṇāyāgato bhagavataḥ śākyamunestathāgatasya sakāśam | amūni ca bhagavannetāvanti bodhisattvaśatasahasrāṇi imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīkaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ śravaṇāyāgatāni | tatsādhu bhagavān deśayatu tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha imaṃ saddharmapuṇḍārīkaṃ dharmaparyāyameṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ vistareṇa | evamukte bhagavān samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - uddhaṭitajñā hi kulaputra ete bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ | api tvayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo yaduta asaṃbhinnatathatā | te bodhisattvā āhuḥ - evametad bhagavan, evametatsugata | atha khalu yāstasyāṃ parṣadi bhikṣubhikṣuṇyupāsakopāsikāśca saṃnipatitāḥ, tāsāṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye pratiṣṭhāpanārthaṃ punarapi bhagavān samantabhadraṃ bodhisattvaṃ mahāsattvametadavocat - caturbhiḥ kulaputra dharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya mātṛgrāmasya ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo hastagato bhaviṣyati | katamaiścaturbhiḥ? yaduta buddhairbhagavadbhiradhiṣṭhito bhaviṣyati, avaropitakuśalamūlaśca bhaviṣyati, nirayarāśivyavasthitaśca bhaviṣyati, sarvasattvaparitrāṇārthamanuttarāyāṃ
samyaksaṃbodhau cittamutpādayiṣyati | ebhiḥ kulaputra caturbhirdharmaiḥ samanvāgatasya mātṛgrāmasya ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo hastagato bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>, from the eastern direction, together with <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> beyond all counting, surrounded and attended [by them], arrived with world-systems trembling, lotuses raining down, <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of hundreds of thousands of musical instruments sounding, with the great majesty of a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-transformation, with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-supernatural power, with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-grandeur, with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-concentration, with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-radiance blazing, with a great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-vehicle, and with great <s>Bodhisattva</s>-miraculous display, surrounded and attended by great gods, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Asuras</s>, <s>Garuḍas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, humans, and non-humans — thus, with such inconceivable miraculous displays, the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> arrived in this world-system. He approached the king of mountains <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> and the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him seven times, and said to the Blessed One: 'I, Blessed One, have come here from the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> of the Blessed One <s>Ratnatejobhyudgatarāja</s> (King Arisen in Jewel-Splendor), <s>Tathāgata</s>.
