Here in this <s>Sahā</s> world-system, Blessed One, this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> is being taught. I have come to hear it, in the presence of the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>. And these many hundreds of thousands of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, O Blessed One, have come to hear this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>. Please, may the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, teach this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> in detail to these <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>.' When this was said, the Blessed One said to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>: 'These <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> are indeed of keen understanding, O son of good family. Moreover, this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> is none other than undivided suchness.' Those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> said: 'So it is, Blessed One; so it is, <s>Sugata</s>.' Then the Blessed One, for the purpose of establishing those monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen assembled in that assembly in the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>, again addressed the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>: 'By four qualities endowed, O son of good family, will a woman have this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> in hand. Which four? She will be sustained by the <s>Buddhas</s>, Blessed Ones; she will have planted roots of merit; she will be established in the aggregate of determination; and she will generate the aspiration for supreme perfect awakening for the purpose of rescuing all beings. By these four qualities endowed, O son of good family, will a woman have this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> in hand.'

body.text: atha khalu samantabhadro bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantametadavocat - ahaṃ bhagavan paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ vartamānāyāmevaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ rakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi, svastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmi, daṇḍaparihāraṃ kariṣyāmi, viṣadūṣaṇaṃ kariṣyāmi, yathā na kaścitteṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmavatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ lapsyate | na māraḥ pāpīyānavatāraprekṣī avatāragaveṣī avatāraṃ lapsyate, na māraputrā na mārakāyikā devaputrā na mārakanyā na mārapārṣadyā yāvanna bhūyo māraparyutthito bhaviṣyati | na devaputrā na yakṣā na pretā na pūtanā na kṛtyā na vetālāstasya dharmabhāṇakasyāvatāraprekṣiṇo 'vatāragaveṣiṇo 'vatāraṃ lapsyante | ahaṃ bhagavaṃstasya dharmabhāṇakasya satatasamitaṃ nityakālaṃ rakṣāṃ
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> said to the Blessed One: 'I, Blessed One, in the final age, the final time, in the last five hundred years, will provide protection for such monks who are holders of <s>sūtras</s>. I will provide safety, protection from punishment, and neutralization of poison, so that no one seeking an opening, searching for an opportunity against those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, shall find an opportunity. Neither <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, seeking and searching for an opening, shall find an opening; nor <s>Māra</s>'s sons, nor <s>Mārakāyika</s> deities, nor <s>Māra</s>'s daughters, nor <s>Māra</s>'s retinue — none shall be any longer dominated by <s>Māra</s>. Neither deities, nor <s>Yakṣas</s>, nor hungry ghosts, nor <s>Pūtanas</s>, nor <s>Kṛtyās</s>, nor <s>Vetālas</s>, seeking and searching for an opening against that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, shall find an opening. I, Blessed One, will constantly and always provide protection for that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher.

body.text: kariṣyāmi | yadā ca sa dharmabhāṇako 'smin dharmaparyāye cintāyogamanuyuktaścaṃkramābhirūḍho bhaviṣyati, tadāhaṃ bhagavaṃstasya dharmabhāṇakasyāntike śvetaṣaḍdantaṃ gajarājamabhiruhya tasya dharmabhāṇakasya caṃkramakuṭīmupasaṃkramiṣyāmi bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛto 'sya dharmaparyāyasyārakṣāyai | yadā punastasya dharmabhāṇakasya asmin dharmaparyāye cintāyogamanuyuktasya sataḥ ito dharmaparyāyadantaśaḥ padavyañjanaṃ paribhraṣṭaṃ bhaviṣyati, tadāhaṃ tasmin śvetaṣaḍdante gajarāje 'bhiruhya tasya dharmabhāṇakasya saṃmukhamupadarśayitvā imaṃ dharmaparyāyamavikalaṃ pratyuccārayiṣyāmi | sa ca dharmabhāṇako mamātmabhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā imaṃ ca dharmaparyāyamavikalaṃ mamāntikācchrutvā tuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhūyasyā mātrayā asmin dharmaparyāye vīryamārapsyate, āttamanāḥ pramuditaḥ prītisaumanasyajāto bhūyasyā mātrayā asmin dharmaparyāye vīryamārapsyate, mama ca sahadarśanena samādhiṃ pratilapsyate, dhāraṇyāvartāṃ ca nāma dhāraṇīṃ pratilapsyate, koṭīśatasahasrāvartāṃ ca nāma dhāraṇīṃ pratilapsyate, sarvarutakauśalyāvartāṃ ca nāma dhāraṇīṃ pratilapsyate ||
body.translated_text: And when that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, engaged in the contemplative practice of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, ascends to walking meditation, then I, Blessed One, mounting a white six-tusked elephant-king, surrounded by a company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, will approach that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher's walking-meditation cell for the protection of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. And when that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, engaged in the contemplative practice of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, has forgotten even a single word or syllable of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, then I, mounted on that white six-tusked elephant-king, having shown myself face to face to that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, will recite this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in full to him. And that <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, having seen my bodily form and having heard this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in full from me, will be satisfied, uplifted, delighted, filled with joy and happiness, and will generate even greater vigor in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. Delighted and filled with joy and happiness, he will generate even greater vigor in this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse. And by seeing me, he will attain <s>samādhi</s>, and he will attain a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Dhāraṇyāvartā</s> (Revolution of <s>Dhāraṇī</s>), and he will attain a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Koṭīśatasahasrāvartā</s> (Revolution of a Hundred-Thousand <s>Koṭis</s>), and he will attain a <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Sarvarutakauśalyāvartā</s> (Revolution of Skill in All Sounds).'

body.text: ye ca bhagavan paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcāśatyāṃ bhikṣavo vā bhikṣūṇyo vā upāsakā vā upāsikā vā evaṃ sūtrāntadhārakā evaṃ sūtrāntalekhakā evaṃ sūtrāntamārgakā evaṃ sūtrāntavācakā ye paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāmasmin dharmaparyāye trisaptāhamekaviṃśatidivasāni caṃkramābhirūḍhā abhiyuktā bhaviṣyanti, teṣāmahaṃ sarvasattvapriyadarśanamātmabhāvaṃ saṃdarśayiṣyāmi | tameva śvetaṃ ṣaḍdantaṃ gajarājamabhiruhya bodhisattvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ ekaviṃśatime divase teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ caṃkramamāgamiṣyāmi | āgatya ca tān dharmabhāṇakān parisaṃharṣayiṣyāmi samādāpayiṣyāmi samuttejayiṣyāmi saṃpraharṣayiṣyāmi | dhāraṇīṃ caiṣāṃ dāsyāmi, yathā te dharmabhāṇakā na kenaciddharṣaṇīyā bhaviṣyanti | na caiṣāṃ manuṣyā vā amanuṣyā vā avatāraṃ lapsyante, na ca nāryo 'pasaṃhariaṣyanti | rakṣāṃ caiṣāṃ kariṣyāmi, svastyayanaṃ kariṣyāmi, daṇḍaparihāraṃ kariṣyāmi, viṣadūṣaṇaṃ kariṣyāmi | teṣāṃ vayaṃ bhagavan dharmabhāṇakānāmimāni dhāraṇīpadāni dāsyāmi | tāni bhagavan dhāraṇīpadāni | tadyathā -
body.translated_text: 'And those monks, nuns, laymen, or laywomen, O Blessed One, in the final age, the final time, in the last five hundred years, who are holders of such <s>sūtras</s>, writers of such <s>sūtras</s>, seekers of such <s>sūtras</s>, reciters of such <s>sūtras</s> — who, in the final age, the final time, in the last five hundred years, will be engaged in diligent practice of this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse, ascending to walking meditation for three times seven, that is twenty-one days — for them I will display my bodily form that is pleasing to all beings. Mounted on that very white six-tusked elephant-king, surrounded by a company of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, on the twenty-first day I will come to the walking-meditation ground of those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. Having come, I will rejoice with, encourage, inspire, and delight those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers. And I will give them <s>dhāraṇī</s>, so that those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers will not be assailable by anyone. Neither humans nor non-humans shall find an opening against them, nor shall women seduce them. I will provide them protection, safety, protection from punishment, and neutralization of poison. To those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, O Blessed One, we will give these <s>dhāraṇī</s>-syllables. O Blessed One, these are the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-syllables, namely:' —

body.text: adaṇḍe daṇḍapati daṇḍāvartani daṇḍakuśale daṇḍasudhāri sudhārapati buddhapaśyane sarvadhāraṇi āvartani saṃvartani saṃghaparīkṣite saṃghanirghātani dharmaparīkṣite sarvasattvarutakauśalyānugate siṃhavikrīḍite anuvarte vartani vartāli svāhā ||
body.translated_text: <s>adaṇḍe daṇḍapati daṇḍāvartani daṇḍakuśale daṇḍasudhāri sudhārapati buddhapaśyane sarvadhāraṇi āvartani saṃvartani saṃghaparīkṣite saṃghanirghātani dharmaparīkṣite sarvasattvarutakauśalyānugate siṃhavikrīḍite anuvarte vartani vartāli svāhā</s>.

body.text: imāni tāni bhagavan dhāraṇīpadāni yasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya śrotrendriyasyāvabhāsamāgamiṣyanti, veditavyametat samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyādhiṣṭhānamiti ||
body.translated_text: 'These, O Blessed One, are the <s>dhāraṇī</s>-syllables. Whatever <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s>'s faculty of hearing these [syllables] shall approach — let it be known that this is the sustaining power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>.'

body.text: ayaṃ ca bhagavan saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo 'smin jambudvīpe pracaramāṇo yeṣāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ hastagato bhaviṣyati, tairbhagavan dharmabhāṇakairevaṃ veditavyam - samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasyānubhāvena yadasmākamayaṃ dharmaparyāyo hastagataḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya tejasā | samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya
body.translated_text: 'And this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s>, O Blessed One, circulating in this <s>Jambudvīpa</s> — those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> who will have it in hand, those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, O Blessed One, should understand thus: "It is by the power of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> that we have this <s>Dharma</s>-discourse in hand — by the splendor of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>. By the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>'s

body.text:
mahāsattvasya caryāyāste bhagavan sattvā lābhino bhaviṣyanti | bahubuddhāvaropitakuśalamūlāśca te sattvā bhaviṣyanti | tathāgatapāṇiparimārjitamūrdhānaśca te bhagavan sattvā bhaviṣyati | ye idaṃ sūtraṃ likhiṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti, mama tairbhagavan priyaṃ kṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati | ya idaṃ sūtraṃ likhisyanti, ye ca asyārthamanubhotsyante, likhitvā ca te bhagavannidaṃ sūtramitaścyutvā trāyastriṃśatāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāya upapatsyante, sahopapannānāṃ caiṣāṃ caturaśītirapsarasāṃ sahasrāṇyupasaṃkramiṣyanti | bherīmātreṇa mukuṭena te devaputrāstāsāmapsarasāṃ madhye sthāsyanti | īdṛśaḥ kulaputrā imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ likhitvā puṇyaskandhaḥ | kaḥ punarvādo ye etamuddekṣyanti svādhyāyiṣyanti cintayiṣyanti manasi kariṣyanti | tasmāttarhi kulaputrāḥ satkṛtya ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo likhitavyaḥ, sarvadetaḥ samanvāhṛtya | yaśca avikṣiptena manasikāreṇa likhiṣyati, tasya buddhasahasraṃ hastamupanāmayiṣyati, maraṇakāle cāsya buddhasahasraṃ saṃmukhamupadarśanaṃ kariṣyati | na ca durgativinipātagāmī bhaviṣyati | itaścyutaśca tuṣitānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyopapatsyate, yatra sa maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvastiṣṭhati, dvātriṃśadvaralakṣaṇo bodhisattvasattvagaṇaparivṛto 'psaraḥkoṭīnayutaśatasahasrapuraskṛto dharmaṃ deśayati | tasmāttarhi kulaputrāḥ paṇḍitena kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitā vā ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyaḥ satkṛtya likhitavyaḥ satkṛtyoddeṣṭavyaḥ, satkṛtya svādhyāyitavyaḥ, satkṛtya manasikartavyaḥ | imaṃ kulaputrā dharmaparyāyaṃ likhitvā uddiśya svādhyāyitvā bhāvayitvā manasikṛtvā evamaprameyā guṇā bhaviṣyanti | tasmāttarhi tena paṇḍitena bhagavan kulaputreṇa vā kuladuhitrā vā ayaṃ saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyo dhārayitavyaḥ | etāvantasteṣāṃ guṇānuśaṃsā bhaviṣyanti
| tasmāttarhi bhagavan ahamapi tāvadimaṃ dharmaparyāyamadhiṣṭhāsyāmi, yathā bhagavan mamādhiṣṭhānena ayaṃ dharmaparyāyo 'smin jambudvīpe pracariṣyati ||
body.translated_text: those beings, O Blessed One, will be gainers through the conduct of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> [<s>Samantabhadra</s>]. Those beings will have planted roots of merit under many <s>Buddhas</s>. Those beings, O Blessed One, will have their heads stroked by the hand of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Those who will write and uphold this <s>sūtra</s> — they will have done what is dear to me, O Blessed One. Those who will write this <s>sūtra</s> and comprehend its meaning — having written it, O Blessed One, upon departing from this [life], they will be reborn in the assembly of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods. And at their rebirth, eighty-four thousand <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) will approach them. Those sons of the gods, wearing drum-shaped crowns, will stand in the midst of those <s>apsarases</s>. Such, O sons of good family, is the heap of merit from merely writing this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. How much more so for those who will recite it, study it, contemplate it, and reflect upon it! Therefore, sons of good family, this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> should be written with respect, with full attention. And whoever will write it with undistracted attention — a thousand <s>Buddhas</s> will extend their hands to him, and at the time of death, a thousand <s>Buddhas</s> will appear before him face to face. And he will not go to the lower realms of misfortune. Having departed from here, he will be reborn in the assembly of the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods, where the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> dwells, endowed with the thirty-two supreme marks, surrounded by a company of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-beings, attended by hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>apsarases</s>, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Therefore, sons of good family, a wise son of good family or daughter of good family should write this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> with respect, recite it with respect, study it with respect, and reflect upon it with respect. Having written, recited, studied, cultivated, and reflected upon this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, O sons of good family, such immeasurable qualities will result. Therefore, that wise son of good family or daughter of good family, O Blessed One, should uphold this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Such will be the benefits and blessings for them. Therefore, O Blessed One, I too shall sustain this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> with my power, so that through my sustaining power, this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will spread throughout this <s>Jambudvīpa</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu tasyāṃ velāyāṃ bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ samantabhadrāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya sādhukāramadāt - sādhu sādhu samantabhadra, yatra hi nāma tvamevaṃ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāyai mahato janakāyasyārthāya hitāya sukhāya pratipannaḥ | evamacintyadharmasamanvāgato 'si mahākaruṇāsaṃgṛhītenādhyāśayena, acintyasaṃgṛhītena cittotpādena, yastvaṃ svayameva teṣāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāmadhiṣṭhānaṃ karoṣi | ye kecit kulaputrāḥ samantabhadrasya bodhisattvasya mahāsattvasya nāmadheyaṃ dhārayiṣyanti, veditavyaṃ taiḥ śākyamunistathāgato dṛṣṭa iti | ayaṃ ca saddharmapuṇḍarīko dharmaparyāyastasya bhagavataḥ śākyamunerantikācchrutaḥ | śākyamuniśca tathāgatastaiḥ pūjitaḥ | śākyamuneśca tathāgatasya dharmaṃ deśayataḥ sādhukāro 'nupradattaḥ | anumoditaścāyaṃ dharmaparyāyo bhaviṣyati śākyamuninā ca tathāgatena teṣāṃ mūrdhni pāṇiḥ pratiṣṭhāpito bhaviṣyati | bhagavāṃśca śākyamunistaiścīvarairavacchādito bhaviṣyati | tathāgataśāsanaparigrāhakāśca te samantabhadra kulaputrā vā kuladuhitaro
body.translated_text: Then, at that time, the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, gave his approval to the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s>: 'Excellent, excellent, <s>Samantabhadra</s>! Since you have indeed set forth for the benefit of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world. You are endowed with such inconceivable <s>dharmas</s>, possessed of an aspiration embraced by great compassion, with inconceivably embraced aspiration — you who of your own accord sustain those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers with your power. Those sons of good family who will hold the name of the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva</s> <s>Samantabhadra</s> should know: "The <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> has been seen by them." And this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s> has been heard from that Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> has been worshipped by them. And approval has been given to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> while teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. And this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> will have been rejoiced in. And the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> will have placed his hand upon their heads. And the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s> will have been covered with their robes. Those sons of good family or daughters of good family, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, should be known as upholders of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s teaching.

body.text:
vā veditavyāḥ | na ca teṣāṃ lokāyate rucirbhaviṣyati, na kāvyaprasṛtāḥ sattvāsteṣāmabhirucitā bhaviṣyanti, na nṛttakā na mallā na nartakā na śauṇḍikaurabhrikakaukkuṭikasaukarikastrīpoṣakāḥ sattvāsteṣāmabhirucitā bhaviṣyanti | īdṛśāṃśca sūtrāntān śrutvā likhitvā dhārayitvā vācayitvā vā na teṣāmanyadabhirucitaṃ bhaviṣyati | svabhāvadharmasamanvāgatāśca te sattvā veditavyāḥ | pratyātmikaśca teṣāṃ yoniśomanasikāro bhaviṣyati | svapuṇyabalādhārāśca te sattvā bhaviṣyanti, priyadarśanāśca te bhaviṣyanti sattvānām | evaṃ sūtrāntadhārakāśca ye bhikṣavo bhaviṣyanti, na teṣāṃ rāgo vyābādhiṣyati, na dveṣo na moho nerṣyā na mātsaryaṃ na mrakṣo na māno nādhimāno na mithyāmānaḥ | svalābhasaṃtuṣṭāśca te samantabhadra dharmabhāṇakā bhaviṣyanti | yaḥ samantabhadra paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ vartamānāyāmasya saddharmapuṇḍarīkasya dharmaparyāyasya dhārakaṃ bhikṣuṃ paśyet, evaṃ cittamutpādayitavyam - gamiṣyatyayaṃ kulaputro bodhimaṇḍam, nirjeṣyatyayaṃ kulaputro mārakalicakram,
pravartayiṣyatyayaṃ dharmacakram, parāhaniṣyatyayaṃ dharmadundubhim, prapūrayiṣyatyayaṃ dharmaśaṅkham, pravarṣayiṣyatyayaṃ dharmavarṣam, abhirokṣyatyayaṃ dharmasiṃhāsanam | ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ paścime kāle paścime samaye paścimāyāṃ pañcaśatyāṃ vartamānāyāṃ dhārayiṣyanti, na te bhikṣavo lubdhā bhaviṣyanti, na cīvaragṛddhā na pātragṛddhā bhaviṣyanti | ṛjukāśca te dharmabhāṇakā bhaviṣyanti | trivimokṣalābhinaśca te dharmabhāṇakā bhaviṣyanti | dṛṣṭadhārmikaṃ ca teṣāṃ nivartiṣyati | ya evaṃ sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ dharmabhāṇakānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ mohaṃ dāsyanti, jātyandhāste sattvā bhaviṣyanti | ye caivaṃrūpāṇāṃ sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāmavarṇaṃ saṃśrāvayiṣyanti, teṣāṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme kāyaścitro bhaviṣyati | ya evaṃ sūtrāntalekhakānāmuccagghanaṃ kariṣyanti ullapiṣyanti, te khaṇḍadantāśca bhaviṣyanti, varaladantāśca bhaviṣyanti, bībhatsoṣṭhāśca bhaviṣyanti, cipiṭanāsāśca bhaviṣyanti, viparītahastapādāśca bhaviṣyanti, viparītanetrāśca bhaviṣyanti, durgandhikāyāśca bhaviṣyanti, gaṇḍapiṭakavicarcidadrukaṇḍvākīrṇaśarīrāśca bhaviṣyanti | ye īdṛśānāṃ sūtrāntalekhakānāṃ sūtrāntavācakānāṃ ca sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ ca sūtrāntadeśakānāṃ ca apriyāṃ vācaṃ bhūtāmabhūtāṃ vā saṃśrāvayiṣyanti, teṣāmidamāgāḍhataraṃ pāpakaṃ karma veditavyam | tasmāttarhi samantabhadra asya dharmaparyāyasya dhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ dūrata eva pratyutthātavyam | yathā tathāgatasyāntike gauravaṃ kartavyam, tathā teṣāmeva sūtrāntadhārakāṇāṃ bhikṣūṇāmevaṃ gauravaṃ kartavyam ||
body.translated_text: They will have no taste for worldly philosophy. Beings devoted to poetry will not be agreeable to them. Neither dancers, nor wrestlers, nor performers, nor drunkards, butchers, fowlers, swineherds, or keepers of women — such beings will not be agreeable to them. And having heard, written, upheld, or recited such <s>sūtras</s>, they will have no taste for anything else. Those beings should be known as endowed with the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>. They will have wise attention directed inward. Those beings will be sustained by the power of their own merit, and they will be pleasing to behold by beings. And those monks who will be holders of such <s>sūtras</s> — passion will not afflict them, nor hatred, nor delusion, nor envy, nor jealousy, nor deceit, nor pride, nor conceit, nor wrong pride. Those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, will be content with little gain. Whoever, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, in the final time, in the final age, during the current final five hundred [years], sees a monk who upholds this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> <s>dharmaparyāya</s>, should generate this thought: 'This son of good family will go to the seat of awakening. This son of good family will defeat the hosts of <s>Māra</s>. He will turn the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel. He will beat the <s>Dharma</s>-drum. He will fill the <s>Dharma</s>-conch. He will rain the <s>Dharma</s>-rain. He will ascend the <s>Dharma</s> lion-throne.' Those monks who will uphold this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> in the final time, in the final age, during the current final five hundred [years] — they will not be greedy, nor desirous of robes, nor desirous of alms-bowls. Those <s>Dharma</s>-preachers will be upright. They will be attainers of the three liberations. The fruits will manifest in this very life for them. Those who give delusion to such monks who are holders of such <s>sūtras</s> and <s>Dharma</s>-preachers — those beings will be born blind. And those who spread ill-repute about such monks who hold <s>sūtras</s> — their bodies will become mottled in this very life. Those who will mock or ridicule such writers of <s>sūtras</s> — they will have broken teeth, gapped teeth, ugly lips, flat noses, crooked hands and feet, crooked eyes, foul-smelling bodies, and bodies covered with boils, tumors, skin disease, scabs, and itching. Those who will utter unpleasant words, whether true or false, to such writers, reciters, holders, and teachers of <s>sūtras</s> — their evil <s>karma</s> should be known as even more severe. Therefore, <s>Samantabhadra</s>, one should rise from afar for those monks who uphold this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Just as one should show respect in the presence of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, so should one show such respect to those very monks who uphold <s>sūtras</s>.'

body.text: asmin khalu punaḥ samantabhadrotsāhanaparivarte nirdiśyamāne gaṅgānadīvālikāsamānāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ mahāsattvānāṃ koṭīśatasahasrāvartāyā dhāraṇyāḥ pratilambho 'bhūt ||
body.translated_text: Now, while this <s>Samantabhadrotsāhana</s> (Encouragement of <s>Samantabhadra</s>) chapter was being taught, <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> equal in number to the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> attained the <s>Koṭīśatasahasrāvartā Dhāraṇī</s> (Dhāraṇī of Hundreds of Thousands of Koṭis of Revolutions).

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye samantabhadrotsāhanaparivarto nāma ṣaḍviṃśatimaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter of the noble <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s>, the <s>dharmaparyāya</s> (discourse), named the Chapter on the Encouragement of <s>Samantabhadra</s>.

body.text: Saddhp_27: anuparīndanāparivartaḥ |
body.translated_text: <s>Saddhp</s> 27: The Chapter on the Entrustment.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha utthāya tasmāddharmāsanāt sarvāṃstān bodhisattvāan piṇḍīkṛtya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā ṛddhayabhisaṃskārapariniṣpannena dakṣiṇahasteṣvadhyālambya tasyāṃ velāyāmetadavocat - imāmahaṃ kulaputrā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrasamudānītāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ yuṣmākaṃ haste parindāmi anuparindāmi nikṣipāmi upanikṣipāmi | yathā vipulā vaistārikī bhavet, tathā yuṣmābhiḥ kulaputrāḥ karaṇīyam | dvaitīyakamapi traitīyakamapi bhagavān sarvāvantaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇināadhyālambyaitadavocat - imāmahaṃ kulaputrā asaṃkhyeyakalpakoṭīnayutaśatasahasrasamudānītāmanuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ yuṣmākaṃ haste parindāmi anuparindāmi nikṣipāmi upanikṣipami | yuṣmābhiḥ kulaputra udgrahītavyā dhārayitavyā vācayitavyā paryavāptavyā deśayitavyā prakāśayitavyā | sarvasattvānāṃ ca saṃśrāvayitavyā | amātsaryo 'haṃ kulaputrā aparigṛhītacitto viśārado buddhajñānasya dātā, tathāgatajñānasya svayaṃbhūjñānasya dātā | mahādānapatirahaṃ kulaputrāḥ | yuṣmābhirapi kulaputrā mamaivānuśikṣitavyam | amatsaribhirbhūtvemaṃ tathāgatajñānadarśanaṃ mahopāyakauśalyamāgatānāṃ kulaputrāṇāṃ kuladuhitṛṇāṃ ca ayaṃ dharmaparyāyaḥ saṃśrāvayitavyaḥ | ye ca aśrāddhāḥ sattvāste 'smin dharmaparyāye samādāpayitavyāḥ | evaṃ yuṣmābhiḥ kulaputrāstathāgatānāṃ pratikāraḥ kṛto bhaviṣyati ||
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, rising from that <s>Dharma</s>-seat, gathered together all those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and grasping [them] with his right hand, perfected through the exercise of supernatural power, resting upon their right hands, at that time said this: 'I entrust to your hands, O sons of good family, this supreme perfect awakening, gathered over incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. I entrust it, I further entrust it, I deposit it, I hand it over. Let it become vast and widespread — thus should you act, O sons of good family.' A second time and a third time too, the Blessed One, grasping the entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> with his right hand, said this: 'I entrust to your hands, O sons of good family, this supreme perfect awakening, gathered over incalculable hundreds of thousands of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>nayutas</s> of <s>kalpas</s>. I entrust it, I further entrust it, I deposit it, I hand it over. You should take it up, O sons of good family, uphold it, recite it, master it, teach it, and illuminate it. And you should cause all beings to hear it. I am not miserly, O sons of good family; my mind is without grasping; I am a confident giver of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, a giver of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, of Self-Existent knowledge. I am a great lord of giving, O sons of good family. You too, O sons of good family, should follow my example. Being without miserliness, you should cause those sons and daughters of good family who come [to hear] this <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge and vision, this great skill in means — this <s>dharmaparyāya</s> — to hear it. And those beings who lack faith — they should be established in this <s>dharmaparyāya</s>. Thus, O sons of good family, you will have repaid the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: evamuktāste bodhisattva mahāsattva bhagavatā śākyamuninā tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena mahatā prītiprāmodyena sphutā abhūvan | mahacca gauravamutpādya yena bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhana samyaksaṃbuddhastenāvanatakāyāḥ praṇatakāyāḥ saṃnatakāyāḥ śirāṃsyavanāmya añjaliṃ pragṛhya sarva ekasvaranirghoṣeṇa bhagavantaṃ śākyamuniṃ tathāgatamarhantaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhametadūcuḥ - tathā bhagavan kariṣyāmo yathā tathāgata ājñāpayati | sarveṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmājñāṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, paripūrayiṣyāmaḥ | alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu yathāsukhavihārī | dvaitīyakamapi, traitīyakamapi sa sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇa ekasvaranirghoṣeṇa evaṃ bhāṣate sma - alpotsuko bhagavān bhavatu yathāsukhavihārī | tathā bhagavan kariṣyāmo yathā tathāgata ājñāpayati | sarveṣāṃ ca tathāgatānāmājñāṃ paripūrayiṣyāmaḥ ||
body.translated_text: When this was said, those <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>, addressed by the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, were pervaded with great joy and gladness. And generating great reverence, they bent their bodies, bowed their bodies, inclined their bodies toward the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One, lowered their heads, and with joined palms, all with a single voice, said this to the Blessed One <s>Śākyamuni</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One: 'So shall we do, O Blessed One, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> commands. We shall carry out the command of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and we shall fulfill it. May the Blessed One be at ease, dwelling in comfort.' A second time and a third time too, that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, with a single voice, spoke thus: 'May the Blessed One be at ease, dwelling in comfort. So shall we do, O Blessed One, as the <s>Tathāgata</s> commands. We shall fulfill the command of all the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.'

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān śākyamunistathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sarvāṃstāṃstathāgatānarhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhānanyebhyo lokadhātubhyaḥ samāgatān visarjayati sma | yathāsukhavihāraṃ ca teṣāṃ tathāgatānāmārocayati sma - yathāsukhaṃ tathāgatā viharantvarhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā iti | taṃ ca tasya bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya ratnastūpaṃ yathābhūmau sthāpayāmāsa | tasyāpi tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya yathāsukhavihāramārocayāmāsa ||
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dismissed all those <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones who had come from other world-systems. He announced to those <s>Tathāgatas</s> that they should dwell in comfort: 'May the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones dwell in comfort.' And he restored to the ground the jeweled <s>stūpa</s> of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One. And he also announced to that <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, that he should dwell in comfort.

body.text: idamavocad bhagavānāttamanāḥ | te cāprameyā asaṃkhyeyāstathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā anyalokadhātvāgatā ratnavṛkṣamūleṣu siṃhāsanopaviṣṭāḥ, prabhutaratnaśca tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sa ca sarvāvān bodhisattvagaṇaḥ, te ca viśiṣṭacāritrapramukhā aprameyā asaṃkhyeyā bodhisattva mahāsattvā ye pṛthivīvivarebhyo 'bhyudgatāḥ, te ca mahāśrāvakāḥ tāśca catasraḥ parṣadaḥ, sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandanniti ||
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rejoicing. And those immeasurable, innumerable <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones who had come from other world-systems, seated on lion-thrones at the bases of jeweled trees, and <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and that entire assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and those immeasurable, innumerable <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s> led by <s>Viśiṣṭacāritra</s> who had emerged from the crevices of the earth, and those great <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and those four assemblies, and the world with its <s>Devas</s>, humans, <s>Asuras</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> — all rejoiced at the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: iti śrīsaddharmapuṇḍarīke dharmaparyāye 'nuparīndanāparivarto nāma saptaviṃśatimaḥ samāptaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, named '<s>Anuparīndanā</s>' (Entrustment), in the <s>Śrī Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Dharmaparyāya</s> (the Sacred Lotus of the True Dharma).

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃ vādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus teaches the great ascetic.
